college-writing-000032.en: Zoé L. Albright has been involved in diverse aspects of education for twenty-five years.
college-writing-000032.zh: 佐伊·L·奥尔布赖特从事教育的各个领域工作已有25年。

college-writing-000033.en: For the last twenty-one years, she has been a faculty member at Metropolitan Community College–Longview, teaching developmental writing, composition, and literature.
college-writing-000033.zh: 在过去的二十一年里，她一直是大都会社区学院-朗维的教职员工，教授发展性写作、写作与文学课程。

college-writing-000034.en: She has created and implemented traditional and online curricula for high school and college English and composition courses and for a variety of literature courses.
college-writing-000034.zh: 她创建了并实施了针对高中及大学英语与写作课程以及各种文学课程的传统与在线课程。

college-writing-000035.en: She continues to research new educational theory and practices.
college-writing-000035.zh: 她继续研究新的教育理论与实践。

college-writing-000036.en: In addition to this extensive teaching experience, Zoé served as co-author of the previous edition of College Writing Skills with Readings and has most recently served as co-author of English Skills with Readings, tenth edition, and Exploring Writing, fourth edition.
college-writing-000036.zh: 除了这些丰富的教学经验之外，Zoé还担任了前版《大学写作技巧与阅读》一书的合著者，最近又参与了第十版《英语技能与阅读》以及第四版《探索写作》一书的合著工作。

college-writing-000037.en: She has also been a contributing author to other John Langan texts, including earlier editions of the Exploring Writing books and College Writing Skills with Readings.
college-writing-000037.zh: 她还作为合著者参与了其他关于约翰·兰根的作品的撰写，包括《探索写作》系列书籍的早期版本以及《大学写作技巧与阅读》一书。

college-writing-000038.en: She received her M.A. from Goldsmiths, University of London; B.S. and B.A. from the University of Idaho; and A.A. from Cottey College.
college-writing-000038.zh: 她毕业于伦敦大学金史密斯学院获得文学硕士学位；爱达荷大学获得理学学士学位和文学学士学位；科蒂学院则获得艺术学士学位。

college-writing-000039.en: She holds a Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction from the University of Kansas, where her focus was on developmental writers and their identities.
college-writing-000039.zh: 她拥有堪萨斯大学课程与教学专业的博士学位，她的研究重点是发展性作家及其身份问题。

college-writing-000040.en: Zoé currently resides near Kansas City, Missouri, with her family.
college-writing-000040.zh: 目前，佐伊与家人一起居住在密苏里州堪萨斯城附近。

college-writing-000041.en: John Langan has taught reading and writing at Atlantic Cape Community College near Atlantic City, New Jersey, for more than twenty-five years.
college-writing-000041.zh: 约翰·兰根在新泽西州大西洋城附近的大西洋角社区学院教授阅读和写作课程，已超过25年。

college-writing-000042.en: The author of a popular series of college textbooks on both writing and reading, John enjoys the challenge of developing materials that teach skills in an especially clear and lively way.
college-writing-000042.zh: 作为一套关于写作与阅读的受欢迎大学教材的作者，约翰乐于挑战以清晰生动的方式开发教学材料。

college-writing-000043.en: Before teaching, he earned advanced degrees in writing at Rutgers University and in reading at Rowan University.
college-writing-000043.zh: 在从事教学工作之前，他在罗格斯大学获得了写作方面的高级学位，在罗文大学获得了阅读方面的学位。

college-writing-000044.en: He also spent a year writing fiction that, he says, “is now at the back of a drawer waiting to be discovered and acclaimed posthumously.”
college-writing-000044.zh: 他还花了一年时间创作小说，他说这些作品“现在被藏在抽屉里，等待在死后被发掘和赞赏”。

college-writing-000045.en: While in school, he supported himself by working as a truck driver, a machinist, a battery assembler, a hospital attendant, and an apple packer.
college-writing-000045.zh: 在学校期间，他通过做卡车司机、机械师、电池组装工、医院服务员和苹果包装工来维持生活。

college-writing-000046.en: John now lives with his wife, Judith Nadell, near Philadelphia.
college-writing-000046.zh: 现在，约翰与他的妻子朱迪丝·纳德尔一起居住在费城附近。

college-writing-000047.en: In addition to his wife and Philly sports teams, his passions include reading and turning on nonreaders to the pleasure and power of books.
college-writing-000047.zh: 除了他的妻子和费城体育队之外，他的爱好还包括阅读，以及引导不读书的人体验书籍带来的乐趣与力量。

college-writing-000048.en: Through Townsend Press, his educational publishing company, he has developed the nonprofit “Townsend Library”—a collection of more than one hundred new and classic stories that appeal to readers of any age.
college-writing-000048.zh: 通过他的教育出版公司Townsend Press，他创建了非营利组织“Townsend图书馆”——该图书馆收录了超过一百篇新作与经典故事，适合各个年龄段的读者阅读。

college-writing-000247.zh: xiv 阅读内容，按修辞模式排列

college-writing-000249.en: The skills of writing and thinking critically about one’s world are not only important to a successful college career, they are also important to success in life.
college-writing-000249.zh: 批判性思考与写作的能力不仅对成功的大学学业至关重要，对人生成功也非常重要。

college-writing-000250.en: Especially now, as misinformation and disinformation run rampant, the ability to critically evaluate what we are reading and writing about is more essential than ever.
college-writing-000250.zh: 尤其是现在，在错误信息和虚假信息泛滥的情况下，能够批判性地评估我们所阅读和撰写的内容，比以往任何时候都更为重要。

college-writing-000251.en: It is because of these shifting needs that I have worked hard to increase the critical thinking lessons throughout this text while still emphasizing the strong pedagogy surrounding good writing.
college-writing-000251.zh: 正因这些不断变化的需求，我努力在本文中增加批判性思维相关的内容，同时仍强调与优秀写作相关的有效教学方法。

college-writing-000252.en: Students are introduced to topics that will challenge their perceptions and beliefs, including a new research essay titled “Environmental Health” that examines food waste.
college-writing-000252.zh: 学生将接触到能够挑战他们认知与信念的课题，其中包括一篇名为“环境健康”的新研究论文，该论文探讨了食物浪费问题。

college-writing-000253.en: Many of the new readings are from marginalized voices.
college-writing-000253.zh: 许多新的解读来自被边缘化的声音。

college-writing-000254.en: For some students, these readings will serve as an introduction to unfamiliar points of view, and for other students, these readings may echo their own lived experiences.
college-writing-000254.zh: 对于某些学生来说，这些阅读材料可以作为了解不同观点入门的途径；而对于其他学生来说，这些阅读材料则可能反映他们自身的实际经历。

college-writing-000255.en: These new essays and readings should encourage lively discussions in the classroom.
college-writing-000255.zh: 这些新的文章和阅读材料应当能激发课堂上的热烈讨论。

college-writing-000256.en: As an educator who has been in the classroom for almost three decades, I have seen my students’ and colleagues’ needs change.
college-writing-000256.zh: 作为一名在课堂上任教了近三十年的教师，我见证了我的学生及同事的需求不断变化。

college-writing-000257.en: Strong grammar foundations have been shaken by social media use and texting.
college-writing-000257.zh: 社交媒体和短信的使用已经动摇了扎实的语法基础。

college-writing-000258.en: Search engines and databases have affected the art of research and the incorporation of research into writing.
college-writing-000258.zh: 搜索引擎和数据库影响了研究工作的进行方式以及研究成果转化为文字的形式。

college-writing-000259.en: The constant bombardment of new information has had a negative impact on the ability to think through a topic slowly.
college-writing-000259.zh: 不断涌入的新信息对缓慢思考某个主题的能力产生了负面影响。

college-writing-000260.en: This new edition of College Writing Skills with Readings was developed with the goal of addressing these changes.
college-writing-000260.zh: 这本新版《大学写作技巧与阅读》旨在应对这些变化而编写。

college-writing-000261.en: Its lessons are designed to help students gain the strong foundational skills that they need to navigate what it means to be not only a college student in the twenty-first century but also an active and responsible citizen of the world.
college-writing-000261.zh: 这些课程旨在帮助学生掌握必要的基础技能，使他们能够应对作为21世纪的大学生以及世界上有责任、有担当的公民所面临的挑战。

college-writing-000262.en: A W O R D F R O M Z O É L .

college-writing-000263.en: A L B R I G H T
college-writing-000263.zh: A L B R I G H T

college-writing-000266.en: College Writing Skills with Readings is designed to help students gain the strong foundational skills that they need to succeed in college and in their lives beyond college.
college-writing-000266.zh: 《大学写作技能与阅读》课程旨在帮助学生获得在大学及大学之后的人生中取得成功所需的必备基础技能。

college-writing-000267.en: It does this by focusing on the four bases of unity, support, coherence, and sentence skills; emphasizing writing for personal, academic, and workplace settings; focusing on information literacy and research writing; and demonstrating for students how the stages of the writing process work together.
college-writing-000267.zh: 它通过关注团结、支持、连贯性和句子表达这四大要素来实现这一点；强调在个人、学术和职场场景下的写作需求；注重信息素养与研究性写作；并向学生展示写作过程的各个阶段是如何相互关联的。

college-writing-000268.en: Mastering the Four Bases: Unity, Support, Coherence, Sentence Skills
college-writing-000268.zh: 掌握四种基础：统一性、支持性、连贯性、句子技巧

college-writing-000269.en: College Writing Skills with Readings, eleventh edition, emphasizes writing skills and process.
college-writing-000269.zh: 《带阅读的高校写作技巧》第11版着重于写作技巧与写作过程。

college-writing-000270.en: By referring to a set of four skills for effective writing, College Writing Skills with Readings, eleventh edition, encourages new writers to see writing as a skill that can be learned and a process that must be explored.
college-writing-000270.zh: 《带阅读的高校写作技巧》第11版中提到了有效写作的四大技能，鼓励新作者将写作视为一种可以学习的技能，以及需要探索的过程。

college-writing-000271.en: The four skills, or bases, for effective writing are as follows:
college-writing-000271.zh: 有效写作的四种技能或基础如下：

college-writing-000272.en: • Unity: Discover a clearly stated point, or topic sentence, and make sure that all other information in the paragraph or essay supports that point.
college-writing-000272.zh: • 统一性：找出一个明确表述的观点或主题句，并确保段落或文章中的所有其他信息都支持这一观点。

college-writing-000273.en: • Support: Support the points with specific evidence, and plenty of it.
college-writing-000273.zh: • 支持：用具体的证据来支持这些观点，而且要有大量的证据。

college-writing-000274.en: • Coherence: Organize and connect supporting evidence so that paragraphs and essays transition smoothly from one bit of supporting information to the next.
college-writing-000274.zh: • 连贯性：组织并衔接支撑论点的证据，让段落和文章从一条论据自然过渡到下一条。

college-writing-000275.en: • Sentence skills: Revise and edit so that sentences are error-free for clearer and more effective communication.
college-writing-000275.zh: • 句子表达技巧：对文本进行修订与编辑，确保句子无错误，从而实现更清晰、更有效的沟通。

college-writing-000276.en: The four bases are essential to effective writing, whether it be a narrative paragraph, a cover letter for a job application, or an essay assignment.
college-writing-000276.zh: 这四种基本结构对于有效写作至关重要，无论是叙述性段落、求职申请信，还是论文作业。

college-writing-000277.en: Twenty-seven professional readings support the development of the four bases by modeling effective writing, as well as inspiring lively class discussion and providing a continuing source of high-interest material for a wide range of writing assignments.
college-writing-000277.zh: 27篇专业阅读材料通过示范有效的写作方式，为四个基础领域的发展提供了支持；同时还能激发活跃的课堂讨论，并为各种写作任务提供持续的高兴趣素材来源。

college-writing-000278.en: Reflecting the diversity of backgrounds, experiences, and identities of the college writing classroom and students’ broader communities, 50 percent of the readings are written by authors of historically marginalized groups.
college-writing-000278.zh: 反映了大学写作课堂以及学生所在更广泛群体的背景、经历与身份的多样性，50%的阅读材料由历史上被边缘化的群体的作者所撰写。

college-writing-000279.en: For some students, these readings will serve as an introduction to unfamiliar points of view, and for other students, their own lived experiences may be echoed by these readings.
college-writing-000279.zh: 对于某些学生来说，这些阅读材料可以作为了解不同观点入门的途径；而对于其他学生而言，他们自身的经历也可能通过这些阅读材料得到体现。

college-writing-000281.zh: 发现一个明确表述的观点，

college-writing-000282.en: or topic sentence, and make sure that all other information
college-writing-000282.zh: 或主题句，并确保所有其他信息也符合要求。

college-writing-000287.en: evidence so that paragraphs and essays transition smoothly
college-writing-000287.zh: 以便段落和文章能够流畅衔接

college-writing-000291.en: Revise and edit so that sentences
college-writing-000291.zh: 进行修改和编辑，使句子

college-writing-000292.en: are error-free for clearer and more effective communication.
college-writing-000292.zh: 无错误，有助于更清晰、更有效的沟通。

college-writing-000294.zh: 用具体的内容支持这些观点

college-writing-000298.en: College Writing Skills with Readings, eleventh edition, is flexible and emphasizes personal learning, academic learning, and workplace preparation.
college-writing-000298.zh: 《基于阅读的大学生写作技能》第11版具有灵活性，注重个人学习、学术学习与职场准备。

college-writing-000299.en: Students are exposed to examples of writing that reflect these three key realms of their lives to help them understand the critical way in which writing will have an impact on the many facets of their lives.
college-writing-000299.zh: 学生可以接触到体现他们生活这三个关键领域的写作范例，以帮助他们理解写作对他们生活的诸多方面所产生的深远影响。

college-writing-000300.en: To help students learn the different characteristics of each type of writing, icons identifying specific writing pieces, examples, and assignments are integrated throughout the chapters.
college-writing-000300.zh: 为了帮助学生理解各类写作的不同特点，各章节中都包含了标识特定写作类型的图标、示例以及作业内容。

college-writing-000301.en: Writings that employ first-person point of view, narrative, and/or an informal tone are marked “Personal.”
college-writing-000301.zh: 采用第一人称视角、叙述风格和/或非正式语气的写作被标记为“个人化”。

college-writing-000302.en: Writings that employ a third-person point of view, a formal tone, and focus on academic topics are identified as “Academic.”
college-writing-000302.zh: 采用第三人称视角、正式语气，并围绕学术主题撰写的文章被归类为“学术类”。

college-writing-000303.en: Writings that employ a third-person point of view, a formal tone, and focus on employment-related topics are marked “Work.”
college-writing-000303.zh: 采用第三人称视角、正式语气，并聚焦于就业相关话题的文章会被标记为“工作”。

college-writing-000304.en: In addition to these abundant examples, there are writing assignments and activities emphasizing each of these categories throughout the chapters and readings anthology, so students can gain practice writing for a variety of audiences and situations.
college-writing-000304.zh: 除了这些丰富的例子之外，各章节和阅读选集中还有各种写作任务与活动，旨在帮助学生练习针对不同受众和情境进行写作。

college-writing-000305.en: This variety provides flexibility in the kinds of assignments you may wish to give.
college-writing-000305.zh: 这种品种能够让你拥有更大的灵活性，可以布置各种任务。

college-writing-000307.en: Emphasis on Information Literacy and Research Writing
college-writing-000307.zh: 强调信息素养与研究写作能力

college-writing-000308.en: College Writing Skills with Readings, eleventh edition, continues to focus strongly on information literacy, research, and source-based essay writing.
college-writing-000308.zh: 《基于阅读的大学生写作技巧》第11版继续强调信息素养、研究与基于来源的文章写作。

college-writing-000309.en: Students are introduced to using and locating online sources effectively and efficiently and employing critical thinking skills to determine the reliability and validity of sources found.
college-writing-000309.zh: 学生将学习如何有效、高效地使用和查找在线资料，并运用批判性思维技能来判断所找到的资料的可靠性与有效性。

college-writing-000310.en: Resources available at most college libraries─including the expertise of resource librarians and how to make best use of that expertise─are discussed in detail.
college-writing-000310.zh: 大多数大学图书馆所拥有的资源——包括资源馆员的专业知识以及如何充分利用这些专业知识——将进行详细探讨。

college-writing-000311.en: In addition to learning how to choose sources, students are exposed to a new, more detailed look at the skills of paraphrasing and summarizing.
college-writing-000311.zh: 除了学习如何选择资料来源外，学生还能了解到关于释义和概括技巧的更详细内容。

college-writing-000312.en: As well, students are given an in-depth experience devoted to sourcebased essay writing and research, including how to create a plan to meet deadlines set by instructors; how to take good notes; how to incorporate sources to avoid plagiarism; and how to use proper MLA format.
college-writing-000312.zh: 此外，学生还将获得针对基于文献的论文写作与研究的深入培训，包括如何制定计划以按时完成教师规定的任务；如何做好笔记；如何引用参考文献以避免抄袭；以及如何使用正确的MLA格式。

college-writing-000313.en: Along with a full-length sample research paper, students are also given the opportunity to read several source-based literary analyses throughout the textbook.
college-writing-000313.zh: 除了完整的样本研究论文外，学生还有机会在教材中阅读多个基于资料的文学分析文章。

college-writing-000315.en: College Writing Skills with Readings, eleventh edition, provides strong writing pedagogy.
college-writing-000315.zh: 《带阅读的大学生写作技巧》第11版提供了优秀的写作教学方法。

college-writing-000316.en: To help students see the whole picture and walk actively through the steps of the entire writing process, Chapter 7 provides an extended example of one student’s complete writing process, demonstrating the student’s prewriting, organizing, drafting, revision, editing, and resulting (but still evolving) final draft.
college-writing-000316.zh: 为了帮助学生全面理解写作过程，并主动遵循整个写作流程的各个环节，第7章提供了一个学生完整写作过程的详细示例，展示了该学生的预写作、组织、草稿、修改、编辑以及最终成品（仍在不断完善中）的整个过程。

college-writing-000317.en: This chapter culminates Part 1, in which the six preceding chapters offer in-depth instruction about different facets and steps of the writing process from prewriting through revision.
college-writing-000317.zh: 本章是第一部分的收尾部分，前六章详细介绍了从构思阶段到修改阶段的写作过程中的各种方面与步骤。

college-writing-000318.en: Chapter 1 explains why writing is important in all aspects of life.
college-writing-000318.zh: 第一章阐述了为什么写作在生活的各个方面都至关重要。

college-writing-000319.en: Chapter 2 offers an overview of the writing process.
college-writing-000319.zh: 第二章对写作过程进行了概述。

college-writing-000320.en: Chapters 3, 4, and 5 break down the steps of the writing process, providing explanations and extensive activities to help students practice, and Chapter 6 helps students understand and apply the Four Bases for revising.
college-writing-000320.zh: 第3、4和5章详细介绍了写作过程的各个步骤，并提供了解释和丰富的练习内容以帮助学生练习；第6章则帮助学生理解并应用修改的四大基础。

college-writing-000322.en: C H A P T E R - B Y- C H A P T E R C H A N G E S
college-writing-000322.zh: 第B章 第C章 变化

college-writing-000323.en: The eleventh edition of College Writing Skills with Readings includes the following chapter-by-chapter changes:
college-writing-000323.zh: 《大学写作技巧与阅读资料》第十一版包含以下逐章修改内容：

college-writing-000324.en: Part 1: Essay Writing • Revised and updated section on using technology to write and study efficiently • Revised and updated coverage of MLA guidelines, including such key areas as inclusive language and formatting in research writing • Reorganized and augmented coverage of purpose and audience • Enhanced discussion of peer and personal review • More clearly identified steps and stages in Chapter 7's full length student essay, which demonstrates the writing process from prewriting through peer review, self-evaluation, and revising
college-writing-000324.zh: 第一部分：论文写作 • 对如何利用技术高效写作与学习的相关内容进行了修订与更新 • 对MLA规范要求的介绍也进行了更新，包括研究写作中涉及的语言包容性及格式要求等关键内容 • 对写作目的与受众的相关内容进行了重新整理与补充 • 对同行评审与个人评审的相关内容进行了更深入的探讨 • 第7章中完整的学生论文的写作流程有了更清晰的步骤与阶段说明，该论文展示了从构思阶段到同行评审、自我评估以及修改的整个写作过程

college-writing-000325.en: Part 2: Patterns of Essay Development • All student essays and Writing Assignments thoroughly examined and revised as needed for sensitivity to culture, gender, and differences in ability • Several Model Essays repositioned to better fit within a particular pattern, each incorporating new pedagogy • Continued emphasis on essays with more than three supporting paragraphs • More clearly called-out and identified examples of Literary Analysis • All Four Bases Checklists thoroughly examined and revised as necessary, to insure focus on the specific needs of the targeted mode
college-writing-000325.zh: 第二部分：文章写作的模式 • 所有学生文章及写作任务都经过了详细审查与修改，以更好地适应文化、性别以及能力差异的要求 • 几篇范文被重新调整，以更契合特定模式，其中每篇都融入了新的教学理念 • 继续强调包含超过三个支持段落的文章 • 对文学分析示例的标注更加明确 • 所有四个检查清单也经过详细审查与必要修改，以确保满足特定写作模式的具体需求

college-writing-000326.en: Part 3: Researching, Writing, and Documenting • Full and updated coverage of students’ use of the Internet, technology, and the library in the digital age • Revised, newly focused, and enhanced treatment of paraphrasing • Expanded coverage of note-taking that fully illustrates and explains two different methods • New discussion of misinformation and disinformation
college-writing-000326.zh: 第三部分：研究、写作与记录 • 全面且更新了关于学生在数字时代使用互联网、技术和图书馆的情况 • 对释义性写作进行了修订、重新聚焦与优化处理 • 对笔记记录方式进行了更详细的介绍，同时阐明了两种不同的方法 • 对错误信息和虚假信息进行了新的探讨

college-writing-000327.en: • New full length student research paper that illustrates key research skills including the essential steps in writing a good research paper • Revised and updated examples of correct source citation per recent MLA guidelines • Updated and increased coverage of identifying and avoiding plagiarism • More clearly called-out and identified examples of Rhetorical Analysis and Literary Analysis • Text explanations and discussions formatted to make them more accessible to students
college-writing-000327.zh:
• 新的完整版学生研究论文，展示了关键的研究技能，包括撰写优秀研究论文所需的基本步骤  
• 根据最新的MLA规范，对正确的资料引用方式进行了修订和更新  
• 对识别与避免剽窃的内容进行了更新和补充  
• 对修辞分析与文学分析的例子进行了更清晰的说明与标注  
• 文本说明与讨论部分进行了优化，以便学生更容易理解

college-writing-000328.en: Part 4: Handbook of Sentence Skills • All grammar activities, exercises, and Review Tests thoroughly updated for currency • Pronoun instruction and examples reworked and updated to reflect gender-neutral usage • Grammar activities, exercises, and Review Tests continue to incorporate personal, academic, and workplace-related themes • Many tests and activities focused on single issue so that each reads as a unified passage
college-writing-000328.zh: 第四部分：句子技能手册 • 所有语法活动、练习及复习测试均进行了全面更新 • 代词相关说明与示例也经过修改，以反映性别中立的用法 • 语法活动、练习及复习测试继续包含与个人生活、学术及职场相关的主题 • 许多测试与活动都聚焦于某一特定主题，因此整体来看这些内容属于一个连贯的体系

college-writing-000329.en: Part 5: Readings for Writers • Readings updated to include selections by diverse voices • New readings with accompanying questions and assignments include: • “Colleges Must Confront Structural Racism” by Kevin V. Collymore • “What Academics Misunderstand about ‘Public Writing’” by Irina Dumitrescu • “Purposefully Mispronouncing Kamala Harris’s Name is Racist, Plain and Simple” by Duaa Israr • “Memes and the Art of Nonsense” by Serena G. Pellegrino • “A Memoir Reflects on What Happens to the ‘Fairest’ of Them All” by Hope Wabuke
college-writing-000329.zh: 第五部分：供写作者阅读的文本 • 这些文本已更新，包含了来自不同作者的作品 • 新增的文本以及相应的问题与作业包括：• 凯文·V·科利莫尔所著的《大学必须面对结构性种族主义》 • 伊丽娜·杜米特雷斯库所著的《学者们对‘公共写作’的误解》 • 杜阿·伊斯拉尔所著的《故意误读卡玛拉·哈里斯的名字是种族主义，很简单》 • 塞雷娜·G·佩莱格里诺所著的《模因与荒谬的艺术》 • 霍普·瓦布克所著的《一部回忆录，反映了那些‘最美丽’的人所遭遇的事》

college-writing-000332.en: R E S O U R C E S T O S U P P O R T Y O U R T E A C H I N G
college-writing-000332.zh: 结果取决于你的努力程度

college-writing-000333.en: Connect Writing for College Writing Skills with Readings
college-writing-000333.zh: 将写作训练与阅读内容相结合，以提升大学写作能力

college-writing-000334.en: Connect is a highly reliable, easy-to-use homework and learning management solution that embeds learning science and award-winning adaptive tools to improve student results.
college-writing-000334.zh: Connect是一款非常可靠、易于使用的作业与学习管理工具，它融合了学习科学理念及获奖的自适应功能，有助于提升学生的学习成果。

college-writing-000335.en: Connect Writing offers comprehensive, reliable writing and research content that is designed to actively engage students and help prepare them to be successful writers.
college-writing-000335.zh: Connect Writing提供全面、可靠的写作与研究内容，旨在激发学生的参与热情，帮助他们成为优秀的作家。

college-writing-000336.en: This is done through Connect components such as Adaptive Learning Assignment, Power of Process, the College Writing Skills with Readings eBook, and Writing Assignment Plus.
college-writing-000336.zh: 这是通过诸如自适应学习任务、流程的力量、包含阅读内容的大学写作技能电子书以及写作任务加等连接组件来实现的。

college-writing-000337.en: Adaptive Learning Assignment Adaptive Learning Assignment provides each student a personalized path to learning concepts instructors assign in their course.
college-writing-000337.zh: 自适应学习任务分配系统为每位学生提供个性化的学习路径，以便他们能够掌握课程中教师所教授的概念。

college-writing-000338.en: The assignments continually adapt to the individual, identifying knowledge gaps and focusing on areas where remediation is needed.
college-writing-000338.zh: 这些任务会不断根据个人情况进行调整，识别知识空白点，并聚焦需要弥补的领域。

college-writing-000339.en: All adaptive content─including questions and integrated concept resources─is specifically targeted to, and directly aligned with, the individual learning objectives being assessed in the course.
college-writing-000339.zh: 所有适应性内容——包括题目和整合概念资源——都是针对课程中所评估的个性化学习目标而设计的，并与之直接对齐。

college-writing-000341.en: Power of Process One overarching goal is at the heart of Power of Process: for students to become self-regulating, strategic readers and writers.
college-writing-000341.zh: “过程的力量”这一理念的核心目标就是：让学生成为能够自我调节、具备战略思维的读者和作家。

college-writing-000342.en: Power of Process facilitates engaged reading and writing processes using research-based best practices suggested by major professional reading and writing organizations.
college-writing-000342.zh: “过程力量”机制促进了以主要专业阅读与写作机构所推荐的基于研究的最佳实践为方法的阅读与写作活动。

college-writing-000343.en: Instructors can choose from a bank of carefully chosen readings within Power of Process, readings from College Writing Skills with Readings, or upload their own readings.
college-writing-000343.zh: 教师可以从“过程力量”平台中精心挑选的阅读材料库中选择材料，也可以选择《大学写作技能与阅读材料》中的内容，或者上传自己的阅读材料。

college-writing-000344.en: As with the professional readings in the text, 50 percent of the forty-six additional readings in Power of Process are written by Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) authors.
college-writing-000344.zh: 与文本中的专业作品一样，Power of Process系列中另外46篇作品中有50%是由黑人、原住民和有色人种（BIPOC）作者所写。

college-writing-000345.en: College Writing Skills with Readings eBook The entire College Writing Skills with Readings text can be accessed through Connect or as a standalone ebook.
college-writing-000345.zh: 《College Writing Skills with Readings》电子书：整个《College Writing Skills with Readings》教材可以通过Connect平台访问，也可以作为独立电子书使用。

college-writing-000346.en: At McGraw Hill Higher Education, our mission is to accelerate learning through intuitive, engaging, efficient, and effective experiences, grounded in research.
college-writing-000346.zh: 在麦格哈里尔高等教育机构，我们的使命是通过基于研究、直观、有趣、高效且有效的体验来加速学习进程。

college-writing-000347.en: Assignments in Connect are WCAG compliant, and updates to the ebook of the eleventh edition of College Writing Skills go beyond WCAG compliance to create an improved reading experience for all learners.
college-writing-000347.zh: Connect平台中的任务符合WCAG标准，而《大学写作技巧》第十一版电子书的更新内容则不仅满足WCAG标准，还旨在为所有学习者提供更好的阅读体验。

college-writing-000348.en: These enhancements include improved functionality for viewing annotated readings and editing marks.
college-writing-000348.zh: 这些改进包括优化了标注阅读内容查看和编辑标记的功能。

college-writing-000349.en: We are committed to creating universally accessible products that unlock the full potential of each learner, including individuals with disabilities.
college-writing-000349.zh: 我们致力于打造具有普遍可访问性的产品，从而释放每个学习者的全部潜力，包括残障人士的潜力。

college-writing-000350.en: Writing Assignment Plus McGraw Hill’s new Writing Assignment Plus tool delivers a learning experience that improves students’ written communication skills and conceptual understanding with every assignment.
college-writing-000350.zh: “写作作业加”麦格劳希尔的新工具能够为学生提供学习体验，通过每次作业都能提升学生的写作能力和概念理解能力。

college-writing-000351.en: Assign, monitor, and provide feedback on writing more efficiently and grade assignments within
college-writing-000351.zh: 能够更高效地分配任务、监控进度并提供反馈，同时能在内部对作业进行评分。

college-writing-000363.en: Writing Assignment Plus gives you time-saving tools with just-in-time basic writing and originality checker.
college-writing-000363.zh: Writing Assignment Plus提供了节省时间的工具，包括即时基础写作功能和创意检测器。

college-writing-000365.en: The Annotated Instructor’s Edition consists of the student text, including answers to all activities and tests, as well as a complete Instructor’s Guide.
college-writing-000365.zh: 《带注释的讲师版教材》包含学生용教材，包含所有练习和测试的答案，以及完整的讲师指南。

college-writing-000366.en: Available within Connect are a number of instructional materials, including the instructor’s manual, chapter quizzes, a variety of handouts, and PowerPoint® slides that may be tailored to course needs.
college-writing-000366.zh: 在Connect平台上提供多种教学材料，包括教师手册、章节测验、各种讲义以及可根据课程需求定制的PowerPoint®幻灯片。

college-writing-000367.zh: 学习管理系统集成服务

college-writing-000368.en: Connect Writing integrates with your local Learning Management System (Blackboard, Canvas, and others).
college-writing-000368.zh: Connect Writing可以与您当地的学习管理系统（Blackboard、Canvas等）相集成。

college-writing-000391.en: Even accomplished political leaders like Franklin D. Roosevelt have to write several drafts of speeches before creating the final product.
college-writing-000391.zh: 就连像富兰克林·D·罗斯福这样成就卓著的政治领袖，在最终确定演讲内容之前，也不得不撰写多个初稿。

college-writing-000392.en: Study this excerpted draft of FDR’s address to Congress asking for a declaration of war after Pearl Harbor was attacked by the Japanese during World War II.
college-writing-000392.zh: 研究一下富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福在二战期间日本袭击珍珠港后向国会发表的演讲草稿，他在演讲中请求宣布战争。

college-writing-000393.en: Choose one aspect of this revision and explain why and how it makes the speech more effective.
college-writing-000393.zh: 选择这一修订中的某个方面，说明为什么以及如何使其演讲更加有效。

college-writing-000415.en: Be sure to include your reasons for wanting such a job.

college-writing-000421.en: Observations from co-author John Langan: The experience I had writing my first college essay helped shape this book.
college-writing-000421.zh: 合著者约翰·兰根的观点：我撰写第一份大学申请文书的经历，对这本书的创作起到了重要作用。

college-writing-000422.en: I received a C– for the essay.

college-writing-000423.en: Scrawled beside the grade was the comment “Not badly written, but ill-conceived.”
college-writing-000423.zh: 在年级旁边写着这样的评论：“书写不差，但构思不佳。”

college-writing-000424.en: I remember going to the instructor after class, asking about his comment as well as the word Log that he had added in the margin at various spots.
college-writing-000424.zh: 我记得下课后去问老师，询问他关于他的评论，以及他在各个地方在页边空白处添加的“Log”一词。

college-writing-000425.en: “What are all these logs you put in my paper?”
college-writing-000425.zh: “你把我论文里塞进的这些日志是什么东西？”

college-writing-000426.en: I asked, trying to make a joke of it.
college-writing-000426.zh: 我试着开个玩笑来问这个问题。

college-writing-000427.en: He looked at me a little wonderingly.
college-writing-000427.zh: 他带着几分诧异地看了我一眼。

college-writing-000428.zh: “逻辑，兰根先生，”他回答道，“就是逻辑。”

college-writing-000429.en: He went on to explain that I had not thought out my paper clearly.
college-writing-000429.zh: 他进一步说明，我的论文没有阐述得清晰明了。

college-writing-000430.en: There were actually two ideas rather than one in my thesis, one supporting paragraph had nothing to do with either idea, another paragraph lacked a topic sentence, and so on.
college-writing-000430.zh: 我的论文实际上包含两个观点，而不是一个；其中一个支持性段落与这两个观点都无关；另一个段落则没有主题句，诸如此类的问题都存在。

college-writing-000433.en: I’ve never forgotten his last words: “If you don’t think clearly,” he said, “you won’t write clearly.”
college-writing-000433.zh: 他最后对我说的话，我一直没有忘记：“如果思路不清楚，”他说，“就写不清楚。”

college-writing-000434.en: I was speechless, and I felt confused and angry.
college-writing-000434.zh: 我无言以对，感到困惑和愤怒。

college-writing-000435.en: I didn’t like being told that I didn’t know how to think.
college-writing-000435.zh: 我不喜欢别人说我不知道如何思考。

college-writing-000436.en: I went back to my room and read over my paper several times.
college-writing-000436.zh: 我回到房间，反复阅读我的论文。

college-writing-000437.en: Eventually, I decided that my instructor was right.
college-writing-000437.zh: 最终，我意识到我的指导老师是对的。

college-writing-000438.en: “No more logs,” I said to myself.

college-writing-000439.en: “I’m going to get these logs out of my papers.”
college-writing-000439.zh: “我要把这些文件从我的文件里拿出来。”

college-writing-000440.zh: 我的指导老师的建议非常宝贵。

college-writing-000441.en: I learned that clear, disciplined thinking is the key to effective writing.
college-writing-000441.zh: 我了解到，清晰、有纪律的思考是有效写作的关键。

college-writing-000442.en: College Writing Skills with Readings develops this idea by breaking down the writing process into a series of four logical, easily followed steps.
college-writing-000442.zh: 《大学写作技巧与阅读》通过将写作过程分解为四个逻辑清晰、易于遵循的步骤，来阐述这一理念。

college-writing-000443.en: These steps, combined with practical advice about prewriting and revision, will help you write strong papers.
college-writing-000443.zh: 这些步骤，加上关于预写作和修改的实用建议，将帮助你写出优秀的论文。

college-writing-000444.en: Here are the four steps in a nutshell:
college-writing-000444.zh: 以下是四个步骤的简要概述：

college-writing-000445.en: 1. Discover a clearly stated point, or thesis.
college-writing-000445.zh: 1. 找出一个明确表述的观点或论点。

college-writing-000446.en: 2. Provide logical, detailed support for your thesis.
college-writing-000446.zh: 2. 为你的论点提供逻辑性强、内容详尽的支持。

college-writing-000447.en: 3. Organize and connect your supporting material.
college-writing-000447.zh: 3. 整理并连接你的辅助材料。

college-writing-000448.en: 4. Revise and edit so that your sentences are effective and error-free.
college-writing-000448.zh: 4. 修改和编辑，确保句子表达清晰且无错误。

college-writing-000449.en: Part 1 of this book explains each of these steps in detail and provides many practice materials to help you master them.
college-writing-000449.zh: 本书第一部分详细介绍了这些步骤，并提供了许多练习材料以帮助你掌握它们。

college-writing-000450.en: Point and Support An Important Difference between Writing and Talking In everyday conversation, you make all kinds of points or assertions.
college-writing-000450.zh: 观点与表达：写作与口语之间的重要差异。在日常对话中，我们会提出各种观点或主张。

college-writing-000451.en: You say, for example, “My boss is a hard person to work for,” “It’s not safe to walk in our neighborhood after dark,” or “Poor study habits keep getting me into trouble.”
college-writing-000451.zh: 例如，你可以说：“我的老板是个难以共事的人”，“夜色过后在我们社区行走并不安全”，或者“糟糕的学习习惯总是让我陷入麻烦”。

college-writing-000452.en: The points that you make concern personal matters as well as, at times, outside issues: “That trade will be a disaster for the team,” “Many advertisements are degrading to women,” “Students are better off working for a year before attending college.”
college-writing-000452.zh: 你提到的这些观点涉及个人问题，有时也涉及外部问题：“那种贸易行为会对团队造成破坏”，“许多广告对女性有贬低作用”，“学生们不如先工作一年再上大学好。”

college-writing-000453.en: The people you are talking with do not always challenge you to give reasons for your statements.
college-writing-000453.zh: 你交谈的人并不总要求你为自己的言论提供理由。

college-writing-000454.en: They may know why you feel as you do, or they may already
college-writing-000454.zh: 他们可能知道你为何会有这样的感受，或者他们可能已经……

college-writing-000456.en: agree with you, or they simply may not want to put you on the spot; and so they do not always ask why.
college-writing-000456.zh: 同意你的观点，或者他们可能根本不想让你陷入尴尬的境地；因此他们并不总是询问原因。

college-writing-000457.en: But the people who read what you write may not know you, agree with you, or feel in any way obliged to you.
college-writing-000457.zh: 但阅读你作品的人可能并不认识你，也不认同你，更没有任何义务去支持你。

college-writing-000458.en: If you want to communicate effectively with readers, you must provide solid evidence for any point you make.
college-writing-000458.zh: 如果你想与读者有效沟通，就必须为所提出的观点提供有力的证据。

college-writing-000459.en: An important difference, then, between writing and talking is this: In writing, any idea that you advance must be supported with specific reasons or details.
college-writing-000459.zh: 那么，写作与说话之间的一个重要区别在于：在写作中，所提出的任何观点都必须有具体的理由或细节作为支撑。

college-writing-000460.en: Think of your readers as reasonable people.
college-writing-000460.zh: 把你的读者视为理性的人。

college-writing-000461.en: They will not simply accept your views, but they are willing to accept what you say as long as you support it.
college-writing-000461.zh: 他们不会轻易接受你的观点，但只要你支持他们的观点，他们就愿意接受。

college-writing-000462.en: Therefore, remember to support with specific evidence any point that you make.
college-writing-000462.zh: 因此，请记住，对于所提出的任何观点，都要用具体证据来支撑。

college-writing-000463.en: Point and Support in a Paragraph In conversation, you might say to a friend who has suggested a movie, “No, thanks. Going to the movies is just too much of a hassle. Parking, people, everything.”
college-writing-000463.zh: 用一段话表达观点与支持。在交谈中，当朋友推荐一部电影时，你可以对他说：“不用了，谢谢。去电影院实在太麻烦了——停车、人群、诸如此类的问题。”

college-writing-000464.en: From shared past experiences, your friend may know what you are talking about so that you will not have to explain your statement.
college-writing-000464.zh: 从共同的过往经历来看，你的朋友可能知道你在谈论什么，这样你就无需再解释自己的话了。

college-writing-000465.en: But in writing, your point would have to be backed up, or supported, with specific reasons and details.
college-writing-000465.zh: 但书面表达时，你的观点必须辅以具体的理由和细节来加以支持。

college-writing-000466.en: Below is a paragraph, written by a student named Finley Woods, on why moviegoing is a nuisance.
college-writing-000466.zh: 以下是一段由名为芬利·伍兹的学生撰写的文章，内容阐述了观看电影为何是一种麻烦。

college-writing-000467.en: A paragraph is a short paper of around 150 to 200 words.
college-writing-000467.zh: 段落是一篇约150到200词的短文。

college-writing-000468.en: It usually consists of an opening point, called a topic sentence, followed by a series of sentences that support that point.
college-writing-000468.zh: 它通常由一个被称为主题句的起始点，以及支持该观点的若干句子组成。

college-writing-000470.en: Although I love movies, I’ve found that there are drawbacks to moviegoing.
college-writing-000470.zh: 虽然我喜欢看电影，但我也发现看电影也有其弊端。

college-writing-000471.en: One problem is just the inconvenience of it all.
college-writing-000471.zh: 其中一个问题仅仅是这一切带来的不便。

college-writing-000472.en: To get to the theater, I have to drive for at least fifteen minutes, or more if traffic is bad.
college-writing-000472.zh: 要到达剧院，我必须开车至少十五分钟，如果交通拥堵的话，时间可能会更长。

college-writing-000473.en: It can take forever to find a parking spot, and then I have to walk across a huge parking lot to the theater.
college-writing-000473.zh: 找停车位可能要花很长时间，然后我还得穿过巨大的停车场去剧院。

college-writing-000474.en: There I encounter long lines, sold-out shows, and ever-increasing prices.
college-writing-000474.zh: 在那里，我看到了排长队的情况、售罄的演出，以及不断上涨的价格。

college-writing-000475.en: And I hate sitting with my feet sticking to the floor because of other people’s spilled snacks.
college-writing-000475.zh: 我讨厌因为别人洒出的零食而让脚粘在地板上。

college-writing-000476.en: Another problem is my lack of self-control at the theater.
college-writing-000476.zh: 另一个问题是我在剧院中缺乏自我控制力。

college-writing-000477.en: I often stuff myself with unhealthy calorie-laden snacks.
college-writing-000477.zh: 我经常吃那些热量过高、不健康的零食。

college-writing-000478.en: My choices might include a bucket of popcorn, a box of Milk Duds, a giant soda, or all three.
college-writing-000478.zh: 我的选择可能包括一桶爆米花、一盒牛奶饮料，或者一瓶大瓶汽水，或者以上三种都选。

college-writing-000479.en: The worst problem is some of the other moviegoers.
college-writing-000479.zh: 最糟糕的是其他一些观众。

college-writing-000480.en: Kids run up and down the aisle.
college-writing-000480.zh: 孩子们在过道上来回跑。

college-writing-000481.en: Teenagers laugh and shout at the screen.
college-writing-000481.zh: 青少年们在屏幕上笑着大喊。

college-writing-000482.en: People of all ages drop soda cups and popcorn tubs, cough and burp, and talk to one another.
college-writing-000482.zh: 各年龄段的人都会扔掉汽水杯和爆米花桶，咳嗽、打嗝，并互相交谈。

college-writing-000483.en: All in all, I would rather stay home and stream a movie in the comfort of my own living room.
college-writing-000483.zh: 总的来说，我更愿意待在家里，在舒适的客厅里观看电影。

college-writing-000485.en: Notice what the supporting evidence does here.
college-writing-000485.zh: 注意这里支撑论点的证据起到了什么作用。

college-writing-000486.en: It provides you, the reader, with a basis for understanding why the writer makes the point that is made.
college-writing-000486.zh: 它为读者提供了理解作者为何提出那个观点的基础。

college-writing-000487.en: Through this specific evidence, the writer has explained and successfully communicated the idea that moviegoing can be a nuisance.
college-writing-000487.zh: 通过这一具体证据，作者阐述并成功传达了“观看电影可能会带来困扰”这一观点。

college-writing-000488.en: The evidence that supports the point in a paper often consists of a series of reasons followed by examples and details that support the reasons.
college-writing-000488.zh: 支持某篇论文观点的证据通常包含一系列理由，以及支撑这些理由的实例和细节。

college-writing-000489.en: That is true of the paragraph above: three reasons are provided, with examples and details that back up those reasons.
college-writing-000489.zh: 上述段落确实如此：提出了三个原因，并提供了支持这些原因的例子和细节。

college-writing-000490.en: Supporting evidence in a paper can also consist of anecdotes, personal experiences, facts, studies, statistics, and the opinions of experts.
college-writing-000490.zh: 文章中支撑论点的证据还可以包括轶事、个人经历、事实、研究、统计数据和专家意见。

college-writing-000491.en: The paragraph on moviegoing, like almost any piece of effective writing, has two essential parts: (1) a point is advanced, and (2) that point is then supported.
college-writing-000491.zh: 关于观看电影的段落，就像几乎所有有效的写作内容一样，有两个基本组成部分：(1) 提出一个观点；(2) 对该观点进行论证。

college-writing-000492.en: Taking a minute to outline “The Hazards of Moviegoing” will help you understand these basic parts.
college-writing-000492.zh: 花一分钟来概述“观看电影的隐患”，有助于你理解这些基本问题。

college-writing-000493.en: Write in the following space the point that has been advanced in the paragraph.
college-writing-000493.zh: 在下方空白处写下该段落中提出的观点。

college-writing-000494.en: Then add the words needed to complete the paragraph’s outline.
college-writing-000494.zh: 然后添加完成段落提纲所需的词语。

college-writing-000496.zh: 开车15分钟即可到达剧院

college-writing-000499.en: Long lines, sold-out shows, and increasing prices
college-writing-000499.zh: 长队排队、演出门票售罄，且价格不断上涨

college-writing-000503.en: Often stuff myself with unhealthy snacks
college-writing-000503.zh: 经常吃大量不健康的零食。

college-writing-000505.en: Might have popcorn, candy, soda, or all three
college-writing-000505.zh: 可能有爆米花、糖果、汽水，或者这三种都有

college-writing-000509.en: People of all ages make noise.
college-writing-000509.zh: 各个年龄段的人都会发出声音。

college-writing-000510.en: Point and Support in an Essay An excellent way to learn how to write clearly and logically is to practice composing the traditional college essay─a paper of about five hundred words that typically consists of an introductory paragraph, three or more supporting paragraphs, and a concluding paragraph.
college-writing-000510.zh: 文章中的要点与支持内容：学习如何清晰、逻辑地写作的绝佳方法就是练习撰写传统的大学论文——这种大约五百词的论文通常包含一段引言段落、三个或更多的支持性段落，以及一段结论段落。

college-writing-000511.en: The central idea, or point, developed in any essay is called a thesis statement (rather than, as in a paragraph, a topic sentence).
college-writing-000511.zh: 文章所展开的中心观点称为中心论点句；在一个段落中，起同样作用的句子则叫主题句。

college-writing-000512.en: The thesis appears in the introductory paragraph, and the specific support for the thesis appears in the paragraphs that follow.
college-writing-000512.zh: 该论点出现在引言段落中，而对该论点的具体支持则出现在后续的段落中。

college-writing-000513.zh: 那些辅助段落为……提供了可能

college-writing-000517.en: a fuller treatment of the evidence that backs up the central point than would be possible in a single-paragraph paper.
college-writing-000517.zh: 对支持核心观点的证据进行更全面的阐述，这比单段论文所能呈现的更为充分。

college-writing-000518.en: Unlike paragraphs that are usually developed using one mode of writing, like description, essays are usually developed using several modes of writing to support the single point.
college-writing-000518.zh: 与通常采用单一写作方式来撰写的段落不同，文章通常会采用多种写作方式来支撑其核心观点。

college-writing-000519.en: Structure of the Traditional Essay A Model Essay The following model will help you understand the form of an essay.
college-writing-000519.zh: 传统文章的结构 模型文章 以下模型将帮助您理解文章的格式。

college-writing-000520.en: Finley Woods, the writer of the paragraph on moviegoing, later decided to develop her subject more fully.
college-writing-000520.zh: 撰写了关于看电影的段落的芬利·伍兹，后来决定更全面地展开她的主题。

college-writing-000521.en: Here is the essay that resulted.
college-writing-000521.zh: 以下是最终形成的文章。

college-writing-000524.en: My friends count on me to know movie trivia (who was the pigtailed little girl in E.T.: The Extra-Terrestrial? Drew Barrymore) and to remember every big Oscar awarded since I was in grade school (Best Picture, 2020? Parasite).
college-writing-000524.zh: 我的朋友们依赖我来记住各种电影相关的小知识（比如《E.T. 外星人》里那个扎着马尾的小女孩是谁？是德鲁·巴里摩尔）；同时，我也记得自我小学时代以来所有获得奥斯卡奖的作品（2020年最佳影片？《寄生虫》）。

college-writing-000525.en: My friends, though, have stopped asking me if I want to go out to the movies.
college-writing-000525.zh: 不过，我的朋友们不再问我是否想出去看电影了。

college-writing-000526.en: While I love movies as much as ever, the inconvenience of going out, the temptations of the concession stand, and the behavior of some patrons are reasons for me to wait and stream the film.
college-writing-000526.zh: 虽然我依然非常喜欢电影，但出门的不便、 concession店里的诱惑，以及一些观众的行为，都让我选择等待并在线观看电影。

college-writing-000527.en: To begin with, I just don’t enjoy the general hassle of the evening.
college-writing-000527.zh: 首先，我实在不喜欢夜晚那些繁琐的麻烦事。

college-writing-000528.en: Since small local movie theaters are a thing of the past, I have to drive for fifteen minutes to get to the nearest multiplex.
college-writing-000528.zh: 由于小型本地电影院已不复存在，我必须开车十五分钟才能到达最近的多厅影院。

college-writing-000529.en: The parking lot is shared with several restaurants and a supermarket, so it’s always jammed.
college-writing-000529.zh: 这个停车场被几家餐厅和一家超市共享使用，所以总是人满为患。

college-writing-000530.en: I have to drive around at a snail’s pace until I spot another driver backing out.
college-writing-000530.zh: 我得以极慢的速度开车，直到遇到另一个倒车出来的司机。

college-writing-000531.en: Then it’s time to stand in an endless line, waiting to have our tickets scanned, so we can enter.
college-writing-000531.zh: 然后就是站成一排等待的行列，等待我们的门票被扫描，以便能够进入。

college-writing-000532.en: Once we do get in, we often find our reserved seats are occupied.
college-writing-000532.zh: 一旦进入，往往会发现我们预订的座位已被占满。

college-writing-000533.en: We then have to find an employee to help us access our seats.
college-writing-000533.zh: 然后，我们必须找到一名员工来帮助我们获取座位。

college-writing-000534.en: I have to shell out a ridiculous amount of money—up to $11—for a ticket.
college-writing-000534.zh: 我得花一大笔钱——高达11美元——才能买到一张票。

college-writing-000535.en: That entitles me to sit while my shoes seal themselves to a sticky floor coated with spilled soda, bubble gum, and crushed Raisinets.
college-writing-000535.zh: 这让我有权利坐下来，我的鞋子会沾上被洒出的汽水、泡泡糖以及压碎的葡萄干所弄脏的黏糊糊的地板。

college-writing-000536.en: Second, the theater offers tempting snacks that I really don’t need.
college-writing-000536.zh: 其次，剧院提供一些我其实不需要的诱人小吃。

college-writing-000537.en: Like most of us, I have to battle an expanding waistline.
college-writing-000537.zh: 和大多数人一样，我也不得不应对不断增加的腰围问题。

college-writing-000538.en: At home I do pretty well by simply not buying stuff that is bad for me. I can make do with snacks like celery and carrot sticks because there is no ice cream in the freezer.
college-writing-000538.zh: 在家时，只要不购买对身体有害的东西，我就能过得不错。我可以用芹菜、胡萝卜条之类的零食来充饥，因为冰箱里没有冰淇淋。

college-writing-000539.en: Going to the theater, however, is like spending my evening in a 7-Eleven that’s been equipped with a movie screen and
college-writing-000539.zh: 不过，去剧院看电影就像是在一个配备了电影屏幕的7-Eleven里度过夜晚。

college-writing-000545.en: Parts of an Essay “The Hazards of Moviegoing” is a good example of the standard short essay you will write in college English.
college-writing-000545.zh: 《看电影的隐患》这篇文章，就是你在大学英语课程中需要撰写的标准短文的好例子。

college-writing-000546.en: It is a composition of over five hundred words that consists of a one-paragraph introduction, a three-paragraph body, and a one-paragraph conclusion.
college-writing-000546.zh: 这是一篇超过五百字的文章，包含一段引言、三段正文和一段结论。

college-writing-000547.en: The roles of these paragraphs are described and illustrated below.
college-writing-000547.zh: 下面对这些段落的作用进行了描述和说明。

college-writing-000549.en: The introductory paragraph of an essay should start with several sentences that attract the reader’s interest.
college-writing-000549.zh: 文章的引言段落应以几句话开始，以吸引读者的兴趣。

college-writing-000550.en: It should then advance the central idea, or thesis, that will be developed in the essay.
college-writing-000550.zh: 然后应阐述文章中将要发展的核心观点或论点。

college-writing-000551.en: The thesis often includes a plan of development─a “preview” of the major points that will support the thesis.
college-writing-000551.zh: 中心论点句通常带有展开提纲，也就是先预告用来支撑中心论点的几个要点。

college-writing-000552.en: These supporting points should be listed in the order in which they will appear in the essay.
college-writing-000552.zh: 这些支持观点应按其在文章中的出现顺序列出。

college-writing-000553.en: Such a thesis might assert, “Winter is my favorite season because I like the weather, the holidays, and the sports,” leading to an essay that has a paragraph about weather, followed by a paragraph about winter holidays, and so on.
college-writing-000553.zh: 这样的论点可能会这样表述：“冬天是我最喜欢的季节，因为我喜欢那里的天气、节日以及各种运动活动。”由此会形成一篇文章，其中有一段内容涉及天气，接着又有一段内容涉及冬季节日，如此循环。

college-writing-000554.en: In some cases, however, the plan of
college-writing-000554.zh: 然而在某些情况下，计划却是……

college-writing-000556.en: As I try to persuade myself to just have a sparkling water, the smell of fresh popcorn dripping with butter soon overcomes me.
college-writing-000556.zh: 当我试图说服自己只喝一杯气泡水时，那股带着黄油味的新鲜爆米花气味很快便让我难以抗拒。

college-writing-000557.en: Chocolate bars the size of small automobiles seem to jump into my hands.
college-writing-000557.zh: 像小型汽车那么大的巧克力棒似乎会突然掉进我的手中。

college-writing-000558.en: I risk pulling out my fillings as I chew enormous mouthfuls of Milk Duds.
college-writing-000558.zh: 吃下一大口牛奶团时，我可能会把牙齿给咬掉。

college-writing-000559.en: By the time I leave the theater, I feel bloated and full.
college-writing-000559.zh: 当我离开剧院时，我感到腹胀且饱腹。

college-writing-000560.en: Many of the other patrons are even more of a problem than the concession stand.
college-writing-000560.zh: 其他许多顾客比小吃摊更成问题。

college-writing-000561.en: Little kids race up and down the aisles, usually in giggling packs.
college-writing-000561.zh: 小孩子们在过道上来回奔跑，通常都是成群结队地笑着。

college-writing-000562.en: Teenagers try to impress their friends by talking back to the screen, whistling, and making what they consider to be hilarious noises.
college-writing-000562.zh: 青少年试图通过对着屏幕回嘴、吹口哨以及发出他们认为有趣的噪音来给朋友留下深刻印象。

college-writing-000563.en: Adults act as if they were at home in their own living room.
college-writing-000563.zh: 成年人表现得就像在自己家里一样。

college-writing-000564.en: They comment loudly on the ages of the stars and reveal plot twists that are supposed to be a secret until the film’s end.
college-writing-000564.zh: 他们大声评论恒星的年龄，并揭示出那些本应作为秘密直到影片结尾才揭晓的剧情转折。

college-writing-000565.en: Additionally, people of all ages create disgusting messes and rude distractions.
college-writing-000565.zh: 此外，各个年龄段的人都会制造令人厌恶的混乱和无礼的干扰。

college-writing-000566.en: They leave tacky remnants of candy on the hand rests, stick gum on their seats, and drop popcorn tubs or cups of crushed ice and soda on the floor.
college-writing-000566.zh: 他们会在手肘处留下粘糊糊的糖果残骸，在座位上粘上口香糖，还会把爆米花容器或装有碎冰与汽水的杯子扔在地上。

college-writing-000567.en: They also cough and burp, squirm endlessly in their seats, file out for repeated trips to the restrooms or concession stands, and elbow me out of the armrest on either side of my seat.
college-writing-000567.zh: 他们还会咳嗽、打嗝，在座位上不停地扭动身体，频繁前往洗手间或小吃摊，还把我的座位两侧的扶手让给我。

college-writing-000568.en: After arriving home from the movies one night, I decided that I was not going to be a moviegoer anymore.
college-writing-000568.zh: 某天晚上从电影院回家后，我决定再也不当电影观众了。

college-writing-000569.en: I was tired of the problems involved in getting to the theater, resisting unhealthy snacks, and dealing with the patrons.
college-writing-000569.zh: 我厌倦了去剧院时遇到的各种问题、抵制不健康的零食以及与顾客相处时的麻烦。

college-writing-000570.en: The next day, I subscribed to Disney+, Netflix, and Hulu.
college-writing-000570.zh: 第二天，我订阅了迪士尼+、Netflix和Hulu。

college-writing-000571.en: I may now see movies a bit later than other people, but I’ll be more relaxed watching box office hits in the comfort of my own living room.
college-writing-000571.zh: 现在我可能比其他人晚一些看电影，但在自己的客厅里观看那些热门电影时，我会更放松。

college-writing-000576.en: For example, a thesis that claims, “Education can be a key to socioeconomic security” doesn’t state how the essay will be developed but still advances a central idea.
college-writing-000576.zh: 例如，一个声称“教育可以成为社会经济安全的关键”的论点，虽然没有说明文章将如何展开，但依然提出了一个核心观点。

college-writing-000577.en: 1. In “The Hazards of Moviegoing,” which sentence or sentences are used to attract the reader’s interest?
college-writing-000577.zh: 在《看电影的隐患》一文中，哪一句或几句话能够吸引读者的兴趣呢？

college-writing-000581.en: 2. In which sentence is the thesis of the essay presented?
college-writing-000581.zh: 2. 哪一句中提出了文章的论点？

college-writing-000584.en: 3. Does the thesis include a plan of development?
college-writing-000584.zh: 3. 中心论点句是否包含展开提纲？

college-writing-000587.en: 4. Write the words in the thesis that announce the three major supporting points in the essay:
college-writing-000587.zh: 4. 在论文中写出那些用于说明文章三个主要支撑观点的词语：

college-writing-000592.en: Many essays have three supporting points, developed at length over three separate paragraphs.
college-writing-000592.zh: 许多文章包含三个支撑点，这些支撑点在三个独立的段落中详细阐述。

college-writing-000593.en: However, more developed essays require four or more body paragraphs to support the thesis.
college-writing-000593.zh: 然而，更成熟的文章需要四个或更多主体段落来支撑论点。

college-writing-000594.en: This is very common in essays with thesis statements that omit a plan of development.
college-writing-000594.zh: 在中心论点句省略展开提纲的文章中，这种情况很常见。

college-writing-000595.en: Each of the supporting paragraphs should begin with a topic sentence that states the point to be detailed in that paragraph.
college-writing-000595.zh: 每个支持段落都应以主题句开头，该主题句会说明该段落中要详细阐述的内容。

college-writing-000596.en: Just as a thesis provides a focus for the entire essay, the topic sentence provides a focus for a supporting paragraph.
college-writing-000596.zh: 正如论点为整篇文章提供了主题，主题句则为支持性段落提供了主题。

college-writing-000597.en: 1. What is the topic sentence for the first supporting paragraph of the model essay?
college-writing-000597.zh: 1. 模型文章的第一个支持段落的主题句是什么？

college-writing-000598.en: 2. The first topic sentence is then supported by the following details (fill in the missing details):
college-writing-000598.zh: 2. 第一个主题句随后由以下细节加以支持（请填写缺失的内容）：

college-writing-000599.en: a. Have to drive fifteen minutes
college-writing-000599.zh: a. 必须驾驶十五分钟

college-writing-000605.zh: 漫长的售票窗口排队队伍

college-writing-000610.en: 3. What is the topic sentence for the second supporting paragraph of the essay?
college-writing-000610.zh: 3. 这篇文章第二个支持段落的主题句是什么？

college-writing-000611.en: 4. The second topic sentence is then supported by the following details:
college-writing-000611.zh: 4. 第二个主题句随后由以下细节加以支持：

college-writing-000612.en: a. At home, only snacks are celery and carrot sticks.
college-writing-000612.zh: a. 在家里，只有芹菜和胡萝卜条作为零食。

college-writing-000613.en: b. Theater is like a 7-Eleven with seats.
college-writing-000613.zh: b. 剧院就像一个有座位的7-Eleven商店。

college-writing-000615.en: 5. What is the topic sentence for the third supporting paragraph of the essay?
college-writing-000615.zh: 5. 这篇文章第三个支持段落的主题句是什么？

college-writing-000616.en: 6. The third topic sentence is then supported by the following details:
college-writing-000616.zh: 6. 第三个主题句随后由以下细节加以支持：

college-writing-000619.en: c. Adults talk loudly and reveal plot twists.
college-writing-000619.zh: c. 成年人说话声音很大，还会透露剧情中的转折。

college-writing-000620.en: d. People of all ages create disgusting messes and rude distractions.
college-writing-000620.zh: d. 各个年龄段的人都会制造令人厌恶的混乱和无礼的干扰。

college-writing-000622.en: The concluding paragraph often summarizes the essay by briefly restating the thesis and, at times, the main supporting points.
college-writing-000622.zh: 结尾段落通常会通过简要重申论点，有时还会重申主要支撑点，来总结整篇文章。

college-writing-000623.en: In addition, the writer often presents a concluding thought about the subject of the paper.
college-writing-000623.zh: 此外，作者通常会对论文主题提出一个总结性观点。

college-writing-000624.en: 1. Which two sentences in the concluding paragraph restate the thesis and supporting points of the essay?
college-writing-000624.zh: 结论段中的哪两句话又重申了文章的论点及支持观点？

college-writing-000630.en: 2. Which sentence in the concluding paragraph contains the final thought of the essay?
college-writing-000630.zh: 2. 结尾段落中的哪一句包含了文章的最终观点？

college-writing-000634.en: Diagram of an Essay The following diagram shows you at a glance the different parts of a standard college essay, also known as a one-three-one essay.
college-writing-000634.zh: 文章结构图 下面的图可以让你一目了然地了解标准大学文章的各个组成部分，也被称为“一三一”结构文章。

college-writing-000635.en: This diagram will serve as a helpful guide when you are writing or evaluating essays.
college-writing-000635.zh: 这个图表将在你写作或评估文章时起到有益的指导作用。

college-writing-000638.zh: 总结（可选）总体结束发言（或两者都有）

college-writing-000640.en: Opening remarks to catch reader’s interest Thesis statement Plan of development (optional)
college-writing-000640.zh: 开场语：引起读者兴趣；中心论点句；展开提纲（可选）。

college-writing-000642.zh: 主题句1（支持观点1）具体证据

college-writing-000643.zh: 主题句2（支持观点2）具体证据

college-writing-000644.zh: 主题句3（支持观点3）具体证据

college-writing-000646.en: You now have an overview of the traditional form of the essay.
college-writing-000646.zh: 现在你已经了解了文章的传统形式。

college-writing-000647.en: In Chapter 2, you will learn how to go about writing an effective essay.
college-writing-000647.zh: 在第二章中，你将学习如何撰写有效的文章。

college-writing-000648.en: First, though, it will be helpful to consider the following: the benefits of writing traditional essays, the advantage of seeing writing as both a skill and a process of discovery, the value of keeping a journal, and the ways a computer can enhance the writing process.
college-writing-000648.zh: 不过，首先考虑以下方面会很有帮助：撰写传统文章的好处，将写作视为一种技能与发现过程的优势，记日记的价值，以及计算机如何提升写作过程。

college-writing-000649.en: Benefits of Writing the Traditional Essay

college-writing-000650.en: Learning to write a traditional essay offers at least three benefits.
college-writing-000650.zh: 学习撰写传统文章至少带来三个好处。

college-writing-000651.en: First of all, mastering the traditional essay will help make you a better writer.
college-writing-000651.zh: 首先，掌握传统写作技巧能帮助你成为更优秀的作家。

college-writing-000652.en: For other courses, you’ll often compose papers that will be variations on the essay form─for example, examination essays, reports, and research papers.
college-writing-000652.zh: 对于其他课程，你通常会撰写以文章形式呈现的论文——例如考试论文、报告和研究论文。

college-writing-000653.en: Becoming comfortable with the basic structure of the traditional essay, with its emphasis on a clear point and well-organized, logical support, will help with almost every kind of writing that you have to do.
college-writing-000653.zh: 熟悉传统文章的基本结构，即强调清晰的观点和条理清晰、逻辑严密的论证方式，将有助于你完成几乎所有类型的写作任务。

college-writing-000654.en: Second, the discipline of writing an essay will strengthen your skills as a reader and listener.
college-writing-000654.zh: 其次，撰写文章的技巧将提升你作为读者和听众的能力。

college-writing-000655.en: As a reader, you’ll become more critically aware of other writers’ ideas and the evidence they provide (or fail to provide) to support those ideas.
college-writing-000655.zh: 作为读者，你将能够更批判性地审视其他作家的观点，以及他们为支持这些观点所提供或未能提供的证据。

college-writing-000656.en: Essay writing will also help you become a better speaker.
college-writing-000656.zh: 论文写作也能帮助你成为更出色的演讲者。

college-writing-000657.en: You’ll be more prepared to develop the three basic parts of an effective speech─an appealing introduction, a solidly developed body, and a well-rounded conclusion─because of your experience writing three-part essays.
college-writing-000657.zh: 由于你有撰写三段式文章的经历，你将更能准备好撰写有效的演讲的三个基本部分——吸引人的开头、扎实的主体内容以及完整的结尾。

college-writing-000658.en: Most important, essay writing will make you a stronger thinker.
college-writing-000658.zh: 最重要的是，写作训练会让你成为更优秀的思考者。

college-writing-000659.en: Writing a solidly reasoned traditional essay requires mental discipline and close attention to a set of logical rules.
college-writing-000659.zh: 撰写逻辑严谨的传统论文需要心智上的自律，以及对一系列逻辑规则的严格遵循。

college-writing-000660.en: Creating an essay in which there is an overall thesis statement and in which each of three supporting paragraphs begins with a topic sentence is more challenging than writing a free-form or expressive paper.
college-writing-000660.zh: 撰写一篇包含总体中心论点句，且三个支持段落都以主题句开头的文章，比撰写自由式或富有表现力的文章更具挑战性。

college-writing-000661.en: Such an essay obliges you to carefully sort out, think through, and organize your ideas.
college-writing-000661.zh: 这样的文章要求你仔细梳理、思考并组织你的想法。

college-writing-000662.en: You’ll learn to discover and express just what your ideas are and to develop those ideas in a logical, reasoned way.
college-writing-000662.zh: 你将学会发现并表达自己的想法，并以逻辑、理性的方式发展这些想法。

college-writing-000663.en: Traditional essay writing, in short, will train your mind to think clearly, and that ability will prove to be of value in every phase of your life.
college-writing-000663.zh: 简而言之，传统的文章写作能够训练你的思维清晰思考，而这种能力将在你人生的各个阶段发挥重要作用。

college-writing-000665.en: A realistic attitude about writing must build on the idea that writing is a skill, not a “natural gift.”
college-writing-000665.zh: 对写作的务实态度应当基于这样的观念：写作是一种技能，而非“天赐良材”。

college-writing-000666.en: It is a skill like driving, typing, or cooking; like any skill, it can be learned.
college-writing-000666.zh: 这是一种类似于驾驶、打字或烹饪的技能；和任何技能一样，它可以被学习。

college-writing-000667.en: If you have the determination to learn, this book will give you the extensive practice needed to develop your writing skills.
college-writing-000667.zh: 如果你有学习的决心，这本书将为你提供所需的丰富练习，以提升你的写作能力。

college-writing-000668.en: People often fear they are the only ones for whom writing is unbearably difficult.
college-writing-000668.zh: 人们常常担心自己是唯一一个觉得写作极其困难的人。

college-writing-000669.en: They believe that everyone else finds writing easy or at least tolerable.
college-writing-000669.zh: 他们认为其他人都能轻松或至少能够忍受写作。

college-writing-000672.en: people typically say, “I’m not any good at writing,” or “English was not one of my good subjects.”
college-writing-000672.zh: 人们通常会说：“我不擅长写作，”或者“英语不是我的强项科目。”

college-writing-000673.en: They imply that they simply do not have a talent for writing, while others do.
college-writing-000673.zh: 他们暗示自己根本不擅长写作，而其他人却很擅长。

college-writing-000674.en: Often, the result of this attitude is that people try to avoid writing, and when they do write, they don’t try their best.
college-writing-000674.zh: 通常，这种态度会导致人们避免写作，而当他们写作时，也不会全力以赴。

college-writing-000675.en: Their attitude then becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy: their writing fails chiefly because they have brainwashed themselves into thinking that they don’t have the “natural talent” needed to write.
college-writing-000675.zh: 他们的态度便成为一种自我实现的预言：他们的写作失败，主要是因为他们自我催眠认为自己没有写作所需的“天赋”。

college-writing-000676.en: Many people find it difficult to do the intense, active thinking that clear writing demands.
college-writing-000676.zh: 许多人觉得难以进行清晰写作所要求的那种深入、主动的思考。

college-writing-000677.en: It is frightening to sit down before a blank sheet of paper or computer screen and know that an hour later, nothing on it may be worth keeping.
college-writing-000677.zh: 坐在一张空白的纸张或电脑屏幕前，却知道一小时后上面的内容可能就不再值得保留，这令人恐惧。

college-writing-000678.en: It is frustrating to discover how much of a challenge it is to transfer thoughts and feelings from one’s head onto the page.
college-writing-000678.zh: 发现将想法和感受从头脑转移到纸上的过程有多么困难，真是令人沮丧。

college-writing-000679.en: It is upsetting to find that an apparently simple subject often turns out to be complicated.
college-writing-000679.zh: 令人沮丧的是，一个看似简单的主题往往最终变得复杂。

college-writing-000680.en: But writing is not an automatic process: we will not get something for nothing─and we should not expect to.
college-writing-000680.zh: 但写作并非自动完成的过程：我们不会不劳而获——也不应期望如此。

college-writing-000681.en: For almost everyone, competent writing comes from plain hard work─from determination, sweat, and struggle.
college-writing-000681.zh: 对几乎所有人来说，优秀的写作都源于辛勤的付出——源于决心、汗水与努力。

college-writing-000682.en: The good news is that the skill of writing can be mastered, and if you are ready to work, you will learn what you need to know.
college-writing-000682.zh: 好消息是，写作技巧是可以掌握的，如果你愿意努力，就会学会所需的知识。

college-writing-000683.en: Writing as a Process of Discovery
college-writing-000683.zh: 将写作视为一种发现过程

college-writing-000684.en: In addition to believing that writing is a natural gift, many people falsely believe that writing should flow in a simple, straight line from the writer’s head onto the written page.
college-writing-000684.zh: 除了认为写作是一种天赋之外，许多人还错误地认为，写作应该以简单、笔直的线条从作者头脑中流淌到书写页面上。

college-writing-000685.en: But writing is seldom an easy, one-step journey in which a finished paper comes out in a first draft.
college-writing-000685.zh: 但写作很少是一蹴而成的简单过程，最终能直接得到一份初稿。

college-writing-000686.en: The truth is that writing is a process of discovery involving a series of steps, and those steps are very often a zigzag journey.
college-writing-000686.zh: 事实上，写作是一个发现的过程，包含一系列步骤，而这些步骤往往呈曲折的走向。

college-writing-000687.en: Look at the following illustrations of the writing process:
college-writing-000687.zh: 看看以下关于写作过程的示意图：

college-writing-000688.zh: 这已经不是那个案子了

college-writing-000692.en: Very often, writers do not discover just what they want to write about until they explore their thoughts in writing.
college-writing-000692.zh: 通常，作家在将他们的想法以文字形式表达出来之前，并不会知道自己想要写什么。

college-writing-000693.en: For example, Finley Woods (the author of the paragraph and essay on moviegoing) had been assigned to write about an annoyance in everyday life.
college-writing-000693.zh: 例如，Finley Woods（撰写了关于看电影的段落和文章的人）被要求撰写关于日常生活中令人烦恼的事情。

college-writing-000694.en: She did not know what annoyance she would choose; instead, she just began writing about annoyances in general, in order to discover a topic.
college-writing-000694.zh: 她不知道该选择哪种烦恼来写，于是便开始泛泛地谈论各种烦恼，希望能找到一个主题。

college-writing-000695.en: One of those annoyances was traffic, which seemed promising, so she began putting down ideas and details that came to her about traffic.
college-writing-000695.zh: 那些令人烦恼的事情中就有交通问题，不过情况似乎有希望，于是她开始记录下关于交通的种种想法和细节。

college-writing-000696.en: One detail was the traffic she had to deal with in going to the movies.
college-writing-000696.zh: 其中一个细节就是去电影院时不得不处理的交通问题。

college-writing-000697.zh: 这让她有了这样的想法

college-writing-000699.en: of the traffic in the parking lot at the theater complex.
college-writing-000699.zh: 剧院综合体停车场内的交通情况。

college-writing-000700.en: At that point, she realized that moviegoing itself was an annoyance.
college-writing-000700.zh: 那时，她意识到看电影本身是一种麻烦。

college-writing-000701.en: She switched the focus and began writing down ideas and details about moviegoing.
college-writing-000701.zh: 她转移了注意力，开始记录关于看电影的种种想法和细节。

college-writing-000702.en: As Finley wrote, she realized how much other moviegoers annoyed her, and she began thinking that other movie patrons might be her main idea in a paper.
college-writing-000702.zh: 正如芬利所写的那样，她意识到其他观众给她带来了多大的困扰，于是开始认为其他电影观众可能是她论文中的主要主题。

college-writing-000703.en: But when she was writing about patrons who loudly drop popcorn tubs onto the floor, she realized how much all the snacks at the concession stand tempted her.
college-writing-000703.zh: 但当她描写那些大声把爆米花罐子扔到地上的顾客时，她意识到小吃摊上的所有零食对她的诱惑有多大。

college-writing-000704.en: She changed direction again, thinking now that maybe she could talk about patrons and tempting snacks.
college-writing-000704.zh: 她又改变了方向，心想或许可以聊聊顾客以及诱人的小吃。

college-writing-000705.en: She kept writing, just putting down more and more details about her movie experiences, still not having figured out exactly how she would fit both patrons and snacks into the paper.
college-writing-000705.zh: 她继续写作，不断写下关于她的电影体验的更多细节，但始终没有弄清楚如何同时兼顾观众和零食的安排。

college-writing-000706.en: Even though her paper had not quite jelled, she was not worried, because she knew that if she kept writing, it would eventually come together.
college-writing-000706.zh: 虽然她的论文还没有完全成型，但她并不担心，因为她知道只要继续写作，最终就会整理好。

college-writing-000707.en: The point is that writing is often a process of continuing discovery; as you write, you may suddenly switch direction or double back.
college-writing-000707.zh: 关键在于，写作往往是一个持续探索的过程；在写作过程中，你可能会突然改变方向或倒回过去。

college-writing-000708.en: You may be working on a topic sentence and realize suddenly that it could be your concluding thought.
college-writing-000708.zh: 你可能正在撰写主题句，突然意识到那可能就是你的结论性观点。

college-writing-000709.en: Or you may be developing a supporting idea and then decide that it should be the main point of your paper.
college-writing-000709.zh: 或者，你可能在构思一个辅助观点，然后决定它应成为你论文的核心内容。

college-writing-000710.en: Chapter 2 will treat the writing process more directly.
college-writing-000710.zh: 第二章将更直接地探讨写作过程。

college-writing-000711.en: What is important to remember here is that writers frequently do not know their exact destination as they begin to write.
college-writing-000711.zh: 这里需要记住的是，作家在开始写作时往往并不清楚自己的最终目标。

college-writing-000712.en: Very often they discover the direction and shape of a paper during the process of writing.
college-writing-000712.zh: 在写作过程中，他们常常能发现纸张的方向和形状。

college-writing-000713.en: Writing as a Way to Communicate with Others
college-writing-000713.zh: 写作作为一种与他人沟通的方式

college-writing-000714.en: When you talk, chances are you do not treat everyone the same.
college-writing-000714.zh: 说话时，你很可能不会对每个人一视同仁。

college-writing-000715.en: For example, you are unlikely to speak to your boss in the same way that you chat with a young child.
college-writing-000715.zh: 例如，你不太可能像与小孩聊天那样与老板交谈。

college-writing-000716.en: Instead, you adjust what you say to suit the people who are listening to you─your audience.
college-writing-000716.zh: 相反，你应该根据倾听你的听众——你的受众——来调整自己的言辞。

college-writing-000717.en: Similarly, you probably change your speech each day to suit whatever purpose you have in mind when you are speaking.
college-writing-000717.zh: 同样，你可能每天都会调整自己的说话方式，以符合说话时的目的。

college-writing-000718.en: For instance, if you wanted to tell someone how to get to your new apartment, you would speak differently than if you were describing your favorite movie.
college-writing-000718.zh: 例如，如果你想告诉某人如何到达你的新公寓，你的说话方式会与描述你最喜欢的电影时不同。

college-writing-000719.en: To communicate effectively, people must constantly adjust their speech to suit their purpose and audience.
college-writing-000719.zh: 为了有效沟通，人们必须不断调整自己的言辞，以符合其目的和受众。

college-writing-000720.en: This same idea is true for writing.
college-writing-000720.zh: 这一理念在写作中同样适用。

college-writing-000721.en: When you write for others, it is crucial to know both your purpose for writing and the audience who will be reading your work.
college-writing-000721.zh: 当为他人写作时，明确写作的目的以及阅读你作品的受众至关重要。

college-writing-000722.en: The ability to adjust your writing to suit your purpose and audience will serve you well not only in the classroom but also in the workplace and beyond.
college-writing-000722.zh: 能够根据自己的目的和受众调整写作方式，不仅会在课堂上有帮助，在职场及其他领域也同样重要。

college-writing-000723.en: Chapter 7 will provide a more detailed explanation of purpose and audience and how to use this knowledge to better develop your writing.
college-writing-000723.zh: 第七章将详细阐述目的与受众，以及如何利用这些知识来更好地提升你的写作水平。

college-writing-000726.en: Because writing is a skill, it makes sense that the more you practice writing, the better you will write.
college-writing-000726.zh: 因为写作是一项技能，所以越多练习写作，你的写作水平就会越高，这是合乎逻辑的。

college-writing-000727.en: One excellent way to get practice in writing, even before you begin composing essays, is to keep a daily or almost daily journal.
college-writing-000727.zh: 在开始写作文章之前，一个很好的练习方式就是保持每日或几乎每日的日记。

college-writing-000728.en: Writing in a journal will help you develop the habit of thinking on paper and will show you how ideas can be discovered in the process of writing.
college-writing-000728.zh: 在日记中写作有助于培养在纸上思考的习惯，也能让你看到在写作过程中如何发现想法。

college-writing-000729.en: A journal can make writing a familiar part of your life and can serve as a continuing source of ideas for papers.
college-writing-000729.zh: 一个日记本可以让写作成为你生活中的一部分，并能作为撰写论文的持续灵感来源。

college-writing-000730.en: At some point during the day─perhaps during a study period after your last class of the day, or right before dinner, or right before going to bed─spend fifteen minutes or so writing in your journal.
college-writing-000730.zh: 在一天中的某个时刻——也许是在当天最后一节课后的学习时间、晚餐前，或是睡前——花大约15分钟时间写写你的日记。

college-writing-000731.en: Keep in mind that you do not have to plan what to write about, or be in the mood to write, or worry about making mistakes
college-writing-000731.zh: 请记住，你不必规划要写什么内容，也不必有写作的兴致，也不必担心会犯错。

college-writing-000732.en: as you write; just write down whatever words come out.
college-writing-000732.zh: 你随意书写即可；只要把想说的话都写下来就行了。

college-writing-000733.en: You should write at least one page in each session.
college-writing-000733.zh: 每次会议至少应写一页内容。

college-writing-000734.en: You may want to use a notebook that you can easily carry with you so that you can write any time ideas present themselves.
college-writing-000734.zh: 你可能需要使用一个便于携带的笔记本，这样就能随时记录下出现的想法。

college-writing-000735.en: Or you may decide to write on loose-leaf paper that can be transferred later to a journal folder on your desk.
college-writing-000735.zh: 或者，你可以选择用散页纸来书写，之后可以将这些纸张放入桌上的日记文件夹中。

college-writing-000736.en: Many students choose to keep their journals on their home computer or laptop.
college-writing-000736.zh: 许多学生选择使用家庭电脑或笔记本电脑来记录日记。

college-writing-000737.en: No matter how you proceed, be sure to date all entries.
college-writing-000737.zh: 无论采取何种方式，都务必对所有条目进行日期标注。

college-writing-000738.en: Your instructor may ask you to make journal entries a specific number of times a week, for a specific number of weeks.
college-writing-000738.zh: 您的导师可能会要求您每周进行特定次数的日记记录，持续特定周数。

college-writing-000739.en: They may have you turn in your journal every so BraunS/Getty Images
college-writing-000739.zh: 这可能会迫使你每次都查看你的日志——BraunS/Getty Images

college-writing-000744.en: If you are keeping the journal on your own, try to make entries three to five times a week every week of the semester.
college-writing-000744.zh: 如果你自己记录日志，建议在本学期的每週里，每周尝试做三到五次记录。

college-writing-000745.zh: 利用技术实现高效工作

college-writing-000746.en: • If you are using computers at your school to work on your essays, allow enough time.
college-writing-000746.zh: • 如果你在学校使用电脑撰写论文，请预留足够的时间。

college-writing-000747.en: You may have to wait for a computer or printer to be available.
college-writing-000747.zh: 你可能需要等待电脑或打印机可用。

college-writing-000748.en: In addition, you may need several sessions at a computer and printer to complete your paper.
college-writing-000748.zh: 此外，你可能需要使用电脑和打印机进行多次操作才能完成你的论文。

college-writing-000749.en: • There are numerous programs you can use to type and save your work.
college-writing-000749.zh: • 有许多程序可用于输入和保存你的工作。

college-writing-000750.en: Google Docs, Pages, Open Office, and Microsoft Office are all programs that offer helpful features for typing and saving students’ papers.
college-writing-000750.zh: Google Docs、Pages、Open Office和Microsoft Office都是提供有助于学生撰写和保存论文的便利功能的程序。

college-writing-000751.en: • Every program allows you to save your writing by clicking one or more icons.
college-writing-000751.zh: • 每个程序都允许你通过点击一个或多个图标来保存你的写作内容。

college-writing-000752.en: Save your work frequently as you write your draft.
college-writing-000752.zh: 在撰写草稿时，要经常保存你的工作成果。

college-writing-000753.en: A saved file is stored safely on the computer or network.
college-writing-000753.zh: 保存的文件被安全存储在计算机或网络上。

college-writing-000754.en: A file that is not saved will be lost if the computer crashes or if there is a loss of power.
college-writing-000754.zh: 如果计算机崩溃或断电，未保存的文件将会丢失。

college-writing-000755.en: • Always keep copies of your work in at least two places.
college-writing-000755.zh: • 务必在至少两个地方保存你的作品副本。

college-writing-000756.en: Some local options include your computer’s hard drive or a USB flash drive, while some remote options include cloud options like Google Drive or your school’s network storage.
college-writing-000756.zh: 一些本地选项包括计算机的硬盘或USB闪存盘，而一些远程选项则包括谷歌云端硬盘或学校的网络存储等云存储服务。

college-writing-000757.en: • If you have a hard time proofreading on screen, print out your paper, so you can proofread by hand.
college-writing-000757.zh: • 如果在屏幕上校对比较困难，可以打印出论文，这样就可以手动校对了。

college-writing-000758.en: This also gives you an additional hard copy backup in case something happens to your electronic backups.
college-writing-000758.zh: 这还能为你提供一份额外的纸质备份，以防电子备份出现任何问题。

college-writing-000759.en: • Work in single spacing so that you can see as much of your writing on the screen at one time as possible.
college-writing-000759.zh: • 使用单倍行距，这样你就能一次看到尽可能多的文字内容。

college-writing-000760.en: Just before you print out your work, change to double spacing.
college-writing-000760.zh: 在打印作品之前，将间距改为双倍。

college-writing-000761.en: • Before making major changes in a paper, create a copy of your file.
college-writing-000761.zh: • 在对文档进行重大修改之前，先复制一份文件。

college-writing-000762.en: For example, if your file is titled “Worst Job,” create a file called “Worst Job 2.”
college-writing-000762.zh: 例如，如果您的文件名为“最糟糕的工作”，请创建一个名为“最糟糕的工作2”的文件。

college-writing-000763.en: Then make all your changes in that new file.
college-writing-000763.zh: 然后在该新文件中进行所有修改。

college-writing-000764.en: If the changes don’t work out, you can always go back to the original file.
college-writing-000764.zh: 如果这些修改没有效果，你随时可以回到原始文件。

college-writing-000765.en: Using Technology to Communicate Effectively Much communication that takes place between instructors and students occurs electronically, through either e-mail or a discussion forum on a learning management system like Blackboard, Canvas, or Schoology.
college-writing-000765.zh: 利用技术有效沟通：教师与学生之间的许多沟通都通过电子邮件或如 Blackboard、Canvas 或 Schoology 这样的学习管理系统上的讨论论坛以电子形式进行。

college-writing-000766.en: While students are used to texting friends and corresponding through social media, they should remember that correspondence with a professor should be treated differently.
college-writing-000766.zh: 虽然学生习惯于给朋友发短信以及通过社交媒体交流，但他们应该记住，与教授的沟通应该采用不同的方式。

college-writing-000767.en: E-mails and other correspondence with an instructor should be seen as a more formal type of writing.
college-writing-000767.zh: 与指导老师的电子邮件及其他通信应被视为更为正式的文体。

college-writing-000769.zh: 一个合适的讨论论坛帖子

college-writing-000770.en: Students should keep the following points in mind when posting on a discussion forum.
college-writing-000770.zh: 学生在在讨论论坛发帖时，应记住以下要点。

college-writing-000771.en: (An example of a properly formatted forum post follows this list.)
college-writing-000771.zh: （格式正确的论坛帖子示例在列表下方。）

college-writing-000772.en: • Discussion forums should be treated like formal writing assignments.
college-writing-000772.zh: • 讨论论坛应被视为正式的写作任务。

college-writing-000773.en: • You should include a title line that explains what the post will be about.
college-writing-000773.zh: • 你应该包含一个标题行，说明该帖子的内容主题。

college-writing-000774.en: • You don’t need to explain who you are and what class you are in, as forums are set up in individual classes and are automatically attached to students’ accounts.
college-writing-000774.zh: • 你无需解释自己是谁以及属于哪个班级，因为论坛是按班级设立的，会自动绑定到学生的账户上。

college-writing-000778.en: Send now Send Later Draft Trash Attachment Signature
college-writing-000778.zh: 立即发送 稍后发送 草稿 垃圾文件 附件 签名

college-writing-000783.en: My name is Byan Ahrens, and I am a student in your English 95 class that meets on Monday/Wednesday/ Friday at 9:00 a.m.
college-writing-000783.zh: 我叫拜安·阿伦斯，我是你们英语95班的学生，课程在周一、周三和周五上午9:00进行。

college-writing-000784.en: I have a question about the narrative essay assignment.
college-writing-000784.zh: 关于叙事文作业，我有一个问题。

college-writing-000785.en: I wrote down that the assignment is due next Wednesday, but in class you stated it was due on Friday instead.
college-writing-000785.zh: 我记着这项作业下周三交，但在课堂上你却说下周五交。

college-writing-000786.en: I wanted to make sure that I understood you correctly, and that you are giving us an extension.
college-writing-000786.zh: 我想确保我理解得正确，而且你是在给我们延期。

college-writing-000788.zh: 一封恰当的正式电子邮件

college-writing-000789.en: Students should keep the following points in mind when corresponding via e-mail with an instructor.
college-writing-000789.zh: 学生与导师通过电子邮件交流时，应记住以下要点。

college-writing-000790.en: (An example of a properly formatted e-mail follows this list.)
college-writing-000790.zh: （格式正确的电子邮件示例列在下方。）

college-writing-000791.en: • E-mail should be treated like a formal writing assignment.
college-writing-000791.zh: • 电子邮件应被视为一项正式写作任务。

college-writing-000792.en: • You should include a subject line, a formal greeting, an explanation of who you are and what class you are enrolled in, a detailed message, and a formal closing.
college-writing-000792.zh: • 你应该包含主题行、正式的问候语、对自身的介绍以及你所报课程的说明、详细的内容说明，最后再加上正式的结束语。

college-writing-000793.en: • You should revise for clarity and edit for mistakes prior to sending your message.
college-writing-000793.zh: • 在发送消息之前，你应该先检查内容的清晰度，并修正其中的错误。

college-writing-000794.en: • You should not expect immediate responses from instructors.
college-writing-000794.zh: • 你不应期望教师能立即回复。

college-writing-000795.en: You may have to wait up to forty-eight hours before hearing back from an instructor.
college-writing-000795.zh: 你可能需要等待长达48小时才能收到教练的回复。

college-writing-000797.en: Either write a formal e-mail to your instructor or post the following information to your class discussion forum.
college-writing-000797.zh: 要么给您的导师写一封正式邮件，要么将以下信息发布到班级讨论论坛中。

college-writing-000798.zh: 您的正式邮件应包含以下内容：

college-writing-000804.en: Your discussion forum post should include:
college-writing-000804.zh: 您的讨论论坛帖子应包含以下内容：
