college-writing-000808.en: Using a Computer at Each Stage of the Writing Process Following are some ways to make computer use a part of your writing.
college-writing-000808.zh: 写作过程的每个阶段都使用计算机。以下是将计算机使用纳入写作中的几种方法。

college-writing-000809.en: Note that this section may be more meaningful after you have worked through Chapter 2 of this book.
college-writing-000809.zh: 请注意，在您完成了本书第二章的内容后，这一部分可能会更有意义。

college-writing-000812.zh: 论坛帖子 论坛发布

college-writing-000813.en: Byan Ahrens 1 Question about Narrative Essay
college-writing-000813.zh: 拜安·阿伦斯 1 关于叙事文的问题

college-writing-000815.en: I wrote down that the assignment is due next Wednesday, but in class you stated it was due on Friday instead.
college-writing-000815.zh: 我记着这项作业下周三交，但在课堂上你却说下周五交。

college-writing-000816.en: I wanted to make sure that I understood you correctly, and that you are giving us an extension.
college-writing-000816.zh: 我想确保我理解得正确，而且你是在给我们延期。

college-writing-000825.en: • Revise for clarity and edit for mistakes prior to sending your message.
college-writing-000825.zh: 在发送消息之前，请先检查内容的清晰度并修正错误。

college-writing-000826.en: • You should not expect immediate responses from instructors.
college-writing-000826.zh: • 你不应期望教师能立即回复。

college-writing-000827.en: You may have to wait up to forty-eight hours before hearing back from an instructor.
college-writing-000827.zh: 你可能需要等待长达48小时才能收到教练的回复。

college-writing-000830.en: If you’re a fast typist, many kinds of prewriting will work well on a computer.
college-writing-000830.zh: 如果你是个打字速度很快的人，许多预写作方式在电脑上都能很好地使用。

college-writing-000831.en: With freewriting in particular, you can get ideas onto the screen almost as quickly as they occur to you.
college-writing-000831.zh: 尤其是通过自由写作的方式，你可以几乎以想到那个点就立刻将其呈现在屏幕上。

college-writing-000832.en: (See Chapter 2 for an explanation of prewriting and freewriting.)
college-writing-000832.zh: （关于预写作和自由写作的说明，请参见第2章。）

college-writing-000833.en: A passing thought that could be productive is not likely to get lost.
college-writing-000833.zh: 那些可能具有启发性的想法不会被忽略。

college-writing-000834.en: You may even find it helpful, when freewriting, to dim the monitor screen so that you can’t see what you’re typing.
college-writing-000834.zh: 在自由写作时，你可能会发现把屏幕亮度调暗很有帮助，这样你就不会看到自己正在输入的内容了。

college-writing-000835.en: If you temporarily can’t see the screen, you won’t have to worry about grammar or spelling or typing errors (all of which do not matter in prewriting); instead, you can concentrate on getting down as many ideas and details as possible about your subject.
college-writing-000835.zh: 如果暂时无法看到屏幕内容，不必担心语法、拼写或输入错误的问题（这些在预写作阶段并不重要）；相反，你可以专注于尽可能多地记录关于主题的想法和细节。

college-writing-000836.en: After any initial freewriting, questioning, and list-making on a computer, it’s often very helpful to print out a hard copy of what you’ve done.
college-writing-000836.zh: 在在计算机上完成最初的自由写作、提问和列表整理之后，打印出所写内容的纸质版本通常非常有帮助。

college-writing-000837.en: With a clean printout in front of you, you’ll be able to see everything at once and revise and expand your work with handwritten comments in the margins of the paper.
college-writing-000837.zh: 当您面前有清晰的打印内容时，就能一次性看清所有内容，并借助纸张边缘的手写评论来修改和扩展作品。

college-writing-000838.en: Don’t underestimate the power of working on a printed copy.
college-writing-000838.zh: 不要低估使用打印版文件所带来的优势。

college-writing-000839.en: By allowing yourself the freedom to mark up the printed copy, you will free up more ideas.
college-writing-000839.zh: 允许自己自由地标注打印版本的内容，就能激发更多创意。

college-writing-000840.en: If you have prepared a list of items, you may be able to turn that list into a scratch outline right on the screen.
college-writing-000840.zh: 如果你已经整理好了清单，或许可以把该清单直接作为屏幕上的草图大纲。

college-writing-000841.en: Create a copy of your list below the original, and then using the copy, delete the ideas you feel should not be in your paper, and add any new ideas that occur to you.
college-writing-000841.zh: 在原列表下方创建一个副本，然后利用该副本删除那些你认为不应出现在论文中的观点，同时添加任何你想到的新观点。

college-writing-000842.en: Then use the cut and paste functions to shuffle the supporting ideas around until you find the best order for your paper.
college-writing-000842.zh: 然后使用剪切粘贴功能对相关观点进行重新排列，直到找到适合你论文的最佳顺序。

college-writing-000843.en: If you find that you accidentally deleted an idea that would now work, you can use the copy and paste feature to take that idea from your original list and place it in your scratch outline.
college-writing-000843.zh: 如果你发现自己不小心删除了某个现在可以实施的想法，可以使用复制粘贴功能，将那个想法从原始列表中提取出来，放入你的草稿大纲中。

college-writing-000844.en: Using the computer also makes it easy for you to experiment with the wording of the point of your paper.
college-writing-000844.zh: 使用电脑还能让你轻松尝试调整论文内容的措辞。

college-writing-000845.en: You can try a number of versions in a short time.
college-writing-000845.zh: 你可以在短时间内尝试多种版本。

college-writing-000846.en: After you have decided on the version that works best, you can easily delete the other versions─or simply move them to a temporary “leftover” section at the end of the paper.
college-writing-000846.zh: 确定出最合适的版本后，你可以轻松删除其他版本——或者 simply将它们移到纸张末尾的临时“剩余”区域。

college-writing-000847.en: At any point in the prewriting, outlining, or drafting process, you might experience writer’s block or need some inspiration.
college-writing-000847.zh: 在构思、大纲制定或写作过程中，你可能会遇到写作障碍或需要灵感。

college-writing-000848.en: One way to get ideas flowing is to do some Google searches based on keywords in your topic.
college-writing-000848.zh: 让灵感涌现的一种方式，就是根据你主题中的关键词进行一些谷歌搜索。

college-writing-000849.en: For instance, you could do a search for “worst jobs” and find some funny lists or sad stories on the topic, and one of these stories could remind you of a bad job experience.
college-writing-000849.zh: 例如，你可以搜索“最糟糕的工作”，然后找到一些关于这个话题的有趣列表或悲伤故事。其中某个故事可能会让你想起自己糟糕的工作经历。

college-writing-000850.en: It’s easy to get caught up in Web searching for hours, so restrict your search to ten or twenty minutes.
college-writing-000850.zh: 很容易陷入网络搜索中数小时，因此请将搜索时间限制在十到二十分钟。

college-writing-000851.en: Set an alarm so that you won’t go over your time limit.
college-writing-000851.zh: 设置闹钟，以免超过时间限制。

college-writing-000855.en: Like many writers, you may want to write out your first draft by hand and then type it into the computer for the next steps in writing.
college-writing-000855.zh: 像许多作家一样，你可能希望先手工写出初稿，然后再将其输入电脑，以便进行后续的写作工作。

college-writing-000856.en: Even as you type your handwritten draft, you may find yourself making some changes and improvements.
college-writing-000856.zh: 在输入手写的草稿时，你可能会发现需要做一些修改和改进。

college-writing-000857.en: And once you have a draft on the screen, or printed out, you will find it much easier to revise than a handwritten one.
college-writing-000857.zh: 一旦在屏幕上或打印出草稿，修改起来就会比手写版本容易得多。

college-writing-000858.en: If you feel comfortable composing directly on a computer and you typed your prewriting, you can benefit from its special features.
college-writing-000858.zh: 如果你觉得直接在电脑上写作很方便，且已经完成了预写作工作，那么就可以利用它的特殊功能获得优势。

college-writing-000859.en: For example, if you have written an anecdote in your freewriting that you plan to use in your paper, simply copy the story from your freewriting file and insert it where it fits in your paper.
college-writing-000859.zh: 例如，如果你在自由写作中写了一个故事，打算在论文中使用这个故事，只需将故事从自由写作文件中复制出来，然后将其插入到论文的合适位置即可。

college-writing-000860.en: You can refine it then or later.
college-writing-000860.zh: 你可以之后或稍后再进行改进。

college-writing-000861.en: Or if you discover while typing that a sentence is out of place, cut it out from where it is and paste it wherever you wish.
college-writing-000861.zh: 或者，在输入时发现某个句子位置不当，就将其从原处剪下，然后粘贴到您希望的位置。

college-writing-000862.en: And if while writing you realize that an earlier sentence can be expanded, just move your cursor back to that point and type in the additional material.
college-writing-000862.zh: 如果在写作过程中发现某个句子可以进一步扩展，只需将光标移回该位置，然后输入额外的内容即可。

college-writing-000864.en: It is during revision that the advantages of using a computer really shine.
college-writing-000864.zh: 正是在修订过程中，使用计算机的优势才真正显现出来。

college-writing-000865.en: All substituting, adding, deleting, and rearranging can be done easily within an existing file.
college-writing-000865.zh: 在现有文件内，可以轻松进行替换、添加、删除和重新排列操作。

college-writing-000866.en: All changes instantly take their proper places within the paper, not scribbled above the line or squeezed into the margin.
college-writing-000866.zh: 所有修改内容都会立即出现在文档中，不会被潦草地写在行外或挤在页边。

college-writing-000867.en: You can concentrate on each change you want to make, because you never have to type from scratch or work on a messy draft.
college-writing-000867.zh: 你可以专注于想要进行的每一项修改，因为无需从零开始输入，也无需处理混乱的草稿。

college-writing-000868.en: You can carefully go through your paper to check that all your supporting evidence is relevant and to add new support as needed here and there.
college-writing-000868.zh: 你可以仔细检查文章，确保所有支撑论点的证据都切题，并在需要的地方补充论据。

college-writing-000869.en: Anything you decide to eliminate can be deleted in a keystroke.
college-writing-000869.zh: 你决定删除的任何内容都可以通过一次按键操作被删除。

college-writing-000870.en: Anything you add can be inserted precisely where you choose.
college-writing-000870.zh: 你可以将任何内容插入到任意位置。

college-writing-000871.en: If you change your mind, all you have to do is delete or cut and paste.
college-writing-000871.zh: 如果你改变主意，只需删除或剪切后粘贴即可。

college-writing-000872.en: Then you can sweep through the paper, focusing on other changes, such as improving word choice, increasing sentence variety, and eliminating wordiness.
college-writing-000872.zh: 然后你可以浏览全文，关注其他方面的改进，比如优化词汇选择、增加句子多样性以及减少冗余词。

college-writing-000874.en: Editing and proofreading also benefit richly from computers.
college-writing-000874.zh: 编辑和校对工作也从计算机中获得了极大的便利。

college-writing-000875.en: Most programs have spell-checker and grammar-checker features.
college-writing-000875.zh: 大多数程序都具备拼写检查器和语法检查器功能。

college-writing-000876.en: If your own program doesn’t have
college-writing-000876.zh: 如果您的程序本身没有

college-writing-000877.en: If you are trying to find a new topic or can’t think of one, try reviewing recent e-mails, text messages, posts on Twitter or Facebook, or even your school library website.
college-writing-000877.zh: 如果你正在寻找新话题，或者想不出什么话题，可以查看最近的邮件、短信、推特或脸书上的帖子，甚至你的学校图书馆网站。

college-writing-000878.en: What have you been talking about with friends, family, or classmates?
college-writing-000878.zh: 你与朋友、家人或同学谈论了什么？

college-writing-000879.en: What topics have been hotly discussed on your campus?
college-writing-000879.zh: 你们校园里有哪些话题引发了热烈讨论？

college-writing-000880.en: Write about something that interests you.
college-writing-000880.zh: 写关于你感兴趣的内容。

college-writing-000882.en: these options, your college computers will likely provide them, or you can use an online program like Grammarly or SpellCheckPlus.
college-writing-000882.zh: 这些功能，你的大学电脑很可能就能提供，或者你可以使用 Grammarly 或 SpellCheckPlus 这样的在线工具。

college-writing-000883.en: The spell-checker function tells you when a word is not in the program’s dictionary.
college-writing-000883.zh: 拼写检查功能会提示某个词不在程序的词典中。

college-writing-000884.en: Keep in mind, however, that the spell-checker cannot tell you how to spell a name correctly or when you have mistakenly used, for example, their instead of there.
college-writing-000884.zh: 不过，请记住，拼写检查器无法告诉你如何正确拼写一个名字，或者你是否错误地使用了“their”而不是“there”。

college-writing-000885.en: To a spell-checker, Thank ewe four the complement is as correct as Thank you for the compliment.
college-writing-000885.zh: 对于校对工具来说，感谢的补充语与“谢谢”这种赞美语一样正确。

college-writing-000886.en: The grammar-checker is a good feature, but use it with caution.
college-writing-000886.zh: 语法检查器是一个很好的功能，但使用时需谨慎。

college-writing-000887.en: It will look for mistakes like fragments and run-ons, but it isn’t always correct.
college-writing-000887.zh: 它会寻找诸如片段和句子断落等错误，但结果并不总是正确的。

college-writing-000888.en: Any errors it doesn’t uncover are still your responsibility.
college-writing-000888.zh: 任何未被发现的错误仍由你负责。

college-writing-000889.en: Once you have checked your essay, you should print it out for a final readthrough.
college-writing-000889.zh: 检查完文章后，你应该将其打印出来，进行最后的阅读。

college-writing-000890.en: Reading aloud, slowly, will help you catch any typos or awkward sentences the programs didn’t identify.
college-writing-000890.zh: 大声、缓慢地朗读，有助于你发现程序未能识别的任何拼写错误或不自然的句子。

college-writing-000891.en: A printed paper, with its clean appearance and handsome formatting, often looks so good that you may feel it is in better shape than it really is.
college-writing-000891.zh: 这种印刷品，以其干净的外观和美观的排版，往往看起来非常出色，以至于你会觉得它的实际状况比实际更好。

college-writing-000893.en: Take sufficient time to review your grammar, punctuation, and spelling carefully.
college-writing-000893.zh: 花足够的时间仔细审查你的语法、标点和拼写问题。

college-writing-000894.en: Even after you hand in your paper, save the computer file.
college-writing-000894.zh: 即使你交了论文，也请保存电脑文件。

college-writing-000895.en: Your teacher may ask you to do some revising, and then the file will save you from having to completely retype the paper.
college-writing-000895.zh: 您的老师可能会要求您进行一些修改，这样就能避免您必须完全重新输入论文内容。

college-writing-000896.en: In future assignments, you may be asked to incorporate images or links into a paper.
college-writing-000896.zh: 在未来的任务中，你可能需要将图片或链接整合到论文中。

college-writing-000897.en: Think of these as garnishes on a dinner plate or lemon slices in glasses of water─they are there to add a bit of color and flavor, not to overwhelm the main dish.
college-writing-000897.zh: 可以把它们视为晚餐菜肴上的装饰，或是水杯中的柠檬片——它们的作用只是增添一些色彩和风味，而不是掩盖主菜的味道。

college-writing-000898.en: Incorporate visuals or links into a paper only with your instructor’s approval and guidance.
college-writing-000898.zh: 只有在得到指导老师的许可和指导后，才可以在论文中加入图片或链接。

college-writing-000899.en: Know and follow rules, both legal and ethical, about when and how to use others’ images as well as how to credit them.
college-writing-000899.zh: 了解并遵守法律与道德方面的规定，包括何时以及如何使用他人的图像，以及如何注明出处。

college-writing-000900.en: You probably know the saying, “A picture speaks a thousand words.”
college-writing-000900.zh: 你可能知道那句话：“一图胜千言。”

college-writing-000901.en: Remember this when selecting an image; you should aim to find one that illustrates or supports your paper’s main idea.
college-writing-000901.zh: 选择图片时请记住这一点：你应该寻找能够体现或支持你的论文核心观点的图片。

college-writing-000902.en: Links should be used when they provide useful information that enhances the content of your paper.
college-writing-000902.zh: 应使用那些能够提供有助于提升论文内容的有用信息的链接。

college-writing-000903.en: As with images, avoid links that might distract readers from the central point of your paper.
college-writing-000903.zh: 就像处理图片一样，要避免那些可能让读者偏离文章核心内容的链接。

college-writing-000907.en: Essays in English classes must be submitted in MLA format.
college-writing-000907.zh: 英语课程论文必须按MLA格式提交。

college-writing-000908.en: While many students might think this applies only to the use of citations within resource-based essays, MLA format also dictates the formal characteristics of the paper including paper size, margins, spacing, and font.
college-writing-000908.zh: 虽然许多学生可能认为这仅适用于基于资源类论文中的引用方式，但MLA格式还规定了论文的正式格式要求，包括纸张尺寸、边距、行距和字体。

college-writing-000909.en: All essays should be formatted like this:
college-writing-000909.zh: 所有文章都应按照此格式排版：

college-writing-000914.en: Successful Families: Fighting for Their Kids
college-writing-000914.zh: 成功的家庭：为他们的孩子而战

college-writing-000915.en: It’s a terrible time to be a teenager, or even a teenager’s
college-writing-000915.zh: 作为青少年，甚至只是青少年时期，这是非常糟糕的时期。

college-writing-000919.en: newspapers are all full of frightening stories about teenagers and
college-writing-000919.zh: 报纸上到处都是关于青少年的恐怖故事。

college-writing-000921.en: They say that America’s families are falling apart, that kids
college-writing-000921.zh: 他们说美国的家庭正在瓦解，那些孩子……

college-writing-000922.en: don’t care about anything, and that parents have trouble doing
college-writing-000922.zh: 我不在乎任何事情，而父母也很难做到

college-writing-000928.en: Leave a one-inch margin on all sides.
college-writing-000928.zh: 在所有侧边留出一英寸的边距。

college-writing-000929.en: Model First Page of MLA- Style Paper

college-writing-000930.en: Here is a checklist you should use when preparing a paper:
college-writing-000930.zh: 以下是撰写论文时应使用的检查清单：

college-writing-000931.en: • Is the paper full-size, 81⁄2 by 11 inches?
college-writing-000931.zh: • 这份文件是标准尺寸吗？81⁄2乘11英寸？

college-writing-000932.en: • Is there a heading that includes your name, your professor’s name, your class, and date?
college-writing-000932.zh: • 是否有包含你的姓名、教授的姓名、班级名称以及日期的标题？

college-writing-000933.en: • Is there a header with your last name and the page number?
college-writing-000933.zh: • 是否有以你的姓氏和页码为标题的页面？

college-writing-000934.en: • Are your margins one inch all around the paper?
college-writing-000934.zh: • 纸张四周的边距是否都是一英寸？

college-writing-000936.en: • Is the title of your paper about two inches from the top of the page, centered, and separate from the body of the essay?
college-writing-000936.zh: • 您论文的标题应位于页面顶部两英寸处，居中排列，且与文章正文分开。

college-writing-000937.en: Have you been careful not to put quotation marks around the title and not to underline or boldface it?
college-writing-000937.zh: 你有没有注意不在标题周围加上引号，也不将其加下划线或加粗显示？

college-writing-000938.en: Have you capitalized all the words in the title except short connecting words like of, for, the, and, it, and to?
college-writing-000938.zh: 除了“of”、“for”、“the”、“and”、“it”和“to”这样的短连接词之外，你是否使用了标题中的所有单词的首字母大写？

college-writing-000939.en: • Have you skipped a line between the title and the first line of your paper?
college-writing-000939.zh: • 你是否跳过了论文标题与第一行之间的那一行？

college-writing-000940.en: • Have you indented the first line of each paragraph five spaces (half an inch or tab) from the left-hand margin?
college-writing-000940.zh: • 你是否将每个段落的第一行从左边缘向内缩进五个空格（半英寸或Tab键距离）？

college-writing-000941.zh: • 你的文章是双行距排版吗？

college-writing-000942.en: • Have you turned off the hyphenation feature in your word processing program so words are not divided at the end of a line?
college-writing-000942.zh: • 你是否关闭了文字处理程序中的连字符功能，这样单词就不会在行尾被分开？

college-writing-000943.en: • Does your essay use an easy-to-read typeface (e. g., Times New Roman or Calibri) in a 12-point font throughout, including the title?
college-writing-000943.zh: • 你的文章是否全程使用了易阅读的字体（例如Times New Roman或Calibri），字号为12号，包括标题部分也是如此？

college-writing-000945.en: Also ask yourself these important questions about the title and the first sentence of your paper:
college-writing-000945.zh: 同时，请自己思考关于论文标题和首句的那些重要问题：

college-writing-000946.en: • Is your title a phrase, not a complete sentence?
college-writing-000946.zh: • 你的标题是一个短语，而不是一个完整的句子吗？

college-writing-000947.en: Is your title made up of several words that tell what the paper is about?
college-writing-000947.zh: 你的标题是由几个描述文章内容的词组成的吗？

college-writing-000948.en: (The title should hint at the topic, not focus on what assignment it fulfills.)
college-writing-000948.zh: （标题应暗示主题，而非强调其属于何种任务。）

college-writing-000949.en: • Does the first sentence of your paper stand independent of the title?
college-writing-000949.zh: • 你论文的第一句话能否独立于标题而存在？

college-writing-000950.en: (The reader should not have to use the words in the title to make sense of the opening sentence.)
college-writing-000950.zh: （读者无需使用标题中的词汇就能理解首句的意思。）

college-writing-000951.en: Part 3 will explain MLA format in much more detail, including integration and documentation of sources, proper citation, and proper format of papers that integrate outside sources.
college-writing-000951.zh: 第三部分将更详细地说明MLA格式，包括来源的整合与标注、正确的引用方式，以及包含外部资料的论文的正确格式。

college-writing-000952.en: Additionally, Chapter 20 includes a properly formatted, complete research essay.
college-writing-000952.zh: 此外，第20章还包含一篇格式规范、内容完整的研究论文。

college-writing-000955.en: Answering the following questions will help you evaluate your attitude about writing.
college-writing-000955.zh: 回答以下问题有助于你评估自己的写作态度。

college-writing-000956.en: 1. How much practice were you given writing compositions in high school?
college-writing-000956.zh: 高中时，你们被要求练习写作作文的时长有多少？

college-writing-000958.en: 2. How much feedback (positive or negative comments) from teachers were you given on your compositions?
college-writing-000958.zh: 2. 你的作文得到了多少来自老师的反馈（正面或负面的评价）？

college-writing-000962.en: 3. How did your teachers seem to regard your writing?
college-writing-000962.zh: 3. 你的老师对你的写作有何评价？

college-writing-000964.en: 4. Do you feel that some people simply have a gift for writing and others do not?
college-writing-000964.zh: 4. 你觉得有些人天生就具备写作天赋，而其他人则没有吗？

college-writing-000966.en: 5. When do you start writing a paper?
college-writing-000966.zh: 5. 你什么时候开始撰写论文？

college-writing-000967.en: __________ Several days before it is due

college-writing-000968.en: __________ About a day before it is due

college-writing-000970.en: explanation: Many people who answer Little to questions 1 and 2 often answer Poor, Yes, and At the last possible minute to questions 3, 4, and 5.
college-writing-000970.zh: 解释：许多回答第1和第2题时回答“差”或“是”的人，在回答第3、4和5题时往往会在最后一刻做出回答。

college-writing-000971.en: On the other hand, people who answer Much or Some to questions 1 and 2 also tend to have more favorable responses to the other questions.
college-writing-000971.zh: 另一方面，对问题1和2回答“很多”或“一些”的人，对其他问题的回答也往往更积极。

college-writing-000972.en: The point is that people with little practice in the skill of writing often have understandably negative feelings about their writing ability.
college-writing-000972.zh: 关键在于，那些在写作技能上练习较少的人，往往会对自己的写作能力有负面的看法，这是可以理解的。

college-writing-000973.en: They need not have such feelings, however, because writing is a skill that they can learn with practice.
college-writing-000973.zh: 不过，他们不必有这种感觉，因为写作是一种可以通过练习来学习的技能。

college-writing-000974.en: 6. What kinds of writing do you do on a computer?
college-writing-000974.zh: 6. 你用电脑做哪些类型的写作？

college-writing-000975.en: What additional types of writing might you want to undertake on the computer?
college-writing-000975.zh: 你可能在电脑上想要从事哪些其他类型的写作？

college-writing-000976.en: 7. Have you ever kept a diary or journal like the one explained in this chapter?
college-writing-000976.zh: 7. 你曾经写过像本章所介绍的那种日记或日志吗？

college-writing-000977.en: If so, what kinds of ideas, images, or other information have you put into your journal?
college-writing-000977.zh: 如果是这样的话，你会在日记中记录哪些想法、图像或其他信息呢？

college-writing-000978.en: If you have never kept a journal, why not?
college-writing-000978.zh: 如果你从未写过日记，那为什么不呢？

college-writing-000979.en: Does this fact have anything to do with how you think of writing?
college-writing-000979.zh: 这一事实与你对写作的看法有何关联？

college-writing-000980.en: 8. In your own words, explain what it means to say that writing is often a zigzag journey rather than a straight-line journey.
college-writing-000980.zh: 8. 用你自己的话来说，解释一下“写作往往是一段曲折的旅程，而非直线式的旅程”这一说法的含义。

college-writing-000982.en: Following is an excerpt from Finley’s journal.
college-writing-000982.zh: 以下是芬利日记的摘录。

college-writing-000983.en: As you read, look for a general point and supporting material that could be the basis for an interesting paper.
college-writing-000983.zh: 在阅读过程中，请寻找一个普遍观点和支撑材料，这些可能成为撰写一篇有价值论文的基础。

college-writing-000986.en: I received the results of my first history test today.
college-writing-000986.zh: 今天我收到了第一次历史考试的结果。

college-writing-000988.en: thought I had studied a lot, but my grade was terrible.
college-writing-000988.zh: 我以为自己学习了很多，但成绩却很糟糕。

college-writing-000990.en: school, I never needed to study much, and I still received As and
college-writing-000990.zh: 在学校里，我从来不需要学习太多，仍然能得到A级成绩。

college-writing-000992.en: My teachers always provided a study guide of some sort, and
college-writing-000992.zh: 我的老师总是会提供某种形式的学习指南，

college-writing-000993.en: working through it usually guaranteed a good grade.
college-writing-000993.zh: 通过努力完成它通常能确保获得好成绩。

college-writing-000995.en: professor didn’t give us anything to study from.
college-writing-000995.zh: 教授没有给我们任何可以学习的资料。

college-writing-000997.en: about a study guide, I was told that our text, notes, and
college-writing-000997.zh: 关于学习指南，有人告诉我我们的教材、笔记以及……

college-writing-000999.en: How was I supposed to figure

college-writing-001000.en: out what was and wasn’t important?
college-writing-001000.zh: 找出什么重要，什么不重要的？

college-writing-001001.en: At first I was really angry at my

college-writing-001002.en: professor that she hadn’t helped me more.
college-writing-001002.zh: 教授没有给予我更多的帮助。

college-writing-001004.en: through the class listening to her go over the exam and
college-writing-001004.zh: 通过课堂听她复习考试内容

college-writing-001005.en: reprimanding the class for not doing well.
college-writing-001005.zh: 因班级表现不佳而责备学生。

college-writing-001006.en: I felt like telling her that

college-writing-001007.en: maybe it was her fault if so many people did poorly.
college-writing-001007.zh: 如果真是如此，那么多人都表现不佳，或许也是她的错。

college-writing-001009.en: was over, I ended up storming out, promising myself that I was
college-writing-001009.zh: 事情结束后，我气冲冲地离开了，对自己说，我一定不会……

college-writing-001010.en: going to complain to the dean.

college-writing-001011.en: I headed to the dean’s office to

college-writing-001012.en: formally complain, but was told by the assistant that if I hadn’t
college-writing-001012.zh: 正式投诉，但助手告诉我如果我没有

college-writing-001013.en: spoken to my professor first, the dean wasn’t going to listen to my
college-writing-001013.zh: 首先找我的教授谈，院长不会听我的……

college-writing-001015.en: As upset as I was, I headed back to my professor’s
college-writing-001015.zh: 尽管我很沮丧，我还是回到了我的教授那里。

college-writing-001017.en: When she arrived, she seemed really

college-writing-001018.en: pleased to see me. I was totally surprised!
college-writing-001018.zh: 很高兴见到你。我真的非常惊讶！

college-writing-001020.en: happy that I was coming in to talk about my test and would be
college-writing-001020.zh: 很高兴能来谈谈我的测试情况，那将会

college-writing-001021.en: more than pleased to show me where I had gone wrong.
college-writing-001021.zh: 非常高兴能告诉我哪里出了错。

college-writing-001023.en: forty-five minutes, I completely understood what I had missed and
college-writing-001023.zh: 45分钟里，我完全明白了自己忽略了什么。

college-writing-001024.en: what I needed to do for future tests.

college-writing-001025.zh: 我们的会议以我的结束。

college-writing-001026.en: professor making me promise to visit her again—before the next exam—to make sure I understood the material.
college-writing-001026.zh: 教授要求我承诺在下次考试之前再去她那里一次，以确保我彻底理解了所学内容。

college-writing-001029.en: 1. If Finley was looking for ideas for an essay, she could probably find several in this single entry.
college-writing-001029.zh: 1. 如果芬利想要寻找写作文的灵感，或许可以在这一篇文章中找到几个好点子。

college-writing-001030.en: For example, she might write a story about the differences between high school teachers and college professors.
college-writing-001030.zh: 例如，她可能会写一篇关于高中教师与大学教授之间差异的故事。

college-writing-001031.en: See if you can find an idea in the entry that might be the basis for an interesting essay, and write your point in the space below.
college-writing-001031.zh: 看看能否在文中找到某个观点，作为撰写一篇有趣文章的基础，然后在下方空白处写下你的观点。

college-writing-001032.en: 2. Take fifteen minutes now to write a journal entry on this day in your life.
college-writing-001032.zh: 现在花15分钟时间，写下关于这一天你生活的日记。

college-writing-001033.en: On a separate sheet of paper, just start writing about anything that you have seen, said, heard, thought, or felt today, and let your thoughts take you where they may.
college-writing-001033.zh: 在另一张纸上，只需写下你今天所看到、听到、想到或感受到的任何内容，让你的思绪自由驰骋。

college-writing-001035.en: Here is a suggested sequence for using this book if you are working on your own.
college-writing-001035.zh: 如果您是独立学习，以下是使用本书的建议顺序。

college-writing-001036.en: 1. After completing this introduction, read Chapters 2 through 7 in Part 1 and work through as many of the activities as you need to master the ideas in these chapters.
college-writing-001036.zh: 完成本介绍后，请阅读第1部分的第2至第7章内容，并尽可能完成所有相关练习，以掌握这些章节中的知识点。

college-writing-001037.en: By the end of Part 1, you will have covered all the basic theory needed to write effective papers.
college-writing-001037.zh: 到第一部分结束时，你将掌握撰写有效论文所需的所有基础理论。

college-writing-001038.en: 2. Work through some of the chapters in Part 2, which describe a number of ways to organize and develop essays.
college-writing-001038.zh: 2. 研读第二部分中的部分章节，这些章节介绍了多种撰写和完善文章的方法。

college-writing-001039.en: You may want to integrate “Exemplification,” “Process,” and “Argument.”
college-writing-001039.zh: 你可能需要将“示例”、“过程”和“论点”结合起来。

college-writing-001040.en: Each chapter opens with a brief introduction to a specific pattern, followed by two student essays and one model essay written in a way that emphasizes that pattern.
college-writing-001040.zh: 每一章都以对特定模式的简要介绍开始，随后是两篇学生文章和一篇以强调该模式为特色的范文。

college-writing-001041.en: Included are a series of questions so that you can evaluate the essays in terms of the basic principles of writing explained in Part 1.
college-writing-001041.zh: 包含了一系列问题，以便您可以根据第一部分所阐述的写作原则来评估文章。

college-writing-001042.en: Finally, a number of writing topics are presented, along with hints about prewriting and revising to help you plan and write an effective paper.
college-writing-001042.zh: 最后，列举了若干写作主题，并提供了关于预写作和修改的提示，以帮助你规划并撰写出有效的文章。

college-writing-001043.en: 3. Turn to Part 3 as needed for help with skills essential to academic writing in college: information literacy, summarizing and paraphrasing, writing source-based essays, and writing research papers.
college-writing-001043.zh: 如需获取大学学术写作所需的关键技能指导，请随时参阅第三部分：信息素养、摘要与转述技巧、基于文献的论文写作，以及研究论文写作。

college-writing-001047.en: from this test than just history!
college-writing-001047.zh: 从这一测试来看，不仅仅是历史！

college-writing-001048.en: I now realize that professors expect
college-writing-001048.zh: 我现在意识到，教授们是有所期待的

college-writing-001049.en: us to take responsibility for our learning, which means going to see
college-writing-001049.zh: 让我们对自己的学习负责，这意味着要付诸实践

college-writing-001050.en: them for help and not waiting for them to spoon-feed us.
college-writing-001050.zh: 寻求他们的帮助，而不是等待他们一勺一勺地喂我们。

college-writing-001052.en: that these kinds of writing are variations of the essay form you have already learned in Part 1 and have further explored in Part 2.
college-writing-001052.zh: 这些写作形式其实都是你在第一部分已经学习过的文章形式的变体，并在第二部分中得到了进一步探讨。

college-writing-001053.en: 4. In addition, refer to Part 4 as needed for review and practice in the skills needed to write effective, error-free sentences.
college-writing-001053.zh: 4. 此外，可根据需要参考第4部分，以练习和掌握撰写有效、无错误的句子所需的技能。

college-writing-001054.en: 5. Finally, read some of the selections in Part 5 and respond to the activities that follow the selections.
college-writing-001054.zh: 5. 最后，阅读第5部分中的部分选文，并回答选文后的相关任务。

college-writing-001055.en: For your convenience, the book includes the following:
college-writing-001055.zh: 为了您的方便，本书包含以下内容：

college-writing-001056.en: • At the back of the book, there is a checklist of the four basic steps in effective writing.
college-writing-001056.zh: • 在书的背面，有一份有效写作的四个基本步骤的清单。

college-writing-001057.en: • At the end of Part 4, there is a list of commonly used correction symbols.
college-writing-001057.zh: • 第4部分的末尾有一个常用修正符号列表。

college-writing-001058.en: Get into the habit of regularly referring to these guides; they’ll help you produce clearly thought-out, well-written essays.
college-writing-001058.zh: 养成定期参考这些指南的习惯；它们将帮助你写出思路清晰、文笔优美的文章。

college-writing-001059.en: College Writing Skills with Readings will help you learn, practice, and apply the thinking and writing skills you need to communicate effectively.
college-writing-001059.zh: “大学写作技能与阅读”课程将帮助你学习、练习并运用所需的思考与写作技能，从而有效进行交流。

college-writing-001060.en: But the starting point must be your own determination to do the work needed to become a strong writer.
college-writing-001060.zh: 但起点必须是你自己决定要完成成为优秀作家所需的工作。

college-writing-001061.en: The ability to express yourself clearly and logically can open doors of opportunity for you, both in school and in your career.
college-writing-001061.zh: 能够清晰、逻辑地表达自己，能为你打开学校和职业生涯中的机会之门。

college-writing-001062.en: If you decide─and only you can decide─that you want such language power, this book will help you reach that goal.
college-writing-001062.zh: 如果你决定——也只有你能够决定——想要拥有这种语言力量，这本书将帮助你实现这一目标。

college-writing-001063.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate • the sequence of steps in writing an effective essay • prewriting • drafting • revising • editing
college-writing-001063.zh: 本章将解释并说明•撰写有效文章的步骤顺序•预写作、草稿撰写、修改、编辑。

college-writing-001065.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-001066.en: Think about an electronic device you use every day; it could be your cell phone, radio, computer, music player, tablet, etc.
college-writing-001066.zh: 想想你每天使用的电子设备吧；它可能是你的手机、收音机、电脑、音乐播放器、平板电脑等。

college-writing-001067.en: See if you can write for ten minutes about why you couldn’t live without it.
college-writing-001067.zh: 看看你能不能写十分钟关于为什么没有它就无法生活的内容。

college-writing-001068.en: Don’t worry about spelling and punctuation; just get your thoughts down on paper.
college-writing-001068.zh: 不必担心拼写和标点，只要把你的想法写在纸上即可。

college-writing-001070.en: Chapter 1 introduced you to the essay form and to some basics of writing.
college-writing-001070.zh: 第一章向您介绍了文章形式以及写作的一些基础。

college-writing-001071.en: This chapter explains and illustrates the sequence of steps in writing an effective essay.
college-writing-001071.zh: 本章阐述并展示了撰写有效文章的步骤顺序。

college-writing-001072.en: In particular, the chapter focuses on prewriting and revising─ strategies that can help with every essay you write.
college-writing-001072.zh: 特别是，这一章重点介绍了预写作与修改的方法——这些策略对你撰写的每篇文章都有帮助。

college-writing-001073.en: For many people, writing is a process that involves the following steps:
college-writing-001073.zh: 对许多人来说，写作是一个包含以下步骤的过程：

college-writing-001074.zh: 1. 发现论点——通常是通过预写作过程。

college-writing-001075.en: 2. Developing solid support for the thesis─often through more prewriting.
college-writing-001075.zh: 2. 为论点发展坚实的支撑——通常通过更多的预写作过程来实现。

college-writing-001078.en: If you are like many people, you may have trouble getting started with writing.
college-writing-001078.zh: 如果你和许多人一样，可能会在写作初期遇到困难。

college-writing-001079.en: A mental block may develop when you sit down before a blank sheet of paper or an empty computer screen.
college-writing-001079.zh: 当你坐在空白的纸张或空白的电脑屏幕上时，可能会产生思维障碍。

college-writing-001080.en: You may not be able to think of an interesting topic or thesis.
college-writing-001080.zh: 你可能想不出一个有趣的主题或论点。

college-writing-001081.en: Or you may have trouble coming up with relevant details to support a possible thesis.
college-writing-001081.zh: 或者，你可能会难以找到相关的细节来支持可能的论点。

college-writing-001082.en: And even after starting an essay, you may hit snags─moments when you wonder, What else can I say?
college-writing-001082.zh: 即使开始写作文后，也可能会遇到障碍——那些让人不禁想：“还能说些什么呢？”的时刻。

college-writing-001083.en: or Where do I go next?
college-writing-001083.zh: 或者，我接下来该去哪里呢？

college-writing-001084.en: The following pages describe five prewriting techniques that will help you think about and develop a topic and get words written down: (1) freewriting, (2) questioning, (3) making a list, (4) clustering, and (5) preparing a scratch outline.
college-writing-001084.zh: 以下页面介绍了五种写作前技巧，它们将帮助你思考并构思主题，并将想法写下来：(1) 自由写作；(2) 提问；(3) 列清单；(4) 分类整理；(5) 准备草稿大纲。

college-writing-001085.en: These techniques help you think about and create material, and they are a central part of the writing process.
college-writing-001085.zh: 这些技巧有助于你思考和创作内容，它们是写作过程的核心部分。

college-writing-001086.en: Technique 1: Freewriting Freewriting means jotting down in rough sentences or phrases everything that comes to mind about a possible topic.
college-writing-001086.zh: 技巧1：自由写作。自由写作指的是用粗略的句子或短语来记录关于某个主题的所有想法。

college-writing-001087.en: See if you can write nonstop for ten minutes or more.
college-writing-001087.zh: 看看你能否连续写作十分钟或更长时间。

college-writing-001088.en: Do not worry about spelling or punctuating correctly, about erasing mistakes, about organizing material, or about finding exact words.
college-writing-001088.zh: 不必担心拼写或标点是否正确，不必担心擦除错误、整理材料或寻找精确词汇。

college-writing-001089.en: Instead, explore an idea by putting down whatever pops into your head.
college-writing-001089.zh: 相反，可以随便写下脑海中出现的任何想法来探索这个想法。

college-writing-001090.en: If you get stuck for words, repeat yourself until more words come.
college-writing-001090.zh: 如果找不到合适的词，就重复说，直到能找到合适的词为止。

college-writing-001091.en: There is no need to feel inhibited, since mistakes do not count and you do not have to hand in your freewriting.
college-writing-001091.zh: 无需感到拘束，因为错误并不被计入，你也不必提交你的自由写作内容。

college-writing-001092.en: Freewriting will limber up your writing muscles and make you familiar with the act of writing.
college-writing-001092.zh: 自由写作能锻炼你的写作能力，让你更熟悉写作的过程。

college-writing-001093.en: It is a way to break through mental blocks about writing.
college-writing-001093.zh: 这是一种突破写作心理障碍的方法。

college-writing-001095.en: 3. Organizing the thesis and supporting material and writing it out in a first draft.
college-writing-001095.zh: 3. 整理论文及辅助材料，撰写初稿。

college-writing-001096.en: 4. Revising and then editing carefully to ensure an effective, error-free essay.
college-writing-001096.zh: 4. 修改后仔细编辑，以确保文章有效且无错误。

college-writing-001097.en: Learning this sequence will help give you confidence when the time comes to write.
college-writing-001097.zh: 掌握这个序列能让你在写作时更有信心。

college-writing-001098.en: You’ll know that you can use prewriting as a way to think on paper and to gradually discover just what ideas you want to develop.
college-writing-001098.zh: 你会意识到，预写作是一种在纸上思考的方式，可以逐步发现你想发展的想法。

college-writing-001099.en: You’ll understand that there are four clear-cut goals─unity, support, organization, and error-free sentences─to aim for in your writing.
college-writing-001099.zh: 你会明白，在写作中需要实现四个明确的目标：统一性、支持性、组织性以及无错误语句。

college-writing-001100.en: You’ll realize that you can use revision to rework an essay until it is a strong and effective piece of writing.
college-writing-001100.zh: 你会意识到，可以使用修订功能对文章进行修改，直到它成为一篇扎实且有效的作品。

college-writing-001101.en: And you’ll be able to edit your writing so that your sentences are clear and error free.
college-writing-001101.zh: 你可以对你的写作进行编辑，使句子清晰且无错误。

college-writing-001103.en: you do not have to worry about mistakes, you can focus on discovering what you want to say about a subject.
college-writing-001103.zh: 你不必担心错误，可以专注于探索你想对某个主题表达的内容。

college-writing-001104.en: Your initial ideas and impressions will often become clearer after you have gotten them written down, and they may lead to other impressions and ideas.
college-writing-001104.zh: 一旦把你的初步想法和印象写下来，它们通常会变得更加清晰，而且这些想法和印象可能会带来其他新的想法。

college-writing-001105.en: Through continued practice in freewriting, you will develop the habit of thinking as you write.
college-writing-001105.zh: 通过持续的自由写作练习，你将养成边写边思考的习惯。

college-writing-001106.en: And you will learn a helpful technique for getting started on almost any writing you have to do.
college-writing-001106.zh: 你将学习到一种有助于入门的技巧，无论你需要进行何种写作工作，都可以运用它。

college-writing-001108.en: Finley Woods’s essay “The Hazards of Moviegoing” in Chapter 1 was developed in response to an assignment to write about some annoyance in everyday life.
college-writing-001108.zh: 芬利·伍兹在第一章中的文章《看电影的种种麻烦》是作为关于日常生活中某些烦恼的写作任务而创作的。

college-writing-001109.en: Finley began by doing some general freewriting and thinking about things that annoy her.
college-writing-001109.zh: Finley首先进行了一些自由写作，思考那些令她烦恼的事情。

college-writing-001111.en: There are lots of things I get annoyed by.
college-writing-001111.zh: 有很多事情让我感到恼火。

college-writing-001112.en: One of them that comes to mind is politishans, in fact I am so annoyed by them that I don’t want to say anything about them the last thing I want is to write about them.
college-writing-001112.zh: 我立刻想到的是politisans。事实上，我对他们感到非常恼火，以至于不想谈论他们；我最不希望做的就是写关于他们的内容。

college-writing-001113.en: Another thing that bothers me are people who keep complaining about everything.
college-writing-001113.zh: 另一个让我困扰的是那些对一切事情都抱怨不已的人。

college-writing-001114.en: If you’re having trouble, do something about it just don’t keep complaining and just talking.
college-writing-001114.zh: 如果你遇到麻烦，就采取行动解决它，不要只抱怨和空谈。

college-writing-001115.en: I am really annoyed by traffic.
college-writing-001115.zh: 我真的对交通感到很恼火。

college-writing-001116.en: There are too many cars in our block and its not surprising.
college-writing-001116.zh: 我们小区里的汽车太多了，这并不奇怪。

college-writing-001117.en: Everyone has a car, the parents have cars and the parents are just too induljent and the kids have cars, and theyre all coming and going all the time and often driving too fast.
college-writing-001117.zh: 每个人都有车，父母也有车，只是父母太放纵了，孩子们也有车。他们总是来来去去，而且经常开得过快。

college-writing-001118.en: Speeding up and down the street.

college-writing-001119.en: We need a speed limit sign but here I am back with politiks again.
college-writing-001119.zh: 我们需要一个限速标志，但如今我又回到了政治话题上。

college-writing-001120.en: I am really bothered when I have to drive to the movies all the congestion along the way plus there are just so many cars there at the mall.
college-writing-001120.zh: 当不得不开车去看电影时，我真的很困扰，路上的交通拥堵让人难以忍受，而且商场里还有太多车辆。

college-writing-001121.en: No space even though the parking lot is huge it just fills up with cars.
college-writing-001121.zh: 尽管停车场很大，却还是被汽车填满了。

college-writing-001122.en: Movies are a bother anyway because the people can be annoying who are sitting there in the theater with you, talking and dropping popcorn cups and acting like they’re at home when they’re not.
college-writing-001122.zh: 电影本身就让人厌烦，因为那些坐在电影院里和你一起看电影的人很烦人：他们说话、扔掉爆米花杯，还表现得像在家里一样，其实并非如此。

college-writing-001123.en: At this point, Finley read over her notes and, as she later commented, “I realized that I had several potential topics. I said to myself, ‘What point can I make that I can cover in an essay? What do I have the most information about?’ I decided that maybe I could narrow my topic down to the annoyances involved in going to the movies. I figured I would have more details for that topic.”
college-writing-001123.zh: 此时，芬利复习了她的笔记。正如她后来所说：“我意识到自己有几个潜在的主题。我对自己说：‘我能从文章中阐述什么观点呢？我对什么有最多的信息呢？’我决定或许可以把主题缩小到去电影院时遇到的那些麻烦事上。我觉得关于这个主题，我会有更多的细节可以写。”

college-writing-001124.en: Finley then did more focused freewriting to accumulate details for an essay on problems with moviegoing:
college-writing-001124.zh: 随后，Finley进行了更专注的自由写作，以积累关于看电影问题的文章所需的细节：

college-writing-001126.en: Notice that there are errors in spelling, grammar, and punctuation in Finley’s freewriting.
college-writing-001126.zh: 请注意，Finley的自由写作中存在拼写、语法和标点符号错误。

college-writing-001127.en: Finley is not worried about such matters, nor should she be.
college-writing-001127.zh: 芬利不必为这些事情担心，也不应该担心。

college-writing-001128.en: At this stage, she just wants to do some thinking and get some material down on the page.
college-writing-001128.zh: 现阶段，她只是想进行一些思考，把一些想法写在纸上。

college-writing-001129.en: She knows that this is a good first step, a good way of getting started, and that she will then be able to go on and shape the material.
college-writing-001129.zh: 她知道这是一项良好的第一步，也是开始工作的好方法，之后她就能继续对材料进行加工完善。

college-writing-001130.en: You should take the same approach when freewriting: explore your topic without worrying at all about being correct.
college-writing-001130.zh: 进行自由写作时也应采用同样的方法：探索你的主题，完全不必担心是否正确。

college-writing-001131.en: Figuring out what you want to say and getting raw material down on the page should have all of your attention at this early stage of the writing process.
college-writing-001131.zh: 在写作过程的早期阶段，你需要明确自己想要表达的内容，并将相关素材写在纸上。这应该是你全部注意力所集中的重点。

college-writing-001132.en: To get a sense of the freewriting process, take a sheet of paper and freewrite about some of the everyday annoyances in your life.
college-writing-001132.zh: 为了了解自由写作的过程，拿一张纸，自由地写下你生活中一些常见的烦恼。

college-writing-001133.en: See how much material you can accumulate in ten minutes.
college-writing-001133.zh: 看看你能在十分钟内积累多少材料。

college-writing-001134.en: And remember not to worry about mistakes; you’re just thinking on paper.
college-writing-001134.zh: 记住不要为错误而烦恼；你只是在纸上思考而已。

college-writing-001135.en: Technique 2: Questioning In questioning, you generate ideas and details by asking questions about your subject.
college-writing-001135.zh: 技巧二：提问在提问过程中，通过针对主题提出问题来产生想法和细节。

college-writing-001136.en: Such questions include why, when, where, who, what, and how.
college-writing-001136.zh: 这些问题包括为什么、何时、何地、谁、什么以及如何。

college-writing-001137.en: Ask as many questions as you can think of.
college-writing-001137.zh: 想问多少问题就问多少。

college-writing-001139.en: I really find it annoying to go see movies anymore.
college-writing-001139.zh: 我真的觉得现在去看电影很烦人了。

college-writing-001141.en: Traffic to Cinema Six is awful.
college-writing-001141.zh: 通往六号电影院的交通状况很糟糕。

college-writing-001142.en: I hate looking for a parking place, the lot isn’t big enough for the theaters and other stores.
college-writing-001142.zh: 我讨厌寻找停车位，那个停车场对于剧院和其他商店来说太小了。

college-writing-001143.en: You just keep driving to find a parking space and hoping someone will pull out and no one else will pull in ahead of you.
college-writing-001143.zh: 你只需继续开车，寻找一个停车位，希望有人能驶出，而没有人会先于你驶入。

college-writing-001144.en: Then you don’t want there to be a long line and end up finding out someone is sitting in your seat.
college-writing-001144.zh: 那样的话，你就不希望排成长队，最终发现有人坐在你的座位上。

college-writing-001145.en: Then I’m in the theater with the smell of popcorn all around.
college-writing-001145.zh: 然后我走进剧院，周围弥漫着爆米花的气味。

college-writing-001146.en: Sitting there smelling it trying to ignore it and just wanting to pour a whole bucket of popcorn with melted butter down my throat.
college-writing-001146.zh: 坐在那里闻着它，试图忽略它，只希望能倒一桶加了融化的黄油爆米花灌进我的喉咙里。

college-writing-001147.en: I can’t stop thinking about the choclate bars either.
college-writing-001147.zh: 我也无法停止思考巧克力棒的事。

college-writing-001148.en: I love the stuff but I don’t need it.
college-writing-001148.zh: 我喜欢那些东西，但我不需要它。

college-writing-001149.en: The people who are there sometimes drive me nuts.
college-writing-001149.zh: 那些人在那里有时真的让我抓狂。

college-writing-001150.en: Talking and laughing, kids running around, packs of teens hollaring, who can listen to the movie?
college-writing-001150.zh: 孩子们谈笑风生，跑来跑去，一群青少年吵吵闹闹，谁会听电影呢？

college-writing-001151.en: And I might run into my old boyfriend—the last thing I need.
college-writing-001151.zh: 而且我可能会遇到我的前男友——这是我最不想看到的。

college-writing-001152.en: Also sitting thru all the previews and commercals.
college-writing-001152.zh: 也坚持不观看所有的预告片和商业广告。

college-writing-001153.en: If I arrive late enough to miss that junk I have to try and find my seat in the dark.
college-writing-001153.zh: 如果我到达的时间足够晚，以至于错过那个东西，我就得在黑暗中努力找到自己的座位。

college-writing-001156.en: Here are some questions that Finley Woods might have asked while developing her essay.
college-writing-001156.zh: 以下是芬利·伍兹在撰写文章时可能提出的一些问题。

college-writing-001158.en: Why don’t I like to go

college-writing-001163.en: Could be any time—when a movie is popular, the
college-writing-001163.zh: 随时都可能——当一部电影很受欢迎时，

college-writing-001164.en: theater is too crowded; when traffic is bad, the trip
college-writing-001164.zh: 剧院人太多；交通不顺畅时，行程就难以进行

college-writing-001168.en: On the highway, in the parking lot, at the
college-writing-001168.zh: 在高速公路上，在停车场里，在

college-writing-001169.en: concession stand, in the theater itself.
college-writing-001169.zh: 在剧院内部设有特许经营权展台。

college-writing-001172.en: I do by wanting to eat too much.

college-writing-001175.en: The theater owners do by not

college-writing-001176.en: having enough parking space and showing too many
college-writing-001176.zh: 有足够的停车位，却展示出太多

college-writing-001180.en: I can stay home and stream movies.
college-writing-001180.zh: 我可以待在家里观看电影流媒体。

college-writing-001181.en: Asking questions can be an effective way of getting yourself to think about a topic from a number of different angles.
college-writing-001181.zh: 提问可以是一种有效的方法，能让你从多个不同角度思考某个主题。

college-writing-001182.en: The questions can really help you generate details about a topic.
college-writing-001182.zh: 这些问题确实可以帮助你获取关于某个主题的详细信息。

college-writing-001183.en: To get a sense of the questioning process, use a sheet of paper to ask yourself a series of questions about a good or bad experience that you have had recently.
college-writing-001183.zh: 为了了解提问过程，可以用一张纸来问自己一系列关于你最近所经历的好或坏经历的问题。

college-writing-001184.en: See how many details you can accumulate in ten minutes.
college-writing-001184.zh: 看看你能在十分钟内积累多少细节。

college-writing-001185.en: And remember again not to be concerned about mistakes, because you are just thinking on paper.
college-writing-001185.zh: 再次提醒，不要为错误而烦恼，因为你只是在纸上思考而已。

college-writing-001186.en: Technique 3: Making a List In making a list, also known as brainstorming, you collect ideas and details that relate to your subject.
college-writing-001186.zh: 技巧3：列出清单。在列出清单的过程中，也就是进行头脑风暴时，你会收集与主题相关的想法和细节。

college-writing-001187.en: Pile these items up, one after another, without trying to sort out major details from minor ones or trying to put the details in any special order.
college-writing-001187.zh: 将这些项目一个接一个地堆放在一起，不试图区分主要细节与次要细节，也不试图对细节进行任何特殊的排序。

college-writing-001188.en: Your goal is just to make a list of everything about your subject that occurs to you.
college-writing-001188.zh: 你的目标只是列出关于你的主题的所有想法。

college-writing-001191.en: Making a List: A Student Model

college-writing-001192.en: After Finley did her freewriting about moviegoing, she made up the following list of details.
college-writing-001192.zh: 在芬利完成关于观看电影的自由写作后，她列出了以下细节清单。

college-writing-001193.en: Traffic is bad between my house and theater
college-writing-001193.zh: 我家和剧院之间的交通状况很糟糕。

college-writing-001195.en: Don’t want to run into Jeremy
college-writing-001195.zh: 不想与杰里米发生冲突

college-writing-001196.en: Hard to be on a diet

college-writing-001198.en: I’m crowded into seats between strangers who push me off armrests
college-writing-001198.zh: 我被挤坐在陌生人之间，那些人把我的身体从扶手上推下去

college-writing-001200.en: Parking lot needs to be expanded

college-writing-001202.en: Can’t pause or fast-forward as you can when you stream
college-writing-001202.zh: 在观看流媒体时无法暂停或快进，就像在普通观看时那样。

college-writing-001205.en: Too many temptatons at snack stand

college-writing-001206.en: Commercials for food on the screen

college-writing-001207.en: Can prepare healthy snacks for myself at home
college-writing-001207.zh: 可以在家为自己准备健康的零食

college-writing-001210.en: Candy has always been my downfall
college-writing-001210.zh: 糖果一直是我失败的根源

college-writing-001211.en: People who’ve seen movie before talk along with actors and give away plot twists
college-writing-001211.zh: 之前看过这部电影的人会与演员互动，并透露剧情中的隐藏信息。

college-writing-001213.zh: 地板上有些令人不悦的东西

college-writing-001214.zh: 青少年大声喊叫、炫耀自己

college-writing-001215.en: One detail led to another as Finley expanded her list.
college-writing-001215.zh: 一个细节引出了另一个细节，于是芬利扩展了她的清单。

college-writing-001216.en: Slowly but surely, more details emerged, some of which she could use in developing her paper.
college-writing-001216.zh: 慢慢地但坚定地，更多细节逐渐显现出来，其中一些她可以在撰写论文时加以利用。

college-writing-001219.en: time she was done with her list, she was ready to plan an outline of her paragraph and then to write her first draft.
college-writing-001219.zh: 当她完成清单后，她便可以规划段落的框架，然后开始撰写初稿。

college-writing-001220.en: To get a sense of list-making, list on a sheet of paper a series of realistic goals, major or minor, that you would like to accomplish between today and one year from today.
college-writing-001220.zh: 为了感受一下列清单的感觉，请在纸上列出一系列现实的目标，无论大小，这些目标都是你希望在今天到一年后之间实现的目标。

college-writing-001221.en: Your goals can be personal, academic, or career-related.
college-writing-001221.zh: 你的目标可以是个人目标、学术目标或职业相关目标。

college-writing-001222.en: Technique 4: Clustering Clustering, also known as diagramming or mapping, is another strategy that can be used to generate material for an essay.
college-writing-001222.zh: 技巧4：聚类分析。聚类分析也被称为图表制作或映射，是另一种可用于撰写论文素材的方法。

college-writing-001223.en: This method is helpful for people who like to do their thinking in a visual way.
college-writing-001223.zh: 这种方法对于喜欢以视觉方式思考的人很有帮助。

college-writing-001224.en: In clustering, you use lines, boxes, arrows, and circles to show relationships among the ideas and details that occur to you.
college-writing-001224.zh: 在聚类分析中，你使用线条、框、箭头和圆圈来展示你所想到的各种想法和细节之间的关联。

college-writing-001225.en: Begin by stating your subject in a few words in the center of a blank sheet of paper.
college-writing-001225.zh: 首先在空白纸张中央用几句话简要说明你的主题。

college-writing-001226.en: Then, as ideas and details come to you, put them in boxes or circles around the subject and draw lines to connect them to each other and to the subject.
college-writing-001226.zh: 然后，当各种想法和细节浮现出来时，将它们放入框中或围绕主题画圈，并画线将它们与主题以及彼此相连。

college-writing-001227.en: Put minor ideas or details in smaller boxes or circles, and use connecting lines to show how they relate as well.
college-writing-001227.zh: 将较小的想法或细节用较小的方框或圆圈表示出来，并用连接线来说明它们之间的关联。

college-writing-001229.en: Keep in mind that there is no right or wrong way of clustering or diagramming.
college-writing-001229.zh: 请记住，对数据进行聚类或图表绘制没有绝对的对错之分。

college-writing-001230.en: It is a way to think on paper about how various ideas and details relate to one another.
college-writing-001230.zh: 这是一种在纸上思考各种想法与细节之间相互关联的方式。

college-writing-001231.en: Below is an example of what Finley might have done to develop her ideas.
college-writing-001231.zh: 以下便是芬利可能用于发展其想法的做法示例。

college-writing-001234.en: Use clustering (diagramming) to organize the list of year-ahead goals that you created for the previous activity (Activity 3).
college-writing-001234.zh: 使用聚类（图表化）来整理你在之前活动（活动3）中制定的未来一年目标清单。

college-writing-001235.en: Technique 5: Preparing a Scratch Outline A scratch outline, or informal outline, is an excellent sequel to the first four prewriting techniques.
college-writing-001235.zh: 技巧5：制作草图大纲。草图大纲或非正式大纲是前四种写作准备技巧的绝佳补充。

college-writing-001236.en: A scratch outline often follows freewriting, questioning, listmaking, or diagramming; or it may gradually emerge in the midst of these strategies.
college-writing-001236.zh: 草图轮廓通常源于自由写作、提问、列表或图表绘制；也可能在这些策略的过程中逐渐显现出来。

college-writing-001237.en: In fact, trying to make a scratch outline is a good way to see if you need to do more prewriting.
college-writing-001237.zh: 实际上，尝试制作一个粗略的提纲是一种很好的方法，可以让你知道是否还需要进行更多的预写作工作。

college-writing-001238.en: If you cannot come up with a solid outline, then you know you need to do more prewriting to clarify your main point or its several kinds of support.
college-writing-001238.zh: 如果你无法制定出清晰的提纲，那么你就知道需要进行更多的预写作工作，以明确你的主要观点或其各种支撑点。

college-writing-001239.en: In a scratch outline, you think carefully about the point you are making, the supporting items for that point, and the order in which you will arrange those items.
college-writing-001239.zh: 在草图阶段，你需要仔细思考你要表达的观点、支撑该观点的内容，以及这些内容的排列顺序。

college-writing-001240.en: The scratch outline is a plan or blueprint to help you achieve a unified, supported, well-organized essay.
college-writing-001240.zh: 写作大纲是一份计划或蓝图，有助于你撰写出结构清晰、逻辑连贯的文章。

college-writing-001242.en: As Finley was working on her list of details, she suddenly realized what the plan of her essay could be.
college-writing-001242.zh: 当芬利在整理她的细节清单时，她突然意识到这篇论文的构思可能是什么。

college-writing-001243.en: She could organize many of her details into one of three supporting groups: (1) annoyances in going out, (2) too many tempting snacks, and (3) other people.
college-writing-001243.zh: 她可以将许多细节分为三个类别：(1)外出时令人烦恼的事情；(2)太多吸引人的零食；(3)其他人。

college-writing-001244.en: She then went back to the list, crossed out items that she now saw did not fit, and numbered the items according to the group where they fit.
college-writing-001244.zh: 然后她重新查看列表，划掉那些现在看来不符合要求的项目，并根据它们适用的类别对项目进行编号。

college-writing-001245.en: Here is what Finley did with her list:
college-writing-001245.zh: 以下是芬利对她所写的清单所做的处理：

college-writing-001247.en: In addition to helping generate material, clustering can give you an early sense of how ideas and details relate to one another.
college-writing-001247.zh: 除了有助于生成材料外，聚类分析还能让你尽早了解各种想法与细节之间的关联。

college-writing-001248.en: For example, the cluster for Finley’s essay suggests that different kinds of noisy people could be the focus of one paragraph and that different kinds of temptations could be the focus of another paragraph.
college-writing-001248.zh: 例如，Finley的文章中的段落结构表明，不同类型的“吵闹人物”可以成为某一段落的重点，而不同类型的诱惑则可以是另一段落的重点。

college-writing-001250.en: 1 Traffic is bad between my house and the theater
college-writing-001250.zh: 我家与剧院之间的交通状况很糟糕。

college-writing-001252.en: Don’t want to run into Jeremy
college-writing-001252.zh: 不想与杰里米发生冲突

college-writing-001255.en: Under the list, Finley was now able to prepare her scratch outline:
college-writing-001255.zh: 根据这份清单，芬利现在能够准备她的草图大纲了：

college-writing-001256.en: 2 Hard to be on a diet

college-writing-001258.en: 3 I’m crowded into seats between strangers who push me off armrests
college-writing-001258.zh: 3 我被挤到了陌生人之间的座位上，那些人把我的身体从扶手上推下去

college-writing-001260.en: 1 Parking lot needs to be expanded

college-writing-001262.en: Can’t pause or fast-forward as you can when you stream
college-writing-001262.zh: 在观看流媒体时无法暂停或快进，就像在普通观看时那样。

college-writing-001265.en: 2 Too many temptations at snack stand

college-writing-001266.en: Commercials for food on the screen

college-writing-001267.en: 2 Can prepare healthy snacks for myself at home
college-writing-001267.zh: 2 可以在家为自己准备健康的零食

college-writing-001269.en: Candy has always been my downfall
college-writing-001269.zh: 糖果一直是我失败的根源

college-writing-001271.en: 3 People who’ve seen movie before talk along with actors and give away plot twists
college-writing-001271.zh: 3位之前看过这部电影的人与演员一起讨论，并透露剧情中的隐藏线索

college-writing-001273.zh: 地板上有些令人不悦的东西

college-writing-001280.en: After all her prewriting, Finley was pleased.
college-writing-001280.zh: 经过所有的预写工作后，芬利感到满意。

college-writing-001281.en: She knew that she had a promising essay─one with a clear point and solid support.
college-writing-001281.zh: 她知道自己有一篇有潜力的文章——一篇观点明确、论据扎实的文章。

college-writing-001282.en: She saw that she could organize the material into a strong essay consisting of an introduction, several supporting paragraphs, and a conclusion.
college-writing-001282.zh: 她意识到可以将这些材料整理成一篇结构严谨的文章，包括引言、几个支持性段落以及结论部分。

college-writing-001283.en: She was now ready to write the first draft of her essay, using her outline as a guide.
college-writing-001283.zh: 现在，她已经准备好以提纲为指导，撰写论文的初稿。

college-writing-001284.en: Chances are that if you do enough prewriting and thinking on paper, you will eventually discover the point and support of your essay.
college-writing-001284.zh: 如果你在纸上进行足够的预写作和思考，最终就能找到文章的要点和支撑点。

college-writing-001286.en: Create a scratch outline that could serve as a guide if you were to write an essay about your year-ahead goals.
college-writing-001286.zh: 创建一个简要大纲，作为你撰写关于未来一年目标的文章的参考。

college-writing-001288.en: When you write a first draft, be prepared to put in additional thoughts and details that did not emerge during prewriting.
college-writing-001288.zh: 在撰写初稿时，请准备好添加那些在预写作阶段没有出现的想法和细节。

college-writing-001289.en: And don’t worry if you hit a snag.
college-writing-001289.zh: 如果遇到困难，也别担心。

college-writing-001290.en: Just leave a blank space or add a comment such as “Do later” and press on to finish the essay.
college-writing-001290.zh: 只需留一个空白空格，或添加如“稍后做”这样的评论，然后继续完成文章。

college-writing-001291.en: Also, don’t worry yet about grammar, punctuation, or spelling.
college-writing-001291.zh: 另外，现在不必担心语法、标点或拼写问题。

college-writing-001292.en: You don’t want to take time correcting words or sentences that you may decide to remove later.
college-writing-001292.zh: 你不想花费时间修正那些你之后可能决定删除的单词或句子。

college-writing-001293.en: Instead, make it your goal to state your thesis clearly and develop the content of your essay with plenty of specific details.
college-writing-001293.zh: 相反，你应该将明确陈述论点作为目标，并通过大量具体的细节来展开文章内容。

college-writing-001294.en: Writing a First Draft: A Student Model Here is Finley’s first draft:
college-writing-001294.zh: 撰写初稿：学生模型。这是芬利的首个初稿：

college-writing-001296.en: Even though I love movies, my friends have stopped asking me to go.
college-writing-001296.zh: 虽然我喜欢看电影，但我的朋友们不再邀请我去了。

college-writing-001297.en: There are just too many problems involved in going to the movies.
college-writing-001297.zh: 去看电影涉及的问题太多了。

college-writing-001298.en: There are no small theaters anymore, I have to drive fifteen minutes to a big multaplex.
college-writing-001298.zh: 现在没有小影院了，我得开车十五分钟去大影城。

college-writing-001299.en: Because of a supermarket and restarants, the parking lot is filled.
college-writing-001299.zh: 由于有超市和餐馆，停车场被占满了。

college-writing-001300.en: I have to keep driving around to find a space.
college-writing-001300.zh: 我得继续开车寻找一个空位。

college-writing-001301.en: Then I have to stand in a long line.

college-writing-001302.en: Waiting to get my tickets scanned.
college-writing-001302.zh: 正在等待我的门票被扫描完成。

college-writing-001303.en: Finally, I have to pay too much money for a ticket.
college-writing-001303.zh: 最后，我不得不支付过高的票价。

college-writing-001304.en: Putting out that much money, I should not have to deal with a floor that is sticky seems coated with rubber cement.
college-writing-001304.zh: 投入那么多资金，我本不应面对那种像被橡胶胶水覆盖的黏糊糊的地面。

college-writing-001305.en: By the end of a movie, my shoes are often sealed to a mix of spilled soda, bubble gum, and other stuff.
college-writing-001305.zh: 电影结束时，我的鞋子上往往沾满了洒出的汽水、泡泡糖以及其他污物。

college-writing-001308.en: The theater offers temptations in the form of snacks I really don’t need.
college-writing-001308.zh: 剧院以我真正不需要的零食形式提供诱惑。

college-writing-001309.en: Like most of us I have to worry about weight gain.
college-writing-001309.zh: 和大多数人一样，我必须担心体重增加的问题。

college-writing-001310.en: At home I do pretty well by simply watching what I keep in the house and not buying stuff that is bad for me. I can make do with healthy snacks because there is nothing in the house.
college-writing-001310.zh: 在家时，我只要留意家里有什么东西，不购买对身体有害的东西，就能过得不错。因为家里没有东西，我也能用健康的零食来充饥。

college-writing-001311.en: Going to the theater is like spending my evening in a market 7-Eleven that’s been equiped with a movie screen and there are seats which are comfortable.
college-writing-001311.zh: 去电影院就像是在一个配备了电影屏幕且座位舒适的7-Eleven商店里度过夜晚。

college-writing-001312.en: I try to persuade myself to just have a sparkling water.
college-writing-001312.zh: 我试图说服自己只喝一杯气泡水。

college-writing-001313.en: The smell of popcorn soon overcomes me.
college-writing-001313.zh: 爆米花的气味很快便让我难以忍受。

college-writing-001314.en: My friends are as tempted as I am.
college-writing-001314.zh: 我的朋友们和我一样受到诱惑。

college-writing-001315.en: Choclate bars seem to jump into your hands, I am eating enormous mouthfuls of milk duds.
college-writing-001315.zh: 巧克力棒仿佛会跳进你的手中，我大口大口地吃着牛奶食品。

college-writing-001316.en: By the time I leave the theater I feel sick.
college-writing-001316.zh: 当我离开剧院时，我感到恶心。

college-writing-001317.en: Some of the other moviegoers are the worst problem.
college-writing-001317.zh: 其他一些观众则是最大的麻烦。

college-writing-001318.en: There are teenagers who try to impress their friends in one way or another.
college-writing-001318.zh: 有些青少年试图以各种方式给朋友留下深刻印象。

college-writing-001319.en: Little kids race up and down the aisles, gigling and laughing.
college-writing-001319.zh: 小孩子们在过道上来回奔跑，咯咯笑着。

college-writing-001320.en: Adults act as if they’re watching the movie at home.
college-writing-001320.zh: 成年人表现得就像在家看电影一样。

college-writing-001321.en: They talk loudly about the ages of the stars and give away the plot.
college-writing-001321.zh: 他们大声谈论恒星的年龄，并透露了剧情。

college-writing-001322.en: Other people are droping popcorn tubs or cups of soda crushed ice and soda on the floor.
college-writing-001322.zh: 其他人则把爆米花罐、苏打水碎冰和苏打水倒在地上。

college-writing-001323.en: Also coughing a lot and doing other stuff—bms!
college-writing-001323.zh: 还经常咳嗽，还会做其他事情——BMS！

college-writing-001324.en: I decided one night that I was not going to be a moviegoer anymore.
college-writing-001324.zh: 某天晚上，我决定再也不去看电影了。

college-writing-001325.en: I joined Netflix, and I’ll watch movies comfortable in my own living room.
college-writing-001325.zh: 我加入了 Netflix，以后会在自己的客厅里舒适地观看电影。

college-writing-001326.en: After Finley finished the first draft, she was able to put it aside until the next day.
college-writing-001326.zh: 芬利完成初稿后，便将其放在一边，直到第二天再处理。

college-writing-001327.en: You will benefit as well if you can allow some time between finishing a draft and starting to revise.
college-writing-001327.zh: 如果你能在完成初稿和开始修改之间留出一些时间，你也会从中受益。

college-writing-001329.en: Team up with someone in your class and see if you can fill in the missing words in the following explanation of Finley’s first draft.
college-writing-001329.zh: 与班级中的某个人组队，看看能否补全以下对芬利初稿的解析中缺失的单词。

college-writing-001330.en: 1. Finley has a very brief introduction─no more than an opening sentence and a second sentence that states the .
college-writing-001330.zh: 1. 芬利的描述非常简短——不超过两句话：第一句作为开头，第二句则说明了内容。

college-writing-001331.en: She knows she can develop the introduction more fully in a later draft.
college-writing-001331.zh: 她知道可以在后续的草稿中更全面地完善这一介绍部分。

college-writing-001332.en: 2. Of Finley’s three supporting paragraphs, only the paragraph lacks a topic sentence.
college-writing-001332.zh: 2. 在芬利的三个支持段落中，只有其中一个没有主题句。

college-writing-001333.en: She realizes that this is something to work on in the next draft.
college-writing-001333.zh: 她意识到这是下一个版本中需要改进的地方。

college-writing-001335.en: Finley doesn’t worry about spelling at this point.
college-writing-001335.zh: 目前，芬利并不在意拼写问题。

college-writing-001336.en: She just wants to get down as much of the substance of her paper as possible.
college-writing-001336.zh: 她只是希望尽可能抓住论文的核心内容。

college-writing-001341.en: 4. There are various punctuation errors, such as the run-on sentences in the paragraphs.
college-writing-001341.zh: 4. 文中有多种标点错误，例如段落里的粘连句。

college-writing-001342.en: Again, Finley is focusing on content; she knows she can attend to punctuation and grammar later.
college-writing-001342.zh: 同样，芬利专注于内容方面；她知道之后可以处理标点符号和语法问题。

college-writing-001343.en: 5. At several points in the essay, Finley revises on the spot to make images more : she changes “is sticky” to “seems coated with rubber cement,” “market” to “7-Eleven,” and “cups of soda” to “cups of crushed ice and soda.”
college-writing-001343.zh: 在文章的几个段落中，芬利当场进行了修改，使描述更清晰：她将“很黏”改为“似乎被橡胶胶水覆盖着”，将“市场”改为“7-Eleven”，将“杯装苏打水”改为“杯装碎冰和苏打水”。

college-writing-001344.en: 6. Near the end of her essay, Finley can’t think of added details to insert, so she simply puts the letters “ ” at that point to remind herself to “be more specific” in the next draft.
college-writing-001344.zh: 6. 在文章结尾处，芬利想不出还能添加哪些细节，于是就在那个位置加上了“ ”这样的符号，以提醒自己在下一稿中“更具体地描述”。

college-writing-001345.en: She then goes on to finish her first draft.
college-writing-001345.zh: 然后，她完成了她的初稿。

college-writing-001346.en: 7. Her is as brief as her introduction.

college-writing-001347.en: Finley knows she can round off her essay more fully during revision.
college-writing-001347.zh: 芬利知道在修改阶段她可以更全面地完善她的文章。

college-writing-001349.en: Revising is as much a stage in the writing process as prewriting, outlining, and doing the first draft.
college-writing-001349.zh: 修改同样是写作过程中的一个阶段，与预写、列提纲和撰写初稿一样重要。

college-writing-001350.en: Revising means rewriting an essay, building on what has already been done, to make it stronger.
college-writing-001350.zh: 修订意味着重写文章，在已有成果的基础上加以改进，以使其更完善。

college-writing-001351.en: One writer has said about revision, “It’s like cleaning house─getting rid of all the junk and putting things in the right order.”
college-writing-001351.zh: 一位作家关于修订评论道：“这就像打扫房子——清除所有垃圾，把东西按正确的顺序排列。”

college-writing-001352.en: But it is not just “straightening up”; instead, you must be ready to roll up your sleeves and do whatever is needed to create an effective essay.
college-writing-001352.zh: 但这不仅仅是“整理整齐”的问题；相反，你必须准备好全力以赴，采取一切必要措施来写出一篇有效的文章。

college-writing-001353.en: Too many students think that the first draft is the essay.
college-writing-001353.zh: 太多学生认为初稿就是文章。

college-writing-001354.en: They start to become writers when they realize that revising a rough draft three or four times is often at the heart of the writing process.
college-writing-001354.zh: 当他们意识到修改三到四份初稿往往是写作过程的核心环节时，他们便开始成为作家。

college-writing-001355.en: Here are some quick hints that can help make revision easier.
college-writing-001355.zh: 以下是一些有助于简化修改的实用提示。

college-writing-001356.en: First, set your first draft aside for a while.
college-writing-001356.zh: 首先，先把初稿搁置一段时间。

college-writing-001357.en: A few hours will do, but a day or two would be better.
college-writing-001357.zh: 几个小时即可，但一两天会更好。

college-writing-001358.en: You can then come back to the draft with a fresh, more objective point of view.
college-writing-001358.zh: 然后，你可以以更新颖、更客观的观点来重新审视这份草案。

college-writing-001359.en: Second, work from typed or printed text.
college-writing-001359.zh: 其次，从打印或手写的文本中进行工作。

college-writing-001360.en: You’ll be able to see the essay more impartially in this way than if you were just looking at your own familiar handwriting.
college-writing-001360.zh: 通过这种方式，你能够更公正地看待这篇文章，而不只是看到自己熟悉的笔迹。

college-writing-001361.zh: 接下来，大声朗读你的草稿。

college-writing-001362.en: Hearing how your writing sounds will help you pick up problems with meaning as well as with style.
college-writing-001362.zh: 听听你的写作听起来如何，有助于你发现语义和风格上的问题。

college-writing-001363.en: Finally, as you do all these things, add your thoughts and changes above the lines or in the margins of your essay.
college-writing-001363.zh: 最后，在完成所有这些工作后，在文章的横线或边注处添加你的想法与修改内容。

college-writing-001364.en: Your written comments can serve as a guide when you work on the next draft.
college-writing-001364.zh: 您的书面评论可以作为您撰写下一稿时的参考。

college-writing-001365.en: There are two stages to the revising process:
college-writing-001365.zh: 修订过程分为两个阶段：

college-writing-001369.en: Revising Content To revise the content of your essay, ask these questions:
college-writing-001369.zh: 修改内容：若需修改论文的内容，请提出以下问题：

college-writing-001370.zh: 1. 我的文章结构是否统一？

college-writing-001371.en: • Do I have a thesis that is clearly stated or implied in the introductory paragraph of my essay?
college-writing-001371.zh: • 我的论文引言段落中是否明确或隐含了我的论点？

college-writing-001372.en: • Do all my supporting paragraphs truly support and back up my thesis?
college-writing-001372.zh: • 所有的支持性段落是否真正支持并支撑了我的论点？

college-writing-001373.zh: 2. 我的文章有支撑依据吗？

college-writing-001374.en: • Are there three separate supporting points for the thesis?
college-writing-001374.zh: • 该论点是否有三个独立的支撑点？

college-writing-001375.en: • Do I have specific evidence for each of the three supporting points?
college-writing-001375.zh: • 对于这三个支撑论点，我有具体的证据吗？

college-writing-001376.en: • Is there plenty of specific evidence for each supporting point?
college-writing-001376.zh: • 每个支持观点是否有足够的具体证据？

college-writing-001378.en: • Do I have an interesting introduction, a solid conclusion, and an accurate title?
college-writing-001378.zh: • 我的引言有趣吗？结论扎实吗？标题准确吗？

college-writing-001379.en: • Do I have a clear method of organizing my essay?
college-writing-001379.zh: • 我是否有一种清晰的文章组织方法？

college-writing-001380.en: • Do I use transitions and other connecting words?
college-writing-001380.zh: • 我会使用过渡词和其他连接词吗？

college-writing-001381.en: Chapters 3 and 4 will give you practice in achieving unity, support, and organization in your writing.
college-writing-001381.zh: 第3章和第4章将帮助你练习如何在写作中实现团结、支持与组织性。

college-writing-001382.en: Revising Sentences To revise sentences in your essay, ask yourself the following questions:
college-writing-001382.zh: 修改句子 要修改文章中的句子，请思考以下问题：

college-writing-001383.en: 1. Do I use parallelism to balance my words and ideas?
college-writing-001383.zh: 1. 我是否使用平行结构来平衡我的文字与观点？

college-writing-001384.en: 2. Do I have a consistent point of view?
college-writing-001384.zh: 2. 我是否持有一致的观点？

college-writing-001385.zh: 3. 我使用了特定的词汇吗？

college-writing-001386.zh: 4. 我使用主动语态的动词吗？

college-writing-001387.en: 5. Do I use words effectively by avoiding slang, clichés, pretentious lan-
college-writing-001387.zh: 5. 我是否通过避免俚语、陈词滥调和矫饰性的表达，有效地运用语言呢？

college-writing-001388.zh: 语言，以及词汇的丰富性？

college-writing-001389.zh: 6. 我会改变我的句子结构吗？

college-writing-001390.en: Chapter 5 will give you practice in revising sentences.
college-writing-001390.zh: 第5章将让你练习修改句子。

college-writing-001393.en: After you have revised your essay for content and style, you are ready to edit─ check for and correct─errors in grammar, punctuation, capitalization, sentence structure, word usage, and spelling.
college-writing-001393.zh: 在对文章的内容与风格进行修改后，就可以开始编辑了——检查并修正语法、标点、大小写、句子结构、词汇使用及拼写方面的错误。

college-writing-001394.en: Students often find it hard to edit their writing carefully.
college-writing-001394.zh: 学生往往难以仔细地修改他们的写作。

college-writing-001395.en: They have put so much, or so little, work into their writing that it’s almost painful for them to look at the essay one more time.
college-writing-001395.zh: 他们在写作中投入了太多或太少的精力，以至于再次查看这篇文章对他们来说几乎是一种痛苦。

college-writing-001396.en: You may simply have to will yourself to perform this important closing step in the writing process.
college-writing-001396.zh: 你只需强迫自己完成写作过程中这一重要的收尾步骤。

college-writing-001397.en: Remember that eliminating sentence-skill mistakes will improve an average essay and help ensure a strong grade on a good essay.
college-writing-001397.zh: 记住，消除句子表达上的错误能够提升文章的整体质量，也有助于确保优秀文章获得高分。

college-writing-001398.en: Further, as you get into the habit of checking your writing, you will also get into the habit of using the sentence skills consistently.
college-writing-001398.zh: 此外，当你养成检查自己写作的习惯后，也会逐渐养成始终运用各种句子技巧的习惯。

college-writing-001399.en: They are an integral part of clear and effective writing.
college-writing-001399.zh: 它们是清晰、有效的写作不可或缺的一部分。

college-writing-001400.en: Once you have completed your editing, you should always double-check everything by proofreading what you have written.
college-writing-001400.zh: 完成编辑后，请务必通过校对所写内容来再次检查所有内容是否无误。

college-writing-001401.en: During proofreading you look out for small errors like typos and spacing issues.
college-writing-001401.zh: 在校对过程中，要注意检查诸如拼写错误和间距问题这类小错误。

college-writing-001402.en: Proofreading focuses on correcting careless mistakes rather than on the essay’s contents.
college-writing-001402.zh: 校对的重点是纠正粗心的错误，而非文章的内容。

college-writing-001403.en: Chapter 5 and Part 4 of this book will serve as a guide while you are editing your essay for mistakes in sentence skills.
college-writing-001403.zh: 本书的第5章和第4部分将作为指导，帮助你在修改文章时纠正句子表达上的错误。

college-writing-001404.en: An Illustration of the Revising and Editing Processes Revising with a Second Draft: A Student Model
college-writing-001404.zh: 修订与编辑过程的示例：通过第二稿进行修订：以学生为例

college-writing-001486.en: Once again, Finley makes her changes in longhand right on the printout of her essay.
