college-writing-003596.zh: 中产阶级劳动者在存钱或为应急储备资金方面面临巨大困难。

college-writing-003597.en: 7. We thought the television program that was on last night was enjoyable,
college-writing-003597.zh: 7. 我们认为昨晚的电视节目很有趣。

college-writing-003598.en: whereas our parents reacted with dislike to the content of the show.
college-writing-003598.zh: 而我们的父母对该节目的内容表示不满。

college-writing-003599.en: 8. Because of the bad weather, the school district felt it would be safer to cancel
college-writing-003599.zh: 8. 由于天气恶劣，学区认为取消课程更为安全。

college-writing-003600.en: classes and let everyone stay home than to risk people having accidents on the way to school.
college-writing-003600.zh: 让同学们待在家里，这样就不必担心他们在去学校的路上发生意外了。

college-writing-003601.en: 9. Out of all the regrets in my life so far, one of my greatest ones to the present
college-writing-003601.zh: 9. 在我人生中所有的遗憾中，目前最让我痛心的那一个……

college-writing-003602.en: time is that I did not take additional art classes when I was still in high school and had a chance to do so.
college-writing-003602.zh: 问题是，我在高中时没有选修额外的艺术课程，后来才有机会这么做。

college-writing-003603.en: 10. It seems obvious to me, and it should be to everyone else, too, that people can be harmed as much by emotional abuse as by physical abuse, even if no one lays a hand on them.
college-writing-003603.zh: 10. 在我看来，对其他人来说也是如此，人们可能受到情感虐待的伤害程度与身体虐待的伤害程度相当，即使没有人真的动手伤害他们。

college-writing-003604.en: Chapter 5 The Fourth Step in Essay Writing 129
college-writing-003604.zh: 第五章 写作的第四步 129

college-writing-003605.en: Vary Your Sentences One part of effective writing is to vary the kinds of sentences you write.
college-writing-003605.zh: 变换句子结构 有效写作的一个要点就是变换所写的句子类型。

college-writing-003606.en: If every sentence follows the same pattern, writing may become monotonous to read.
college-writing-003606.zh: 如果每个句子都遵循相同的模式，写作就会显得单调乏味。

college-writing-003607.en: This section explains four ways you can create variety and interest in your writing style.
college-writing-003607.zh: 本节介绍了四种能够让你的写作风格更具多样性与吸引力的方法。

college-writing-003608.en: It also describes coordination and subordination─two important techniques for achieving different kinds of emphasis in writing.
college-writing-003608.zh: 它还描述了协调与从属关系——实现不同写作强调效果的两个重要技巧。

college-writing-003609.en: The following are four methods you can use to revise simple sentences, making them more complex and sophisticated:
college-writing-003609.zh: 以下是四种可以用来修改简单句子、使其更加复杂和精妙的方法：

college-writing-003610.zh: • 添加第二个完整的想法（协调）。

college-writing-003611.zh: • 添加一个从属思想（隶属关系）。

college-writing-003612.en: • Begin with a special opening word or phrase.
college-writing-003612.zh: • 以一个特别的开头词或短语开始。

college-writing-003613.en: • Place adjectives or verbs in a series.
college-writing-003613.zh: • 将形容词或动词按顺序排列。

college-writing-003614.en: Revise by Adding a Second Complete Thought
college-writing-003614.zh: 通过添加第二个完整想法来修订

college-writing-003615.en: When you add a second complete thought to a simple sentence, the result is a compound (or double) sentence.
college-writing-003615.zh: 当在简单的句子中加入第二个完整的想法时，就形成了复合（或双重）句子。

college-writing-003616.en: The two complete statements in a compound sentence are usually connected by a comma and a joining or coordinating word (and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet).
college-writing-003616.zh: 复合句中的两个完整陈述句通常通过逗号以及连接或并列词（and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet）连接在一起。

college-writing-003617.en: A compound sentence is used to give equal weight to two closely related ideas.
college-writing-003617.zh: 复合句用于让两个紧密相关的概念具有同等重要性。

college-writing-003618.en: The technique of showing that ideas have equal importance is called coordination.
college-writing-003618.zh: 展示各种观点具有同等重要性的方法被称为协调。

college-writing-003620.en: In each case, the sentence contains two ideas that the writer considers equal in importance.
college-writing-003620.zh: 在每一个案例中，句子都包含两个作者认为同等重要的观点。

college-writing-003621.en: Anderius worked on the engine for three hours, but the car still wouldn’t start.
college-writing-003621.zh: 安德里乌斯花了三个小时研究发动机，但汽车仍然无法启动。

college-writing-003622.en: Bananas were on sale this week, so I bought a bunch for the children’s lunches.
college-writing-003622.zh: 本周香蕉有优惠活动，所以我买了一些作为孩子们的午餐食物。

college-writing-003623.en: We laced up our ice skates, and then we moved cautiously onto the rink.
college-writing-003623.zh: 我们穿上冰鞋，然后小心翼翼地走向冰面。

college-writing-003624.en: Combine the following pairs of simple sentences into compound sentences.
college-writing-003624.zh: 将以下简单的句子对合并为复合句。

college-writing-003625.en: Use a comma and a logical joining word (and, but, for, so) to connect each pair of statements.
college-writing-003625.zh: 使用逗号以及合理的连接词（and, but, for, so）来连接每对陈述。

college-writing-003627.en: HINT If you are not sure what and, but, for, and so mean, check Chapter 23.
college-writing-003627.zh: 提示：如果您不确定“what”、“but”、“for”等词的含义，请查看第23章。

college-writing-003628.en: example The weather was cold and windy.

college-writing-003629.en: Remy brought a thick blanket to the football game.
college-writing-003629.zh: 雷米带了一块厚毯子去参加足球比赛。

college-writing-003630.en: The weather was cold and windy, so Remy brought a thick blanket to the football game.
college-writing-003630.zh: 天气寒冷且风大，因此雷米带了一块厚毯子去参加足球比赛。

college-writing-003631.zh: 130 第一部分 论文写作

college-writing-003632.en: 1. My son can’t eat peanut butter snacks or sandwiches.
college-writing-003632.zh: 我的儿子无法吃花生酱零食或三明治。

college-writing-003635.en: The thought of tomorrow’s math exam kept me awake.
college-writing-003635.zh: 明天数学考试的念头让我无法入睡。

college-writing-003636.en: 3. The poet Ezra Pound left America in 1908.
college-writing-003636.zh: 3. 诗人埃兹拉·庞德于1908年离开了美国。

college-writing-003637.en: He was dissatisfied with the artistic climate of his native country.
college-writing-003637.zh: 他对祖国的艺术氛围感到不满。

college-writing-003638.en: 4. My philosophy professor believes that every student can learn.
college-writing-003638.zh: 4. 我的哲学教授认为每个学生都能学习。

college-writing-003639.en: He spends much of his extra time tutoring his students.
college-writing-003639.zh: 他把多余的时间都用于辅导学生。

college-writing-003640.en: 5. I didn’t have enough money to buy my parents an anniversary present.
college-writing-003640.zh: 5. 我没有足够的钱给父母买周年纪念礼物。

college-writing-003641.en: I offered to mow their lawn for the whole summer.
college-writing-003641.zh: 我提出愿意整个夏天为他们修剪草坪。

college-writing-003642.en: Revise by Adding a Dependent Thought When you add a dependent thought to a simple sentence, the result is a complex sentence.
college-writing-003642.zh: 通过添加从属思想进行修改：当在简单句子中加入从属思想时，就会形成复杂的句子。

college-writing-003643.en: * A dependent thought begins with one of the subordinating words listed in the box on the next page.
college-writing-003643.zh: * 一个依赖性的想法以下一页方框中列出的一个从属词作为起点。

college-writing-003644.en: *The two parts of a complex sentence are sometimes called an independent clause and a dependent clause.
college-writing-003644.zh: 复杂句子中的两个部分有时被称为独立分句和从属分句。

college-writing-003645.en: A clause is simply a word group that contains a subject and a verb.
college-writing-003645.zh: 条款本质上就是一个包含主语和动词的词语组。

college-writing-003646.en: An independent clause expresses a complete thought and can stand alone.
college-writing-003646.zh: 独立分句能够表达完整的思想，可以独立存在。

college-writing-003647.en: A dependent clause does not express a complete thought in itself and depends on the independent clause to complete its meaning.
college-writing-003647.zh: 从属分句本身表达不了完整的意思，要依靠独立分句补足句意。

college-writing-003648.en: Dependent clauses always begin with a dependent or subordinating word.
college-writing-003648.zh: 从属分句总是以引导从属关系的词开头。

college-writing-003649.en: Chapter 5 The Fourth Step in Essay Writing 131
college-writing-003649.zh: 第五章 写作的第四步 131

college-writing-003650.en: A complex sentence is used to emphasize one idea over another.
college-writing-003650.zh: 复合句用于强调其中一个概念，以突出另一个概念。

college-writing-003651.en: Look at the following complex sentence:

college-writing-003652.en: Although the exam room was very quiet, I still couldn’t concentrate.
college-writing-003652.zh: 虽然考场非常安静，但我还是无法集中注意力。

college-writing-003653.en: The idea that the writer wishes to emphasize here─I still couldn’t concentrate─is expressed as a complete thought.
college-writing-003653.zh: 作者想要在此强调的观点——我仍然无法集中注意力——被表达为一个完整的思想。

college-writing-003654.en: The less important idea─Although the exam room was very quiet─is subordinated to the complete thought.
college-writing-003654.zh: 不那么重要的想法——虽然考场很安静——从属于完整的想法。

college-writing-003655.en: The technique of giving one idea less emphasis than another is called subordination.
college-writing-003655.zh: 对某个观点给予较少重视的技巧被称为“从属关系”。

college-writing-003656.en: Following are other examples of complex sentences.
college-writing-003656.zh: 以下是其他复杂句子的例子。

college-writing-003657.en: In each case, the part starting with the dependent word is the less emphasized part of the sentence.
college-writing-003657.zh: 在每种情况下，以依赖单词开头的部分是句子中不太强调的部分。

college-writing-003658.en: Even though I was tired, I stayed up to watch the horror movie.
college-writing-003658.zh: 尽管很累，我还是熬夜看了那部恐怖电影。

college-writing-003659.en: Before I take a bath, I check for spiders in the tub.
college-writing-003659.zh: 洗澡前，我会检查浴缸里是否有蜘蛛。

college-writing-003660.en: When Ivy feels nervous, she pulls on her earlobe.
college-writing-003660.zh: 当艾薇感到紧张时，她会拉着她的耳垂。

college-writing-003661.en: Use logical subordinating words to combine the following pairs of simple sentences into sentences that contain a dependent thought.
college-writing-003661.zh: 使用逻辑从属词将以下成对的简单句子组合成包含依赖思想的句子。

college-writing-003662.en: Place a comma after a dependent statement when it starts the sentence.
college-writing-003662.zh: 开始句子时，在依赖语句后放置逗号。

college-writing-003663.en: example Rita bit into the hard taffy.
college-writing-003663.zh: 示例 rita 咬住了硬太妃糖。

college-writing-003665.en: 1. Many Americans blamed President Herbert Hoover for the Great Depression,
college-writing-003665.zh: 1. 许多美国人将大萧条归咎于赫伯特·胡佛总统，

college-writing-003667.en: They elected Franklin Roosevelt president in 1932.
college-writing-003667.zh: 1932年，他们当选富兰克林·罗斯福总统。

college-writing-003669.en: When Rita bit into the hard taffy, she broke a filling.
college-writing-003669.zh: 当丽塔咬着硬太妃糖时，她打破了一个馅料。

college-writing-003671.en: after if, even if when, whenever although, though in order that where, wherever as since whether because that, so that which, whichever before unless while even though until who how what, whatever whose
college-writing-003671.zh: after：在……之后；if：如果；even if：即使；when：当……时；whenever：每当／无论何时；although：尽管；though：虽然；in order that：为了使；where：在……的地方；wherever：无论在哪里；as：当……时／因为；since：自从／因为；whether：是否；because：因为；that：引出从句的连接词；so that：以便／以致；which：哪一个／所指的事物；whichever：无论哪一个；before：在……之前；unless：除非；while：当……时／而；even though：即使／尽管；until：直到；who：谁／引导指人的从句；how：如何；what：什么／……的事物；whatever：无论什么；whose：谁的。

college-writing-003673.en: 2. The bear turned over the rotten log.

college-writing-003674.en: Fat white grubs crawled in every direction.
college-writing-003674.zh: 胖白的蛴螬向各个方向爬行。

college-writing-003675.en: 3. Europe had suffered a great deal of damage during World War II.
college-writing-003675.zh: 3. 欧洲在二战期间遭受了很大的破坏。

college-writing-003676.en: The United States helped rebuild its infrastructure and economy.
college-writing-003676.zh: 美国帮助重建了其基础设施和经济。

college-writing-003677.en: 4. Some people are allergic to wool.

college-writing-003678.en: They buy sweaters made only from synthetic fibers.
college-writing-003678.zh: 他们购买仅由合成纤维制成的毛衣。

college-writing-003679.en: 5. A woman I know can type almost one hundred words a minute.
college-writing-003679.zh: 5. 我认识的一个女人每分钟可以打出近一百个单词。

college-writing-003680.en: She is having trouble landing a job.
college-writing-003680.zh: 她在找工作时遇到了困难。

college-writing-003681.en: Revise by Beginning with a Special Opening Word or Phrase
college-writing-003681.zh: 从特殊的开头词或短语开始修改

college-writing-003682.en: Among the special openers that can be used to start sentences are -ed words, -ing words, -ly words, to word groups, and prepositional phrases.
college-writing-003682.zh: 可用于开始句子的特殊开头包括 -ed 单词、-ing 单词、-ly 单词、单词组和介词短语。

college-writing-003683.en: Additional information can be found in Chapters 21, 22, and 26.
college-writing-003683.zh: 其他信息可以在第 21、22 和 26 章中找到。

college-writing-003684.en: Here are examples of all five kinds of openers:
college-writing-003684.zh: 以下是所有五种开瓶器的示例：

college-writing-003685.en: -ed WORD Concerned about his son’s fever, Paulo called a doctor.
college-writing-003685.zh: - 担心他儿子发烧的消息，保罗打电话给医生。

college-writing-003686.en: -ing WORD Humming softly, the woman browsed through the rack of dresses.
college-writing-003686.zh: - 女人轻轻地哼着字，浏览着连衣裙的架子。

college-writing-003687.en: -ly WORD Hurriedly, Sue approached the instructor’s desk.
college-writing-003687.zh: - 苏急忙说道，苏走近教官的办公桌。

college-writing-003688.en: Chapter 5 The Fourth Step in Essay Writing 133
college-writing-003688.zh: 第5章 论文写作的第四步 133

college-writing-003689.en: to WORD GROUP To protect their hair, Alex uses the lowest setting on their blow dryer.
college-writing-003689.zh: 为了保护他们的头发，亚历克斯使用了他们吹风机上的最低设置。

college-writing-003690.en: PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE During the exam, drops of water fell from the ceiling.
college-writing-003690.zh: 介词短语 在考试中，水滴从天花板上掉下来。

college-writing-003691.en: Combine each of the following pairs of simple sentences into one sentence by using the opener shown at the left and omitting repeated words.
college-writing-003691.zh: 使用左侧显示的开头器并省略重复的单词，将以下每对简单句子组合成一个句子。

college-writing-003692.en: Use a comma to set off the opener from the rest of the sentence.
college-writing-003692.zh: 使用逗号从句子的其余部分引出开启器。

college-writing-003693.en: example -ing word The pelican scooped small fish into its baggy bill.
college-writing-003693.zh: 示例 - 鹈鹕将小鱼舀入其宽松的钞票中。

college-writing-003698.en: 2. Eva and Olaf wanted to find the shortest route over the mountain.
college-writing-003698.zh: 2. Eva 和 Olaf 想找到上过山的最短路线。

college-writing-003699.en: They bought a map of the local hiking trails.
college-writing-003699.zh: 他们买了一张当地远足径的地图。

college-writing-003700.en: 3. The accused murderer grinned at the witnesses.
college-writing-003700.zh: 3. 被指控的凶手对证人咧嘴一笑。

college-writing-003701.en: He did this during the trial.
college-writing-003701.zh: 他在审判期间这样做了。

college-writing-003702.en: 4. The vet’s office was noisy and confusing.
college-writing-003702.zh: 4. 兽医办公室嘈杂且令人困惑。

college-writing-003703.en: It was crowded with nervous pets.

college-writing-003704.en: 5. Barry tried to find something worth watching.
college-writing-003704.zh: 5. 巴里试图找到值得一看的东西。

college-writing-003705.en: He flipped from channel to channel.
college-writing-003705.zh: 他从一个通道到另一个通道。

college-writing-003707.en: Dipping into the waves, the pelican scooped small fish into its baggy bill.
college-writing-003707.zh: 沉浸在海浪中，鹈鹕把小鱼舀进它宽松的钞票里。

college-writing-003714.en: Revise by Placing Adjectives or Verbs in a Series Various parts of a sentence may be placed in a series.
college-writing-003714.zh: 通过在一个系列中放置形容词或动词进行修改 句子的各个部分可以放在一个系列中。

college-writing-003715.en: Among these parts are adjectives (descriptive words) and verbs.
college-writing-003715.zh: 这些部分中有形容词（描述性词）和动词。

college-writing-003716.en: (Additional information can be found in Chapter 29.)
college-writing-003716.zh: （其他信息可以在第 29 章中找到。）

college-writing-003717.en: Here are examples of both in a series:
college-writing-003717.zh: 以下是一个系列中的两个示例：

college-writing-003718.en: ADJECTIVES I gently applied a sticky new Band-Aid to the deep, ragged cut on my finger.
college-writing-003718.zh: 形容词我轻轻地在我的手指上涂上了一个粘稠的新创可贴。

college-writing-003719.en: VERBS The truck bounced off a guardrail, sideswiped a tree, and plunged down the embankment.
college-writing-003719.zh: 动词 卡车从护栏上弹起，侧扫一棵树，然后冲下路堤。

college-writing-003720.en: Combine the simple sentences into one sentence by using adjectives or verbs in a series and by omitting repeated words.
college-writing-003720.zh: 通过在一个系列中使用形容词或动词并省略重复的单词，将简单的句子组合成一个句子。

college-writing-003721.en: Use a comma when necessary between adjectives or verbs in a series.

college-writing-003751.en: After revising sentences in a paper so that they flow smoothly and clearly, you need to edit the paper for mistakes in grammar, punctuation, mechanics, usage, and spelling.
college-writing-003751.zh: 在修改了论文中的句子以使它们流畅而清晰地进行后，您需要编辑论文以查找语法、标点符号、机制、用法和拼写方面的错误。

college-writing-003752.en: Even if a paper is otherwise well written, it will make an unfavorable impression on readers if it contains such mistakes.
college-writing-003752.zh: 即使一篇论文写得很好，如果它包含这样的错误，它也会给读者留下不利的印象。

college-writing-003753.en: To edit a paper, check it against the agreed-upon rules, or conventions, of written English─simply called sentence skills in this book.
college-writing-003753.zh: 要编辑一篇论文，请根据商定的规则或约定书面英语进行检查——在本书中简称为句子技能。

college-writing-003754.en: Here are the most common of these conventions:
college-writing-003754.zh: 以下是这些约定中最常见的：

college-writing-003755.en: ✔ Write complete sentences rather than fragments.
college-writing-003755.zh: ✔ 写完整的句子而不是片段。

college-writing-003758.en: ✔ Make sure that subject, verbs, and pronouns agree.
college-writing-003758.zh: ✔ 确保主语、动词和代词一致。

college-writing-003760.zh: 136 第一部分 作文写作

college-writing-003761.en: These sentence skills are treated in detail in individual chapters in Part 4 of this book, and they can be referred to easily as needed, by chapter title.
college-writing-003761.zh: 这些句子技巧在本书第 4 部分的各个章节中进行了详细介绍，并且可以根据需要轻松地按章节标题来引用它们。

college-writing-003762.en: In addition, a checklist of sentence skills is provided at the back of the book, and a corrections symbols list is included at the end of Part 4.
college-writing-003762.zh: 此外，书的背面还提供了一个句子技巧清单，第 4 部分的末尾包含了更正符号列表。

college-writing-003763.en: Hints about Editing These hints can help you edit the next-to-final draft of a paper for sentence-skill mistakes:
college-writing-003763.zh: 有关编辑这些提示的提示可以帮助您编辑论文的下一个到最后的草稿，以解决句子技能错误：

college-writing-003764.en: 1. Have your paper fully typed and in proper MLA format before you spend time editing.
college-writing-003764.zh: 1. 在您花时间编辑之前，请将您的论文以正确的 MLA 格式打字。

college-writing-003765.en: 2. Run grammar- and spell-check applications: these are essential tools for editing your essays, but they are not foolproof.
college-writing-003765.zh: 2. 运行语法和拼写检查应用程序：这些是编辑论文的基本工具，但它们并非万无一失。

college-writing-003766.en: In addition, have a good dictionary and a grammar handbook (you can use the one in Part 4 of this text) to help you decide whether or not to accept the suggested changes from the grammar and spelling checks.
college-writing-003766.zh: 此外，有一本好的词典和一本语法手册（您可以使用本文第 4 部分中的一本）来帮助您决定是否接受语法和拼写检查中的建议更改。

college-writing-003768.en: It is better to work on a printed draft rather than to make corrections electronically; use a pen with colored ink so any corrections will stand out.
college-writing-003768.zh: 最好是在印刷的草稿上工作，而不是以电子方式进行更正； 使用带彩色墨水的笔，因此任何校正都会脱颖而出。

college-writing-003769.en: 4. Use a sheet of paper to cover your essay so that only one sentence at a time will be exposed.
college-writing-003769.zh: 4. 用一张纸覆盖你的论文，这样一次只暴露一句话。

college-writing-003770.en: Look for errors in grammar, spelling, and typing.
college-writing-003770.zh: 查找语法、拼写和打字中的错误。

college-writing-003771.en: It may help to read each sentence out loud.
college-writing-003771.zh: 大声读出每个句子可能会有所帮助。

college-writing-003772.en: If a sentence does not read clearly and smoothly, chances are something is wrong.
college-writing-003772.zh: 如果一个句子读得不清楚流畅，很可能有问题。

college-writing-003773.en: Pay special attention to the kinds of errors you tend to make.
college-writing-003773.zh: 特别注意你倾向于犯的错误种类。

college-writing-003774.en: For example, if you tend to write run-ons or fragments, be especially on the lookout for those errors.
college-writing-003774.zh: 例如，如果您倾向于编写运行或片段，请特别注意这些错误。

college-writing-003775.en: 5. Once you have worked through the printed draft, make your changes on your final draft.
college-writing-003775.zh: 5. 完成打印草稿后，对最终草稿进行更改。

college-writing-004133.en: The purpose of each adventure was fun, but occasionally things got out of hand.
college-writing-004133.zh: 每次冒险的目的都很有趣，但偶尔事情就会失控。

college-writing-004134.en: In my search for good times, I was involved in three notable incidents, ranging from fairly harmless to fairly serious.
college-writing-004134.zh: 在我寻找美好时光的过程中，我卷入了三起值得注意的事件，从相当无害到相当严重。

college-writing-004135.en: The first caper proved that good, clean fun does not have to be dull.
college-writing-004135.zh: 第一次刺山柑证明了良好、干净的乐趣不必沉闷。

college-writing-004136.en: As a high school student, I was credited with making the world’s largest dessert.
college-writing-004136.zh: 作为一名高中生，我被认为是世界上最大的甜点。

college-writing-004137.en: With several friends, I spent an entire year collecting boxes of Jell-O.
college-writing-004137.zh: 和几个朋友一起，我花了一整年的时间收集果冻盒。

college-writing-004138.en: Entering our school’s indoor pool one night, we turned the water temperature up as high as it would go and poured in box after box of the strawberry powder.
college-writing-004138.zh: 一晚进入我们学校的室内游泳池，我们把水温调高了，把一盒又一盒的草莓粉倒了一盒。

college-writing-004139.en: The next morning, school officials arrived to find the pool filled with thirteen thousand gallons of the quivering, rubbery stuff.
college-writing-004139.zh: 第二天早上，学校官员赶到，发现游泳池里装满了 13000 加仑的颤抖、橡胶般的东西。

college-writing-004140.en: No one was hurt by the prank, but we did suffer through three days of a massive cleanup and had to pay for the repairs to the pump.
college-writing-004140.zh: 没有人被恶作剧伤害，但我们确实经历了三天的大规模清理工作，不得不支付维修费用。

college-writing-004144.en: Not all my antics were harmless, and one involved risking my life.
college-writing-004144.zh: 并非我所有的滑稽动作都是无害的，其中一种涉及冒着生命危险。

college-writing-004145.en: As soon as I got my driver’s license, I wanted to join the Fliers’ Club.
college-writing-004145.zh: 我一拿到驾照，就想加入飞行俱乐部。

college-writing-004146.en: Membership in this club was limited to those who could make their cars fly a distance of at least ten feet.
college-writing-004146.zh: 该俱乐部的会员资格仅限于那些可以让他们的汽车飞行至少十英尺的距离的人。

college-writing-004147.en: The qualifying site was an old quarry field where friends and I had built a ramp made of dirt.
college-writing-004147.zh: 排位赛场地是一个古老的采石场，我和朋友们在那里建造了一个用泥土制成的坡道。

college-writing-004148.en: I drove my battered Mercury Cougar up this ramp as fast as it would go.
college-writing-004148.zh: 我把破烂的水星美洲狮赶到这个坡道上，尽可能快地走上这条坡道。

college-writing-004149.en: The Cougar flew ten feet, but one of the tires exploded when I landed.
college-writing-004149.zh: 美洲狮飞了十英尺，但当我降落时，其中一个轮胎爆炸了。

college-writing-004150.en: The car rolled on its side, and I luckily escaped with only a bruised arm.
college-writing-004150.zh: 车侧翻了，幸运的是，我只有一只手臂被擦伤了。

college-writing-004151.en: Risking my own life was bad enough, but there was another episode in which other people could have been hurt, too.
college-writing-004151.zh: 冒着自己的生命危险已经够糟糕的了，但还有一个其他人也可能受到伤害的情节。

college-writing-004152.en: On this occasion, I accidentally set a valley on fire.
college-writing-004152.zh: 这一次，我不小心点燃了一个山谷。

college-writing-004153.en: Two of my friends and I were sitting on a hill sharing a few beers.
college-writing-004153.zh: 我和我的两个朋友坐在山上分享几杯啤酒。

college-writing-004154.en: It was a warm summer night, and there was absolutely nothing to do.
college-writing-004154.zh: 那是一个温暖的夏夜，绝对无事可做。

college-writing-004155.en: The idea came like a thunderclap.
college-writing-004155.zh: 这个想法就像雷声一样。

college-writing-004156.en: We collected a supply of large plastic trash bags, emergency highway flares, and a half tank of helium left over from a science-fair experiment.
college-writing-004156.zh: 我们收集了大量塑料垃圾袋、紧急公路照明弹和科学博览会实验遗留的半罐氦气供应。

college-writing-004157.en: Then we began to construct a fleet of UFOs.
college-writing-004157.zh: 然后我们开始建造一支不明飞行物。

college-writing-004158.en: Filling the bags with helium, we tied them closed with wire and suspended several burning flares below each bag.
college-writing-004158.zh: 用氦气装满袋子，我们用电线将它们紧紧地系起来，并在每个袋子下方悬挂了几个燃烧的照明弹。

college-writing-004159.en: Our UFOs leaped into the air like an army of invading Martians.
college-writing-004159.zh: 我们的不明飞行物像一支入侵火星人的军队一样跃入空中。

college-writing-004160.en: Rising and darting in the blackness, they convinced even us.
college-writing-004160.zh: 在黑暗中起飞和飞奔，他们甚至说服了我们。

college-writing-004161.en: Our fun turned into horror, though, as we watched the balloons begin to drop onto the wooded valley below.
college-writing-004161.zh: 然而，当我们看着气球开始落到下面树木繁茂的山谷时，我们的乐趣变成了恐怖。

college-writing-004162.en: Soon, a brushfire started and, quickly sobered, we called the fire department.
college-writing-004162.zh: 很快，一场灌木火开始了，很快就清醒了，我们打电话给消防部门。

college-writing-004163.en: The punishment we received for this prank put an end to my risky antics.
college-writing-004163.zh: 我们对这个恶作剧的惩罚结束了我冒险的滑稽动作。

college-writing-004164.en: Every so often, I think back on the things that I did as a teenager.
college-writing-004164.zh: 每隔一段时间，我就会回想起我十几岁时所做的事情。

college-writing-004165.en: I feel lucky that I didn't harm myself or others, though I do feel regret that my actions had a negative impact on others.
college-writing-004165.zh: 我很幸运没有伤害自己或他人，尽管我确实为自己的行为对他人产生了负面影响而感到遗憾。

college-writing-004166.en: Today I’m older, wiser, and more aware of the repercussions my actions can cause.
college-writing-004166.zh: 今天，我更老、更聪明、更清楚我的行为可能造成的影响。

college-writing-004168.en: In the unreal world of television situation comedies, teenagers are carefree, smart, funny, wisecracking, secure kids.
college-writing-004168.zh: 在不真实的电视情景喜剧世界中，青少年是无忧无虑、聪明、有趣、俏皮、安全的孩子。

college-writing-004169.en: In fact, most of them are more “together” than the adults on the shows.
college-writing-004169.zh: 事实上，他们中的大多数人比节目中的成年人更“在一起”。

college-writing-004170.en: This, however, isn’t how I recall my teenage years at all.
college-writing-004170.zh: 然而，这根本不是我回忆起我的青少年时期的方式。

college-writing-004171.zh: 作为一个青少年，我受了苦。

college-writing-004172.en: Every day, I battled the terrible physical, family, and social troubles of adolescence.
college-writing-004172.zh: 每天，我都在与青春期可怕的身体、家庭和社会问题作斗争。

college-writing-004173.en: For one thing, I had to deal with a demoralizing physical problem — acne.
college-writing-004173.zh: 一方面，我不得不处理一个令人沮丧的身体问题——痤疮。

college-writing-004174.en: Some days, I would wake up in the morning with a red bump the size of a taillight on my nose.
college-writing-004174.zh: 有些日子，我会在早上醒来，鼻子上有一个尾灯大小的红色凸起。

college-writing-004175.en: Since I worried constantly about my appearance anyway, acne outbreaks could turn me into a crying, screaming maniac.
college-writing-004175.zh: 由于无论如何我一直担心自己的外表，痤疮爆发可能会让我变成一个哭泣、尖叫的疯子。

college-writing-004176.en: Plastering on a layer of (at the time) orange-colored Clearasil, which didn’t fool anybody, I would slink into school, hoping that the boy I had a crush on would be absent that day.
college-writing-004176.zh: 在一层（当时）橙色的 Clearasil 上贴上一层没有愚弄任何人的东西，我会溜进学校，希望我暗恋的那个男孩那天会缺席。

college-writing-004179.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 153
college-writing-004179.zh: 第6章 修订论文的四个基础 153

college-writing-004181.en: Essay makes its point more clearly and effectively because explanation: Essay 1 is more effective because it is unified.
college-writing-004181.zh: 论文更清楚、更有效地表达了它的观点，因为解释：论文 1 更有效，因为它是统一的。

college-writing-004184.en: Within the last few years, however, treatments for acne have improved.
college-writing-004184.zh: 然而，在过去的几年里，痤疮的治疗有所改善。

college-writing-004185.en: Now, skin doctors prescribe special drugs that clear up pimples almost immediately.
college-writing-004185.zh: 现在，皮肤医生开出几乎立即清除粉刺的特殊药物。

college-writing-004186.en: An acne attack could shatter whatever small amount of selfesteem I had managed to build up.
college-writing-004186.zh: 痤疮发作可能会粉碎我设法建立的任何少量自尊心。

college-writing-004187.en: In addition to fighting acne, I felt compelled to fight my family.
college-writing-004187.zh: 除了与痤疮作斗争，我还感到不得不与家人战斗。

college-writing-004188.en: As a teenager, I needed to be independent.
college-writing-004188.zh: 作为一个青少年，我需要独立。

college-writing-004189.en: At that time, the most important thing in life was to be close to my friends and to try out new, more adult experiences.
college-writing-004189.zh: 那时，生活中最重要的事情是与我的朋友亲近并尝试新的、更多成人的经历。

college-writing-004190.en: Unfortunately, my family seemed to get in the way.
college-writing-004190.zh: 不幸的是，我的家人似乎妨碍了我。

college-writing-004191.en: My little brother, for instance, turned into my enemy.
college-writing-004191.zh: 例如，我的小弟弟变成了我的敌人。

college-writing-004193.en: In fact, Eddie recently painted my new apartment for me.
college-writing-004193.zh: 事实上，埃迪最近为我画了我的新公寓。

college-writing-004194.en: Eddie used to barge into my room, make calls on my cell phone, and read my e-mail.
college-writing-004194.zh: 埃迪过去常常闯入我的房间，用手机拨打电话，阅读我的电子邮件。

college-writing-004195.en: I would threaten to tie him up and leave him in a garbage dumpster.
college-writing-004195.zh: 我威胁要把他绑起来，把他留在垃圾箱里。

college-writing-004196.en: He would scream, my mother would yell, and all hell would break loose.
college-writing-004196.zh: 他会尖叫，我妈妈会大喊大叫，所有地狱都会爆发。

college-writing-004198.en: They wouldn’t let me stay out late, wear the clothes I wanted to wear, or hang around with the friends I liked.
college-writing-004198.zh: 他们不会让我在外面呆到很晚，穿我想穿的衣服，或者和我喜欢的朋友一起闲逛。

college-writing-004199.en: So I tried to get revenge on them by being miserable, sulky, and sarcastic at home.
college-writing-004199.zh: 所以我试图通过在家里悲惨、闷闷不乐和讽刺来报复他们。

college-writing-004200.en: Worst of all, I had to face the social traumas of being a teenager.
college-writing-004200.zh: 最糟糕的是，我不得不面对青少年的社会创伤。

college-writing-004201.en: Things that were supposed to be fun, like dates and dances, were actually horrible.
college-writing-004201.zh: 应该很有趣的事情，比如约会和舞蹈，实际上是可怕的。

college-writing-004202.en: On the few occasions when I had a real date, I agonized over everything — my hair, my weight, my pimples.
college-writing-004202.zh: 在我真正约会的少数情况下，我为一切——我的头发、我的体重、我的粉刺感到痛苦。

college-writing-004203.en: After a date, I would come home, raid the kitchen, and drown my insecurities in a sea of junk food.
college-writing-004203.zh: 约会后，我会回家，搜查厨房，把我的不安全感淹没在垃圾食品的海洋中。

college-writing-004204.zh: 舞蹈也是有压力的事件。

college-writing-004205.en: My friends and I would sneak a couple of beers just to get up the nerve to walk into the school gym.
college-writing-004205.zh: 我和我的朋友们会偷偷喝几杯啤酒，只是为了鼓起勇气走进学校的健身房。

college-writing-004206.en: Now I realize that teenage drinking is dangerous.
college-writing-004206.zh: 现在我意识到青少年饮酒是危险的。

college-writing-004207.en: I read recently that the number-one killer of teenagers is drunk driving.
college-writing-004207.zh: 我最近读到，青少年的第一杀手是酒后驾车。

college-writing-004208.zh: 在舞会上，我从来没有放松过。

college-writing-004209.en: It was too important to look exactly right, to act really cool, and to pretend I was having fun.
college-writing-004209.zh: 看起来完全正确、表现得非常酷和假装我玩得开心太重要了。

college-writing-004210.en: I’m glad I’m not a teenager anymore.
college-writing-004210.zh: 我很高兴我不再是青少年了。

college-writing-004211.en: I wouldn’t ever want to feel so unattractive, so confused, and so insecure again.
college-writing-004211.zh: 我再也不想感到如此没有吸引力、如此困惑和如此不安全。

college-writing-004212.en: I’ll gladly accept the crow’s-feet and stomach bulge of adulthood in exchange for a little peace of mind.
college-writing-004212.zh: 我很乐意接受成年的乌鸦脚和腹部隆起，以换取一点内心的平静。

college-writing-004213.zh: 154 第一部分 作文写作

college-writing-004214.en: The difference between these first two essays leads us to the first base, or standard, of effective writing: unity.
college-writing-004214.zh: 前两篇论文之间的差异使我们找到了有效写作的第一个基础或标准：统一。

college-writing-004215.en: To achieve unity is to have all the details in your paper related to your thesis and to your supporting topic sentences.
college-writing-004215.zh: 实现统一就是在论文中包含与您的论文和您的支持 主题句 相关的所有细节。

college-writing-004216.en: Each time you think of something to put into your paper, ask yourself whether it relates to your thesis and your supporting points.
college-writing-004216.zh: 每次你想到要写在论文中的东西时，问问自己它是否与你的论文和你的支持点有关。

college-writing-004217.en: If it does not, leave it out.
college-writing-004217.zh: 如果没有，请将其排除在外。

college-writing-004218.en: For example, if you were writing a paper about the problems of being unemployed and then spent a couple of sentences talking about the pleasures of having a lot of free time, you would be missing the first and most essential base of good writing.
college-writing-004218.zh: 例如，如果您正在写一篇关于失业问题的论文，然后花了几句话谈论有大量空闲时间的乐趣，那么您将错过良好写作的第一个也是最重要的基础。

college-writing-004219.en: Revising for Unity Go back to essay 2 and cross out the two sentences in the first supporting paragraph (paragraph 2), the one sentence in the second supporting paragraph (paragraph 3), and the two sentences in the third supporting paragraph (paragraph 4) that are off target and do not support their topic sentences.
college-writing-004219.zh: 修改统一 回到第 2 篇，将第一个支持段（第 2 段）中的两个句子划掉，第二个支持段落中的一个句子（第 3 段），以及第三个支持段落中的两个句子（第 4 段）中的两个句子（第 4 段） 主题句。

college-writing-004220.en: Base 2: Support Understanding Support The following essays were written on the topic “Handling Disappointment.”
college-writing-004220.zh: 基础 2：支持 理解 支持 以下论文是关于“处理失望”的主题。

college-writing-004221.en: Both are unified, but one communicates more clearly and effectively.
college-writing-004221.zh: 两者都是统一的，但一种是更清晰有效的沟通。

college-writing-004225.en: All the details in this essay are on target; they support and develop each of its three topic sentences (“The first caper proved that good, clean fun does not have to be dull”; “Not all my antics were harmless, and one involved risking my life”; and “Risking my own life was bad enough, but there was another episode where other people could have been hurt, too”).
college-writing-004225.zh: 本文中的所有细节都在目标上； 他们支持和发展它的三个主题句（“第一次刺探证明，好的，干净的乐趣不必沉闷”；“不是我所有的滑稽动作都是无害的，一个人冒着生命危险”；“冒着自己的生命危险，但还有另一个 其他人也可能受到伤害的情节”）。

college-writing-004226.en: On the other hand, essay 2 contains some details irrelevant to its topic sentences.
college-writing-004226.zh: 另一方面，论文 2 包含一些与其 主题句 无关的细节。

college-writing-004227.en: In the first supporting paragraph (paragraph 2), for example, the sentences “Within the last few years, however, treatments for acne have improved. Now, skin doctors prescribe special drugs that clear up pimples almost immediately” do not support the writer’s topic statement that she had to deal with the physical problem of acne.
college-writing-004227.zh: 在第一段（第2段）中，例如，“在过去几年中，痤疮的治疗方法有所改善。现在，皮肤医生开出几乎立即清除粉刺的特殊药物”不支持作者的主题陈述，即她必须处理身体问题 的痤疮。

college-writing-004228.en: Such details should be left out in the interest of unity.
college-writing-004228.zh: 为了统一的利益，应该把这些细节留在外面。

college-writing-004229.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 155
college-writing-004229.zh: 第6章 修订论文的四个基础 155

college-writing-004231.en: One way to look at life is as a series of disappointments.
college-writing-004231.zh: 看待生活的一种方式是一系列失望。

college-writing-004232.en: Life can certainly appear that way because disappointment crops up in the life of everyone more often, it seems, than satisfaction.
college-writing-004232.zh: 生活肯定会这样出现，因为似乎每个人的生活中的失望都比满足更频繁地出现。

college-writing-004233.en: How disappointments are handled can have a great bearing on how life is viewed.
college-writing-004233.zh: 如何处理失望会对如何看待生活产生重大影响。

college-writing-004234.en: People can react negatively by sulking or by blaming others, or they can try to understand the reasons behind the disappointment.
college-writing-004234.zh: 人们可以通过生闷气或指责他人来做出消极的反应，或者他们可以尝试了解失望背后的原因。

college-writing-004235.en: Sulking is one way to deal with disappointment.
college-writing-004235.zh: 闷闷不乐是应对失望的一种方式。

college-writing-004236.en: This attitude — Why does everything always happen to me?
college-writing-004236.zh: 这种态度——为什么一切总是发生在我身上？

college-writing-004237.en: — is common because it is easy to adopt, but it is not very productive.
college-writing-004237.zh: ——很常见，因为它很容易采用，但它不是很有成效。

college-writing-004238.en: Everyone has had the experience of meeting people who specialize in feeling sorry for themselves.
college-writing-004238.zh: 每个人都有结识专门为自己感到难过的人的经历。

college-writing-004239.en: A sulky manner will often discourage others from wanting to lend support, and it prevents the sulker from making positive moves toward self-help.
college-writing-004239.zh: 闷闷不乐的方式常常会阻止他人想要提供支持，这会阻止闷闷不乐的人向自助采取积极的行动。

college-writing-004240.en: It becomes easier just to sit back and sulk.
college-writing-004240.zh: 只是坐下来闷闷不乐变得更容易。

college-writing-004241.en: Unfortunately, feeling sorry for oneself does nothing to lessen the pain of disappointment.
college-writing-004241.zh: 不幸的是，为自己感到难过并不能减轻失望的痛苦。

college-writing-004242.en: It may, in fact, increase the pain.
college-writing-004242.zh: 事实上，它可能会增加疼痛。

college-writing-004243.en: It certainly does not make future disappointments easier to bear.
college-writing-004243.zh: 它当然不会让未来的失望更容易忍受。

college-writing-004244.en: Blaming others is another negative and unproductive way to cope with disappointment.
college-writing-004244.zh: 指责他人是另一种消极和非生产性的方式来应对失望。

college-writing-004245.en: This all-too-common response of pointing the finger at someone else doesn’t help one’s situation.
college-writing-004245.zh: 这种将手指指向别人的非常常见的反应对一个人的处境没有帮助。

college-writing-004246.en: This posture will lead only to anger, resentment, and, therefore, further unhappiness.
college-writing-004246.zh: 这种姿势只会导致愤怒、怨恨，从而导致进一步的不快乐。

college-writing-004247.en: Disappointment in another’s performance does not necessarily indicate that the performer is at fault.
college-writing-004247.zh: 对他人表现的失望并不一定表明表演者有过错。

college-writing-004248.en: Perhaps expectations were too high, or there could have been a misunderstanding as to what the performer actually intended to accomplish.
college-writing-004248.zh: 也许期望太高了，或者可能对表演者的实际打算完成的事情存在误解。

college-writing-004249.en: A positive way to handle disappointment is to try to understand the reasons behind the disappointment.
college-writing-004249.zh: 处理失望的一种积极方法是试图了解失望背后的原因。

college-writing-004250.en: An analysis of the causes of disappointment can have an excellent chance of producing desirable results.
college-writing-004250.zh: 分析失望的原因可能有很好的机会产生理想的结果。

college-writing-004251.en: Often understanding alone can help alleviate the pain of disappointment and can help prevent future disappointments.
college-writing-004251.zh: 通常，单独理解可以帮助减轻失望的痛苦，并有助于防止未来的失望。

college-writing-004252.en: Also, it is wise to try to remember that what would be ideal is not necessarily what is reasonable to expect in any given situation.
college-writing-004252.zh: 此外，明智的做法是尝试记住，理想的情况不一定是在任何给定情况下可以合理预期的。

college-writing-004253.en: The ability to look disappointment squarely in the face and then go on from there is the first step on the road back.
college-writing-004253.zh: 直视脸上然后从那里继续前进的能力是回归的第一步。

college-writing-004254.en: Continuous handling of disappointment in a negative manner can lead to a negative view of life itself.
college-writing-004254.zh: 以消极的方式持续处理失望可能会导致对生活本身的负面看法。

college-writing-004255.en: Chances for personal happiness in such a state of being are understandably slim.
college-writing-004255.zh: 在这种存在状态下获得个人幸福的机会是可以理解的，这是可以理解的。

college-writing-004256.en: Learning not to expect perfection in an imperfect world and keeping in mind those times when expectations were actually surpassed are positive steps toward allowing the joys of life to prevail.
college-writing-004256.zh: 学会在一个不完美的世界中不要期待完美，并牢记那些真正超越期望的时候，是让生活中的快乐盛行的积极步骤。

college-writing-004260.en: Ben Franklin said that the only sure things in life are death and taxes.
college-writing-004260.zh: 本富兰克林说，生命中唯一确定的事情是死亡和税收。

college-writing-004261.en: He left something out, however: disappointment.
college-writing-004261.zh: 然而，他遗漏了一些东西：失望。

college-writing-004262.en: No one gets through life without experiencing many disappointments.
college-writing-004262.zh: 没有人经历过许多失望的生活。

college-writing-004263.en: Strangely, though, most people seem unprepared for disappointment and react to it in negative ways.
college-writing-004263.zh: 然而，奇怪的是，大多数人似乎对失望没有准备，并以消极的方式对其做出反应。

college-writing-004264.en: They feel depressed or try to escape their troubles instead of using disappointment as an opportunity for growth.
college-writing-004264.zh: 他们感到沮丧或试图摆脱困境，而不是将失望作为成长的机会。

college-writing-004265.en: One negative reaction to disappointment is depression.
college-writing-004265.zh: 对失望的一种负面反应是抑郁症。

college-writing-004266.en: For example, Helena, a woman trying to win a promotion, works hard for over a year in her department.
college-writing-004266.zh: 例如，一个试图赢得晋升的女性海伦娜在她的部门努力工作了一年多。

college-writing-004267.en: Helena is so sure she will get the promotion, in fact, that she has already picked out the car she will buy when her salary increase comes through.
college-writing-004267.zh: 海伦娜非常确定她会得到晋升，事实上，她已经挑选出了她在加薪时会买的汽车。

college-writing-004268.en: However, the boss names one of Helena’s coworkers to the spot.
college-writing-004268.zh: 然而，老板将海伦娜的一位同事当场命名。

college-writing-004269.en: The fact that all the other department employees tell Helena that she is the one who really deserved the promotion doesn’t help her deal with the crushing disappointment.
college-writing-004269.zh: 所有其他部门的员工都告诉海伦娜，她是真正值得晋升的人，这一事实并不能帮助她应对巨大的失望。

college-writing-004270.en: Deeply depressed, Helena decides that all her goals are doomed to defeat.
college-writing-004270.zh: 海伦娜深感沮丧，决定她的所有目标注定要失败。

college-writing-004271.en: She loses her enthusiasm for her job and can barely force herself to show up every day.
college-writing-004271.zh: 她失去了对工作的热情，几乎不能强迫自己每天都出现。

college-writing-004272.en: Helena tells herself that she is a failure and that doing a good job just isn’t worth the work.
college-writing-004272.zh: 海伦娜告诉自己，她是一个失败者，做好工作是不值得的。

college-writing-004273.en: Another negative reaction to disappointment, and one that often follows depression, is the desire to escape.
college-writing-004273.zh: 对失望的另一种负面反应，以及经常伴随抑郁的一种负面反应，是逃避的愿望。

college-writing-004274.en: Jamal fails to get into the college his brother is attending, the college that was the focus of all his dreams, and decides to escape his disappointment.
college-writing-004274.zh: 贾马尔未能进入他兄弟正在就读的大学，这所大学是他所有梦想的焦点，并决定摆脱他的失望。

college-writing-004275.en: Why worry about college at all?

college-writing-004276.en: Instead, he covers up his real feelings by giving up on his schoolwork and getting completely involved with friends, parties, and “good times.”
college-writing-004276.zh: 相反，他通过放弃学业并与朋友、聚会和“美好时光”完全互动来掩盖自己的真实感受。

college-writing-004277.en: Or Carla doesn’t make the varsity basketball team — something she wanted very badly — and so refuses to play sports at all.
college-writing-004277.zh: 或者卡拉没有成为大学篮球队——她非常想要的东西——所以根本拒绝参加体育运动。

college-writing-004278.en: She decides to hang around with a new set of friends who get high every day; then she won’t have to confront her disappointment and learn to live with it.
college-writing-004278.zh: 她决定和一群每天都很兴奋的新朋友一起闲逛； 然后她就不必面对她的失望并学会忍受它。

college-writing-004279.en: The positive way to react to disappointment is to use it as a chance for growth.
college-writing-004279.zh: 对失望做出反应的积极方式是将其作为成长的机会。

college-writing-004280.en: This isn’t easy, but it’s the only useful way to deal with an inevitable part of life.
college-writing-004280.zh: 这并不容易，但它是处理生活中不可避免的部分的唯一有用方法。

college-writing-004281.en: Helena, the woman who wasn’t promoted, could have handled her disappointment by looking at other options.
college-writing-004281.zh: 没有升职的女性海伦娜本可以通过寻找其他选择来应对她的失望。

college-writing-004282.en: If her boss doesn’t recognize her talent and hard work, perhaps she could transfer to another department.
college-writing-004282.zh: 如果她的老板不认识她的才华和辛勤工作，也许她可以转移到另一个部门。

college-writing-004283.en: Or she could ask the boss how to improve her performance so that she would be a shoo-in for the next promotion.
college-writing-004283.zh: 或者她可以问老板如何提高她的表现，这样她就可以成为下一次晋升的热门人选。

college-writing-004284.en: Jamal, the boy who didn’t get into the college of his choice, should look into other schools.
college-writing-004284.zh: 贾马尔，一个没有进入他选择的大学的男孩，应该看看其他学校。

college-writing-004285.en: Going to another college may encourage him to be his own person, step out of his brother’s shadow, and realize that being turned down by one college isn’t a final judgment on his abilities or potential.
college-writing-004285.zh: 去另一所大学可能会鼓励他成为自己的人，走出他兄弟的阴影，并意识到被一所大学拒绝并不是对他的能力或潜力的最终判断。

college-writing-004286.en: Rather than escape into drugs, Carla could improve
college-writing-004286.zh: 卡拉可以改善而不是逃避毒品

college-writing-004289.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 157
college-writing-004289.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 157

college-writing-004290.en: her basketball skills for a year or pick up another sport — like swimming or tennis — that would probably turn out to be more useful to her as an adult.
college-writing-004290.zh: 她一年的篮球技巧或选择另一项运动——比如游泳或网球——这对她成年后可能更有用。

college-writing-004291.en: Disappointments are unwelcome but regular visitors to everyone’s life.
college-writing-004291.zh: 失望是不受欢迎的，但每个人的生活都是常客。

college-writing-004292.en: We can feel depressed about them, or we can try to escape from them.
college-writing-004292.zh: 我们可以因他们而感到沮丧，也可以试图逃离他们。

college-writing-004293.en: The best thing, though, is to accept a disappointment and then try to use it somehow: step over the unwelcome visitor on the doorstep and get on with life.
college-writing-004293.zh: 不过，最好的事情是接受失望，然后尝试以某种方式使用它：跨过门口的不受欢迎的访客，继续生活。

college-writing-004295.en: Essay makes its point more clearly and effectively because
college-writing-004295.zh: 论文更清楚、更有效地表达了它的观点，因为

college-writing-004297.en: explanation: Here, essay 2 is more effective, for it offers specific examples of the ways people deal with disappointment.
college-writing-004297.zh: 解释：在这里，论文 2 更有效，因为它提供了人们处理失望的方式的具体例子。

college-writing-004298.en: We see for ourselves the kinds of reactions people have to disappointment.
college-writing-004298.zh: 我们亲眼目睹了人们对人们的失望反应。

college-writing-004299.en: Essay 1, on the other hand, gives us no specific evidence.
college-writing-004299.zh: 另一方面，论文 1 没有给我们具体的证据。

college-writing-004300.en: The writer tells us repeatedly that sulking, blaming others, and trying to understand the reasons behind a disappointment are the reactions people have to a letdown.
college-writing-004300.zh: 作者一再告诉我们，闷闷不乐、指责他人以及试图理解失望背后的原因是人们对失望的反应。

college-writing-004301.en: However, the writer never shows us any of these responses in action.
college-writing-004301.zh: 然而，作者从不向我们展示这些反应中的任何一个。

college-writing-004302.en: Exactly what kinds of disappointments is the writer talking about?
college-writing-004302.zh: 作者到底在说什么样的失望？

college-writing-004303.en: And how, for instance, does someone analyze the causes of disappointment?
college-writing-004303.zh: 例如，如何分析失望的原因？

college-writing-004304.en: Would a person write a list of causes on a piece of paper, or review the causes with a concerned friend, or speak to a professional therapist?
college-writing-004304.zh: 一个人会在一张纸上写下原因清单，还是与相关的朋友一起回顾原因，或者与专业治疗师交谈？

college-writing-004305.en: In an essay like this, we would want to see examples of how sulking and blaming others are negative ways of dealing with disappointment.
college-writing-004305.zh: 在这样的文章中，我们希望看到如何闷闷不乐和指责他人是对付失望的消极方式。

college-writing-004306.en: Consideration of these two essays leads us to the second base of effective writing: support.
college-writing-004306.zh: 考虑这两篇文章，我们找到了有效写作的第二个基础：支持。

college-writing-004307.en: After realizing the importance of specific supporting details, one student writer revised a paper they had done on being lost in the woods as the worst experience of their childhood.
college-writing-004307.zh: 在意识到特定 支撑细节 的重要性后，一位学生作家修改了他们所做的一篇关于迷失在树林中的论文，作为他们童年最糟糕的经历。

college-writing-004308.en: In the revised paper, instead of talking about “the terror of being separated from my parents,” they referred to such specifics as “tears streamed down my cheeks as I pictured the faces I would never see again” and “I clutched the locket my parents had given me as if it were a lucky charm that could help me find my way back to the campsite.”
college-writing-004308.zh: 在修订后的论文中，他们没有谈论“与父母分开的恐惧”，而是将这些细节称为“当我描绘出我再也见不到的面孔时，我的脸颊上流下了泪水”和“我抓住了父母给我的挂坠盒，好像它是一个幸运的魅力 可以帮我找到回到露营地的路。”

college-writing-004311.en: All your papers should include such vivid details.
college-writing-004311.zh: 您所有的论文都应包含如此生动的细节。

college-writing-004312.en: Revising for Support On a separate sheet of paper, revise one of the three supporting paragraphs in “Dealing with Disappointment” by providing specific supporting examples.
college-writing-004312.zh: 修改单独纸张的支持，通过提供具体的支持示例修改“处理失望”中的三个支持段落之一。

college-writing-004313.en: Base 3: Coherence Understanding Coherence The following two essays were written on the topic “Positive or Negative Effects of Television.”
college-writing-004313.zh: 基础 3：连贯性 理解 连贯性 以下两篇论文是关于“电视的正面或负面影响”的主题。

college-writing-004314.en: Both are unified, and both are supported.
college-writing-004314.zh: 两者是统一的，并且都支持。

college-writing-004315.en: However, one communicates more clearly and effectively.
college-writing-004315.zh: 然而，一种更清晰、更有效的沟通方式。

college-writing-004319.en: In a recent cartoon, one character said to another, “When you think of the awesome power of television to educate, aren’t you glad it doesn’t?”
college-writing-004319.zh: 在最近的一部漫画中，一个角色对另一个角色说：“当你想到电视的强大力量教育时，你不高兴它没有吗？”

college-writing-004320.en: It’s true that television has the power to educate and to entertain, but unfortunately, these benefits are outweighed by the harm it does to dedicated viewers.
college-writing-004320.zh: 确实，电视具有教育和娱乐的能力，但不幸的是，这些好处被它对敬业观众的伤害所抵消。

college-writing-004321.en: Television is harmful because it creates passivity, discourages communication, and presents a false picture of reality.
college-writing-004321.zh: 电视是有害的，因为它会产生被动性、阻碍交流，并呈现出现实的虚假画面。

college-writing-004323.en: Children who have an electronic babysitter spend most of their waking hours in a semiconscious state.
college-writing-004323.zh: 有电子保姆的孩子大部分醒着的时间都处于半清醒的状态。

college-writing-004324.en: Older viewers watch tennis matches and baseball games with none of the excitement of being in the stands.
college-writing-004324.zh: 年长的观众观看网球比赛和棒球比赛，没有在看台上的兴奋。

college-writing-004325.en: Even if children are watching Sesame Street or Daniel Tiger's Neighborhood, they are being educated passively.
college-writing-004325.zh: 即使孩子们在看芝麻街或丹尼尔·泰格的邻居，他们也在接受被动教育。

college-writing-004326.en: The child actors are going on nature walks, building crafts projects, playing with animals, and participating in games, but the little viewers are simply watching.
college-writing-004326.zh: 儿童演员正在进行自然漫步、建造手工艺品项目、与动物玩耍和参与游戏，但小观众只是在观看。

college-writing-004327.en: Older viewers watch guests discuss hot topics on The View, but the hosts don’t converse with the home viewers about their opinions.
college-writing-004327.zh: 年长的观众观看客人在视图上讨论热门话题，但主持人不会与家庭观众谈论他们的意见。

college-writing-004328.en: Worst of all, TV presents a false picture of reality that leaves viewers frustrated because they don’t have the beauty or wealth of the characters on television.
college-writing-004328.zh: 最糟糕的是，电视呈现出现实的虚假画面，让观众感到沮丧，因为他们没有电视上角色的美丽或财富。

college-writing-004329.en: Viewers absorb the idea that everyone else in the United States owns a lavish apartment, a suburban house, a sleek car, and an expensive wardrobe.
college-writing-004329.zh: 观众们接受了美国其他人都拥有豪华公寓、郊区房屋、时尚汽车和昂贵衣橱的想法。

college-writing-004333.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 159
college-writing-004333.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 159

college-writing-004334.en: baron, and lawyer, male or female, is extremely good-looking and fit.
college-writing-004334.zh: 男爵和律师，无论男女，都非常好看和合身。

college-writing-004335.en: The material possessions on TV shows and commercials contribute to the false image of reality.
college-writing-004335.zh: 电视节目和广告中的物质财产助长了现实的虚假形象。

college-writing-004336.en: News anchors and reporters, with their perfect hair and makeup, must fit television’s standard of beauty.
college-writing-004336.zh: 新闻主播和记者，拥有完美的发型和妆容，必须符合电视的美容标准。

college-writing-004337.en: From their modest homes or cramped apartments, many viewers tune in daily to the upper-middle-class world that TV glorifies.
college-writing-004337.zh: 从他们朴素的住宅或狭窄的公寓，许多观众每天都在收听电视美化的中上层世界。

college-writing-004339.en: Families watching television do very little talking except for brief exchanges during commercials.
college-writing-004339.zh: 看电视的家庭很少说话，除了广告期间的短暂交流。

college-writing-004340.en: If Uncle Scott or the next-door neighbors drop in for a visit, the most comfortable activity for everyone may be not conversation but watching ESPN.
college-writing-004340.zh: 如果斯科特叔叔或隔壁邻居来拜访，对每个人来说最舒适的活动可能不是交谈，而是在看 ESPN。

college-writing-004341.en: The family may not even be watching the same set; instead, in some households, all the family members head for their own rooms to watch their own sets.
college-writing-004341.zh: 家人甚至可能没有看同一组； 相反，在一些家庭中，所有家庭成员都前往自己的房间观看自己的套装。

college-writing-004342.en: At dinner, plates are plopped on the coffee table in front of the set, and the meal is wolfed down during NBC Nightly News.
college-writing-004342.zh: 晚餐时，盘子前的咖啡桌上扑通一声，这顿饭在 NBC 晚间新闻中被狼吞虎咽。

college-writing-004343.en: During commercials, the only communication a family has all night may consist of questions like “Do we have any popcorn?” and “Where’s the remote?”
college-writing-004343.zh: 在广告中，一个家庭整夜的唯一交流可能包括“我们有爆米花吗？”之类的问题。 和“遥控器在哪里？”

college-writing-004344.en: Television, like cigarettes or saccharin, is harmful to our health.
college-writing-004344.zh: 电视，如香烟或糖精，对我们的健康有害。

college-writing-004345.en: We are becoming isolated, passive, and frustrated.
college-writing-004345.zh: 我们变得孤立、被动和沮丧。

college-writing-004346.en: And, most frightening, the average viewer now spends more time watching television than ever before.
college-writing-004346.zh: 而且，最可怕的是，普通观众现在花费的时间比以往任何时候都多。

college-writing-004348.en: We hear a lot about the negative effects of television on the viewer.
college-writing-004348.zh: 我们听到很多关于电视对观众的负面影响。

college-writing-004349.en: Obviously, television can be harmful if it is watched constantly to the exclusion of other activities.
college-writing-004349.zh: 显然，如果电视经常被观看以排除其他活动，电视可能是有害的。

college-writing-004350.en: It would be just as harmful to surf the Internet all the time or to eat constantly.
college-writing-004350.zh: 一直在网上冲浪或经常吃东西同样有害。

college-writing-004351.en: However, when television is watched in moderation, it is extremely valuable, as it provides relaxation, entertainment, and education.
college-writing-004351.zh: 然而，当电视节目被适度观看时，它非常有价值，因为它提供了放松、娱乐和教育。

college-writing-004352.en: First of all, watching TV has the value of sheer relaxation.
college-writing-004352.zh: 首先，看电视具有纯粹放松的价值。

college-writing-004353.en: Watching television can be soothing and restful after an eight-hour day of pressure, challenges, or concentration.
college-writing-004353.zh: 经过八小时的压力、挑战或注意力，看电视可以舒缓和安宁。

college-writing-004354.en: After working hard all day, people look forward to a new episode of a favorite show or yet another showing of Parasite or Captain Marvel.
college-writing-004354.zh: 经过一整天的努力，人们期待着最喜欢的节目的新一集，或者又一次展示寄生虫或惊奇队长。

college-writing-004355.en: This period of relaxation leaves viewers refreshed and ready to take on the world again.
college-writing-004355.zh: 这段放松的时期让观众精神焕发，准备再次迎接世界。

college-writing-004356.en: Watching TV also seems to reduce stress in some people.
college-writing-004356.zh: 看电视似乎也减轻了一些人的压力。

college-writing-004357.en: This benefit of television is just beginning to be recognized.
college-writing-004357.zh: 电视的这种好处才刚刚开始得到认可。

college-writing-004358.en: In addition to being relaxing, television is entertaining.
college-writing-004358.zh: 除了放松之外，电视还很有趣。

college-writing-004359.en: Along with the standard comedies, dramas, and game shows that provide enjoyment to viewers, television offers a variety of movies and sports events.
college-writing-004359.zh: 除了为观众提供乐趣的标准喜剧、戏剧和游戏节目外，电视还提供各种电影和体育赛事。

college-writing-004365.en: Moreover, viewers can pay a monthly fee for services like Disney+, YouTube TV, or Sling.
college-writing-004365.zh: 此外，观众可以为 Disney+、YouTube TV 或 Sling 等服务支付月费。

college-writing-004366.en: Viewers can watch first-run movies, rock and classical music concerts, and specialized sports events, like international soccer and pay-per-view boxing matches.
college-writing-004366.zh: 观众可以观看首映的电影、摇滚和古典音乐会以及专门的体育赛事，如国际足球和按次付费的拳击比赛。

college-writing-004367.en: Viewers can also buy or rent movies and TV shows through streaming services.
college-writing-004367.zh: 观众还可以通过流媒体服务购买或租用电影和电视节目。

college-writing-004368.en: Still another popular area of TV entertainment is video games.
college-writing-004368.zh: 电视娱乐的另一个受欢迎的领域是电子游戏。

college-writing-004369.en: PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo consoles allow the owner to have a video-game arcade in the living room.
college-writing-004369.zh: PlayStation、Xbox 和 Nintendo 游戏机允许所有者在客厅中拥有一个视频游戏街机。

college-writing-004370.zh: 最重要的是，电视具有教育意义。

college-writing-004371.en: Preschoolers learn colors, numbers, and letters from public television programs, like Sesame Street, that use animation and puppets to make learning fun.
college-writing-004371.zh: 学龄前儿童从公共电视节目（如芝麻街）学习颜色、数字和信件，这些节目使用动画和木偶来使学习变得有趣。

college-writing-004372.en: Science shows for older children go on location to analyze everything from volcanoes to rocket launches.
college-writing-004372.zh: 为年龄较大的儿童提供的科学节目前往现场分析从火山到火箭发射的一切。

college-writing-004373.en: Adults, too, can learn from shows like NOVA, DIY home improvement programs, and cooking shows.
college-writing-004373.zh: 成年人也可以从 Nova、DIY 家居装修计划和烹饪节目等节目中学习。

college-writing-004374.en: Also, television widens our knowledge by covering important events and current news.
college-writing-004374.zh: 此外，电视通过报道重要事件和当前新闻来拓宽我们的知识。

college-writing-004375.en: Viewers can see and hear presidents’ speeches, state funerals, natural disasters, and election results as they are happening.
college-writing-004375.zh: 观众可以看到和听到总统的演讲、国葬、自然灾害和选举结果。

college-writing-004376.en: Perhaps because television is such a powerful force, we like to criticize it and search for its flaws.
college-writing-004376.zh: 也许是因为电视是如此强大的力量，我们喜欢批评它并寻找它的缺陷。

college-writing-004377.en: However, the benefits of television should not be ignored.
college-writing-004377.zh: 但是，电视的好处不应被忽视。

college-writing-004378.en: We can use television to relax, to have fun, and to make ourselves smarter.
college-writing-004378.zh: 我们可以用电视来放松，玩得开心，让自己变得更聪明。

college-writing-004379.en: This electronic wonder, then, is a servant, not a master.
college-writing-004379.zh: 那么，这个电子奇迹是一个仆人，而不是一个主人。

college-writing-004381.en: Essay makes its point more clearly and effectively because
college-writing-004381.zh: 论文更清楚、更有效地表达了它的观点，因为

college-writing-004383.en: explanation: In this case, essay 2 is more effective because the material is organized clearly and logically.
college-writing-004383.zh: 解释：在这种情况下，论文 2 更有效，因为材料的组织清晰、逻辑清晰。

college-writing-004384.en: Using emphatic order, the writer develops three positive uses of television, ending with the most important use: television as an educational tool.
college-writing-004384.zh: 使用强调秩序，作者开发了电视的三种积极用途，以最重要的用途结束：电视作为一种教育工具。

college-writing-004385.en: The writer includes transitional words that act as signposts, making movement from one idea to the next easy to follow.
college-writing-004385.zh: 作者包括充当路标的过渡词，使从一个想法到下一个想法的转变很容易理解。

college-writing-004386.en: The major transitions include First of all, In addition, and Most important; transitions within paragraphs include such words as Moreover, Still another, too, and Also.
college-writing-004386.zh: 主要过渡包括首先，此外，最重要的； 段落中的过渡包括诸如此外，还有另一个词。

college-writing-004387.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 161
college-writing-004387.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 161

college-writing-004389.en: And this writer also uses a linking sentence (“In addition to being relaxing, television is entertaining”) to tie the first and second supporting paragraphs together clearly.
college-writing-004389.zh: 作者还使用链接句子（“除了放松，电视很有趣”）将第一个和第二个支持段落清晰地联系在一起。

college-writing-004390.en: Although essay 1 is unified and supported, the writer does not have any clear and consistent way of organizing the material.
college-writing-004390.zh: 虽然论文 1 是统一和支持的，但作者没有任何清晰一致的方式来组织材料。

college-writing-004391.en: The most important idea (signaled by the phrase Worst of all) is discussed in the second supporting paragraph instead of being saved for last.
college-writing-004391.zh: 最重要的想法（由最糟糕的短语表示）在第二个支持段落中讨论，而不是最后保存。

college-writing-004392.en: None of the supporting paragraphs organizes its details in a logical fashion.
college-writing-004392.zh: 没有一个支持段落以逻辑方式组织其细节。

college-writing-004393.en: The first supporting paragraph, for example, discusses older viewers, then goes to younger viewers, then jumps back to older people again.
college-writing-004393.zh: 例如，第一个支持段落讨论了年长的观众，然后去看年轻的观众，然后再次跳回老年人。

college-writing-004394.en: The third supporting paragraph, like the first, leaps from an opening idea (families talking only during commercials) to several intervening ideas and then back to the original idea (talking during commercials).
college-writing-004394.zh: 第三个支持段落，和第一个一样，从一个开放的想法（家庭在广告中只说话）跳到几个中间的想法，然后回到原来的想法（在广告中说话）。

college-writing-004395.en: In addition, essay 1 uses practically no transitional devices to guide the reader.
college-writing-004395.zh: 此外，论文 1 几乎不使用过渡设备来指导读者。

college-writing-004396.en: These two essays lead us to the third base of effective writing: coherence.
college-writing-004396.zh: 这两篇文章引出了有效写作的第三个基础：连贯性。

college-writing-004397.en: All the supporting ideas and sentences in a paper must be organized so that they cohere, or “stick together.”
college-writing-004397.zh: 论文中的所有支持性想法和句子都必须组织起来，以便它们连贯或“团结在一起”。

college-writing-004398.en: As has been discussed in Chapter 4, key techniques for tying together the material in a paper include a clear method of organization (such as time order or emphatic order), transitions, and other connecting words.
college-writing-004398.zh: 正如第 4 章中所讨论的，将论文中的材料捆绑在一起的关键技术包括清晰的组织方法（例如时间顺序或强调顺序）、过渡和其他连接词。

college-writing-004399.en: Revising for Coherence On a separate sheet of paper, revise one of the three supporting paragraphs in “Harmful Effects of Watching Television” by providing a clear method of organizing the material and transitional words.
college-writing-004399.zh: 修改另一张纸上的连贯性，通过提供清晰的材料和过渡词的组织方法来修改“看电视的有害影响”中的三个支持段落之一。

college-writing-004400.en: Base 4: Sentence Skills Understanding Sentence Skills Following are the opening paragraphs from two essays.
college-writing-004400.zh: 基础 4：句子技巧 理解句子技能 以下是两篇文章的开场白。

college-writing-004401.en: Both are unified, supported, and organized, but one version communicates more clearly and effectively.
college-writing-004401.zh: 两者都是统一的、支持的和有组织的，但一种版本的沟通更清晰、更有效。

college-writing-004406.en: 1 Revenge is one of those things that many people enjoys.
college-writing-004406.zh: 1. 复仇是许多人喜欢的事情之一。

college-writing-004407.en: 2 People don’t like to talk about it, though.
college-writing-004407.zh: 2. 不过，人们不喜欢谈论它。

college-writing-004408.en: 3 Just the same, there is nothing more tempting, more satisfying, or with the reward of a bit of revenge.
college-writing-004408.zh: 3. 同样，没有什么比复仇更诱人、更令人满意或有回报的回报了。

college-writing-004409.en: 4 The purpose is not to harm the victims.

college-writing-004410.en: 5 But to let them know that they have been doing something that is upsetting.
college-writing-004410.zh: 5. 但是让他们知道他们一直在做令人不安的事情。

college-writing-004411.en: 6 Careful plotting can provide relief from bothersom coworkers, gossiping friends, or nagging family members.
college-writing-004411.zh: 6. 仔细的绘图可以缓解麻烦的同事、八卦的朋友或唠叨的家人。

college-writing-004412.en: 7 Coworkers who make comments about the fact that a person is always fifteen minutes late for work can be taken care of very simply.
college-writing-004412.zh: 7. 同事们评论一个人总是迟到十五分钟的事实可以得到非常简单的照顾。

college-writing-004413.en: 8 The first thing that a person seeking revenge should do is to get up extra early one day.
college-writing-004413.zh: 8. 一个寻求报复的人应该做的第一件事就是有一天要早起。

college-writing-004414.en: 9 Before the sun comes up, they should drive to each coworker’s house, park near the coworker’s car, reach under the hood of the car, and disconnected the wire on the pos.
college-writing-004414.zh: 9. 在太阳升起之前，他们应该开车到每个同事的家，停在同事的车附近，到达汽车的引擎盖下，并断开 POS 上的电线。

college-writing-004416.en: 10 The car will be unharmed, but it will not start.
college-writing-004416.zh: 10. 汽车将不受伤害，但不会启动。

college-writing-004417.en: 11 All of the victims will be late for work on the same day.
college-writing-004417.zh: 11. 所有受害者将在同一天上班迟到。

college-writing-004418.en: 12If the person seeking revenge is really lucky, the boss might notice that no one else is on time and will reward the person who did show up.
college-writing-004418.zh: 12如果寻求报复的人真的很幸运，老板可能会注意到没有其他人准时并且会奖励出现的人。

college-writing-004419.en: 13 Later if guilt becomes an issue anonymous calls to the coworkers to tell them how to get their car running again may help ease those feelings. . . .
college-writing-004419.zh: 13. 稍后，如果内疚成为一个问题，匿名呼吁同事告诉他们如何让他们的汽车再次运转可能有助于缓解这些感觉。 。 。 。

college-writing-004422.en: Revenge is one of those things that many people enjoy.
college-writing-004422.zh: 复仇是许多人喜欢的事情之一。

college-writing-004423.en: People don’t like to talk about it, though.
college-writing-004423.zh: 不过，人们不喜欢谈论它。

college-writing-004424.en: Just the same, there is nothing more tempting, more satisfying, or more rewarding than a bit of revenge.
college-writing-004424.zh: 同样，没有什么比一点报复更诱人、更令人满意或更有价值的了。

college-writing-004425.en: The purpose is not to harm the victims but to let them know that they have been doing something that is upsetting.
college-writing-004425.zh: 目的不是伤害受害者，而是让他们知道他们一直在做令人不安的事情。

college-writing-004426.en: Careful plotting can provide relief from bothersome coworkers, gossiping friends, or nagging family members.
college-writing-004426.zh: 仔细的绘图可以缓解麻烦的同事、八卦的朋友或唠叨的家人。

college-writing-004427.en: Coworkers who make comments about the fact that a person is always fifteen minutes late for work can be taken care of very simply.
college-writing-004427.zh: 同事们评论一个人总是迟到十五分钟的事实可以得到非常简单的照顾。

college-writing-004428.en: The first thing that a person seeking revenge should do is to get up extra early one day.
college-writing-004428.zh: 一个寻求报复的人应该做的第一件事就是有一天要早起。

college-writing-004429.en: Before the sun comes up, they should drive to each coworker’s house, park near the coworker’s car, reach under the hood of the car, and disconnect the wire on the positive battery terminal.
college-writing-004429.zh: 在太阳升起之前，他们应该开车到每个同事的家，停在同事的车附近，到达汽车的引擎盖下，并断开电池正极端子上的电线。

college-writing-004430.en: The car will be unharmed, but it will not start.
college-writing-004430.zh: 汽车将不受伤害，但不会启动。

college-writing-004431.en: All of the victims will be late for work on the same day.
college-writing-004431.zh: 所有受害者将在同一天上班迟到。

college-writing-004432.en: If the person seeking revenge is really lucky, the boss might notice that no one else is on time and will reward the person who did show up.
college-writing-004432.zh: 如果寻求报复的人真的很幸运，老板可能会注意到没有其他人准时，并且会奖励确实出现的人。

college-writing-004433.en: Later, if guilt becomes an issue, anonymous calls to the coworkers to tell them how to get their cars running again may help ease those feelings. . . .
college-writing-004433.zh: 后来，如果内疚成为一个问题，匿名呼吁同事告诉他们如何让他们的汽车再次运转可能有助于缓解这些感觉。 。 。 。

college-writing-004435.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 163
college-writing-004435.zh: 第6章 修订论文的四个基础 163

college-writing-004437.en: Essay makes its point more clearly and effectively because
college-writing-004437.zh: 论文更清楚、更有效地表达了它的观点，因为

college-writing-004439.en: explanation: Essay 2 is more effective because it uses sentence skills, the fourth base of competent writing.
college-writing-004439.zh: 解释：论文 2 更有效，因为它使用了句子技巧，这是能力写作的第四个基础。

college-writing-004440.en: Here are the sentence-skills mistakes in essay 1: • The title should not be set off in quotation marks.
college-writing-004440.zh: 以下是论文 1 中的句子技巧错误： • 标题不应以引号引号。

college-writing-004441.en: • The first letter of the title should be capitalized.
college-writing-004441.zh: • 标题的第一个字母应大写。

college-writing-004442.en: • The plural subject people in sentence 1 should have a plural verb: enjoys should be enjoy.
college-writing-004442.zh: • 句子 1 中的复数主语 people 应该有一个复数动词：享受应该是享受。

college-writing-004443.en: • There is a lack of parallelism in sentence 3: with the reward of should be more rewarding.
college-writing-004443.zh: • 第 3 句缺乏平行性：与奖励应该更有回报。

college-writing-004444.en: • Word group 5 is a fragment; it can be corrected by attaching it to the previous sentence.
college-writing-004444.zh: • 单词组 5 是一个片段； 可以通过将它附加到上一句话来纠正它。

college-writing-004445.en: • The word bothersom in sentence 6 is misspelled; it should be bothersome.
college-writing-004445.zh: • 第 6 句中的麻烦一词拼错了； 应该很麻烦。

college-writing-004446.en: • The word disconnected in sentence 9 should be disconnect to be consistent in tense with reach, the other verb in the sentence.
college-writing-004446.zh: • 句子 9 中断开连接的单词应断开连接，以与 REACH 一致，句子中的另一个动词。

college-writing-004448.en: in sentence 9 should be spelled out in full: positive.
college-writing-004448.zh: 在第 9 句中应完整拼写：积极。

college-writing-004449.en: • Commas must be added in sentence 13 to set off the interrupting words.
college-writing-004449.zh: • 必须在句子 13 中添加逗号以启动中断词。

college-writing-004450.en: • The word car in sentence 13 needs to be changed to agree with their and coworkers.
college-writing-004450.zh: • 第 13 句中的 car 一词需要更改为与他们和同事达成一致。

college-writing-004451.en: Revising for Sentence Skills Here are the final three paragraphs from the two essays.
college-writing-004451.zh: 修改句子技巧这里是两篇文章的最后三段。

college-writing-004452.en: Edit the sentences in the first essay to make the corrections needed.
college-writing-004452.zh: 编辑第一篇文章中的句子以进行所需的更正。

college-writing-004453.en: Note that comparing essays 1 and 2 will help you locate the mistakes.
college-writing-004453.zh: 请注意，比较论文 1 和 2 将帮助您找到错误。

college-writing-004454.en: This activity will also help you identify some of the sentence skills you may want to review in Part 4.
college-writing-004454.zh: 此活动还将帮助您确定您可能希望在第 4 部分中复习的一些句子技能。

college-writing-004497.en: The plan works equally well for male or female friends.
college-writing-004497.zh: 该计划同样适用于男性或女性朋友。

college-writing-004501.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 165
college-writing-004501.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 165

college-writing-004502.en: Parents and siblings can also be victims of harmless revenge, especially when they have been really annoying.
college-writing-004502.zh: 父母和兄弟姐妹也可能成为无害报复的受害者，尤其是当他们真的很烦人的时候。

college-writing-004503.en: It may be just the way to make them quiet down for a while.
college-writing-004503.zh: 这可能只是让他们安静一段时间的方法。

college-writing-004504.en: The dinner table, where most of the nagging probably happens, is a likely place.
college-writing-004504.zh: 餐桌上可能发生的大部分唠叨，可能是一个地方。

college-writing-004505.en: Just before the meal begins, the person should throw a handful of raisins into the food.
college-writing-004505.zh: 就在饭菜开始之前，这个人应该把一把葡萄干扔进食物里。

college-writing-004506.en: After about five minutes, once everyone has begun to eat, the person should then begin to make odd noises and yell, “Bugs!”
college-writing-004506.zh: 大约五分钟后，一旦每个人都开始吃饭，这个人就应该开始发出奇怪的声音并大喊：“虫子！”

college-writing-004507.en: The others will all dump their food in the disposal, jump into the car, and head quickly for McDonald’s.
college-writing-004507.zh: 其他人都将把他们的食物倒进处置，跳进车里，然后迅速前往麦当劳。

college-writing-004508.en: After they leave, the meal will be quiet and peaceful.
college-writing-004508.zh: 他们离开后，这顿饭将变得安静祥和。

college-writing-004509.en: Well-planned revenge does not have to hurt anyone.
college-writing-004509.zh: 精心策划的报复不必伤害任何人。

college-writing-004510.en: The object is simply to let other people know that they are being a bother.
college-writing-004510.zh: 目的只是让其他人知道他们是一个麻烦。

college-writing-004511.en: Anyone who plans revenge should remember, though, to stay on guard after completing the revenge.
college-writing-004511.zh: 不过，任何计划复仇的人都应该记住，在完成复仇后保持警惕。

college-writing-004512.en: The reason for this is simple.

college-writing-004513.en: Coworkers, friends, and family can also plan revenge.
college-writing-004513.zh: 同事、朋友和家人也可以计划复仇。

college-writing-004514.en: Practice in Using the Four Bases

college-writing-004515.en: You are now familiar with four standards, or bases, of effective writing: unity, support, coherence, and sentence skills.
college-writing-004515.zh: 您现在熟悉有效写作的四个标准或基础：团结、支持、连贯性和句子技能。

college-writing-004516.en: In this section you will expand and strengthen your understanding of the four bases as you evaluate and revise essays for each of them.
college-writing-004516.zh: 在本节中，您将在评估和修改每个基础的论文时扩展和加强您对这四个基础的理解。

college-writing-004517.en: Revising Essays for Unity Both of the following essays contain irrelevant sentences that do not relate to the thesis of the essay or support the topic sentence of the paragraph in which they appear.
college-writing-004517.zh: 为统一性修改论文 以下两篇文章都包含与论文的论文或支持它们出现的段落的 主题句 无关的句子。

college-writing-004518.en: Cross out the irrelevant sentences and write the numbers of those sentences in the spaces provided.
college-writing-004518.zh: 划掉不相关的句子，并在提供的空格中写下这些句子的编号。

college-writing-004521.en: 1 For the past three summers, I have played first base on a softball team known as the Browns.
college-writing-004521.zh: 1. 在过去的三个夏天，我在一支被称为布朗队的垒球队打了一垒。

college-writing-004522.en: 2We play a long schedule, including playoffs, and everybody takes the games pretty seriously.
college-writing-004522.zh: 2我们的赛程很长，包括季后赛，每个人都非常重视比赛。

college-writing-004523.en: 3In that respect, we’re no different from any other of the thousand or so teams in our city.
college-writing-004523.zh: 3在这方面，我们与我们城市的数千支球队中的任何其他球队没有什么不同。

college-writing-004524.en: 4 But in one respect, we are different.
college-writing-004524.zh: 4. 但在一方面，我们是不同的。

college-writing-004525.en: 5In an all-male league, we have a woman on the team — me. 6Thus I’ve had a chance to observe something about human nature by seeing how the men have treated me. 7Some have been disbelieving; some have been patronizing; and, fortunately, some have simply accepted me.
college-writing-004525.zh: 5 在全男性联赛中，我们有一个女人——我。 6因此，我有机会通过看到男人如何对待我来观察一些关于人性的事情。 7有些人一直不信； 有些人一直在光顾； 而且，幸运的是，有些人只是接受了我。

college-writing-004529.en: The number of the irrelevant sentence:

college-writing-004530.en: The number of the irrelevant sentence:

college-writing-004532.en: 8 One new team in the league was particularly flabbergasted to see me start the game at first base.
college-writing-004532.zh: 8. 联盟中的一支新球队看到我在一垒开始比赛特别震惊。

college-writing-004533.en: 9 Nobody on the Comets had commented one way or the other when he saw me warming up, but playing in the actual game was another story.
college-writing-004533.zh: 9. 当他看到我热身时，彗星上的任何人都没有发表评论，但在实际游戏中玩耍是另一回事。

college-writing-004534.en: 10 The Comets’ first-base coach leaned over to me with a disbelieving grin and said, “You mean, you’re starting, and those three guys are on the bench?” 11I nodded and he shrugged, still amazed.
college-writing-004534.zh: 10. 彗星队的一垒教练带着难以置信的笑容靠在我身边说：“你的意思是，你开始了，这三个人在替补席上？” 11我点点头，他耸了耸肩，仍然惊讶。

college-writing-004535.en: 12He probably thought I was the manager’s wife.
college-writing-004535.zh: 12他可能以为我是经理的妻子。

college-writing-004536.en: 13 When I came up to bat, the Comet pitcher smiled and called to his outfielders to move way in on me.
college-writing-004536.zh: 13. 当我上来击球时，彗星投手微笑着呼唤他的外野手向我移动。

college-writing-004537.en: 15I used to work out on the exercise machines at a local health club until it closed, and now I lift weights at home a couple of times a week.
college-writing-004537.zh: 15 我过去常常在当地一家健身俱乐部锻炼健身器材，直到它关闭，现在我每周在家里举重几次。

college-writing-004538.en: 16I wiped the smirks off their faces with a line drive double over the left fielder’s head.
college-writing-004538.zh: 16i 在左外野手的头上用线路驱动器擦去了他们脸上的假笑。

college-writing-004539.en: 17 The next game, we played another new team, the Argyles, and their attitude was patronizing.
college-writing-004539.zh: 17. 下一场比赛，我们与另一支新球队 Argyles 比赛，他们的态度是光顾的。

college-writing-004540.en: 18 The Argyles had seen me take batting practice, so they didn’t do anything so rash as to draw their outfield way in.
college-writing-004540.zh: 18. Argyles 看到我进行击球练习，所以他们没有做任何事情来吸引他们的外场方式。

college-writing-004541.en: 19 They had respect for my ability as a player.
college-writing-004541.zh: 19. 他们尊重我作为球员的能力。

college-writing-004542.en: 20 However, they tried to annoy me with phony concern.
college-writing-004542.zh: 20. 然而，他们试图用虚假的担忧来惹恼我。

college-writing-004543.en: 21 For example, a redheaded Argyle got on base in the first inning and said to me, “You’d better be careful, hon.
college-writing-004543.zh: 21. 例如，一个红发的 Argyle 在第一局就上垒，对我说：“你最好小心点，亲爱的。

college-writing-004544.en: 25 Well, this delicate little girl survived the season without injury, which is more than I can say for some of the he-men on the Argyles.
college-writing-004544.zh: 25. 好吧，这个精致的小女孩没有受伤地活了下来，这对我所能说的对阿盖尔斯的一些赫斯曼来说是无法说的。

college-writing-004545.en: 26 Happily, most of the teams in the league have accepted me, just as the Browns did.
college-writing-004545.zh: 26. 令人高兴的是，联盟中的大多数球队都接受了我，就像布朗队一样。

college-writing-004546.en: 27 The men on the Browns coached and criticized me (and occasionally cursed me) just like anyone else.
college-writing-004546.zh: 27. 布朗队上的人像其他人一样指导和批评我（偶尔会诅咒我）。

college-writing-004547.en: 28 Because I’m a religious person, I don’t approve of cursing, but I don’t say anything about it to my teammates.
college-writing-004547.zh: 28. 因为我是一个虔诚的人，我不赞成诅咒，但我不会对我的队友说任何话。

college-writing-004548.en: 29 They are not amazed when I get a hit or
