college-writing-004728.en: if it were a defect I could do nothing about.
college-writing-004728.zh: 如果这是一个缺陷，我无能为力。

college-writing-004729.en: 15 With my good grades, I could have chosen almost any major the college offered, but I had limited my goal to teaching kindergarten because I felt that little children wouldn’t judge how I looked.
college-writing-004729.zh: 15. 凭借我的好成绩，我几乎可以选择学院提供的任何专业，但我的目标仅限于教幼儿园，因为我觉得小孩子不会评判我的外表。

college-writing-004730.en: 16 Once I was no longer overweight, I realized that I love working with all sorts of people.
college-writing-004730.zh: 16. 一旦我不再超重，我意识到我喜欢与各种各样的人一起工作。

college-writing-004731.en: 17I became a campus guide and even had small parts in college theater productions.
college-writing-004731.zh: 17i 成为校园向导，甚至在大学戏剧作品中占有一小部分。

college-writing-004732.en: 18As a result, last year I changed my major to public relations.
college-writing-004732.zh: 18 结果，去年我将专业改为公共关系。

college-writing-004733.en: 19 The area fascinates me, and I now have good job prospects there.
college-writing-004733.zh: 19. 该地区让我着迷，我现在在那里有很好的工作前景。

college-writing-004734.en: 20I have also become more emotionally honest.

college-writing-004735.en: 21 Rose, at the college counseling center, helped me see that my “fat and jolly” personality had been false.
college-writing-004735.zh: 21. 罗斯在大学咨询中心帮助我看到我的“肥胖而快乐”的性格是错误的。

college-writing-004736.en: 22I was afraid others would reject me if I didn’t always go along with their suggestions.
college-writing-004736.zh: 22如果我不总是同意他们的建议，我害怕别人会拒绝我。

college-writing-004737.en: 23I eventually put Rose’s advice to the test.
college-writing-004737.zh: 23我最终对罗斯的建议进行了测试。

college-writing-004738.en: 24My roommates were planning an evening at a Greek restaurant.
college-writing-004738.zh: 24 我的室友正计划在一家希腊餐厅度过一个晚上。

college-writing-004739.en: 25I loved the restaurant’s atmosphere, but there wasn’t much I liked on the menu.
college-writing-004739.zh: 25我喜欢餐厅的氛围，但菜单上没有我喜欢的东西。

college-writing-004740.en: 26 Finally, in a shaky voice I said, “Actually, I’m not crazy about lamb. 27 How about Chinese food?” 28They scolded me for not mentioning it before, and we had dinner at a Chinese restaurant.
college-writing-004740.zh: 26. 最后，我用颤抖的声音说：“其实，我不为羊肉发疯。27中国菜怎么样？” 28他们骂我之前没有提过，我们在中餐馆吃过晚饭。

college-writing-004741.en: 29We all agreed it was one of our best evenings out.
college-writing-004741.zh: 29我们都同意这是我们最好的夜晚之一。

college-writing-004742.en: 30 Fortunately, the low point of my first year turned out to be the turning point, leading to what promises to be an exciting senior year.
college-writing-004742.zh: 30. 幸运的是，我第一年的低谷变成了转折点，导致了一个令人兴奋的大四。

college-writing-004743.en: 31 Greg’s cruel joke became a strange sort of favor, and I’ve gone from wanting to resign from the human race to welcoming each day as a source of fresh adventure and self-discovery.
college-writing-004743.zh: 31. 格雷格残酷的笑话变成了一种奇怪的方式，我已经从想要从人类中辞职，变成了欢迎每一天，作为新的冒险和自我发现的源泉。

college-writing-004744.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 175
college-writing-004744.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 175

college-writing-004745.en: Revising Essays for All Four Bases: Unity, Support, Coherence, and Sentence Skills In this activity, you will evaluate and revise two essays in terms of all four bases: unity, support, coherence, and sentence skills.
college-writing-004745.zh: 修改所有四个基础的论文：统一、支持、连贯性和句子技能 在本活动中，您将根据所有四个基础评估和修改两篇论文：团结、支持、连贯性和句子技能。

college-writing-004746.zh: 评论遵循每个支持段落。

college-writing-004747.en: Circle the letter of the statement that applies in each case.
college-writing-004747.zh: 圈出适用于每种情况的语句的字母。

college-writing-004750.en: I had lived my whole life not knowing what chiggers are.
college-writing-004750.zh: 我一生都在不知道什么是木屑。

college-writing-004751.en: I thought they were probably a type of insect someone might encounter on an Amazon River cruise.
college-writing-004751.zh: 我以为它们可能是有人在亚马逊河游轮上可能遇到的一种昆虫。

college-writing-004752.en: I never had any real reason to care, until one day last summer.
college-writing-004752.zh: 直到去年夏天的一天，我才有真正的理由去关心。

college-writing-004753.en: Within twenty-four hours, I had vividly experienced what chigger bites are, learned how to treat them, and learned how to prevent them.
college-writing-004753.zh: 在二十四小时内，我生动地体验了什么是桤木咬伤，学会了如何治疗它们，并学会了如何预防它们。

college-writing-004754.en: First of all, I learned that chiggers are the larvae of tiny mites found in the woods and that their bites are always multiple and cause intense itching.
college-writing-004754.zh: 首先，我了解到小穴是在树林中发现的小螨虫的幼虫，它们的叮咬总是多发的，会引起剧烈的瘙痒。

college-writing-004755.en: A beautiful summer day seemed perfect for a walk in the woods.
college-writing-004755.zh: 一个美丽的夏日似乎非常适合在树林里散步。

college-writing-004756.en: I am definitely not a city person, for I couldn’t stand to be surrounded by people, noise, and concrete.
college-writing-004756.zh: 我绝对不是一个城市的人，因为我无法忍受被人、噪音和混凝土所包围。

college-writing-004757.en: As I walked through the ferns and pines, I noticed what appeared to be a dusting of reddish seeds or pollen on my slacks.
college-writing-004757.zh: 当我穿过蕨类植物和松树时，我注意到我的裤子上似乎有一层红色的种子或花粉的灰尘。

college-writing-004758.en: Looking more closely, I realized that each speck was a tiny insect.
college-writing-004758.zh: 更仔细地看，我意识到每个斑点都是一只小昆虫。

college-writing-004759.en: I casually brushed off a few and gave them no further thought.
college-writing-004759.zh: 我随便刷了几下，没有再考虑。

college-writing-004760.en: I woke up the next morning feeling like a victim staked to an anthill by an enemy wise in the ways of torture.
college-writing-004760.zh: 第二天早上，我醒来时感觉就像一个受害者，被一个智者在酷刑的方式上赌上了蚁丘。

college-writing-004761.en: Most of my body was speckled with measlelike bumps that at the slightest touch burned and itched like a mosquito bite raised to the twentieth power.
college-writing-004761.zh: 我的大部分身体都散布着麻疹状的肿块，只要轻轻一触，就会像被蚊虫叮咬一样发痒，就像被提升到第 20 次的力量一样。

college-writing-004762.en: When antiseptics and calamine lotion failed to help, I raced to my doctor for emergency aid.
college-writing-004762.zh: 当防腐剂和炉甘石洗剂未能提供帮助时，我跑到我的医生那里寻求紧急援助。

college-writing-004764.zh: 第 2 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004766.en: Paragraph 2 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004766.zh: 第 2 段在一个关键点缺少 支撑细节。

college-writing-004768.en: Time order in paragraph 2 is confused.
college-writing-004768.zh: 第 2 段中的时间顺序混淆了。

college-writing-004770.zh: 第 2 段包含两个运行程序。

college-writing-004771.en: Healing the bites of chiggers, as the doctor diagnosed them to be, is not done overnight.
college-writing-004771.zh: 正如医生诊断出的那样，治愈 Chiggers 的叮咬不是一夜之间完成的。

college-writing-004772.en: It seems that there is really no wonder drug or commercial product to help.
college-writing-004772.zh: 似乎真的没有什么奇怪的药物或商业产品可以提供帮助。

college-writing-004773.en: The victim must rely on a primitive home remedy and mostly wait out the course of the painful bites.
college-writing-004773.zh: 受害者必须依靠原始的家庭疗法，并且主要等待痛苦的叮咬过程。

college-writing-004774.en: First, the doctor explained, the skin must be bathed carefully with warm soapy water.
college-writing-004774.zh: 首先，医生解释说，皮肤必须用温热的肥皂水小心地沐浴。

college-writing-004775.en: An antihistamine spray applied several hours later will not cure the bites but will soothe the intense itching and help prevent infection.
college-writing-004775.zh: 几小时后使用抗组胺药喷雾不会治愈咬伤，但可以缓解剧烈的瘙痒并有助于防止感染。

college-writing-004780.en: A few days after the treatment, the bites finally healed.
college-writing-004780.zh: 治疗后几天，咬伤终于痊愈了。

college-writing-004781.en: Although I was in pain, and desperate for relief, I followed the doctor’s instructions.
college-writing-004781.zh: 虽然我很痛苦，迫切希望得到缓解，但我还是听从了医生的指示。

college-writing-004783.zh: 第 3 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004785.en: Paragraph 3 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004785.zh: 第 3 段在一个关键点缺少 支撑细节。

college-writing-004787.en: Time order in paragraph 3 is confused.
college-writing-004787.zh: 第 3 段中的时间顺序混淆了。

college-writing-004789.zh: 第 3 段包含一个片段。

college-writing-004790.en: Most important of all, I learned what to do to prevent getting chigger bites in the future.
college-writing-004790.zh: 最重要的是，我学会了如何防止将来被咬伤。

college-writing-004791.en: Mainly, of course, stay out of the woods in the summertime.
college-writing-004791.zh: 当然，主要是在夏季远离树林。

college-writing-004792.en: But if the temptation is too great on an especially beautiful day, I’ll be sure to wear the right type of clothing, like a long-sleeved shirt, long pants, knee socks, and closed shoes.
college-writing-004792.zh: 但如果在特别美好的日子里的诱惑太大，我一定会穿合适的衣服，比如长袖衬衫、长裤、膝袜和封闭的鞋子。

college-writing-004793.en: In addition, I’ll cover myself with clouds of superstrength insect repellent.
college-writing-004793.zh: 此外，我会用超强力驱虫剂的云遮住自己。

college-writing-004794.en: I will then shower thoroughly as soon as I get home, I also will probably burn all my clothes if I notice even one suspicious red speck.
college-writing-004794.zh: 然后我一回到家就彻底淋浴，如果我注意到一个可疑的红色斑点，我可能也会烧掉我所有的衣服。

college-writing-004796.zh: 第 4 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004798.en: Paragraph 4 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004798.zh: 第 4 段在一个关键点缺乏 支撑细节。

college-writing-004802.en: Paragraph 4 contains a run-on and a fragment.
college-writing-004802.zh: 第 4 段包含一个连续和一个片段。

college-writing-004803.en: I will never forget my lessons on the cause, cure, and prevention of chigger bites.
college-writing-004803.zh: 我永远不会忘记我的课程，治愈和预防刺伤的原因、治疗和预防。

college-writing-004804.en: I’d gladly accept the challenge of rattlesnakes and scorpions in the wilds of the West but will never again confront a siege of chiggers in the pinewoods.
college-writing-004804.zh: 我很乐意接受西方荒野中响尾蛇和蝎子的挑战，但再也不会在松林中遇到一群小孩的围攻。

college-writing-004805.en: Navigating the Hunt for a Job

college-writing-004806.en: As economies fluctuate and job markets change, it is important for people to know how to navigate the process of job hunting.
college-writing-004806.zh: 随着经济的波动和就业市场的变化，人们了解如何驾驭求职过程非常重要。

college-writing-004807.en: Getting a new job starts long before the résumé or cover letter, although they are both very important.
college-writing-004807.zh: 找一份新工作很久就在简历或求职信之前开始，尽管它们都非常重要。

college-writing-004808.en: Good hunters learn about the companies they are applying to, put together strong application packets, and extensively prepare for the interviews.
college-writing-004808.zh: 优秀的猎人了解他们申请的公司，整理强大的申请包，并为面试做广泛的准备。

college-writing-004809.en: Securing a good job begins even before the application process.
college-writing-004809.zh: 甚至在申请过程之前就开始获得好工作。

college-writing-004810.en: Seekers should learn about the company they are applying to because knowing information about the company shows interest and conscientiousness.
college-writing-004810.zh: 寻求者应该了解他们申请的公司，因为了解有关公司的信息显示出兴趣和尽责。

college-writing-004811.en: Applicants who know what the company’s history is, what the company does, and what is expected of employees will demonstrate desired attitudes that many companies want.
college-writing-004811.zh: 了解公司历史、公司做什么以及对员工的期望的申请人将表现出许多公司想要的期望态度。

college-writing-004813.en: Chapter 6 Four Bases for Revising Essays 177
college-writing-004813.zh: 第6章 修改论文的四个基础 177

college-writing-004815.en: Also, through research, a job seeker might learn that a potential employer spends 10 percent of the gross income each year on a specific program for underserved children.
college-writing-004815.zh: 此外，通过研究，求职者可能会了解到，潜在雇主每年将总收入的 10% 用于服务不足的儿童的特定计划。

college-writing-004816.en: One company in Chicago spent 20 percent of its gross income on a program for children living in poverty.
college-writing-004816.zh: 芝加哥的一家公司将其总收入的 20% 用于一项针对贫困儿童的计划。

college-writing-004817.en: People who really want a job with that company will then learn about the charitable programs that are important to that company, understand that program, and accept that a job with this company will mean possibly working with that program.
college-writing-004817.zh: 然后，真正想在该公司工作的人将了解对该公司很重要的慈善计划，了解该计划，并接受该公司的工作意味着可能与该计划合作。

college-writing-004819.zh: 第 2 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004821.en: Paragraph 2 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004821.zh: 第 2 段在一个关键点缺少 支撑细节。

college-writing-004825.en: Paragraph 2 contains one fragment and one run-on.
college-writing-004825.zh: 第 2 段有一处不完整句和一处粘连句。

college-writing-004826.en: Once job seekers have researched potential employers, the next step is to prepare strong application packets.
college-writing-004826.zh: 一旦求职者研究了潜在的雇主，下一步是准备强大的申请包。

college-writing-004827.en: This means that an applicant must understand the skills and education requirements listed in the job descriptions and properly fill out the applications.
college-writing-004827.zh: 这意味着申请人必须了解职位描述中列出的技能和教育要求，并正确填写申请表。

college-writing-004828.en: If a job requires a degree in engineering, but the applicant doesn’t have a degree.
college-writing-004828.zh: 如果工作需要工程学位，但申请人没有学位。

college-writing-004829.en: This may not be the right job.
college-writing-004829.zh: 这可能不是合适的工作。

college-writing-004830.en: After the applicant has found a job that is a right fit, it is important to properly fill out the application.
college-writing-004830.zh: 在申请人找到合适的工作后，正确填写申请非常重要。

college-writing-004831.en: An applicant should double check that every question is answered, all the information is correct, and no spelling or grammar mistakes are made.
college-writing-004831.zh: 申请人应仔细检查每个问题是否得到回答，所有信息都是正确的，并且不会出现拼写或语法错误。

college-writing-004832.en: Leaving off a signature or forgetting to fill in areas will not impress the potential employer.
college-writing-004832.zh: 取消签名或忘记填写区域不会给潜在雇主留下深刻印象。

college-writing-004833.en: Cover letters should also be included in the packet they are the first introduction to the applicant and should address the specifics of the job, laying out why the candidate is the best choice.
college-writing-004833.zh: 求职信也应包含在包裹中，它们是对申请人的第一个介绍，并应解决工作的具体情况，说明候选人是最佳选择的原因。

college-writing-004834.en: Cover letters should be error free and well-articulated.
college-writing-004834.zh: 求职信应无错误且清晰地表达。

college-writing-004835.en: Weak application packets that include cover letters and applications that are filled with spelling mistakes, grammar errors, and irrelevant material will hold the applicant back.
college-writing-004835.zh: 包含拼写错误、语法错误和不相关材料的求职信和申请的弱申请包将阻碍申请人。

college-writing-004836.en: Strong application packets will increase the chance of applicants’ moving on to the final step in job hunting.
college-writing-004836.zh: 强大的申请包将增加申请人进入求职的最后一步的机会。

college-writing-004838.zh: 第 3 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004840.en: Paragraph 3 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004840.zh: 第 3 段在一个关键点缺少 支撑细节。

college-writing-004844.en: Paragraph 3 contains one fragment and one run-on.
college-writing-004844.zh: 第 3 段有一处不完整句和一处粘连句。

college-writing-004845.en: The final step in navigating the process is preparing for the interviews, which includes proper grooming and practiced interviewing skills.
college-writing-004845.zh: 导航这个过程的最后一步是准备面试，其中包括适当的修饰和练习的面试技巧。

college-writing-004846.en: Clothes should be appropriate for the interview, shoes should be polished, and bodies should be groomed.
college-writing-004846.zh: 衣服要适合面试，鞋子要打磨，身体也要打扮。

college-writing-004847.en: It isn’t necessary to go out

college-writing-004850.en: and buy a $5,000 suit, but it is important not to wear flip-flops and shorts.
college-writing-004850.zh: 并购买 5,000 美元的西装，但重要的是不要穿人字拖和短裤。

college-writing-004851.en: By visiting the work place ahead of time, if possible, the interviewee can assess how employees are dressed and then wear a similar — or slightly nicer — outfit.
college-writing-004851.zh: 如果可能的话，通过提前访问工作地点，受访者可以评估员工的穿着方式，然后穿上类似或稍微更好的服装。

college-writing-004852.en: Specific interviewing skills should be practiced so that when questioned, the interviewee can eloquently and intelligently respond.
college-writing-004852.zh: 应练习具体的面试技巧，以便在受到质疑时，受访者可以雄辩而明智地做出回应。

college-writing-004853.en: Proper preparation will increase the candidate’s chance of being offered a job because a prepared interviewee often means that they will be a prepared employee.
college-writing-004853.zh: 适当的准备将增加候选人获得工作的机会，因为准备好的面试官通常意味着他们将成为一个有准备的员工。

college-writing-004855.zh: 第 4 段包含一个不相关的句子。

college-writing-004857.en: Paragraph 4 lacks supporting details at one key spot.
college-writing-004857.zh: 第 4 段在一个关键点缺乏 支撑细节。

college-writing-004861.en: Paragraph 4 contains one fragment and one run-on.
college-writing-004861.zh: 第 4 段有一处不完整句和一处粘连句。

college-writing-004862.en: By properly navigating the process of job hunting, people who are seeking a new job will stand out to potential employers.
college-writing-004862.zh: 通过正确导航求职的过程，寻找新工作的人将在潜在雇主中脱颖而出。

college-writing-004863.en: There are thousands of people looking for jobs every day, but by taking hints from the successfully employed, job seekers will have the opportunity to move from seeker to employee.
college-writing-004863.zh: 每天有成千上万的人在找工作，但通过从成功就业的人那里得到暗示，求职者将有机会从寻找者转变为员工。

college-writing-004865.en: p. 169: Source: Beck, Martha, “Conjuring Magic: How to Set Powerful Goals” December 30, 2014.
college-writing-004865.zh: P. 169：来源：贝克，玛莎，“魔术：如何设定强大的目标”，2014 年 12 月 30 日。

college-writing-004867.en: This chapter will • explain the importance of understanding the nature and length of an assignment • explain the importance of knowing your subject, your purpose, and your audience • explain the three different points of view used in writing • show you how to conduct a peer review and a personal review • provide you with a sample student essay that illustrates the writing process in action
college-writing-004867.zh: 本章将 • 解释理解作业的性质和长度的重要性 • 解释了解您的主题、您的目的和受众的重要性 • 解释写作中使用的三个不同观点 • 向您展示如何进行同行评审和个人评论 • 为您提供一个示例的学生论文，说明在行动中的写作过程

college-writing-004869.en: C H A P T E R7
college-writing-004869.zh: C h a p t e r7

college-writing-004870.en: Who do you believe is the intended audience of this advertisement?
college-writing-004870.zh: 你认为这个广告的目标受众是谁？

college-writing-004871.en: Write a description of that intended audience.
college-writing-004871.zh: 写下对目标受众的描述。

college-writing-004872.zh: 丹尼斯麦克唐纳/阿拉米 库存照片

college-writing-004873.en: by Oldest college | Ley RB A grad.
college-writing-004873.zh: 由最古老的学院 | 雷RB 一个毕业生。

college-writing-004877.zh: 180 第 1 部分 作文写作

college-writing-004878.zh: 论文开发中的重要考虑因素

college-writing-004879.en: When you begin work on particular types of essays, keep in mind several general considerations about writing; they are discussed in the following pages.
college-writing-004879.zh: 当您开始撰写特定类型的论文时，请记住有关写作的一些一般性考虑； 它们将在以下页面中讨论。

college-writing-004880.en: Understanding the Nature and Length of an Assignment In all likelihood, your college writing assignments will have a good deal of variety.
college-writing-004880.zh: 了解作业的性质和长度很可能，您的大学写作作业将有很多多样性。

college-writing-004881.en: Sometimes you will be able to write on a topic of your own choosing or on a point you discover within a given topic; at other times you may be given a very specific assignment.
college-writing-004881.zh: 有时，您将能够写下您自己选择的主题或您在给定主题中发现的一个点； 在其他时候，你可能会得到一个非常具体的任务。

college-writing-004882.en: In any case, do not start writing a paper until you know exactly what is expected.
college-writing-004882.zh: 无论如何，在您确切知道预期的内容之前，不要开始写论文。

college-writing-004883.en: First of all, be clear about what kind of paper the instructor has in mind.
college-writing-004883.zh: 首先，要清楚导师的想法是什么样的。

college-writing-004884.en: Do not hesitate to ask an instructor about an assignment.
college-writing-004884.zh: 不要犹豫，向教师询问作业。

college-writing-004885.en: If you are not sure about the nature of an assignment, other students may be confused as well.
college-writing-004885.zh: 如果您不确定作业的性质，其他学生也可能会感到困惑。

college-writing-004886.en: Most instructors are more than willing to provide an explanation.
college-writing-004886.zh: 大多数教师非常愿意提供解释。

college-writing-004887.en: They would rather spend a few minutes of class time explaining an assignment than have students turn in essays that miss the mark and therefore end up with failing grades.
college-writing-004887.zh: 他们宁愿花几分钟的课堂时间来解释一项作业，也不愿让学生上交论文，错过成绩，因此最终成绩不及格。

college-writing-004888.en: Here are some questions to ask:

college-writing-004889.en: • Should it be primarily a research paper summarizing other people’s ideas?
college-writing-004889.zh: • 它应该主要是总结他人想法的研究论文吗？

college-writing-004890.en: • Should it consist entirely of your own ideas?
college-writing-004890.zh: • 它应该完全由您自己的想法组成吗？

college-writing-004891.en: • Should it consist of a comparison of your ideas with those of a given author?
college-writing-004891.zh: • 它是否应该将您的想法与给定作者的想法进行比较？

college-writing-004893.en: Second, find out right at the start how long a paper is expected to be.
college-writing-004893.zh: 其次，在开始时找出一篇论文的预期时间。

college-writing-004894.en: Many instructors will indicate the approximate length of the papers they assign.
college-writing-004894.zh: 许多教师将指出他们分配的论文的大致长度。

college-writing-004895.en: Knowing the expected length of a paper will help you decide exactly how detailed your treatment of a subject should be.
college-writing-004895.zh: 了解论文的预期长度将帮助您确切地确定您对主题的处理应该有多详细。

college-writing-004896.en: Knowing Your Subject Whenever possible, try to write on a subject that interests you.
college-writing-004896.zh: 尽可能了解您的主题，尝试写下您感兴趣的主题。

college-writing-004897.en: You will then find it easier to put more time into your work.
college-writing-004897.zh: 然后，您会发现在工作中投入更多时间更容易。

college-writing-004898.en: Even more important, try to write on a subject that you already know something about.
college-writing-004898.zh: 更重要的是，试着写一个你已经知道的主题。

college-writing-004899.en: If you do not have direct experience with the subject, you should at least have indirect experience─ knowledge gained through thinking, reading, or talking about the subject as well as from prewriting.
college-writing-004899.zh: 如果你没有直接的主题经验，你至少应该有间接的经验——通过思考、阅读或谈论这个主题以及预先写作获得的知识。

college-writing-004900.en: If you are asked to write on a topic about which you have no experience or knowledge, do whatever research is required to gain the background information you may need.
college-writing-004900.zh: 如果您被要求撰写您没有经验或知识的主题，请进行任何研究以获得您可能需要的背景信息。

college-writing-004901.en: Part 3 will show you how to use sources as support in your essays.
college-writing-004901.zh: 第 3 部分将向您展示如何在论文中使用资源作为支持。

college-writing-004902.en: Without direct or indirect experience, or the information you gain through research, you may not be able to provide the specific evidence needed to develop an essay.
college-writing-004902.zh: 如果没有直接或间接的经验，或者您通过研究获得的信息，您可能无法提供撰写论文所需的具体证据。

college-writing-004904.en: Knowing Your Purpose and Audience As was briefly introduced in Chapter 1, it is crucial to know both your purpose for writing and the audience who will be reading your work.
college-writing-004904.zh: 了解您的目标和受众 正如第 1 章中简要介绍的那样，了解您的写作目的和将阅读您的作品的观众至关重要。

college-writing-004906.en: The three most common purposes of writing are to inform, to persuade, and to entertain.
college-writing-004906.zh: 写作的三个最常见的目的是告知、说服和娱乐。

college-writing-004908.en: • To inform─to give information about a subject.
college-writing-004908.zh: • 通知——提供有关主题的信息。

college-writing-004909.en: Authors writing to inform want to provide facts that will explain or teach something to readers.
college-writing-004909.zh: 写作告知的作者希望提供能够向读者解释或教导内容的事实。

college-writing-004910.en: For example, an informative paragraph about sandwiches might begin, “Eating food between two slices of bread─a sandwich─is a practice that has its origins in eighteenth-century England.” • To persuade─to convince the reader to agree with the author’s point of view on a subject.
college-writing-004910.zh: 例如，一段关于三明治的内容可能会开始，“在两片面包之间吃食物——三明治——是一种起源于 18 世纪英格兰的做法。” • 说服——说服读者同意作者对某个主题的观点。

college-writing-004911.en: Authors writing to persuade may give facts, but their main goal is to argue or prove a point to readers.
college-writing-004911.zh: 写作说服的作者可能会给出事实，但他们的主要目标是为读者争论或证明一个观点。

college-writing-004912.en: A persuasive paragraph about sandwiches might begin, “There are good reasons why every sandwich should be made with whole grain bread.” • To entertain─to amuse and delight; to appeal to the reader’s senses and imagination.
college-writing-004912.zh: 关于三明治的有说服力的段落可能会开始，“每个三明治都应该用全麦面包制作。” • 娱乐——娱乐和愉悦； 吸引读者的感官和想象力。

college-writing-004913.en: Authors write to entertain in various ways, through fiction and nonfiction.
college-writing-004913.zh: 作者通过小说和非小说以各种方式写作是为了娱乐。

college-writing-004914.en: An entertaining paragraph about sandwiches might begin, “What I wanted was a midnight snack, but what I got was better─ the biggest, most magical sandwich in the entire world.”
college-writing-004914.zh: 一段关于三明治的有趣段落可能会开始，“我想要的是午夜小吃，但我得到的更好——全世界最大、最神奇的三明治。”

college-writing-004915.zh: 考虑不同背景下的目的

college-writing-004916.en: Of course, the purpose of completing any college writing assignment is to fulfill a course requirement and get a grade.
college-writing-004916.zh: 当然，完成任何大学写作作业的目的是满足课程要求并获得成绩。

college-writing-004917.en: But all writing─whether done for a class, a job, or any other reason─is aimed at accomplishing something far more specific.
college-writing-004917.zh: 但所有的写作——无论是为课堂、工作还是任何其他原因完成的——都旨在完成更具体的事情。

college-writing-004918.en: Following are several important points to keep in mind:
college-writing-004918.zh: 以下是几个要注意的要点：

college-writing-004919.en: • In most cases, you will be given an assignment that explains or at least hints at that purpose.
college-writing-004919.zh: • 在大多数情况下，您将获得一份解释或至少暗示该目的的任务。

college-writing-004920.en: You will be able to spot clues about purpose by looking for key words in the assignment such as define, contrast, argue, illustrate, or explain causes and/or effects.
college-writing-004920.zh: 您将能够通过在作业中寻找关键词来发现有关目的的线索，例如定义、对比、争论、说明或解释原因和/或效果。

college-writing-004921.en: For example, an assignment for a history paper might ask you to explain the causes of World War I. An essay question on a biology midterm might call for the definition of photosynthesis.
college-writing-004921.zh: 例如，一篇历史论文的作业可能会要求您解释第一次世界大战的原因。关于生物学期中学期的论文问题可能需要定义光合作用。

college-writing-004922.en: A political science assignment might ask you to contrast the parliamentary system of government used in several European nations with the federal system used in the United States.
college-writing-004922.zh: 政治科学任务可能会要求您将几个欧洲国家使用的议会制政府制度与美国使用的联邦制度进行对比。

college-writing-004923.en: If you are enrolled in a technical writing course, you may be asked to describe a machine or analyze a natural or mechanical process.
college-writing-004923.zh: 如果您参加了技术写作课程，您可能会被要求描述一台机器或分析自然或机械过程。

college-writing-004924.en: Each of these tasks asks you to accomplish a specific aim.
college-writing-004924.zh: 这些任务中的每一个都要求您完成特定的目标。

college-writing-004925.en: • Having a clear idea of your purpose is just as important for the writing you do outside of college (what many call “real-world writing”).
college-writing-004925.zh: • 清楚地了解您的目标对于您在校外进行的写作同样重要（许多人称之为“现实世界写作”）。

college-writing-004928.en: say your employer asks you to write a report that recommends the purchase of a laptop from a choice of three.
college-writing-004928.zh: 假设您的雇主要求您撰写一份报告，建议您从三种中选择购买笔记本电脑。

college-writing-004929.en: You might have to contrast each on the basis of cost, ease of use, features, and reliability.
college-writing-004929.zh: 您可能必须根据成本、易用性、功能和可靠性对比。

college-writing-004930.en: Then you might have to argue that even though laptop A is more expensive than laptops B and C, it is preferable because it will work best with your company’s software.
college-writing-004930.zh: 那么你可能不得不争辩说，即使笔记本电脑 A 比笔记本电脑 B 和 C 贵，它更可取，因为它最适合您公司的软件。

college-writing-004931.en: Note that unlike a college writing assignment, the job you have been given by your employer does not specify the approaches (contrasting and arguing) you will have to take to complete the project.
college-writing-004931.zh: 请注意，与大学写作作业不同，您的雇主分配的工作没有具体说明您必须采取的方法（对比和争论）。

college-writing-004932.en: You will have to figure that out for yourself by considering the writing’s purpose before you begin.
college-writing-004932.zh: 在开始之前，您将不得不考虑写作的目的，自己弄清楚这一点。

college-writing-004933.en: • As you start gathering information for your paragraph or essay, keep your purpose in mind.
college-writing-004933.zh: • 当您开始为您的段落或论文收集信息时，请牢记您的目的。

college-writing-004934.en: You might want to read your assignment several times, looking for key words such as those mentioned above, and then summarize your purpose in a short sentence of your own on a piece of scrap paper.
college-writing-004934.zh: 您可能想多次阅读您的作业，寻找上述关键词，然后在一张废纸上用您自己的短句总结您的目的。

college-writing-004935.en: Keep this sentence in front of you throughout the prewriting stage.
college-writing-004935.zh: 在整个预写阶段，将这句话放在你面前。

college-writing-004936.en: • As noted previously, much of the writing in this book will involve some form of argumentation or persuasion.
college-writing-004936.zh: • 如前所述，本书中的大部分写作都将涉及某种形式的论证或说服。

college-writing-004937.en: You will advance a point or thesis and then support it in a variety of ways.
college-writing-004937.zh: 您将推进一个观点或论文，然后以多种方式支持它。

college-writing-004938.en: To some extent, also, you will write papers to inform─to provide readers with information about a particular subject.
college-writing-004938.zh: 在某种程度上，您还将撰写论文以告知——为读者提供有关特定主题的信息。

college-writing-004939.en: And since, in practice, writing often combines purposes, you might also find yourself providing vivid or humorous details in order to entertain your readers.
college-writing-004939.zh: 由于在实践中，写作通常结合了目的，您可能还会发现自己提供生动或幽默的细节以娱乐您的读者。

college-writing-004941.en: The audience for a piece of writing is its reader or readers, and like purpose, audience should be considered early in the writing process.
college-writing-004941.zh: 一篇文章的受众是它的读者或读者，并且与目的一样，在写作过程的早期就应该考虑受众。

college-writing-004942.en: In college, your primary audience will be your instructor.
college-writing-004942.zh: 在大学里，你的主要受众将成为你的导师。

college-writing-004943.en: Your instructor, though, is really representative of the larger audience you should see yourself as writing for─an audience of educated adults who expect you to present your ideas in a clear, direct, organized way.
college-writing-004943.zh: 不过，您的讲师确实代表了更多受众，您应该将自己视为为受过教育的成年人的受众群体，他们希望您以清晰、直接、有组织的方式表达您的想法。

college-writing-004944.en: • Current audiences─Some instructors will also require you to share your work with other students, either in small groups or with the class as a whole.
college-writing-004944.zh: • 当前受众——一些教师还会要求您与其他学生分享您的作品，无论是小组还是整个班级。

college-writing-004945.en: In some cases, your writing will be judged on how well it informs or persuades your classmates.
college-writing-004945.zh: 在某些情况下，您的写作将根据其对同学的信息或说服程度进行评判。

college-writing-004946.en: Therefore, you must keep them in mind as you write.
college-writing-004946.zh: 因此，您在写作时必须牢记它们。

college-writing-004947.en: Other academic situations in which you will want to keep your audience in mind include writing a letter to a college newspaper to express an opinion, applying for transfer to another college, or applying for a scholarship.
college-writing-004947.zh: 您希望将受众牢记在心的其他学术情况包括给大学报纸写信以表达意见、申请转移到另一所大学或申请奖学金。

college-writing-004948.en: • Future potential audiences─After you graduate, you will have ample opportunity to write to a wide range of audiences.
college-writing-004948.zh: • 未来的潜在受众——毕业后，您将有充足的机会向广泛的受众写作。

college-writing-004949.en: This is when you will have to pay even more attention to evaluating your audience.
college-writing-004949.zh: 这是您将不得不更加关注评估受众的时候。

college-writing-004950.en: For example, careers in science and technology require employees to write to other experts, who may know a great deal about the subject.
college-writing-004950.zh: 例如，科学和技术职业要求员工写信给其他专家，他们可能对该主题非常了解。

college-writing-004951.en: On the other hand, scientists and technologists are often required to write to laypersons, whose knowledge of a subject might vary from adequate to
college-writing-004951.zh: 另一方面，科学家和技术人员经常被要求写信给外行，他们对某个主题的了解可能从足够的到

college-writing-004954.en: The same is true of those who pursue careers in business, law enforcement, the legal and medical professions, the military, education, or government work.
college-writing-004954.zh: 那些从事商业、执法、法律和医学专业、军事、教育或政府工作的人也是如此。

college-writing-004955.en: • One audience example─Let’s say you get a job as City Administrator and you have to suggest some cost-saving measures for the next year’s budget.
college-writing-004955.zh: • 一个受众示例——假设您找到了城市管理员的工作，您必须为明年的预算提出一些节省成本的措施。

college-writing-004956.en: You may be asked to write a letter explaining to the City Council which measures need to be taken and why.
college-writing-004956.zh: 您可能会被要求写一封信，向市议会解释需要采取哪些措施以及原因。

college-writing-004957.en: Not all of the City Council members may fully understand the measures, so you will likely need to include background information, essential definitions of technical language, and reasons why these specific measures will benefit the city.
college-writing-004957.zh: 并非所有市议会成员都可以完全了解这些措施，因此您可能需要包括背景信息、技术语言的基本定义以及这些具体措施有利于城市的原因。

college-writing-004958.en: You may also need to write letters to city employees about potential impacts on their jobs.
college-writing-004958.zh: 您可能还需要写信给城市员工，了解对他们工作的潜在影响。

college-writing-004959.en: In those letters, your explanation will be more straightforward and focused primarily on the needs of a particular department.
college-writing-004959.zh: 在这些信件中，您的解释将更直接，主要关注特定部门的需求。

college-writing-004960.en: Because the city is a public entity, you may need to write a presentation or explanation to help the public understand why the changes are being implemented and how these changes will benefit the public, as well as how they might result in certain adverse effects.
college-writing-004960.zh: 由于城市是公共实体，您可能需要撰写演示文稿或解释，以帮助公众了解更改实施的原因以及这些更改将如何使公众受益，以及它们如何导致某些不利影响。

college-writing-004961.en: This letter may require more of an effort to convince the readers that any inconveniences they may experience are outweighed by the cost-saving benefits.
college-writing-004961.zh: 这封信可能需要更多的努力说服读者，他们可能遇到的任何不便都被节省成本的好处所抵消。

college-writing-004963.en: Here are a few questions you should ask yourself when evaluating any audience.
college-writing-004963.zh: 以下是您在评估任何受众时应该问自己的一些问题。

college-writing-004964.en: The answers to these questions will help determine your approach to any writing project.
college-writing-004964.zh: 这些问题的答案将有助于确定您对任何写作项目的方法。

college-writing-004965.en: 1. How much does the audience already know about the subject?
college-writing-004965.zh: 1. 观众对这个主题了解多少？

college-writing-004966.en: On the one hand, if you incorrectly assume that your readers know very little, you might bore them with too much basic information.
college-writing-004966.zh: 一方面，如果您错误地假设您的读者知之甚少，您可能会厌倦他们过多的基本信息。

college-writing-004967.en: On the other hand, if you incorrectly assume that they know more than they do, you might confuse them by using unfamiliar technical terminology or neglecting to provide enough informative detail.
college-writing-004967.zh: 另一方面，如果您错误地假设他们比他们知道的更多，您可能会通过使用不熟悉的技术术语或忽略提供足够的信息细节来混淆他们。

college-writing-004968.en: If, for example, you are writing an essay focused on the features of a computer motherboard for a digital electronics class, you wouldn’t have to explain what a motherboard is.
college-writing-004968.zh: 例如，如果您正在撰写一篇文章，重点介绍数字电子课程的计算机主板的功能，您就不必解释什么是主板。

college-writing-004969.en: However, if you were writing that same essay for your Composition 1 class, you would need to assume that many of your classmates may not know what a motherboard is and would need an explanation before they could understand your essay.
college-writing-004969.zh: 但是，如果您为您的作文 1 课写同一篇文章，您需要假设您的许多同学可能不知道主板是什么，并且需要解释才能理解您的论文。

college-writing-004970.en: 2. Why might the reader need or want to read this material?
college-writing-004970.zh: 2. 为什么读者需要或想要阅读这些材料？

college-writing-004971.en: In college, your English professor will use your papers to evaluate your writing skills and determine how you can strengthen them.
college-writing-004971.zh: 在大学里，你的英语教授会用你的论文来评估你的写作技巧，并确定如何加强它们。

college-writing-004972.en: Your professor will probably also use them to establish your course grade.
college-writing-004972.zh: 您的教授可能还会使用它们来确定您的课程成绩。

college-writing-004973.en: If, however, you are writing to a group of residents whose public services are going to be closed at 3:00 p.m. each day, you will have to meet different expectations.
college-writing-004973.zh: 但是，如果您正在写信给一群公共服务将于下午 3:00 关闭的居民。 每天，您都必须满足不同的期望。

college-writing-004974.en: They will want to know why the offices are closing earlier and what benefits they will reap
college-writing-004974.zh: 他们会想知道为什么办公室会提前关闭以及他们将获得什么好处

college-writing-004977.en: As taxpayers, they may also want to know how much the city will be saving and where these savings are going to be directed.
college-writing-004977.zh: 作为纳税人，他们可能还想知道这座城市将节省多少以及将把这些储蓄引导在哪里。

college-writing-004978.en: 3. Is your purpose simply to inform the audience?
college-writing-004978.zh: 3. 你的目的只是为了通知观众吗？

college-writing-004979.en: Perhaps it is to convince readers of something as well?
college-writing-004979.zh: 也许是为了说服读者某事？

college-writing-004980.en: Or perhaps you want to entertain your audience?
college-writing-004980.zh: 或者你想娱乐你的观众？

college-writing-004981.en: If your purpose is to convince or persuade, you may want to use some of the techniques for writing arguments in Chapter 16.
college-writing-004981.zh: 如果您的目的是说服或说服，您可能希望使用第 16 章中的一些写论点的技巧。

college-writing-004982.en: For example, if you are writing a letter to the editor of your local newspaper in support of the new school budget, you may have to persuade voters to approve the budget even though it is sure to raise their property taxes.
college-writing-004982.zh: 例如，如果您正在给当地报纸的编辑写一封信以支持新的学校预算，您可能不得不说服选民批准预算，即使它肯定会提高他们的财产税。

college-writing-004983.en: However, if you are writing an essay to get your audience laughing, you may need to share funny and embarrassing anecdotes and experiences to entertain them.
college-writing-004983.zh: 但是，如果您正在写一篇文章来让您的观众发笑，您可能需要分享有趣和令人尴尬的轶事和经验来娱乐他们。

college-writing-004984.en: 4. What type of language should be used?
college-writing-004984.zh: 4. 应该使用什么类型的语言？

college-writing-004985.en: Are you writing to peers─other college students, or are you communicating with professors, business and community leaders, or government officials?
college-writing-004985.zh: 您是在给同龄人（其他大学生）写信，还是与教授、商业和社区领袖或政府官员进行沟通？

college-writing-004986.en: With peers, you might want to use language that is relaxed, friendly, and informal, and that will win their confidence.
college-writing-004986.zh: 对于同龄人，您可能希望使用轻松、友好和非正式的语言，这将赢得他们的信心。

college-writing-004987.en: If you’re writing to a professor, or to a government official, or an employer, you will have to be more formal.
college-writing-004987.zh: 如果你写信给教授、政府官员或雇主，你必须更正式。

college-writing-004988.en: Determining Your Point of View When you write, you can take any of three approaches, or points of view: first person, second person, or third person.
college-writing-004988.zh: 确定您的观点 在写作时，您可以采用三种方法或观点中的任何一种：第一人称、第二人称或第三人称。

college-writing-004990.en: In the first-person approach─a strongly individualized point of view─you draw on your own experience and speak to your audience in your own voice, using pronouns like I, me, mine, we, our, and us.
college-writing-004990.zh: 在第一人称方法中─强烈个性化的观点——你利用自己的经验，用自己的声音与你的听众交谈，使用我、我、我、我们、我们和我们这样的代词。

college-writing-004991.en: The first-person approach is most common in narrative essays based on personal experience.
college-writing-004991.zh: 第一人称方法在基于个人经验的叙述性论文中最为常见。

college-writing-004992.en: It also suits other essays where most of the evidence presented consists of personal observation.
college-writing-004992.zh: 它也适合其他论文，其中提供的大多数证据都包含个人观察。

college-writing-004993.en: Here is a first-person supporting paragraph from an essay on camping:
college-writing-004993.zh: 这是一篇关于露营的文章的第一人称支持段落：

college-writing-004994.en: First of all, I like comfort when I’m camping.
college-writing-004994.zh: 首先，我喜欢露营时的舒适感。

college-writing-004995.en: My motor home, with its completely equipped kitchen, shower stall, toilet, double bed, and flatscreen television, resembles a mobile motel room.
college-writing-004995.zh: 我的房车，配备齐全的厨房、淋浴间、卫生间、双人床和平板电视，类似于移动汽车旅馆的房间。

college-writing-004996.en: I can sleep on a real mattress, clean sheets, and fluffy pillows.
college-writing-004996.zh: 我可以睡在真正的床垫、干净的床单和蓬松的枕头上。

college-writing-004997.en: Next to my bed are devices that make me feel at home: my cell phone, a Bluetooth speaker, and a remote control.
college-writing-004997.zh: 我的床旁边是让我有宾至如归的感觉的设备：我的手机、蓝牙扬声器和遥控器。

college-writing-004998.en: Unlike the poor campers huddled in tents, I don’t have to worry about cold, rain, heat, or annoying insects.
college-writing-004998.zh: 与挤在帐篷里的可怜的露营者不同，我不必担心寒冷、雨水、炎热或烦人的昆虫。

college-writing-004999.en: After a hot shower, I can slide into my best pajamas, sit comfortably on my down-filled quilt, and read the latest best seller while a thunderstorm booms outside.
college-writing-004999.zh: 洗完热水澡后，我可以穿上我最好的睡衣，舒适地坐在我的羽绒被子上，在外面雷暴轰隆隆的时候阅读最新的畅销书。

college-writing-005002.en: In the second-person approach, the writer speaks directly to the reader, using the pronoun you.
college-writing-005002.zh: 在第二人称方法中，作者使用代词 you 直接与读者交谈。

college-writing-005003.en: The second-person approach is considered appropriate for giving direct instructions and explanations to the reader.
college-writing-005003.zh: 第二人称方法被认为适合向读者提供直接指示和解释。

college-writing-005004.en: This book is written as a manual to help you become a better writer, which is why you is used throughout the book.
college-writing-005004.zh: 这本书是作为手册编写的，以帮助您成为更好的作家，这就是您在整本书中使用的原因。

college-writing-005005.en: You should plan to use the second-person approach only when writing a process essay, although even for this type of essay, the third-person approach is effective.
college-writing-005005.zh: 您应该计划仅在撰写流程论文时使用第二人称方法，尽管即使对于这种类型的论文，第三人称方法也是有效的。

college-writing-005006.en: Otherwise, as a general rule, never use the word you in writing.
college-writing-005006.zh: 否则，作为一般规则，永远不要以书面形式使用你这个词。

college-writing-005008.en: The third-person approach is by far the most common point of view in academic writing.
college-writing-005008.zh: 第三人称方法是迄今为止学术写作中最常见的观点。

college-writing-005009.en: In the third person, the writer includes no direct references to the reader (you) or the self (I, me).
college-writing-005009.zh: 在第三人称中，作者不包括对读者（你）或自我（我，我）的直接引用。

college-writing-005010.en: Third person gets its name from the stance it suggests─ that of an outsider or “third person” observing and reporting on matters of public rather than private importance.
college-writing-005010.zh: 第三人称得名于它所暗示的立场——外人或“第三人”观察和报告公共事务而不是私人重要性的立场。

college-writing-005011.en: In this approach, you draw on information achieved through observation, thinking, or reading.
college-writing-005011.zh: 在这种方法中，您可以利用通过观察、思考或阅读获得的信息。

college-writing-005012.en: Here is a similar paragraph on camping, recast in the third person.
college-writing-005012.zh: 这是关于露营的类似段落，以第三人称重铸。

college-writing-005013.en: Note the third-person pronouns their, them, and they, which all refer to campers in the first sentence.
college-writing-005013.zh: 注意第三人称代词他们、他们和他们，它们都指第一句中的营员。

college-writing-005014.en: First of all, modern campers bring complete bedrooms with them.
college-writing-005014.zh: 首先，现代露营者随身携带完整的卧室。

college-writing-005015.en: Winnebagos, Airstream motor homes, and Fleetwood recreational vehicles lumber into America’s campgrounds every summer like mobile motel rooms.
college-writing-005015.zh: 每年夏天，温尼巴戈斯、Airstream 房车和 Fleetwood 休闲车都会像移动汽车旅馆的房间一样沉入美国的露营地。

college-writing-005016.en: All the comforts of home are provided inside.
college-writing-005016.zh: 家中的所有舒适设施都在里面提供。

college-writing-005017.en: Campers sleep on real mattresses with clean sheets and fluffy pillows.
college-writing-005017.zh: 露营者睡在带有干净床单和蓬松枕头的真正床垫上。

college-writing-005018.en: Next to their beds are the same gadgets that litter their night tables at home—cell phones, Bluetooth speakers, and remote controls.
college-writing-005018.zh: 在他们的床旁边是在家里乱扔床头柜的小玩意——手机、蓝牙音箱和遥控器。

college-writing-005019.en: It’s not necessary for them to worry about annoyances like cold, heat, rain, or buzzing insects, either.
college-writing-005019.zh: 他们也不必担心寒冷、炎热、雨水或嗡嗡的昆虫等烦恼。

college-writing-005020.en: They can sit comfortably in bed and read the latest best sellers while a thunderstorm booms outside.
college-writing-005020.zh: 他们可以舒适地坐在床上，阅读最新的畅销书，而雷暴在外面轰隆隆。

college-writing-005021.en: Using Peer Review In addition to having your instructor as an audience for your writing, you will benefit from having other students in your class as an audience.
college-writing-005021.zh: 使用同行评审 除了让您的导师作为您写作的受众之外，您将受益于让班上的其他学生作为受众。

college-writing-005022.en: Your instructor will most likely require that you work with another student or group of students to peer review each other’s papers.
college-writing-005022.zh: 您的讲师很可能会要求您与另一名学生或一组学生合作，以同行评审对方的论文。

college-writing-005023.en: This may occur during any stage of the writing
college-writing-005023.zh: 这可能发生在写作的任何阶段

college-writing-005025.en: If using you has been a common mistake in your writing, you should review the rule about pronoun point of view in the “Consistency with Pronouns” section in Chapter 5.
college-writing-005025.zh: 如果使用你是你写作中的一个常见错误，你应该在第 5 章的“与代词一致性”一节中查看关于代词观点的规则。

college-writing-005030.en: For some review sessions, you may be discussing your prewriting with a partner and using the questioning technique to create more ideas; for others, you may be looking just at each other’s introductory paragraphs.
college-writing-005030.zh: 对于一些复习会议，您可能会与合作伙伴讨论您的预写作，并使用提问技巧来创造更多的想法； 对于其他人，您可能只是在看彼此的介绍性段落。

college-writing-005031.en: For a formal peer review of rough drafts, you will most likely be required to bring a typed copy of your essay and work with a group of students.
college-writing-005031.zh: 对于草稿的正式同行评审，您很可能需要携带一份类型的论文并与一组学生一起工作。

college-writing-005032.en: To properly prepare for a formal peer review, you should have gone through all the steps of writing and you should bring a clean, typed rough draft to your review.
college-writing-005032.zh: 为了为正式的同行评审做好充分准备，您应该完成了所有写作步骤，并且应该为您的评论带来一份干净、打字的草稿。

college-writing-005033.en: If possible, you should provide extra copies for your peer reviewer or review group to use as you work through your essay.
college-writing-005033.zh: 如果可能，您应该为您的同行评审员或评论小组提供额外的副本，以便在您完成论文时使用。

college-writing-005034.en: Many students worry that they are not strong enough writers to give constructive feedback or that they may hurt the other students’ feelings.
college-writing-005034.zh: 许多学生担心他们没有足够强大的作家来提供建设性的反馈，或者他们可能会伤害其他学生的感情。

college-writing-005035.en: Being open to the process, both as reviewer and author, will make this a more positive experience.
college-writing-005035.zh: 作为审稿人和作者，对这个过程持开放态度将使这成为一种更积极的体验。

college-writing-005036.en: Your instructor is not expecting you to provide a professional-level review, but you are expected to read through the essays and give the best feedback you can.
college-writing-005036.zh: 您的讲师不希望您提供专业级别的评论，但您应该阅读论文并提供最好的反馈。

college-writing-005037.en: Both participants should look at this activity as a way to make their essays better, not as a negative criticism of their writing.
college-writing-005037.zh: 两位参与者都应该将这项活动视为使他们的论文变得更好的一种方式，而不是对他们写作的负面批评。

college-writing-005038.en: The more open each person is to giving and receiving constructive feedback, the more growth both will see in their writing.
college-writing-005038.zh: 每个人对给予和接受建设性反馈的越开放，两人在写作中看到的增长就越多。

college-writing-005039.en: How to Get the Most Out of a Review

college-writing-005040.en: Being prepared is the number one way to benefit from a review.
college-writing-005040.zh: 做好准备是从审查中受益的第一方式。

college-writing-005041.en: If your class is having a formal peer review of rough drafts, the more complete your draft, the more helpful the review session will be.
college-writing-005041.zh: 如果您的班级对草稿进行了正式的同行评审，您的草稿越完整，审查会议就越有帮助。

college-writing-005042.en: If you show up with only an idea─or nothing─your classmates will not be able to give you the help a second (or third) set of eyes provides.
college-writing-005042.zh: 如果你只带着一个想法——或者什么都没有——你的同学将无法为你提供第二（或第三）眼睛提供的帮助。

college-writing-005043.en: Your instructor will most likely provide instructions and/or a handout for your review, but you should also practice the following strategies to get the most out of any type of peer review.
college-writing-005043.zh: 您的讲师很可能会为您的审查提供说明和/或讲义，但您还应该练习以下策略，以充分利用任何类型的同行评审。

college-writing-005044.en: Ideally, you should read the paper aloud while your peer or group listens and follows along (if you have brought extra drafts).
college-writing-005044.zh: 理想情况下，您应该在您的同行或小组倾听并跟随（如果您带来了额外的草稿）时大声朗读论文。

college-writing-005045.en: If reading aloud isn’t practical, read it in a whisper as your peer or group looks on.
college-writing-005045.zh: 如果大声朗读是不切实际的，请在您的同龄人或小组的注视下小声朗读。

college-writing-005046.en: As you read, both you and your partner(s) should look and listen for spots where the paper does not read smoothly and clearly.
college-writing-005046.zh: 当您阅读时，您和您的伴侣都应该寻找和倾听论文读得不流畅和清晰的地方。

college-writing-005047.en: Check or circle the trouble spots where your reading snags.
college-writing-005047.zh: 检查或圈出您的阅读障碍的问题点。

college-writing-005048.en: If you have provided a copy of your essay for your group to work with, you should then work together through the items listed in the next section.
college-writing-005048.zh: 如果您为您的小组提供了一份论文的副本，您应该一起完成下一节中列出的项目。

college-writing-005049.en: If you have only the one copy you are reading from, give this copy to your reviewer so they can work through it, making notes on your essay.
college-writing-005049.zh: 如果您只有一份您正在阅读的副本，请将此副本交给您的审稿人，以便他们可以完成它，在您的论文中做笔记。

college-writing-005050.en: Your reviewer can also make notes on a separate sheet of paper if that is more practical.
college-writing-005050.zh: 如果更实用，您的审稿人也可以在另一张纸上做笔记。

college-writing-005051.en: Once a group has finished with all the essays and before leaving the classroom, students should take time to read over the feedback, make any necessary notes, and ask questions about any comments that are confusing or require clarity.
college-writing-005051.zh: 一旦一个小组完成了所有的论文，在离开教室之前，学生应该花时间阅读反馈，做任何必要的笔记，并就任何令人困惑或需要清晰的评论提出问题。

college-writing-005052.en: Once you are home, you won’t be able to ask your group members, and you may not remember the context of the suggestion.
college-writing-005052.zh: 回到家后，您将无法询问您的小组成员，您可能不记得建议的上下文。

college-writing-005055.en: As many people are sensitive to criticism, it is very important to be constructive with your comments.
college-writing-005055.zh: 由于许多人对批评很敏感，因此对您的评论保持建设性非常重要。

college-writing-005056.en: Try to avoid vague comments like “it’s good”; instead offer helpful suggestions like “your topic sentence is very broad and should be narrowed down.”
college-writing-005056.zh: 尽量避免像“这很好”这样的模糊评论； 而是提供有用的建议，例如“您的 主题句 非常广泛，应该缩小范围”。

college-writing-005057.en: Here are some of the general areas you should comment on while peer reviewing:
college-writing-005057.zh: 以下是您在同行评审时应该评论的一些一般领域：

college-writing-005058.en: • Is there a thesis statement (or topic sentence for a paragraph) that makes a point?
college-writing-005058.zh: • 是否有一个 中心论点句（或段落的 主题句）提出一个观点？

college-writing-005059.en: If not, try to suggest ways the author could improve it.
college-writing-005059.zh: 如果没有，请尝试建议作者改进它的方法。

college-writing-005060.en: • Do the topic sentences directly relate to the thesis statement?
college-writing-005060.zh: • 主题句 是否与 中心论点句 直接相关？

college-writing-005061.en: If not, try to suggest ways the author could revise the topic sentences for better unity.
college-writing-005061.zh: 如果没有，请尝试建议作者如何修改 主题句 以获得更好的统一性。

college-writing-005062.en: • Are there spots in the paper where you see problems with unity, support, or organization?
college-writing-005062.zh: • 论文中是否有一些地方可以看到团结、支持或组织的问题？

college-writing-005063.en: (You’ll find it helpful to refer to the Four Bases checklist at the back of this book.)
college-writing-005063.zh: （您会发现参考本书背面的四个基地清单很有帮助。）

college-writing-005064.zh: 如果是这样，请发表评论。

college-writing-005065.en: For example, you might say, “More details are needed in the first supporting paragraph,” or “Some of the details in the last supporting paragraph don’t really back up your point.”
college-writing-005065.zh: 例如，您可能会说“第一个支持段落需要更多细节”，或者“最后一个支持段落中的一些细节并没有真正支持您的观点。”

college-writing-005066.en: • Make a note of at least two things the author did really well, such as good use of transitions or inclusion of an especially realistic or vivid specific detail.
college-writing-005066.zh: • 至少记下作者做得很好的两件事，例如善用过渡或包含一个特别现实或生动的具体细节。

college-writing-005067.en: • Write down at least two things the author could do to improve the paper, such as adding detail or support in specific areas or using more vibrant and active language.
college-writing-005067.zh: • 至少写下作者可以做的两件事来改进论文，例如在特定领域添加细节或支持，或使用更有活力和活跃的语言。

college-writing-005068.en: • Look at the spots where your reading of the paper snagged.
college-writing-005068.zh: • 查看您阅读论文的位置。

college-writing-005069.en: Try to determine the cause─is there a lack of parallel structure, is there information missing, is it a simple grammar problem?
college-writing-005069.zh: 尝试找出原因——是否缺少平行结构，是否缺少信息，是一个简单的语法问题吗？

college-writing-005070.en: Try to figure out what the problems are and suggest ways to fix them.
college-writing-005070.zh: 尝试找出问题是什么，并提出解决问题的方法。

college-writing-005071.en: • Although sentence skills are important, try not to simply edit a student’s paper as you are reviewing a rough draft.
college-writing-005071.zh: • 尽管句子技巧很重要，但在您查看草稿时，尽量不要简单地编辑学生的论文。

college-writing-005072.en: Extra attention to grammar and punctuation should be given during the editing stage and not the revising stage.
college-writing-005072.zh: 在编辑阶段，而不是修改阶段，应特别注意语法和标点符号。

college-writing-005073.en: Doing a Personal Review While having someone else give constructive feedback is an important step in the writing process, being able to critique your own writing is also very important, especially as you decide what suggestions from your peer review group to incorporate as you revise your paper.
college-writing-005073.zh: 在让别人提供建设性反馈的同时进行个人审查是写作过程中的重要一步，能够批评自己的写作也非常重要，尤其是当您决定在您修改论文时从同行评审小组中提出哪些建议时。

college-writing-005074.en: This requires the ability to look at your writing and any suggestions offered in a nondefensive manner.
college-writing-005074.zh: 这需要能够以非防御性的方式查看您的写作和任何建议。

college-writing-005075.en: It also requires you to step back from your writing and look at it in a less personal way.
college-writing-005075.zh: 它还要求您退后一步，以不那么个人化的方式看待它。

college-writing-005076.en: As you critique your own writing, you should treat it as you would a peer review of someone else’s essay.
college-writing-005076.zh: 当你批评自己的写作时，你应该像对待别人的论文一样对待它。

college-writing-005077.en: As you critique and revise your paper, you should also:
college-writing-005077.zh: 当你批评和修改你的论文时，你还应该：

college-writing-005078.en: 1. Ask the same questions your reviewers asked of you to make sure you have addressed their concerns.
college-writing-005078.zh: 1. 询问您的审稿人向您提出的相同问题，以确保您已经解决了他们的担忧。

college-writing-005080.en: 2. Evaluate your essay in terms of unity, support, and coherence, and find ways to strengthen these qualities.
college-writing-005080.zh: 2. 根据团结、支持和连贯性评估你的论文，并找到加强这些品质的方法。

college-writing-005081.en: 3. Read your essay aloud to catch any small errors or readability issues.
college-writing-005081.zh: 3. 大声朗读您的文章以捕捉任何小错误或可读性问题。

college-writing-005082.en: Once you have completed your revision, you should then focus on evaluating it for sentence skills errors and make any final changes necessary.
college-writing-005082.zh: 完成修订后，您应该专注于评估它的句子技能错误并进行必要的任何最终更改。

college-writing-005083.en: One last critical reading─done aloud─should help you check for any more mistakes or areas of weakness that still need additional revision.
college-writing-005083.zh: 最后的一次批判性阅读——大声完成——应该帮助您检查是否有任何仍然需要额外修改的错误或弱点。

college-writing-005085.en: In Chapters 1 through 6, you learned about the importance of supporting a point in writing, the structure of a traditional essay, and the writing process.
college-writing-005085.zh: 在第 1 章到第 6 章中，您了解了支持写作点的重要性、传统论文的结构和写作过程。

college-writing-005086.en: You also practiced prewriting, creating thesis statements, developing good support, organizing your ideas, and creating effective introductions and conclusions.
college-writing-005086.zh: 您还练习了预写、创建 中心论点句、开发良好的支持、组织您的想法以及创建有效的介绍和结论。

college-writing-005087.en: Finally, you learned the benefits of effective revision.
college-writing-005087.zh: 最后，您了解了有效修订的好处。

college-writing-005088.en: The following pages illustrate the entire writing process─the complete development of an essay from prewriting through planning, drafting, peer review, revision, and final draft.
college-writing-005088.zh: 以下几页说明了整个写作过程——从预写到规划、起草、同行评审、修订和最终草稿的论文的完整发展。

college-writing-005528.en: Mico submitted her essay on self-compassion because it was due, but she knew there were still areas that could have been improved.
college-writing-005528.zh: Mico 提交了她关于自我同情的文章，因为它是应得的，但她知道仍有一些领域可以改进。

college-writing-005529.en: Either on your own or in a group, go through Mico’s essay and look for weak spots.
college-writing-005529.zh: 无论是您自己还是在小组中，浏览 Mico 的文章并寻找弱点。

college-writing-005530.en: Like Mico’s peer reviewers, you should focus on helping Mico improve her essay by examining the important areas first.
college-writing-005530.zh: 像 Mico 的同行评审员一样，您应该首先通过检查重要领域来帮助 Mico 改进她的论文。

college-writing-005531.en: First, look at her thesis statement and decide whether it needs to be made stronger.
college-writing-005531.zh: 首先，看看她的中心论点句，决定是否需要变得更强。

college-writing-005532.en: If so, revise the thesis and then look at the topic sentences to see if they still support your revised thesis.
college-writing-005532.zh: 如果是这样，请修改论文，然后查看 主题句 以查看它们是否仍然支持您的修订论文。

college-writing-005533.en: If not, make the changes necessary to be sure your topic sentences are advancing the claim in the thesis.
college-writing-005533.zh: 如果没有，请进行必要的更改，以确保您的 主题句 正在推进论文中的主张。

college-writing-005534.en: The next step is to read through the individual body paragraphs to make sure they are unified, coherent, and support the topic sentence.
college-writing-005534.zh: 下一步是通读各个正文段落，以确保它们是统一的、连贯的并支持 主题句。

college-writing-005535.en: Any information that doesn’t support the topic sentence should be eliminated and replaced with ideas that advance the main idea of the paragraph.
college-writing-005535.zh: 任何不支持 主题句 的信息都应被消除，并被推进该段主要思想的想法所取代。

college-writing-005536.en: After looking over the body of the essay, go back and read through the introduction, making any necessary changes to improve it.
college-writing-005536.zh: 看完文章的正文后，回去阅读介绍，进行任何必要的改变以改进它。

college-writing-005537.en: For example, Mico chose to start her essay with a quotation, but you might decide that a different type of introduction would make a stronger beginning.
college-writing-005537.zh: 例如，Mico 选择以引文开始她的文章，但您可能会决定不同类型的介绍会成为一个更强大的开始。

college-writing-005538.en: Once you have revised the body paragraphs and introduction, read through the essay and determine whether Mico’s conclusion holds up.
college-writing-005538.zh: 一旦您修改了正文段落和引言，请通读文章并确定 Mico 的结论是否成立。

college-writing-005539.en: If not, decide how you can improve it.
college-writing-005539.zh: 如果没有，请决定如何改进它。

college-writing-005540.en: Finally, go back through her essay and edit it as needed to make sure her sentence skills and MLA format are correct.
college-writing-005540.zh: 最后，回顾她的论文并根据需要编辑它，以确保她的句子技巧和 MLA 格式是正确的。
