college-writing-005748.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Description
college-writing-005748.zh: 开发一篇强调描述的论文

college-writing-005749.en: Considering Purpose and Audience The main purpose of an essay with an emphasis on description is to make readers see─or hear, taste, smell, or feel─what you are writing about.
college-writing-005749.zh: 考虑目的和听众 一篇强调描述的文章的主要目的是让读者看到、味觉、嗅觉或感受——你在写什么。

college-writing-005750.en: Vivid details are the key to good descriptions, enabling your audience to picture and, in a way, experience what you describe.
college-writing-005750.zh: 生动的细节是良好描述的关键，使您的观众能够描绘并在某种程度上体验您所描述的内容。

college-writing-005751.en: Unlike a descriptive paragraph that focuses only on describing the topic, an essay that emphasizes description may also contain cause and effect, comparison or contrast, or narration.
college-writing-005751.zh: 与仅专注于描述主题的描述性段落不同，强调描述的文章也可能包含因果、比较或对比或叙述。

college-writing-005752.en: As you start to think about your own essay, choose a topic that will allow you to write descriptions that appeal strongly to at least one of your senses.
college-writing-005752.zh: 当您开始思考自己的论文时，请选择一个主题，让您能够写出对您的至少一种感官有强烈吸引力的描述。

college-writing-005753.en: Also, when selecting your topic, consider how much your audience already knows about it.
college-writing-005753.zh: 此外，在选择您的主题时，请考虑您的受众对它的了解程度。

college-writing-005754.en: If your topic is a familiar one, you can assume your audience already understands the general idea.
college-writing-005754.zh: 如果您的主题是一个熟悉的主题，您可以假设您的受众已经理解了一般想法。

college-writing-005755.en: However, if you are presenting something new or unfamiliar to your readers─perhaps a description of one of your relatives or a place where you’ve lived─you must provide background information.
college-writing-005755.zh: 但是，如果您向您的读者展示新的或不熟悉的东西——也许是对您的一位亲戚或您居住的地方的描述——您必须提供背景信息。

college-writing-005756.zh: 214 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-005757.en: Once you have selected your topic, focus on the goal or purpose of your essay.
college-writing-005757.zh: 一旦你选择了你的主题，专注于论文的目标或目的。

college-writing-005758.en: It is important to use the specific modes and writing techniques where and when needed.
college-writing-005758.zh: 在需要的时间和地点使用特定的模式和书写技术非常重要。

college-writing-005759.en: The purpose of your essay will determine what events should be told, what events should be eliminated, and what strategies should be employed when writing.
college-writing-005759.zh: 你的论文的目的将决定应该告诉哪些事件，应该消除哪些事件，以及写作时应该采用哪些策略。

college-writing-005760.en: What message do you hope to convey to your audience?
college-writing-005760.zh: 您希望向您的观众传达什么信息？

college-writing-005761.en: For instance, if you chose as your topic a playground you used to visit as a child, decide what dominant impression you want to communicate.
college-writing-005761.zh: 例如，如果您选择了小时候经常访问的游乐场作为主题，请决定要传达的主要印象。

college-writing-005762.en: Is your goal to make readers see the park as a pleasant play area, or do you want them to see it as a dangerous place?
college-writing-005762.zh: 您的目标是让读者将公园视为一个令人愉快的游乐区，还是您希望他们将其视为一个危险的地方？

college-writing-005763.en: If you choose the second option, focus on conveying that sense of danger to your audience.
college-writing-005763.zh: 如果您选择第二个选项，请专注于将这种危险感传达给您的观众。

college-writing-005764.en: Then jot down any details that support that idea.
college-writing-005764.zh: 然后记下支持该想法的任何细节。

college-writing-005765.en: You might describe broken beer bottles on the asphalt, graffiti sprayed on the metal jungle gym, or a decaying and derelict building on a nearby street corner.
college-writing-005765.zh: 您可能会描述沥青上的破碎啤酒瓶、喷洒在金属丛林健身房的涂鸦，或附近街角的破旧和废弃建筑。

college-writing-005766.en: In this case, the details support your overall purpose, creating a threatening picture that your audience can see and understand.
college-writing-005766.zh: 在这种情况下，细节支持您的整体目的，创造出您的观众可以看到和理解的威胁性图片。

college-writing-005767.en: Visualizing the Subject Physical description relies solely on sense impressions.
college-writing-005767.zh: 可视化主题 物理描述仅依赖于感觉印象。

college-writing-005768.en: All five senses can be used when describing, and you should try to use as many as possible.
college-writing-005768.zh: 描述时可以使用所有五种感官，您应该尝试尽可能多地使用。

college-writing-005769.en: One advantage that description has over other methods of development is that it allows the writer to visualize their subject before describing it in words.
college-writing-005769.zh: 描述优于其他开发方法的一个优点是它允许作者在用文字描述它之前将他们的主题可视化。

college-writing-005770.en: If you like to draw or paint, make an image of your subject before you start writing.
college-writing-005770.zh: 如果您喜欢绘画或绘画，请在开始写作之前为您的主题制作图像。

college-writing-005771.en: If possible, use different colors to reveal the complexity of your subject, apply perspective to give your picture depth and contrast, or add small details like a tiny mole, a button on a shirt, or a stain on a tie.
college-writing-005771.zh: 如果可能的话，使用不同的颜色来揭示你的主题的复杂性，应用透视来赋予你的图片深度和对比度，或者添加小细节，比如小痣、衬衫上的纽扣或领带上的污渍。

college-writing-005772.en: When you are done, use the picture as inspiration as you gather information during prewriting.
college-writing-005772.zh: 完成后，在预写过程中收集信息时使用图片作为灵感。

college-writing-005773.en: Including People and Events in the Description of a Place Discussing the type of people who are in a place can sometimes give clues to its character and help describe it.
college-writing-005773.zh: 在一个地方的描述中包括人物和事件 讨论一个地方的人类型，有时可以为它的性格提供线索并帮助描述它。

college-writing-005774.en: The same can be said for what happens there.
college-writing-005774.zh: 那里发生的事情也是如此。

college-writing-005775.en: For example, a bar where middle-aged couples sip drinks and converse is one thing; a bar where young people dance to loud music is quite another.
college-writing-005775.zh: 例如，中年夫妇喝酒交谈的酒吧是一回事； 一个年轻人随着响亮的音乐跳舞，这是另一回事。

college-writing-005776.en: You might even describe animals and their actions to enliven your description of a place.
college-writing-005776.zh: 您甚至可以描述动物及其行动，以使您对一个地方的描述充满活力。

college-writing-005777.en: Say you’re writing about a zoo.
college-writing-005777.zh: 假设您正在写关于动物园的文章。

college-writing-005778.en: It might be worth discussing the antics of chimpanzees or the majestic pacing of a tiger as it struts within its habitat.
college-writing-005778.zh: 可能值得讨论黑猩猩的滑稽动作或老虎在栖息地昂首阔步的雄伟节奏。

college-writing-005780.en: You will learn more about creating dialogue in Chapter 9, “Narration.”
college-writing-005780.zh: 您将在第 9 章“叙述”中了解有关创建对话的更多信息。

college-writing-005781.en: For now just remember that dialogue can sometimes reveal a great deal about a person or a place.
college-writing-005781.zh: 现在请记住，对话有时可以揭示很多关于一个人或一个地方的信息。

college-writing-005782.en: For example, our first clue that the owner of the café in “Lou’s Place” (an essay appearing later in this chapter) is rather feisty is his response to a woman who wants to know if he’s open: “I’m here, aren’t I?”
college-writing-005782.zh: 例如，我们的第一个线索，即“娄的地方”（本章后面出现的一篇文章）咖啡馆的老板是对一个想知道他是否开放的女人的回应：“我在这里，不是吗？”

college-writing-005785.en: Later, when another customer asks for breakfast, Lou says, “I’m reading the paper. . . . Eggs are in the refrigerator.”
college-writing-005785.zh: 后来，当另一位顾客要早餐时，娄说：“我正在看报纸……鸡蛋在冰箱里。”

college-writing-005786.en: Development through Prewriting When Viviana, the author of “Family Portrait,” sat down to think about a topic for her essay, she looked around her apartment for inspiration.
college-writing-005786.zh: 通过预写发展 当“全家福”的作者维维亚娜坐下来思考她的论文的主题时，她环顾了她的公寓寻找灵感。

college-writing-005787.en: First she thought about describing her own bedroom.
college-writing-005787.zh: 首先，她想描述自己的卧室。

college-writing-005788.en: But she had moved into the apartment only recently and hadn’t done much in the way of decorating, so the room struck her as too bare and sterile.
college-writing-005788.zh: 但她最近才搬进公寓，并没有在装饰方面做太多事情，所以房间让她觉得太光秃秃和不育。

college-writing-005789.en: Then she looked out her window, thinking of describing the view.
college-writing-005789.zh: 然后她看着窗外，想着描述这个景色。

college-writing-005790.en: That seemed much more promising: she noticed the sights and sounds of children playing on the sidewalks and a group of older men playing cards, as well as smells─neighbors’ cooking and exhaust from passing traffic.
college-writing-005790.zh: 这似乎更有希望：她注意到人行道上的孩子们和一群年长的男人在打牌的景象和声音，以及邻居的烹饪和排气的气味。

college-writing-005791.en: She was jotting down some details for such an essay when she glanced up at the framed portrait of her great-grandmother on her desk.
college-writing-005791.zh: 当她抬头看了看桌上的曾祖母的相框肖像时，她正在为这样的文章记下一些细节。

college-writing-005792.en: “I stopped and stared at it, as I often do, wondering again about this twenty-year-old girl who became my great-grandmother,” she said.
college-writing-005792.zh: “我停下来盯着它，就像我经常做的那样，再次想知道这个 20 岁的女孩成为我的曾祖母，”她说。

college-writing-005793.en: “While I sat there studying it, I realized that the best topic of all was right under my nose.”
college-writing-005793.zh: “当我坐在那里学习它时，我意识到最好的话题就在我的眼皮底下。”

college-writing-005794.en: As she looked at the photograph, Viviana began to freewrite.
college-writing-005794.zh: 当她看着照片时，薇薇安娜开始自由写作。

college-writing-005796.en: Great-Grandma is twenty in the picture.
college-writing-005796.zh: 照片中的曾祖母是二十岁。

college-writing-005797.en: She’s wearing a beautiful skirt and blouse
college-writing-005797.zh: 她穿着漂亮的裙子和衬衫

college-writing-005798.en: and jewelry she borrowed from Ana.
college-writing-005798.zh: 和她从安娜那里借来的珠宝。

college-writing-005799.en: Looks a lot like me—nose, eyes, mouth.
college-writing-005799.zh: 看起来很像我——鼻子、眼睛、嘴巴。

college-writing-005801.en: than I am but you really can’t tell in picture.
college-writing-005801.zh: 比我是，但你真的无法在图片中分辨。

college-writing-005802.en: Looks a lot like old photos I’ve seen of
college-writing-005802.zh: 看起来很像我见过的旧照片

college-writing-005803.en: Grandma too—all the Diaz women resemble each other.
college-writing-005803.zh: 奶奶也是——所有的迪亚兹女人都像对方。

college-writing-005804.en: Earrings and bracelet are of silver

college-writing-005806.en: Ring might be amber or topaz?
college-writing-005806.zh: 戒指可能是琥珀色或黄玉？

college-writing-005807.en: We’ve laughed about the “other man” who

college-writing-005809.en: Her brown hair is down loose on her shoulders.
college-writing-005809.zh: 她的棕色头发在她的肩膀上松散了。

college-writing-005812.en: doesn’t really look like her—her usual smile is bigger and opens her mouth.
college-writing-005812.zh: 看起来不像她——她平时的笑容更大了，张开了她的嘴。

college-writing-005814.en: the photo makes me a little sad even though I really like it.
college-writing-005814.zh: 这张照片让我有点难过，尽管我真的很喜欢它。

college-writing-005816.en: older she’s getting and I wonder how long she’ll be with us.
college-writing-005816.zh: 她年纪大了，我想知道她会和我们在一起多久。

college-writing-005817.en: It’s funny to see a picture of

college-writing-005818.en: your great-grandmother at a younger age than you are now—stirs up all kinds of weird
college-writing-005818.zh: 你的曾祖母比你现在年轻——激起各种奇怪的

college-writing-005820.en: Picture was taken at a studio in Houston to give to Great-Grandpa.
college-writing-005820.zh: 照片是在休斯顿的一家工作室拍的，送给曾祖父。

college-writing-005824.en: Hard to imagine them being so formal with each other.
college-writing-005824.zh: 很难想象他们会如此正式。

college-writing-005825.zh: 216 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-005826.en: Viviana looked over her notes and thought about how she might organize her essay.
college-writing-005826.zh: Viviana 看着她的笔记，想着她如何组织她的论文。

college-writing-005827.en: First she thought only of describing how the photograph looked.
college-writing-005827.zh: 首先，她只想描述照片的外观。

college-writing-005828.en: With that in mind, she thought her main points might be (1) what her great-grandmother’s face looked like and (2) what her great-grandmother was wearing.
college-writing-005828.zh: 考虑到这一点，她认为她的主要观点可能是（1）她曾祖母的脸和（2）她曾祖母的穿着。

college-writing-005829.en: But she was stuck for a third main point.
college-writing-005829.zh: 但她被困在第三个要点上。

college-writing-005830.en: Studying her notes again, Viviana noticed two other possible main points.
college-writing-005830.zh: Viviana 再次研究她的笔记，注意到另外两个可能的要点。

college-writing-005831.en: One was her own emotional reaction to the photo─how it made her feel.
college-writing-005831.zh: 其中之一是她自己对这张照片的情绪反应——这让她感觉如何。

college-writing-005832.en: The other was the story of the photo─how and why it was taken.
college-writing-005832.zh: 另一个是照片的故事——如何以及为什么拍摄。

college-writing-005833.en: Not sure which of those two she would use as her third main point, she began to write.
college-writing-005833.zh: 不知道这两个中的哪一个会作为她的第三个主要观点，她开始写作。

college-writing-005836.en: I have a photograph of my great-grandmother that was taken seventyfive years ago, when she was only twenty.
college-writing-005836.zh: 我有一张我曾祖母的照片，这是七十五年前拍摄的，当时她只有 20 岁。

college-writing-005837.en: She sent it to me only recently, and I find it very interesting.
college-writing-005837.zh: 她最近才寄给我，我觉得很有趣。

college-writing-005838.en: In the photo, I see a girl who looks a good deal like I do now at twenty-two.
college-writing-005838.zh: 在照片中，我看到一个看起来很像我现在二十二岁的女孩。

college-writing-005839.en: Like most of the women in her family, including me, the girl in the picture has the Diaz family nose, waving brown hair, and large brown eyes.
college-writing-005839.zh: 像她家里的大多数女性一样，包括我在内，照片中的女孩有迪亚兹家族的鼻子、挥舞着棕色的头发和棕色的大眼睛。

college-writing-005840.en: Her mouth is closed and she is smiling slightly.
college-writing-005840.zh: 她的嘴巴闭上了，她微微一笑。

college-writing-005841.en: That isn’t my greatgrandmother’s usual big grin that shows her teeth and her “smile lines.”
college-writing-005841.zh: 这不是我曾祖母通常的大笑，显示出她的牙齿和她的“微笑线条”。

college-writing-005842.en: In the photo, Great-Grandmother is wearing a very pretty skirt and blouse.
college-writing-005842.zh: 在照片中，曾祖母穿着一件非常漂亮的裙子和衬衫。

college-writing-005843.en: They look like something that would be fashionable today.
college-writing-005843.zh: 它们看起来像今天时尚的东西。

college-writing-005844.en: The blouse is made of heavy satin.
college-writing-005844.zh: 这件衬衫是用厚实的缎子制成的。

college-writing-005845.en: The satin falls in lines and hollows that reflect the light.
college-writing-005845.zh: 缎子落在线条和空洞中，反射光。

college-writing-005846.en: It has a turned-down cowl collar and smocking on the shoulders and under the collar.
college-writing-005846.zh: 它有一个翻转的整流领，肩膀和衣领下方有抽吸鞋垫。

college-writing-005847.en: Her skirt is below her knees and looks like it is made of light wool.
college-writing-005847.zh: 她的裙子在她的膝盖下方，看起来像是用浅色羊毛制成的。

college-writing-005849.en: Her silver earrings and bracelet match.
college-writing-005849.zh: 她的银耳环和手镯搭配。

college-writing-005850.en: She had borrowed them from her sister.
college-writing-005850.zh: 她是从姐姐那里借来的。

college-writing-005851.en: Ana eventually gave them both to her, but the bracelet has disappeared.
college-writing-005851.zh: 安娜最终把它们都给了她，但手镯已经消失了。

college-writing-005852.en: On her left hand is a ring with a big yellow stone.
college-writing-005852.zh: 她的左手是一枚带有黄色大石头的戒指。

college-writing-005853.en: When I look at this photo, I feel conflicting emotions.
college-writing-005853.zh: 当我看到这张照片时，我感到矛盾的情绪。

college-writing-005854.en: It gives me pleasure to see my great-grandmother as a pretty young woman.
college-writing-005854.zh: 很高兴看到我的曾祖母是一个漂亮的年轻女子。

college-writing-005855.en: It makes me sad, too, to think how quickly time passes and realize how old she is getting.
college-writing-005855.zh: 想到时间过得有多快，意识到她的年龄，我也很难过。

college-writing-005856.en: It amuses me to read the inscription to my great-grandfather, her boyfriend at the time.
college-writing-005856.zh: 读给我曾祖父，她当时的男朋友的铭文让我很开心。

college-writing-005858.en: It’s hard for me to imagine them ever being so formal with each other.
college-writing-005858.zh: 我很难想象他们彼此如此正式。

college-writing-005859.en: My great-grandmother had the photograph taken at a studio near where she worked in Houston.
college-writing-005859.zh: 我的曾祖母在她在休斯顿工作的地方附近的工作室拍摄了这张照片。

college-writing-005860.en: She spent nearly two weeks’ salary on the outfit she wore for it.
college-writing-005860.zh: 她花了将近两周的薪水买给她穿的衣服。

college-writing-005861.en: She must have really wanted to impress my greatgrandfather to go to all that trouble and expense.
college-writing-005861.zh: 她一定是真的很想给我的曾祖父留下深刻印象，让他付出所有的麻烦和费用。

college-writing-005864.en: Development through Revising Viviana showed this first draft to her classmate Elena, who read it and returned it with these notes jotted in the margin:
college-writing-005864.zh: 通过修订 Viviana 的开发向她的同学 Elena 展示了这份初稿，Elena 阅读并返回，并在页边空白处写下了这些注释：

college-writing-005866.en: Was this the first time you’d seen it?
college-writing-005866.zh: 这是你第一次看到它吗？

college-writing-005871.en: specific about why it interests you.
college-writing-005871.zh: 具体说明它为什么感兴趣。

college-writing-005872.en: The “Diaz family nose” isn’t helpful for

college-writing-005873.en: someone who doesn’t know the Diaz

college-writing-005875.en: Nice beginning, but I still can’t quite
college-writing-005875.zh: 不错的开始，但我仍然不能

college-writing-005882.en: This is nice—I can picture the material.
college-writing-005882.zh: 这很好——我可以想象材料。

college-writing-005886.en: I have a photograph of my great-grandmother that was taken seventy-five years ago, when she was only twenty.
college-writing-005886.zh: 我有一张我曾祖母的照片，这是七十五年前拍摄的，当时她只有 20 岁。

college-writing-005887.en: She sent it to me only recently, and I find it very interesting.
college-writing-005887.zh: 她最近才寄给我，我觉得很有趣。

college-writing-005888.en: In the photo, I see a girl who looks a good deal like I do now at twenty-two.
college-writing-005888.zh: 在照片中，我看到一个看起来很像我现在二十二岁的女孩。

college-writing-005889.en: Like most of the women in her family, including me, the girl in the picture has the Diaz family nose, waving brown hair, and large brown eyes.
college-writing-005889.zh: 像她家里的大多数女性一样，包括我在内，照片中的女孩有迪亚兹家族的鼻子、挥舞着棕色的头发和棕色的大眼睛。

college-writing-005890.en: Her mouth is closed and she is smiling slightly.
college-writing-005890.zh: 她的嘴巴闭上了，她微微一笑。

college-writing-005891.en: That isn’t my great-grandmother’s usual big grin that shows her teeth and her “smile lines.”
college-writing-005891.zh: 这不是我曾祖母一贯的大笑，显示出她的牙齿和她的“微笑线条”。

college-writing-005892.en: In the photo, Great- Grandmother is wearing a very pretty skirt and blouse.
college-writing-005892.zh: 在照片中，曾祖母穿着一件非常漂亮的裙子和衬衫。

college-writing-005893.en: They took like something that would be fashionable today.
college-writing-005893.zh: 他们拿了今天时尚的东西。

college-writing-005894.en: The blouse is made of heavy satin.
college-writing-005894.zh: 这件衬衫是用厚实的缎子制成的。

college-writing-005895.en: The satin falls in lines and hollows that reflect the light.
college-writing-005895.zh: 缎子落在线条和空洞中，反射光。

college-writing-005896.en: It has a turned-down cowl collar and smocking on the shoulders and under the collar.
college-writing-005896.zh: 它有一个翻转的整流领，肩膀和衣领下方有抽吸鞋垫。

college-writing-005897.en: Her skirt is below her knees and looks like it is made of light wool.
college-writing-005897.zh: 她的裙子在她的膝盖下方，看起来像是用浅色羊毛制成的。

college-writing-005899.en: Her silver earrings and bracelet match.
college-writing-005899.zh: 她的银耳环和手镯搭配。

college-writing-005900.en: She had borrowed them from her sister.
college-writing-005900.zh: 她是从姐姐那里借来的。

college-writing-005901.en: Ana eventually gave them both to her, but the bracelet has disappeared.
college-writing-005901.zh: 安娜最终把它们都给了她，但手镯已经消失了。

college-writing-005902.en: On her left hand is a ring with a big yellow stone.
college-writing-005902.zh: 她的左手是一枚带有黄色大石头的戒指。

college-writing-005905.zh: 218 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-005906.en: When I look at this photo, I feel conflicting emotions.
college-writing-005906.zh: 当我看到这张照片时，我感到矛盾的情绪。

college-writing-005907.en: It gives me pleasure to see my greatgrandmother as a pretty young woman.
college-writing-005907.zh: 很高兴看到我的曾祖母年轻时很漂亮。

college-writing-005908.en: It makes me sad, too, to think how quickly time passes and realize how old she is now.
college-writing-005908.zh: 想到时间过得有多快，意识到她现在的年龄，我也很难过。

college-writing-005909.en: It amuses me to read the inscription to my great-grandfather, her boyfriend at the time.
college-writing-005909.zh: 读给我曾祖父，她当时的男朋友的铭文让我很开心。

college-writing-005911.en: It’s hard for me to imagine them ever being so formal with each other.
college-writing-005911.zh: 我很难想象他们彼此如此正式。

college-writing-005912.en: My great-grandmother had the photograph taken at a studio near where she worked in Houston.
college-writing-005912.zh: 我的曾祖母在她在休斯顿工作的地方附近的工作室拍摄了这张照片。

college-writing-005913.en: She spent nearly two weeks’ salary on the outfit she wore for it.
college-writing-005913.zh: 她花了将近两周的薪水买给她穿的衣服。

college-writing-005914.en: She must have really wanted to impress my great-grandfather to go to all that trouble
college-writing-005914.zh: 她一定是真的很想给我的曾祖父留下深刻印象，去找麻烦

college-writing-005915.en: It’d make more sense for the

college-writing-005916.en: main points of the essay to be about

college-writing-005921.en: This is interesting stuff—she really did
college-writing-005921.zh: 这是有趣的东西——她真的做到了

college-writing-005922.en: go to a lot of trouble to have the photo

college-writing-005924.en: I think the story of the photo-

college-writing-005925.en: graph deserves to be a main point.
college-writing-005925.zh: Graph 值得成为一个主要点。

college-writing-005926.en: Making use of Elena’s comments and her own reactions upon rereading her essay, Viviana wrote the final draft that appears at the beginning of this chapter.
college-writing-005926.zh: Viviana 利用 Elena 的评论和她自己在重读文章时的反应，撰写了本章开头出现的最终草稿。

college-writing-005929.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-005929.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-005932.en: Imagine a restaurant where your every whim is catered to, your every want satisfied, your every request granted without hesitation.
college-writing-005932.zh: 想象一家餐厅，您的每一个心血来潮都得到满足，您的每一个愿望都得到满足，您的每一个请求都毫不犹豫地得到了满足。

college-writing-005933.en: The people on the staff live to please you.
college-writing-005933.zh: 工作人员中的人为了取悦你而活着。

college-writing-005934.en: They hover anxiously as you sample your selection, waiting for your judgment.
college-writing-005934.zh: 当您对您的选择进行采样时，他们会焦急地徘徊，等待您的判断。

college-writing-005935.en: Your pleasure is their delight, your dissatisfaction their dismay.
college-writing-005935.zh: 你的快乐是他们的喜悦，你的不满是他们的沮丧。

college-writing-005936.en: Lou’s isn’t that kind of place.

college-writing-005937.en: At Lou’s Kosy Korner Koffee Shop, the mock abuse flows like a cup of spilled Folgers.
college-writing-005937.zh: 在 Lou 的 Kosy Korner Koffee 商店，模拟滥用就像一杯溢出的 Folgers。

college-writing-005938.en: Customers are yelled at, lectured, blamed, mocked, teased, and ignored.
college-writing-005938.zh: 客户被大喊大叫、讲课、责备、嘲笑、嘲笑和忽视。

college-writing-005939.en: They pay for the privilege of pouring their own coffee and scrambling their own
college-writing-005939.zh: 他们为自己倒咖啡和自己炒自己的特权买单

college-writing-005942.en: As in a fond but dysfunctional family, Lou displays his affection through criticism and insults, and his customers respond in kind.
college-writing-005942.zh: 就像在一个喜欢但功能失调的家庭中一样，娄通过批评和侮辱来表达他的感情，他的客户以同样的方式回应。

college-writing-005943.en: If Lou’s had a slogan, it might be, “If I’m polite to you, ask yourself what’s wrong.”
college-writing-005943.zh: 如果卢有一个口号，可能是，“如果我对你有礼貌，问问自己有什么问题。”

college-writing-005944.en: Lou’s is one of three breakfast joints located in the business district of a small mid-Atlantic town.
college-writing-005944.zh: Lou's 是位于大西洋中部小镇商业区的三个早餐店之一。

college-writing-005945.en: The county courthouse is nearby, supplying a steady stream of lawyers, jurors, and office workers looking for a bite to eat.
college-writing-005945.zh: 县法院就在附近，供应源源不断的律师、陪审员和上班族，正在寻找吃点东西。

college-writing-005946.en: A local trucking firm also provides Lou with customers as its drivers come and go in town.
college-writing-005946.zh: 一家当地的货运公司还为 Lou 提供客户来来往往的客户。

college-writing-005948.en: Beside it is a jewelry shop (“In Business Since 1946─Watch Repairs Our Speciality”) and an upscale home accessories store that features bonsai trees and hand-painted birdhouses in its window.
college-writing-005948.zh: 旁边是一家珠宝店（“自 1946 年开始营业——手表维修我们的专长”）和一家高档家居饰品店，橱窗里有盆景树和手绘鸟舍。

college-writing-005949.en: There’s a bus stop in front of Lou’s.

college-writing-005950.en: Lou himself has been known to storm out onto the sidewalk to shoo away people who’ve dismounted from the bus and lingered too long on the corner.
college-writing-005950.zh: 众所周知，娄本人冲到人行道上，把那些从公共汽车上下来并在拐角处徘徊太久的人赶走。

college-writing-005951.en: The sign on Lou’s front door says “Open 7 a.m.–3 p.m.”
college-writing-005951.zh: 楼前门上的牌子上写着“早上7点到下午3点开门”。

college-writing-005952.en: But by 6:40 on a brisk spring morning, the restaurant’s lights are on, the door is unlocked, and Lou is settled in the booth nearest the door, with the Philadelphia Inquirer spread over the table.
college-writing-005952.zh: 但到了 6 点 40 分，在一个轻快的春天早晨，餐厅的灯亮着，门打开了，娄被安顿在离门最近的展位上，费城问询者铺在桌子上。

college-writing-005953.en: Lou is sunk deep into the booth’s brown vinyl seat, its rips neatly mended with silver duct tape.
college-writing-005953.zh: Lou 深深地沉入了展位的棕色乙烯基座椅上，它的撕裂用银色胶带整齐地修补。

college-writing-005954.en: He is studying the box scores from the night before as a would-be customer pauses on the sidewalk, unsure whether to believe the sign or her own eyes.
college-writing-005954.zh: 他正在研究前一天晚上的盒子分数，因为一个潜在的顾客在人行道上停下来，不确定是相信这个标志还是她自己的眼睛。

college-writing-005955.en: She opens the door enough to stick her head in.
college-writing-005955.zh: 她打开门，足以把头伸进去。

college-writing-005957.en: Without lifting his eyes from the paper, Lou answers.
college-writing-005957.zh: 娄没有从纸上抬起眼睛，回答道。

college-writing-005959.en: Unsure how to interpret this remark, the woman enters and sits at a booth.
college-writing-005959.zh: 不确定如何解释这句话，女人进入并坐在一个展位上。

college-writing-005961.en: He begins to hum under his breath.
college-writing-005961.zh: 他开始在他的呼吸中嗡嗡作响。

college-writing-005962.en: The woman starts tracing a pattern on the glass-topped table with her fingernail.
college-writing-005962.zh: 女人开始用指甲在玻璃顶桌上描绘一个图案。

college-writing-005963.en: She pulls out her checkbook and pretends to balance it.
college-writing-005963.zh: 她拿出她的支票簿，假装平衡它。

college-writing-005964.en: After a few long minutes, Lou apparently reaches a stopping point in his reading.
college-writing-005964.zh: 几分钟后，娄显然在他的阅读中达到了一个停止点。

college-writing-005965.en: He rises, his eyes still on the folded newspaper he carries with him.
college-writing-005965.zh: 他站起来，他的眼睛仍然盯着他随身携带的折叠报纸。

college-writing-005966.en: His humming breaks into low-volume song as he trudges behind the counter.
college-writing-005966.zh: 当他在柜台后面跋涉时，他的嗡嗡声变成了低音量的歌曲。

college-writing-005967.en: “Maaaaaaaake someone happy. . . . Make-make-maaaaaake someone happy,” he croons as he lifts the steaming pot that has infused the room with the rich aroma of freshly brewed coffee.
college-writing-005967.zh: “Maaaaaaaaaake 一个快乐的人...... Make-maake-maaaaaaake 一个快乐的人，”他低吟着，在蒸汽锅里充满了新鲜煮熟的咖啡的浓郁香气。

college-writing-005968.en: He carries it to the woman’s table, fills her cup, and drops two single-serving containers of half-and-half nearby.
college-writing-005968.zh: 他把它带到女人的桌子上，装满她的杯子，在附近放了两个半份的单份容器。

college-writing-005969.en: He then peers over the tops of his reading glasses at his customer.
college-writing-005969.zh: 然后，他凝视着老人的老花镜顶部。

college-writing-005970.en: “You want anything else, dear?” he asks, his bushy gray eyebrows rising with the question.
college-writing-005970.zh: “你还想要什么吗，亲爱的？” 他问道，他浓密的灰色眉毛随着这个问题而扬起。

college-writing-005972.en: “I’m meeting someone. I’ll order when he gets here.”
college-writing-005972.zh: “我在见人。他来的时候我会下单的。”

college-writing-005973.en: Lou nods absently, his eyes back on his paper.
college-writing-005973.zh: 娄心不在焉地点点头，目光又回到了他的纸上。

college-writing-005974.en: As he shuffles back to his seat, he mutters over his shoulder, “Hope he shows up before three. I close then.”
college-writing-005974.zh: 当他拖着脚步回到座位上时，他在肩膀上喃喃自语：“希望他在三点之前出现。那我就快点靠近。”

college-writing-005975.en: Lou reads his paper; the woman drinks her coffee and gazes around the room.
college-writing-005975.zh: 娄读他的论文； 女人喝了咖啡，环视了房间。

college-writing-005976.en: It’s a small restaurant: just an eight-seat counter and seven padded booths.
college-writing-005976.zh: 这是一家小餐厅：只有一个八座位的柜台和七个带衬垫的展位。

college-writing-005977.en: A grill, coffeepots, and a huge stainless-steel refrigerator line the wall behind the counter.
college-writing-005977.zh: 柜台后面的墙上排列着一个烤架、咖啡壶和一个巨大的不锈钢冰箱。

college-writing-005978.en: Under the glass top of the tables is the breakfast menu: it offers eggs, pancakes, home fries, bacon, and sausage.
college-writing-005978.zh: 桌子的玻璃顶部是早餐菜单：它提供鸡蛋、煎饼、家常薯条、培根和香肠。

college-writing-005979.en: A wall rack holds Kellogg’s Jumbo Packs of single-serving cereals: smiling toucans and cheerful tigers offer Froot Loops and Frosted Flakes.
college-writing-005979.zh: 壁架上装着 Kellogg 的单份谷物大包：微笑的巨嘴鸟和快乐的老虎提供了 Froot Loops 和 Frosted Flakes。

college-writing-005980.zh: 220 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-005981.en: Two poster-size photographs hang side by side at the far wall.
college-writing-005981.zh: 两张海报大小的照片并排挂在远处的墙上。

college-writing-005982.en: One is of Lou and his wife on their wedding day.
college-writing-005982.zh: 其中一位是娄和他的妻子在婚礼当天。

college-writing-005983.en: They appear to be in their midtwenties.
college-writing-005983.zh: 他们似乎已经二十多岁了。

college-writing-005984.en: He is slim, dark-haired, beaming; his arm circles the shoulders of his fair-haired bride.
college-writing-005984.zh: 他苗条，黑发，喜气洋洋； 他的手臂环绕着他白发新娘的肩膀。

college-writing-005985.en: The other photo shows the same couple in an identical pose─only in this one, Lou looks much as he is today.
college-writing-005985.zh: 另一张照片显示同一对夫妇的姿势相同——只有在这张照片中，娄看起来和他今天一样。

college-writing-005986.en: His short white hair is parted at the side; a cropped white beard emphasizes his prominent red mouth.
college-writing-005986.zh: 他的白发在一边分开； 剪下的白胡子强调了他突出的红嘴。

college-writing-005987.en: His formerly slim figure now expands to take up much of the photograph.
college-writing-005987.zh: 他以前苗条的身材现在扩展到占据了大部分照片。

college-writing-005988.en: But the smile is the same as he embraces his silver-haired wife.
college-writing-005988.zh: 但他的笑容和他拥抱他的银发妻子一样。

college-writing-005989.en: The bell at the door tinkles; two sleepy-eyed men in flannel shirts, work boots, and oil-company caps walk in.
college-writing-005989.zh: 门口的钟声响起； 两个穿着法兰绒衬衫、工作靴和石油公司帽的昏昏欲睡的男人走进来。

college-writing-005990.en: Lou glances up and grunts at them; they nod.
college-writing-005990.zh: 娄抬头看了看他们。 他们点头。

college-writing-005991.en: One picks up an Inquirer from the display stand and leaves two quarters on the cash register.
college-writing-005991.zh: 一个人从展示架上拿起一个询问者，并在收银机上留下了两个季度。

college-writing-005992.en: They drop onto seats at the counter, simultaneously swivel to look at the woman in the booth behind them, and then turn back.
college-writing-005992.zh: 他们落在柜台的座位上，同时旋转着看着身后展位上的女人，然后转身。

college-writing-005993.en: For a few minutes, they flip through the sports section.
college-writing-005993.zh: 有几分钟，他们翻阅了体育部分。

college-writing-005995.en: One man rises from his seat and wanders behind the counter to find cups and the coffeepot.
college-writing-005995.zh: 一名男子从座位上站起来，在柜台后面徘徊，寻找杯子和咖啡壶。

college-writing-005996.en: He fills the cups, returns to his seat, and immerses himself in the paper.
college-writing-005996.zh: 他把杯子装满，回到座位上，沉浸在纸上。

college-writing-005997.en: There is no noise but the occasional slurping of men sipping hot coffee.
college-writing-005997.zh: 没有噪音，但偶尔会啜饮热咖啡的男人啜饮。

college-writing-005999.en: Finally one of the men speaks.

college-writing-006004.en: The man sighs and lumbers behind the counter again.
college-writing-006004.zh: 男人又叹了口气，又在柜台后面打了个招呼。

college-writing-006005.en: “In some restaurants, they actually cook for ya,” he says, selecting eggs from the carton.
college-writing-006005.zh: “在一些餐馆里，他们实际上为你做饭，”他说，从纸箱中挑选鸡蛋。

college-writing-006007.en: “In some restaurants, they wouldn’t let a guy with a face like yours in.”
college-writing-006007.zh: “在一些餐馆，他们不会让像你这样的脸的人进来。”

college-writing-006008.en: The room falls silent again, except for the splatter of grease on the grill and the scrape of the spatula as the customer scrambles his eggs.
college-writing-006008.zh: 房间里又安静了下来，除了烤架上的油条和刮刀的刮擦，顾客打着他的鸡蛋。

college-writing-006009.en: He heaps them onto his plate, prepares some toast, and returns to his seat.
college-writing-006009.zh: 他把它们堆在盘子上，准备了一些吐司，然后回到他的座位上。

college-writing-006010.en: The bell at the door begins tinkling as the breakfast rush begins─men, mostly, about half in work clothes and the rest in suits.
college-writing-006010.zh: 门口的铃声开始响起，早餐热潮开始时——男人，大部分是穿着工作服，其余的人穿着西装。

college-writing-006011.en: They pour in on a wave of talk and laughter.
college-writing-006011.zh: 他们涌入一波谈话和笑声。

college-writing-006012.en: Lou reluctantly rises and goes to work behind the counter, volleying comments with the regulars:
college-writing-006012.zh: 娄不情愿地站起来，在柜台后面工作，与常客们一起抽搐：

college-writing-006014.en: “Three eggs. One heart attack wasn’t enough for you? You want some bacon grease on top of that?”
college-writing-006014.zh: “三个蛋。一颗心脏病发作对你来说还不够？你想要一些培根油脂吗？”

college-writing-006015.en: A large red-haired man in blue jeans and a faded denim shirt walks in with a newspaper, which he reads as he waits for his cup of takeout coffee.
college-writing-006015.zh: 一个穿着蓝色牛仔裤和一件褪色牛仔衬衫的大红发男子带着报纸走进来，他在等他的外卖咖啡杯时读到。

college-writing-006019.en: “Not a damn thing. The only good thing is that the machine down the street got my fifty cents instead of you.”
college-writing-006019.zh: “不是该死的。唯一的好处是街上的机器代替了你的五十美分。”

college-writing-006020.en: Lou flips pancakes as the restaurant fills to capacity.
college-writing-006020.zh: 当餐厅满员时，娄翻转煎饼。

college-writing-006021.en: The hum of voices fills the room as the aromas of coffee, bacon, eggs, and toasting bread mingle in the air.
college-writing-006021.zh: 声音的嗡嗡声充满了房间，咖啡、培根、鸡蛋和烤面包的香气混合在空气中。

college-writing-006022.en: A group of suits* from the nearby courthouse slide into the final empty booth.
college-writing-006022.zh: 附近法院的一组西装*滑入最后一个空的展位。

college-writing-006023.en: After a moment one rises, goes behind the counter, and rummages in a drawer.
college-writing-006023.zh: 片刻后，一站起，走到柜台后面，在抽屉里翻找。

college-writing-006024.en: *suits: business executives or professionals (people wearing business suits).
college-writing-006024.zh: *西装：商务高管或专业人士（穿着西装的人）。

college-writing-006029.en: He finds one, returns to the booth, and wipes crumbs off the tabletop.
college-writing-006029.zh: 他找到了一个，回到展位，擦掉桌面上的碎屑。

college-writing-006030.en: A minute later he is back to drop a slice of ham on the hot grill.
college-writing-006030.zh: 一分钟后，他又回来把一片火腿放在热烤架上。

college-writing-006031.en: He and Lou stand side by side attending to their cooking, as comfortable in their silence as an old married couple.
college-writing-006031.zh: 他和娄并肩站着他们的烹饪，就像一对老夫妇一样在沉默中感到舒适。

college-writing-006032.en: When the ham is sizzling and its rich fragrance reaches the far corners of the room, Ben slides it onto a plate and returns to his booth.
college-writing-006032.zh: 当火腿发出嘶嘶声，其浓郁的香味到达房间的远角时，本将它滑到盘子上，然后回到他的展位。

college-writing-006033.en: Filled plate in hand, Lou approaches a woman sitting at the counter.
college-writing-006033.zh: 手里拿着满满的盘子，卢走近一个坐在柜台旁的女人。

college-writing-006034.en: Her golden hair contrasts with her sunken cheeks and her wrinkled lips sucking an unfiltered Camel.
college-writing-006034.zh: 她的金色头发与她凹陷的脸颊和她皱巴巴的嘴唇形成鲜明对比，吸着一只未经过滤的骆驼。

college-writing-006035.en: “You wanna I put this food in your ashtray, or are you gonna move it?”
college-writing-006035.zh: “你想我把这些食物放在你的烟灰缸里，还是你要搬家？”

college-writing-006037.en: The woman moves the ashtray aside.
college-writing-006037.zh: 女人把烟灰缸移到一边。

college-writing-006039.en: “I’m not really yelling at you, dear,” he answers.
college-writing-006039.zh: “我不是真的在对你大喊大叫，亲爱的，”他回答。

college-writing-006041.zh: “我很高兴你今天早上在这里。”

college-writing-006043.en: “That girl you’ve got working here sometimes, Lou─she doesn’t like me.”
college-writing-006043.zh: “你有时在这里工作的那个女孩，娄——她不喜欢我。”

college-writing-006044.en: Lou rolls his eyes, apparently at the poor taste of the waitress, and moves down to the cash register.
college-writing-006044.zh: 娄翻了个白眼，显然是因为女服务员的可恶品味，然后走到收银机前。

college-writing-006045.en: As he rings up a bill, a teenage girl enters and walks by silently.
college-writing-006045.zh: 当他拨打账单时，一个十几岁的女孩悄悄地走进来。

college-writing-006047.en: “Start the day with a ‘Good morning,’ please,” he instructs.
college-writing-006047.zh: “请以‘早上好’开始新的一天，”他指示道。

college-writing-006049.en: “Very nice,” he mutters, still punching the cash-register buttons.
college-writing-006049.zh: “非常好，”他喃喃自语，还在按下收银员的按钮。

college-writing-006050.en: “Thank you so much for your concern. I get up at the crack of dawn to make your breakfast, but don’t bother saying ‘good morning’ to me.”
college-writing-006050.zh: “非常感谢你的关心。我在黎明时分起床给你做早餐，但不要费心对我说‘早上好’。”

college-writing-006051.en: The day’s earliest arrival, the woman in the booth, has been joined by a companion.
college-writing-006051.zh: 当天最早到来的女人，展位上的女人，已经有一位同伴加入了。

college-writing-006052.en: They order eggs and hash browns.

college-writing-006053.en: As Lou slides the filled plates before them, he reverts briefly to the conventional manners he saves for first-timers.
college-writing-006053.zh: 当 Lou 将装满的盘子滑到他们面前时，他会短暂地恢复到他为初学者保存的传统方式。

college-writing-006057.en: Lou’s reserve of politeness is instantly exhausted.
college-writing-006057.zh: 娄的礼貌储备立即被耗尽。

college-writing-006058.en: “Hot sauce. Jeez. She wants hot sauce!” he announces to the room at large.
college-writing-006058.zh: “辣酱。天哪。她想要辣酱！” 他向整个房间宣布。

college-writing-006059.en: “Anything else? Some caviar on the side, maybe?”

college-writing-006060.en: He disappears behind the counter, reemerging with an enormous red bottle.
college-writing-006060.zh: 他消失在柜台后面，带着一个巨大的红色瓶子重新出现。

college-writing-006061.en: “Here you are. It’s a new bottle. Don’t use it all, please. I’d like to save a little for other customers. Hey, on second thought, use it all if you want. Then I’ll know you’ll like my chili.”
college-writing-006061.zh: “你来了。这是一个新瓶子。请不要全部使用。我想为其他客户节省一点。嘿，再想一想，如果你愿意，就用它。然后我会知道你会喜欢我的辣椒。”

college-writing-006062.en: Laughing loudly at his own joke, he refills the woman’s coffee cup without being asked.
college-writing-006062.zh: 大声笑着自己的笑话，他没有被问到女人的咖啡杯。

college-writing-006063.en: Golden-brown coffee splashes into her saucer.
college-writing-006063.zh: 金棕色的咖啡溅到她的碟子里。

college-writing-006065.en: Lou’s waitress, Stacy, has arrived, and begins taking orders and delivering meals.
college-writing-006065.zh: 娄的女服务员斯泰西来了，开始接受订单和送餐。

college-writing-006066.en: Lou alternates between working the grill and clearing tables.
college-writing-006066.zh: Lou 在工作烤架和清理台之间交替使用。

college-writing-006067.en: Mid-stride, he halts before the golden-haired woman at the counter, who has pushed her plate aside and is lighting another cigarette.
college-writing-006067.zh: 大步走在柜台前的金发女子面前停下来，她把盘子推到一边，正在点燃另一支烟。

college-writing-006069.en: “Looouuu . . .” she begins soothingly, a stream of smoke jetting from her mouth with the word.
college-writing-006069.zh: “卢欧你……” 她开始舒缓地开始，一股烟雾从她嘴里喷出，带着这个词。

college-writing-006071.en: “You don’t eat your toast, you don’t eat your potatoes, you barely touch your eggs. Whatcha gonna live on? Camels?”
college-writing-006071.zh: “你不吃吐司，你不吃土豆，你几乎不碰你的鸡蛋。要靠什么生活？骆驼？”

college-writing-006072.zh: 第222章 论文发展模式

college-writing-006073.en: “Awww, Lou,” she says, but she pulls her plate back and eats a few more bites.
college-writing-006073.zh: “哇，娄，”她说，但她把盘子拉了回来，又吃了几口。

college-writing-006074.en: As the rush of customers slows to a trickle, Lou returns to the register, making change and conversation, talking Phillies and the weather.
college-writing-006074.zh: 随着顾客的匆忙慢慢到涓涓细流，娄回到收银台，做出改变和交谈，谈论费城人队和天气。

college-writing-006075.en: One of the flannel-shirted men rises from his counter seat and heads for the door, dropping his money on the counter.
college-writing-006075.zh: 其中一名穿着法兰绒衬衫的人从柜台上站起来，朝门口走去，把钱丢在柜台上。

college-writing-006076.en: “‘Bye, Stacy,” he says to the waitress.
college-writing-006076.zh: “再见，斯泰西，”他对女服务员说。

college-writing-006082.en: “Who cares what kind of a day you have?”

college-writing-006083.en: Mel disappears into the morning sunshine; the Camel lady pulls a crossword puzzle out of her purse and taps an unlit cigarette rapidly against the counter.
college-writing-006083.zh: 梅尔消失在晨光中； 骆驼夫人从她的钱包里拿出一个填字游戏，快速地将一支未点燃的香烟轻拍在柜台上。

college-writing-006084.en: Stacy wipes the tables and empties a wastebasket of its load of dark, wet coffee grounds.
college-writing-006084.zh: 斯泰西擦了擦桌子，清空了一个废纸篓，里面装满了黑暗、潮湿的咖啡渣。

college-writing-006085.en: Lou butters a piece of toast and returns to his favorite booth.
college-writing-006085.zh: Lou Butters 一块吐司，回到他最喜欢的展位。

college-writing-006086.en: He spreads out his newspaper again, then glances up to catch the eye of the hot-sauce woman.
college-writing-006086.zh: 他又把报纸散开，然后抬头看了看辣酱女人的眼神。

college-writing-006091.en: “No, he didn’t leave me. He just had to go to work . . .” “Dump him,” Lou responds automatically.
college-writing-006091.zh: “不，他没有离开我。他只需要去上班……” “甩了他，”娄自动回应道。

college-writing-006092.en: “And now, if you don’t mind very much, I would like to finish my newspaper.”
college-writing-006092.zh: “现在，如果你不介意，我想完成我的报纸。”

college-writing-006094.en: 1. What is the thesis of Johnson’s essay?
college-writing-006094.zh: 1. 约翰逊论文的论文是什么？

college-writing-006095.en: If it is stated directly, locate the relevant
college-writing-006095.zh: 如果直接说明，请找到相关的

college-writing-006097.en: If it is implied, state the thesis in your own words.
college-writing-006097.zh: 如果有暗示，请用您自己的话说明论文。

college-writing-006098.en: 2. Which statement would best serve as a topic sentence for paragraph 13?
college-writing-006098.zh: 2. 哪项陈述最适合作为第 13 段的 主题句？

college-writing-006100.en: Many of Lou’s customers are, like him, interested in the Philadelphia
college-writing-006100.zh: 娄的许多客户和他一样对费城感兴趣

college-writing-006102.en: b. Lou doesn’t mind if customers serve themselves coffee.
college-writing-006102.zh: B. 娄不介意顾客是否为自己提供咖啡。

college-writing-006103.en: c. Lou apparently disliked the two men in oil-company caps who came into
college-writing-006103.zh: c.  娄显然不喜欢进入石油公司的两个人

college-writing-006106.en: Regular customers at Lou’s are used to taking care of themselves while
college-writing-006106.zh: Lou's的普通客户习惯于照顾自己，同时

college-writing-006109.en: 3. In paragraph 3, Johnson claims that Lou and his customers are fond of one
college-writing-006109.zh: 3. 在第 3 段中，Johnson 声称 Lou 和他的客户喜欢其中一位

college-writing-006111.en: How does she support that claim in the case of the golden-haired woman who is first mentioned in paragraph 26?
college-writing-006111.zh: 对于第 26 段中首次提及的金发妇女，她如何支持这一主张？

college-writing-006114.en: 4. We are told that customers enjoy the unusual atmosphere of Lou’s coffee
college-writing-006114.zh: 4.我们被告知顾客享受娄咖啡的不同寻常的氛围

college-writing-006116.en: What detail in paragraph 25 supports this idea?
college-writing-006116.zh: 第 25 段中的哪些细节支持这一想法？

college-writing-006117.en: 5. Find a paragraph that appeals to three senses and identify those senses.
college-writing-006117.zh: 5. 找到一个吸引三种感官的段落并识别这些感官。

college-writing-006119.en: 6. Which sentence in paragraph 31 contains a change-of-direction signal?
college-writing-006119.zh: 6. 第 31 段中的哪个句子包含方向变化信号？

college-writing-006120.en: 7. Which sentence in paragraph 23 begins with a time signal?
college-writing-006120.zh: 7. 第 23 段中的哪个句子以时间信号开头？

college-writing-006123.en: 8. The sentence that makes up paragraph 38 includes which of the following
college-writing-006123.zh: 8. 构成第 38 段的句子包括以下哪一项

college-writing-006130.en: 9. Johnson begins with a situation that is the opposite of the one that will be
college-writing-006130.zh: 9. 约翰逊从一种与将要发生的情况相反的情况开始

college-writing-006132.en: Rewrite paragraph 1 using another method for introducing essays explained in Chapter 4: a broad statement that gets narrowed or a brief story.
college-writing-006132.zh: 使用另一种方法来重写第 4 章中解释的论文：一个广泛的陈述或一个简短的故事。

college-writing-006133.en: 10. “Lou’s Place” ends with a comment by Lou that characterizes the mood of his shop.
college-writing-006133.zh: 10. “Lou's Place”以 Lou 的评论结尾，描述了他商店的情绪。

college-writing-006134.en: Rewrite this conclusion by using another method for concluding essays as explained in Chapter 4, summarizing the description of the shop or predicting something about the future of the shop or its owner.
college-writing-006134.zh: 通过使用另一种方法来结束论文，如第 4 章所述，重写这个结论，总结对商店的描述或预测商店或其主人的未来。

college-writing-006135.zh: 224 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006136.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Description
college-writing-006136.zh: 写一篇强调描述的论文

college-writing-006137.en: Write an essay that describes your strengths and weaknesses as a student.
college-writing-006137.zh: 写一篇文章，描述你作为学生的长处和短处。

college-writing-006138.en: You will want to use specific details that support your purpose.
college-writing-006138.zh: 您将希望使用支持您的目的的特定细节。

college-writing-006139.en: You may also want to look ahead to Chapter 13, “Comparison and/or Contrast” and Chapter 16, “Argument.”
college-writing-006139.zh: 您可能还想展望第 13 章“比较和/或对比”和第 16 章“论证”。

college-writing-006142.en: Like all essays, this essay must have a thesis.
college-writing-006142.zh: 像所有论文一样，这篇文章必须有论文。

college-writing-006143.zh: 它应该说明你的主导地位

college-writing-006144.en: impression of yourself as a college student.
college-writing-006144.zh: 对自己作为大学生的印象。

college-writing-006145.en: Write a short sentence that summarizes what kind of student you think you are.
college-writing-006145.zh: 写一个简短的句子，总结你认为你是什么样的学生。

college-writing-006146.en: Don’t worry if your thesis doesn’t feel just right─you can always revise later.
college-writing-006146.zh: 如果您的论文感觉不正确，请不要担心——您以后可以随时修改。

college-writing-006147.en: For now, just express your opinion.

college-writing-006148.en: Here are a couple of examples:

college-writing-006149.en: I am a model college student.

college-writing-006150.en: Although I am in college, I haven’t yet acquired good study habits.
college-writing-006150.zh: 虽然我在上大学，但我还没有养成良好的学习习惯。

college-writing-006152.en: Once you have written your sentence, make a list of as many details as you
college-writing-006152.zh: 写完你的句子后，列出尽可能多的细节

college-writing-006153.en: can to support that general impression.

college-writing-006154.en: For example, this could be a list made by a student who thought she was a great college student:
college-writing-006154.zh: 例如，这可能是一个认为她是一名优秀大学生的学生列出的清单：

college-writing-006155.en: always study assigned homework schedule study time every day participate in class attend class every day meet with professors regularly seek tutoring when necessary participate in several clubs
college-writing-006155.zh: 每天学习分配的作业安排学习时间 每天参加课堂 上课 每天与教授会面 定期寻求辅导 参加几个俱乐部

college-writing-006157.en: After creating a list, organize your paper to effectively support your purpose.
college-writing-006157.zh: 创建列表后，组织您的论文以有效支持您的目标。

college-writing-006158.en: If you choose emphatic order, start with your least important example and end with your most important example.
college-writing-006158.zh: 如果您选择强调顺序，请从您最不重要的示例开始，以您最重要的示例结束。

college-writing-006159.en: This will create a more persuasive tone.
college-writing-006159.zh: 这将创造更有说服力的语气。

college-writing-006161.en: Use as many specific details as possible to create a full picture for your reader.
college-writing-006161.zh: 使用尽可能多的特定细节为您的读者创建完整的图片。

college-writing-006162.en: For example, instead of saying, “I study at the same time every day,” you might say, “Each night, I study from 7:00 p.m. until 11:00 p.m. because it is the most quiet time in my house.”
college-writing-006162.zh: 例如，与其说“我每天都在同一时间学习”，而不是说：“我每天晚上7:00到晚上11:00，因为这是我家里最安静的时间。”

college-writing-006164.en: Proceed to write the first draft of your essay.

college-writing-006167.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while─if possible, until the next day.
college-writing-006167.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，将其放在一边——如果可能的话，直到第二天。

college-writing-006168.en: When you review the draft, try to do so as critically as you would if it were not your own work.
college-writing-006168.zh: 当您查看草稿时，请尝试尽可能批判地进行，如果它不是您自己的工作。

college-writing-006169.en: Ask yourself the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-006169.zh: 在本章末尾的四个基础清单中问自己的问题。

college-writing-006170.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-006170.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-006171.en: Write an essay that describes and summarizes the key ideas in a chosen book or essay.
college-writing-006171.zh: 写一篇文章，描述和总结选定的书或论文中的关键思想。

college-writing-006172.en: The work you choose may be assigned by your instructor, or it may require your instructor’s approval.
college-writing-006172.zh: 您选择的工作可能由您的教师分配，也可能需要您的教师的批准。

college-writing-006173.en: You may want to check Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay,” for proper citation of the material you reference from your work.
college-writing-006173.zh: 您可能想查看第 20 章“撰写研究论文”，以正确引用您从作品中引用的材料。

college-writing-006176.en: Find a quote that expresses the main principle of the author’s thesis.
college-writing-006176.zh: 找一个表达作者论文主要原则的引文。

college-writing-006179.en: a. What does the author want you to understand?
college-writing-006179.zh: 一。 作者想让你明白什么？

college-writing-006180.en: b. What is the author’s main purpose?
college-writing-006180.zh: B. 作者的主要目的是什么？

college-writing-006181.en: c. What ideas does the author use to support their purpose?
college-writing-006181.zh: c.  作者用什么想法来支持他们的目的？

college-writing-006183.en: Decide how you will organize your essay.
college-writing-006183.zh: 决定你将如何组织你的论文。

college-writing-006184.en: Your decision will depend on what
college-writing-006184.zh: 你的决定将取决于什么

college-writing-006185.en: seems appropriate for the chosen work.

college-writing-006186.en: You may want to describe the main ideas in the same order as they are originally presented, or you may choose to describe the ideas in emphatic order, saving the most important idea for last.
college-writing-006186.zh: 您可能想按照最初呈现的顺序描述主要思想，或者您可以选择以强调的顺序描述这些想法，将最重要的想法留到最后。

college-writing-006188.en: Make a scratch outline for your essay, based on the organization you have
college-writing-006188.zh: 根据您拥有的组织为您的论文制作草稿大纲

college-writing-006191.en: Using your scratch outline as a guide, make a list of supporting details.
college-writing-006191.zh: 使用您的 Scratch Outline 作为指南，列出 支撑细节。

college-writing-006193.en: Use your scratch outline and list of details to write your first draft.
college-writing-006193.zh: 使用您的草稿大纲和详细信息列表来编写您的初稿。

college-writing-006194.en: REVISING Refer to the FOUR BASES Checklist provided at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-006194.zh: 修订 参考本章末尾提供的四个基础清单。

college-writing-006195.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-006195.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-006196.en: Imagine that you are working for a travel agency and have been asked to write a letter to prospective clients advertising a wonderful vacation destination you have
college-writing-006196.zh: 想象一下，您正在为一家旅行社工作，并被要求给潜在客户写一封信，宣传您拥有的一个美妙的度假目的地

college-writing-006199.zh: 第226章 论文发展模式

college-writing-006201.en: It might be a large city, a seaside town, an archeological site, a theme park that caters to families, a resort for honeymooners, a dude ranch, a lake, or a mountain hideaway.
college-writing-006201.zh: 它可能是一座大城市、一个海滨小镇、一个考古遗址、一个迎合家庭的主题公园、一个度蜜月的度假胜地、一个花花公子的牧场、一个湖泊或一个山区的世外桃源。

college-writing-006202.en: Then again, you might want to advertise a cruise or even a vacation that involves public service, like the kinds sponsored by Habitat for Humanity.
college-writing-006202.zh: 再说一次，您可能想宣传游轮甚至涉及公共服务的假期，例如 Habitat for Humanity 赞助的那种。

college-writing-006203.en: Your purpose is, of course, to get your clients to sign up for the vacation you are advertising.
college-writing-006203.zh: 当然，您的目的是让您的客户注册您正在宣传的假期。

college-writing-006204.en: Focus on a particular type of audience: college students, young professionals, families, singles, or senior citizens, for example.
college-writing-006204.zh: 关注特定类型的受众：例如，大学生、年轻专业人士、家庭、单身人士或老年人。

college-writing-006205.en: You may want to check Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” and Chapter 16, “Argument,” to create a persuasive tone that will sell your destination.
college-writing-006205.zh: 您可能需要查看第 10 章“例证”和第 16 章“论点”，以创建一种有说服力的语气来出售您的目的地。

college-writing-006208.en: First, gather details about the physical appearance, sounds, smells, and even
college-writing-006208.zh: 首先，收集有关外貌、声音、气味甚至甚至

college-writing-006209.en: tastes of the setting your clients will visit.
college-writing-006209.zh: 您的客户将访问的环境的味道。

college-writing-006210.en: Talk about how it feels to swim in a crystal-clear lagoon or describe the taste of a crab sandwich you bought at a straw-covered beach shack.
college-writing-006210.zh: 谈谈在水晶般清澈的泻湖中游泳的感觉，或者描述您在稻草覆盖的海滩小屋中购买的螃蟹三明治的味道。

college-writing-006211.en: Describe the natural setting, as well the kind of weather your clients can expect.
college-writing-006211.zh: 描述自然环境，以及您的客户可以期待的天气。

college-writing-006212.en: Discuss what the living and dining accommodations are like as well.
college-writing-006212.zh: 讨论客厅和餐厅的住宿情况。

college-writing-006213.en: By the way, if you are advertising a public-service vacation, you might have to tell them about the tents they’ll be sleeping in or the outdoor toilets they’ll use.
college-writing-006213.zh: 顺便说一句，如果您正在为公共服务假期做广告，您可能必须告诉他们他们将睡在的帐篷或他们将使用的户外厕所。

college-writing-006214.en: In any case, use as many senses as possible.
college-writing-006214.zh: 无论如何，使用尽可能多的感官。

college-writing-006216.en: Keeping the type of audience you have chosen in mind, tell your readers about
college-writing-006216.zh: 牢记您选择的受众类型，告诉您的读者

college-writing-006217.en: the kinds of people they are likely to meet, both the tourists and permanent residents.
college-writing-006217.zh: 他们可能会遇到的人，包括游客和永久居民。

college-writing-006218.en: Ask yourself questions such as: Are the tourists mostly single, young married couples, families?
college-writing-006218.zh: 问自己一些问题，例如：游客大多是单身、年轻的已婚夫妇、家庭吗？

college-writing-006219.en: Are most of the people young, middle-aged, older?
college-writing-006219.zh: 大多数人都是年轻人、中年人、老年人吗？

college-writing-006220.en: Or is there a mix of ages?
college-writing-006220.zh: 还是有不同年龄的混合体？

college-writing-006221.en: Are these people friendly, helpful, interesting?
college-writing-006221.zh: 这些人友好、乐于助人、有趣吗？

college-writing-006224.en: Are they fun-loving and active or more private and sedate?
college-writing-006224.zh: 他们是爱好玩的、活跃的还是更私密和平静的？

college-writing-006225.en: What about the people who work or live at the place?
college-writing-006225.zh: 在这个地方工作或生活的人呢？

college-writing-006226.zh: 他们友好、乐于助人等吗？

college-writing-006230.en: Finally, provide details about the activities your clients might pursue during
college-writing-006230.zh: 最后，提供有关您的客户可能从事的活动的详细信息

college-writing-006232.en: Does the place offer hang gliding, scuba diving, tours of famous landmarks?
college-writing-006232.zh: 这个地方提供悬挂式滑翔、水肺潜水、著名地标之旅吗？

college-writing-006233.en: Again, if this is a public-service vacation, will your readers be digging wells, framing houses, or constructing schoolhouses?
college-writing-006233.zh: 同样，如果这是一个公共服务假期，您的读者会挖掘井、构筑房屋或建造校舍吗？

college-writing-006235.en: After reading the notes you have gathered, write a rough outline that might
college-writing-006235.zh: 阅读您收集的笔记后，写下可能的大致轮廓

college-writing-006236.en: look like this: A. The place
college-writing-006236.zh: 看起来像这样： A. 地方

college-writing-006247.en: Now, plan your introductory and concluding sections.
college-writing-006247.zh: 现在，计划您的介绍和结论部分。

college-writing-006249.en: state a thesis that is intended to persuade your readers.
college-writing-006249.zh: 陈述旨在说服读者的论文。

college-writing-006250.en: In addition, prepare them for the points you are going to cover and the order in which you will cover them.
college-writing-006250.zh: 此外，为您将要涵盖的积分和覆盖它们的顺序做好准备。

college-writing-006252.en: The setting and accommodations, the people, and the activities make a week at Crystal Bay Resort the ideal family beach vacation.
college-writing-006252.zh: 水晶湾度假村的环境和住宿、人员和活动使一周成为理想的家庭海滩度假。

college-writing-006253.en: Your conclusion might summarize or remind your readers of the best reasons to book the vacation.
college-writing-006253.zh: 您的结论可能会总结或提醒您的读者预订假期的最佳理由。

college-writing-006254.en: Naturally, you will have to mention the cost of accommodations and travel as well.
college-writing-006254.zh: 当然，您还必须提到住宿和旅行的费用。

college-writing-006255.en: DRAFTING Write your rough draft by following your outline closely, but don’t be a slave to it.
college-writing-006255.zh: 起草 通过密切遵循你的大纲来写你的草稿，但不要成为它的奴隶。

college-writing-006256.en: If new ideas or details pop into your mind, put them down.
college-writing-006256.zh: 如果新的想法或细节出现在您的脑海中，请放下它们。

college-writing-006257.en: You can fix any inconsistencies or repetitions when it comes time to revise.
college-writing-006257.zh: 当需要修改时，您可以修复任何不一致或重复。

college-writing-006258.en: Just be as detailed as you can at this point.
college-writing-006258.zh: 在这一点上尽可能详细。

college-writing-006259.en: REVISING Read your first draft to a classmate who is willing to listen carefully and work hard at providing valuable feedback.
college-writing-006259.zh: 修改 阅读您的初稿给愿意仔细倾听并努力提供有价值反馈的同学。

college-writing-006260.en: Refer to the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of the chapter for questions to consider while revising.
college-writing-006260.zh: 请参阅本章末尾的四个基准清单，了解修订时要考虑的问题。

college-writing-006261.zh: 228 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006264.en: Does my essay have a clearly stated thesis, including a dominant impression?
college-writing-006264.zh: 我的文章是否有明确的论点，包括主要印象？

college-writing-006265.en: Does each paragraph, and each sentence within that paragraph, help to develop the description of my topic?
college-writing-006265.zh: 该段落中的每个段落和每个句子是否有助于发展对我的主题的描述？

college-writing-006266.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-006266.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-006268.en: Have I provided rich, specific details that appeal to a variety of senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch)?
college-writing-006268.zh: 我是否提供了丰富、具体的细节来吸引各种感官（视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉）？

college-writing-006269.en: Have I chosen dynamic and vibrant words to enhance my description?
college-writing-006269.zh: 我是否选择了动态和充满活力的词来增强我的描述？

college-writing-006271.en: Do transitional words and phrases, and linking sentences between paragraphs, help make the description clear?
college-writing-006271.zh: 过渡词和短语，以及在段落之间链接句子是否有助于使描述清晰？

college-writing-006272.en: Does my conclusion clearly tie up the essay and explain why this topic was significant enough to describe?
college-writing-006272.zh: 我的结论是否清楚地结合了这篇文章并解释了为什么这个话题的意义足以描述？

college-writing-006274.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-006274.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-006275.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-006275.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-006276.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-006276.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-006278.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-006278.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-006282.en: Used by permission of Townsend Press.
college-writing-006282.zh: 经 Townsend Press 许可使用。

college-writing-006283.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on narration • write an essay with emphasis on narration • revise an essay with emphasis on narration
college-writing-006283.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写以叙事为重点的论文 • 写一篇强调叙述的文章 • 修改文章，强调叙述

college-writing-006284.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize narration • one professional model essay that emphasizes narration
college-writing-006284.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调叙述的学生论文 • 一篇强调叙事的专业模型论文

college-writing-006286.en: Imagine that you are the owner of your own very successful company, which you have built from the ground up.
college-writing-006286.zh: 想象一下，您是您自己非常成功的公司的所有者，这是您从头开始建立的。

college-writing-006287.en: You have been asked to share your experience with a group of young entrepreneurs who have hopes of owning their own businesses someday.
college-writing-006287.zh: 您被要求与一群希望有朝一日拥有自己企业的年轻企业家分享您的经验。

college-writing-006288.en: Write a narrative of your success story, including the type of business you own, how you came up with the idea, and how you managed to make it a success.
college-writing-006288.zh: 写下你的成功故事的叙述，包括你拥有的企业类型，你如何提出这个想法，以及你如何成功地做到这一点。

college-writing-006289.zh: 路透社/阿拉米库存照片

college-writing-006290.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-006291.en: Children beg to hear a beloved story read again and again.
college-writing-006291.zh: 孩子们乞求一遍又一遍地听一个心爱的故事。

college-writing-006292.en: Over dinner, tired adults tell each other about their day.
college-writing-006292.zh: 晚餐时，疲惫的成年人互相讲述他们的一天。

college-writing-006293.en: A restless class is hushed when a teacher says, “Let me tell you something strange that happened to me once.”
college-writing-006293.zh: 当一位老师说：“让我告诉你一次发生在我身上的奇怪事情时，不安分的课堂被安静了下来。”

college-writing-006294.en: Whatever our age, we never outgrow our hunger for stories.
college-writing-006294.zh: 无论我们的年龄如何，我们都不会超越对故事的渴望。

college-writing-006295.en: Just as our ancestors entertained and instructed each other with tales of great hunts and battles, of angry gods and foolish humans, we still love to share our lives and learn about others through storytelling.
college-writing-006295.zh: 正如我们的祖先用伟大的狩猎和战斗、愤怒的神灵和愚蠢的人类的故事互相娱乐和指导一样，我们仍然喜欢通过讲故事来分享我们的生活并了解他人。

college-writing-006296.zh: 230 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006298.en: Narration is storytelling, whether we are relating a single story or several related ones.
college-writing-006298.zh: 叙述是讲故事的，无论我们是在讲一个故事还是几个相关的故事。

college-writing-006299.en: Through narration, we make a statement clear by relating in detail something that has happened to us.
college-writing-006299.zh: 通过叙述，我们通过详细说明发生在我们身上的事情来明确陈述。

college-writing-006300.en: In the story we tell, we present the details in the order in which they happened.
college-writing-006300.zh: 在我们讲述的故事中，我们按照它们发生的顺序呈现细节。

college-writing-006301.en: A person might say, for example, “I was really embarrassed the day I took my driver’s test,” and then go on to develop that statement with an account of the experience.
college-writing-006301.zh: 例如，一个人可能会说，“在我参加驾驶考试的那天，我真的很尴尬”，然后继续开发该声明并说明了这段经历。

college-writing-006302.en: If the story is sharply detailed, we will be able to see and understand just why the speaker felt that way.
college-writing-006302.zh: 如果故事非常详细，我们将能够看到和理解说话者为什么会有这种感觉。

college-writing-006303.en: In this chapter, you’ll be asked to tell a story that illustrates a specific point.
college-writing-006303.zh: 在本章中，您将被要求讲述一个说明特定观点的故事。

college-writing-006304.en: To prepare for this assignment, first read the student essays and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany each piece of writing.
college-writing-006304.zh: 为了准备这项作业，首先阅读学生的论文和模型论文，并解决每篇文章随附的问题。

college-writing-006305.en: All three essays emphasize narration to develop their points.
college-writing-006305.zh: 这三篇文章都强调叙事以发展他们的观点。

college-writing-006307.en: My church recently staged a “Sensitivity Sunday” to make our congregation more aware of the problems faced by people with physical disabilities.
college-writing-006307.zh: 我的教会最近举办了一个“敏感星期天”，让我们的会众更加了解身体残疾人面临的问题。

college-writing-006308.en: We were asked to “take on a disability” for several hours one Sunday morning.
college-writing-006308.zh: 一个星期天早上，我们被要求“承担残疾”几个小时。

college-writing-006309.en: Some members, like me, chose to use wheelchairs.
college-writing-006309.zh: 一些成员，像我一样，选择使用轮椅。

college-writing-006310.en: Others wore sound-blocking earplugs, maneuvered around on crutches, or wore blindfolds.
college-writing-006310.zh: 其他人戴着隔音耳塞，在拐杖上四处移动，或戴着眼罩。

college-writing-006311.en: Just sitting in the wheelchair was instructive.
college-writing-006311.zh: 只是坐在轮椅上很有启发性。

college-writing-006312.en: I had never considered before what it would be like to use one.
college-writing-006312.zh: 我以前从未考虑过使用一种是什么感觉。

college-writing-006313.en: As soon as I sat down, my weight made the chair begin to roll.
college-writing-006313.zh: 我一坐下，我的体重就让椅子开始滚动。

college-writing-006314.en: Its wheels were not locked, and I fumbled clumsily to correct that.
college-writing-006314.zh: 它的轮子没有锁上，我笨拙地摸索着纠正了这一点。

college-writing-006315.en: Something else I didn’t expect was figuring out where and how to place my feet.
college-writing-006315.zh: 我没想到的其他事情是弄清楚我的脚在哪里以及如何放置。

college-writing-006316.en: I fumbled some more to turn the metal footrest into place.
college-writing-006316.zh: 我又摸索了一些将金属脚凳调到位。

college-writing-006317.en: I felt psychologically challenged as well, as I took my first uneasy look at what was to be my only means of transportation for several hours.
college-writing-006317.zh: 我也感到心理上受到了挑战，因为我第一次不安地看了几个小时我唯一的交通工具。

college-writing-006318.en: I realized that for many people, using a wheelchair is not a temporary experiment.
college-writing-006318.zh: 我意识到对于很多人来说，使用轮椅并不是一个临时的实验。

college-writing-006319.en: That was a sobering thought as I sank back into my seat.
college-writing-006319.zh: 当我回到座位上时，这是一个发人深省的想法。

college-writing-006320.en: Once I sat down, I had to learn how to cope with the wheelchair.
college-writing-006320.zh: 坐下后，我必须学习如何应对轮椅。

college-writing-006321.en: I shifted around, trying to find a comfortable position.
college-writing-006321.zh: 我转身，试图找到一个舒适的位置。

college-writing-006322.en: I thought it might be restful, even kind of nice, to be pushed around for a while.
college-writing-006322.zh: 我想可能会被推开一段时间可能会很平静，甚至有点好。

college-writing-006323.en: I glanced around to see who would be pushing me and then realized I would have to navigate the wheelchair by myself.
college-writing-006323.zh: 我环顾四周，看看谁会推我，然后意识到我必须自己驾车轮椅。

college-writing-006327.en: wrist and forearm muscles started to ache as I tugged at the heavy metal wheels.
college-writing-006327.zh: 当我拉扯重金属轮子时，手腕和前臂肌肉开始疼痛。

college-writing-006328.en: I realized, as I veered this way and that, that steering and turning were not going to be easy tasks.
college-writing-006328.zh: 我意识到，当我以这种方式转向时，转向和转向并不是一件容易的事。

college-writing-006329.en: Trying to make a right-angle turn from one aisle to another, I steered straight into a pew.
college-writing-006329.zh: 我试图从一个过道到另一个过道的直角转弯，我直接转向了一个长椅。

college-writing-006330.en: I felt as though everyone was staring at me and commenting on my clumsiness.
college-writing-006330.zh: 我觉得每个人都在盯着我看，评论我的笨拙。

college-writing-006331.en: When the service started, other problems cropped up to frustrate me further.
college-writing-006331.zh: 当服务开始时，其他问题也让我感到沮丧。

college-writing-006332.en: Every time the congregation stood up, my view was blocked.
college-writing-006332.zh: 每次会众站起来，我的视线被挡住了。

college-writing-006333.en: I could not see the minister, the choir, or the altar.
college-writing-006333.zh: 我看不到部长、合唱团或祭坛。

college-writing-006334.en: Also, as the church’s aisles were narrow, I seemed to be in the way no matter where I was.
college-writing-006334.zh: 此外，由于教堂的过道很窄，无论我身在何处，我似乎都挡住了路。

college-writing-006335.en: For instance, the ushers had to squeeze by me to pass the collection plate.
college-writing-006335.zh: 例如，引座员不得不挤在我身边才能通过收集盘。

college-writing-006336.en: This made me feel like a nuisance.
college-writing-006336.zh: 这让我觉得自己很讨厌。

college-writing-006337.en: Thanks to a new building program, however, our church will soon have the wide aisles and wellspaced pews that will make life easier for people with disabilities.
college-writing-006337.zh: 然而，多亏了一个新的建筑计划，我们的教会很快将拥有宽阔的过道和空间宽敞的长椅，这将使残疾人的生活更轻松。

college-writing-006338.en: After the service ended, when people stopped to talk to me, I had to strain my neck and look up at them.
college-writing-006338.zh: 服务结束后，当人们停下来和我说话时，我不得不拉紧脖子并抬头看着他们。

college-writing-006339.en: This made me feel like a little child being talked down to and added to my sense of powerlessness.
college-writing-006339.zh: 这让我觉得自己像个小孩被低声谈论并增加了我的无力感。

college-writing-006340.en: My wheelchair experiment was soon over.
college-writing-006340.zh: 我的轮椅实验很快就结束了。

college-writing-006341.en: It’s true that it made an impression on me. I no longer resent large tax expenditures for rampequipped buses, and I wouldn’t dream of parking my car in a space marked “ADA Accessible.”
college-writing-006341.zh: 确实，它给我留下了深刻的印象。 我不再讨厌装备斜坡的公共汽车的大笔税收支出，我也做不到将车停在标有“ADA 无障碍”的空间中。

college-writing-006342.en: But I also realize how little I know about the daily life of a person with disabilities.
college-writing-006342.zh: 但我也意识到我对残疾人的日常生活知之甚少。

college-writing-006343.en: A few hours of using a wheelchair gave me only a hint of the challenges, both physical and emotional, that people with disabilities must overcome.
college-writing-006343.zh: 几个小时使用轮椅只给了我一些残疾人必须克服的身体和情感挑战。

college-writing-006345.en: According to my history instructor, Adolf Hitler once said that he wanted to sign up “brutal youths” to help him achieve his goals.
college-writing-006345.zh: 根据我的历史教练的说法，阿道夫·希特勒曾经说过他想签下“残酷的年轻人”来帮助他实现自己的目标。

college-writing-006346.en: If Hitler were still alive, he wouldn’t have any trouble recruiting the brutal youths he wanted; he could get them right here in the United States.
college-writing-006346.zh: 如果希特勒还活着，他就不会有任何麻烦招募他想要的残酷年轻人； 他可以在美国得到它们。

college-writing-006347.en: I know, because I was one of them.
college-writing-006347.zh: 我知道，因为我是他们中的一员。

college-writing-006348.en: As a teenager, I ran with a gang.
college-writing-006348.zh: 十几岁的时候，我和一个帮派一起跑步。

college-writing-006349.en: And it took a frightening incident for me to see how violent I had become.
college-writing-006349.zh: 我花了一个可怕的事件才看到我变得多么暴力。

college-writing-006350.en: The incident was planned one Thursday night when I was out with my friends.
college-writing-006350.zh: 这起事件是在星期四晚上我和朋友出去的时候计划的。

college-writing-006351.en: I was still going to school once in a while, but most of my friends weren’t.
college-writing-006351.zh: 我偶尔还在上学，但我的大多数朋友都没有。

college-writing-006352.en: We spent our days on the streets, talking, showing off, sometimes shoplifting a little or shaking people down for a few dollars.
college-writing-006352.zh: 我们在街上度过了我们的日子，聊天，炫耀，有时偷窃一点点，或者为了几美元而动摇人们。

college-writing-006353.en: My friends and I were close, maybe because life hadn’t been very good to any of us.
college-writing-006353.zh: 我和我的朋友很亲近，也许是因为生活对我们中的任何一个人都不是很好。

college-writing-006354.en: On this night, we were drinking wine and vodka on the corner.
college-writing-006354.zh: 在这个晚上，我们在拐角处喝着葡萄酒和伏特加。

college-writing-006355.en: For some reason, we all felt tense and restless.
college-writing-006355.zh: 出于某种原因，我们都感到紧张和不安。

college-writing-006356.en: One of us came up with the idea of robbing one of the old people who lived in the high-rise close by.
college-writing-006356.zh: 我们中的一个人想出了抢劫住在附近高层建筑中的一位老人的想法。

college-writing-006357.en: We would just knock the person over, grab the money, and party with it.
college-writing-006357.zh: 我们只会把那个人打倒，抓住钱，然后和它一起聚会。

college-writing-006372.en: After about an hour, and after more wine and vodka, we spotted an old man.
college-writing-006372.zh: 大约一个小时后，在更多的酒和伏特加之后，我们发现了一个老人。

college-writing-006373.en: He came out of the glass door of the building and started up the street.
college-writing-006373.zh: 他从大楼的玻璃门出来，开始了街道。

college-writing-006374.en: Pine Street had a lot of antique stores as well as apartment buildings.
college-writing-006374.zh: 松街有很多古董店和公寓楼。

college-writing-006375.en: Stuffing our bottles in our jacket pockets, we closed in behind him.
college-writing-006375.zh: 把我们的瓶子塞进我们的夹克口袋里，我们在他身后关了起来。

college-writing-006376.en: Suddenly, the old man whipped out a homemade wooden club from under his jacket and began swinging.
college-writing-006376.zh: 突然，老人从夹克下抽出一根自制的木棍，开始摆动。

college-writing-006377.en: The club thudded loudly against Victor’s shoulder, making him yelp with pain.
college-writing-006377.zh: 俱乐部在维克多的肩膀上大声敲击，让他痛苦地叫喊。

college-writing-006378.en: When we heard that, we went crazy.
college-writing-006378.zh: 当我们听到这个消息时，我们疯了。

college-writing-006379.en: We smashed our bottles over the old man’s head.
college-writing-006379.zh: 我们把瓶子砸在老人的头上。

college-writing-006380.en: Not content with that, Victor kicked him savagely, knocking him to the ground.
college-writing-006380.zh: 维克多不满足于此，将他猛烈地踢倒，将他击倒在地。

college-writing-006381.en: As we ran, I kept seeing him sprawled on the ground, blood from our beating trickling into his eyes.
college-writing-006381.zh: 当我们奔跑时，我一直看到他趴在地上，我们跳动的血迹流入他的眼睛。

college-writing-006382.en: Victor, the biggest of us, had said, “We want your money, old man. Hand it over.”
college-writing-006382.zh: 维克多是我们最大的人，曾说过：“我们想要你的钱，老人。把它交出来。”

college-writing-006383.en: Later, at home, I had a strong reaction to the incident.
college-writing-006383.zh: 后来，在家里，我对这件事有了强烈的反应。

college-writing-006384.en: My head would not stop pounding, and I threw up.
college-writing-006384.zh: 我的头不停地怦怦直跳，我吐了。

college-writing-006385.en: I wasn’t afraid of getting caught; in fact, we never did get caught.
college-writing-006385.zh: 我不怕被抓住； 事实上，我们从来没有被抓到。

college-writing-006386.en: I just knew I had gone over some kind of line.
college-writing-006386.zh: 我只知道我已经越过了某种线。

college-writing-006387.en: I didn’t know if I could step back, now that I had gone so far.
college-writing-006387.zh: 我不知道我是否可以退后一步，现在我已经走了这么远。

college-writing-006388.en: But I knew I had to.
college-writing-006388.zh: 但我知道我必须这样做。

college-writing-006389.en: I had seen plenty of people in my neighborhood turn into the kind of people who hated their lives, people who didn’t care about anything, people who wound up penned in jail or ruled by drugs.
college-writing-006389.zh: 我见过很多人都变成了讨厌自己生活的人，什么都不在乎的人，被关进监狱或被毒品统治的人。

college-writing-006390.en: I didn’t want to become one of them.
college-writing-006390.zh: 我不想成为他们中的一员。

college-writing-006391.en: That night, I realize now, I decided not to become one of Hitler’s “brutal youths.”
college-writing-006391.zh: 那天晚上，我意识到，我决定不成为希特勒的“残酷青年”之一。

college-writing-006392.en: I’m proud of myself for that, even though life didn’t get any easier and no one came along to pin a medal on me. I just decided, quietly, to step off the path I was on.
college-writing-006392.zh: 我为自己感到自豪，尽管生活并没有变得更轻松，也没有人来给我钉一枚奖牌。 我只是决定，悄悄地离开我所走的路。

college-writing-006393.en: I hope my parents and I will get along better now, too.
college-writing-006393.zh: 我希望我的父母和我现在也能相处得更好。

college-writing-006394.en: Maybe the old man’s pain, in some terrible way, had a purpose.
college-writing-006394.zh: 也许老人的痛苦，以某种可怕的方式，有一个目的。
