college-writing-006426.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Narration
college-writing-006426.zh: 开发一篇强调叙事的论文

college-writing-006427.en: Considering Purpose and Audience The main purpose of an essay that emphasizes narration is to make a point by incorporating one central story or several brief stories as support.
college-writing-006427.zh: 考虑到目的和读者，一篇强调叙述的文章的主要目的是通过结合一个中心故事或几个简短的故事作为支持来说明一点。

college-writing-006428.en: Colorful details and interesting events that build up to a point of some kind make narrative essays enjoyable for readers and writers alike.
college-writing-006428.zh: 丰富多彩的细节和有趣的事件在某种程度上形成了某种程度，使叙事文章对读者和作家都变得愉快。

college-writing-006429.en: At one time or another, you have probably listened to someone tell a rambling story that didn’t seem to go anywhere.
college-writing-006429.zh: 有一次，你可能听过有人讲述了一个似乎没有去任何地方的漫无边际的故事。

college-writing-006430.en: You might have impatiently wondered, “Where is this story going?” or “Is there a point here?”
college-writing-006430.zh: 你可能会不耐烦地想：“这个故事去哪儿了？” 或“这里有什么意义吗？”

college-writing-006431.en: Keep such questions in mind as you think about your own essay.
college-writing-006431.zh: 当你想到自己的论文时，请记住这些问题。

college-writing-006432.en: To satisfy your audience, your story must have some overall purpose and point.
college-writing-006432.zh: 为了满足你的观众，你的故事必须有一些整体的目的和要点。

college-writing-006433.en: Also keep in mind that your essay should deal with an event or a topic that will appeal to your audience.
college-writing-006433.zh: 还要记住，您的文章应该处理吸引观众的事件或主题。

college-writing-006434.en: A group of young children, for example, would probably be bored by an essay about your first job interview.
college-writing-006434.zh: 例如，一群年幼的孩子可能会对一篇关于你第一次工作面试的文章感到厌烦。

college-writing-006435.en: They might, however, be very interested if you wrote about a time you were chased by a pack of wild dogs or when you stood up to a bully in your school.
college-writing-006435.zh: 但是，如果您写下您被一群野狗追赶的时间，或者当您站出来对抗学校的恶霸时，他们可能会非常感兴趣。

college-writing-006436.en: In general, essays that emphasize narration involve human conflict─internal or external─and are entertaining to readers of all ages.
college-writing-006436.zh: 一般来说，强调叙述的文章涉及人类冲突——内部或外部——对所有年龄段的读者都很有趣。

college-writing-006437.en: Using Dialogue In Chapter 8, you learned that including people in an essay about a place is important to communicating something about its character or atmosphere.
college-writing-006437.zh: 使用第 8 章中的对话，您了解到在一篇关于一个地方的文章中包含人对于传达有关其性格或氛围的内容很重要。

college-writing-006438.en: Of course, people are essential to narration as are what they do and what they say.
college-writing-006438.zh: 当然，人们对叙述至关重要，因为他们的所作所为和他们所说的是必不可少的。

college-writing-006439.en: You can convey much about a person through the dialogue they have with others or even through the interior conversations they have while thinking silently.
college-writing-006439.zh: 你可以通过与他人的对话，甚至通过他们默默思考的内部对话来传达很多关于一个人的信息。

college-writing-006440.en: But dialogue can also be used to move the plot or action of the story along, to tell what happened before the story began, and to reveal other important facts that will make the story clearer, more suspenseful, or more meaningful.
college-writing-006440.zh: 但对话也可以用来推动故事的情节或动作，讲述故事开始前发生的事情，并揭示将使故事更清晰、更悬疑或更有意义的其他重要事实。

college-writing-006441.en: For example, in “A Night of Violence” Victor’s brutal tendencies become clear when he says, “We want your money, old man. Hand it over.”
college-writing-006441.zh: 例如，在“暴力之夜”中，维克多的残酷倾向变得清晰，他说：“我们想要你的钱，老人。把它交出来。”

college-writing-006442.en: You will also encounter dialogue in Nicholas Gage’s essay “The Teacher Who Changed My Life,” which appears later in this chapter.
college-writing-006442.zh: 您还将在本章后面出现的 Nicholas Gage 的文章“改变我的生活的老师”中遇到对话。

college-writing-006443.en: Here the narrator uses dialogue to acquaint readers with the nature of the main character, Miss Hurd, whose opening line is “What are all you goof-offs doing here?”
college-writing-006443.zh: 在这里，叙述者使用对话让读者了解主角小姐赫德小姐的本性，他的开场白是“你们在这里做什么？”

college-writing-006446.en: Use dialogue especially in the narrative essays you write, but remember to observe a few simple rules:
college-writing-006446.zh: 在你写的叙事文章中使用对话，尤其是在你写的叙述性文章中，但请记住遵守一些简单的规则：

college-writing-006447.en: 1. Place quotation marks around the words, and start a new paragraph when a new character begins speaking.
college-writing-006447.zh: 1. 在单词周围加引号，并在新角色开始说话时开始新段落。

college-writing-006448.en: For this reason, it is easy to tell that there are two different speakers in the following exchange between Lou, the owner of the restaurant in “Lou’s Place” (see Chapter 8), and one of his customers.
college-writing-006448.zh: 出于这个原因，很容易看出以下两个不同的演讲者在“娄的地方”餐厅的老板卢（见第 8 章）和他的一位顾客之间的交流中。

college-writing-006449.en: “You wanna I put this food in your ashtray, or are you gonna move it?”
college-writing-006449.zh: “你想我把这些食物放在你的烟灰缸里，还是你要搬家？”

college-writing-006451.en: The woman moves the ashtray aside.
college-writing-006451.zh: 女人把烟灰缸移到一边。

college-writing-006453.en: “I’m not really yelling at you, dear,” he answers.
college-writing-006453.zh: “我不是真的在对你大喊大叫，亲爱的，”他回答。

college-writing-006455.zh: “我很高兴你今天早上在这里。”

college-writing-006457.en: “That girl you’ve got working here sometimes, Lou—she doesn’t like me.”
college-writing-006457.zh: “你有时在这里工作的那个女孩，娄——她不喜欢我。”

college-writing-006458.en: 2. Record people’s words exactly as they speak them, complete with slang and errors in grammar and punctuation.
college-writing-006458.zh: 2. 准确地记录人们所说的话，包括语法和标点符号上的俚语和错误。

college-writing-006459.en: Notice that, in the dialogue quoted above, Lou says “wanna” rather than “want” and “gonna” rather than “going to.”
college-writing-006459.zh: 请注意，在上面引用的对话中，娄说的是“想要”而不是“想要”和“会”而不是“去”。

college-writing-006460.en: This is not the kind of writing expected in a college essay, but it is completely appropriate when you are recording dialogue.
college-writing-006460.zh: 这不是大学论文中预期的那种写作，但当你录制对话时，它是完全合适的。

college-writing-006461.en: Remember that you are trying to capture the words─the very sounds─that characters uttered just as they said them.
college-writing-006461.zh: 请记住，您正在尝试捕捉单词——这些声音——角色在他们所说的时候说出的声音。

college-writing-006462.en: 3. Make sure your reader knows who is speaking at any given time.
college-writing-006462.zh: 3. 确保您的读者在任何特定时间都知道谁在说话。

college-writing-006463.en: In the “Lou’s Place” passage quoted above, Johnson uses tag lines like “she said” or “says the woman” to explain to the reader that the woman is the speaker.
college-writing-006463.zh: 在上面引用的“Lou's Place”段落中，约翰逊使用诸如“她说”或“说女人”之类的标签来向读者解释这个女人是说话者。

college-writing-006464.en: Later, when we read “he answers,” we know it’s Lou who is talking.
college-writing-006464.zh: 后来，当我们读到“他回答”时，我们知道是卢在说话。

college-writing-006465.en: One way to make sure that readers can identify the speaker is to use tag lines like “she said,” “Lou replied,” or “the man yelled.”
college-writing-006465.zh: 确保读者能够识别说话者的一种方法是使用“她说”、“娄回答”或“那个人大喊大叫”之类的标语。

college-writing-006466.en: 4. Set off tag lines from quotations with commas, as in paragraph 22 of “Lou’s Place”: “Not a thing,” drawls Dan.
college-writing-006466.zh: 4. 用逗号从引号中引出标记行，如“Lou's Place”的第 22 段：“不是什么”，Dan 拖长。

college-writing-006467.en: However, if a tag line is used in the middle of a quotation that is composed of two distinct sentences, place a comma before and a period after it, as in paragraph 33 of “Lou’s Place”: “Thank you,” says the woman.
college-writing-006467.zh: 但是，如果在由两个不同句子组成的引文的中间使用标语，请在“Lou's Place”的第 33 段中放置一个逗号之前和一个句号：“谢谢，”这位女士说。

college-writing-006469.en: In the previous example and text explanation, commas and periods appear within quotation marks, but colons appear outside of them.
college-writing-006469.zh: 在前面的示例和文本解释中，逗号和句点出现在引号内，但冒号出现在它们之外。

college-writing-006470.en: (Semicolons follow the same rule as colons and appear outside quotation marks.)
college-writing-006470.zh: （分号遵循与冒号相同的规则并出现在引号之外。）

college-writing-006471.en: Finally, if the quotation is a question, end it with a question mark without the comma, as in paragraph 35 of “Lou’s Place”: “What? What is this?” he demands.
college-writing-006471.zh: 最后，如果引用是一个问题，用一个没有逗号的问号结束它，如“Lou's Place”的第 35 段：“什么？这是什么？” 他要求。

college-writing-006472.zh: 第236章 论文发展模式

college-writing-006473.en: Lisa, the writer of “Taking on a Disability,” spent a half hour freewriting before she wrote the first draft of her essay.
college-writing-006473.zh: 丽莎是“承担残疾人”的作者，花了半个小时的自由写作，然后才写出论文的初稿。

college-writing-006474.en: Here is what she came up with:

college-writing-006475.en: Development through Prewriting Freewriting is a particularly helpful prewriting technique as you’re planning your essay.
college-writing-006475.zh: 通过预写自由写作的发展是一种特别有用的预写技巧，因为您正在计划您的论文。

college-writing-006476.en: As you think about the story you want to relate, many ideas will crowd into your mind.
college-writing-006476.zh: 当你想想你想要讲述的故事时，很多想法都会涌入你的脑海。

college-writing-006477.en: Simply writing them down in free-form style will jog loose details you may have forgotten and also help you determine what the central point of your story really is.
college-writing-006477.zh: 简单地以自由形式将它们写下来，您可能已经忘记了松散的细节，还可以帮助您确定故事的中心点是什么。

college-writing-006478.en: Our church was planning a building renovation to make the church more accessible to

college-writing-006480.en: Some people thought it was a waste of money and that those with

college-writing-006544.en: First Draft Taking on a Disability

college-writing-006545.en: The pastor at our church suggested that we each “take on a disability” for a few hours on Sunday morning.
college-writing-006545.zh: 我们教会的牧师建议我们每个人在周日早上“承担残疾”几个小时。

college-writing-006546.en: Some members, like me, chose to use wheelchairs.
college-writing-006546.zh: 一些成员，像我一样，选择使用轮椅。

college-writing-006547.en: Others wore earplugs, used crutches, or wore blindfolds.
college-writing-006547.zh: 其他人戴耳塞、用过拐杖或戴眼罩。

college-writing-006548.en: It surprised me that I felt nervous about sitting down in my wheelchair.
college-writing-006548.zh: 令我惊讶的是，我对坐在轮椅上感到紧张。

college-writing-006549.en: I’m not sure why I felt scared about it.
college-writing-006549.zh: 我不知道为什么我对此感到害怕。

college-writing-006550.en: I guess I realized that most people who use wheelchairs don’t do it by choice—they have to.
college-writing-006550.zh: 我想我意识到大多数使用轮椅的人不是选择做的——他们必须这样做。

college-writing-006552.zh: 238 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006553.en: When I sat down, I thought my friend Paula would push me around.
college-writing-006553.zh: 当我坐下时，我以为我的朋友宝拉会推我。

college-writing-006554.en: We had talked about her doing that earlier.
college-writing-006554.zh: 我们之前谈过她这样做。

college-writing-006555.en: But she decided instead to experience what it is like to have blindness by using a blindfold.
college-writing-006555.zh: 但她决定通过使用眼罩来体验失明的感觉。

college-writing-006556.en: I saw her with a blindfold on, trying to fix herself a cup of coffee and knocking it off the table as she stirred it.
college-writing-006556.zh: 我看到她戴着眼罩，试图给自己洗一杯咖啡，然后在她搅拌的时候把它从桌子上敲下来。

college-writing-006557.en: So I had to figure out how to make the chair move by myself.
college-writing-006557.zh: 所以我必须弄清楚如何让椅子自己移动。

college-writing-006559.en: Pushing the wheels made my hands and arms sore.
college-writing-006559.zh: 推轮子让我的手和手臂酸痛。

college-writing-006560.en: I also kept bumping into things.

college-writing-006561.zh: 这出乎意料地具有挑战性。

college-writing-006562.en: I even had trouble locking the wheels and finding the footrest.
college-writing-006562.zh: 我什至无法锁定车轮并找到脚踏板。

college-writing-006563.en: I couldn’t see well as I sat down low in my chair.
college-writing-006563.zh: 当我坐在椅子上的时候，我看不清楚。

college-writing-006564.en: When the rest of the congregation stood up, I could forget about seeing entirely.
college-writing-006564.zh: 当会众的其他人站起来时，我可能会忘记完全看到。

college-writing-006565.en: People would nod or chuckle at something that had happened up at the front of the church and I could only guess what was going on.
college-writing-006565.zh: 人们会对教堂前面发生的事情点头或轻笑，我只能猜测发生了什么。

college-writing-006566.en: Instead of sitting in the pew with everyone else, I was in the aisle, which was really too narrow for the chair.
college-writing-006566.zh: 我没有和其他人一起坐在长椅上，而是在过道上，椅子真的太窄了。

college-writing-006567.en: The new building program our church is planning will make that problem better by widening the aisles and making the pews farther apart.
college-writing-006567.zh: 我们的教会正在计划的新建筑计划将通过拓宽过道并使长椅距离更远，从而使这个问题变得更好。

college-writing-006568.en: It’s going to be expensive, but it’s a worthwhile thing.
college-writing-006568.zh: 这会很昂贵，但这是一件值得的事情。

college-writing-006569.en: Another thing I disliked was how I felt when people talked to me.
college-writing-006569.zh: 我不喜欢的另一件事是人们与我交谈时的感受。

college-writing-006570.en: They had to lean down as though I was a kid, and I had to stare up at them as though I was too.
college-writing-006570.zh: 他们不得不像我还是个孩子一样俯下身子，我不得不盯着他们看，好像我也是。

college-writing-006571.en: One person I talked to who seemed to understand what I was experiencing was Don Henderson, who mentioned that his brother-in-law uses a wheelchair.
college-writing-006571.zh: 与我交谈过的一个似乎了解我正在经历的人是唐·亨德森，他提到他的姐夫使用轮椅。

college-writing-006596.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-006596.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-006597.en: The Teacher Who Changed My Life

college-writing-006599.en: The person who set the course of my life in the new land I entered as a young war refugee─who, in fact, nearly dragged me onto the path that would bring all the blessings I’ve received in America─was a salty-tongued, no-nonsense schoolteacher named Marjorie Hurd.
college-writing-006599.zh: 我作为一个年轻的战争难民进入的新土地上的人生轨迹——事实上，他几乎把我拖到了能带来我在美国得到的所有祝福的道路上…… 学校教师名叫玛乔丽·赫德。

college-writing-006600.en: When I entered her classroom in 1953, I had been to six schools in five years, starting in the Greek village where I was born in 1939.
college-writing-006600.zh: 1953年我进入她的教室时，我在五年内上过六所学校，从1939年出生的希腊村开始。

college-writing-006601.en: When I stepped off a ship in New York Harbor on a gray March day in 1949, I was an undersized 9-year-old in short pants who had lost his mother and was coming to live with the father he didn’t know.
college-writing-006601.zh: 1949 年，当我在纽约港的一个灰色游行日下车时，我是一个身材矮小的 9 岁长裤，失去了母亲，即将与他不认识的父亲一起生活。

college-writing-006602.en: My mother, Eleni Gatzoyiannis, had been imprisoned, tortured and shot by Communist guerrillas for sending me and three of my four sisters to freedom.
college-writing-006602.zh: 我的母亲 Eleni Gatzoyiannis 因将我和我的四个姐妹中的三个送给自由而被共产党游击队监禁、折磨和枪杀。

college-writing-006603.en: She died so that her children could go to their father in the United States.
college-writing-006603.zh: 她死了，以便她的孩子可以去美国的父亲那里。

college-writing-006604.en: The portly, bald, well-dressed man who met me and my sisters seemed a foreign, authoritarian figure.
college-writing-006604.zh: 遇见我和我的姐妹们的肥胖、秃顶、衣冠楚楚的男人似乎是一个外国的、专制的人物。

college-writing-006605.en: I secretly resented him for not getting the whole family out of Greece early enough to save my mother.
college-writing-006605.zh: 我暗暗怨恨他没有早点把全家人赶出希腊来拯救我的母亲。

college-writing-006606.en: Ultimately, I would grow to love him and appreciate how he dealt with becoming a single parent at the age of 56, but at first our relationship was prickly, full of hostility.
college-writing-006606.zh: 最终，我会爱上他，并欣赏他在 56 岁时成为单亲父母的方式，但起初我们的关系是多刺的，充满敌意。

college-writing-006607.en: As Father drove us to our new home─a tenement in Worcester, Mass.
college-writing-006607.zh: 当父亲开车送我们到我们的新家——马萨诸塞州伍斯特的一个物业。

college-writing-006608.en: ─and pointed out the huge brick building that would be our first school in America, I clutched my Greek notebooks from the refugee camp, hoping that my few years of schooling would impress my teachers in this cold, crowded country.
college-writing-006608.zh: ——指出那座巨大的砖砌建筑将成为我们在美国的第一所学校，我从难民营中抓起我的希腊笔记本，希望我几年的学校教育能给我的老师留下深刻的印象。

college-writing-006610.en: When my father led me and my 11-year-old sister to Greendale Elementary School, the grim-faced Yankee principal put the two of us in a class for the mentally retarded.
college-writing-006610.zh: 当我父亲带领我和我 11 岁的妹妹上格林代尔小学时，这位面无表情的洋基校长把我们两个人送上了智障人士的课堂。

college-writing-006611.en: There was no facility in those days for non-English-speaking children.
college-writing-006611.zh: 那时没有为非英语儿童提供便利。

college-writing-006612.en: By the time I met Marjorie Hurd four years later, I had learned English, been placed in a normal, graded class and had even been chosen for the college preparatory track in the Worcester public school system.
college-writing-006612.zh: 四年后，当我遇到 Marjorie Hurd 时，我已经学习了英语，被安排在一个普通的、评分的班级中，甚至被选为伍斯特公立学校系统的大学预备课程。

college-writing-006613.en: I was 13 years old when our father moved us yet again, and I entered Chandler Junior High shortly after
college-writing-006613.zh: 当我们父亲再次感动我们时，我 13 岁，不久我就进入了钱德勒初中

college-writing-006614.zh: 240 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006616.en: I found myself surrounded by richer, smarter and better-dressed classmates, who looked askance at my strange clothes and heavy accent.
college-writing-006616.zh: 我发现自己被更富有、更聪明、穿着得体的同学所包围，他们对我奇怪的衣服和沉重的口音不屑一顾。

college-writing-006617.en: Shortly after I arrived, we were told to select a hobby to pursue during “club hour” on Fridays.
college-writing-006617.zh: 在我到达后不久，我们被告知在星期五的“俱乐部时间”中选择一个爱好来追求。

college-writing-006618.en: The idea of hobbies and clubs made no sense to my immigrant ears, but I decided to follow the prettiest girl in my class─the blue-eyed daughter of the local Lutheran minister.
college-writing-006618.zh: 爱好和俱乐部的想法对我的移民耳朵毫无意义，但我决定跟随班上最漂亮的女孩——当地路德教部长的蓝眼睛女儿。

college-writing-006619.en: She led me through the door marked “Newspaper Club” and into the presence of Miss Hurd, the newspaper adviser and English teacher who would become my mentor and my muse.
college-writing-006619.zh: 她带我穿过标有“报纸俱乐部”的门，进入了赫德小姐，报纸顾问和英语老师，她将成为我的导师和缪斯女神。

college-writing-006620.en: A formidable, solidly built woman with salt-and-pepper hair, a steely eye and a flat Boston accent, Miss Hurd had no patience with layabouts.
college-writing-006620.zh: 赫德小姐对外行人没有耐心，他是一个强大、坚固的女人，有着盐和胡椒的头发、钢铁般的眼睛和平坦的波士顿口音。

college-writing-006621.en: “What are all you goof-offs doing here?” she bellowed at the would-be journalists.
college-writing-006621.zh: “你们这些傻瓜在这里做什么？” 她冲着未来的记者吼道。

college-writing-006622.en: “This is the Newspaper Club! We’re going to put out a newspaper. So if there’s anybody in this room who doesn’t like work, I suggest you go across to the Glee Club now, because you’re going to work your tails off here!”
college-writing-006622.zh: “这是报社！我们要出报纸。所以如果这个房间里有人不喜欢工作，我建议你现在去Glee Club，因为你要在这里努力工作！”

college-writing-006623.en: I was soon under Miss Hurd’s spell.
college-writing-006623.zh: 我很快就被赫德小姐的魔咒所吸引。

college-writing-006624.en: She did indeed teach us to put out a newspaper, skills I honed during my next 25 years as a journalist.
college-writing-006624.zh: 她确实教我们出版一份报纸，这是我在接下来的 25 年里磨练的技能。

college-writing-006625.en: Soon I asked the principal to transfer me to her English class as well.
college-writing-006625.zh: 很快我就要求校长也把我也转移到她的英语课上。

college-writing-006626.en: There, she drilled us on grammar until I finally began to understand the logic and structure of the English language.
college-writing-006626.zh: 在那里，她让我们学习语法，直到我终于开始理解英语的逻辑和结构。

college-writing-006627.en: She assigned stories for us to read and discuss; not tales of heroes, like the Greek myths I knew, but stories of underdogs─poor people, even immigrants, who seemed ordinary until a crisis drove them to do something extraordinary.
college-writing-006627.zh: 她为我们分配了故事供我们阅读和讨论； 不是英雄的故事，比如我所知道的希腊神话，而是失败者的故事——穷人，甚至是移民，他们看起来很普通，直到危机驱使他们做一些非凡的事情。

college-writing-006628.en: She also introduced us to the literary wealth of Greece─giving me a new perspective on my war-ravaged, impoverished homeland.
college-writing-006628.zh: 她还向我们介绍了希腊的文学财富——让我对我饱受战争蹂躏的贫困祖国有了新的认识。

college-writing-006629.en: I began to be proud of my origins.
college-writing-006629.zh: 我开始为自己的起源感到自豪。

college-writing-006630.en: One day, after discussing how writers should write about what they know, she assigned us to compose an essay from our own experience.
college-writing-006630.zh: 有一天，在讨论了作家应该如何写下他们所知道的东西后，她指派我们根据自己的经验撰写一篇文章。

college-writing-006631.en: Fixing me with a stern look, she added, “Nick, I want you to write about what happened to your family in Greece.”
college-writing-006631.zh: 她用严厉的眼神修正我，“尼克，我想让你写下你在希腊的家人发生的事情。”

college-writing-006632.en: I had been trying to put those painful memories behind me and left the assignment until the last moment.
college-writing-006632.zh: 我一直试图把那些痛苦的回忆抛在脑后，直到最后一刻才把任务抛在脑后。

college-writing-006633.en: Then, on a warm spring afternoon, I sat in my room with a yellow pad and pencil and stared out the window at the buds on the trees.
college-writing-006633.zh: 然后，在一个温暖的春天下午，我拿着一个黄色的垫子和铅笔坐在我的房间里，盯着窗外的树上的花蕾。

college-writing-006634.en: I wrote that the coming of spring always reminded me of the last time I said goodbye to my mother on a green and gold day in 1948.
college-writing-006634.zh: 我写道，春天的到来总是让我想起1948年我在绿色和金色的日子里和母亲说再见的时候。

college-writing-006635.en: I kept writing, one line after another, telling how the Communist guerrillas occupied our village, took our home and food, how my mother started planning our escape when she learned that the children were to be sent to re-education camps behind the Iron Curtain and how, at the last moment, she couldn’t escape with us because the guerrillas sent her with a group of women to thresh wheat in a distant village.
college-writing-006635.zh: 我一直在写，一行一行，讲述共产党游击队如何占领我们的村庄，带走我们的家和食物，当我的母亲得知孩子们将被送到铁幕后面的再教育营地时，她如何开始计划我们的逃跑，以及她如何在最后一刻无法逃脱 我们是因为游击队派她和一群妇女去远处的村子里扔小麦。

college-writing-006636.en: She promised she would try to get away on her own, she told me to be brave and hung a silver cross around my neck, and then she kissed me. I watched the line of women being led down into the ravine and up the other side, until they disappeared around the bend─my mother a tiny brown figure at the end who stopped for an instant to raise her hand in one last farewell.
college-writing-006636.zh: 她答应她会努力自己逃脱，她告诉我要勇敢，在我的脖子上挂一个银色的十字架，然后她吻了我。 我看着女人被带到峡谷和另一边的线，直到她们消失在拐弯处——我的母亲最后是一个棕色的小身材，她停了片刻，在最后一次告别中举起了手。

college-writing-006638.en: I wrote about our nighttime escape down the mountain, across the minefields and into the lines of the Nationalist soldiers, who sent us to a refugee camp.
college-writing-006638.zh: 我写了关于我们夜间逃离山峰、穿过雷区和民族主义士兵的队伍，他们把我们送到了一个难民营。

college-writing-006639.en: It was there that we learned of our mother’s execution.
college-writing-006639.zh: 在那里，我们得知了我们母亲的处决。

college-writing-006640.en: I felt very lucky to have come to America, I concluded, but every year, the coming of spring made me feel sad because it reminded me of the last time I saw my mother.
college-writing-006640.zh: 我总结说，我很幸运能来到美国，但每年春天的到来让我感到难过，因为它让我想起了我最后一次见到我妈妈。

college-writing-006641.en: I handed in the essay, hoping never to see it again, but Miss Hurd had it published in the school paper.
college-writing-006641.zh: 我交了论文，希望再也见不到它，但赫德小姐把它发表在学校报纸上。

college-writing-006642.en: This mortified me at first, until I saw that my classmates reacted with sympathy and tact to my family’s story.
college-writing-006642.zh: 起初这让我感到羞愧，直到我看到我的同学们对我家人的故事有同情和机智的反应。

college-writing-006643.en: Without telling me, Miss Hurd also submitted the essay to a contest sponsored by the Freedoms Foundation at Valley Forge, Pa., and it won a medal.
college-writing-006643.zh: 在没有告诉我的情况下，赫德小姐还将这篇文章提交给了宾夕法尼亚州福吉自由基金会赞助的一场比赛，并获得了奖牌。

college-writing-006644.en: The Worcester paper wrote about the award and quoted my essay at length.
college-writing-006644.zh: 伍斯特的论文写了关于这个奖项，并详细引用了我的论文。

college-writing-006645.en: My father, by then a “five-anddime-store chef,” as the paper described him, was ecstatic with pride, and the Worcester Greek community celebrated the honor to one of its own.
college-writing-006645.zh: 正如报纸所描述的那样，我的父亲当时是一位“五角钱店厨师”，自豪地欣喜若狂，伍斯特希腊社区为自己的一个人庆祝了这一荣誉。

college-writing-006646.en: For the first time I began to understand the power of the written word.
college-writing-006646.zh: 我第一次开始理解文字的力量。

college-writing-006647.en: A secret ambition took root in me.
college-writing-006647.zh: 一个秘密的野心在我身上扎根。

college-writing-006648.en: One day, I vowed, I would go back to Greece, find out the details of my mother’s death and write about her life, so her grandchildren would know of her courage.
college-writing-006648.zh: 有一天，我发誓，我会回到希腊，了解我母亲去世的细节，写下她的生活，这样她的孙子们就会知道她的勇气。

college-writing-006649.en: Perhaps I would even track down the men who killed her and write of their crimes.
college-writing-006649.zh: 也许我什至会追查杀了她的人并写下他们的罪行。

college-writing-006650.en: Fulfilling that ambition would take me 30 years.
college-writing-006650.zh: 实现这个野心需要我 30 年。

college-writing-006651.en: Meanwhile, I followed the literary path that Miss Hurd had so forcefully set me on.
college-writing-006651.zh: 与此同时，我走上了赫德小姐如此有力地引领我的文学道路。

college-writing-006652.en: After junior high, I became the editor of my school paper at Classical High School and got a part-time job at the Worcester Telegram and Gazette.
college-writing-006652.zh: 初中后，我成为古典高中学校报纸的编辑，并在伍斯特电报和公报获得了一份兼职工作。

college-writing-006653.en: Although my father could only give me $50 and encouragement toward a college education, I managed to finance four years at Boston University with scholarships and part-time jobs in journalism.
college-writing-006653.zh: 虽然我父亲只能给我 50 美元和鼓励我去大学教育，但我设法在波士顿大学资助了四年的奖学金和兼职工作。

college-writing-006654.en: During my last year of college, an article I wrote about a friend who had died in the Philippines─the first person to lose his life working for the Peace Corps─led to my winning the Hearst Award for College Journalism.
college-writing-006654.zh: 在我大学的最后一年，我写的一篇关于在菲律宾去世的朋友的文章——第一个为和平队工作的人失去了生命——导致我获得了赫斯特大学新闻奖。

college-writing-006655.en: And the plaque was given to me in the White House by President John F. Kennedy.
college-writing-006655.zh: 白宫是约翰·肯尼迪总统给我的牌匾。

college-writing-006656.en: For a refugee who had never seen a motorized vehicle or indoor plumbing until he was 9, this was an unimaginable honor.
college-writing-006656.zh: 对于一个直到 9 岁之前从未见过机动车辆或室内管道的难民来说，这是一种难以想象的荣誉。

college-writing-006657.en: When the Worcester paper ran a picture of me standing next to President Kennedy, my father rushed out to buy a new suit in order to be properly dressed to receive the congratulations of the Worcester Greeks.
college-writing-006657.zh: 当伍斯特报纸上一张我站在肯尼迪总统旁边的照片时，我父亲冲出去买了一套新西装，以便穿着得体，以接受伍斯特希腊人的祝贺。

college-writing-006658.en: He clipped out the photograph, had it laminated in plastic and carried it in his breast pocket for the rest of his life to show everyone he met.
college-writing-006658.zh: 他剪下照片，用塑料层压，并在他的胸前口袋里放在他的胸前口袋里，以展示他遇到的每个人。

college-writing-006659.en: I found the much-worn photo in his pocket on the day he died 20 years later.
college-writing-006659.zh: 20 年后他去世的那天，我在他的口袋里找到了这张陈旧的照片。

college-writing-006660.en: In our isolated Greek village, my mother had bribed a cousin to teach her to read, for girls were not supposed to attend school beyond a certain age.
college-writing-006660.zh: 在我们孤立的希腊村庄，我母亲贿赂了一个表弟教她阅读，因为女孩不应该超过一定年龄上学。

college-writing-006661.en: She had always dreamed of her children receiving an education.
college-writing-006661.zh: 她一直梦想着她的孩子接受教育。

college-writing-006662.en: She couldn’t be there when I graduated from Boston University, but the person who came with my father and shared our joy was my former teacher, Marjorie Hurd.
college-writing-006662.zh: 当我从波士顿大学毕业时，她不能在那里，但和我父亲一起来并分享我们快乐的人是我的前任老师 Marjorie Hurd。

college-writing-006663.en: We celebrated not only my bachelor’s degree but also the scholarships that paid my way to
college-writing-006663.zh: 我们不仅庆祝了我的学士学位，还庆祝了我的奖学金

college-writing-006664.zh: 第242章 论文发展模式

college-writing-006665.zh: 哥伦比亚大学新闻研究生院。

college-writing-006666.en: There, I met the woman who would eventually become my wife.
college-writing-006666.zh: 在那里，我遇到了最终成为我妻子的女人。

college-writing-006667.en: At our wedding and at the baptisms of our three children, Marjorie Hurd was always there, dancing alongside the Greeks.
college-writing-006667.zh: 在我们的婚礼和我们三个孩子的洗礼上，Marjorie Hurd 总是在那里，与希腊人一起跳舞。

college-writing-006668.en: By then, she was Mrs. Rabidou, for she had married a widower when she was in her early 40s.
college-writing-006668.zh: 到那时，她是拉比杜夫人，因为她在 40 岁出头时已经娶了一个鳏夫。

college-writing-006669.en: That didn’t distract her from her vocation of introducing young minds to English literature, however.
college-writing-006669.zh: 然而，这并没有分散她将年轻思想引入英国文学的职业。

college-writing-006670.en: She taught for a total of 41 years and continually would make a “project” of some balky student in whom she spied a spark of potential.
college-writing-006670.zh: 她总共教了 41 年，并且会不断地为某个笨拙的学生做一个“项目”，她在其中发现了潜力的火花。

college-writing-006671.en: Often these were students from the most troubled homes, yet she would alternately bully and charm each one with her own special brand of tough love until the spark caught fire.
college-writing-006671.zh: 这些通常是来自最麻烦家庭的学生，但她会交替欺负和用她自己特殊的严厉爱人魅力，直到火花着火。

college-writing-006672.en: She retired in 1981 at the age of 62 but still avidly follows the lives and careers of former students while overseeing her adult stepchildren and driving her husband on camping trips to New Hampshire.
college-writing-006672.zh: 她于 1981 年退休，享年 62 岁，但仍然热心地追随前学生的生活和职业生涯，同时监督她的成年继子女，并驾驶她的丈夫前往新罕布什尔州露营。

college-writing-006673.en: Miss Hurd was one of the first to call me on Dec. 10, 1987, when President Reagan, in his television address after the summit meeting with Gorbachev, told the nation that Eleni Gatzoyiannis’s dying cry, “My children!” had helped inspire him to seek an arms agreement “for all the children of the world.”
college-writing-006673.zh: 赫德小姐是1987年12月10日第一个给我打电话的人之一，里根总统在与戈尔巴乔夫的首脑会议后的电视讲话中告诉国家，埃莱尼·加佐伊安尼斯的《我的孩子们！》 曾帮助激励他“为全世界的孩子”寻求武器协议。

college-writing-006674.en: “I can’t imagine a better monument for your mother,” Miss Hurd said with an uncharacteristic catch in her voice.
college-writing-006674.zh: “我无法想象你的母亲会有更好的纪念碑，”赫德小姐的声音中带着一丝不寻常的声音说道。

college-writing-006675.en: Although a bad hip makes it impossible for her to join in the Greek dancing, Marjorie Hurd Rabidou is still an honored and enthusiastic guest at all our family celebrations, including my 50th birthday picnic last summer, where the shish kebab was cooked on spits, clarinets and bouzoukis wailed, and costumed dancers led the guests in a serpentine line around our Colonial farmhouse, only 20 minutes from my first home in Worcester.
college-writing-006675.zh: 虽然臀部不好让她无法参加希腊舞蹈，但 Marjorie Hurd Rabidou 仍然是我们所有家庭庆祝活动的一位荣幸和热情的客人，包括我去年夏天的 50 岁生日野餐，烤肉串在烤肉上煮熟， 单簧管和 bouzoukis 哭了起来，穿着盛装的舞者在我们殖民地农舍周围的蛇形线路上带领客人，距离我在伍斯特的第一个家仅 20 分钟路程。

college-writing-006676.en: My sisters and I felt an aching void because my father was not there to lead the line, balancing a glass of wine on his head while he danced, the way he did at every celebration during his 92 years.
college-writing-006676.zh: 我和我的姐妹们感到疼痛的空虚，因为我父亲不在那儿来领导这条线，在他跳舞的时候在他的头上平衡一杯酒，就像他在 92 年的每一次庆祝活动中所做的那样。

college-writing-006677.en: But Miss Hurd was there, surveying the scene with quiet satisfaction.
college-writing-006677.zh: 但赫德小姐在那里，安静地满意地审视着现场。

college-writing-006678.en: Although my parents are gone, her presence was a consolation, because I owe her so much.
college-writing-006678.zh: 虽然我的父母不在了，但她的存在是一种安慰，因为我欠她太多。

college-writing-006679.en: This is truly the land of opportunity, and I would have enjoyed its bounty even if I hadn’t walked into Miss Hurd’s classroom in 1953.
college-writing-006679.zh: 这真的是机会之地，即使我在 1953 年没有走进赫德小姐的教室，我也会很享受它的恩惠。

college-writing-006680.en: But she was the one who directed my grief and pain into writing, and if it weren’t for her, I wouldn’t have become an investigative reporter and foreign correspondent, recorded the story of my mother’s life and death in Eleni and now my father’s story in A Place for Us, which is also a testament to the country that took us in.
college-writing-006680.zh: 但她是把我的悲伤和痛苦引导到写作中的人，如果不是她，我不会成为一名调查记者和外国记者，在埃莱尼记录了我母亲的生与死的故事，现在我父亲的故事在我们的一个地方，这 也证明了把我们带进来的国家。

college-writing-006681.en: She was the catalyst that sent me into journalism and indirectly caused all the good things that came after.
college-writing-006681.zh: 她是让我进入新闻业的催化剂，并间接导致了所有之后的美好事物。

college-writing-006682.en: But Miss Hurd would probably deny this emphatically.
college-writing-006682.zh: 但赫德小姐可能会强调否认这一点。

college-writing-006683.en: A few years ago, I answered the telephone and heard my former teacher’s voice telling me, in that won’t-take-no-for-an-answer tone of hers, that she had decided I was to write and deliver the eulogy at her funeral.
college-writing-006683.zh: 几年前，我接了电话，听到我以前的老师的声音告诉我，她的语气不会接受她的回答，她决定我要在她的葬礼上写下悼词并发表悼词。

college-writing-006684.en: I agreed (she didn’t leave me any choice), but that’s one assignment I never want to do.
college-writing-006684.zh: 我同意（她没有给我留下任何选择），但这是我永远不想做的一项任务。

college-writing-006685.en: I hope, Miss Hurd, that you’ll accept this remembrance instead.
college-writing-006685.zh: 我希望，赫德小姐，你会接受这场纪念。

college-writing-006693.zh: 3. 第 12 段的 主题句 是什么？

college-writing-006695.zh: 4. 列出 Gage 用来描述赫德小姐的几个细节。

college-writing-006696.en: 5. We can infer that the author saw Miss Hurd as a demanding but caring
college-writing-006696.zh: 5. 我们可以推断作者认为赫德小姐是一个要求很高但很关心的人

college-writing-006699.zh: 6. Gage 在第 5 段中所说的“我的导师和我的缪斯”是什么意思？

college-writing-006701.en: a. supports why Ms. Hurd is important to Nicholas Gage.
college-writing-006701.zh: 一。 支持为什么赫德女士对尼古拉斯·盖奇很重要。

college-writing-006702.en: b. explains why Nicholas and his family left his mother behind.
college-writing-006702.zh: B. 解释了为什么尼古拉斯和他的家人把他的母亲抛在了后面。

college-writing-006703.en: c. answers the question about why Nicholas and family were refugees.
college-writing-006703.zh: c.  回答了为什么尼古拉斯和家人是难民的问题。

college-writing-006704.en: d. defends why Nicholas didn’t want to write about his experiences.
college-writing-006704.zh: D. 为为什么尼古拉斯不想写他的经历而辩护。

college-writing-006706.zh: 8. 因为这个故事讲述了赫德小姐影响的年表，盖奇使用

college-writing-006707.en: transitions to signal the passing of time.
college-writing-006707.zh: 过渡到标志着时间的流逝。

college-writing-006716.zh: 写一篇强调叙事的论文

college-writing-006717.en: Think of an experience in your life that supports one of the statements below:
college-writing-006717.zh: 想想你生活中支持以下陈述之一的经历：

college-writing-006718.en: If you never have a dream, you’ll never have a dream come true.
college-writing-006718.zh: 如果你从来没有梦想，你就永远不会梦想成真。

college-writing-006719.en: ─popular saying Before I got married I had six theories about bringing up children; now I have six children and no theories.
college-writing-006719.zh: ─我结婚前流行的说法有六个关于抚养孩子的理论； 现在我有六个孩子，没有理论。

college-writing-006720.en: ─John Wilmot, Earl of Rochester There are some things you learn best in calm, and some in storm.
college-writing-006720.zh: ——约翰·威尔莫特，罗切斯特伯爵 有些事情是你在平静中学得最好的，有些是在风暴中学到的。

college-writing-006721.en: ─Willa Cather Success is 99 percent perspiration and 1 percent inspiration.
college-writing-006721.zh: ─Willa Cather 的成功率为 99% 的汗水和 1% 的灵感。

college-writing-006722.en: ─Thomas Edison Be the change that you wish to see in the world.
college-writing-006722.zh: ─Thomas Edison 是您希望在世界上看到的变化。

college-writing-006723.en: ─Mahatma Gandhi There’s a sucker born every minute.
college-writing-006723.zh: ─圣雄甘地 每分钟都有一个吸盘出生。

college-writing-006725.en: T. Barnum We lie loudest when we lie to ourselves.
college-writing-006725.zh: T. Barnum 当我们对自己撒谎时，我们撒谎的声音最大。

college-writing-006726.en: ─Eric Hoffer You will face many defeats in life, but never let yourself be defeated.
college-writing-006726.zh: ──埃里克·霍弗你会在生活中面临许多失败，但永远不要让自己被打败。

college-writing-006727.en: ─Maya Angelou Hoping and praying are easier but do not produce as good results as hard work.
college-writing-006727.zh: ─玛雅·安杰洛希望和祈祷更容易，但不会产生像努力工作那样好的结果。

college-writing-006728.en: ─Andy Rooney A little learning is a dangerous thing.
college-writing-006728.zh: ──安迪·鲁尼 一点学习是一件危险的事情。

college-writing-006729.en: ─Alexander Pope Nothing is as good as it seems beforehand.
college-writing-006729.zh: ──亚历山大教皇 没有什么比以前看起来那么好了。

college-writing-006730.en: ─George Eliot Life shrinks or expands in proportion to one’s courage.
college-writing-006730.zh: ——乔治·艾略特的生命随着一个人的勇气而缩小或扩大。

college-writing-006731.en: ─Ana ̈ıs Nin When I got to the end of my long journey in life / I realized I was the architect of my own destiny.
college-writing-006731.zh: ─ ana ̈ıs nin 当我走到了漫长的人生旅程的尽头时/我意识到我是我自己命运的建筑师。

college-writing-006732.en: ─Amado Nervo A fool and his money are soon parted.
college-writing-006732.zh: ─Amado nervo 一个傻瓜和他的钱很快就分开了。

college-writing-006736.en: From what we get, we can make a living; what we give, however, makes a life.
college-writing-006736.zh: 从我们得到的，我们可以谋生； 然而，我们给予的东西造就了生活。

college-writing-006737.en: ─Arthur Ashe The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
college-writing-006737.zh: ─亚瑟·阿什 活着的最大荣耀不在于永不堕落，而是在我们每次跌倒时升起。

college-writing-006738.en: ─Nelson Mandela Fear not those who argue but those who dodge.
college-writing-006738.zh: ─纳尔逊·曼德拉 不惧怕那些争吵的人，而是那些躲避的人。

college-writing-006739.en: ─Marie von Ebner-Eschenback Trust in Allah, but tie your camel.
college-writing-006739.zh: ─Marie von Ebner-Eschenback 对真主的信任，但系上你的骆驼。

college-writing-006741.en: Use one of the above statements or another noteworthy saying─perhaps one that has been a guidepost for your life─to write a thesis statement for an essay with emphasis on narration about that experience.
college-writing-006741.zh: 使用上述陈述之一或另一句值得注意的说法——也许是您生活的指南——为一篇强调叙述的文章写一篇 中心论点句 的文章。

college-writing-006742.en: As you develop and write the essay, refer to the suggestions in the following prewriting strategies and rewriting strategies.
college-writing-006742.zh: 在您开发和撰写论文时，请参阅以下预写策略和重写策略中的建议。

college-writing-006743.en: You may also want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” to help create a strong narrative with strong support.
college-writing-006743.zh: 您可能还想回顾第 8 章“描述”，以帮助创建具有强有力支持的强有力的叙述。

college-writing-006744.en: PREWRITING The key to the success of your essay will be your choice of an incident from your life that illustrates the truth of the statement you have chosen.
college-writing-006744.zh: 预写论文成功的关键将是您选择生活中的事件，以说明您选择的陈述的真实性。

college-writing-006745.en: Here are some guidelines to consider as you choose such an incident:
college-writing-006745.zh: 以下是您在选择此类事件时需要考虑的一些准则：

college-writing-006746.en: • The incident should include a conflict, or a source of tension.
college-writing-006746.zh: • 事件应包括冲突或紧张的根源。

college-writing-006747.en: That conflict does not need to be dramatic, such as a fistfight between two characters.
college-writing-006747.zh: 这种冲突不需要是戏剧性的，例如两个角色之间的斗殴。

college-writing-006748.en: Equally effective is a quieter conflict, such as a conflict between a person’s conscience and desires, or a decision that must be made, or a difficult situation that has no clear resolution.
college-writing-006748.zh: 同样有效的是更安静的冲突，例如一个人的良心和欲望之间的冲突，或者必须做出的决定，或者没有明确解决的困难情况。

college-writing-006749.en: • The incident should be limited in time.

college-writing-006750.en: It would be difficult to do justice in such a brief essay to an experience that continued over several weeks or months.
college-writing-006750.zh: 在这样一篇简短的文章中，很难为持续数周或数月的经历伸张正义。

college-writing-006751.en: • The incident should evoke a definite emotional response in you so that it might draw a similar response from your reader.
college-writing-006751.zh: • 该事件应该唤起您明确的情绪反应，以便它可以引起读者的类似反应。

college-writing-006752.en: • The incident must fully support the statement you have chosen, not merely be linked by some of the same ideas.
college-writing-006752.zh: • 事件必须完全支持您选择的声明，而不仅仅是被一些相同的想法联系起来。

college-writing-006753.en: Do not, for example, take the statement “We lie loudest when we lie to ourselves” and then write about an incident in which someone just told a lie.
college-writing-006753.zh: 例如，不要以“当我们对自己撒谎时最响亮的声音”的说法，然后写下某人刚刚撒谎的事件。

college-writing-006754.en: The essay should demonstrate the cost of being untruthful to oneself.
college-writing-006754.zh: 论文应该证明对自己不诚实的代价。

college-writing-006755.en: Here is how one student tested whether her plan for her narrative essay was a good one:
college-writing-006755.zh: 以下是一位学生如何测试她的叙事论文计划是否是一个好的：

college-writing-006756.en: • What statement have I chosen as my thesis?
college-writing-006756.zh: • 我选择了什么陈述作为我的论文？

college-writing-006757.en: The chains of habit are too weak to be felt until they are too strong to be broken.
college-writing-006757.zh: 习惯的锁链太弱了，直到它们太强而无法破碎。

college-writing-006759.zh: 第246章 论文发展模式

college-writing-006760.en: • Does the incident I have chosen include some kind of tension?
college-writing-006760.zh: • 我选择的事件是否包括某种紧张？

college-writing-006762.en: I am going to write about the day I tried to purchase an expensive new shirt but was told that I had maxed out my credit card.
college-writing-006762.zh: 我要写下我试图购买一件昂贵的新衬衫的那天，但被告知我已经用完了我的信用卡。

college-writing-006763.en: When I tried a second card and then a third, I was told that they too had reached their balance limits.
college-writing-006763.zh: 当我尝试第二张牌和第三张牌时，我被告知它们也达到了余额极限。

college-writing-006765.en: That day I realized something about myself─I get the urge to buy things whenever I am lonely, depressed, or just bored.
college-writing-006765.zh: 那天我意识到了自己的一些事情——我有一种在我孤独、沮丧或无聊的时候就有买东西的冲动。

college-writing-006766.en: I also learned that in order to battle that urge, I would have to change my values, my outlook on life.
college-writing-006766.zh: 我还了解到，为了与这种冲动作斗争，我必须改变我的价值观，我的人生观。

college-writing-006767.en: I would have to learn that happiness does not result simply from having nice things.
college-writing-006767.zh: 我必须了解到，幸福并不是仅仅因为拥有美好的事物而产生的。

college-writing-006768.en: • Is the incident limited in time?

college-writing-006770.en: I am going to write about events that happened in one day.
college-writing-006770.zh: 我将写下一天发生的事件。

college-writing-006771.en: • Does the incident evoke an emotional response in me?
college-writing-006771.zh: • 事件是否引起了我的情绪反应？

college-writing-006773.en: I was embarrassed and ashamed of myself.
college-writing-006773.zh: 我为自己感到尴尬和羞愧。

college-writing-006774.en: • Does the incident support the statement I have chosen?
college-writing-006774.zh: • 事件是否支持我选择的声明？

college-writing-006776.en: I was a “shopaholic,” but I did not realize that I was caught in the “chains” of this habit until I was embarrassed into making major changes in my outlook on life.
college-writing-006776.zh: 我是一个“购物狂”，但直到我尴尬地改变了我的人生观，我才意识到我陷入了这种习惯的“链条”。

college-writing-006777.en: REVISING After you have put your essay away for a day, read it to a friend or classmate who will give you honest feedback.
college-writing-006777.zh: 在你把论文收起来一天后修改，读给朋友或同学，他们会给你诚实的反馈。

college-writing-006778.en: You and your reader should consider the questions in the checklist that appears at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-006778.zh: 您和您的读者应考虑本章末尾出现的清单中的问题。

college-writing-006779.en: Continue revising your work until you and your reader can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-006779.zh: 继续修改您的作品，直到您和您的读者可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-006780.en: Write an essay in which you research a historical figure and come to a conclusion about that figure.
college-writing-006780.zh: 写一篇文章，你研究一个历史人物并得出关于这个数字的结论。

college-writing-006781.en: The person you choose may be assigned by your instructor, or may be of your own choosing and require your instructor’s approval.
college-writing-006781.zh: 您选择的人可能由您的讲师分配，也可能是您自己选择的，需要您的教师的批准。

college-writing-006782.en: Options could include Malcolm X, Eva Peron, Vice-President Charles Curtis, or Queen Victoria.
college-writing-006782.zh: 选项可能包括 Malcolm X、Eva Peron、副总统查尔斯·柯蒂斯或维多利亚女王。

college-writing-006783.en: You may want to check Chapter 16, “Argument,” and Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay.”
college-writing-006783.zh: 您可能想查看第 16 章“论点”和第 20 章“撰写研究论文”。

college-writing-006789.en: After choosing your topic, you will want to research as much information as
college-writing-006789.zh: 选择您的主题后，您将希望研究尽可能多的信息

college-writing-006791.en: Not only should you develop a biographical understanding of your subject, but you will also want to learn about some of the more controversial ideas or actions that this figure was known for.
college-writing-006791.zh: 您不仅应该对您的主题进行传记理解，而且您还想了解这个数字众所周知的一些更具争议的想法或行为。

college-writing-006793.en: After researching, you should come to some sort of conclusion about this
college-writing-006793.zh: 经过研究，你应该对这个问题得出某种结论

college-writing-006796.en: Was he really as good as people thought?
college-writing-006796.zh: 他真的和人们想象的一样好吗？

college-writing-006797.en: Did they do underhanded things to get their way?
college-writing-006797.zh: 他们是否做了一些卑鄙的事情来实现自己的道路？

college-writing-006798.zh: 这个人真的是无私的吗？

college-writing-006799.en: Your conclusion should become the basis for your thesis statement.
college-writing-006799.zh: 你的结论应该成为你的 中心论点句 的基础。

college-writing-006801.en: You will then want to create an outline that organizes the story of your sub-
college-writing-006801.zh: 然后，您将想要创建一个大纲来组织您的子故事

college-writing-006802.en: ject’s life in a manner that supports your thesis.
college-writing-006802.zh: 以支持您的论文的方式，Ject 的生活。

college-writing-006804.en: Using your outline as a guide, prepare a rough draft of your paper.
college-writing-006804.zh: 以您的大纲为指导，准备好论文的草稿。

college-writing-006805.en: REVISING Once you have a first draft of your essay completed, use the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter to help you with your revision process.
college-writing-006805.zh: 修订完成论文的初稿后，使用本章末尾的四个基础清单来帮助您完成修订过程。

college-writing-006806.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-006806.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-006807.en: In this essay, you will write with a specific purpose and for a specific audience.
college-writing-006807.zh: 在这篇文章中，您将为特定目的和特定受众写作。

college-writing-006808.en: The use of narration goes beyond the classroom: people share stories online, in print, on TV, and on the radio.
college-writing-006808.zh: 叙述的使用超越了课堂：人们在网上、印刷版、电视和广播中分享故事。

college-writing-006809.en: For stories to get noticed, however, they need to have a purpose.
college-writing-006809.zh: 然而，要让故事被注意到，它们需要有一个目的。

college-writing-006810.en: For instance, when the Black Lives Matter (#BlackLivesMatter) movement began, it was accompanied by many stories that illustrated why the movement was personal to different people.
college-writing-006810.zh: 例如，当 Black Lives Matter (#BlackLivesMatter) 运动开始时，它伴随着许多故事，说明了为什么该运动对不同的人是个人的。

college-writing-006811.en: For this assignment, you are to write an essay that creates a campaign, complete with a hashtag or logo, to improve something in your community.
college-writing-006811.zh: 对于这项作业，您要撰写一篇文章，创建一个带有主题标签或徽标的活动，以改进您的社区中的某些内容。

college-writing-006812.en: First, you will want to find out what issues are affecting your community, like teen suicide, homeless veterans, or decaying parks.
college-writing-006812.zh: 首先，您需要了解哪些问题正在影响您的社区，例如青少年自杀、无家可归的退伍军人或腐烂的公园。

college-writing-006813.en: After you have decided on your topic, you will need to explain what the problem is and why it is important, what your campaign will be like, and what you hope to accomplish with your campaign.
college-writing-006813.zh: 在你决定了你的主题之后，你需要解释问题是什么以及为什么它很重要，你的活动会是什么样子，以及你希望通过你的活动完成什么。

college-writing-006814.en: You may want to review Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” and Chapter 12, “Cause and/or Effect.”
college-writing-006814.zh: 您可能要复习第 10 章“例证”和第 12 章“原因和/或影响”。

college-writing-006816.zh: 248 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-006819.en: Have I included a thesis statement that clearly identifies a single experience or story that I am going to recount?
college-writing-006819.zh: 我是否包含了一个 中心论点句，它清楚地确定了我要讲述的一个经历或故事？

college-writing-006820.en: Does each paragraph, and each sentence within that paragraph, help either to keep the action moving or to reveal important things about the characters?
college-writing-006820.zh: 该段落中的每个段落和每个句子是否有助于保持动作的移动或揭示有关字符的重要内容？

college-writing-006821.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-006821.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-006823.en: Have I included enough vivid exact details, including dialogue, that will help my readers experience the event as it actually happened?
college-writing-006823.zh: 我是否包含了足够生动的确切细节，包括对话，这将帮助我的读者体验实际发生的事件？

college-writing-006824.en: Does my conclusion clearly tie up the story and explain why it is significant?
college-writing-006824.zh: 我的结论是否清楚地结合了故事并解释了为什么它很重要？

college-writing-006825.en: Have I introduced any major characters within the essay?
college-writing-006825.zh: 我在文章中介绍了任何主要人物吗？

college-writing-006827.en: Do transitional words and phrases, and linking sentences between paragraphs, help make the sequence of events clear?
college-writing-006827.zh: 过渡词和短语，以及在段落之间链接句子，是否有助于使事件序列清晰？

college-writing-006828.en: Should I break up the essay by using bits of interesting dialogue instead of narration?
college-writing-006828.zh: 我应该用一些有趣的对话而不是叙述来分解文章吗？

college-writing-006830.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-006830.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-006831.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-006831.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-006832.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-006832.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-006834.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-006834.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-006839.en: Reprinted by permission of the author.

college-writing-006840.en: In what ways did the murder of George Floyd bring people in the United States together?
college-writing-006840.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德的谋杀案以何种方式将美国的人们聚集在一起？

college-writing-006841.en: In what ways have we become a more divided nation?
college-writing-006841.zh: 我们在哪些方面成为一个更加分裂的国家？

college-writing-006842.en: Use examples found in the media, in this photograph, or in your own daily observations to support your point.
college-writing-006842.zh: 使用媒体、照片中或您自己的日常观察中的示例来支持您的观点。

college-writing-006843.zh: 米歇尔·德奥特维奥/阿拉米 库存照片

college-writing-006845.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on exemplification • write an essay with emphasis on exemplification • revise an essay with emphasis on exemplification
college-writing-006845.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写一篇强调范例的论文 • 撰写一篇强调示例的文章 • 修改一篇强调例证的论文

college-writing-006846.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize exemplification • one professional model essay that emphasizes exemplification
college-writing-006846.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调例证的学生论文 • 一篇强调示例的专业模型论文

college-writing-006847.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-006848.en: In our daily conversations, we often provide examples─details, particulars, and specific instances─to explain statements that we make.
college-writing-006848.zh: 在我们的日常对话中，我们经常提供例子——细节、细节和具体实例——来解释我们所做的陈述。

college-writing-006849.en: Here are several statements and supporting examples:
college-writing-006849.zh: 以下是几个陈述和支持示例：

college-writing-006850.en: Statement Examples The first day of school was frustrating.
college-writing-006850.zh: 陈述例子 开学的第一天令人沮丧。

college-writing-006851.zh: 我的社会学课程被取消了。

college-writing-006852.en: Then, I couldn’t find the biology lab.
college-writing-006852.zh: 然后，我找不到生物实验室。

college-writing-006853.en: And the lines at the bookstore were so long that I went home without buying my textbooks.
college-writing-006853.zh: 书店的排队太长了，我没有买教科书就回家了。

college-writing-006854.en: fyi ees 4 f pom Eo = oF, eritash j

college-writing-006859.en: The water temperature can’t be predicted; it stops in midcycle; and it sometimes shreds my clothing.
college-writing-006859.zh: 无法预测水温； 它在周期中期停止； 它有时会撕碎我的衣服。

college-writing-006860.en: My brother is a thrifty person.
college-writing-006860.zh: 我的兄弟是一个节俭的人。

college-writing-006861.en: He washes and reuses aluminum foil.
college-writing-006861.zh: 他清洗和重复使用铝箔。

college-writing-006862.zh: 他把礼物包装在报纸上。

college-writing-006863.en: And he’s worn the same Sunday suit for twenty years.
college-writing-006863.zh: 他穿着同一件周日西装已经二十年了。

college-writing-006864.en: In each case, exemplification helps us see for ourselves the truth of the statement that has been made.
college-writing-006864.zh: 在每种情况下，例证都可以帮助我们亲眼看到所作陈述的真实性。

college-writing-006865.en: In essays, too, explanatory examples help your audience fully understand your point.
college-writing-006865.zh: 在论文中，解释性示例也可以帮助您的听众完全理解您的观点。

college-writing-006866.en: Lively, specific examples also add interest to your paper.
college-writing-006866.zh: 生动的、具体的例子也增加了你的论文的兴趣。

college-writing-006867.en: In this chapter, you will be asked to emphasize exemplification to support your thesis.
college-writing-006867.zh: 在本章中，您将被要求强调例证以支持您的论文。

college-writing-006868.en: Read the student literary analysis essay, the second student essay, and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-006868.zh: 阅读学生文学分析论文、第二篇学生论文，以及随之而来的模型论文，并通过论文随附的问题进行研究。

college-writing-006991.zh: 大多数美国人并非酗酒者。

college-writing-006992.en: Most do not cruise city streets looking to score cocaine or heroin.
college-writing-006992.zh: 大多数人不会在城市街道上寻找可卡因或海洛因。

college-writing-006993.en: Relatively few try to con their doctors into prescribing unneeded mood-altering medications.
college-writing-006993.zh: 相对较少的人试图欺骗医生，要求他们开不必要的调节情绪的药物。

college-writing-006994.en: And yet, many Americans are traveling through life with their minds slightly out of kilter.
college-writing-006994.zh: 然而，许多美国人一生中都处于精神稍显不平稳的状态。

college-writing-006995.en: In its attempt to cope with modern life, the human mind seems to have evolved some defense strategies.
college-writing-006995.zh: 为了应对现代生活，人类大脑似乎演化出了一些防御策略。

college-writing-006996.en: Confronted with inventions like television, the shopping center, and the Internet, the mind will slip—all by itself—into an altered state.
college-writing-006996.zh: 面对电视、购物中心和互联网这类发明，人的思维会自然而然地陷入一种改变的状态。

college-writing-006997.en: Never in the history of humanity have people been expected to sit passively for hours, staring at moving pictures emanating from an electronic box.
college-writing-006997.zh: 在人类的历史上，从未有人期望人们被动地坐着好几个小时，盯着电子盒子发出的动态照片。

college-writing-006998.en: Since too much exposure to flickering images of police officers, detectives, and talk-show hosts can be dangerous to human sanity, the mind automatically goes into a state of TV hypnosis.
college-writing-006998.zh: 由于过多地接触警察、侦探和脱口秀主持人的闪烁图像可能会对人类的理智造成危险，因此大脑会自动进入电视催眠状态。

college-writing-006999.en: The eyes see the sitcom or the dog-food commercial, but the mind goes into a holding pattern.
college-writing-006999.zh: 眼睛看到情景喜剧或狗粮广告，但头脑进入了一种保持模式。

college-writing-007000.en: None of the televised images or sounds actually enter the brain.
college-writing-007000.zh: 没有一个电视转播的图像或声音真正进入大脑。

college-writing-007001.en: This is why, when questioned, people cannot remember commercials they have seen five seconds before or why the TV cops are chasing a certain suspect.
college-writing-007001.zh: 这就是为什么当被问到时，人们无法记住他们在五秒钟前看过的广告，或者电视警察追捕某个嫌疑人的原因。

college-writing-007002.en: In this hypnotic, trancelike state, the mind resembles an armored armadillo.
college-writing-007002.zh: 在这种催眠、恍惚的状态下，心灵就像一个装甲的犰狳。

college-writing-007003.en: It rolls up in self-defense, letting the stream of televised information pass by harmlessly.
college-writing-007003.zh: 它在自卫中卷起，让电视信息流无害地经过。

college-writing-007004.en: If the TV watcher arises from the couch and goes to a shopping mall, they will again cope by slipping into an altered state.
college-writing-007004.zh: 如果电视观众从沙发上站起来去购物中心，他们将再次陷入改变的状态。

college-writing-007005.en: In the mall, the mind is bombarded with the sights, smells, and sounds of dozens of stores, restaurants, and movie theaters competing for its attention.
college-writing-007005.zh: 在商场里，心灵被数十家商店、餐馆和电影院的景象、气味和声音轰炸，争夺它的注意力。

college-writing-007006.en: There are hundreds of questions to be answered.
college-writing-007006.zh: 有数百个问题需要回答。

college-writing-007007.en: Should I start with the upper or lower mall level?
college-writing-007007.zh: 我应该从商场的上层还是下层开始？

college-writing-007008.en: Which stores should I look in?

college-writing-007009.en: Should I bother with the sweater sale at J. Crew?
college-writing-007009.zh: 我应该为 J. Crew 的毛衣销售烦恼吗？

college-writing-007010.en: Should I eat fried chicken or try the healthier sounding Pita Wrap?
college-writing-007010.zh: 我应该吃炸鸡还是尝试更健康的皮塔卷？

college-writing-007012.en: To combat this mental overload, the mind goes into a state resembling the whiteout experienced by mountain climbers trapped in a blinding snowstorm.
college-writing-007012.zh: 为了对抗这种精神上的超负荷，头脑进入了一种类似于被困在令人眼花缭乱的暴风雪中的登山者所经历的白化的状态。

college-writing-007013.zh: 突然间，一切看起来都一样。

college-writing-007014.en: The shopper is unsure where to go next and cannot remember what they came for in the first place.
college-writing-007014.zh: 购物者不确定下一步去哪里，不记得他们一开始是为了什么。

college-writing-007015.en: The mind enters this state deliberately so that the shopper has no choice but to leave.
college-writing-007015.zh: 头脑故意进入这个状态，让购物者别无选择，只能离开。

college-writing-007016.en: Some kids can be in a shopping mall for hours, but they are exceptions to the rule.
college-writing-007016.zh: 有些孩子可以在购物中心呆上几个小时，但他们是规则的例外。

college-writing-007017.en: However, no part of everyday life so quickly triggers the mind’s protective shutdown mode as that favorite pastime of the new millennium: Internet surfing.
college-writing-007017.zh: 然而，日常生活中没有哪一部分能像新千年最喜欢的消遣一样触发心灵的保护性关机模式：互联网冲浪。

college-writing-007018.en: A computer user sits down with the intention of briefly checking e-mail or looking up a fact for a research paper.
college-writing-007018.zh: 计算机用户坐下来的目的是简短地检查电子邮件或查找研究论文的事实。

college-writing-007019.en: But once tapped into the immense storehouse of information, entertainment, and seemingly intimate personal connections that the Internet offers, the user loses all sense of time and priorities.
college-writing-007019.zh: 但是，一旦进入互联网提供的巨大信息、娱乐和看似亲密的个人联系的仓库，用户就会失去所有的时间感和优先级。

college-writing-007020.en: Prospects flood the mind: Should I explore the rise of Nazi Germany?
college-writing-007020.zh: 前景泛滥：我应该探索纳粹德国的崛起吗？

college-writing-007022.en: Hear the life story of a lonely stranger in Duluth?
college-writing-007022.zh: 听到德卢斯一个孤独的陌生人的生活故事吗？

college-writing-007023.en: With a mind dazed with information overload, the user numbly hits one key after another, leaping from topic to topic, from
college-writing-007023.zh: 脑袋被信息过载所困扰，用户麻木地按下一个键，从一个主题跳到另一个话题，从

college-writing-007027.en: Hours fly by as the user sits hunched over the keyboard, unable to account for the time that has passed.
college-writing-007027.zh: 当用户蹲在键盘上时，数小时飞逝而过，无法解释经过的时间。

college-writing-007028.en: These poor victims are merely trying to cope with the mind-numbing inventions of modern life and are not responsible for their glazed eyes and robotic motions.
college-writing-007028.zh: 这些可怜的受害者只是试图应对现代生活中令人麻木的发明，而不是对他们的眼睛和机器人动作负责。

college-writing-007029.en: People need to be aware of them and treat them with kindness and understanding.
college-writing-007029.zh: 人们需要意识到它们并以善良和理解对待它们。

college-writing-007030.en: Going out of the way to bring these coma sufferers back to real life is the job of all those who have managed to avoid the side effects of television, shopping, and the Internet; otherwise, humanity will suffer.
college-writing-007030.zh: 让这些昏迷患者回到现实生活中，是所有设法避免电视、购物和互联网的副作用的人的工作； 否则，人性就会受苦。

college-writing-007067.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Exemplification Considering Purpose and Audience Use Various Types of Examples
college-writing-007067.zh: 开发一篇强调体现目的和受众的论文，使用各种类型的例子

college-writing-007068.en: All examples act as concrete representations of the abstract idea you are trying to communicate, but there are several kinds you can choose from depending on your purpose and audience.
college-writing-007068.zh: 所有示例都充当您尝试交流的抽象概念的具体表示，但您可以根据您的目的和受众选择几种类型。

college-writing-007069.en: Varying the types of examples will help make your writing interesting.
college-writing-007069.zh: 改变示例类型将有助于使您的写作变得有趣。

college-writing-007070.en: Readers would certainly become bored if you simply listed the different kinds of sports or other extracurricular activities your college offers in an attempt to prove that there are many good ways to spend your time.
college-writing-007070.zh: 如果您只是简单地列出您的大学提供的不同类型的运动或其他课外活动，以证明有许多好方法可以消磨时间，读者肯定会感到无聊。

college-writing-007071.en: So, you might also include a couple of anecdotes (brief stories) about the interesting club trips you have been on in the past year or the fascinating people you met while planning a language-club fundraiser last semester.
college-writing-007071.zh: 因此，您可能还可以包括一些轶事（简短的故事），讲述您在过去一年的有趣俱乐部旅行或您在上学期计划语言俱乐部筹款活动时遇到的迷人的人。

college-writing-007073.en: Mention People, Places, Actions, and Things
college-writing-007073.zh: 提及人、地点、行动和事物

college-writing-007074.en: Some effective examples refer to people, places, actions, and things that readers recognize or can relate to.
college-writing-007074.zh: 一些有效的例子指的是读者认识或可以与之相关的人、地点、行动和事物。

college-writing-007075.en: If you wanted to prove that your town is making a strong effort to improve the environment, you might mention actions like the building of the new sewer treatment plant, the reduction in bus fares to encourage the use of public transportation, or the funding of an empty-lot cleanup project.
college-writing-007075.zh: 如果您想证明您的城镇正在努力改善环境，您可能会提到建造新的下水道处理厂、减少公共交通的巴士票价，或为空地清理项目提供资金等行动。

college-writing-007076.en: If you were trying to prove that modern computers owe their existence to women, you might want to focus on the contributions of Grace Hopper.
college-writing-007076.zh: 如果您试图证明现代计算机的存在归功于女性，您可能希望专注于 Grace Hopper 的贡献。

college-writing-007078.en: You could use facts if you wanted to explain that ancient Athens was not a democracy in the modern sense because poor people could not participate in government, women had no voice in the affairs of the city, and Athenians owned slaves.
college-writing-007078.zh: 如果你想解释古代雅典不是现代意义上的民主国家，你可以使用事实，因为穷人不能参与政府，妇女在城市事务中没有发言权，雅典人拥有奴隶。

college-writing-007079.en: You might discuss World War I, World War II, the Korean War, the Vietnam War, and the Persian Gulf War to prove that, in the twentieth century, Americans fought in many global conflicts.
college-writing-007079.zh: 您可能会讨论第一次世界大战、第二次世界大战、朝鲜战争、越南战争和波斯湾战争，以证明在 20 世纪，美国人在许多全球冲突中作战。

college-writing-007081.en: Anecdotes are brief, informative stories that can serve as examples.
college-writing-007081.zh: 轶事是简短的、内容丰富的故事，可以作为例子。

college-writing-007082.en: Although they are brief, they go beyond the mere mention of something and actually tell a genuine story that serves to make an abstract idea more understandable.
college-writing-007082.zh: 尽管它们很简短，但它们超越了对某事的提及，实际上讲述了一个真实的故事，使抽象的想法更容易理解。

college-writing-007083.en: There are several such stories in “Dad,” an essay that appears later in this chapter.
college-writing-007083.zh: “爸爸”中有几个这样的故事，一篇文章在本章后面出现。

college-writing-007085.en: Examples should always relate directly to the idea that they are being used to support.
college-writing-007085.zh: 示例应始终与它们被用于支持的想法直接相关。

college-writing-007086.en: Let’s say you are trying to prove that taking public transportation can sometimes be inconvenient.
college-writing-007086.zh: 假设您试图证明乘坐公共交通有时会很不方便。

college-writing-007087.en: Telling your readers that you often read on the bus while traveling to work won’t help you.
college-writing-007087.zh: 告诉您的读者您在上班时经常在公共汽车上阅读对您没有帮助。

college-writing-007088.en: In fact, being able to read while commuting is an advantage.
college-writing-007088.zh: 事实上，在通勤时能够阅读是一个优势。

college-writing-007089.en: Neither will it help to say that bus fares have risen lately.
college-writing-007089.zh: 说最近巴士票价上涨了，这也无济于事。

college-writing-007090.en: Remember that you are trying to explain the term “inconvenient,” not “expensive.”
college-writing-007090.zh: 请记住，您试图解释“不方便”一词，而不是“昂贵”。

college-writing-007091.en: A better example would be the fact that three days this week the bus was so crowded you had to stand up for the entire half-hour trip.
college-writing-007091.zh: 一个更好的例子是，这周的三天公共汽车太拥挤了，你不得不站起来进行整个半小时的行程。

college-writing-007092.en: Development through Prewriting When Cedric, the student author of “Altered States,” was considering a topic for his exemplification essay, he looked around his dorm for inspiration.
college-writing-007092.zh: 通过预写的发展 当“改变国家”的学生作者塞德里克正在为他的典范论文考虑一个主题时，他环顾了他的宿舍以寻找灵感。

college-writing-007093.en: He first considered writing about examples of some different types of people: athletes, musicians, math majors.
college-writing-007093.zh: 他首先考虑写一些不同类型的人的例子：运动员、音乐家、数学专业。

college-writing-007094.en: Then he thought about examples of housekeeping in dorm rooms: the Slob Kingdom, the Neat Freak Room, and the Packrat’s Place.
college-writing-007094.zh: 然后他想到了宿舍里的家政服务的例子：懒惰的王国、整洁的怪异房间和 Packrat 的地方。

college-writing-007095.zh: 第258章 论文发展模式

college-writing-007096.en: “But that evening I was noticing how my roommate acted as he was cruising the Internet,” Cedric said.
college-writing-007096.zh: “但那天晚上，我注意到我的室友在互联网巡游时的表现，”塞德里克说。

college-writing-007097.en: “He sat down to write his brother a brief e-mail, and three hours later he was still there, cruising from website to website. His eyes were glassy and he seemed out of touch with reality. It reminded me of how spaced out I get when I go to a busy shopping mall. I began to think about how our minds have to adjust to challenges that our grandparents didn’t grow up with. I added ‘watching television’ as the third category, and I had a pretty good idea what my essay would be about.”
college-writing-007097.zh: “他坐下来给他的兄弟写了一封简短的电子邮件，三个小时后他还在那里，从一个网站到另一个网站。 “我们的思想必须适应我们祖父母没有成长的挑战。

college-writing-007098.en: Cedric had his three categories, but he needed to do some more work to generate supporting details for each.
college-writing-007098.zh: Cedric 有他的三个类别，但他需要做更多的工作来为每个类别生成 支撑细节。

college-writing-007099.en: He used the technique of clustering, or diagramming, to help inspire his thinking.
college-writing-007099.zh: 他使用聚类或图表技术来帮助激发他的思维。

college-writing-007100.en: Here is what his diagram looked like:

college-writing-007103.en: Modern life makes demands on the human mind that no other period of history has made.
college-writing-007103.zh: 现代生活对人类的思想提出了其他历史时期的要求。

college-writing-007104.en: As society becomes more and more complex, the mind has developed some defense mechanisms.
college-writing-007104.zh: 随着社会变得越来越复杂，心灵已经形成了一些防御机制。

college-writing-007105.en: Confronted with inventions like the Internet, television, and the shopping center, the mind will slip—all by itself—into an altered state.
college-writing-007105.zh: 面对互联网、电视和购物中心等发明，思想会独自滑入一个改变的状态。

college-writing-007106.en: Surfing the Internet can quickly make the mind slip into a strange state.
college-writing-007106.zh: 上网冲浪可以很快使头脑滑入一种奇怪的状态。

college-writing-007107.en: A computer user sits down to check his e-mail or look up something.
college-writing-007107.zh: 计算机用户坐下来查看他的电子邮件或查找某些内容。

college-writing-007108.en: But once tapped into the Internet, the user loses all sense of time.
college-writing-007108.zh: 但是一旦进入互联网，用户就会失去所有的时间感。

college-writing-007109.en: He can chat with strangers, research any topic, play a game, or shop for any product.
college-writing-007109.zh: 他可以与陌生人聊天、研究任何主题、玩游戏或购买任何产品。

college-writing-007110.en: Some people begin to think of the online world and online friends as more real than the people in their own homes.
college-writing-007110.zh: 有些人开始认为在线世界和在线朋友比自己家中的人更真实。

college-writing-007111.en: While my roommate is absorbed in the Internet, he can even have brief conversations with people who come into our room, yet not be able to remember the conversations later.
college-writing-007111.zh: 当我的室友沉浸在互联网上时，他甚至可以与进入我们房间的人进行简短的交谈，但以后无法记住这些对话。

college-writing-007112.en: He sits there in a daze from information overload.
college-writing-007112.zh: 他因信息过载而发呆地坐在那里。

college-writing-007113.en: He seems numb as he hits key after key, going from website to website.
college-writing-007113.zh: 他似乎麻木了，因为他接着一个接一个地，从一个网站到另一个网站。

college-writing-007115.en: Growing up, our grandparents could not have imagined the idea of sitting passively for hours, staring at moving pictures emanating from a box.
college-writing-007115.zh: 长大后，我们的祖父母无法想象被动地坐了几个小时，盯着盒子发出的动态照片的想法。

college-writing-007116.en: It’s not a normal state of affairs, so the mind goes into something like a hypnotic trance.
college-writing-007116.zh: 这不是一种正常的状态，所以头脑会进入催眠状态之类的东西。

college-writing-007117.en: You see the sitcom or the dog-food commercial, but your mind goes into a holding pattern.
college-writing-007117.zh: 你会看到情景喜剧或狗粮广告，但你的思想进入了一种保持模式。

college-writing-007118.en: You don’t really absorb the pictures or sounds.
college-writing-007118.zh: 你并没有真正吸收图片或声音。

college-writing-007119.en: Five minutes after I watch a show I can’t remember commercials I’ve seen or why the TV cops are chasing a certain suspect.
college-writing-007119.zh: 在我看了一个节目五分钟后，我不记得我看过的广告或电视警察为什么追捕某个嫌疑人。

college-writing-007120.en: If the TV watcher arises from the couch and journeys into the real world, he often goes to the shopping center.
college-writing-007120.zh: 如果电视观众从沙发上站起来，进入现实世界，他经常去购物中心。

college-writing-007121.en: Here, the mind is bombarded with the sights, smells, and sounds of dozens of stores, restaurants, and movie theaters competing for its attention.
college-writing-007121.zh: 在这里，心中被数十家商店、餐馆和电影院争夺注意力的景象、气味和声音轰炸。

college-writing-007122.en: Dazed shoppers begin to feel like mountain climbers trapped in a blinding snowstorm.
college-writing-007122.zh: 目瞪口呆的购物者开始觉得像登山者被困在令人眼花缭乱的暴风雪中。

college-writing-007123.zh: 突然间，一切看起来都一样。

college-writing-007124.en: My father is the worst of all when it comes to shopping in an altered state.
college-writing-007124.zh: 在改变状态下购物时，我的父亲是最糟糕的。

college-writing-007125.en: He comes back from the mall looking like he’d been through a war.
college-writing-007125.zh: 他从商场回来，看起来像是经历了一场战争。

college-writing-007126.en: After about fifteen minutes of shopping, he can’t concentrate enough to know what he’s looking for.
college-writing-007126.zh: 经过大约 15 分钟的购物，他无法集中注意力，无法知道自己在寻找什么。

college-writing-007127.en: Internet surfers, TV viewers, and shoppers all have one thing in common.
college-writing-007127.zh: 互联网冲浪者、电视观众和购物者都有一件事。

college-writing-007128.en: They’re just trying to cope with the mind-numbing inventions of modern life.
college-writing-007128.zh: 他们只是想应对现代生活中令人麻木的发明。

college-writing-007129.en: I hope that someday we’ll turn away from such inventions and return to a simpler and more healthy way of life.
college-writing-007129.zh: 我希望有一天我们会远离这些发明，回到更简单、更健康的生活方式。

college-writing-007130.en: Looking at his diagram, Cedric saw that he would have no trouble supporting the thesis that people’s minds go into an “altered state” when they watch TV, go to shopping centers, or use the Internet.
college-writing-007130.zh: 看着他的图表，塞德里克发现他在看电视、去购物中心或使用互联网时，会毫不费力地支持人们的思想进入“改变状态”的论点。

college-writing-007131.en: As he quickly jotted down details in cluster form, he had easily come up with enough ideas for his essay.
college-writing-007131.zh: 当他迅速以集群形式记下细节时，他很容易为他的论文提出足够的想法。

college-writing-007132.en: He started writing and produced this first draft.
college-writing-007132.zh: 他开始写作并制作了这份初稿。
