college-writing-007590.en: Next, she decided to group her items into three steps: (1) getting organized, (2) sending the complaint to the president, and (3) following up with further action.
college-writing-007590.zh: 接下来，她决定将她的项目分为三个步骤：（1）组织起来，（2）将投诉发送给总统，以及（3）跟进进一步的行动。

college-writing-007592.en: With that preparation done, Meghan wrote her first draft.
college-writing-007592.zh: 完成这项准备后，梅根写下了她的初稿。

college-writing-007594.en: Because I find that a consumer has to watch out for herself and be ready to speak up if a product or service isn’t satisfactory, I have developed the following consumer’s guide to complaining effectively.
college-writing-007594.zh: 因为我发现消费者必须注意自己，并准备好在产品或服务不令人满意的情况下发声，我已经制定了以下消费者的有效抱怨指南。

college-writing-007595.en: The first step is getting organized.

college-writing-007596.en: I save all sales slips, original boxes, warranty cards, and appliance guarantees.
college-writing-007596.zh: 我保存所有销售单、原装盒、保修卡和电器保证。

college-writing-007597.en: This file does not prevent a product from falling apart the day after the guarantee runs out.
college-writing-007597.zh: 该文件不会阻止产品在保证用完后的第二天分崩离析。

college-writing-007598.en: One of the problems in our country is the shoddy workmanship that goes into many products.
college-writing-007598.zh: 我国的问题之一是许多产品的劣质做工。

college-writing-007599.en: That way I know the date of the purchase, the correct price, where the item was purchased, and an exact description of the product.
college-writing-007599.zh: 这样我就知道购买日期、正确的价格、购买商品的地点以及产品的确切描述。

college-writing-007600.en: The next step is to send the complaint to the person who will get results quickly.
college-writing-007600.zh: 下一步是将投诉发送给能够快速获得结果的人。

college-writing-007601.en: I call the company to find out the president’s name and then I write directly to that person.
college-writing-007601.zh: 我打电话给公司找出总统的名字，然后我直接写信给那个人。

college-writing-007602.en: For example, the head of AMF arranged to replace my son’s bike.
college-writing-007602.zh: 例如，AMF 的负责人安排更换我儿子的自行车。

college-writing-007603.en: Another time, the president of a Philadelphia department store finally had a twenty-dollar overcharge on my bill corrected.
college-writing-007603.zh: 还有一次，费城一家百货公司的总裁终于在我的账单上收取了 20 美元的多收费用。

college-writing-007604.en: If I get no response to a written complaint within ten days, I follow through with a personal telephone call.
college-writing-007604.zh: 如果我在十天内没有收到书面投诉的回复，我会通过个人电话进行跟进。

college-writing-007605.en: When I had a new bathtub installed a few years ago, the plumber left a gritty black substance on the bottom of the tub.
college-writing-007605.zh: 几年前我安装了一个新浴缸时，水管工在浴缸底部留下了一种坚硬的黑色物质。

college-writing-007606.en: I tried everything to get it off.
college-writing-007606.zh: 我尽一切努力把它取下来。

college-writing-007607.en: Finally, I made a personal phone call to the president of the firm.
college-writing-007607.zh: 最后，我给公司总裁打了一个私人电话。

college-writing-007608.en: Within days a well-dressed executive showed up at my door.
college-writing-007608.zh: 几天之内，一位穿着考究的高管出现在我家门口。

college-writing-007609.en: In a business suit, white shirt, striped tie, and rubber gloves, he cleaned the tub.
college-writing-007609.zh: 他穿着西装、白衬衫、条纹领带和橡胶手套，清洗了浴缸。

college-writing-007610.en: Before he left, he said, “You didn’t have to call the president.”
college-writing-007610.zh: 在他离开之前，他说：“你不必给总统打电话。”

college-writing-007611.en: Therefore, my advice to consumers is to keep accurate records, and when you have to complain, go right to the top.
college-writing-007611.zh: 因此，我对消费者的建议是保持准确的记录，当您必须抱怨时，请直接登上顶峰。

college-writing-007612.en: It has always worked for me.

college-writing-007614.en: Development through Revising After she had written the first draft, Meghan set it aside for several days.
college-writing-007614.zh: 发展通过修改后，梅根将其搁置了好几天。

college-writing-007615.en: When she reread it, she was able to look at it more critically.
college-writing-007615.zh: 当她重读它时，她能够更批判性地看待它。

college-writing-007617.en: I think this first draft is OK as the "bare bones" of an essay, but it needs to be fleshed out
college-writing-007617.zh: 我认为这个初稿是一篇文章的“裸骨”，但它需要充实

college-writing-007619.en: For instance, in paragraph 2, I need to explain why it’s important to know the
college-writing-007619.zh: 例如，在第 2 段中，我需要解释为什么知道

college-writing-007621.en: And in paragraph 3, I need to explain more about what happened with
college-writing-007621.zh: 在第 3 段中，我需要更多地解释一下发生了什么

college-writing-007622.en: the bike and the department store overcharge.
college-writing-007622.zh: 自行车和百货商店多收。

college-writing-007623.en: In paragraph 4, especially, I need to explain
college-writing-007623.zh: 特别是在第 4 段中，我需要解释

college-writing-007625.zh: 278 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-007626.en: With that self-critique in mind, Meghan wrote the version of “How to Complain” that appears at the beginning of this chapter.
college-writing-007626.zh: 考虑到这种自我批评，梅根写了本章开头出现的“如何抱怨”版本。

college-writing-007629.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-007629.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-007630.en: How to Do Well on a Job Interview
college-writing-007630.zh: 如何在工作面试中取得好成绩

college-writing-007632.en: Ask a random selection of people for a listing of their least favorite activities, and right up there with “getting my teeth drilled” is likely to be “going to a job interview.”
college-writing-007632.zh: 随机选择一个人，列出他们最不喜欢的活动，就在“让我的牙齿钻孔”的情况下，很可能是“去参加工作面试”。

college-writing-007633.en: The job interview is often regarded as a confusing, humiliating, and nerve-racking experience.
college-writing-007633.zh: 工作面试通常被认为是一种令人困惑、羞辱和神经紧张的经历。

college-writing-007634.en: First of all, you have to wait for your appointment in an outer room, often trapped there with other people applying for the same job.
college-writing-007634.zh: 首先，你必须在外面的房间里等待你的约会，经常被困在那里和其他人申请相同的工作。

college-writing-007635.en: You sit nervously, trying not to think about the fact that only one of you may be hired.
college-writing-007635.zh: 你紧张地坐着，尽量不去想只有你们中的一个人可能被雇用的事实。

college-writing-007636.en: Then you are called into the interviewer’s office.
college-writing-007636.zh: 然后你被叫到面试官办公室。

college-writing-007637.en: Faced with a complete stranger, you have to try to act both cool and friendly as you are asked all sorts of questions.
college-writing-007637.zh: 面对一个完全陌生的人，当你被问到各种问题时，你必须尝试表现得既酷又友好。

college-writing-007638.en: Some questions are personal: “What is your greatest weakness?”
college-writing-007638.zh: 有些问题是个人的：“你最大的弱点是什么？”

college-writing-007639.en: Others are confusing: “Why should we hire you?”
college-writing-007639.zh: 其他人则感到困惑：“我们为什么要雇用你？”

college-writing-007640.en: The interview probably takes about twenty minutes but seems like two hours.
college-writing-007640.zh: 面试可能需要大约二十分钟，但似乎需要两个小时。

college-writing-007641.en: Finally, you go home and wait for days and even weeks.
college-writing-007641.zh: 最后，你回家等待几天甚至几周。

college-writing-007642.en: If you get the job, great.
college-writing-007642.zh: 如果你得到了这份工作，那就太好了。

college-writing-007643.en: But if you don’t, you’re rarely given any reason why.
college-writing-007643.zh: 但如果你不这样做，你很少会得到任何理由。

college-writing-007644.en: The job-interview “game” may not be much fun, but it is a game you can win if you play it right.
college-writing-007644.zh: 工作面试“游戏”可能不是很有趣，但如果你玩得对，它是一个你可以赢的游戏。

college-writing-007645.en: The name of the game is standing out of the crowd─in a positive way.
college-writing-007645.zh: 游戏的名称以积极的方式脱颖而出。

college-writing-007646.en: If you go to the interview in a clown suit, you’ll stand out of the crowd, all right, but not in a way that is likely to get you hired.
college-writing-007646.zh: 如果你穿着小丑西装去面试，你会在人群中脱颖而出，好吧，但不是以可能让你被雇用的方式。

college-writing-007647.en: Here are guidelines to help you play the interview game to win:
college-writing-007647.zh: 以下是帮助您玩面试游戏以获胜的指南：

college-writing-007649.en: Instantly, the way you dress, speak, and move gives the interviewer more information about you than you would think possible.
college-writing-007649.zh: 立即，您的穿着、说话和移动方式为面试官提供了比您想象的更多的关于您的信息。

college-writing-007650.en: how I tried to solve the problem with the bathtub before I called the president.
college-writing-007650.zh: 在我打电话给总统之前，我如何尝试用浴缸解决问题。

college-writing-007652.en: make it clear that I don’t immediately go to the top as soon as I have a problem—I give the
college-writing-007652.zh: 明确表示，一旦我遇到问题，我不会立即登顶——我给

college-writing-007653.en: people at a lower level a chance to fix it first.
college-writing-007653.zh: 较低级别的人有机会首先修复它。

college-writing-007654.en: All in all, my first draft looks as if I just
college-writing-007654.zh: 总而言之，我的初稿看起来好像我只是

college-writing-007655.en: rushed to get the basic ideas down on paper.
college-writing-007655.zh: 急于把基本的想法写在纸上。

college-writing-007656.en: Now I need to take the time to back up my
college-writing-007656.zh: 现在我需要花时间备份我的

college-writing-007659.en: You doubt that this is true?

college-writing-007660.en: Consider this: a professional job recruiter, meeting a series of job applicants, was asked to signal the moment he decided not to hire each applicant.
college-writing-007660.zh: 考虑一下：一名专业的工作招聘人员会见了一系列求职者，被要求在他决定不雇用每个申请人的那一刻发出信号。

college-writing-007661.en: The thumbs-down decision was often made in less than forty-five seconds—even before the applicant thought the interview had begun.
college-writing-007661.zh: 拒绝的决定通常是在不到四十五秒的时间内做出的——甚至在申请人认为面试已经开始之前。

college-writing-007662.en: How can you keep from becoming a victim of an instant “no” decision?
college-writing-007662.zh: 您如何才能避免成为即时“不”决定的受害者？

college-writing-007664.en: This means business clothing: usually a suit and tie or a conservative dress or skirt suit.
college-writing-007664.zh: 这意味着商务服装：通常是西装和领带或保守的连衣裙或裙子套装。

college-writing-007665.zh: 不要穿休闲的学生服装。

college-writing-007666.en: On the other hand, don’t overdress: you’re going to a job interview, not a party.
college-writing-007666.zh: 另一方面，不要穿得过分：你要去参加工作面试，而不是参加派对。

college-writing-007667.en: If you’re not sure what’s considered appropriate business attire, do some spying before the interview.
college-writing-007667.zh: 如果您不确定什么被认为是合适的商务着装，请在面试前进行一些间谍活动。

college-writing-007668.en: Walk past your prospective place of employment at lunch or quitting time and check out how the employees are dressed.
college-writing-007668.zh: 在午餐或退出时间走过您未来的工作地点，看看员工的着装情况。

college-writing-007669.en: Your goal is to look as though you would fit in with that group of people.
college-writing-007669.zh: 你的目标是看起来好像你适合那群人。

college-writing-007671.en: Untidy hair, body odor, dandruff, unshined shoes, a hanging hem, stains on your tie, excessive makeup or cologne, a sloppy job of shaving─if the interviewer notices any of these, your prospect of being hired takes a probably fatal hit.
college-writing-007671.zh: 头发不整齐，体臭，头皮屑，不亮的鞋子，挂下摆，领带上的污渍，过度化妆或古龙水，剃须的工作马虎——如果面试官注意到其中任何一个，你被雇用的前景可能会致命 击中。

college-writing-007672.zh: • 看起来警觉、镇定和友好。

college-writing-007673.en: When that interviewer looks into the waiting room and calls your name, he or she is getting a first impression of your behavior.
college-writing-007673.zh: 当面试官看着候诊室并呼唤你的名字时，他或她会对你的行为有第一印象。

college-writing-007674.en: If you’re slouched in your chair, dozing or lost in the pages of a magazine; if you look up with an annoyed “Huh?”; if you get up slowly and wander over with your hands in your pockets, the interviewer will not be favorably impressed.
college-writing-007674.zh: 如果你在椅子上懒散，在杂志的页面上打瞌睡或迷路； 如果你抬起头来恼怒的“嗯？”； 如果你慢慢起床，双手插在口袋里徘徊，面试官不会留下深刻的印象。

college-writing-007675.en: What will earn you points is rising promptly and walking briskly toward the interviewer.
college-writing-007675.zh: 能为你赢得积分的是迅速上升，并迅速走向面试官。

college-writing-007676.en: Smiling and looking directly at that person, extend your hand to shake theirs, saying, “I’m Regina Brown. Thank you for seeing me today.”
college-writing-007676.zh: 微笑着直视着那个人，伸出你的手握着他们的手，说：“我是雷吉娜·布朗。谢谢你今天见到我。”

college-writing-007677.en: • Expect to make a little small talk.

college-writing-007678.en: This is not a waste of time; it is the interviewer’s way of checking your ability to be politely sociable, and it is your opportunity to cement the good impression you’ve already made.
college-writing-007678.zh: 这不是浪费时间； 这是面试官检查你礼貌社交的能力的方式，也是你巩固你已经给人留下的好印象的机会。

college-writing-007679.en: The key is to follow the interviewer’s lead.
college-writing-007679.zh: 关键是跟随面试官的领导。

college-writing-007680.en: If the interviewer wants to chat about the weather for a few minutes, do so.
college-writing-007680.zh: 如果面试官想聊几分钟的天气，那就去做吧。

college-writing-007681.en: But don’t drag it out; as soon as you get a signal that it’s time to talk about the job, be ready to get down to business.
college-writing-007681.zh: 但不要把它拖出来； 一旦你得到一个信号，它是时候谈论这份工作了，准备好开始做生意。

college-writing-007682.en: Be ready for the interviewer’s questions.
college-writing-007682.zh: 为面试官的问题做好准备。

college-writing-007683.en: The same questions come up again and again in many job interviews.
college-writing-007683.zh: 在许多工作面试中，同样的问题一次又一次地出现。

college-writing-007684.en: You should plan ahead for all these questions!
college-writing-007684.zh: 您应该提前计划所有这些问题！

college-writing-007685.en: Think carefully about each question, outline your answer, and memorize each outline.
college-writing-007685.zh: 仔细思考每个问题，概述你的答案，并记住每个大纲。

college-writing-007686.en: Then practice reciting the answers to yourself.
college-writing-007686.zh: 然后练习背诵答案给自己。

college-writing-007687.en: Only in this way are you going to be prepared.
college-writing-007687.zh: 只有这样，你才能做好准备。

college-writing-007688.en: Here are common questions, what they really mean, and how to answer them:
college-writing-007688.zh: 以下是常见问题，它们的真正含义以及如何回答：

college-writing-007690.en: This question is raised to see how organized you are.
college-writing-007690.zh: 提出这个问题是为了了解您的组织程度。

college-writing-007691.en: The wrong way to answer it is to launch into a wandering, disjointed response or─worse yet─to demand defensively, “What do you want to know?” or “What do you mean?”
college-writing-007691.zh: 回答这个问题的错误方法是开始流浪、脱节的反应，或者——更糟糕的是——防御性地要求：“你想知道什么？” 或“什么意思？”

college-writing-007693.zh: 280 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-007694.en: you should be prepared to give a brief summary of your life and work experience─where you grew up, where your family lives now, where you went to school, what jobs you’ve had, and how you happen to be here now looking for the challenge of a new job.
college-writing-007694.zh: 你应该准备好简要总结你的生活和工作经历——你在哪里长大，你的家人现在住在哪里，你在哪里上学，你有过什么工作，以及你现在是如何在这里寻找新工作的挑战的。

college-writing-007696.en: In talking about your strong points, mention traits that will serve you well in this particular job.
college-writing-007696.zh: 在谈论你的优点时，提及在这项特定工作中对您很有帮助的特质。

college-writing-007697.en: If you are well organized, a creative problem-solver, a good team member, or a quick learner, be ready to describe specific ways those strengths have served you in the past.
college-writing-007697.zh: 如果您组织良好、有创造力的问题解决者、优秀的团队成员或快速学习者，请准备好描述这些优势过去为您服务的具体方式。

college-writing-007698.en: Don’t make the mistake of saying, “I don’t have any real weaknesses.”
college-writing-007698.zh: 不要误以为“我没有任何真正的弱点”。

college-writing-007699.en: You’ll come across as more believable if you admit a flaw─but make it one that an employer might actually like.
college-writing-007699.zh: 如果你承认一个缺陷，你会觉得更可信——但要让它成为雇主可能真正喜欢的一个。

college-writing-007700.en: For instance, admit that you are a workaholic or a perfectionist.
college-writing-007700.zh: 例如，承认你是一个工作狂或完美主义者。

college-writing-007702.en: Remember that it is up to you to convince the interviewer that you’re the person for this job.
college-writing-007702.zh: 请记住，您有责任说服面试官您是这项工作的人。

college-writing-007703.en: If you just sit there and hope that the interviewer will magically discern your good qualities, you are likely to be disappointed.
college-writing-007703.zh: 如果你只是坐在那里，希望面试官能神奇地辨别你的优点，你可能会失望。

college-writing-007704.en: Don’t be afraid to sell yourself.

college-writing-007705.en: Tell the recruiter that from your research you have learned that the interviewer’s company is one you would like to work for, and that you believe the company’s needs and your skills are a great match.
college-writing-007705.zh: 告诉招聘人员，您从您的研究中了解到，面试官的公司是您想为之工作的公司，并且您相信公司的需求和技能是绝佳的匹配。

college-writing-007706.en: • “Why did you leave your last job?”
college-writing-007706.zh: • “你为什么离开你的上一份工作？”

college-writing-007707.en: This may seem like a great opportunity to cry on the interviewer’s shoulder about what a jerk your last boss was or how unappreciated you were.
college-writing-007707.zh: 这似乎是一个很好的机会，可以在面试官的肩膀上哭泣，说你的上一个老板是个什么混蛋，或者你是多么不欣赏。

college-writing-007709.en: The experts agree: never bad-mouth anyone when you are asked this question.
college-writing-007709.zh: 专家们同意：当你被问到这个问题时，永远不要说任何人的坏话。

college-writing-007710.en: Say that you left in order to seek greater responsibilities or challenges.
college-writing-007710.zh: 说你离开是为了寻求更大的责任或挑战。

college-writing-007711.zh: 是积极的，而不是消极的。

college-writing-007712.en: No matter how justified you may feel about hating your last job or boss, if you give voice to those feelings in an interview, you’re going to make the interviewer suspect that you’re a whiner and hard to work with.
college-writing-007712.zh: 无论你对讨厌你上一份工作或老板的感觉有多有道理，如果你在面试中表达这些感受，你会让面试官怀疑你是一个发牢骚且难以相处的人。

college-writing-007714.en: This is the time to stress one last time how interested you are in this particular job.
college-writing-007714.zh: 这是最后一次强调您对这项特定工作的兴趣的时候了。

college-writing-007715.en: Ask a question or two about specific aspects of the job, pointing out again how well your talents and the company’s needs are matched.
college-writing-007715.zh: 就工作的具体方面提出一两个问题，再次指出您的人才和公司的需求是否匹配。

college-writing-007716.en: Even if you’re dying to know how much the job pays and how much vacation you get, don’t ask.
college-writing-007716.zh: 即使你很想知道这份工作的报酬和你的假期是多少，也不要问。

college-writing-007717.en: There will be time enough to cover those questions after you’ve been offered the job.
college-writing-007717.zh: 在您获得工作后，将有足够的时间来解决这些问题。

college-writing-007718.en: Today, your task is to demonstrate what a good employee you would be.
college-writing-007718.zh: 今天，您的任务是展示您将成为什么样的优秀员工。

college-writing-007720.en: Once you’ve gotten past the interview, there is one more chance for you to make a fine impression.
college-writing-007720.zh: 一旦你通过了面试，你就有更多的机会给人留下美好的印象。

college-writing-007721.en: As soon as you can─certainly no more than one or two days after the interview─write a note of thanks.
college-writing-007721.zh: 面试结束后肯定不超过一两天——写一封感谢信。

college-writing-007722.en: In it, briefly remind the interviewer of when you came in and what job you applied for.
college-writing-007722.zh: 在其中，简要提醒面试官您何时进来以及您申请了什么工作。

college-writing-007723.en: As well as thanking the interviewer for seeing you, reaffirm your interest in the job and mention again why you think you are the best candidate for it.
college-writing-007723.zh: 除了感谢面试官见到你，重申你对这份工作的兴趣，并再次提及为什么你认为你是最好的候选人。

college-writing-007724.en: Make the note courteous, businesslike, and brief─just a paragraph or two.
college-writing-007724.zh: 把笔记做有礼貌、务实和简短——只是一两段。

college-writing-007727.en: is wavering between several equally qualified candidates, such a note could tip the scales in your favor.
college-writing-007727.zh: 在几个同样合格的候选人之间摇摆不定，这样的音符可能会使您的天平对您有利。

college-writing-007728.en: No amount of preparation is going to make interviewing for a job your favorite activity.
college-writing-007728.zh: 再多的准备工作也无法使面试工作成为您最喜欢的活动。

college-writing-007729.en: But if you go in well-prepared and with a positive attitude, your potential employer can’t help thinking highly of you.
college-writing-007729.zh: 但是，如果你准备充分并以积极的态度进行，你的潜在雇主会不禁对你高度重视。

college-writing-007730.en: And the day will come when you are the one who wins the job.
college-writing-007730.zh: 那一天你是赢得工作的那一位。

college-writing-007732.en: 1. Either of two sentences in “How to Do Well on a Job Interview” might serve
college-writing-007732.zh: 1. “如何在工作面试中做好”中的两个句子中的任何一个都可能服务

college-writing-007734.en: Write the opening words of either of these sentences:
college-writing-007734.zh: 写下这两个句子中的任何一个的开头词：

college-writing-007735.en: 2. Which statement would make the best topic sentence for paragraph 4?
college-writing-007735.zh: 2. 哪项陈述最适合第 4 段 主题句？

college-writing-007737.en: b. Interviewers care only about how applicants dress.
college-writing-007737.zh: B. 面试官只关心申请人的穿着方式。

college-writing-007738.en: c. Professional job recruiters meet many applicants for a single job.
college-writing-007738.zh: c.  专业工作招聘人员会见许多单一工作的申请人。

college-writing-007739.en: d. You should present yourself as a winner because first impressions count
college-writing-007739.zh: D. 您应该将自己展示为赢家，因为第一印象很重要

college-writing-007741.en: 3. Write an appropriate topic sentence for the list item that talks about strengths
college-writing-007741.zh: 3. 为讨论优势的列表项目写一个适当的 主题句

college-writing-007744.en: 4. What does the author mean by “dress appropriately” in paragraph 5?
college-writing-007744.zh: 4. 作者在第 5 段中所说的“穿着得体”是什么意思？

college-writing-007745.en: 5. According to Davis, what is the best reason for sending a thank-you note?
college-writing-007745.zh: 5. 根据戴维斯的说法，发送感谢信的最佳理由是什么？

college-writing-007747.en: 6. In paragraph 1, what three transitional words or phrases are used to begin
college-writing-007747.zh: 6. 在第 1 段中，使用哪三个过渡词或短语开始

college-writing-007748.en: sentences as the author describes the process of interviewing?
college-writing-007748.zh: 作者的句子描述了采访的过程？

college-writing-007750.zh: 第282章 论文发展模式

college-writing-007751.en: 7. The main method of organization of paragraph 1 is
college-writing-007751.zh: 7. 第 1 款的主要组织方法是

college-writing-007754.en: 8. Find three change-of-direction signals in the listed items following paragraph 5.
college-writing-007754.zh: 8. 在第 5 段所列项目中找到三个变向信号。

college-writing-007757.en: 9. Which statement best describes the introductory paragraph of “How to Do
college-writing-007757.zh: 9. 哪项陈述最能描述“如何做”的介绍性段落

college-writing-007760.en: It begins with a broad, general statement about job interviews and
college-writing-007760.zh: 它以关于工作面试的广泛而笼统的陈述开始

college-writing-007761.en: narrows it down to the thesis statement.
college-writing-007761.zh: 将其缩小到 中心论点句。

college-writing-007762.en: b. It describes a typical job interview and its aftermath.
college-writing-007762.zh: B. 它描述了典型的工作面试及其后果。

college-writing-007763.en: c. It explains the importance of doing well on a job interview.
college-writing-007763.zh: c.  它解释了在工作面试中取得好成绩的重要性。

college-writing-007764.en: d. It ends with a quotation about the importance of preparing for an interview.
college-writing-007764.zh: D. 它以关于准备面试的重要性的引文结束。

college-writing-007765.en: 10. What method for writing conclusions explained in Chapter 4 does Davis use?
college-writing-007765.zh: 10. 戴维斯在第 4 章中解释的结论的写作方法是什么？

college-writing-007766.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Process
college-writing-007766.zh: 写一篇强调过程的论文

college-writing-007767.en: Everyone is an expert at something.
college-writing-007767.zh: 每个人都是某事的专家。

college-writing-007768.en: Using your personal experiences and insights, write an essay with an emphasis on process.
college-writing-007768.zh: 利用你的个人经验和见解，写一篇强调过程的论文。

college-writing-007769.en: If you are a parent, you might write about how you taught your children to read.
college-writing-007769.zh: 如果您是父母，您可能会写下您如何教孩子阅读。

college-writing-007770.en: If you work as a sales representative, you might write about how monthly sales quotas are met.
college-writing-007770.zh: 如果您担任销售代表，您可能会写下如何满足每月销售配额。

college-writing-007771.en: If you are a recovering addict, you might write about how the twelve-step recovery process works.
college-writing-007771.zh: 如果您是一个正在康复的瘾君子，您可能会写下十二步恢复过程的工作原理。

college-writing-007772.en: If you know how to cook well, you could write about what it takes to make one of your favorite dishes.
college-writing-007772.zh: 如果您知道如何烹饪，您可以写下制作您最喜欢的菜肴的方法。

college-writing-007773.en: As a college student, you might write about how the registration process works at your school.
college-writing-007773.zh: 作为一名大学生，您可以写下您学校的注册过程如何运作。

college-writing-007774.en: Each of these topics will require you to incorporate several modes of writing, such as those discussed in Chapter 8, “Description,” and Chapter 9, “Narration.”
college-writing-007774.zh: 这些主题中的每一个都要求您结合几种写作模式，例如第 8 章“描述”和第 9 章“叙述”中讨论的那些。

college-writing-007780.en: Choose a prewriting technique that works for you, and for ten minutes use
college-writing-007780.zh: 选择适合您并使用十分钟的预写技术

college-writing-007781.en: that technique to generate ideas on the topic you have tentatively chosen.
college-writing-007781.zh: 这种技术可以就您暂时选择的主题产生想法。

college-writing-007782.en: Don’t worry about spelling, grammar, organization, or anything other than getting your thoughts down on the page.
college-writing-007782.zh: 除了将您的想法放在页面上之外，不要担心拼写、语法、组织或其他任何事情。

college-writing-007783.en: If ideas are still flowing at the end of ten minutes, keep on writing.
college-writing-007783.zh: 如果想法在十分钟结束时仍在流动，请继续写作。

college-writing-007784.en: Once you have finished getting your thoughts down, you should have a base of raw material that you can draw on in the next phase of your work.
college-writing-007784.zh: 一旦你完成了你的想法，你应该有一个可以在下一阶段工作的原材料基础。

college-writing-007785.en: Judging from what you have produced, do you think you have enough material to support your essay?
college-writing-007785.zh: 从你制作的内容来看，你认为你有足够的材料来支持你的论文吗？

college-writing-007786.en: If so, keep following the steps below.
college-writing-007786.zh: 如果是这样，请继续遵循以下步骤。

college-writing-007787.en: If not, choose another topic and spend about ten minutes generating ideas to see if this other topic might be a better choice.
college-writing-007787.zh: 如果没有，请选择另一个主题并花费大约十分钟的时间来产生想法，看看这个其他主题是否可能是更好的选择。

college-writing-007789.en: Develop a single clear sentence that will serve as your thesis.
college-writing-007789.zh: 制定一个明确的句子，作为你的论文。

college-writing-007791.en: should demonstrate why it is important that your readers know about this process.
college-writing-007791.zh: 应该说明为什么您的读者了解这个过程很重要。

college-writing-007793.en: Make a list of the steps you are describing.

college-writing-007795.en: Number your items in time order.
college-writing-007795.zh: 按时间顺序对您的物品编号。

college-writing-007796.en: Strike out items that do not fit in the list;
college-writing-007796.zh: 删除不适合列表的项目；

college-writing-007797.en: add others as they occur to you.

college-writing-007799.en: After making the list, decide how the items can be grouped into a minimum
college-writing-007799.zh: 创建列表后，决定如何将项目分组为最小值

college-writing-007801.en: With a topic like “How to Raise Kind Children,” you might divide the process into (1) infancy and toddlerhood; (2) elementary years; and (3) teen years.
college-writing-007801.zh: 对于像“如何抚养善良的孩子”这样的话题，您可以将这个过程分为（1）婴儿期和幼儿期； (2) 小学； (3) 青少年年。

college-writing-007803.en: Use your list as a guide to write the first rough draft of your paper.
college-writing-007803.zh: 以您的清单为指南，撰写论文的第一份草稿。

college-writing-007804.en: Do not expect to finish your paper in one draft.
college-writing-007804.zh: 不要期望在一份草稿中完成您的论文。

college-writing-007805.en: You should be ready to write a series of drafts as you work toward the goals of unity, support, and coherence.
college-writing-007805.zh: 当你朝着团结、支持和连贯的目标努力时，你应该准备好写一系列草稿。

college-writing-007806.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-007806.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-007807.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-007807.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-007808.en: Keep in mind the points and questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-007808.zh: 请记住本章末尾四个基准清单中的要点和问题。

college-writing-007809.en: Ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-007809.zh: 请您的朋友也回复他们。

college-writing-007810.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to the checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-007810.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改论文时，请继续参考清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-007812.en: Write an essay in which you explain how something has happened or happens rather than how to do something.
college-writing-007812.zh: 写一篇文章，你解释某事是如何发生或发生的，而不是如何做某事。

college-writing-007814.en: The topic you choose may be assigned by your instructor, or it may require your instructor’s approval.
college-writing-007814.zh: 您选择的主题可能由您的讲师分配，也可能需要您的教师的批准。

college-writing-007815.en: For example, instead of trying to discuss the workings of the U.S. government, explain the process by which a bill presented in Congress eventually becomes law.
college-writing-007815.zh: 例如，与其试图讨论美国政府的运作方式，不如解释国会提出的法案最终成为法律的过程。

college-writing-007816.en: Instead of explaining how World War II happened, focus on the events that led to America’s
college-writing-007816.zh: 与其解释第二次世界大战是如何发生的，不如关注导致美国的事件

college-writing-007818.zh: 第284章 论文发展模式

college-writing-007820.en: You may want to check Chapter 12, “Cause and/or Effect,” Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” and Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay,” for additional ways to support your thesis.
college-writing-007820.zh: 您可能想查看第 12 章“原因和/或效果”，第 19 章，“撰写基于来源的论文”和第 20 章“撰写研究论文”，以获得支持论文的其他方法。

college-writing-007821.en: Here are other topics you might choose to explain:
college-writing-007821.zh: 以下是您可以选择解释的其他主题：

college-writing-007822.en: • the process for conducting clinical trials of a new prescription drug • how a virus can become a pandemic • how a student theater production happens • how a company like Apple became so profitable
college-writing-007822.zh: • 进行新处方药临床试验的过程 • 病毒如何成为大流行 • 学生影院制作 • 像苹果这样的公司如何变得如此有利可图

college-writing-007825.en: Select a topic you know a lot about.
college-writing-007825.zh: 选择一个你非常了解的主题。

college-writing-007826.en: However, if necessary, gather more detail
college-writing-007826.zh: 但是，如有必要，收集更多细节

college-writing-007827.en: by reading about your topic in the library or on the Internet.
college-writing-007827.zh: 通过在图书馆或互联网上阅读您的主题。

college-writing-007828.en: Before researching, use freewriting, listing, or some other information-gathering technique to write down all the information and ideas in your head.
college-writing-007828.zh: 在研究之前，使用自由写作、列表或其他一些信息收集技术来写下你脑海中的所有信息和想法。

college-writing-007829.en: This will help you remember what information should be cited and what information is your personal knowledge.
college-writing-007829.zh: 这将帮助您记住应该引用哪些信息以及您的个人知识是哪些信息。

college-writing-007831.en: If you do need to do research, remember to check Chapter 19, “Writing a
college-writing-007831.zh: 如果您确实需要进行研究，请记住检查第 19 章，“写

college-writing-007832.en: Source-Based Essay,” and Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay,” to properly cite your information and avoid plagiarism.
college-writing-007832.zh: 基于来源的论文”和第 20 章，“撰写研究论文”，以正确引用您的信息并避免抄袭。

college-writing-007833.en: c. Look over your notes and make a list of steps involved in the process.
college-writing-007833.zh: c.  查看您的笔记并列出过程中涉及的步骤。

college-writing-007834.en: d. Organize your list to be chronological and orderly.
college-writing-007834.zh: D. 将您的列表按时间顺序排列。

college-writing-007835.en: e. You have just prepared the beginnings of a scratch outline.
college-writing-007835.zh: e. 您刚刚准备了划痕大纲的开头。

college-writing-007837.en: by filling in information under each main point.
college-writing-007837.zh: 通过在每个要点下填写信息。

college-writing-007838.en: Then use this outline as a guide as you write the first drafts of your paper.
college-writing-007838.zh: 然后在撰写论文的初稿时使用此大纲作为指南。

college-writing-007839.en: REVISING As you read through your first draft and subsequent drafts, ask yourself the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-007839.zh: 修改当您阅读初稿和后续草稿时，请在本章末尾的四个基础清单中问自己问题。

college-writing-007840.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to this checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-007840.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改您的论文时，请继续参考此清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-007841.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-007841.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-007842.en: Many jobs require people to provide reports that make recommendations.
college-writing-007842.zh: 许多工作要求人们提供提出建议的报告。

college-writing-007843.en: In this essay, you will write a report that analyzes and explains a process at your job and proposes a better, more effective process.
college-writing-007843.zh: 在这篇文章中，您将撰写一份报告，分析和解释您的工作过程，并提出一个更好、更有效的过程。

college-writing-007844.en: For example, you could analyze the hiring process and suggest ways to make it more efficient, or you could analyze the process a restaurant customer’s order goes through and propose ways to get the food to the customer more quickly.
college-writing-007844.zh: 例如，您可以分析招聘流程并提出提高效率的方法，或者您可以分析餐厅客户的订单经过的流程，并提出更快地将食物送达客户的方法。

college-writing-007848.en: You may want to check Chapter 16, “Argument,” to help you create a persuasive tone to your essay.
college-writing-007848.zh: 您可能想查看第 16 章“论点”，以帮助您为您的论文创造一种有说服力的语气。

college-writing-007849.zh: 流程核对清单：四个基地

college-writing-007851.en: Have I included a thesis statement that clearly identifies the process I am going to discuss?
college-writing-007851.zh: 我是否包含了一个 中心论点句 来清楚地确定我将要讨论的过程？

college-writing-007852.en: Does my essay describe the steps in a clear, logical way?
college-writing-007852.zh: 我的文章是否以清晰、合乎逻辑的方式描述了这些步骤？

college-writing-007853.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-007853.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-007855.en: Does my essay describe the necessary steps so that a reader could perform the task described?
college-writing-007855.zh: 我的文章是否描述了必要的步骤，以便读者可以执行所描述的任务？

college-writing-007856.en: Is essential information that could help the reader understand the process missing?
college-writing-007856.zh: 是否可以帮助读者理解缺失的过程的基本信息？

college-writing-007858.en: Have I organized my essay in a consistent manner that is appropriate to my subject?
college-writing-007858.zh: 我是否以适合我主题的一致方式组织了我的论文？

college-writing-007859.en: Do I have a concluding paragraph that provides a summary of the process, a final thought about the process, or both?
college-writing-007859.zh: 我是否有一个总结段落提供了对过程的总结、对过程的最终想法，或两者兼而有之？

college-writing-007861.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-007861.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-007862.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-007862.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-007863.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-007863.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-007865.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-007865.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-007870.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on cause and/or effect • write an essay with emphasis on cause and/or effect • revise an essay with emphasis on cause and/or effect
college-writing-007870.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写一篇强调因果和/或效果的文章 • 撰写一篇强调因果和/或效果的文章 • 修改文章，重点是因和/或效果

college-writing-007871.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize cause and/or effect • one professional model essay that emphasizes cause and/or effect
college-writing-007871.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调因果和/或效果的学生论文 • 一篇强调因果和/或效果的专业模型论文

college-writing-007872.en: Write an essay in which you discuss the causes or effects of our society’s fascination with reality TV.
college-writing-007872.zh: 写一篇文章，讨论我们社会对真人秀的迷恋的原因或影响。

college-writing-007873.en: An essay on the causes would discuss why Americans are so intrigued with reality television shows.
college-writing-007873.zh: 一篇关于原因的文章将讨论为什么美国人对真人秀节目如此感兴趣。

college-writing-007874.en: An essay on the effects would show how this fascination with reality TV has affected American society.
college-writing-007874.zh: 一篇关于效果的文章将展示这种对真人秀的迷恋如何影响美国社会。

college-writing-007876.en: Why did Emma decide to move out of her parents’ house?
college-writing-007876.zh: 为什么艾玛决定搬出她父母的房子？

college-writing-007877.en: What made you quit a well-paying job?
college-writing-007877.zh: 是什么让你辞掉了一份高薪的工作？

college-writing-007878.en: Why are horror movies so popular?
college-writing-007878.zh: 为什么恐怖电影如此受欢迎？

college-writing-007879.en: Why has Benjamin missed so many classes?
college-writing-007879.zh: 为什么本杰明错过了这么多课程？

college-writing-007880.en: Why did our team fail to make the league play-offs?
college-writing-007880.zh: 为什么我们的球队未能进入联赛附加赛？

college-writing-007881.en: Every day we ask questions like these and look for answers.
college-writing-007881.zh: 每天我们都会问这样的问题并寻找答案。

college-writing-007882.en: We realize that many actions do not occur without causes, and we realize also that a given action can have a series of effects─good or bad.
college-writing-007882.zh: 我们意识到许多动作并非没有原因，我们也意识到给定的动作可以产生一系列效果——好坏。

college-writing-007883.en: By examining the causes or effects of an action, we seek to understand and explain things that happen in our lives.
college-writing-007883.zh: 通过检查行动的原因或影响，我们试图理解和解释我们生活中发生的事情。

college-writing-007884.en: C H A P T E R 12 12 Cause and/or Effect
college-writing-007884.zh: C h a p t e r 12 12 原因和/或效果

college-writing-007887.zh: 第288章 论文发展模式

college-writing-007889.en: You will be asked in this chapter to do some detective work by examining the cause of something or the effects of something.
college-writing-007889.zh: 本章要求您通过检查某事的原因或某物的影响来做一些侦探工作。

college-writing-007890.en: First read the student essays and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-007890.zh: 首先阅读学生论文和模型论文，并通过随附的问题进行研究。

college-writing-007891.en: All three essays support their thesis statements by explaining a series of causes or a series of effects.
college-writing-007891.zh: 所有三篇文章都通过解释一系列原因或一系列效果来支持他们的 中心论点句。

college-writing-007892.en: The Joys of an Old Car

college-writing-007893.en: Some of my friends can’t believe that my car still runs.
college-writing-007893.zh: 我的一些朋友不敢相信我的车还在运行。

college-writing-007894.en: Others laugh when they see it parked outside the house and ask if it’s an antique.
college-writing-007894.zh: 其他人看到它停在房子外面时会笑，问它是否是古董。

college-writing-007895.en: But they aren’t being fair to my twenty-year-old Toyota Camry.
college-writing-007895.zh: 但它们对我 20 岁的丰田凯美瑞不公平。

college-writing-007896.en: In fact, my “antique” has opened my eyes to the rewards of owning an old car.
college-writing-007896.zh: 事实上，我的“古董”让我看到了拥有一辆旧车的回报。

college-writing-007897.en: One obvious reward of owning my old Toyota is economy.
college-writing-007897.zh: 拥有我的旧丰田汽车的一个明显回报是经济。

college-writing-007898.en: Twenty years ago, when my husband and I were newly married and nearly broke, we bought the car—a shiny red year-old leftover—for a mere $5,000.
college-writing-007898.zh: 二十年前，当我丈夫和我刚结婚并差点破产时，我们只花了 5,000 美元就买了这辆车——一个闪亮的红色一年前的剩菜。

college-writing-007899.en: Today it would cost four times as much.
college-writing-007899.zh: 今天它的成本将是它的四倍。

college-writing-007900.en: We save money on insurance, since it’s no longer worthwhile for us to have collision coverage.
college-writing-007900.zh: 我们在保险上省钱，因为我们不再值得拥有碰撞保险。

college-writing-007901.en: Old age has even been kind to the Toyota’s engine, which has required only three major repairs in the last several years.
college-writing-007901.zh: 老年甚至对丰田的发动机很友善，在过去的几年里，它只需要进行三次大修。

college-writing-007902.en: And it still delivers twenty-eight miles per gallon in the city and forty-one on the highway—not bad for such a mature machine!
college-writing-007902.zh: 它仍然在城市中提供每加仑 28 英里的距离，在高速公路上提供 41 英里——对于如此成熟的机器来说还不错！

college-writing-007903.en: I’ve heard that when a Toyota passes the twenty-thousand-mile mark with no problems, it will probably go on forever.
college-writing-007903.zh: 我听说当丰田一辆没有问题的 2000 英里标记时，它可能会永远持续下去。

college-writing-007905.en: Our Toyota breezed past that mark many years ago.
college-writing-007905.zh: 多年前，我们的 Toyota 轻而易举地超越了这个标记。

college-writing-007906.en: Since then, I’ve been able to count on it to sputter to life and make its way down the driveway on the coldest, snowiest mornings.
college-writing-007906.zh: 从那时起，我就可以指望它在最寒冷、最雪的早晨在车道上飞驰而过。

college-writing-007907.en: When my boss got stuck with his brand-new BMW in the worst snowstorm of the year, I sauntered into work on time.
college-writing-007907.zh: 当我的老板在今年最严重的暴风雪中遇到他全新的宝马时，我准时上班。

college-writing-007908.en: The single time my Toyota didn’t start, unfortunately, was the day I had a final exam.
college-writing-007908.zh: 不幸的是，我的丰田一次没有开始的那一天是我进行期末考试的那一天。

college-writing-007909.en: The Toyota may have the body of an old car, but beneath its elderly hood hums the engine of a teenager.
college-writing-007909.zh: 丰田汽车可能有一辆旧车的车身，但在它老人的引擎盖下，却是一个青少年的引擎。

college-writing-007910.en: Last of all, having the same car for many years offers the advantage of familiarity.
college-writing-007910.zh: 最后，多年拥有同一辆车提供了熟悉的优势。

college-writing-007911.en: When I open the door and slide into the driver’s seat, the soft vinyl surrounds me like a well-worn glove.
college-writing-007911.zh: 当我打开车门并滑入驾驶座时，柔软的乙烯基就像破旧的手套一样环绕着我。

college-writing-007912.en: I know to the millimeter exactly how much room I have when I turn a corner or back into a curbside parking space.
college-writing-007912.zh: 当我拐弯或回到路边停车位时，我确切地知道我有多少空间。

college-writing-007913.en: When my gas gauge points to “empty,” I know that 1.3 gallons are still in reserve, and I can plan accordingly.
college-writing-007913.zh: 当我的气表指向“空”时，我知道 1.3 加仑仍在储备中，我可以相应地进行计划。

college-writing-007916.zh: 第12章 原因和/或效果289

college-writing-007917.en: begin to shake when I go more than sixty-five miles an hour, reminding me that I am exceeding the speed limit.
college-writing-007917.zh: 当我每小时超过 65 英里时开始颤抖，提醒我我已经超出了速度限制。

college-writing-007918.en: With the Toyota, the only surprises I face come from other drivers.
college-writing-007918.zh: 有了丰田，我面临的唯一惊喜来自其他司机。

college-writing-007919.en: I prize my twenty-year-old Toyota’s economy and dependability, and most of all, its familiarity.
college-writing-007919.zh: 我重视我 20 岁的丰田的经济和可靠性，最重要的是，它的熟悉程度。

college-writing-007920.en: It is faded, predictable, and comfortable, like a well-worn pair of jeans.
college-writing-007920.zh: 它褪色、可预测和舒适，就像一条破旧的牛仔裤。

college-writing-007921.en: And, like a well-worn pair of jeans, it will be difficult to throw away.
college-writing-007921.zh: 而且，就像一条破旧的牛仔裤，很难扔掉。

college-writing-007922.en: The Only Thing We Have to Fear
college-writing-007922.zh: 我们唯一要害怕的事情

college-writing-007923.en: During the Great Depression, President Roosevelt claimed, “The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.”
college-writing-007923.zh: 在大萧条时期，罗斯福总统声称，“我们唯一需要害怕的就是恐惧本身。”

college-writing-007924.en: He wanted to inspire citizens as a way to spur the economy.
college-writing-007924.zh: 他想激励公民作为刺激经济的一种方式。

college-writing-007925.en: In his Nobel Prize acceptance speech delivered in December 1950, William Faulkner, the great American novelist, said, “The basest of all things is to be afraid.”
college-writing-007925.zh: 在1950年12月发表的诺贝尔奖获奖感言中，伟大的美国小说家威廉·福克纳说：“最根本的是害怕。”

college-writing-007926.en: Uttered many decades ago, both these ideas still have relevance.
college-writing-007926.zh: 几十年前说，这两个想法仍然具有相关性。

college-writing-007927.en: Some young people make important life decisions based on deep-seated anxieties.
college-writing-007927.zh: 一些年轻人根据根深蒂固的焦虑做出重要的人生决定。

college-writing-007928.en: They fear that they won’t be accepted by others, that they won’t find a mate, or that they just aren’t living life to the fullest.
college-writing-007928.zh: 他们担心自己不会被别人接受，他们不会找到伴侣，或者他们只是没有过上充实的生活。

college-writing-007929.en: As a result, they pervert their identities, becoming adults they don’t want to become and living lives they never intended.
college-writing-007929.zh: 结果，他们歪曲了自己的身份，成为他们不想成为的成年人，过着他们从未想过的生活。

college-writing-007930.en: A logical question is why so many people spend money—often money they don’t have—on costly toys they don’t need.
college-writing-007930.zh: 一个合乎逻辑的问题是，为什么这么多人花钱——通常是他们没有的钱——花在他们不需要的昂贵玩具上。

college-writing-007931.en: Deep in the pits of their stomachs is the gnawing fear that, without such toys, their friends will abandon them and they will have to sit home weekends watching sitcom reruns.
college-writing-007931.zh: 在他们的胃深处深处是一种咬牙切齿的恐惧，没有这些玩具，他们的朋友会抛弃它们，他们将不得不坐在家里周末观看情景喜剧重播。

college-writing-007932.en: They are frightened they won’t fit in, so frightened, in fact, that they have become blind to the true meaning of friendship.
college-writing-007932.zh: 他们害怕他们不适合，事实上，他们对友谊的真正含义视而不见。

college-writing-007933.en: They have forgotten that, to those of character, possessions and image are far less important than integrity, honesty, and compassion.
college-writing-007933.zh: 他们忘记了，对于那些有品格、财产和形象的人来说，远不如正直、诚实和同情心重要。

college-writing-007934.en: Such people are worth knowing, and they are everywhere.
college-writing-007934.zh: 这样的人是值得知道的，他们无处不在。

college-writing-007935.en: To find them, all people need to do is to show a little character themselves.
college-writing-007935.zh: 要找到它们，人们需要做的就是展示自己的一点性格。

college-writing-007936.en: Some individuals fear they will never be able to attract and keep a lifelong partner.
college-writing-007936.zh: 有些人担心他们永远无法吸引和保持终身伴侣。

college-writing-007937.en: Therefore, they make gargantuan efforts to re-create themselves in the Hollywood image.
college-writing-007937.zh: 因此，他们为在好莱坞的形象中重新创造自己做出了巨大的努力。

college-writing-007938.en: For example, they follow ludicrous diets, exercise for hours each day, and drink expensive commercial concoctions to curb their appetites and lose weight.
college-writing-007938.zh: 例如，他们遵循荒谬的饮食，每天锻炼数小时，喝昂贵的商业混合物来抑制他们的食欲和减肥。

college-writing-007940.en: Others, looking ahead to their more mature years, plan to get collagen injections, hair plugs, and even breast implants.
college-writing-007940.zh: 其他人，展望他们更成熟的岁月，计划进行胶原蛋白注射、发塞，甚至乳房植入物。

college-writing-007941.en: If people simply trusted in the goodness of someone who might love them for who they are and not for the smoothness of their skins or the fullness of their hair, their lives could be so much easier.
college-writing-007941.zh: 如果人们只是相信一个可能爱他们的人的善良，而不是因为他们的皮肤光滑或头发的丰满，他们的生活可能会轻松得多。

college-writing-007945.en: 1. Which supporting paragraph in “The Joys of an Old Car” lacks a topic sentence?
college-writing-007945.zh: 1.《老车的乐趣》中的哪个支持段落缺少主题句？

college-writing-007949.en: 2. Which sentence in paragraph 3 of “The Joys of an Old Car” should be omitted
college-writing-007949.zh: 二、“旧车的乐趣”第3段中的哪句话应该省略

college-writing-007950.en: in the interest of paragraph unity?

college-writing-007952.en: 3. Rewrite the thesis statement of “The Joys of an Old Car” to include a plan of
college-writing-007952.zh: 3. 改写“旧车的乐趣”的中心论点句，包括一个计划

college-writing-007954.en: However, the fear that causes the greatest damage to the human spirit is the one that makes people question the value and fullness of their own lives.
college-writing-007954.zh: 然而，对人类精神造成最大伤害的恐惧是使人们质疑自己生活的价值和充实性的恐惧。

college-writing-007955.en: Too many—young and old alike, if the truth be told—are afraid that they might miss out on “the good life,” which, the media tells us, is part of a life fulfilled.
college-writing-007955.zh: 太多的——无论是年轻人还是老年人，如果说实话——害怕他们会错过“美好生活”，媒体告诉我们，这就是实现生活的一部分。

college-writing-007956.en: Influenced by the glitz of Hollywood and Madison Avenue, people equate happiness with owning the best of everything.
college-writing-007956.zh: 受好莱坞和麦迪逊大道的浮华影响，人们将幸福等同于拥有一切最好的东西。

college-writing-007957.en: So, they take a second and even a third job to afford the sexiest car, the biggest house, or the largest flat screen.
college-writing-007957.zh: 因此，他们需要第二份甚至第三份工作才能负担得起最性感的汽车、最大的房子或最大的平板屏幕。

college-writing-007958.en: This is the worst perversion of all, for it robs human beings of their humanity.
college-writing-007958.zh: 这是最严重的变态，因为它剥夺了人类的人性。

college-writing-007959.en: They don’t own the car, the house, the television; they are owned by the possessions.
college-writing-007959.zh: 他们不拥有汽车、房子、电视； 它们归属地所有。

college-writing-007960.en: It cannot be called anything but servitude.
college-writing-007960.zh: 除了奴役，它不能被称为任何东西。

college-writing-007961.en: The irony is, of course, that, in seeking the good life, people have lost the good life.
college-writing-007961.zh: 当然，具有讽刺意味的是，在寻求美好生活时，人们已经失去了美好的生活。

college-writing-007962.en: Instead of having the luxury to relax at home, talk to family, enjoy dinner, go for long walks, or watch the sun set, too many people are rushing off to an evening of more work to pay off the bills.
college-writing-007962.zh: 与其在家里放松、与家人交谈、享用晚餐、散步或观看日落，不如有太多人冲着忙着去做更多的工作来偿还账单。

college-writing-007963.en: Cowering to silly fears, getting and taking, or changing to fit in with the ridiculous images created by a plastic society is harmful, and it is blurring American’s moral vision.
college-writing-007963.zh: 屈服于愚蠢的恐惧、获得、接受或改变以适应塑料社会创造的荒谬形象是有害的，它模糊了美国人的道德愿景。

college-writing-007964.en: People need to realize once more that the true source of happiness, the measure of a life fulfilled, is the ability to see eternal beauty in the night sky, to become inspired by gently falling snow, and to make those ever important human connections.
college-writing-007964.zh: 人们需要再次意识到，真正的幸福源泉，实现的生命的尺度，是能够在夜空中看到永恒的美丽，从轻轻飘落的雪中获得灵感，并建立那些重要的人际关系。

college-writing-007990.zh: 第292章 论文发展模式

college-writing-007991.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Cause and/or Effect Considering Purpose and Audience The primary purpose of an essay that emphasizes cause and/or effect is to support your main point by using examples that explain (1) the causes of a particular event or situation; (2) the effects of an event or a situation; or more rarely (3) a combination of both.
college-writing-007991.zh: 撰写一篇强调原因和/或效果的论文，考虑目的和受众 强调因果和/或效果的文章的主要目的是通过使用解释（1）特定事件或情况的原因的例子来支持你的主要观点； (2) 事件或情况的影响； 或更罕见 (3) 两者的组合。

college-writing-007992.en: The type of essay you write depends on your topic and main point.
college-writing-007992.zh: 你写的论文类型取决于你的主题和要点。

college-writing-007993.en: If you want to tell readers the impact a person had on your life, your essay would focus on effects.
college-writing-007993.zh: 如果你想告诉读者一个人对你生活的影响，你的文章将集中在效果上。

college-writing-007994.en: If you want to explain why you moved out of your family home, it would focus on causes.
college-writing-007994.zh: 如果你想解释你搬出家的原因，它会专注于原因。

college-writing-007995.en: Essays that emphasize cause and/or effect are like essays that emphasize process.
college-writing-007995.zh: 强调原因和/或效果的论文就像强调过程的论文。

college-writing-007996.en: However, while process explains how something happens, cause and/or effect discusses the reasons for or results of an event or situation.
college-writing-007996.zh: 然而，虽然过程解释某事如何发生，但原因和/或效果讨论了事件或情况的原因或结果。

college-writing-007997.en: Exams in science, history, economics, and other courses include questions that demand the explanation of causes, effects, or both.
college-writing-007997.zh: 科学、历史、经济学和其他课程的考试包括需要解释原因、影响或两者兼而有之的问题。

college-writing-007998.en: For example, you might be asked to explain the economic causes of the Russian Revolution or the atmospheric effects of cutting down trees in the rain forest.
college-writing-007998.zh: 例如，您可能会被要求解释俄罗斯革命的经济原因或在雨林中砍伐树木的大气影响。

college-writing-007999.en: At first, this can seem simple.

college-writing-008000.en: However, analyzing causes and effects is often complicated.
college-writing-008000.zh: 然而，分析的原因和影响往往很复杂。

college-writing-008001.en: For example, in the essay, “The Only Thing We Have to Fear,” the writer claims that many young people desire to possess the same type of clothing or electronic gadgets that their friends have.
college-writing-008001.zh: 例如，在文章“我们唯一需要害怕的东西”中，作者声称许多年轻人希望拥有与朋友相同的服装或电子产品。

college-writing-008002.en: This stems from an ultimate or primary cause: the fear of being alone.
college-writing-008002.zh: 这源于一个最终或主要原因：对孤独的恐惧。

college-writing-008003.en: A more proximate cause (one that is closer to the effect) is the desire to be popular, part of a group.
college-writing-008003.zh: 一个更接近的原因（一个更接近结果的原因）是渴望成为群体的一部分。

college-writing-008004.en: In short, the writer has not simply discussed a cause but has explained a causal chain: (1) fear of being alone (ultimate cause); (2) desire to be popular (proximate cause); (3) need to have what others have (effect).
college-writing-008004.zh: 简而言之，作者并没有简单地讨论一个原因，而是解释了一个因果链：（1）害怕孤独（终极原因）； (2) 渴望受欢迎（近因）； (3) 需要有他人拥有的东西（效果）。

college-writing-008005.en: Of course, the author could have extended the chain to explain the cause behind the fear of being alone: low self-esteem, difficult family life, or peer pressure, for example.
college-writing-008005.zh: 当然，作者本可以扩展链条来解释孤独恐惧背后的原因：例如，低自尊、困难的家庭生活或同龄人的压力。

college-writing-008006.en: Analyzing effects can also be tricky because one cause may lead to multiple effects.
college-writing-008006.zh: 分析效果也可能很棘手，因为一种原因可能会导致多种效果。

college-writing-008007.en: In addition, one cause may yield a long-term effect as well as an immediate effect.
college-writing-008007.zh: 此外，一种原因可能产生长期效果和即时效果。

college-writing-008008.en: Take the case of a young construction worker who decided to go back to college to study architecture five years after having graduated from high school.
college-writing-008008.zh: 以一位年轻的建筑工人为例，他在高中毕业五年后决定回到大学学习建筑。

college-writing-008009.en: The immediate effects of the worker’s decision include (1) having to budget money more carefully to compensate for no longer being employed full-time; (2) having less time to socialize with friends; and (3) getting a lot less physical exercise.
college-writing-008009.zh: 工人决定的直接影响包括（1）必须更仔细地预算资金以补偿不再全职工作； (2) 与朋友交往的时间更少； (3) 减少体育锻炼。

college-writing-008010.en: However, there are several long-term effects as well: (1) securing a high-paying position after graduation; (2) making new friends at college and at the new job; and
college-writing-008010.zh: 然而，也有几个长期影响：（1）在毕业后确保高薪职位； (2) 在大学和新工作中结交新朋友； 和

college-writing-008011.zh: 第12章 原因和/或影响 293

college-writing-008012.en: (3) developing new tastes in music and film as a result of taking college humanities courses.
college-writing-008012.zh: （3）通过上大学人文课程，发展音乐和电影的新品味。

college-writing-008013.en: Depending on your topic and purpose, you can decide whether to focus on causes or effects.
college-writing-008013.zh: 根据您的主题和目的，您可以决定是否专注于原因或影响。

college-writing-008014.en: If you want to balance your paper, you can discuss both.
college-writing-008014.zh: 如果你想平衡你的论文，你可以讨论两者。

college-writing-008015.en: Consider each of the following scenarios and decide whether it requires discussing causes, effects, or both.
college-writing-008015.zh: 考虑以下每个场景，并决定是否需要讨论原因、影响或两者兼而有之。

college-writing-008016.en: 1. A young couple decides to buy a two-family house and rent out the top floor to tenants.
college-writing-008016.zh: 1. 一对年轻夫妇决定买一栋两户住宅，然后将顶层出租给租户。

college-writing-008017.en: 2. A new television reality show becomes an instant sensation, and the “actors” achieve instant fame.
college-writing-008017.zh: 2. 新的电视真人秀节目立即成为轰动，“演员”一举成名。

college-writing-008018.en: 3. Residents of an assisted living facility meet with administrators to address the increase in residents’ fees.
college-writing-008018.zh: 3. 辅助生活设施的居民与管理人员会面，以解决居民费用的增加。

college-writing-008019.en: Students writing on the first item might focus on effects; those writing on the second might discuss causes.
college-writing-008019.zh: 在第一项上写作的学生可能会关注效果； 那些写在第二个的人可能会讨论原因。

college-writing-008020.en: The third item might be approached by writing about both.
college-writing-008020.zh: 第三个项目可以通过写下两者来处理。

college-writing-008021.en: Whichever approach you choose, remember that you can’t discuss effects without at least mentioning causes, and vice versa.
college-writing-008021.zh: 无论您选择哪种方法，请记住，您不能在不提及原因的情况下讨论效果，反之亦然。

college-writing-008022.en: While discussing the problems that the young couple had with their tenants (effects of their decision to rent out the top floor), you might also explain their reason for becoming landlords in the first place: to earn rent money that would help them meet their mortgage payments.
college-writing-008022.zh: 在讨论这对年轻夫妇与租户的问题（他们决定出租顶层的影响）时，您可能还可以首先解释他们成为房东的原因：赚取租金，以帮助他们支付抵押贷款。

college-writing-008023.en: As with all essays, pick a topic that appeals to your readers.
college-writing-008023.zh: 与所有论文一样，选择一个吸引读者的主题。

college-writing-008024.en: An essay on the negative effects of steroids on professional athletes may interest sports fans; it might not appeal to people who dislike sports.
college-writing-008024.zh: 一篇关于类固醇对职业运动员的负面影响的文章可能会引起体育爱好者的兴趣； 它可能不会吸引不喜欢运动的人。

college-writing-008025.en: In addition, make your main point clear so that your audience can follow the cause-and-effect relationship.
college-writing-008025.zh: 此外，明确你的主要观点，以便你的受众能够遵循因果关系。

college-writing-008026.en: You might even announce specific causes or effects by signaling them to readers: “One effect steroid use has on athletes is to . . .”
college-writing-008026.zh: 你甚至可以通过向读者发出信号来宣布具体的原因或影响：“使用类固醇对运动员的一种影响是……”

college-writing-008027.en: Development through Prewriting The best essays are often those written about a topic that the author genuinely cares about.
college-writing-008027.zh: 通过预写最好的论文的发展通常是关于作者真正关心的主题的文章。

college-writing-008028.en: When Scarlett, the author of “The Joys of an Old Car,” was assigned an essay with emphasis on cause and/or effect, she welcomed the assignment.
college-writing-008028.zh: 当《老车的欢乐》的作者斯嘉丽被分配了一篇强调因果和/或效果的论文时，她对这项任务表示欢迎。

college-writing-008029.en: She explains, “My husband and I believe in enjoying what we have and living simply, rather than ‘keeping up with the Joneses.’ Our beat-up old car is an example of that way of life. People often say to me, ‘Surely you could buy a nicer car!’ I enjoy explaining to them why we keep our old ‘clunker.’ So when I heard ‘essay that emphasizes cause and/ or effect,’ I immediately thought of the car as a topic. Writing this essay was just an extension of a conversation I’ve had many times.”
college-writing-008029.zh: 她解释说：“我和我的丈夫相信享受我们所拥有的生活和简单的生活，而不是‘跟上琼斯’。我们破旧的旧车就是这种生活方式的一个例子。人们经常对我说，‘你肯定能买到更好的车！’我喜欢向他们解释为什么 “我们保留了旧的‘Clunker’。所以当我听到“强调因果和/或效果的文章”时，我立即将汽车视为一个主题。写这篇文章只是我多次对话的延伸。”

college-writing-008030.zh: 294 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-008031.en: When Scarlett reviewed her list, she saw that the items fell into three major categories.
college-writing-008031.zh: 当斯嘉丽审查她的清单时，她看到这些物品分为三大类。

college-writing-008032.en: They were (1) the car’s economy; (2) its familiarity; and (3) its dependability.
college-writing-008032.zh: 它们是 (1) 汽车的经济性； (2) 熟悉； (3) 其可靠性。

college-writing-008033.en: She went back and noted which category each of the items best fit.
college-writing-008033.zh: 她回去指出每个项目最适合哪个类别。

college-writing-008034.en: Then she crossed out those items that didn’t seem to belong in any of the categories.
college-writing-008034.zh: 然后她划掉了那些似乎不属于任何类别的项目。

college-writing-008067.en: When people see my beat-up old car, they sometimes laugh at it.
college-writing-008067.zh: 当人们看到我破旧的旧车时，他们有时会嘲笑它。

college-writing-008068.en: But I tell them that owning a twenty-year-old Toyota has its good points.
college-writing-008068.zh: 但我告诉他们，拥有一辆 20 岁的丰田有其优点。

college-writing-008069.zh: 一种明显的回报是经济。

college-writing-008070.en: My husband and I bought the car when we were newly married.
college-writing-008070.zh: 我和我丈夫刚结婚的时候买了这辆车。

college-writing-008071.zh: 我们为此支付了 5,000 美元。

college-writing-008072.en: That seemed like a lot of money then, but today we’d spend four times that much for a similar car.
college-writing-008072.zh: 那似乎是一大笔钱，但今天我们花了四倍的钱买一辆类似的汽车。

college-writing-008073.en: We also save money on insurance.

college-writing-008074.en: In the twenty years we’ve had it, the Toyota has needed only a few major repairs.
college-writing-008074.zh: 在我们拥有它的 20 年里，丰田汽车只需要进行几次大修。

college-writing-008075.en: It even gets good gas mileage.
college-writing-008075.zh: 它甚至获得良好的油耗。

college-writing-008076.en: I like the familiar feel of the car.
college-writing-008076.zh: 我喜欢这辆车熟悉的感觉。

college-writing-008077.en: I’m so used to it that driving anything else feels very strange.
college-writing-008077.zh: 我已经习惯了，驾驶其他任何东西都感觉很奇怪。

college-writing-008078.en: When I visited my sister recently, I drove her new Prius to the grocery store.
college-writing-008078.zh: 当我最近拜访我姐姐时，我开车送她的新普锐斯去杂货店。

college-writing-008080.en: I couldn’t even figure out how to turn on the radio.
college-writing-008080.zh: 我什至不知道如何打开收音机。

college-writing-008081.en: I was relieved to get back to my own car.
college-writing-008081.zh: 回到自己的车上，我松了一口气。

college-writing-008082.en: Finally, my car is very dependable.

college-writing-008083.en: No matter how cold and snowy it is, I know the Toyota will start quickly and get me where I need to go.
college-writing-008083.zh: 不管多冷多雪，我知道丰田会很快开始，把我带到我需要去的地方。

college-writing-008084.en: Unfortunately, one day it didn’t start, and naturally that day I had a final exam.
college-writing-008084.zh: 不幸的是，有一天它没有开始，那天我自然有期末考试。

college-writing-008085.en: But otherwise it just keeps on going and going.
college-writing-008085.zh: 但除此之外，它只会继续前进。

college-writing-008086.en: My Toyota reminds me of a favorite piece of clothing that you wear forever and can’t bear to throw away.
college-writing-008086.zh: 我的丰田让我想起了你永远穿的最喜欢的一件衣服，不能忍受扔掉。

college-writing-008087.en: Now Scarlett had three main points and several items to support each point.
college-writing-008087.zh: 现在斯嘉丽有三个要点和几个项目来支持每个点。

college-writing-008148.en: By evening the ice melted to water for washing.

college-writing-008149.en: I got sick a lot that winter because the fire would go out at night before the clothes were dry.
college-writing-008149.zh: 那年冬天我生病了很多，因为晚上衣服干了，火就会熄灭。

college-writing-008150.en: In the morning I’d put them on, wet or dry, because they were the only clothes I had.
college-writing-008150.zh: 早上我会穿上它们，无论是干湿的还是干的，因为它们是我唯一的衣服。

college-writing-008151.en: Everybody’s got a Helene Tucker, a symbol of everything you want.
college-writing-008151.zh: 每个人都有一个 Helene Tucker，一个你想要的一切的象征。

college-writing-008152.en: I loved her for her goodness, her cleanness, her popularity.
college-writing-008152.zh: 我爱她，因为她的善良，她的清洁，她的人气。

college-writing-008153.en: She’d walk down my street and my brothers and sisters would yell, “Here comes Helene,” and I’d rub my tennis sneakers on the back of my pants and wish my hair wasn’t so nappy and the white folks’ shirt fit me better.
college-writing-008153.zh: 她会走在我的街上，我的兄弟姐妹们会大喊：“海伦来了，”我会在裤子后面擦我的网球运动鞋，希望我的头发不要那么尿布，白人的衬衫更适合我。

college-writing-008154.en: I’d run out on the street.

college-writing-008155.en: If I knew my place and didn’t come too close, she’d wink at me and say hello.
college-writing-008155.zh: 如果我知道我的位置并且没有靠得太近，她会对我眨眼并打招呼。

college-writing-008157.en: Sometimes I’d follow her all the way home, and shovel the snow off her walk and try to make friends with her Momma and her aunts.
college-writing-008157.zh: 有时我会一直跟着她回家，把她走路上的雪铲掉，试着和她妈妈和阿姨们交朋友。

college-writing-008158.en: I’d drop money on her stoop late at night on my way back from shining shoes in the taverns.
college-writing-008158.zh: 在我深夜从小酒馆里闪亮的鞋子回来的路上，我会把钱放在她的门廊上。

college-writing-008159.en: And she had a Daddy, and he had a good job.
college-writing-008159.zh: 她有一个爸爸，他的工作很好。

college-writing-008161.en: I guess I would have gotten over Helene by summertime, but something happened in that classroom that made her face hang in front of me for the next twenty-two years.
college-writing-008161.zh: 我想我会在夏天之前克服海伦的，但在接下来的二十二年里，那个教室里发生了一些事情，让她的脸挂在我面前。

college-writing-008162.en: When I played the drums in high school it was for Helene and when I broke track records in college it was for Helene and when I started standing behind microphones and heard applause I wished Helene could hear it, too.
college-writing-008162.zh: 当我在高中打鼓时，那是为了海伦，当我在大学里打破记录时，是为了海伦，当我开始站在麦克风后面听到掌声时，我希望海伦也能听到。

college-writing-008163.en: It wasn’t until I was twenty-nine years old and married and making money that I finally got her out of my system.
college-writing-008163.zh: 直到我 29 岁结婚并赚钱，我才终于把她从我的系统中解救出来。

college-writing-008164.en: Helene was sitting in that classroom when I learned to be ashamed of myself.
college-writing-008164.zh: 当我学会为自己感到羞耻时，海伦正坐在那间教室里。

college-writing-008166.en: I was sitting in the back of the room, in a seat with a chalk circle drawn around it.
college-writing-008166.zh: 我坐在房间的后面，在一个座位上画着一个粉笔圆圈。

college-writing-008167.en: The idiot’s seat, the troublemaker’s seat.
college-writing-008167.zh: 白痴的座位，麻烦制造者的座位。

college-writing-008168.en: The teacher thought I was stupid.

college-writing-008169.en: Couldn’t spell, couldn’t read, couldn’t do arithmetic.
college-writing-008169.zh: 不会拼写，不能阅读，不能做算术。

college-writing-008171.en: Teachers were never interested in finding out that you couldn’t
college-writing-008171.zh: 老师从来没有兴趣发现你不能

college-writing-008172.zh: 298 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-008173.en: concentrate because you were so hungry, because you hadn’t had any breakfast.
college-writing-008173.zh: 集中注意力，因为你太饿了，因为你没有吃任何早餐。

college-writing-008174.en: All you could think about was noontime, would it ever come?
college-writing-008174.zh: 你能想到的只是中午，它会来吗？

college-writing-008175.en: Maybe you could sneak into the cloakroom and steal a bite of some kid’s lunch out of a coat pocket.
college-writing-008175.zh: 也许你可以偷偷溜进衣帽间，从外套口袋里偷一口孩子的午餐。

college-writing-008178.en: You can’t really make a meal of paste, or put it on bread for a sandwich, but sometimes I’d scoop a few spoonfuls out of the big paste jar in the back of the room.
college-writing-008178.zh: 你不能真正做一顿糊状物，或者把它放在面包上做三明治，但有时我会从房间后面的大糊罐里舀出几勺。

college-writing-008179.zh: 怀孕的人有奇怪的味道。

college-writing-008181.en: Pregnant with dirt and pregnant with smells that made people turn away, pregnant with cold and pregnant with shoes that were never bought for me, pregnant with five other people in my bed and no Daddy in the next room, and pregnant with hunger.
college-writing-008181.zh: 怀有污垢，怀着让人转身的气味，怀着寒冷，怀孕的鞋子，我的床上有另外五个人，隔壁房间里没有爸爸，怀着饥饿感。

college-writing-008182.en: Paste doesn’t taste too bad when you’re hungry.
college-writing-008182.zh: 当你饿的时候，糊状物的味道不会太糟糕。

college-writing-008183.en: The teacher thought I was a troublemaker.
college-writing-008183.zh: 老师以为我是个麻烦制造者。

college-writing-008184.en: All she saw from the front of the room was a little black boy who squirmed in his idiot’s seat and made noises and poked the kids around him.
college-writing-008184.zh: 她从房间前面看到的只是一个黑人小男孩，他在白痴的座位上蠕动着，发出声音，并戳了戳他周围的孩子。

college-writing-008185.en: I guess she couldn’t see a kid who made noises because he wanted someone to know he was there.
college-writing-008185.zh: 我猜她看不到一个发出声音的孩子，因为他想让别人知道他在那里。

college-writing-008186.en: It was on a Thursday, the day before the Negro payday.
college-writing-008186.zh: 那是在黑人发薪日的前一天的星期四。

college-writing-008187.en: The eagle always flew on Friday.

college-writing-008188.en: The teacher was asking each student how much his father would give to the Community Chest.
college-writing-008188.zh: 老师问每个学生他的父亲会给社区胸部多少钱。

college-writing-008189.en: On Friday night, each kid would get the money from his father, and on Monday he would bring it to the school.
college-writing-008189.zh: 周五晚上，每个孩子都会从父亲那里得到钱，周一他会把钱带到学校。

college-writing-008190.en: I decided I was going to buy a Daddy right then.
college-writing-008190.zh: 我决定那时我要买一个爸爸。

college-writing-008191.en: I had money in my pocket from shining shoes and selling papers, and whatever Helene Tucker pledged for her Daddy I was going to top it.
college-writing-008191.zh: 我的口袋里有钱，来自闪亮的鞋子和卖纸，无论 Helene Tucker 为她爸爸承诺的任何东西，我都会把它放在上面。

college-writing-008192.en: And I’d hand the money right in.

college-writing-008193.en: I wasn’t going to wait until Monday to buy me a Daddy.
college-writing-008193.zh: 我不会等到星期一才给我买爸爸。

college-writing-008194.en: I was shaking, scared to death.

college-writing-008195.en: The teacher opened her book and started calling out names alphabetically.
college-writing-008195.zh: 老师打开她的书，开始按字母顺序叫名字。

college-writing-008196.en: “Helene Tucker?” “My Daddy said he’d give two dollars and fifty cents.” “That’s very nice, Helene. Very, very nice indeed.”
college-writing-008196.zh: “海伦·塔克？” “我爸爸说他会给两美元五十美分。” “这很好，海伦。非常非常好。”

college-writing-008197.en: That made me feel pretty good.

college-writing-008198.en: It wouldn’t take too much to top that.
college-writing-008198.zh: 不需要太多就可以做到这一点。

college-writing-008199.en: I had almost three dollars in dimes and quarters in my pocket.
college-writing-008199.zh: 我的口袋里有将近三美元的硬币和四分之一。

college-writing-008200.en: I stuck my hand in my pocket and held on to the money, waiting for her to call my name.
college-writing-008200.zh: 我把手插在口袋里，拿着钱，等着她叫我的名字。

college-writing-008201.en: But the teacher closed her book after she called everybody else in the class.
college-writing-008201.zh: 但是老师在她打电话给班上的其他人后合上了她的书。

college-writing-008202.en: I stood up and raised my hand.

college-writing-008205.en: “I don’t have time to be playing with you, Richard.” “My Daddy said he’d . . .” “Sit down, Richard, you’re disturbing the class.” “My Daddy said he’d give . . . fifteen dollars.”
college-writing-008205.zh: “我没有时间和你一起玩，理查德。” “我爸说他会……” “坐下，理查德，你打扰了全班同学。” “我爸说他会给……十五美元。”

college-writing-008206.en: She turned around and looked mad.

college-writing-008207.en: “We are collecting this money for you and your kind, Richard Gregory. If your Daddy can give fifteen dollars you have no business being on relief.” “I got it right now, I got it right now, my Daddy gave it to me to turn in today, my Daddy said . . .”
college-writing-008207.zh: “我们正在为你和你的同胞收取这笔钱，理查德·格雷戈里。如果你爸爸能给我十五美元，你就没有办法救济。” “我现在拿到了，我现在就拿到了，我爸爸把它给了我今天上交，我爸爸说……”

college-writing-008208.zh: 第12章 原因和/或影响 299

college-writing-008209.en: “And furthermore,” she said, looking right at me, her nostrils getting big and her lips getting thin and her eyes opening wide, “we know you don’t have a Daddy.”
college-writing-008209.zh: “而且，”她说，看着我，她的鼻孔变大，嘴唇变薄，睁大眼睛，“我们知道你没有爸爸。”

college-writing-008210.en: Helene Tucker turned around, her eyes full of tears.
college-writing-008210.zh: 海伦·塔克转过身来，眼中充满了泪水。

college-writing-008212.en: Then I couldn’t see her too well because I was crying, too.
college-writing-008212.zh: 然后我也不能很好地看到她，因为我也哭了。

college-writing-008214.en: And I always thought the teacher kind of liked me.
college-writing-008214.zh: 我一直认为老师有点喜欢我。

college-writing-008215.en: She always picked me to wash the blackboard on Friday, after school.
college-writing-008215.zh: 她总是在星期五放学后选我洗黑板。

college-writing-008216.en: That was a big thrill; it made me feel important.
college-writing-008216.zh: 那是一个很大的刺激。 这让我觉得很重要。

college-writing-008217.en: If I didn’t wash it, come Monday the school might not function right.
college-writing-008217.zh: 如果我不洗它，周一来学校可能无法正常工作。

college-writing-008219.en: I walked out of school that day, and for a long time I didn’t go back very often.
college-writing-008219.zh: 那天我走出学校，很长一段时间我都没有经常回去。

college-writing-008222.en: It seemed like the whole world had been inside that classroom, everyone had heard what the teacher had said, everyone had turned around and felt sorry for me.
college-writing-008222.zh: 好像全世界都在那个教室里，每个人都听到了老师说的话，每个人都转身，为我感到难过。

college-writing-008223.en: There was shame in going to the Worthy Boys Annual Christmas Dinner for you and your kind, because everybody knew what a worthy boy was.
college-writing-008223.zh: 为你和你的同类参加 Worthy Boys 年度圣诞晚宴是一种耻辱，因为每个人都知道一个有价值的男孩是什么。

college-writing-008224.en: Why couldn’t they just call it the Boys Annual Dinner─why’d they have to give it a name?
college-writing-008224.zh: 为什么他们不能把它叫做男孩年度晚宴——他们为什么要给它起个名字？

college-writing-008225.en: There was shame in wearing the brown and orange and white plaid mackinaw1 the welfare gave to three thousand boys.
college-writing-008225.zh: 穿着福利给三千男孩的棕色和橙色和白色格子 Mackinaw1 是一种耻辱。

college-writing-008226.en: Why’d it have to be the same for everybody so when you walked down the street the people could see you were on relief?
college-writing-008226.zh: 为什么每个人都必须如此，所以当你走在街上时，人们可以看到你正在解脱？

college-writing-008227.en: It was a nice warm mackinaw and it had a hood, and my Momma beat me and called me a little rat when she found out I stuffed it in the bottom of a pail full of garbage way over on Cottage Street.
college-writing-008227.zh: 这是一个温暖的麦基诺，它有一个引擎盖，当她发现我把它塞进了小屋街上一桶装满垃圾的垃圾桶的底部时，我妈妈打了我，叫我一只老鼠。

college-writing-008228.en: There was shame in running over to Mister Ben’s at the end of the day and asking for his rotten peaches, there was shame in asking Mrs. Simmons for a spoonful of sugar, there was shame in running out to meet the relief truck.
college-writing-008228.zh: 一天结束时跑到本先生那里并要他腐烂的桃子是一种耻辱，向西蒙斯夫人要一勺糖是一种耻辱，跑出去迎接救援车是一种耻辱。

college-writing-008229.en: I hated that truck, full of food for you and your kind.
college-writing-008229.zh: 我讨厌那辆卡车，为你和你的同类装满了食物。

college-writing-008230.en: I ran into the house and hid when it came.
college-writing-008230.zh: 我跑进屋子，当它来的时候躲起来了。

college-writing-008231.en: And then I started to sneak through alleys, to take the long way home so the people going into White’s Eat Shop wouldn’t see me.
college-writing-008231.zh: 然后我开始偷偷穿过小巷，带路回家，这样进入怀特餐厅的人就看不到我。

college-writing-008232.en: Yeah, the whole world heard the teacher that day─we all know you don’t have a Daddy.
college-writing-008232.zh: 是的，那天全世界都听到了老师的声音——我们都知道你没有爸爸。

college-writing-008233.en: It lasted for a while, this kind of numbness.
college-writing-008233.zh: 它持续了一段时间，这种麻木。

college-writing-008234.en: I spent a lot of time feeling sorry for myself.
college-writing-008234.zh: 我花了很多时间为自己感到难过。

college-writing-008235.en: And then one day I met this wino in a restaurant.
college-writing-008235.zh: 然后有一天，我在一家餐厅遇到了这个酒庄。

college-writing-008236.en: I’d been out hustling all day, shining shoes, selling newspapers, and I had googobs of money in my pocket.
college-writing-008236.zh: 我一整天都在外面忙碌，闪闪发光，卖报纸，口袋里有很多钱。

college-writing-008237.en: Bought me a bowl of chili for fifteen cents, and a cheeseburger for fifteen cents, and a Pepsi for five cents, and a piece of chocolate cake for ten cents.
college-writing-008237.zh: 给我买了一碗辣椒 15 美分，一个 15 美分的芝士汉堡，5 美分的百事可乐，一块巧克力蛋糕 10 美分。

college-writing-008239.en: I was eating when this old wino came in.
college-writing-008239.zh: 当这只老酒庄进来时，我正在吃东西。

college-writing-008240.en: I love winos because they never hurt anyone but themselves.
college-writing-008240.zh: 我爱 Winos，因为他们从不伤害任何人，除了他们自己。

college-writing-008241.en: The old wino sat down at the counter and ordered twenty-six cents worth of food.
college-writing-008241.zh: 老维诺在柜台坐下，点了价值二十六美分的食物。

college-writing-008242.en: He ate it like he really enjoyed it.
college-writing-008242.zh: 他吃了它，就像他真的很喜欢它一样。

college-writing-008243.en: When the owner, Mister Williams, asked him to pay the check, the old wino didn’t lie or go through his pocket like he suddenly found a hole.
college-writing-008243.zh: 当老板威廉姆斯先生要求他付支票时，老维诺没有撒谎或从口袋里翻出来，就像他突然发现了一个洞一样。

college-writing-008244.en: He just said: “Don’t have no money.”

college-writing-008245.en: The owner yelled: “Why in hell did you come in here and eat my food if you don’t have no money? That food cost me money.”
college-writing-008245.zh: 店主大喊：“你到底为什么没有钱，你来这里吃我的食物，那食物要花钱。”

college-writing-008246.en: 1mackinaw: a short, heavy woolen coat, usually plaid and double-breasted.
college-writing-008246.zh: 1Mackinaw：一件短而厚的羊毛外套，通常格子和双排扣。

college-writing-008247.zh: 300 第二部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-008248.en: Mister Williams jumped over the counter and knocked the wino off his stool and beat him over the head with a pop bottle.
college-writing-008248.zh: 威廉姆斯先生跳过柜台，将酒野从他的凳子上敲下来，用一个流行瓶子打了他的头。

college-writing-008249.en: Then he stepped back and watched the wino bleed.
college-writing-008249.zh: 然后他退后一步，看着 Wino 流血。

college-writing-008252.en: I looked at the wino with blood all over his face and I went over.
college-writing-008252.zh: 我看着他脸上全是鲜血的wino，我走了过去。

college-writing-008253.en: “Leave him alone, Mister Williams. I’ll pay the twenty-six cents.”
college-writing-008253.zh: “别管他，威廉姆斯先生。我要付二十六美分。”

college-writing-008254.en: The wino got up, slowly, pulling himself up to the stool, then up to the counter, holding on for a minute until his legs stopped shaking so bad.
college-writing-008254.zh: Wino 慢慢地站了起来，慢慢地把自己拉到凳子上，然后站到柜台上，坚持了一分钟，直到他的腿停止了剧烈摇晃。

college-writing-008255.en: He looked at me with pure hate.
college-writing-008255.zh: 他带着纯粹的仇恨看着我。

college-writing-008256.en: “Keep your twenty-six cents. You don’t have to pay, not now. I just finished paying for it.”
college-writing-008256.zh: “保持你的二十六美分。你不用付钱，不是现在。我刚付完钱。”

college-writing-008257.en: He started to walk out, and as he passed me, he reached down and touched my shoulder.
college-writing-008257.zh: 他开始走出去，当他经过我时，他伸手摸了摸我的肩膀。

college-writing-008258.en: “Thanks, sonny, but it’s too late now. Why didn’t you pay it before?”
college-writing-008258.zh: “谢谢，桑尼，但现在已经太晚了。你为什么不付钱？”

college-writing-008259.en: I was pretty sick about that.

college-writing-008260.en: I waited too long to help another man.
college-writing-008260.zh: 我等了太久才帮助另一个人。

college-writing-008262.en: 1. Which of the following statements best represents the main idea of the selection?
college-writing-008262.zh: 1. 以下哪项陈述最能代表选择的主要思想？

college-writing-008263.en: a. Richard felt that being poor was humiliating.
college-writing-008263.zh: 一。 理查德觉得贫穷是羞辱性的。

college-writing-008264.en: b. Helene Tucker was a symbol of everything Richard wanted.
college-writing-008264.zh: B. 海伦·塔克是理查德想要的一切的象征。

college-writing-008265.en: c. Richard had to work hard as a child.
college-writing-008265.zh: c.  理查德小时候必须努力工作。

college-writing-008267.en: 2. What is the topic sentence for paragraph 2?
college-writing-008267.zh: 2. 第 2 段的 主题句 是什么？

college-writing-008270.en: 3. In paragraphs 1 and 2, Gregory mentions several steps he took to impress
college-writing-008270.zh: 3. 在第 1 段和第 2 段中，格雷戈里提到了他为给人留下深刻印象的几个步骤

college-writing-008273.en: 4. This essay is about Gregory’s experience growing up.
college-writing-008273.zh: 4. 这篇文章是关于格雷戈里成长的经历。

college-writing-008274.en: What is the main effect he

college-writing-008276.en: What are some of the causes?

college-writing-008277.en: The main effect The main cause
college-writing-008277.zh: 主要影响 主要原因

college-writing-008280.zh: 第12章 原因和/或影响 301

college-writing-008281.en: 5. In paragraphs 5 and 6, Gregory explains his teacher thought he was stupid and
college-writing-008281.zh: 5. 在第 5 段和第 6 段中，格雷戈里解释说他的老师认为他很愚蠢，而且

college-writing-008282.en: a troublemaker because he couldn’t read, spell, or do arithmetic, would squirm in his seat, and sometimes ate paste.
college-writing-008282.zh: 一个麻烦制造者，因为他不会阅读、拼写或做算术，会在座位上蠕动，有时会吃糊状物。

college-writing-008291.zh: 8. 格雷戈里在第 28 段中使用了多少次羞耻这个词？
