college-writing-008300.zh: 10. 在文章的结尾，格雷戈里将注意力从教室转移到涉及餐厅“wino”的场景。

college-writing-008301.en: What is the connection between this closing scene and the rest of the essay?
college-writing-008301.zh: 这个结束场景和文章的其余部分有什么联系？

college-writing-008302.zh: 第302章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008304.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Cause and/or Effect
college-writing-008304.zh: 写一篇强调因果和/或效果的论文

college-writing-008305.en: Are you as good a writer as you want to be?
college-writing-008305.zh: 你是你想成为的好作家吗？

college-writing-008306.en: Write an essay analyzing the reasons you have become a good writer or explaining why you are not as good as you’d like to be.
college-writing-008306.zh: 写一篇文章，分析你成为一名优秀作家的原因，或者解释你为什么不如你想成为的那么好。

college-writing-008307.en: Begin by considering some factors that may have influenced your writing ability.
college-writing-008307.zh: 首先考虑一些可能影响您写作能力的因素。

college-writing-008308.en: Your family background: Did you see people writing at home?
college-writing-008308.zh: 你的家庭背景：你看到人们在家写作吗？

college-writing-008309.en: What were the attitudes toward writing in your home?
college-writing-008309.zh: 在家里写作的态度是什么？

college-writing-008310.en: Your school experience: Did you have good writing teachers?
college-writing-008310.zh: 你的学校经历：你有优秀的写作老师吗？

college-writing-008311.en: Did you have a history of failure or success with writing?
college-writing-008311.zh: 你有过失败或写作成功的历史吗？

college-writing-008312.en: Was writing fun, or was it a chore?
college-writing-008312.zh: 写作很有趣，还是一件苦差事？

college-writing-008314.en: Social influences: What were your friends’ attitudes toward writing?
college-writing-008314.zh: 社会影响：你朋友对写作的态度是什么？

college-writing-008315.en: What feelings about writing did you pick up from your friends?
college-writing-008315.zh: 你从朋友那里得到了什么对写作的感受？

college-writing-008321.zh: 第12章 原因和/或影响 303

college-writing-008322.en: You might want to organize your essay by describing the three greatest influences on your skill (or your lack of skill) as a writer.
college-writing-008322.zh: 您可能希望通过描述对您作为作家的技能（或您缺乏技能）的三个最大影响来组织您的论文。

college-writing-008323.en: Show how each of these has contributed to the present state of your writing.
college-writing-008323.zh: 展示每一个都对你写作的当前状态做出了贡献。

college-writing-008324.en: You will want to check Chapter 16, “Argument,” to help create a persuasive and effective essay.
college-writing-008324.zh: 您将需要查看第 16 章“论点”，以帮助撰写有说服力且有效的论文。

college-writing-008327.en: Choose a prewriting technique that works for you, and for ten minutes use that
college-writing-008327.zh: 选择适合您的预写技术，并在十分钟内使用它

college-writing-008329.en: Don’t worry about spelling, grammar, organization, or anything other than getting your thoughts down on the page.
college-writing-008329.zh: 除了将您的想法放在页面上之外，不要担心拼写、语法、组织或其他任何事情。

college-writing-008330.en: If ideas are still flowing at the end of ten minutes, keep on writing.
college-writing-008330.zh: 如果想法在十分钟结束时仍在流动，请继续写作。

college-writing-008331.en: Once you have finished getting your thoughts down, you should have a base of raw material that you can draw on in the next phase of your work.
college-writing-008331.zh: 一旦你完成了你的想法，你应该有一个可以在下一阶段工作的原材料基础。

college-writing-008332.en: Judging from what you have produced, do you think you have enough material to support your essay?
college-writing-008332.zh: 从你制作的内容来看，你认为你有足够的材料来支持你的论文吗？

college-writing-008333.en: If so, keep following the steps below.
college-writing-008333.zh: 如果是这样，请继续遵循以下步骤。

college-writing-008334.en: If not, plan to spend at least another ten minutes generating additional ideas.
college-writing-008334.zh: 如果没有，计划至少再花十分钟来产生额外的想法。

college-writing-008336.en: Develop a single clear sentence that will serve as your thesis.
college-writing-008336.zh: 制定一个明确的句子，作为你的论文。

college-writing-008338.en: demonstrate how you feel about your writing and why.
college-writing-008338.zh: 展示您对写作的感受以及原因。

college-writing-008340.en: Decide whether you will support each of your main points with short examples
college-writing-008340.zh: 用简短的例子决定你是否支持你的每个要点

college-writing-008343.en: Write a first draft of an introduction that attracts the reader’s interest, states
college-writing-008343.zh: 写出引人入胜的引言的初稿，指出

college-writing-008344.en: your thesis, and presents a plan of development.
college-writing-008344.zh: 你的论文，并提出了 展开提纲。

college-writing-008345.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while (if possible).
college-writing-008345.zh: 修改 完成论文初稿后，将其放在一边（如果可能）。

college-writing-008346.en: Then read it aloud to a friend or classmate.
college-writing-008346.zh: 然后大声朗读给朋友或同学。

college-writing-008347.en: As you listen to your words, you should keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-008347.zh: 当你听你的话时，你应该牢记本章末尾的四个基础清单中的问题。

college-writing-008348.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-008348.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-008349.en: Write an essay in which you advance an idea about a poem, story, play, film, literary essay, or novel.
college-writing-008349.zh: 写一篇文章，在其中推进关于诗歌、故事、戏剧、电影、文学论文或小说的想法。

college-writing-008350.en: The work you choose may be assigned by your instructor or may require your instructor’s approval.
college-writing-008350.zh: 您选择的工作可能由您的教师分配，或者可能需要您的教师的批准。

college-writing-008351.en: To develop your idea, use a series of two or more reasons and specific evidence for each reason.
college-writing-008351.zh: 为了发展您的想法，请针对每个原因使用一系列两个或多个原因和具体证据。

college-writing-008352.en: You may want to check Chapter 8, “Description,” Chapter 18, “Summarizing and Paraphrasing,” and Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay,” to properly present and cite your information.
college-writing-008352.zh: 您可能需要查看第 8 章“描述”、第 18 章“总结和释义”和第 20 章“撰写研究论文”，以正确呈现和引用您的信息。

college-writing-008448.en: OPTION 1 Assume that there has been a series of large cuts in your school district’s budget.
college-writing-008448.zh: 选项 1 假设您学区的预算出现了一系列大幅削减。

college-writing-008449.en: What might be the causes of the cuts?
college-writing-008449.zh: 削减的原因可能是什么？

college-writing-008450.en: Where are the cuts mostly taking place?

college-writing-008451.en: Spend some time thinking about possible causes.
college-writing-008451.zh: 花一些时间思考可能的原因。

college-writing-008452.en: Then, as a principal or superintendent, write a letter to the families in your school district explaining the causes of the cuts and the decisions behind what areas were affected.
college-writing-008452.zh: 然后，作为校长或主管，给您学区的家庭写一封信，解释削减的原因以及哪些地区受到影响的决定。

college-writing-008453.en: Your purpose is to provide information to the families so they understand the resulting cuts.
college-writing-008453.zh: 您的目的是向家庭提供信息，以便他们了解由此产生的削减。

college-writing-008454.en: OPTION 2 Alternatively, think about how severe school district budget cuts would have an impact on your family.
college-writing-008454.zh: 选项 2 或者，想想学区的预算削减会对您的家庭产生多大的影响。

college-writing-008455.en: Write a letter to the principal or superintendent explaining how you see the consequences of the budget cuts affecting your family and the community at large.
college-writing-008455.zh: 写信给校长或主管，解释您如何看待预算削减影响您的家庭和整个社区的后果。

college-writing-008456.en: Your purpose is to provide administrators with useful information that may be used to persuade the school board to rethink where the budget has been cut.
college-writing-008456.zh: 您的目的是为管理员提供有用的信息，这些信息可用于说服学校董事会重新考虑预算已被削减的地方。

college-writing-008466.en: Cause and/or Effect Checklist: THE FOUR BASES
college-writing-008466.zh: 原因和/或影响清单：四个基础

college-writing-008468.en: Do I have a thesis that is narrow and focused, and contains a claim about the causes and/or effects of my topic?
college-writing-008468.zh: 我的论文是否狭隘而集中，并包含对我的主题的原因和/或影响的主张？

college-writing-008469.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-008469.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-008471.en: Have I backed up each main point with one extended example or several shorter examples?
college-writing-008471.zh: 我是否用一个扩展示例或几个较短的示例备份了每个要点？

college-writing-008472.en: Do my examples clearly support the cause, the effect, or both?
college-writing-008472.zh: 我的例子是否清楚地支持原因、结果或两者兼而有之？

college-writing-008473.en: Are there any repetitive areas that need to be revised?
college-writing-008473.zh: 是否有需要修改的重复领域？

college-writing-008475.en: Have I organized my essay in a manner that clearly expresses whether this is a cause, an effect, or both?
college-writing-008475.zh: 我是否以清晰表达这是原因、结果或两者兼而有之的方式组织了我的论文？

college-writing-008476.en: Do I have a concluding paragraph that effectively supports and completes my essay?
college-writing-008476.zh: 我是否有一个有效支持和完成我的论文的结论段落？

college-writing-008478.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-008478.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-008479.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-008479.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-008480.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-008480.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-008482.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-008482.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-008483.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on comparison and/or contrast • write an essay with emphasis on comparison and/or contrast • revise an essay with emphasis on comparison and/or contrast
college-writing-008483.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写一篇强调比较和/或对比的文章 • 撰写一篇强调比较和/或对比的论文 • 修改文章，重点是比较和/或对比

college-writing-008484.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize comparison and/or contrast • one professional model essay that emphasizes comparison and/or contrast
college-writing-008484.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调比较和/或对比的学生论文 • 一篇强调比较和/或对比的专业模型论文

college-writing-008486.en: Looking at the two photographs above, write an essay in which you compare or contrast in-person classes with online learning.
college-writing-008486.zh: 看着上面的两张照片，写一篇文章，将你的课程与在线学习进行比较或对比。

college-writing-008488.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-008489.zh: 托马斯·伊莫/阿拉米 库存照片

college-writing-008495.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 309

college-writing-008497.en: An essay that emphasizes comparison and/or contrast calls for one of two types of development.
college-writing-008497.zh: 一篇强调比较和/或对比的文章需要两种类型的发展之一。

college-writing-008498.en: Details can be presented one side at a time or point by point.
college-writing-008498.zh: 细节可以在时间或点一侧呈现。

college-writing-008500.en: One Side at a Time Look at the following supporting paragraph from “A Vote for McDonald’s,” one of the model essays that will follow.
college-writing-008500.zh: 一方面，一次看“投票给麦当劳”的以下支持段落，这是将随之而来的示范论文之一。

college-writing-008501.en: Comparison and contrast are two thought processes we go through constantly in everyday life.
college-writing-008501.zh: 比较和对比是我们在日常生活中不断经历的两个思维过程。

college-writing-008502.en: When we compare two things, we show how they are similar; when we contrast two things, we show how they are different.
college-writing-008502.zh: 当我们比较两件事时，我们展示了它们的相似之处； 当我们对比两件事时，我们会展示它们是如何不同的。

college-writing-008503.en: We may compare or contrast two brand-name products (for example, Pepsi and Coca-Cola), two television shows, two cars, two teachers, two jobs, two friends, or two possible solutions to a problem we are facing.
college-writing-008503.zh: 我们可能会比较或对比两种品牌产品（例如百事可乐和可口可乐）、两个电视节目、两辆汽车、两辆汽车、两名教师、两份工作、两名朋友，或者解决我们面临的问题的两种可能的解决方案。

college-writing-008504.en: The purpose of comparing or contrasting is to understand each of the two things more clearly and, at times, to make judgments about them.
college-writing-008504.zh: 比较或对比的目的是更清楚地理解这两件事中的每一个，有时，对它们做出判断。

college-writing-008505.en: You will be asked in this chapter to write an essay that emphasizes comparison and/or contrast.
college-writing-008505.zh: 本章要求您写一篇强调比较和/或对比的文章。

college-writing-008506.en: To prepare for this assignment, first read about the two methods of development you can use in writing your essay.
college-writing-008506.zh: 为了准备这项作业，首先了解您可以在撰写论文时使用的两种发展方法。

college-writing-008507.en: Then read the first student essay; the student literary analysis essay; and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-008507.zh: 然后阅读第一篇学生论文； 学生文学分析论文； 以及随之而来的模型论文，并解决了随笔附带的问题。

college-writing-008508.en: For one thing, going to the Chalet is more difficult than going to McDonald’s.
college-writing-008508.zh: 一方面，去小木屋比去麦当劳更难。

college-writing-008509.en: The Chalet has a jacket-and-tie rule, which means I have to dig a sport coat and tie out of the back of my closet, make sure they’re semiclean, and try to steam out the wrinkles somehow.
college-writing-008509.zh: 小木屋有一个夹克和领带规则，这意味着我必须从壁橱后面挖出运动外套并系好，确保它们是半洁净的，并尝试以某种方式消除皱纹。

college-writing-008511.en: Since it is downtown, I have to leave an hour early to give myself time to find a parking space within six blocks of the restaurant.
college-writing-008511.zh: 由于是市中心，我必须提前一个小时离开，让自己有时间在餐厅的六个街区内找到一个停车位。

college-writing-008512.en: The Chalet cancels reservations if a party is more than ten minutes late.
college-writing-008512.zh: 如果聚会延迟超过十分钟，小木屋将取消预订。

college-writing-008513.en: Going to McDonald’s, on the other hand, is easy.
college-writing-008513.zh: 另一方面，去麦当劳很容易。

college-writing-008514.en: I can feel comfortable wearing my jeans or warm-up suit.
college-writing-008514.zh: 穿上牛仔裤或热身西装，我可以感到舒适。

college-writing-008515.en: I don’t have to do any advance planning.
college-writing-008515.zh: 我不必做任何提前计划。

college-writing-008516.en: I can leave my house whenever I’m ready and pull into a doorside parking space within fifteen minutes.
college-writing-008516.zh: 我可以随时离开我的房子，并在十五分钟内把车停在门边的停车位。

college-writing-008517.zh: 310 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-008518.en: The first half of this paragraph fully explains one side of the contrast (the difficulty of going to the Chalet).
college-writing-008518.zh: 本段的前半部分完全解释了对比的一侧（去小木屋的困难）。

college-writing-008519.en: The second half of the paragraph deals entirely with the other side (the ease of going to McDonald’s).
college-writing-008519.zh: 本段的后半部分完全涉及另一方（去麦当劳的便利性）。

college-writing-008520.en: When you use this method, be sure to follow the same order of points of contrast (or comparison) for each side.
college-writing-008520.zh: 当您使用此方法时，请务必遵循相同的对比点（或比较）的每一侧。

college-writing-008521.en: An outline of the paragraph shows how the points for each side are developed in a consistent sequence.
college-writing-008521.zh: 该段落的大纲显示了如何以一致的顺序发展每一侧的点。

college-writing-008522.en: Point by Point Now look at the supporting paragraph below, which is taken from a student literary analysis essay you will read, “The Lone Ranger and Tonto Fistfight with Smoke Signals”:
college-writing-008522.zh: 现在逐点查看下面的支持段落，该段落来自您将阅读的学生文学分析文章，“独行侠和 Tonto Fist Fight with Smoke Signals”：

college-writing-008523.en: Outline One Side at a Time

college-writing-008524.en: Thesis: Going to the Chalet is more difficult than going to McDonald’s.
college-writing-008524.zh: 论文：去小木屋比去麦当劳更难。

college-writing-008540.en: Leave only fifteen minutes ahead of time

college-writing-008543.en: The book and film both illustrate how desperately Victor desires his father’s love.
college-writing-008543.zh: 这本书和电影都说明了维克多渴望父亲的爱。

college-writing-008544.en: Smoke Signals shows this desire only through Victor’s eyes, whereas The Lone Ranger and Tonto Fistfight in Heaven uses the collective stories and emotions of the residents on the reservation to show that Victor’s desires are shared by many.
college-writing-008544.zh: 烟雾信号只有通过维克多的眼睛才能表现出这种愿望，而独行侠和天堂中的通托斗殴则使用保留地上居民的集体故事和情感来表明维克多的愿望被许多人分享。

college-writing-008545.en: In “Because My Father Always Said He Was the Only Indian Who Saw Jimi Hendrix Play ‘The Star Spangled Banner’ at Woodstock,” the reader sees Victor’s pain and longing as he sits at his drunken father’s feet while listening to Hendrix.
college-writing-008545.zh: 在“因为我父亲总是说他是唯一一个在伍德斯托克看到吉米·亨德里克斯（Jimi Hendrix）在伍德斯托克（Woodstock）演奏‘星条旗’的印度人时，他看到了维克多坐在醉醺醺的父亲的脚边听亨德里克斯的痛苦和渴望。

college-writing-008547.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 311

college-writing-008549.en: Thesis: Through Victor’s story, the reader and the viewer are introduced to complex
college-writing-008549.zh: 论文：通过维克多的故事，读者和观众被介绍给复杂

college-writing-008550.en: situations and emotions experienced by American Indians, but the book conveys a more
college-writing-008550.zh: 美洲印第安人经历的情况和情绪，但这本书传达了更多

college-writing-008552.en: 1. Victor’s desire for his father’s love

college-writing-008557.en: 2. Victor’s journey from child to adult
college-writing-008557.zh: 2. 维克多从儿童到成人的旅程

college-writing-008564.en: In “A Train Is an Order of Occurrence Designed to Lead to Some Result,” the reader’s emotions are once again tugged as Samuel, isolated and distanced from his children, lies down in front of an oncoming train.
college-writing-008564.zh: 在“火车是旨在导致某种结果的发生顺序”中，读者的情绪再次被拉扯，因为塞缪尔与他的孩子们隔绝和疏远，躺在迎面而来的火车前。

college-writing-008565.en: These incidents demonstrate that the father-son connection is not just Victor’s problem, but a reservation problem.
college-writing-008565.zh: 这些事件表明，父子的联系不仅仅是维克多的问题，而是一个保留问题。

college-writing-008566.en: Like most of the book’s characters, Victor doesn’t have a moment of enlightenment, a true happy ending.
college-writing-008566.zh: 像这本书的大多数角色一样，维克多没有启蒙的时刻，一个真正幸福的结局。

college-writing-008567.en: Instead, he continues to fumble through a series of good and bad moments, much as might happen in real life.
college-writing-008567.zh: 相反，他继续在一系列好的和坏的时刻摸索，就像现实生活中可能发生的那样。

college-writing-008568.en: In contrast, the film focuses only on Victor’s path to enlightenment from broken-hearted angry boy needing his father to a healed mature adult.
college-writing-008568.zh: 相比之下，这部电影只关注维克多的启蒙之路，从心碎的愤怒男孩需要他的父亲到一个痊愈的成熟成年人。

college-writing-008569.en: With the help of the humorous Thomas, Victor travels to Phoenix to claim his father’s belongings.
college-writing-008569.zh: 在幽默的托马斯的帮助下，维克多前往凤凰城领取他父亲的财物。

college-writing-008570.en: After Victor is given his father’s ashes, he realizes the anger he has clung to so tightly for fifteen years has been self-defeating.
college-writing-008570.zh: 在维克多得到父亲的骨灰后，他意识到十五年来他如此紧紧地抓住的愤怒一直是弄巧成拙。

college-writing-008571.en: He lets the anger go and experiences a rebirth.
college-writing-008571.zh: 他让愤怒消失，经历了重生。

college-writing-008572.en: The Victor that returns to the reservation is a new person and a man.
college-writing-008572.zh: 回到保留地的胜利者是一个新人和一个男人。

college-writing-008573.en: The paragraph contrasts a short story collection and a film point by point.
college-writing-008573.zh: 该段落逐点对比短篇小说集和电影。

college-writing-008574.en: The following outline illustrates the point-by-point method.
college-writing-008574.zh: 下面的大纲说明了逐点方法。

college-writing-008575.en: When you begin writing an essay that emphasizes comparison and/or contrast, you should decide right away which format you will use: one side at a time or point by point.
college-writing-008575.zh: 当你开始写一篇强调比较和/或对比的文章时，你应该立即决定你将使用哪种格式：一次或一点一点。

college-writing-008576.en: Use that format as you create the outline for your paper.
college-writing-008576.zh: 在为纸张创建大纲时使用该格式。

college-writing-008577.en: Remember that an outline is an essential step in planning and writing a clearly organized paper.
college-writing-008577.zh: 请记住，大纲是规划和撰写组织清晰的论文的重要步骤。

college-writing-008578.zh: 第312章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008581.en: For my birthday this month, my wife has offered to treat me to dinner at the restaurant of my choice.
college-writing-008581.zh: 这个月我的生日，我的妻子提出请我去我选择的餐厅吃晚饭。

college-writing-008582.en: I think she expects me to ask for a meal at the Chalet, the classiest, most expensive restaurant in town.
college-writing-008582.zh: 我想她希望我在镇上最优雅、最昂贵的餐厅 The Chalet 要求一顿饭。

college-writing-008583.en: However, I’m going to eat my birthday dinner at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008583.zh: 然而，我要去麦当劳吃生日晚餐。

college-writing-008584.en: When I compare the two restaurants, the advantages of eating at McDonald’s are clear.
college-writing-008584.zh: 与两家餐厅相比，在麦当劳用餐的优势非常明显。

college-writing-008585.en: For one thing, going to the Chalet is more difficult than going to McDonald’s.
college-writing-008585.zh: 一方面，去小木屋比去麦当劳更难。

college-writing-008586.en: The Chalet has a jacket-and-tie rule, which means I have to dig a sport coat and tie out of the back of my closet, make sure they’re semiclean, and try to steam out the wrinkles somehow.
college-writing-008586.zh: 小木屋有一个夹克和领带规则，这意味着我必须从壁橱后面挖出运动外套并系好，确保它们是半洁净的，并尝试以某种方式消除皱纹。

college-writing-008588.en: Since it is downtown, I have to leave an hour early to give myself time to find a parking space within six blocks of the restaurant.
college-writing-008588.zh: 由于是市中心，我必须提前一个小时离开，让自己有时间在餐厅的六个街区内找到一个停车位。

college-writing-008589.en: The Chalet cancels reservations if a party is more than ten minutes late.
college-writing-008589.zh: 如果聚会延迟超过十分钟，小木屋将取消预订。

college-writing-008590.en: Going to McDonald’s, on the other hand, is easy.
college-writing-008590.zh: 另一方面，去麦当劳很容易。

college-writing-008591.en: I can feel comfortable wearing my jeans or warm-up suit.
college-writing-008591.zh: 穿上牛仔裤或热身西装，我可以感到舒适。

college-writing-008592.en: I don’t have to do any advance planning.
college-writing-008592.zh: 我不必做任何提前计划。

college-writing-008593.en: I can leave my house whenever I’m ready and pull into a doorside parking space within fifteen minutes.
college-writing-008593.zh: 我可以随时离开我的房子，并在十五分钟内把车停在门边的停车位。

college-writing-008594.en: The Chalet is a dimly lit, formal place.
college-writing-008594.zh: 小木屋是一个光线昏暗、正式的地方。

college-writing-008595.en: While I’m struggling to see what’s on my plate, I worry that I’ll knock one of the fragile glasses off the table.
college-writing-008595.zh: 当我在努力看看我盘子里有什么时，我担心我会把一张脆弱的眼镜从桌子上敲下来。

college-writing-008596.en: The waiters at the Chalet can be uncomfortably formal, too.
college-writing-008596.zh: 小木屋的服务员也可能很正式。

college-writing-008597.en: As I awkwardly pronounce the French words on the menu, I get the feeling that I don’t quite live up to their standards.
college-writing-008597.zh: 当我尴尬地说出菜单上的法语单词时，我觉得我不太符合他们的标准。

college-writing-008598.en: Even the other diners can make me feel uncomfortable.
college-writing-008598.zh: 即使是其他食客也会让我感到不舒服。

college-writing-008599.en: And though the food at the Chalet is gourmet, I prefer simpler meals.
college-writing-008599.zh: 虽然小木屋的食物是美食，但我更喜欢简单的饭菜。

college-writing-008600.en: I don’t like unfamiliar food swimming in a pasty white sauce.
college-writing-008600.zh: 我不喜欢在糊状白酱中游泳的不熟悉的食物。

college-writing-008601.en: Eating at the Chalet is, to me, less enjoyable than eating at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008601.zh: 对我来说，在小木屋吃饭比在麦当劳吃饭更不愉快。

college-writing-008602.en: McDonald’s is a pleasant place where I feel at ease.
college-writing-008602.zh: 麦当劳是一个令人愉快的地方，我感到很自在。

college-writing-008603.en: It is well lit, and the bright-colored decor is informal.
college-writing-008603.zh: 它光线充足，色彩鲜艳的装饰是非正式的。

college-writing-008604.en: The employees serve with a smile, and the food is easy to pronounce and identify.
college-writing-008604.zh: 员工面带微笑，食物很容易发音和识别。

college-writing-008605.en: I know what I’m going to get when I order a certain type of sandwich.
college-writing-008605.zh: 当我点了某种类型的三明治时，我知道我会得到什么。

college-writing-008606.en: The most important difference between the Chalet and McDonald’s, though, is price.
college-writing-008606.zh: 不过，Chalet与麦当劳之间最关键的差异在于价格。

college-writing-008607.en: Dinner for two at the Chalet, even without appetizers or desserts, would easily cost $100.
college-writing-008607.zh: 在chalet里享用二人晚餐，即使没有开胃菜和甜点，费用也很容易达到100美元。

college-writing-008608.en: And the $100 doesn’t include the cost of parking the car and tipping the waiter, which can come to an additional $20.
college-writing-008608.zh: 那100美元还不包括停车以及给服务员小费的费用，这些可能还会额外增加20美元。

college-writing-008609.en: Once, I forgot to bring enough money.
college-writing-008609.zh: 有一次，我忘了带足够的钱。

college-writing-008610.en: At McDonald’s, a filling meal for two will cost around $15.
college-writing-008610.zh: 在麦当劳，双人套餐大约需要15美元。

college-writing-008611.en: With the extra $105, my wife and I can eat at McDonald’s seven more times, or go to the movies five times, or buy tickets to a local theater production.
college-writing-008611.zh: 有了那额外的105美元，我和妻子可以再在麦当劳吃七次饭，或者去电影院看五次电影，或者购买当地剧院的演出门票。

college-writing-008612.en: So, for my birthday dinner, or any other time, I prefer to eat at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008612.zh: 所以，对于我的生日晚餐或任何其他时间，我更喜欢在麦当劳吃饭。

college-writing-008613.en: It is convenient, friendly, and cheap.

college-writing-008765.en: Developing a Comparison and/or Contrast Essay Considering Purpose and Audience The purpose of an essay that emphasizes comparison and/or contrast is to make a point by including examples that show how distinct items or people are either similar or different.
college-writing-008765.zh: 考虑目的和受众的比较和/或对比性论文 强调比较和/或对比的文章的目的是通过包含显示不同项目或人如何相似或不同的示例来说明一点。

college-writing-008766.en: Whether you choose to use comparison or contrast depends on the specific point you want to convey to readers.
college-writing-008766.zh: 您是否选择使用比较或对比取决于您要传达给读者的具体点。

college-writing-008767.en: Suppose, for instance, the main point of your essay is that home-cooked hamburgers are superior to fast-food burgers.
college-writing-008767.zh: 例如，假设你的文章的重点是自制汉堡包优于快餐汉堡。

college-writing-008768.en: To convince your audience of your claim, you might contrast the two items, pointing out those differences─price, taste, and nutrition─that make the homemade dish better.
college-writing-008768.zh: 为了让你的观众相信你的主张，你可能会对比这两个项目，指出这些差异——价格、味道和营养——让自制菜肴更好。

college-writing-008769.en: If, however, your main point is that tap water is just as good as store-bought bottled water, you could compare the two, pointing out the similarities that support your main point.
college-writing-008769.zh: 但是，如果您的主要观点是自来水与商店购买的瓶装水一样好，您可以比较两者，指出支持您的主要观点的相似之处。

college-writing-008770.en: Tap water and bottled water, for example, might be equally clean, fresh, and mineral-rich.
college-writing-008770.zh: 例如，自来水和瓶装水可能同样干净、新鲜和富含矿物质。

college-writing-008771.en: In both examples above, comparing or contrasting is used to convince readers of a larger main point.
college-writing-008771.zh: 在上面的两个示例中，比较或对比用于说服读者更大的要点。

college-writing-008772.en: As you think about your own composition, ask yourself what type of essay would benefit from this type of support.
college-writing-008772.zh: 当您考虑自己的作文时，请问自己哪种类型的论文会从这种支持中受益。

college-writing-008773.en: Then determine whether you want to focus on the differences between the items or their similarities.
college-writing-008773.zh: 然后确定是否要专注于项目之间的差异或它们的相似之处。

college-writing-008774.en: You may even decide that you want to do both.
college-writing-008774.zh: 你甚至可以决定你想同时做这两件事。

college-writing-008775.en: If, say, you choose to persuade your readers that they should purchase a specific type of computer, you may include paragraphs on the similarities and differences between Mac and PC computers.
college-writing-008775.zh: 例如，如果您选择说服您的读者他们应该购买特定类型的计算机，您可以包含有关 Mac 和 PC 计算机之间的异同的段落。

college-writing-008776.en: But remember, no matter what topic you select, be sure that your comparison or contrast is connected to a main point that readers can see and understand.
college-writing-008776.zh: 但请记住，无论您选择哪个主题，请确保您的比较或对比与读者可以看到和理解的要点有关。

college-writing-008777.en: Be sure to keep your audience in mind when planning your essay.
college-writing-008777.zh: 在规划论文时，请务必牢记听众。

college-writing-008778.en: If you were writing about Macs and PCs for computer majors, for example, you could assume your readers were familiar with the two systems.
college-writing-008778.zh: 例如，如果您正在为计算机专业编写 Mac 和 PC，您可以假设您的读者熟悉这两个系统。

college-writing-008779.en: On the other hand, if your audience were made up of liberal arts majors, you could not make such an assumption, and it would be up to you to provide background information.
college-writing-008779.zh: 另一方面，如果你的听众是由文科专业组成的，你就不能做出这样的假设，提供背景信息取决于你。

college-writing-008780.en: Thinking about your audience will help you determine the tone of your essay as well.
college-writing-008780.zh: 考虑你的听众也将帮助你确定论文的基调。

college-writing-008781.en: Once again, if you are writing for an audience of programmers, it is appropriate to write in an objective, technical tone.
college-writing-008781.zh: 再一次，如果你是为程序员的观众写作，用客观的技术语气写作是合适的。

college-writing-008782.en: But if you are writing for a more general audience, you should assume a friendly, informal tone.
college-writing-008782.zh: 但是，如果您为更一般的观众写作，您应该假设一种友好、非正式的语气。

college-writing-008783.zh: 第318章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008784.en: The Chalet is a beautiful restaurant and it’s sweet of Lilly to want to take me there.
college-writing-008784.zh: 小木屋是一家美丽的餐厅，想要带我去那里是莉莉的甜蜜。

college-writing-008785.en: But I honestly like McDonald’s better.
college-writing-008785.zh: 但老实说，我更喜欢麦当劳。

college-writing-008786.en: To me, food is food, and a meal at the Chalet is not
college-writing-008786.zh: 对我来说，食物就是食物，而在小屋里吃饭不是

college-writing-008787.en: seven times better than a meal at McDonald’s but that’s what it costs.
college-writing-008787.zh: 比在麦当劳吃饭要好七倍，但这就是它的成本。

college-writing-008789.en: cheeseburger better than something I can’t pronounce or identify.
college-writing-008789.zh: 芝士汉堡比我无法发音或识别的东西更好。

college-writing-008791.en: are snooty and make me feel awkward—how can you enjoy eating when you’re tensed up
college-writing-008791.zh: 傲慢，让我感到尴尬——当你紧张起来时，你怎么能享受吃的乐趣

college-writing-008793.en: Have to wear jacket and tie to the Chalet and I’ve gained weight; not sure jacket
college-writing-008793.zh: 必须在小屋上穿夹克和领带，我的体重增加了； 不确定夹克

college-writing-008795.en: Sweats or jeans are great at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008795.zh: 运动衫或牛仔裤在麦当劳很不错。

college-writing-008796.en: Desserts at Chalet are great, better
college-writing-008796.zh: 小木屋的甜点很棒，更好

college-writing-008797.en: than McCookies or whatever they’re called.
college-writing-008797.zh: 比 McCookies 或任何他们被称为的东西。

college-writing-008798.en: Parking is a hassle at the Chalet and easy at
college-writing-008798.zh: 停车场很麻烦，而且很容易

college-writing-008800.zh: 也不要在 MCD 上小费。

college-writing-008801.en: I don’t know why they keep it so dark at the Chalet—
college-writing-008801.zh: 我不知道为什么他们在小木屋里保持如此黑暗——

college-writing-008802.en: guess it’s supposed to be relaxing, but seems creepy to me.
college-writing-008802.zh: 猜猜它应该是放松的，但对我来说似乎令人毛骨悚然。

college-writing-008804.en: Development through Prewriting When Jesse, one of the student writers featured earlier, had to choose a topic for his essay, the Chalet and McDonald’s quickly came to mind: “My wife and I had been talking that morning about where I wanted to go for my birthday,” he said.
college-writing-008804.zh: 通过预写的发展，当杰西（Jesse），一位早先的学生作家不得不为他的论文选择一个主题时，很快就想到了小木屋和麦当劳：“那天早上我和我的妻子一直在谈论我想去哪里过生日，”他说。

college-writing-008805.en: “I’d been thinking how I would explain to her that I’d really prefer McDonald’s. So the comparisons and contrasts between the two restaurants were fresh in my mind.”
college-writing-008805.zh: “我一直在想我会如何向她解释我真的更喜欢麦当劳。所以这两家餐厅的比较和对比在我看来是新鲜的。”

college-writing-008806.en: To generate ideas for his paper, Jesse turned to the technique of freewriting.
college-writing-008806.zh: 为了为他的论文产生想法，杰西转向了自由写作的技术。

college-writing-008807.en: Without concerning himself with organization, finding the perfect word, or even spelling, he simply wrote whatever came into his mind as he asked himself, Why would I rather eat at McDonald’s than at the Chalet?
college-writing-008807.zh: 他不关心组织，找到完美的词，甚至拼写，他只是在他问自己的时候写下他脑海中的任何东西，我为什么宁愿在麦当劳吃饭而不是在小屋里吃饭？

college-writing-008808.en: Here is what Jesse came up with:

college-writing-008809.en: As Jesse looked over his freewriting, he saw that most of what he had written fell into three categories that he could use as the three supporting points of his essay.
college-writing-008809.zh: 当杰西查看他的自由写作时，他看到他所写的大部分内容都分为三类，他可以将其用作论文的三个支持点。

college-writing-008810.en: Using these three points, he prepared this first scratch outline for the essay:
college-writing-008810.zh: 利用这三点，他为论文准备了第一个草图大纲：

college-writing-008811.en: Would rather eat my special dinner at McDonald’s than at the Chalet
college-writing-008811.zh: 宁愿在麦当劳吃我的特别晚餐，也不愿在木屋里吃

college-writing-008812.en: • can wear anything I want to McD’s
college-writing-008812.zh: • 可以穿任何我想去的 MCD 的东西

college-writing-008813.en: • waiters, lighting, menu at Chalet make me feel awkward
college-writing-008813.zh: • 服务员、灯光、木屋菜单让我感到尴尬

college-writing-008814.en: • Chalet much more expensive than McD’s
college-writing-008814.zh: • 小木屋比 MCD 贵得多

college-writing-008815.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 319

college-writing-008816.en: Would rather eat my special dinner at McDonald’s than at the Chalet
college-writing-008816.zh: 宁愿在麦当劳吃我的特别晚餐，也不愿在木屋里吃

college-writing-008817.en: • Going to the Chalet is a hassle

college-writing-008818.zh: ∘ 必须穿夹克，领带到小木屋

college-writing-008820.zh: ∘ 长途驾驶； 停车问题

college-writing-008821.en: • Waiters, lighting, menu at Chalet make me feel awkward
college-writing-008821.zh: • 服务员、灯光、木屋菜单让我感到尴尬

college-writing-008824.en: ∘ French names on menu don’t mean anything to me
college-writing-008824.zh: ∘ 菜单上的法语名字对我来说没有任何意义

college-writing-008825.en: • Chalet much more expensive than McD’s
college-writing-008825.zh: • 小木屋比 MCD 贵得多

college-writing-008826.en: ∘ meal costs seven times as much

college-writing-008827.en: ∘ parking, tips on top of that

college-writing-008828.en: ∘ rather spend that money on other things
college-writing-008828.zh: ∘ 宁愿把钱花在其他事情上

college-writing-008829.en: Working from this scratch outline, Jesse wrote the following first draft of his essay.
college-writing-008829.zh: 杰西从这个零碎的大纲开始工作，写了他的论文的以下初稿。

college-writing-008830.en: Next, Jesse went back and inserted some supporting details that fit in with his three main points.
college-writing-008830.zh: 接下来，Jesse 回去插入了一些符合他的三个主要点的 支撑细节。

college-writing-008832.en: Lilly has offered to take me anywhere I want for my birthday dinner.
college-writing-008832.zh: 莉莉提出带我去任何我想去的地方吃生日晚餐。

college-writing-008833.en: She thinks I’ll choose the Chalet, but instead I want to eat at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008833.zh: 她认为我会选择小木屋，但我想在麦当劳吃饭。

college-writing-008834.en: The Chalet has a jacket-and-tie rule, and I hate wearing a jacket and tie, and the jacket’s probably too tight for me anyway.
college-writing-008834.zh: 小木屋有夹克和领带的规则，我讨厌穿夹克和领带，而且夹克对我来说可能太紧了。

college-writing-008835.en: I have to dig them out of the closet and get them cleaned.
college-writing-008835.zh: 我必须把它们从壁橱里挖出来，然后把它们清理干净。

college-writing-008836.en: I can wear any old thing to McDonald’s.
college-writing-008836.zh: 我可以穿任何旧的东西去麦当劳。

college-writing-008837.en: We’d also have to leave the house early, since the Chalet requires reservations.
college-writing-008837.zh: 我们还必须早点离开家，因为小木屋需要预订。

college-writing-008838.en: Since it is downtown, I have to leave an hour early so I’m sure to have time to park.
college-writing-008838.zh: 由于是市中心，我必须提前一个小时离开，所以我一定有时间停车。

college-writing-008839.en: The Chalet cancels reservations if a party is more than ten minutes late.
college-writing-008839.zh: 如果聚会延迟超过十分钟，小木屋将取消预订。

college-writing-008843.zh: 第320章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008844.en: to McDonald’s, on the other hand, is easy.
college-writing-008844.zh: 另一方面，对麦当劳来说，这很容易。

college-writing-008845.en: I don’t have to do any advance planning.
college-writing-008845.zh: 我不必做任何提前计划。

college-writing-008846.en: I can leave my house whenever I’m ready.
college-writing-008846.zh: 只要准备好，我就可以离开家。

college-writing-008847.en: McDonald’s is a pleasant place where I feel at ease.
college-writing-008847.zh: 麦当劳是一个令人愉快的地方，我感到很自在。

college-writing-008848.en: It is bright and well lit.

college-writing-008849.en: The employees serve with a smile, and the food is easy to pronounce and identify.
college-writing-008849.zh: 员工面带微笑，食物很容易发音和识别。

college-writing-008850.en: I know what I’m going to get when I order a certain type of sandwich.
college-writing-008850.zh: 当我点了某种类型的三明治时，我知道我会得到什么。

college-writing-008851.en: I like simple meals more than gourmet ones.
college-writing-008851.zh: 我更喜欢简单的饭菜而不是美食。

college-writing-008853.en: While I’m struggling to see what’s on my plate, I worry that I’ll knock one of the glasses off the table.
college-writing-008853.zh: 当我在努力看看我的盘子里有什么时，我担心我会把一副眼镜从桌子上敲下来。

college-writing-008854.en: The waiters at the Chalet can be uncomfortably formal, too.
college-writing-008854.zh: 小木屋的服务员也可能很正式。

college-writing-008855.en: I get the feeling that I don’t quite live up to their standards.
college-writing-008855.zh: 我觉得我没有达到他们的标准。

college-writing-008856.en: Even the other diners can make me feel uncomfortable.
college-writing-008856.zh: 即使是其他食客也会让我感到不舒服。

college-writing-008857.en: There’s a big price difference between the Chalet and McDonald’s.
college-writing-008857.zh: 小木屋和麦当劳之间存在很大的价格差异。

college-writing-008858.en: Dinner for two at the Chalet can easily cost $100, even without any “extras” like appetizers and dessert.
college-writing-008858.zh: 即使没有开胃菜和甜点等任何“额外”，在小木屋的两人晚餐也很容易花费 100 美元。

college-writing-008859.en: And the $100 doesn’t include the cost of parking the car and tipping the waiter.
college-writing-008859.zh: 100 美元不包括停车和给服务员小费的成本。

college-writing-008860.en: Once, I forgot to bring enough money.
college-writing-008860.zh: 有一次，我忘了带足够的钱。

college-writing-008861.en: At McDonald’s, a meal for two will cost around $15.
college-writing-008861.zh: 在麦当劳，两人的一餐费用约为 15 美元。

college-writing-008862.en: So, for my birthday dinner, or any other time, I prefer to eat at McDonald’s.
college-writing-008862.zh: 所以，对于我的生日晚餐或任何其他时间，我更喜欢在麦当劳吃饭。

college-writing-008863.en: It is convenient, friendly, and cheap.

college-writing-008864.en: Development through Revising Jesse put the first draft of his essay aside and took it to his writing class the next day.
college-writing-008864.zh: 通过修改 Jesse 将他的论文的初稿放在一边，并在第二天将其带到他的写作课上。

college-writing-008865.en: His instructor asked Jesse and the other students to work in small groups reading their drafts aloud and making suggestions for revision to one another.
college-writing-008865.zh: 他的导师要求杰西和其他学生分组工作，大声朗读他们的草稿，并提出修改建议。

college-writing-008866.en: Here are the notes Jesse made on his group’s comments:
college-writing-008866.zh: 以下是杰西在他的小组评论中所做的注释：

college-writing-008867.en: • I need to explain that Lilly is my wife.
college-writing-008867.zh: • 我需要解释莉莉是我的妻子。

college-writing-008868.en: • I’m not consistent in developing my paragraphs.
college-writing-008868.zh: • 我在开发我的段落方面并不一致。

college-writing-008869.en: I forgot to do a “one side at a time”

college-writing-008871.en: I think I’ll try “one side at a time.”
college-writing-008871.zh: 我想我会尝试“一次一侧”。

college-writing-008873.en: each paragraph what the Chalet is like, then what McDonald’s is like.
college-writing-008873.zh: 每一段小木屋是什么样的，那么麦当劳是什么样的。

college-writing-008874.en: • I could use more support for some of my points, like when I say that the waiters at
college-writing-008874.zh: • 我可以为我的一些观点使用更多的支持，比如当我说服务员在

college-writing-008876.en: I should give some examples of what I mean by that.
college-writing-008876.zh: 我应该举一些我的意思的例子。

college-writing-008877.en: • I want to say something about what I’d rather do with the money we save by going to
college-writing-008877.zh: • 我想说一些我宁愿用我们节省的钱做什么

college-writing-008879.en: For me that’s important—we can “eat” that money at the Chalet, or do
college-writing-008879.zh: 对我来说，这很重要——我们可以在小屋里“吃”那笔钱，或者

college-writing-008880.en: other things with it that we both enjoy.
college-writing-008880.zh: 我们都喜欢的其他东西。

college-writing-008881.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 321

college-writing-008882.en: After making these observations about his first draft, Jesse proceeded to write the version of his essay that appears at the beginning of this chapter.
college-writing-008882.zh: 在对他的初稿进行了这些观察后，Jesse 继续写下他的文章版本，出现在本章的开头。

college-writing-008883.en: A Model Essay to Consider Read the following essay.
college-writing-008883.zh: 需要考虑的模型论文阅读以下文章。

college-writing-008884.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-008884.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-008887.en: Yonder sky that has wept tears of compassion on our fathers for centuries untold, and which, to us, looks eternal, may change.
college-writing-008887.zh: 几个世纪以来，天空为我们的祖先哭泣着同情的泪水，对我们来说，这看起来是永恒的，可能会改变。

college-writing-008888.en: Today it is fair, tomorrow it may be overcast with clouds.
college-writing-008888.zh: 今天是公平的，明天可能会被云彩笼罩。

college-writing-008889.en: My words are like the stars that never set.
college-writing-008889.zh: 我的话就像从未落下的星星。

college-writing-008890.en: What Seattle says, the great chief, Washington . . . can rely upon, with as much certainty as our paleface brothers can rely upon the return of the seasons.
college-writing-008890.zh: 西雅图所说的，华盛顿的伟大酋长。 。 。 可以依靠，就像我们的苍白兄弟可以依靠季节的回归一样确定。

college-writing-008891.en: The son [a reference to Territorial Governor Stevens] of the White Chief says his father sends us greetings of friendship and good will.
college-writing-008891.zh: 白人酋长的儿子（提到领土州长史蒂文斯）说，他的父亲向我们致以友谊和善意的问候。

college-writing-008892.en: This is kind, for we know he has little need of our friendship in return, because his people are many.
college-writing-008892.zh: 这是善良的，因为我们知道他几乎不需要我们的友谊作为回报，因为他的人很多。

college-writing-008893.en: They are like the grass that covers the vast prairies, while my people are few, and resemble the scattering trees of a storm-swept plain.
college-writing-008893.zh: 它们就像覆盖广阔草原的草地，而我的人很少，就像风暴席卷的平原上散落的树木。

college-writing-008894.en: The great, and I presume also good, white chief sends us word that he wants to buy our lands but is willing to allow us to reserve enough to live on comfortably.
college-writing-008894.zh: 伟大的，我想也很好，白人酋长给我们发消息说他想买我们的土地，但愿意让我们预留足够的钱来舒适地生活。

college-writing-008895.en: This indeed appears generous, for the red man no longer has rights that he need respect, and the offer may be wise, also, for we are no longer in need of a great country.
college-writing-008895.zh: 这确实看起来很慷慨，因为红人不再拥有他需要尊重的权利，而且这个提议可能是明智的，因为我们不再需要一个伟大的国家。

college-writing-008896.en: There Was a Time There was a time when our people covered the whole land, as the waves of a wind-ruffled sea cover its shell-paved floor.
college-writing-008896.zh: 曾经有一段时间，我们的人民覆盖了整个土地，因为一片风波的大海的海浪覆盖了它的贝壳地板。

college-writing-008897.en: But that time has long since passed away with the greatness of tribes now almost forgotten.
college-writing-008897.zh: 但那个时代早已过去，随着部落的伟大，现在几乎被遗忘了。

college-writing-008898.en: I will not mourn over our untimely decay, nor reproach my pale-face brothers for hastening it, for we, too, may have been somewhat to blame.
college-writing-008898.zh: 我不会为我们不合时宜的衰败而哀悼，也不会责备我苍白的兄弟加速它，因为我们也可能在某种程度上受到责备。

college-writing-008899.en: When our young men grow angry at some real or imaginary wrong, and disfigure their faces with black paint, their hearts, also, are disfigured and turn black, and then their cruelty is relentless and knows no bounds, and our old men are not able to restrain them.
college-writing-008899.zh: 当我们的年轻人对一些真实的或虚构的错误感到愤怒，用黑色的油漆毁容他们的脸时，他们的心也被毁容并变成了黑色，然后他们的残忍是无情的，没有任何界限，我们的老人无法约束他们。

college-writing-008900.en: But let us hope that hostilities between the red-man and his pale-face brothers may never return.
college-writing-008900.zh: 但让我们希望红人和他苍白的兄弟之间的敌对行动可能永远不会回来。

college-writing-008901.en: We would have everything to lose and nothing to gain.
college-writing-008901.zh: 我们将失去一切，一无所获。

college-writing-008902.zh: 第322章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008903.en: True it is, that revenge, with our young braves, is considered gain, even at the cost of their own lives, but old men who stay at home in times of war, and old women, who have sons to lose, know better.
college-writing-008903.zh: 诚然，与我们年轻的勇士一起复仇，即使是以生命为代价，也被认为是收获，但在战争时期留在家中的老人和有儿子要失去的老年人更清楚。

college-writing-008904.en: Our great father Washington, for I presume he is now our father, as well as yours, since George [a reference to King George III, i.e., Great Britain] has moved his boundaries to the north; our great and good father, I say, sends us word by his son, who, no doubt, is a great chief among his people, that if we do as he desires, he will protect us.
college-writing-008904.zh: 我们伟大的华盛顿父亲，因为我认为他现在是我们的父亲，也是你们的，因为乔治三世（即英国国王）已经将他的边界移到了北方； 我说，我们伟大的好父亲向我们传来他的儿子的话，他毫无疑问是他的人民中的伟大酋长，如果我们按照他的意愿去做，他就会保护我们。

college-writing-008905.en: His brave armies will be to us a bristling wall of strength, and his great ships of war will fill our harbors so that our ancient enemies far to the northward, the Simsiams [Tsimshian] and Hydas [Haidas], will no longer frighten our women and old men.
college-writing-008905.zh: 他勇敢的军队将成为我们强大的力量之墙，他的伟大战舰将填满我们的港口，使我们远在北方的古老敌人 Simsiams [Tsimshian] 和 Hydas [Haidas] 不再吓唬我们的女性和 老人。

college-writing-008906.en: Then he will be our father and we will be his children.
college-writing-008906.zh: 然后他将成为我们的父亲，我们将成为他的孩子。

college-writing-008908.en: Your God loves your people and hates mine; he folds his strong arms lovingly around the white man and leads him as a father leads his infant son, but he has forsaken his red children; he makes your people wax strong every day, and soon they will fill the land; while my people are ebbing away like a fast-receding tide, that will never flow again.
college-writing-008908.zh: 你的上帝爱你的人民，恨我的人； 他亲切地搂着白人，把他强壮的手臂抱在怀里，带领他带领他年幼的儿子，但他已经抛弃了他的红色孩子； 他让你的人民每天都变得强大，很快他们就会充满土地； 当我的人民像一个快速后退的潮水一样消退时，它再也不会流动了。

college-writing-008909.en: The white man’s God cannot love his red children or he would protect them.
college-writing-008909.zh: 白人的上帝不能爱他的红色孩子，否则他会保护他们。

college-writing-008910.en: They seem to be orphans who can look nowhere for help.
college-writing-008910.zh: 他们似乎是无法寻求帮助的孤儿。

college-writing-008911.en: How then can we become brothers?
college-writing-008911.zh: 那么我们如何成为兄弟呢？

college-writing-008912.en: How can your father become our father and bring us prosperity and awaken in us dreams of returning greatness?
college-writing-008912.zh: 你的父亲如何成为我们的父亲，带给我们繁荣，唤醒我们的梦想，回报伟大？

college-writing-008913.en: Your God seems to us to be partial.
college-writing-008913.zh: 在我们看来，你的上帝是部分的。

college-writing-008914.en: He came to the white man.

college-writing-008915.en: We never saw Him; never even heard His voice; He gave the white man laws but He had no word for His red children whose teeming millions filled this vast continent as the stars fill the firmament.
college-writing-008915.zh: 我们从未见过他； 甚至从未听到过他的声音； 他给了白人法则，但他对他的红色孩子们没有任何消息，当星星充满苍穹时，他们的红宝石充满了这片广阔的大陆。

college-writing-008916.en: No, we are two distinct races and must remain ever so.
college-writing-008916.zh: 不，我们是两个不同的种族，必须永远保持这种状态。

college-writing-008917.en: There is little in common between us.
college-writing-008917.zh: 我们之间几乎没有共同点。

college-writing-008918.en: The ashes of our ancestors are sacred and their final resting place is hallowed ground, while you wander away from the tombs of your fathers seemingly without regret.
college-writing-008918.zh: 我们祖先的骨灰是神圣的，他们最后的安息之地是神圣的土地，而你似乎没有遗憾地离开你父亲的坟墓。

college-writing-008919.en: Your religion was written on tables of stone by the iron finger of an angry God, lest you might forget it.
college-writing-008919.zh: 你的宗教是愤怒的神的铁手指在石头上写的，以免你忘记它。

college-writing-008920.en: The red man could never remember nor comprehend it.
college-writing-008920.zh: 红人永远无法记住或理解它。

college-writing-008921.en: Our religion is the traditions of our ancestors, the dreams of our old men, given them by the great Spirit, and the visions of our sachems, and is written in the hearts of our people.
college-writing-008921.zh: 我们的宗教是我们祖先的传统，是我们老人的梦想，由伟大的精神赋予他们，以及我们的 sachems 的异象，写在我们人民的心中。

college-writing-008922.en: Your dead cease to love you and the homes of their nativity as soon as they pass the portals of the tomb.
college-writing-008922.zh: 一旦他们经过坟墓的门户，你的死者就会不再爱你和他们诞生的家园。

college-writing-008923.en: They wander far off beyond the stars, are soon forgotten, and never return.
college-writing-008923.zh: 他们漫步在星空之外，很快就会被遗忘，再也没有回来。

college-writing-008924.en: Our dead never forget the beautiful world that gave them being.
college-writing-008924.zh: 我们的死者永远不会忘记赋予他们存在的美丽世界。

college-writing-008925.en: They still love its winding rivers, its great mountains and its sequestered vales, and they ever yearn in tenderest affection over the lonely hearted living and often return to visit and comfort them.
college-writing-008925.zh: 他们仍然热爱它蜿蜒的河流、大山和被隔离的山谷，他们永远渴望最温柔的爱情，并经常回来探访和安慰他们。

college-writing-008926.en: Day and night cannot dwell together.
college-writing-008926.zh: 白天和黑夜不能在一起。

college-writing-008927.en: The red man has ever fled the approach of the white man, as the changing mists on the mountain side flee before the blazing morning sun.
college-writing-008927.zh: 红人曾经逃离白人的接近，因为山边不断变化的雾气在烈日的阳光下逃跑。

college-writing-008928.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 323

college-writing-008929.en: However, your proposition seems a just one, and I think my folks will accept it and will retire to the reservation you offer them, and we will dwell apart and in peace, for the words of the great white chief seem to be the voice of nature speaking to my people out of the thick darkness that is fast gathering around them like a dense fog floating inward from a midnight sea.
college-writing-008929.zh: 然而，你的提议似乎只是一个，我想我的人会接受它，并将退到你提供的保留地，我们将分居和平安，因为大白领的话似乎是大自然的声音，从周围快速聚集的浓密黑暗中对我的人民说话 它们就像从午夜大海向内漂浮的浓雾。

college-writing-008930.en: It matters but little where we pass the remainder of our days.
college-writing-008930.zh: 我们剩余的日子在哪里度过，这无关紧要。

college-writing-008931.en: They Are Not Many The Indian’s night promises to be dark.
college-writing-008931.zh: 他们不是很多印度人的夜晚承诺是黑暗的。

college-writing-008932.en: No bright star hovers above the horizon.
college-writing-008932.zh: 没有明亮的星星在地平线上方盘旋。

college-writing-008933.en: Sad-voiced winds moan in the distance.

college-writing-008934.en: Some grim Nemesis of our race is on the red man’s trail, and wherever he goes he will still hear the sure approaching footsteps of the fell destroyer and prepare to meet his doom, as does the wounded doe that hears the approaching footsteps of the hunter.
college-writing-008934.zh: 我们种族的一些严峻的克星在红人的轨道上，无论他走到哪里，他仍然会听到倒下的毁灭者的脚步声，并准备迎接他的厄运，就像听到猎人接近的脚步声的伤员一样。

college-writing-008935.en: A few more moons, a few more winters, and not one of all the mighty hosts that once filled this broad land or that now roam in fragmentary bands through these vast solitudes will remain to weep over the tombs of a people once as powerful and as hopeful as your own.
college-writing-008935.zh: 再多几个月亮，再来几个冬天，而不是曾经充满这片广阔土地的所有强大的主人之一，或者现在在这些广阔的孤独中漫游在零碎的带子中，将继续为曾经强大和充满希望的民族的坟墓哭泣。

college-writing-008936.zh: 但我们为什么要屈尊呢？

college-writing-008937.en: Why should I murmur at the fate of my people?
college-writing-008937.zh: 为什么我要对我的人民的命运低声说？

college-writing-008938.en: Tribes are made up of individuals and are no better than they.
college-writing-008938.zh: 部落是由个人组成的，并不比他们好。

college-writing-008939.en: Men come and go like the waves of a sea.
college-writing-008939.zh: 人来来去去，像海浪一样。

college-writing-008940.en: A tear, a tamanawus, a dirge, and they are gone from our longing eyes forever.
college-writing-008940.zh: 一滴眼泪，一颗塔玛纳维斯，一艘挽歌，它们永远从我们渴望的眼睛上消失了。

college-writing-008941.en: Even the white man, whose God walked and talked with him, as friend to friend, is not exempt from the common destiny.
college-writing-008941.zh: 即使是上帝与他同行和交谈的白人，作为朋友的朋友，也不能免于共同的命运。

college-writing-008942.en: We may be brothers after all.

college-writing-008944.en: We will ponder your proposition, and when we have decided we will tell you.
college-writing-008944.zh: 我们会思考你的提议，当我们决定时，我们会告诉你。

college-writing-008945.en: But should we accept it, I here and now make this the first condition: That we will not be denied the privilege, without molestation, of visiting at will the graves of our ancestors and friends.
college-writing-008945.zh: 但如果我们接受它，我在这里和现在将其作为第一个条件：我们不会被剥夺不受骚扰的特权，而不是随意访问我们祖先和朋友的坟墓。

college-writing-008946.en: Every part of this country is sacred to my people.
college-writing-008946.zh: 这个国家的每一个地方对我的人民来说都是神圣的。

college-writing-008947.en: Every hillside, every valley, every plain and grove has been hallowed by some fond memory or some sad experience of my tribe.
college-writing-008947.zh: 每一个山坡，每一个山谷，每一个平原和小树林，都被我部落的一些美好回忆或一些悲伤的经历所描绘。

college-writing-008948.en: Even the Rocks Even the rocks that seem to lie dumb as they swelter in the sun along the silent seashore in solemn grandeur thrill with memories of past events connected with the fate of my people, and the very dust under your feet responds more lovingly to our footsteps than to yours, because it is the ashes of our ancestors, and our bare feet are conscious of the sympathetic touch, for the soil is rich with the life of our kindred.
college-writing-008948.zh: 即使是岩石，当它们在寂静的海滨中闷热时，它们似乎是哑巴的岩石，在沉默的海滨中闷闷不乐，在对过去事件与我人民的命运有关的记忆中激动不已，你脚下的灰尘对我们的脚步反应比对我们的脚步更有爱心 你的，因为它是我们祖先的灰烬，我们赤脚意识到有同情心的触摸，因为土壤中充满了我们同族的生命。

college-writing-008949.en: The sable braves, and fond mothers, and glad-hearted maidens, and the little children who lived and rejoiced here, and whose very names are now forgotten, still love these solitudes, and their deep fastnesses at eventide grow shadowy with the presence of dusky spirits.
college-writing-008949.zh: 黑貂勇士，好心的妈妈，心地喜乐的少女，和在这里生活和欢乐的小孩，他们的名字现在被遗忘了，他们仍然爱这些孤独，他们在晚年的深处，随着昏暗的存在变得模糊不清 灵魂。

college-writing-008950.en: And when the last red man shall have perished from the earth and his memory among white men shall have become a myth, these shores shall swarm with the invisible dead of my tribe, and when your children’s children shall think themselves alone in the field, the store, the shop, upon the highway or in the silence of the woods they will not be alone.
college-writing-008950.zh: 当最后一个红人从地上灭亡，白人的记忆将成为神话时，这些海岸将聚集在我部落的无形死者中，当您的孩子的孩子将独自一人认为自己在田野、商店、商店、高速公路或寂静中时，这些海岸将蜂拥而至。 他们不会孤单。

college-writing-008951.zh: 第324章 论文发展模式

college-writing-008953.en: In all the earth there is no place dedicated to solitude.
college-writing-008953.zh: 在整个地球上，没有专门用于孤独的地方。

college-writing-008954.en: At night, when the streets of your cities and villages shall be silent, and you think them deserted, they will throng with the returning hosts that once filled and still love this beautiful land.
college-writing-008954.zh: 到了晚上，当你的城市和村庄的街道静音时，你认为它们被遗弃了，它们将聚集在曾经充满并仍然热爱这片美丽土地的归来的主人中。

college-writing-008955.en: The white man will never be alone.

college-writing-008956.en: Let him be just and deal kindly with my people, for the dead are not altogether powerless.
college-writing-008956.zh: 让他公正，善待我的人民，因为死者并非完全无能为力。

college-writing-009005.zh: 第326章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009006.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Comparison and/or Contrast1
college-writing-009006.zh: 写一篇强调比较和/或对比的论文1

college-writing-009007.en: Write an essay about a change (positive or negative) in a person you know, and explain the causes and process of that change.
college-writing-009007.zh: 写一篇关于你认识的人的变化（积极或消极）的文章，并解释这种变化的原因和过程。

college-writing-009008.en: You should provide a specific description of the person both before and after the change.
college-writing-009008.zh: 您应该在更改之前和之后提供有关人员的具体描述。

college-writing-009009.en: You will want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” Chapter 11, “Process,” and Chapter 12, “Cause and/or Effect,” to help you provide good support for your essay.
college-writing-009009.zh: 您将需要查看第 8 章“描述”、第 11 章“过程”和第 12 章“原因和/或效果”，以帮助您为论文提供良好的支持。

college-writing-009012.en: Gather information about the person you’ve selected by using a prewriting
college-writing-009012.zh: 使用预写程序收集有关您选择的人员的信息

college-writing-009014.en: Write down as much information as possible within a ten-minute period.
college-writing-009014.zh: 在十分钟内写下尽可能多的信息。

college-writing-009015.en: Don’t worry about spelling, grammar, organization, or anything other than getting your thoughts down on the page.
college-writing-009015.zh: 除了将您的想法放在页面上之外，不要担心拼写、语法、组织或其他任何事情。

college-writing-009016.en: If ideas are still flowing at the end of ten minutes, keep on writing.
college-writing-009016.zh: 如果想法在十分钟结束时仍在流动，请继续写作。

college-writing-009017.en: Once you have finished getting your thoughts down, you should have a base of raw material that you can draw on in the next phase of your work.
college-writing-009017.zh: 一旦你完成了你的想法，你应该有一个可以在下一阶段工作的原材料基础。

college-writing-009018.en: Judging from what you have produced, do you think you have enough material to support your essay?
college-writing-009018.zh: 从你制作的内容来看，你认为你有足够的材料来支持你的论文吗？

college-writing-009019.en: If so, keep following the steps below.
college-writing-009019.zh: 如果是这样，请继续遵循以下步骤。

college-writing-009020.en: If not, choose another person and spend about ten minutes generating ideas to see if they might be a better subject for your essay.
college-writing-009020.zh: 如果没有，请选择另一个人并花费大约十分钟的时间来产生想法，看看它们是否可能是您论文的更好主题。

college-writing-009022.en: Develop a single clear sentence that will serve as your thesis.
college-writing-009022.zh: 制定一个明确的句子，作为你的论文。

college-writing-009024.en: should demonstrate why it is important that your readers know about this person and the change they went through.
college-writing-009024.zh: 应该说明为什么您的读者了解这个人以及他们所经历的变化很重要。

college-writing-009026.en: Decide which method of development you will use to design your essay: one
college-writing-009026.zh: 决定你将使用哪种开发方法来设计你的论文：一

college-writing-009027.en: side at a time or point by point.
college-writing-009027.zh: 在一个时间或一点点侧面。

college-writing-009028.en: Be consistent in your use of one method or the other in each of your paragraphs.
college-writing-009028.zh: 在每个段落中使用一种或另一种方法时要保持一致。

college-writing-009030.en: Write the first draft of your essay.

college-writing-009031.en: REVISING Reread your essay and then show it to a friend or classmate who will give you honest feedback.
college-writing-009031.zh: 修改重新阅读您的论文，然后将其展示给会给您诚实反馈的朋友或同学。

college-writing-009032.en: You should both review it, keeping in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-009032.zh: 你们都应该复习它，牢记本章末尾四个基础清单中的问题。

college-writing-009033.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you and your reader can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-009033.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改您的论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您和您的读者可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-009036.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 327

college-writing-009037.en: Write an essay in which you contrast two attitudes on a controversial subject.
college-writing-009037.zh: 写一篇文章，在一个有争议的主题上对比两种态度。

college-writing-009038.en: You may want to contrast your views with those of someone else, or contrast the way you felt about the subject in the past with the way you feel now.
college-writing-009038.zh: 您可能想将您的观点与其他人的观点进行对比，或者将您对过去主题的感受与您现在的感觉进行对比。

college-writing-009039.en: You might consider writing about one of these subjects:
college-writing-009039.zh: 您可能会考虑写下以下主题之一：

college-writing-009040.en: • Adopting a vegan diet • Assisted suicide • Climate change • Factory farming • Free college • Genetically modified foods • Immigration policies in the United States • Legalization of marijuana • Mandatory vaccinations • Obligatory military service • The public’s right to know about elected officials’ private lives • Regulating social media • Same-sex couples fostering and/or adopting children • Standardized tests and college admissions
college-writing-009040.zh: • 采用纯素饮食 • 辅助自杀 • 气候变化 • 工厂化农业 • 免费大学 • 转基因食品 • 美国的移民政策 • 大麻合法化 • 强制性疫苗接种 • 强制性服兵役 • 公众了解民选官员私生活的权利 • 监管社交媒体 • 同性伴侣 寄养和/或收养儿童 • 标准化考试和大学录取

college-writing-009043.en: To gather information for the point of view that contrasts
college-writing-009043.zh: 为对比的观点收集信息

college-writing-009044.en: with your own, you will need to do some research.
college-writing-009044.zh: 有了你自己的，你需要做一些研究。

college-writing-009045.en: In addition to the Internet, you’ll find useful material if you go to the library and search through article indexes for recent newsmagazines.
college-writing-009045.zh: 除了互联网之外，如果您去图书馆搜索文章索引，您还可以找到有用的材料，以获取最近的新闻杂志。

college-writing-009046.en: (If you need help, ask your instructor or the research librarian.)
college-writing-009046.zh: （如果您需要帮助，请咨询您的讲师或研究图书馆员。）

college-writing-009047.en: Or interview friends and acquaintances whose attitude on the subject is different from yours.
college-writing-009047.zh: 或者采访对这个主题的态度与你不同的朋友和熟人。

college-writing-009049.en: To generate ideas for your essay, try the following two-part exercise.
college-writing-009049.zh: 要为您的论文产生想法，请尝试以下两部分练习。

college-writing-009050.en: • Part 1: Pretend that a visitor from Mars who has never heard of the topic of your paper has asked you to explain it, as well as why you take the attitude you do toward it.
college-writing-009050.zh: • 第 1 部分：假装一位从未听说过您论文主题的来自火星的访客要求您解释它，以及您为什么采取对它的态度。

college-writing-009051.en: Using the technique of freewriting─not worrying about sentence structure, organization, spelling, repetition, etc.
college-writing-009051.zh: 使用自由写作的技术——不用担心句子结构、组织、拼写、重复等。

college-writing-009053.en: Throw in every reason you can think of for your attitude.
college-writing-009053.zh: 把你能想到的一切理由都放在你的态度上。

college-writing-009054.en: • Part 2: Now the Martian asks you to do the same, taking the opposing point of view.
college-writing-009054.zh: • 第 2 部分：现在火星人要求您也这样做，以相反的观点。

college-writing-009055.en: Remember that it’s up to you to make this interplanetary
college-writing-009055.zh: 请记住，这取决于您制作这个星球

college-writing-009073.en: Write an essay that contrasts two characters or two points of view in one or more poems, stories, plays, or novels.
college-writing-009073.zh: 写一篇文章，在一首或多首诗、故事、戏剧或小说中对比两个角色或两个观点。

college-writing-009074.en: The work you choose may be assigned by your instructor, or it may require your instructor’s approval.
college-writing-009074.zh: 您选择的工作可能由您的教师分配，也可能需要您的教师的批准。

college-writing-009075.en: For this assignment, your essay may have two supporting paragraphs, with each paragraph representing one side of the contrast.
college-writing-009075.zh: 对于这个作业，你的文章可能有两个支持段落，每个段落代表对比的一侧。

college-writing-009076.en: You will want to check Chapter 18, “Summarizing and Paraphrasing,” Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” and Chapter 20, “Writing a Research Essay,” to ensure that you properly present and cite the information from your chosen works.
college-writing-009076.zh: 您将需要查看第 18 章“总结和释义”，第 19 章，“撰写基于来源的论文”和第 20 章，“撰写研究论文”，以确保您正确呈现和引用所选作品中的信息。

college-writing-009089.en: Consider closing with a final comment that makes it clear why you stand where you do.
college-writing-009089.zh: 考虑以最终评论结束，以清楚地说明您为什么站在您所在的位置。

college-writing-009091.en: Refer to the guidelines for rewriting provided in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter.
college-writing-009091.zh: 请参阅本章末尾的四个基础清单中提供的重写指南。

college-writing-009140.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-009141.en: In this comparison and/or contrast essay, you will write with a specific purpose and for a specific audience.
college-writing-009141.zh: 在这篇比较和/或对比文章中，您将以特定目的和特定受众写作。

college-writing-009142.en: Write a letter to your boss in which you compare your abilities with those of the ideal candidate for a position to which you’d like to be promoted.
college-writing-009142.zh: 给老板写一封信，将你的能力与你想升职的理想候选人的能力进行比较。

college-writing-009143.en: Use the pointby-point method, discussing each desired qualification and then describing how well you measure up to it.

college-writing-009144.en: Consider the requirements of a job you are familiar with, ideally a job you would really like to apply for.

college-writing-009166.zh: 第13章 比较和/或对比 331

college-writing-009167.en: Comparison and/or Contrast Checklist: THE FOUR BASES
college-writing-009167.zh: 比较和/或对比清单：四个基础

college-writing-009169.en: Have I included a thesis statement that clearly identifies whether I am comparing, contrasting, or using both processes to discuss my subject?
college-writing-009169.zh: 我是否包含了一个 中心论点句，它清楚地确定了我是在比较、对比还是使用这两个过程来讨论我的主题？

college-writing-009170.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-009170.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-009172.en: Does my essay include strong details that help the reader understand my claim?
college-writing-009172.zh: 我的文章是否包含帮助读者理解我的主张的详细细节？

college-writing-009173.en: Does every paragraph support my thesis in some way?
college-writing-009173.zh: 每一段都以某种方式支持我的论文吗？

college-writing-009175.en: Is my essay organized as point-by-point or one side at a time?
college-writing-009175.zh: 我的论文是逐点组织的还是一次一侧的？

college-writing-009176.en: Is the current organization the most effective choice?
college-writing-009176.zh: 当前的组织是最有效的选择吗？

college-writing-009177.en: Do I use logical transitions to make points of comparison and/or contrast clear?
college-writing-009177.zh: 我是否使用逻辑转换来使比较点和/或对比清晰？

college-writing-009178.en: Do I have a concluding paragraph that supports my overall essay and thesis?
college-writing-009178.zh: 我有一个结论段落来支持我的整体论文和论文吗？

college-writing-009180.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-009180.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-009181.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-009181.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-009182.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-009182.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-009184.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-009184.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-009188.en: In Scraps From a Diary─Chief Seattle―A Gentleman by Instinct─His Native Eloquence by H. A. Smith.
college-writing-009188.zh: 在《日记》的碎片中——西雅图首席——本能的绅士——他的本土口才，由 H. A. Smith 撰写。

college-writing-009190.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on definition • write an essay with emphasis on definition • revise an essay with emphasis on definition
college-writing-009190.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写以定义为重点的论文 • 撰写一篇强调定义的论文 • 修改文章，强调定义

college-writing-009191.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize definition • one professional model essay that emphasizes definition
college-writing-009191.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调定义的学生论文 • 一篇强调定义的专业模型论文

college-writing-009193.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-009194.en: In talking with other people, we sometimes offer informal definitions to explain just what we mean by a particular term.
college-writing-009194.zh: 在与其他人交谈时，我们有时会提供非正式的定义来解释我们所说的特定术语的含义。

college-writing-009195.en: Suppose, for example, we say to a friend, “Lucas is really an inconsiderate person.”
college-writing-009195.zh: 例如，假设我们对朋友说：“卢卡斯真的是一个不体贴的人。”

college-writing-009196.en: We might then explain what we mean by “inconsiderate” by saying, “He borrowed my accounting book ‘overnight’ but didn’t return it for a week. And when I got it back, it was covered with coffee stains.”
college-writing-009196.zh: 然后，我们可以通过说“他借了我的会计书‘过夜’但一周没有退货”来解释“不体贴”的含义。

college-writing-009197.en: In a written definition, we make clear in a more complete and formal way our own personal understanding of a term.
college-writing-009197.zh: 在书面定义中，我们以更完整和正式的方式明确了我们自己对一个术语的理解。

college-writing-009198.en: Such a definition typically starts with one meaning of a term.
college-writing-009198.zh: 这样的定义通常以一个术语的一种含义开始。

college-writing-009199.en: The meaning is then illustrated with a series of details.
college-writing-009199.zh: 然后用一系列细节来说明意义。

college-writing-009200.en: What does it mean to be a successful student?
college-writing-009200.zh: 成为一名成功的学生意味着什么？

college-writing-009201.en: What qualities and attributes does a successful student possess?
college-writing-009201.zh: 一个成功的学生有什么品质和属性？

college-writing-009202.en: Looking at the photograph above and thinking about these questions, write an essay in which you define what it means to be a successful student.
college-writing-009202.zh: 看着上面的照片并思考这些问题，写一篇文章，你可以在其中定义成为一名成功学生的意义。

college-writing-009207.en: In this chapter, you will be asked to write an essay in which you define and illustrate a term.
college-writing-009207.zh: 在本章中，您将被要求写一篇文章，您在其中定义和说明一个术语。

college-writing-009208.en: To prepare for this assignment, first read the student essays and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-009208.zh: 为了准备这项作业，首先阅读学生的论文和模型论文，并解决随附的问题。

college-writing-009211.en: Not every person who likes football falls into the category of a football fan.
college-writing-009211.zh: 不是每个喜欢足球的人都属于足球迷的范畴。

college-writing-009212.en: The word “fan” is an abbreviation of “fanatic,” meaning “a person marked or motivated by an extreme, unreasoning enthusiasm.”
college-writing-009212.zh: “风扇”一词是“狂热者”的缩写，意思是“被极端、不合理的热情所标记或激励的人”。

college-writing-009213.en: In the case of football fans, the term is appropriate.
college-writing-009213.zh: 在足球迷的情况下，这个词是合适的。

college-writing-009214.en: They behave unreasonably, they are unreasonable about the past, and they are extremely loyal.
college-writing-009214.zh: 他们表现得不合理，对过去不合理，而且非常忠诚。

college-writing-009215.en: Football fans wear their official team T-shirts and warm-up jackets to the mall, the supermarket, the classroom, and even—if they can get away with it—to work.
college-writing-009215.zh: 足球迷穿着他们的官方 T 恤和热身夹克去购物中心、超市、教室，甚至——如果他们能逃脱的话——去工作。

college-writing-009216.en: If the team offers a giveaway item, the fans rush to the stadium to claim the hat or sports bag or water bottle that is being handed out that day.
college-writing-009216.zh: 如果球队提供赠品，球迷们会冲到体育场领取当天分发的帽子、运动包或水瓶。

college-writing-009217.en: Baseball fans get similarly enthusiastic when their favorite teams give away some attractive freebie.
college-writing-009217.zh: 当他们最喜欢的球队赠送一些有吸引力的免费赠品时，棒球迷也会变得同样热情。

college-writing-009218.en: Football fans just plain behave unreasonably.
college-writing-009218.zh: 足球迷只是不合理地行事。

college-writing-009219.en: Even the fact that fans spend the coldest months of the year huddling on icy metal benches in places like Chicago proves it.
college-writing-009219.zh: 即使是粉丝们在一年中最冷的几个月里挤在芝加哥等地的冰冷金属长凳上，这也证明了这一点。

college-writing-009220.en: In addition, football fans decorate their houses with football-related items of every kind.
college-writing-009220.zh: 此外，足球迷们用各种与足球相关的物品来装饰他们的房子。

college-writing-009221.en: To them, team bumper stickers belong not only on car bumpers, but also on fireplace mantels and front doors.
college-writing-009221.zh: 对他们来说，团队保险杠贴纸不仅属于汽车保险杠，还属于壁炉壁炉架和前门。

college-writing-009222.en: When they go to a game, which they do as often as possible, they also decorate their bodies.
college-writing-009222.zh: 当他们尽可能多地去看游戏时，他们也会装饰自己的身体。

college-writing-009223.en: True football fans not only put on their team jackets and grab their pennants but also paint their heads to look like helmets or wear glow-in-the-dark cheeseheads.
college-writing-009223.zh: 真正的足球迷不仅穿上他们的球队夹克，拿起他们的旗帜，还把他们的头涂成看起来像头盔或戴着发光的奶酪头。

college-writing-009224.en: At the game, these fans devote enormous energy to trying to get a “wave” going.
college-writing-009224.zh: 在比赛中，这些球迷们投入了巨大的精力，试图让“浪潮”继续前进。

college-writing-009225.en: Football fans are extremely fascinated by the past.
college-writing-009225.zh: 足球迷对过去非常着迷。

college-writing-009226.en: They talk about William “Refrigerator” Perry’s 1985 Super Bowl touchdown as though it had happened last week.
college-writing-009226.zh: 他们谈论威廉“冰箱”佩里 1985 年的超级碗触地得分，就好像它发生在上周一样。

college-writing-009227.en: They excitedly discuss Peyton Manning and the Colts’ fourth-quarter comeback over the New England Patriots in 2009.
college-writing-009227.zh: 他们兴奋地讨论佩顿曼宁和小马队在2009年对新英格兰爱国者队的复出。

college-writing-009228.en: They reminisce about Patrick Mahomes’s left-handed pass late in the fourth quarter that secured a Chiefs 2018 win over Denver.
college-writing-009228.zh: 他们回忆起帕特里克·马霍姆斯在第四节末段的左撇子传球，这确保了酋长队在 2018 年战胜丹佛的比赛。

college-writing-009229.en: And if a person can’t manage to get excited about such ancient history, they are considered unreasonable.
college-writing-009229.zh: 如果一个人无法对如此古老的历史感到兴奋，他们就被认为是不合理的。

college-writing-009230.en: Last of all, football fans are extremely loyal to the team of their choice, often dangerously so.
college-writing-009230.zh: 最后，足球迷对他们选择的球队非常忠诚，通常是危险的。

college-writing-009231.en: Should their beloved team lose three in a row, fans
college-writing-009231.zh: 如果他们心爱的球队连续输掉三场，球迷

college-writing-009233.zh: 第334章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009234.en: may begin to react negatively as a way to hide their broken hearts.
college-writing-009234.zh: 可能会开始产生消极的反应，以隐藏他们破碎的心。

college-writing-009235.en: They still obsessively watch each game and spend the entire day afterward reading and listening to the postgame commentary in newspapers, on TV sports segments, and on sports websites.
college-writing-009235.zh: 他们仍然痴迷于观看每场比赛，并在之后的一整天里阅读和收听报纸、电视体育节目和体育网站上的赛后评论。

college-writing-009236.en: Further, this intense loyalty makes fans dangerous.
college-writing-009236.zh: 此外，这种强烈的忠诚使粉丝变得危险。

college-writing-009237.en: To anyone who dares to say to a loyal fan that another team has better players or coaches or to anyone wandering near the home cheering section wearing the jacket of the opposing team, physical damage is a real possibility.
college-writing-009237.zh: 对于任何敢于对忠实的球迷说，另一支球队有更好的球员或教练的人，或者对于穿着对方球队的夹克在主场附近徘徊的任何人来说，身体伤害是一个真正的可能性。

college-writing-009238.en: Bloody noses, black eyes, and broken bones are just some of the injuries inflicted on people cheering the wrong team when fans are around.
college-writing-009238.zh: 流血的鼻子、黑眼睛和骨折只是当球迷在身边时为错误的球队加油的人的一些伤害。

college-writing-009239.en: In 2014, thirty-one fans were arrested and ninety-three were ejected from the game when fights broke out between Raiders and 49ers fans.
college-writing-009239.zh: 2014 年，当突袭者和 49 人队球迷之间爆发战斗时，31 名球迷被捕，93 人被逐出比赛。

college-writing-009240.en: From February through August, football fans act like any other human beings.
college-writing-009240.zh: 从二月到八月，球迷们的行为就像任何其他人一样。

college-writing-009241.en: They pay their taxes, take out the garbage, and complain about the high cost of living.
college-writing-009241.zh: 他们交税，倒垃圾，抱怨生活成本高。

college-writing-009242.en: But when September rolls around, the colors go on, and the flat screens stream endlessly, the record books come off the shelves, and the devotion returns.
college-writing-009242.zh: 但是当九月来临时，颜色还在继续，平板屏幕无休止地流淌，记录簿下架，虔诚又回来了。

college-writing-009243.en: For the true football fan, another season of extremism has begun.
college-writing-009243.zh: 对于真正的足球迷来说，另一个极端主义赛季已经开始。

college-writing-009245.zh: 学校将人分为不同类别。

college-writing-009246.en: From the early grades, students are labeled “college track” or “vocational-technical” or “model citizen” or “troublemaker.”
college-writing-009246.zh: 从早期开始，学生就被标记为“大学赛道”或“职业技术”或“模范公民”或“麻烦制造者”。

college-writing-009247.en: Students pigeonhole their fellow students, too.
college-writing-009247.zh: 学生也会把其他学生归为特定的类别。

college-writing-009248.en: We’ve all known the “brain,” the “jock,” the “clown,” and the “teacher’s pet.”
college-writing-009248.zh: 我们都知道那种“学霸”、“运动员”、“小丑”以及“老师的宠儿”。

college-writing-009249.en: In most cases, these narrow labels are misleading and inaccurate.
college-writing-009249.zh: 在大多数情况下，这些狭窄的标签具有误导性且不准确。

college-writing-009250.en: But there is one label for a certain type of college student that says it all: “zombie.”
college-writing-009250.zh: 但有一种标签能概括某种类型的大学生：那就是“僵尸”。

college-writing-009252.en: Most of us haven’t known a lot of real zombies personally, but we do know how they act.
college-writing-009252.zh: 我们中的大多数人个人并不认识很多真正的僵尸，但我们确实知道它们的行为方式。

college-writing-009253.en: We have movies and television shows to guide us.
college-writing-009253.zh: 我们有电影和电视节目来指导我们。

college-writing-009254.en: The special effects in movies are much better these days.
college-writing-009254.zh: 如今，电影中的特效要好得多。

college-writing-009255.en: Over the years, we’ve learned from these sources that zombies stalk around graveyards, staring with empty, open eyes, and bumping like cheap toy robots into living people.
college-writing-009255.zh: 多年来，我们从这些来源中了解到，僵尸在墓地周围徘徊，空洞的眼睛睁着眼睛，像廉价的玩具机器人一样撞到活人。

college-writing-009256.en: Zombie students in college do just about the same thing.
college-writing-009256.zh: 大学里的僵尸学生也做同样的事情。

college-writing-009257.en: They stalk around campus, eyes glazed, staring off into space.
college-writing-009257.zh: 他们在校园里徘徊，眼睛呆滞，凝视着太空。

college-writing-009258.en: When they do manage to wander into a classroom, they sit down mechanically and contemplate the ceiling.
college-writing-009258.zh: 当他们设法走进教室时，他们机械地坐下来思考天花板。

college-writing-009259.en: Zombie students rarely eat, talk, laugh, or toss Frisbees on campus lawns.
college-writing-009259.zh: 僵尸学生很少在校园草坪上吃饭、说话、大笑或折腾飞盘。

college-writing-009260.en: Instead, they vanish when class is dismissed and return only when some mysterious zombie signal summons them back into a classroom.
college-writing-009260.zh: 取而代之的是，当一些神秘的僵尸信号将它们召唤回教室时，它们会在上课被解雇时消失并返回。

college-writing-009261.en: The signal may not occur for weeks.
college-writing-009261.zh: 信号可能在数周内不会出现。

college-writing-009262.en: Zombies are controlled by some mysterious force.
college-writing-009262.zh: 僵尸被某种神秘的力量控制。

college-writing-009263.en: According to legend, real zombies are corpses that have been brought back to life to
college-writing-009263.zh: 根据传说，真正的僵尸是被复活的尸体

college-writing-009267.zh: 1.《足球迷的定义》中的支持段落有一个话题
