college-writing-009277.zh: 主题等等应该被淘汰吗？

college-writing-009280.en: do the bidding of a magical master.

college-writing-009281.en: Student zombies, too, seem directed by a strange power.
college-writing-009281.zh: 学生僵尸似乎也被一种奇怪的力量所指挥。

college-writing-009282.en: They continue to attend school although they have no apparent desire to do so.
college-writing-009282.zh: 尽管他们没有明显的愿望，但他们继续上学。

college-writing-009283.en: They show no interest in college-related activities like tests, grades, papers, and projects.
college-writing-009283.zh: 他们对考试、成绩、论文和项目等与大学相关的活动没有兴趣。

college-writing-009284.en: And yet some inner force compels them to wander through the halls of higher education.
college-writing-009284.zh: 然而，一些内在力量迫使他们在高等教育的大厅里徘徊。

college-writing-009285.en: An awful fate awaits all zombies unless something happens to break the spell they’re under.
college-writing-009285.zh: 除非发生什么事情来打破他们所在的咒语，否则可怕的命运等待着所有僵尸。

college-writing-009286.en: In the movies, zombies are often shot, stabbed, drowned, electrocuted, and run over by large vehicles, all to no avail.
college-writing-009286.zh: 在电影中，僵尸经常被大型车辆射击、刺伤、淹死、触电和碾过，但都无济于事。

college-writing-009287.en: Finally the hero or heroine realizes that a potion is needed.
college-writing-009287.zh: 最后，英雄或女主角意识到需要一种药水。

college-writing-009288.en: Once the potion is made, with the appropriate props of chicken feet, human hair, and bats’ eyeballs, the zombie-corpse can return peacefully to its coffin.
college-writing-009288.zh: 一旦制作了药水，用鸡脚、人发和蝙蝠的眼球的适当道具，僵尸尸体可以平静地返回到它的棺材中。

college-writing-009289.en: The only hope for a student zombie to change is for them to undergo an awakening experience.
college-writing-009289.zh: 学生僵尸改变的唯一希望是让他们经历觉醒的体验。

college-writing-009290.en: All college students know that it’s not necessary to see Night of the Living Dead or The Walking Dead in order to see zombies in action—or nonaction.
college-writing-009290.zh: 所有大学生都知道，没有必要看到活死人或行尸走肉的夜晚，才能看到僵尸在行动或不作为。

college-writing-009291.en: They can forget the campus film series or the late-late show.
college-writing-009291.zh: 他们可以忘记校园电影系列或迟到的节目。

college-writing-009292.en: All they need to do is just sit in a classroom and wait.
college-writing-009292.zh: 他们需要做的只是坐在教室里等待。

college-writing-009293.en: They know what they’re looking for—the students who walk in without books or papers and sit in the very last row of seats.
college-writing-009293.zh: 他们知道他们在寻找什么——那些在没有书本或论文的情况下走进来并坐在最后一排座位上的学生。

college-writing-009294.en: The ones plugged constantly into their smartphone earbuds don’t count as zombies—that’s a whole different category of “student.”
college-writing-009294.zh: 那些经常插入智能手机耳塞的耳塞不算作僵尸——这是完全不同的“学生”类别。

college-writing-009295.en: Day of the Living Dead is showing every day at a college nearby.
college-writing-009295.zh: 活死人的日子每天都在附近的一所大学举行。

college-writing-009326.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Definition
college-writing-009326.zh: 写一篇强调定义的论文

college-writing-009327.en: Considering Purpose and Audience When you write an essay that emphasizes definition, your main purpose is to explain to readers your understanding of a key term or concept, while your secondary purpose is to persuade them that your definition is a legitimate one.
college-writing-009327.zh: 考虑目的和受众 当您撰写一篇强调定义的文章时，您的主要目的是向读者解释您对关键术语或概念的理解，而您的次要目的是说服他们您的定义是合法的。

college-writing-009328.en: Keep in mind that when you present a definition in your essay, you should not simply repeat a word’s
college-writing-009328.zh: 请记住，当您在论文中提出定义时，您不应该简单地重复一个单词的

college-writing-009331.en: Instead, you should convey what a particular term means to you by using persuasive examples.
college-writing-009331.zh: 相反，您应该通过使用有说服力的例子来传达特定术语对您的意义。

college-writing-009332.en: For example, if you were to write about the term patriotism, you might begin by presenting your definition of the word.
college-writing-009332.zh: 例如，如果你要写爱国主义这个词，你可以从展示你对这个词的定义开始。

college-writing-009333.en: You might say patriotism means turning out for Fourth of July parades or displaying the flag.
college-writing-009333.zh: 你可能会说爱国主义意味着参加七月四日的游行或展示国旗。

college-writing-009334.en: Or perhaps you think patriotism is about becoming politically aware and voting.
college-writing-009334.zh: 或者，也许你认为爱国主义是要在政治上意识到和投票。

college-writing-009335.en: Whatever definition you choose, be sure to provide specific instances so that readers can fully understand your meaning of the term.
college-writing-009335.zh: 无论您选择什么定义，请务必提供特定的实例，以便读者可以完全理解您对该术语的含义。

college-writing-009336.en: For example, in writing an essay on patriotism, you might describe three people whom you see as truly patriotic.
college-writing-009336.zh: 例如，在写一篇关于爱国主义的文章时，你可能会描述三个你认为真正爱国的人。

college-writing-009337.en: Writing about each person will help ensure that readers see and understand the term as you do.
college-writing-009337.zh: 写每个人将有助于确保读者像您一样看到和理解该术语。

college-writing-009338.en: As with other essay forms, keep your audience in mind.
college-writing-009338.zh: 与其他论文形式一样，请记住您的听众。

college-writing-009339.en: If, for instance, you were proposing a new definition of “patriotism,” an audience of war veterans might require different examples than would an audience of college students.
college-writing-009339.zh: 例如，如果您提出了“爱国主义”的新定义，退伍军人的观众可能需要与大学生观众不同的例子。

college-writing-009340.en: Development through Prewriting Brian, the author of “Definition of a Football Fan,” spent a few minutes jotting down a number of possible essay topics, keeping in mind the question, “What do I know a good deal about, or at least have an interest in exploring?”
college-writing-009340.zh: 通过预写《足球迷的定义》的作者布赖恩的预写，花了几分钟记下了一些可能的论文主题，记住了一个问题，“我知道什么，或者至少有兴趣探索？”

college-writing-009341.en: Here is his list of topic ideas.
college-writing-009341.zh: 这是他的主题想法列表。

college-writing-009342.en: Notice how they reflect Brian’s interest in outdoor activities, sports, and history:
college-writing-009342.zh: 注意它们如何反映布赖恩对户外活动、运动和历史的兴趣：

college-writing-009346.en: A reenactor of Civil War battles

college-writing-009347.en: People who vacation at national parks

college-writing-009352.en: After looking over his list, Brian selected “A Green Bay Packers fan” as the topic that interested him most.
college-writing-009352.zh: 在查看了他的名单后，布赖恩选择了“绿湾包装工队的球迷”作为他最感兴趣的话题。

college-writing-009353.en: He thought it would lend itself well to a lighthearted essay that defined the sometimes eccentric fans of the Wisconsin football team.
college-writing-009353.zh: 他认为这很适合一篇轻松的文章，该文章定义了威斯康星州足球队有时古怪的球迷。

college-writing-009354.en: After giving it further thought, however, Brian decided to broaden his topic to
college-writing-009354.zh: 然而，在进一步考虑之后，布赖恩决定将他的主题扩大到

college-writing-009355.zh: 第338章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009357.en: “I realized I just didn’t know enough specifically about Green Bay fans to support an entire essay,” he said.
college-writing-009357.zh: “我意识到我对绿湾球迷的了解不够多，无法支持整篇文章，”他说。

college-writing-009358.en: A person who likes to think in visual terms, Brian decided to develop ideas and details about his topic by clustering his thoughts.
college-writing-009358.zh: 一个喜欢以视觉方式思考的人，布赖恩决定通过聚集他的想法来发展关于他的主题的想法和细节。

college-writing-009359.en: When he looked over his diagram, Brian realized that he could characterize each of his three main topics as a kind of extremism.
college-writing-009359.zh: 当他查看他的图表时，布赖恩意识到他可以将他的三个主要主题中的每一个描述为一种极端主义。

college-writing-009360.en: He decided on a thesis (he would define football fans as extreme and unreasonable) that would indicate his essay’s plan of development (“they behave unreasonably, they are unreasonable about the past, and they are extremely loyal”).
college-writing-009360.zh: 他决定发表一篇论文（他将球迷定义为极端和不合理），以表明他的文章的 展开提纲（“他们的行为不合理，他们对过去不合理，而且他们非常忠诚”）。

college-writing-009361.en: With that thesis and plan of development in mind, Brian wrote the first draft of his essay.
college-writing-009361.zh: 考虑到这篇论文和 展开提纲，布赖恩写了他的论文的初稿。

college-writing-009364.en: Football fans are by definition eccentric.
college-writing-009364.zh: 足球迷们根据定义是古怪的。

college-writing-009365.en: They behave unreasonably, they are unreasonable about the past, and they are extremely loyal.
college-writing-009365.zh: 他们表现得不合理，对过去不合理，而且非常忠诚。

college-writing-009366.en: If their team gives away something free, the fans rush to the stadium to get the hat or whatever.
college-writing-009366.zh: 如果他们的球队免费赠送一些东西，球迷们会冲到体育场去拿帽子或其他什么。

college-writing-009367.en: Football fans just plain behave unreasonably.
college-writing-009367.zh: 足球迷只是不合理地行事。

college-writing-009368.en: Baseball fans get similarly enthusiastic when their favorite teams give away some attractive freebie.
college-writing-009368.zh: 当他们最喜欢的球队赠送一些有吸引力的免费赠品时，棒球迷也会变得同样热情。

college-writing-009369.en: But football fans are even worse.

college-writing-009370.en: Football fans freeze themselves in order to watch their favorite game.
college-writing-009370.zh: 足球迷们为了观看他们最喜欢的比赛而冻结自己。

college-writing-009371.en: In addition, football fans decorate their houses with football-related items of every kind.
college-writing-009371.zh: 此外，足球迷们用各种与足球相关的物品来装饰他们的房子。

college-writing-009372.en: When they go to a game, which they do as often as possible, the true football fans make themselves look ridiculous by decorating themselves in weird team-related ways.
college-writing-009372.zh: 当他们尽可能多地去看一场比赛时，真正的足球迷通过以与球队相关的奇怪方式装饰自己，让自己看起来很荒谬。

college-writing-009373.en: At the game, these fans do the “wave” more than they watch the game.
college-writing-009373.zh: 在比赛中，这些球迷的“挥手”比他们观看比赛的次数多。

college-writing-009374.en: Football fans love to talk about the past.

college-writing-009375.en: They talk about William “Refrigerator” Perry’s 1985 Super Bowl touchdown as though it had happened last week.
college-writing-009375.zh: 他们谈论威廉“冰箱”佩里 1985 年的超级碗触地得分，就好像它发生在上周一样。

college-writing-009376.en: They discuss Peyton Manning’s fourth-quarter comeback in 2009.
college-writing-009376.zh: 他们讨论了佩顿曼宁在 2009 年第四季度的复出。

college-writing-009377.en: They reminisce about Patrick Mahomes’s fourthquarter pass that secured a win over Denver.
college-writing-009377.zh: 他们回忆起帕特里克·马霍姆斯（Patrick Mahomes）的第四节传球，该传球确保了对丹佛的胜利。

college-writing-009378.en: They think everyone should be as excited as they are about such old stories.
college-writing-009378.zh: 他们认为每个人都应该对这些古老的故事感到兴奋。

college-writing-009379.en: Last of all, football fans are extremely loyal to the team of their choice.
college-writing-009379.zh: 最后，足球迷对他们选择的球队非常忠诚。

college-writing-009380.en: Football fans wear their team T-shirts and warm-up jackets everywhere, even to work.
college-writing-009380.zh: 足球迷到处都穿着他们的球队 T 恤和热身夹克，甚至可以工作。

college-writing-009381.en: Of course, if they have to dress up in business clothes, they can’t do that.
college-writing-009381.zh: 当然，如果他们必须穿上商务服装，他们就做不到。

college-writing-009382.en: Should their beloved team lose three in a row, their fans may begin to criticize their team.
college-writing-009382.zh: 如果他们心爱的球队连续输掉三场，他们的球迷可能会开始批评他们的球队。

college-writing-009383.en: But these reactions only hide their broken hearts.
college-writing-009383.zh: 但这些反应只会隐藏他们破碎的心。

college-writing-009384.en: They still obsessively watch each game and read all the newspaper stories about it.
college-writing-009384.zh: 他们仍然痴迷地观看每场比赛并阅读所有关于它的报纸故事。

college-writing-009385.en: This intense loyalty makes fans dangerous.
college-writing-009385.zh: 这种强烈的忠诚使粉丝变得危险。

college-writing-009386.en: To anyone who dares to say to a loyal fan that another team is better or to anyone wandering near the home cheering section wearing the jacket of the opposing team, physical damage is a real possibility.
college-writing-009386.zh: 对于任何敢于对忠实粉丝说另一支球队更好的人或穿着对方球队的队伍在主场欢呼区附近徘徊的人来说，身体伤害是一个真正的可能性。

college-writing-009387.en: Incidents of violence in football stadiums have increased in recent years and are a matter of growing concern.
college-writing-009387.zh: 近年来，足球场的暴力事件有所增加，是一个越来越受关注的问题。

college-writing-009388.zh: 足球迷真的表现得很荒谬。

college-writing-009389.en: They behave unreasonably, they are unreasonable about the past, and they’re too loyal.
college-writing-009389.zh: 他们的行为不合理，他们对过去不合理，而且他们太忠诚了。

college-writing-009451.zh: 当今广告中的宣传技巧

college-writing-009453.en: Americans, adults and children alike, are being seduced.
college-writing-009453.zh: 美国人、成人和儿童都被引诱。

college-writing-009457.en: Because the seducers and the brainwashers are the advertisers we willingly invite into our homes.
college-writing-009457.zh: 因为诱惑者和洗脑者是我们愿意邀请到我们家中的广告商。

college-writing-009458.en: We are victims, content─even eager─to be victimized.
college-writing-009458.zh: 我们是受害者，内容——甚至渴望成为受害者。

college-writing-009459.en: We read advertisers’ propaganda messages on social media and news sources; we watch their alluring images on television.
college-writing-009459.zh: 我们在社交媒体和新闻来源上阅读广告商的宣传信息； 我们在电视上观看他们迷人的图像。

college-writing-009460.en: We absorb their messages and images into our subconscious.
college-writing-009460.zh: 我们将他们的信息和图像吸收到我们的潜意识中。

college-writing-009461.en: We all do it─even those of us who claim to see through advertisers’ tricks and therefore feel immune to advertising’s charm.
college-writing-009461.zh: 我们都这样做了——即使是我们这些声称看穿广告商的技巧并因此对广告的魅力感到免疫的人。

college-writing-009462.en: Advertisers lean heavily on propaganda to sell products, whether the “products” are a brand of toothpaste, a candidate for office, or a particular political viewpoint.
college-writing-009462.zh: 广告商严重依赖宣传销售产品，无论“产品”是牙膏品牌、办公室候选人还是特定的政治观点。

college-writing-009463.en: Propaganda is a systematic effort to influence people’s opinions, to win them over to a certain view or side.
college-writing-009463.zh: 宣传是一种系统性的努力，旨在影响人们的意见，将他们吸引到某个观点或一边。

college-writing-009464.en: Propaganda is not necessarily concerned with what is true or false, good or bad.
college-writing-009464.zh: 宣传不一定关注什么是真假，好坏。

college-writing-009465.en: Propagandists simply want people to believe the messages being sent.
college-writing-009465.zh: 宣传者只是希望人们相信发送的信息。

college-writing-009466.en: Often, propagandists will use outright lies or more subtle deceptions to sway people’s opinions.
college-writing-009466.zh: 通常，宣传者会使用直接的谎言或更微妙的欺骗来影响人们的意见。

college-writing-009467.en: In a propaganda war, any tactic is considered fair.
college-writing-009467.zh: 在宣传战争中，任何策略都被认为是公平的。

college-writing-009468.en: When we hear the word “propaganda,” we usually think of a foreign menace: anti-American messages broadcast by a totalitarian regime or brainwashing tactics practiced on hostages.
college-writing-009468.zh: 当我们听到“宣传”这个词时，我们通常会想到外国的威胁：极权政权传播的反美信息或对人质实施的洗脑策略。

college-writing-009469.en: Although propaganda may seem relevant only in the political arena, the concept can be applied fruitfully to the way products and ideas are sold in advertising.
college-writing-009469.zh: 尽管宣传似乎仅在政治领域相关，但该概念可以有效地应用于广告中产品和创意的销售方式。

college-writing-009470.en: Indeed, the vast majority of us are targets in advertisers’ propaganda war.
college-writing-009470.zh: 事实上，我们中的绝大多数人都是广告商宣传战争的目标。

college-writing-009471.en: Every day, we are bombarded with slogans, print and Internet pop-up ads, commercials, packaging claims, billboards, trademarks, logos, and designer brands─all forms of propaganda.
college-writing-009471.zh: 每天，我们都会被口号、印刷和互联网弹出式广告、广告、包装声明、广告牌、商标、标志和设计师品牌——所有宣传形式的宣传。

college-writing-009472.en: One study reports that each of us, during an average day, is exposed to over five hundred advertising claims of various types.
college-writing-009472.zh: 一项研究报告称，我们每个人在平均一天中都会接触到五百多种不同类型的广告声明。

college-writing-009474.zh: 第342章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009475.en: may even increase in the future, since current trends include ads on movie screens, shopping carts, and even public television.
college-writing-009475.zh: 未来甚至可能增加，因为当前的趋势包括电影屏幕、购物车甚至公共电视上的广告。

college-writing-009476.en: What kind of propaganda techniques do advertisers use?
college-writing-009476.zh: 广告商使用什么样的宣传技巧？

college-writing-009479.en: Name calling is a propaganda tactic in which negatively charged names are hurled against the opposing side or competitor.
college-writing-009479.zh: 辱骂是一种宣传策略，其中负荷的名字被投向对方或竞争对手。

college-writing-009480.en: By using such names, propagandists try to arouse feelings of mistrust, fear, and hate in their audiences.
college-writing-009480.zh: 通过使用这些名字，宣传者试图在观众中引起不信任、恐惧和仇恨的感觉。

college-writing-009481.en: For example, a political advertisement may label an opposing candidate a “loser,” “fence-sitter,” or “warmonger.”
college-writing-009481.zh: 例如，政治广告可能会将对方候选人标记为“失败者”、“围栏保姆”或“Warmonger”。

college-writing-009482.en: Depending on the advertiser’s target market, labels such as “a friend of big business” or “a dues-paying member of the party in power” can be the epithets that damage an opponent.
college-writing-009482.zh: 根据广告商的目标市场，“大企业的朋友”或“当权党的会费成员”等标签可能是损害对手的绰号。

college-writing-009483.en: Ads for products may also use name calling.
college-writing-009483.zh: 产品广告也可能使用点名。

college-writing-009484.en: An American manufacturer may refer, for instance, to a “foreign car” in its commercial─not an “imported” one.
college-writing-009484.zh: 例如，一家美国制造商可能会在其商业中提到一辆“外国汽车”——而不是“进口”汽车。

college-writing-009485.en: The label of foreignness will have unpleasant connotations in many people’s minds.
college-writing-009485.zh: 外来的标签在许多人的脑海中会带有不愉快的内涵。

college-writing-009486.en: A childhood rhyme claims that “names can never hurt me,” but name calling is an effective way to damage the opposition, whether it is another car maker or a congressional candidate.
college-writing-009486.zh: 童年押韵声称“名字永远不会伤害我”，但辱骂是损害反对派的有效方式，无论是另一位汽车制造商还是国会候选人。

college-writing-009488.en: Using glittering generalities is the opposite of name calling.
college-writing-009488.zh: 使用闪闪发光的一般性与辱骂相反。

college-writing-009489.en: In this case, advertisers surround their products with attractive─and slippery─words and phrases.
college-writing-009489.zh: 在这种情况下，广告商用有吸引力的——和滑溜溜的——词和短语来包围他们的产品。

college-writing-009490.en: They use vague terms that are difficult to define and that may have different meanings to different people: freedom, democratic, all-American, patriotic, and justice.
college-writing-009490.zh: 他们使用难以定义的、可能对不同人有不同含义的含糊术语：自由、民主、全美、爱国和正义。

college-writing-009491.en: Many such words have strong affirmative overtones.
college-writing-009491.zh: 许多这样的词都有强烈的肯定语气。

college-writing-009492.en: This kind of language stirs positive feelings in people, feelings that may spill over to the product or idea being pitched.
college-writing-009492.zh: 这种语言在人们中激起了积极的感觉，这些感觉可能会溢出到产品或想法上。

college-writing-009493.en: As with name calling, the emotional response may overwhelm logic.
college-writing-009493.zh: 与辱骂一样，情绪反应可能会压倒逻辑。

college-writing-009494.en: Target audiences accept the product without thinking very much about what the glittering generalities mean─or whether they even apply to the product.
college-writing-009494.zh: 目标受众在不考虑闪闪发光的一般性含义或是否适用于产品的情况下接受产品。

college-writing-009495.en: After all, how can anyone oppose “truth, justice, and the American way”?
college-writing-009495.zh: 毕竟，谁能反对“真相、正义和美国的方式”？

college-writing-009496.en: The ads for politicians and political causes often use glittering generalities because such “buzzwords” can influence votes.
college-writing-009496.zh: 政治家和政治事业的广告经常使用闪闪发光的一般性，因为这样的“流行语”会影响选票。

college-writing-009497.en: Election slogans include high-sounding but basically empty phrases like the following:
college-writing-009497.zh: 选举口号包括高音但基本上是空的短语，如下所示：

college-writing-009499.en: (That’s nice, but is he a better candidate than his opponent?)
college-writing-009499.zh: （这很好，但他是比对手更好的候选人吗？）

college-writing-009502.zh: “他们会让这个国家再次伟大。”

college-writing-009503.en: (What does “great” mean? Does “great” mean the same thing to others as it does to me?)
college-writing-009503.zh: （“伟大”是什么意思？“伟大”对其他人来说和对我的意思一样吗？）

college-writing-009506.en: “If you love America, vote for Rosa Martineau.” (If I don’t vote for Martineau, does that mean I don’t love America?)
college-writing-009506.zh: “如果你爱美国，请投票给罗莎·马丁诺。” （如果我不投票给马丁诺，这是否意味着我不爱美国？）

college-writing-009507.en: Ads for consumer goods are also sprinkled with glittering generalities.
college-writing-009507.zh: 消费品广告也散布着闪闪发光的一般性。

college-writing-009508.en: Product names, for instance, are supposed to evoke good feelings: Luvs diapers, Stayfree feminine hygiene products, Joy liquid detergent, Loving Care hair color, Almost Home cookies, Yankee Doodle pastries.
college-writing-009508.zh: 例如，产品名称应该唤起良好的感觉：Luvs 尿布、Stayfree 女性卫生用品、Joy Liquid 洗涤剂、爱护头发颜色、几乎家用饼干、洋基涂鸦糕点。

college-writing-009511.en: Product slogans lean heavily on vague but comforting phrases: . . . General Electric “brings good things to life,” and Dow Chemical “lets you do great things.”
college-writing-009511.zh: 产品口号严重依赖模糊但令人欣慰的短语： . 。 。 通用电气“给生活带来美好的事物”，陶氏化学“让你做伟大的事情”。

college-writing-009512.en: Chevrolet, we are told, is the “heartbeat of America,” and Chrysler boasts that “Inspiration comes standard.”
college-writing-009512.zh: 我们被告知雪佛兰是“美国的心跳”，克莱斯勒吹嘘“灵感是标准的”。

college-writing-009514.en: In transfer, advertisers try to improve the image of a product by associating it with specific symbols like the American flag, a powerful animal, or an image that evokes a feeling of comfort.
college-writing-009514.zh: 在转移中，广告商试图通过将产品与美国国旗、强大的动物或唤起舒适感的图像等特定符号联系起来来改善产品的形象。

college-writing-009515.en: The advertisers hope that the prestige attached to the symbol will carry over to the product.
college-writing-009515.zh: 广告商希望附在符号上的声望能够延续到产品上。

college-writing-009516.en: Many companies use transfer devices to identify their products: AmeriFreight’s logo is an eagle with wings reflective of the American flag; Liberty Mutual’s corporate symbol is the Statue of Liberty; The Hartford’s logo is a powerful buck with a full rack of antlers; Allstate’s name is cradled by a pair of protective hands.
college-writing-009516.zh: 许多公司使用转移设备来识别他们的产品：Amerifreight 的标志是一只长着美国国旗的翅膀的鹰； Liberty Mutual 的企业标志是自由女神像； 哈特福德的标志是一块强大的雄鹿，里面有满满的鹿角； Allstate 的名字被一双保护性手托着。

college-writing-009517.en: Corporations also use the transfer technique when they sponsor television shows.
college-writing-009517.zh: 公司在赞助电视节目时也会使用转移技术。

college-writing-009518.en: These shows function as symbols of dignity and class.
college-writing-009518.zh: 这些显示作为尊严和阶级的象征。

college-writing-009519.en: Koch Industries, through multiple foundations, has supported many public television series like Nova; The Home Depot is a major sponsor of Ask This Old House; Johnson & Johnson sponsors the PBS News Hour.
college-writing-009519.zh: Koch Industries 通过多个基金会支持了许多公共电视连续剧，如 Nova； Home Depot 是 Ask This Old House 的主要赞助商； 强生赞助 PBS 新闻时间。

college-writing-009520.en: In this way, corporations can reach an educated, influential audience and, perhaps, improve their public image by associating themselves with quality programming.
college-writing-009520.zh: 通过这种方式，公司可以接触到受过教育的、有影响力的受众，并通过将自己与优质节目联系起来来改善他们的公众形象。

college-writing-009521.en: Political ads, of course, practically wrap themselves in the flag.
college-writing-009521.zh: 当然，政治广告实际上将自己包裹在国旗中。

college-writing-009522.en: Ads for a political candidate often show either the Washington Monument, a Fourth of July parade, the Stars and Stripes, a bald eagle soaring over the mountains, or a white-steepled church on the village green.
college-writing-009522.zh: 政治候选人的广告通常会显示华盛顿纪念碑、七月四日的游行、星条旗、在山上翱翔的秃鹰，或者村庄的绿地上的白色陡峭教堂。

college-writing-009523.en: The national anthem or “America the Beautiful” may play in the background.
college-writing-009523.zh: 国歌或“美洲美洲”可能会在背景中播放。

college-writing-009524.en: Such appeals to Americans’ love of country can surround the candidate with an aura of patriotism and integrity.
college-writing-009524.zh: 这种对美国人热爱国家的呼吁可以包围候选人的爱国主义和正直的光环。

college-writing-009526.en: The testimonial is one of advertisers’ most-loved and most-used propaganda techniques.
college-writing-009526.zh: 推荐信是广告商最受欢迎和最常用的宣传技巧之一。

college-writing-009527.en: Similar to the transfer device, the testimonial capitalizes on the admiration people have for a celebrity to make the product shine more brightly─even though the celebrity is not an expert on the product being sold.
college-writing-009527.zh: 与转移装置类似，证明利用人们对名人的钦佩来使产品更加闪亮——尽管名人不是所销售产品的专家。

college-writing-009528.en: Print and television ads offer a nonstop parade of testimonials: here’s Betty White eating a Snickers bar; Jennifer Garner and Samuel L. Jackson both ask “What’s in your Wallet?” for Capital One; dozens of celebrities (including Rihanna) advertise clothing brands; and Sophia Vergara touts Head & Shoulders dandruff shampoo as the best.
college-writing-009528.zh: 印刷和电视广告提供了不间断的推荐游行：这是贝蒂怀特吃士力架； 詹妮弗·加纳和塞缪尔·杰克逊都问“你的钱包里有什么？” 对于资本一； 数十名名人（包括蕾哈娜）宣传服装品牌； Sophia Vergara 将头部和肩部头皮屑洗发水称为最好的。

college-writing-009529.en: Testimonials can sell movies, too; ads for films often feature favorable comments by well-known reviewers.
college-writing-009529.zh: 推荐书也可以卖电影； 电影广告通常会受到知名审稿人的好评。

college-writing-009530.en: And, in recent years, testimonials have played an important role in pitching books; the backs of paperbacks frequently list complimentary blurbs by celebrities.
college-writing-009530.zh: 而且，近年来，推荐书在推销书籍中发挥了重要作用。 平装本的背面经常列出名人的免费简介。

college-writing-009531.en: Political candidates, as well as their ad agencies, know the value of testimonials.
college-writing-009531.zh: 政治候选人以及他们的广告机构都知道推荐的价值。

college-writing-009532.en: Taylor Swift lent her support and music to the presidential campaign of Joe Biden, while Herschel Walker threw his support behind Donald J. Trump.
college-writing-009532.zh: 泰勒斯威夫特为乔·拜登的总统竞选提供了支持和音乐，而赫歇尔·沃克则支持唐纳德·J·特朗普。

college-writing-009533.en: Even controversial social issues are debated by celebrities.
college-writing-009533.zh: 甚至有争议的社会问题也被名人辩论。

college-writing-009534.en: Celebrities like Leonardo DiCaprio and Shailene Woodley regularly speak out about the dangers of climate change.
college-writing-009534.zh: 莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥和谢琳·伍德利等名人经常公开谈论气候变化的危险。

college-writing-009535.zh: 第344章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009536.en: As illogical as testimonials sometimes are (Pepsi’s Michael Jackson, for instance, was a health-food adherent who did not drink soft drinks), they are effective propaganda.
college-writing-009536.zh: 就像推荐信有时是不合逻辑的（例如，百事可乐的迈克尔杰克逊是一个不喝软饮料的健康食品追随者），它们是有效的宣传。

college-writing-009537.en: We like the person so much that we like the product too.
college-writing-009537.zh: 我们非常喜欢这个人，以至于我们也喜欢这个产品。

college-writing-009539.en: The plain folks approach says, in effect, “Buy me or vote for me. I’m just like you.”
college-writing-009539.zh: 平淡的人的做法实际上是说，“买我或投票给我。我和你一样。”

college-writing-009540.en: Regular folks will surely like Bob Evans’s Down on the Farm Country Sausage or good old-fashioned Countrytime Lemonade.
college-writing-009540.zh: 普通人肯定会喜欢 Bob Evans 的《农场乡村香肠》或老式乡村柠檬水。

college-writing-009541.en: Some ads emphasize the idea that “we’re all in the same boat.”
college-writing-009541.zh: 一些广告强调“我们都在同一条船上”的想法。

college-writing-009542.en: We see people video chatting for just the reasons we do─to put the baby on the phone to Grandma or to tell Mom we love her.
college-writing-009542.zh: 我们看到人们在视频聊天的原因只是我们这样做的原因——把婴儿打电话给奶奶或告诉妈妈我们爱她。

college-writing-009543.en: And how do these folksy, warmhearted (usually saccharine1) scenes affect us?
college-writing-009543.zh: 这些民俗、热情（通常是 saccharine1）的场景如何影响我们？

college-writing-009544.en: They’re supposed to make us feel that T-Mobile─the multinational corporate giant─has the same values we do.
college-writing-009544.zh: 他们应该让我们感觉到T-Mobile——跨国企业巨头——具有与我们相同的价值观。

college-writing-009545.en: Similarly, we are introduced to the little people at Ford, the ordinary folks who work on the assembly line, not to bigwigs in their executive offices.
college-writing-009545.zh: 同样，我们被介绍给福特的小人，在流水线上工作的普通人，而不是他们的行政办公室里的大人物。

college-writing-009546.en: What’s the purpose of such an approach?
college-writing-009546.zh: 这种方法的目的是什么？

college-writing-009547.en: To encourage us to buy a car built by these honest, hardworking “everyday people” who care about quality as much as we do.
college-writing-009547.zh: 鼓励我们购买一辆由这些诚实、勤奋的“日常人”制造的汽车，他们和我们一样关心质量。

college-writing-009548.en: Political advertisements make almost as much use of the “plain folks” appeal as they do of transfer devices.
college-writing-009548.zh: 政治广告利用“普通人”的吸引力几乎与使用转移设备的吸引力一样多。

college-writing-009549.en: Candidates wear hard hats, farmers’ caps, and assembly-line coveralls.
college-writing-009549.zh: 候选人戴安全帽、农民帽和流水线连体衣。

college-writing-009550.en: They jog around the block and carry their own luggage through the airport.
college-writing-009550.zh: 他们在街区周围慢跑，并携带自己的行李穿过机场。

college-writing-009551.en: The idea is to convince voters that the candidates are average people, not the elite─not wealthy lawyers or executives but common citizens.
college-writing-009551.zh: 这个想法是让选民相信候选人是普通人，而不是精英——不是富有的律师或高管，而是普通的公民。

college-writing-009553.en: When people say that “the cards were stacked against me,” they mean that they were never given a fair chance.
college-writing-009553.zh: 当人们说“卡片对我不利”时，他们的意思是他们从来没有得到过公平的机会。

college-writing-009554.en: Applied to propaganda, card stacking means that one side may suppress or distort evidence, tell half-truths, oversimplify the facts, or set up a “straw man”─a false target─to divert attention from the issue at hand.
college-writing-009554.zh: 适用于宣传，卡片堆叠是指一方可以压制或扭曲证据，说半实话，过分简化事实，或者设置“稻草人”——一个虚假的目标——将注意力从手头的问题上转移出来。

college-writing-009555.en: Card stacking is a difficult form of propaganda both to detect and to combat.
college-writing-009555.zh: 卡片堆叠是一种难以检测和战斗的宣传形式。

college-writing-009556.en: When a candidate claims that an opponent has “changed his mind five times on this important issue,” we tend to accept the claim without investigating whether the candidate had good reasons for changing his mind.
college-writing-009556.zh: 当候选人声称对手“在这个重要问题上五次改变主意”时，我们倾向于接受这一主张，而没有调查候选人是否有充分的理由改变主意。

college-writing-009557.en: Many people are simply swayed by the distorted claim that the candidate is “waffling” on the issue.
college-writing-009557.zh: 许多人只是被扭曲的说法所左右，即候选人在这个问题上“胡扯”。

college-writing-009558.en: Advertisers often stack the cards in favor of the products they are pushing.
college-writing-009558.zh: 广告商经常堆积卡片以支持他们正在推动的产品。

college-writing-009559.en: They may, for instance, use what are called “weasel words.”
college-writing-009559.zh: 例如，他们可以使用所谓的“黄鼠语”。

college-writing-009560.en: These are small words that usually slip right past us, but that make the difference between reality and illusion.
college-writing-009560.zh: 这些是通常从我们身边溜走的小词，但它们会产生现实和幻觉的区别。

college-writing-009561.en: The weasel words are underlined in the following claims:
college-writing-009561.zh: 黄鼠狼词在以下声明中有下划线：

college-writing-009562.en: “Helps control dandruff symptoms.” (The audience usually interprets this as stops dandruff.)
college-writing-009562.zh: “有助于控制头皮屑症状。” （观众通常将此解释为停止头皮屑。）

college-writing-009563.en: “Most dentists surveyed recommend sugarless gum for their patients who chew gum.” (We hear the “most dentists” and “for their patients,” but we don’t think about how many were surveyed or whether or not the dentists first recommended that the patients not chew gum at all.)
college-writing-009563.zh: “大多数接受调查的牙医建议为咀嚼口香糖的患者推荐无糖口香糖。” （我们听到“大多数牙医”和“为他们的患者”，但我们没有考虑过有多少人接受过调查，或者牙医是否首先建议患者根本不要嚼口香糖。）

college-writing-009566.en: “Sticker price $1,000 lower than most comparable cars.” (How many is “most”? What car does the advertiser consider “comparable”?)
college-writing-009566.zh: “标价比大多数同类汽车低1,000美元。” （“大多数”是多少？广告商认为什么车“可比较”？）

college-writing-009567.en: Advertisers also use a card stacking trick when they make an unfinished claim.
college-writing-009567.zh: 广告商在提出未完成的声明时也会使用卡片堆叠技巧。

college-writing-009568.en: For example, they will say that their product has “twice as much pain reliever.”
college-writing-009568.zh: 例如，他们会说他们的产品“止痛药是两倍”。

college-writing-009569.en: We are left with a favorable impression.
college-writing-009569.zh: 我们留下了良好的印象。

college-writing-009570.en: We don’t usually ask, “Twice as much pain reliever as what?”
college-writing-009570.zh: 我们通常不会问，“止痛药是什么？”

college-writing-009571.en: Or advertisers may make extremely vague claims that sound alluring but have no substance: Toyota’s “Oh, what a feeling!”; Coke’s “the real thing”; Cheerios’ “be happy be healthy.”
college-writing-009571.zh: 或者广告商可能会做出极其模糊的说法，听起来很诱人，但没有实质内容：丰田的“哦，多么有感觉！”； 可口可乐的“真实事物”； Cheerios的“快乐健康”。

college-writing-009572.en: Another way to stack the cards in favor of a certain product is to use scientific-sounding claims that are not supported by sound research.
college-writing-009572.zh: 堆叠卡片以支持某种产品的另一种方法是使用不受良好研究支持的科学性声明。

college-writing-009573.en: When Ford claimed that its LTD model was “400 percent quieter,” many people assumed that its LTD must be quieter than all other cars.
college-writing-009573.zh: 当福特声称其 LTD 车型“安静 400%”时，许多人认为其 LTD 必须比所有其他汽车都更安静。

college-writing-009574.en: When taken to court, however, Ford admitted that the phrase referred to the difference between the noise level inside and outside the LTD.
college-writing-009574.zh: 然而，当被告上法庭时，福特承认该短语指的是有限公司内外噪音水平之间的差异。

college-writing-009575.en: Other scientific-sounding claims use mysterious ingredients that are never explained as selling points: Retsyn, “special whitening agents,” “the ingredient doctors recommend.”
college-writing-009575.zh: 其他听起来很科学的说法使用了从未被解释为卖点的神秘成分：retsyn，“特殊美白剂”，“医生推荐的成分”。

college-writing-009577.en: In the bandwagon technique, advertisers pressure, “Everyone’s doing it. Why don’t you?”
college-writing-009577.zh: 在潮流技术中，广告商施压，“每个人都在做。你为什么不呢？”

college-writing-009578.en: This kind of propaganda often succeeds because many people have a deep desire not to be different.
college-writing-009578.zh: 这种宣传往往会成功，因为很多人都渴望不与众不同。

college-writing-009579.en: Political ads tell us to vote for the “winning candidate.”
college-writing-009579.zh: 政治广告告诉我们投票给“获胜的候选人”。

college-writing-009580.en: The advertisers know we tend to feel comfortable doing what others do; we want to be on the winning team.
college-writing-009580.zh: 广告商知道我们倾向于在做别人做的事情时感到自在； 我们想加入获胜的团队。

college-writing-009581.en: Or ads show a series of people proclaiming, “I’m voting for the senator. I don’t know why anyone wouldn’t.”
college-writing-009581.zh: 或者广告展示了一系列人宣称：“我在投票给参议员。我不知道为什么有人不会。”

college-writing-009582.en: Again, the audience feels under pressure to conform.
college-writing-009582.zh: 同样，观众感到压力要符合要求。

college-writing-009583.en: In the marketplace, the bandwagon approach lures buyers.
college-writing-009583.zh: 在市场上，潮流的方法吸引了买家。

college-writing-009584.en: Ads tell us that “nobody doesn’t like Sara Lee” (the message is that you must be weird if you don’t).
college-writing-009584.zh: 广告告诉我们“没有人不喜欢 Sara Lee”（信息是如果你不喜欢，你一定很奇怪）。

college-writing-009585.en: They tell us that “most people prefer Brand X two to one over other leading brands” (to be like the majority, we should buy Brand X).
college-writing-009585.zh: 他们告诉我们，“大多数人更喜欢二比一的品牌，而不是其他领先品牌”（与大多数人一样，我们应该购买品牌 X）。

college-writing-009586.en: If we don’t drink Pepsi, we’re left out of “the Pepsi generation.”
college-writing-009586.zh: 如果我们不喝百事可乐，我们就会被排除在“百事可乐一代”之外。

college-writing-009587.en: To take part in “America’s favorite health kick,” the National Dairy Council asks us, “Got Milk?”
college-writing-009587.zh: 为了参加“美国最喜欢的健康运动”，国家乳制品委员会问我们，“有牛奶吗？”

college-writing-009588.en: Maybelline advertisements for Great Lash mascara claim it is “America’s Favorite Mascara!”
college-writing-009588.zh: Great Lash睫毛膏的美宝莲广告声称这是“美国最喜欢的睫毛膏！”

college-writing-009589.en: Why do these propaganda techniques work?
college-writing-009589.zh: 为什么这些宣传技巧有效？

college-writing-009590.en: Why do so many of us buy the products, viewpoints, and candidates urged on us by propaganda messages?
college-writing-009590.zh: 为什么我们中的许多人会购买通过宣传信息敦促我们的产品、观点和候选人？

college-writing-009591.en: They work because they appeal to our emotions, not to our minds.
college-writing-009591.zh: 它们之所以起作用，是因为它们吸引了我们的情绪，而不是我们的思想。

college-writing-009592.en: Often, in fact, they capitalize on our prejudices and biases.
college-writing-009592.zh: 事实上，他们经常利用我们的偏见和偏见。

college-writing-009593.en: For example, if we are convinced that environmentalists are radicals who want to destroy America’s record of industrial growth and progress, then we will applaud the candidate who refers to them as “tree huggers.”
college-writing-009593.zh: 例如，如果我们确信环保主义者是想要破坏美国工业增长和进步记录的激进分子，那么我们将为将他们称为“树木拥抱者”的候选人鼓掌。

college-writing-009594.en: Clear thinking requires hard work: analyzing a claim, researching the facts, examining both sides of an issue, using logic to see the flaws in an argument.
college-writing-009594.zh: 清晰的思维需要努力工作：分析主张，研究事实，检查问题的双方，使用逻辑来查看论点中的缺陷。

college-writing-009595.en: Many of us would rather let the propagandists do our thinking for us.
college-writing-009595.zh: 我们中的许多人宁愿让宣传者为我们思考。

college-writing-009596.zh: 第346章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009597.en: Because propaganda is so effective, it is important to detect it and understand how it is used.
college-writing-009597.zh: 因为宣传非常有效，因此检测它并了解它的使用方式非常重要。

college-writing-009598.en: We may conclude, after close examination, that some propaganda sends a truthful, worthwhile message.
college-writing-009598.zh: 经过仔细研究，我们可以得出结论，一些宣传传递了一个真实、有价值的信息。

college-writing-009599.en: Some advertising, for instance, urges that we not drive drunk, that we become volunteers, or that we contribute to charity.
college-writing-009599.zh: 例如，一些广告敦促我们不要酒后驾车，我们成为志愿者，或者我们为慈善事业做出贡献。

college-writing-009600.en: Even so, we must be aware that propaganda is being used.
college-writing-009600.zh: 即便如此，我们必须意识到正在使用宣传。

college-writing-009601.en: Otherwise, we have consented to handing over to others our independence of thought and action.
college-writing-009601.zh: 否则，我们同意将我们的思想和行动的独立性交给他人。

college-writing-009603.en: 1. Which sentence best expresses the main idea of McClintock’s essay?
college-writing-009603.zh: 1. 哪句话最能表达麦克林托克论文的主要思想？

college-writing-009605.en: Americans may be exposed daily to over five hundred advertising claims
college-writing-009605.zh: 美国人每天可能会接触到五百多个广告声明

college-writing-009608.en: The testimonial takes advantage of the admiration people have for

college-writing-009609.en: celebrities, even though they have no expertise on the product being sold.
college-writing-009609.zh: 名人，尽管他们对所销售的产品没有专业知识。

college-writing-009611.en: People should detect and understand common propaganda techniques,
college-writing-009611.zh: 人们应该发现和理解常见的宣传技巧，

college-writing-009612.en: which appeal to the emotions rather than to logic.
college-writing-009612.zh: 它吸引了情感而不是逻辑。

college-writing-009614.en: Americans need to understand that advertising, a huge industry, affects
college-writing-009614.zh: 美国人需要明白，一个巨大的行业广告会影响广告

college-writing-009615.zh: 他们的生活方式有很多。

college-writing-009616.en: 2. Which statement would best serve as a topic sentence for paragraph 6?
college-writing-009616.zh: 2. 哪项陈述最适合作为第 6 段的 主题句？

college-writing-009618.en: Using glittering generalities is a technique that stirs positive feelings in
college-writing-009618.zh: 使用闪闪发光的一般性是一种激发积极情绪的技术

college-writing-009621.en: Using glittering generalities is the opposite of name calling.
college-writing-009621.zh: 使用闪闪发光的一般性与辱骂相反。

college-writing-009623.en: Glittering generalities use vague terms that have different meanings to
college-writing-009623.zh: 闪闪发光的一般性使用具有不同含义的模糊术语

college-writing-009624.en: them, so they affect people differently.
college-writing-009624.zh: 他们，所以它们对人们的影响不同。

college-writing-009626.en: Glittering generalities are used by politicians and political causes.
college-writing-009626.zh: 政治家和政治事业使用了闪闪发光的一般性。

college-writing-009628.en: 3. In paragraph 1, McClintock’s choice of words reveals her attitudes toward
college-writing-009628.zh: 3. 在第 1 段中，麦克林托克的措辞表明了她对

college-writing-009629.zh: 无论是宣传者还是公众。

college-writing-009630.en: What specific words reveal her attitudes, and what attitudes do they represent?
college-writing-009630.zh: 哪些具体的话语揭示了她的态度，它们代表了什么态度？

college-writing-009633.en: 4. What key term does McClintock define in paragraph 2?
college-writing-009633.zh: 4. 麦克林托克在第 2 段中定义了什么关键术语？

college-writing-009636.en: Where else in the essay does she use the technique of definition?
college-writing-009636.zh: 她在文章中还有什么地方使用定义的技术？

college-writing-009637.en: 5. McClintock provides abundant examples throughout her essay.
college-writing-009637.zh: 5. 麦克林托克在她的文章中提供了丰富的例子。

college-writing-009640.en: What does she accomplish with this technique?
college-writing-009640.zh: 她用这种技术完成了什么？

college-writing-009642.en: 6. List the parts of this essay that show its organization.
college-writing-009642.zh: 6. 列出这篇文章中展示其组织的部分。

college-writing-009643.en: 7. The main method of organization of paragraph 3 is
college-writing-009643.zh: 7. 第 3 款的主要组织方法是

college-writing-009648.en: 8. The author uses several transitions in paragraph 20.
college-writing-009648.zh: 8. 作者在第 20 段中使用了几个过渡。

college-writing-009651.en: 9. What is the relationship between the essay’s first paragraph and its concluding
college-writing-009651.zh: 9. 论文第一段与结尾有什么关系

college-writing-009653.en: 10. The conclusion of “Propaganda Techniques in Today’s Advertising” is made up of
college-writing-009653.zh: 10、《当今广告宣传技巧》的结论是

college-writing-009654.en: a. a summary of the techniques she discussed and a final thought.
college-writing-009654.zh: 一。 总结她讨论的技术和最后的想法。

college-writing-009655.en: b. a quotation about propaganda and its effects on people.
college-writing-009655.zh: B. 关于宣传及其对人的影响的引文。

college-writing-009656.en: c. final thoughts and a recommendation about remaining vigilant.
college-writing-009656.zh: c.  最后的想法和关于保持警惕的建议。

college-writing-009657.en: d. final questions that people need to ask themselves.
college-writing-009657.zh: D. 人们需要问自己的最后一个问题。

college-writing-009658.zh: 第348章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009659.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Definition
college-writing-009659.zh: 写一篇强调定义的论文

college-writing-009660.en: The term hero is used so much that it is at risk of losing its meaning.
college-writing-009660.zh: 英雄一词的使用如此之多，以至于它有失去意义的风险。

college-writing-009661.en: In this extended definition essay, you are to identify someone who has been a hero in your life and explain why that person is a hero.
college-writing-009661.zh: 在这篇扩展定义文章中，您要确定在您生活中一直是英雄的人，并解释为什么该人是英雄。

college-writing-009662.en: Your definition may identify sensory characteristics of your hero, compare your hero to another person who is not a hero, and/or compare your hero to the dictionary definition.
college-writing-009662.zh: 您的定义可能会识别您的英雄的感官特征，将您的英雄与不是英雄的另一个人进行比较，和/或将您的英雄与字典定义进行比较。

college-writing-009663.en: You may want to review Chapter 13, “Comparison and/or Contrast,” Chapter 8, “Description,” and Chapter 9, “Narration,” to incorporate different types of support for your profile.
college-writing-009663.zh: 您可能想查看第 13 章“比较和/或对比”，第 8 章，“描述”和第 9 章“叙述”，以包含对您的个人资料的不同类型的支持。

college-writing-009666.en: Look up the dictionary definition of hero and decide if it does or doesn’t
college-writing-009666.zh: 查找 Hero 的字典定义并决定它是否存在

college-writing-009667.en: support your idea of a hero.

college-writing-009669.en: Gather information about your subject by using a prewriting method of your
college-writing-009669.zh: 使用您的预写方法收集有关您的主题的信息

college-writing-009671.en: You will want to write down as much information as possible within a ten-minute period.
college-writing-009671.zh: 您需要在十分钟内写下尽可能多的信息。

college-writing-009672.en: Don’t worry about spelling, grammar, organization, or anything other than getting your thoughts down on the page.
college-writing-009672.zh: 除了将您的想法放在页面上之外，不要担心拼写、语法、组织或其他任何事情。

college-writing-009673.en: If ideas are still flowing at the end of ten minutes, keep on writing.
college-writing-009673.zh: 如果想法在十分钟结束时仍在流动，请继续写作。

college-writing-009675.en: Once you have finished getting your thoughts down, you should have a base
college-writing-009675.zh: 一旦你完成了你的想法，你应该有一个基础

college-writing-009676.en: of raw material that you can draw on in the next phase of your work.
college-writing-009676.zh: 您可以在下一阶段工作的原材料。

college-writing-009677.en: Judging from what you have produced, do you think you have enough material to support your essay?
college-writing-009677.zh: 从你制作的内容来看，你认为你有足够的材料来支持你的论文吗？

college-writing-009678.en: If so, keep following the steps below.
college-writing-009678.zh: 如果是这样，请继续遵循以下步骤。

college-writing-009679.en: If not, choose another person and spend about ten minutes generating ideas to see if they might be a better subject.
college-writing-009679.zh: 如果没有，请选择另一个人并花费大约十分钟的时间来产生想法，看看他们是否可能是一个更好的主题。

college-writing-009681.en: As you devise your opening paragraph, don’t begin with the overused phrase
college-writing-009681.zh: 当你设计你的开头段落时，不要从过度使用的短语开始

college-writing-009684.en: Remember that the thesis of your definition is a version of “What a hero means
college-writing-009684.zh: 请记住，您的定义的论点是“英雄的含义”的版本

college-writing-009686.en: ” Your thesis should demonstrate why this person is a hero to you.
college-writing-009686.zh: ” 你的论文应该证明为什么这个人对你来说是英雄。

college-writing-009688.en: You may find outlining to be a helpful organizational strategy for this essay.
college-writing-009688.zh: 您可能会发现大纲是本文的有用组织策略。

college-writing-009690.en: Now write the first draft of your essay.
college-writing-009690.zh: 现在写下你论文的初稿。

college-writing-009691.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-009691.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-009692.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-009692.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-009693.en: Keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of
college-writing-009693.zh: 牢记末尾四个基准清单中的问题

college-writing-009697.en: this chapter as you hear your own words, and ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-009697.zh: 这一章你听到你自己的话，并请你的朋友也回应它们。

college-writing-009698.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-009698.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-009699.en: Choose one of the terms below as the subject of an essay that emphasizes definition.
college-writing-009699.zh: 选择以下术语之一作为强调定义的文章的主题。

college-writing-009700.en: Each term refers to a certain kind of person.
college-writing-009700.zh: 每个术语指的是某种类型的人。

college-writing-009701.en: Good neighbor Busybody Whiner Con artist Optimist Pessimist Team player Bully Scapegoat Snob Practical joker Procrastinator Loner Type A Outlier Character Original Influencer Foodie Visionary Planner Colleague
college-writing-009701.zh: 好邻居 忙碌的抱怨 骗子 乐观主义者 悲观主义 团队 玩家 恶霸 scapegoat snob 恶作剧

college-writing-009704.en: As you devise your opening paragraph, you may want to refer to the dictionary
college-writing-009704.zh: 当您设计开头段落时，您可能需要参考字典

college-writing-009706.en: If so, be sure to use only one meaning of the term.
college-writing-009706.zh: 如果是这样，请确保仅使用该术语的一种含义。

college-writing-009707.en: (Dictionaries often provide several different meanings for a term.)
college-writing-009707.zh: （字典通常为一个术语提供几种不同的含义。）

college-writing-009708.en: Don’t begin your paper with the overused phrase “According to Webster. . . . ”
college-writing-009708.zh: 不要以“根据韦伯斯特的说法……”过度使用的短语开始你的论文。

college-writing-009714.zh: 350 第 2 部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-009716.en: Remember that the thesis of a definition essay is a version of “What X means
college-writing-009716.zh: 请记住，定义论文的论文是“x 的含义”的一个版本

college-writing-009718.en: ” The thesis presents what your experience has made you think the term actually means.
college-writing-009718.zh: ”这篇论文展示了你的经验让你认为这个词的实际含义。

college-writing-009720.en: As you plan your supporting paragraphs, think of different parts or qualities
college-writing-009720.zh: 当你计划你的支持段落时，想想不同的部分或品质

college-writing-009722.en: Here, for example, are the three-part divisions of the student essays considered in this chapter:
college-writing-009722.zh: 例如，这里是本章所考虑的学生论文的三部分部分：

college-writing-009723.en: Football fans are extreme in terms of their behavior, their fascination with the past, and their loyalty.
college-writing-009723.zh: 足球迷在他们的行为、对过去的迷恋和忠诚方面都是极端的。

college-writing-009724.en: Student zombies are the “living dead,” are controlled by a “mysterious force,” and are likely to suffer an “awful fate.”
college-writing-009724.zh: 学生僵尸是“活死人”，被“神秘力量”控制，很可能遭受“可怕的命运”。

college-writing-009726.en: Support each part of your division with either a series of examples or a single
college-writing-009726.zh: 用一系列示例或一个单一的示例支持您部门的每个部分

college-writing-009729.en: You may find outlining to be the most helpful prewriting strategy for your
college-writing-009729.zh: 您可能会发现轮廓是最有用的预写策略

college-writing-009731.en: As a guide, write your thesis and at least three supporting points in the spaces below.
college-writing-009731.zh: 作为指南，在下面的空格中写下你的论文和至少三个支持点。

college-writing-009734.en: REVISING Once you have the first draft of your essay completed, read it aloud to a friend or classmate.
college-writing-009734.zh: 修改论文的初稿后，大声朗读给朋友或同学。

college-writing-009735.en: The two of you should review it with the FOUR BASES Checklist in mind.
college-writing-009735.zh: 你们两个应该考虑到四个基础清单。

college-writing-009736.en: In this extended definition essay, you are to define a term from another course.
college-writing-009736.zh: 在这篇扩展定义文章中，您将定义另一门课程的术语。

college-writing-009737.en: For instance, if you are studying anthropology, you might define culture, or if you are studying criminal justice, you might define environmental crime.
college-writing-009737.zh: 例如，如果您正在学习人类学，您可能会定义文化，或者如果您正在学习刑事司法，您可能会定义环境犯罪。

college-writing-009738.en: Not only will you need to write an extended definition, but you should also create a persuasive tone for your essay in order to convince your audience that you truly understand the term and that your definition is a correct one.
college-writing-009738.zh: 你不仅需要写一个扩展的定义，而且你还应该为你的论文创造一种有说服力的语气，以说服你的听众你真正理解这个词，你的定义是正确的。

college-writing-009743.en: You will want to check Chapter 16, “Argument,” to help you create a persuasive tone.
college-writing-009743.zh: 您将需要查看第 16 章“论点”，以帮助您创建有说服力的语气。

college-writing-009746.en: As you devise your opening paragraph, it would be helpful to refer to the class
college-writing-009746.zh: 当你设计你的开头段落时，参考课程会很有帮助

college-writing-009747.en: in which you are studying the term in order to provide an introduction for the reader and to establish a context for the term.
college-writing-009747.zh: 您正在学习该术语，以便为读者提供介绍并为该术语建立上下文。

college-writing-009749.en: Your thesis should demonstrate why the term is important to understand in
college-writing-009749.zh: 你的论文应该证明为什么这个词对理解很重要

college-writing-009751.en: It should also describe how your own experience has influenced your understanding of what the term actually means.
college-writing-009751.zh: 它还应该描述您自己的经验如何影响您对该术语实际含义的理解。

college-writing-009753.en: As you plan your supporting paragraphs, you may find outlining to be a
college-writing-009753.zh: 当您计划支持段落时，您可能会发现 Outline 是一个

college-writing-009754.en: helpful organizational strategy for this essay emphasizing definition.
college-writing-009754.zh: 这篇文章强调定义的有用组织策略。

college-writing-009756.en: Now write the first draft of your essay.
college-writing-009756.zh: 现在写下你论文的初稿。

college-writing-009757.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-009757.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-009758.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-009758.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-009759.en: Keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter as you hear your own words, and ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-009759.zh: 当您听到自己的话时，请记住本章末尾的四个基础清单中的问题，并要求您的朋友也回复它们。

college-writing-009760.en: As you revise your essay through one or more additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-009760.zh: 当您通过一份或多份附加草稿修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-009761.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-009761.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-009762.en: In the past year, your school has had problems with parents demonstrating poor sportsmanship at school events.
college-writing-009762.zh: 在过去的一年里，您的学校遇到了家长在学校活动中表现出不良体育精神的问题。

college-writing-009763.en: At one football game, two parents started yelling at a player because he missed a pass.
college-writing-009763.zh: 在一场足球比赛中，两名父母开始对一名球员大喊大叫，因为他错过了传球。

college-writing-009764.en: At a theater production, several parents ridiculed a young girl who had forgotten her lines.
college-writing-009764.zh: 在剧院制作中，几位父母嘲笑了一个忘记台词的年轻女孩。

college-writing-009765.en: At a chess tournament, a mother whose child was losing started accusing everyone else of cheating.
college-writing-009765.zh: 在国际象棋比赛中，一位孩子正在失去的母亲开始指责其他人作弊。

college-writing-009766.en: The principal has decided to address this behavior, so he has asked you to create a handout, defining school standards and explaining what good sportsmanship is and how it applies to school events.
college-writing-009766.zh: 校长决定解决这种行为，因此他要求您创建一份讲义，定义学校标准，并解释什么是良好的体育精神以及它如何应用于学校活动。

college-writing-009767.en: Your definitions will need to focus on both attitudes and actions.
college-writing-009767.zh: 您的定义需要关注态度和行动。

college-writing-009768.en: You may want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” and Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” to help you develop and support your essay.
college-writing-009768.zh: 您可能想回顾第 8 章“描述”和第 10 章“示例”，以帮助您开发和支持您的论文。

college-writing-009771.zh: 第352章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009774.en: Does my thesis statement indicate why the term is important and how I define the term?
college-writing-009774.zh: 我的 中心论点句 是否表明该术语很重要以及我如何定义该术语？

college-writing-009775.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-009775.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-009777.en: Have I supported my definition with an extended example?
college-writing-009777.zh: 我是否通过扩展示例支持我的定义？

college-writing-009778.en: Do my details help explain my definition of the term?
college-writing-009778.zh: 我的详细信息是否有助于解释我对该术语的定义？

college-writing-009780.en: Have I consistently used a single method of development in each supporting paragraph?
college-writing-009780.zh: 我是否在每个支持段落中始终使用单一的开发方法？

college-writing-009781.en: Is there a clear sense of organization in my essay?
college-writing-009781.zh: 我的论文中是否有清晰的组织意识？

college-writing-009782.en: Does my essay have a conclusion that emphasizes the main idea and gives an impression of resolution to the essay?
college-writing-009782.zh: 我的论文是否有一个强调主要思想并给论文带来决心的印象的结论？

college-writing-009784.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-009784.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-009785.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-009785.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-009786.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-009786.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-009788.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-009788.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-009792.en: Used by permission of Townsend Press.
college-writing-009792.zh: 经 Townsend Press 许可使用。

college-writing-009793.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on divisionclassification • write an essay with emphasis on divisionclassification • revise an essay with emphasis on divisionclassification
college-writing-009793.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 开发一篇强调分裂分类的论文 • 写一篇强调分裂分类的论文 • 修改一篇强调分裂分类的论文

college-writing-009794.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize divisionclassification • one professional model essay that emphasizes divisionclassification
college-writing-009794.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调分裂分类的学生论文 • 一篇强调分裂分类的专业模型论文

college-writing-009796.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-009797.en: When you return home from your weekly trip to the supermarket with five bags packed with your purchases, how do you sort them out?
college-writing-009797.zh: 当您每周带着五个袋子装满您购买的东西回家时，您如何整理它们？

college-writing-009798.en: You might separate food items from nonfood items (like toothpaste, paper towels, and detergent).
college-writing-009798.zh: 您可能会将食品与非食品（如牙膏、纸巾和洗涤剂）分开。

college-writing-009799.en: Or you might divide and classify the items into groups intended
college-writing-009799.zh: 或者您可以将项目划分为预期的组

college-writing-009800.en: Visit an online library like the Library of Congress at http://www.loc.
college-writing-009800.zh: 访问 http://www.loc 之类的国会图书馆等在线图书馆。

college-writing-009801.en: gov and browse through the various categories.

college-writing-009802.en: If you are more interested in music, visit Pandora at http://www.pandora.com and browse the different categories of music.
college-writing-009802.zh: 如果您对音乐更感兴趣，请访问 http://www.pandora.com 并浏览不同类别的音乐。

college-writing-009803.en: Or, visit a site like Overstock at http://www.overstock.com and browse the categories of items for sale.
college-writing-009803.zh: 或者，在 http://www.overstock.com 访问 Overstock 等网站并浏览待售商品的类别。

college-writing-009804.en: Then design your own site selling, lending, or streaming something similar.
college-writing-009804.zh: 然后设计您自己的网站销售、借贷或流式传输类似的东西。

college-writing-009805.en: (You can be as creative as you like.)
college-writing-009805.zh: （你可以随心所欲地发挥创意。）

college-writing-009806.en: Provide at least five categories for your “product” and explain what distinguishes each one.
college-writing-009806.zh: 为您的“产品”提供至少五个类别，并解释每个类别的区别。

college-writing-009807.en: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
college-writing-009807.zh: 国会图书馆印刷和照片司

college-writing-009815.zh: 第354章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009816.en: for the freezer compartment, the refrigerator, and the kitchen cupboards.
college-writing-009816.zh: 用于冷冻室、冰箱和厨房橱柜。

college-writing-009817.en: You might even put the items into groups like “to be used tonight,” “to be used soon,” and “to be used last.”
college-writing-009817.zh: 您甚至可以将这些项目分成“今晚使用”、“很快使用”和“最后使用”等组。

college-writing-009818.en: Sorting supermarket items in such ways is just one simple example of how we spend a great deal of our time organizing our environment in one manner or another.
college-writing-009818.zh: 以这种方式对超市商品进行分类只是我们如何花费大量时间以一种或另一种方式组织环境的一个简单示例。

college-writing-009819.en: In this chapter, you will be asked to write an essay in which you divide or classify a subject according to a single principle.
college-writing-009819.zh: 在本章中，您将被要求写一篇文章，根据一个单一的原则对主题进行划分或分类。

college-writing-009820.en: To prepare for this assignment, first read the student essays and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-009820.zh: 为了准备这项作业，首先阅读学生的论文和模型论文，并解决随附的问题。

college-writing-009823.en: People often question what goes into “having fun.”
college-writing-009823.zh: 人们经常质疑“玩得开心”的内容。

college-writing-009824.en: For many, “fun” involves getting out of the house, seeing other people, having something interesting to look at, and enjoying a choice of activities, all at a reasonable price.
college-writing-009824.zh: 对许多人来说，“乐趣”包括走出家门，看到其他人，有一些有趣的东西看，并享受各种活动的选择，所有这些都是合理的价格。

college-writing-009825.en: Going out to dinner or to the movies may satisfy some of those desires, but often not all.
college-writing-009825.zh: 出去吃饭或看电影可能会满足其中的一些欲望，但通常不是全部。

college-writing-009826.en: However, an attractive alternative does exist in the form of the free-admission shopping mall.
college-writing-009826.zh: 然而，以免费入场购物中心的形式存在一个有吸引力的替代方案。

college-writing-009827.en: Teenagers, couples on dates, and the nuclear family can all be observed having a good time at the mall.
college-writing-009827.zh: 可以观察到青少年、情侣约会和核心家庭在商场玩得很开心。

college-writing-009828.en: Teenagers are drawn to the mall to pass time with pals and to see and be
college-writing-009828.zh: 青少年被吸引到商场与朋友们打发时间，看看和成为

college-writing-009830.en: The guys saunter by in sneakers, T-shirts, and jeans, carrying sodas and snacks from the food court.
college-writing-009830.zh: 这些家伙穿着运动鞋、T 恤和牛仔裤漫步，带着来自美食广场的苏打水和零食。

college-writing-009831.en: The girls stumble along in midriff-baring tank tops, with a cell phone tucked snugly in the rear pocket of their low-waisted jeans.
college-writing-009831.zh: 女孩们穿着露腰背心绊倒，低腰牛仔裤的后袋里紧贴着手机。

college-writing-009832.en: Traveling in a gang that resembles a wolf pack, the teenagers make the shopping mall their hunting ground.
college-writing-009832.zh: 在一个像狼群一样的团伙旅行中，这些青少年将购物中心变成了狩猎场。

college-writing-009835.en: Over the years shopping malls have evolved from one primary type—indoor enclosed spaces—to encompass a variety of possible layouts and types, including those like the one in this photo that are set up outdoors to resemble village streets.
college-writing-009835.zh: 多年来，购物中心已经从一种主要类型（室内封闭空间）演变而来，包括各种可能的布局和类型，包括像这张照片中的那些类似的那些设置在户外类似于乡村街道的那些。

college-writing-009836.en: As you read this essay, think about the types of shopping malls you have been to and the people you have observed.
college-writing-009836.zh: 当您阅读这篇文章时，想想您去过的购物中心类型和您观察到的人。

college-writing-009843.en: have obviously made a decision to attract all this teenage activity.
college-writing-009843.zh: 显然已经决定吸引所有这些青少年活动。

college-writing-009844.en: The kids’ raised voices and loud laughter can be heard from as far as half a mall away.
college-writing-009844.zh: 从半个商场可以听到孩子们提高的声音和大声的笑声。

college-writing-009845.en: They come to “pick up girls,” to “meet guys,” and just to “hang out.”
college-writing-009845.zh: 他们来“接女孩”，去“认识男人”，只是为了“出去玩”。

college-writing-009846.en: Couples find fun of another sort at shopping malls.
college-writing-009846.zh: 情侣在购物中心找到另一种乐趣。

college-writing-009847.en: The young lovers are easy to spot because they walk hand in hand, stopping to sneak a quick kiss after every few steps.
college-writing-009847.zh: 年轻的恋人很容易被发现，因为他们手拉手走，每隔几步就偷偷亲吻。

college-writing-009848.en: They first pause at a jewelry store window so that they can gaze at diamond engagement rings and platinum wedding bands.
college-writing-009848.zh: 他们首先在珠宝店的橱窗停留，这样他们就可以凝视钻石订婚戒指和铂金结婚戒指。

college-writing-009849.en: Then, they wander into furniture departments in the large mall stores.
college-writing-009849.zh: 然后，他们漫步到大型商场商店的家具部门。

college-writing-009850.en: Finally, they drift away, their arms wrapped around each other’s waist.
college-writing-009850.zh: 最后，他们飘走了，双臂环住了对方的腰。

college-writing-009851.en: Mom, Dad, little Toni, and Carlos visit the mall on Friday and Saturday evenings for inexpensive recreation.
college-writing-009851.zh: 周五和周六晚上，妈妈、爸爸、小托尼和卡洛斯参观了购物中心，享受廉价的娱乐活动。

college-writing-009852.en: Hearing the music of the antique carousel housed there, Toni begs to ride her favorite pony with its shining golden mane.
college-writing-009852.zh: 听到那里装有古董旋转木马的音乐，托尼恳求骑着她最喜欢的小马，它闪亮的金色鬃毛。

college-writing-009853.en: Carlos shouts, "I'm starving!" and drags the family toward the food court, where he detects the seductive odor of pizza.
college-writing-009853.zh: 卡洛斯喊道：“我饿了！” 并将家人拖向美食广场，在那里他发现了披萨的诱人气味。

college-writing-009854.en: Mom walks through a fabric store, running her hand over the soft velvets and slippery silks.
college-writing-009854.zh: 妈妈走过一家面料店，用手抚过柔软的天鹅绒和光滑的丝绸。

college-writing-009855.en: Meanwhile, Dad has wandered into a cooking store and is admiring the enameled cookware he’d love to buy someday.
college-writing-009855.zh: 与此同时，爸爸走进一家烹饪店，正在欣赏他希望有一天能买到的珐琅炊具。

college-writing-009856.en: The mall provides something special for every member of the family.
college-writing-009856.zh: 商场为每个家庭成员提供了一些特别的东西。

college-writing-009857.en: Sure, some people visit the mall in a brief, businesslike way, just to pick up a specific purchase or two.
college-writing-009857.zh: 当然，有些人以一种简短、商务的方式参观商场，只是为了购买一两次特定的商品。

college-writing-009858.en: But many more are shopping for inexpensive recreation.
college-writing-009858.zh: 但更多的人正在购买廉价的娱乐。

college-writing-009859.en: The teenagers, the dating couples, and the nuclear families all find cheap entertainment at the mall.
college-writing-009859.zh: 青少年、约会夫妇和核心家庭都在商场找到便宜的娱乐活动。

college-writing-009861.en: Netflix has become a mainstay in many people’s lives.
college-writing-009861.zh: Netflix已成为许多人生活中的中流砥柱。

college-writing-009862.en: Even before it was a streaming service, Netflix’s DVD delivery service allowed people to experience the excitement and wonder of the world of movies.
college-writing-009862.zh: 甚至在流媒体服务之前，Netflix 的 DVD 传送服务让人们体验到电影世界的兴奋和奇迹。

college-writing-009863.en: Netflix categorizes movies into genres like action comedy, horror, dramas, and cult films, which makes it very easy to pick a film according to one’s tastes and/or moods.
college-writing-009863.zh: Netflix 将电影分为动作喜剧、恐怖、戏剧和邪典电影等类型，这使得根据自己的品味和/或心情选择电影变得非常容易。

college-writing-009864.en: Netflix also allows five individual profiles for each account; these profiles allow family members to organize their own individual queues and get individualized recommendations from Netflix.
college-writing-009864.zh: Netflix 还为每个帐户允许五个单独的个人资料； 这些配置文件允许家庭成员组织自己的个人队列并从 Netflix 获得个性化的推荐。

college-writing-009865.en: The individual profiles and their corresponding queues tell a lot about the viewer.
college-writing-009865.zh: 各个配置文件及其相应的队列说明了很多关于查看器的信息。

college-writing-009866.en: In the group “Romance,” movies like To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before, Romance is a Bonus Book, and Roped are available.
college-writing-009866.zh: 在团体“浪漫”中，电影喜欢我以前爱过的所有男孩，浪漫是一本奖金书，并且可以使用绳索。

college-writing-009867.en: The viewer could spend hundreds of hours watching boy meets girl, boy and girl fall in love, boy and girl fight, boy and girl reunite.
college-writing-009867.zh: 观众可以花数百小时观看男孩遇见女孩、男孩和女孩坠入爱河、男孩和女孩的战斗、男孩和女孩的重聚。

college-writing-009869.zh: 第356章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009871.en: If, however, the viewer is looking for more holiday-specific movies, a quick search of “Romantic Christmas,” reveals hours more of fun with films like The Holiday Calendar, A Christmas Prince, The Princess Switch, and Operation Christmas Drop.
college-writing-009871.zh: 然而，如果观众正在寻找更多特定于假期的电影，那么快速搜索“浪漫圣诞节”会在节日日历、圣诞节王子、公主开关和圣诞节行动等电影中展示出更多的乐趣。

college-writing-009872.en: Finally, a quick search of “Love & Friendship” brings up another large group of movies and television shows like Outlander, Bridgerton, and Orange Is the New Black.
college-writing-009872.zh: 最后，对“爱与友谊”的快速搜索带来了另一大群电影和电视节目，如欧蓝德、布里杰顿和橙色是新的黑色。

college-writing-009873.en: Setting up a profile based solely on romance movies will provide hours of love and first kisses.
college-writing-009873.zh: 仅根据浪漫电影设置个人资料将提供数小时的爱和初吻。

college-writing-009874.en: It’s clear that the Netflix viewer who wants to binge-watch only “cheesy chick flicks” can find many different movies to fill the queue.
college-writing-009874.zh: 很明显，只想看“俗气的小鸡电影”的 Netflix 观众可以找到许多不同的电影来填补队列。

college-writing-009875.en: Not all Netflix viewers want to watch romantic movies; some want to spend their time watching more thoughtful and educational films.
college-writing-009875.zh: 并非所有 Netflix 观众都想看浪漫电影。 有些人想花时间观看更周到和更具教育意义的电影。

college-writing-009876.en: The category “Documentaries” is perfect for the more serious-minded Netflix customer; in fact, Netflix places enough importance on this category to have dedicated subcategories.
college-writing-009876.zh: “纪录片”类别非常适合头脑更严肃的 Netflix 客户； 事实上，Netflix 对这一类别的重视程度足以拥有专门的子类别。

college-writing-009877.en: In “Science & Nature Docs,” the viewer can find films like My Octopus Teacher, Night on Earth, and Spycraft.
college-writing-009877.zh: 在“科学与自然文档”中，观众可以找到像我的章鱼老师、地球之夜和间谍世界这样的电影。

college-writing-009878.en: By watching films in the “Biographical Documentaries” category, a person can learn about Nina Simone in What Happened, Miss Simone?
college-writing-009878.zh: 通过观看“传记纪录片”类别中的电影，一个人可以了解尼娜·西蒙娜发生的事情，西蒙娜小姐？

college-writing-009879.en: ; Natascha Kampusch in Natascha Kampusch; and Walter Mercado in Mucho Mucho Amor.
college-writing-009879.zh: ; Natascha Kampusch 的 Natascha Kampusch； 和 Mucho Mucho Amor 中的 Walter Mercado。

college-writing-009880.en: The best way to learn about musicians is through documentaries because old footage is usually included.
college-writing-009880.zh: 了解音乐家的最佳方式是通过纪录片，因为通常包括旧镜头。

college-writing-009881.en: For a person who wants to travel to exotic lands, but doesn’t have the money or time, the category “Travel & Adventure Documentaries” offers hours of discovery with titles like The Summit, a film about K2, the second highest mountain in the world; They Call It Myanmar, a film about Burma; and Rock the Park, a series of episodes about America’s national parks.
college-writing-009881.zh: 对于一个想去异国旅行但没有金钱或时间的人来说，“旅行与冒险纪录片”类别提供了数小时的发现，其中包括关于 K2 的电影，这是一部关于 K2 的电影，这是世界上第二高的山峰； 他们称之为缅甸，一部关于缅甸的电影； 和摇滚公园，关于美国国家公园的一系列剧集。

college-writing-009883.en: Like the “Documentaries” category, this category also has subcategories to help parents quickly find shows that are age or topic appropriate.

college-writing-009884.zh: 子类别是“2 至 4 岁的电影”和“11 至 12 岁的电影”。

college-writing-009885.en: There is also a subcategory called “Movies Based on Children’s Books”; it is suited to anyone—young or old—who wants to see favorite books come to life on the screen.
college-writing-009885.zh: 还有一个名为“基于儿童读物的电影”的子类别； 它适合任何希望看到最喜欢的书籍在屏幕上栩栩如生的人——无论老少。

college-writing-009886.en: Films such as these that are family-friendly and based on familiar stories offer hours of safe and enjoyable viewing.
