college-writing-009936.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Division-Classification Considering Purpose and Audience When writing an essay that emphasizes division and classification, your purpose is to present your audience with your own unique way of dividing and classifying particular topics.
college-writing-009936.zh: 撰写一篇强调划分分类的论文 考虑目的和受众 在撰写强调划分和分类的文章时，您的目的是向您的听众展示您自己独特的方式来划分和分类特定主题。

college-writing-009937.en: In order to write a successful essay, you will need to first choose a topic that interests readers and lends itself to support that can be divided and classified.
college-writing-009937.zh: 为了写一篇成功的论文，你需要首先选择一个读者感兴趣的主题，并借此支持可以划分和分类的支持。

college-writing-009938.en: Once you pick your topic and decide on the support you will use, you will then have to come up with your own specific sorting system─one that readers will be able to understand.
college-writing-009938.zh: 一旦你选择了你的主题并决定了你将使用的支持，你将不得不提出你自己的特定排序系统——读者将能够理解的一个系统。

college-writing-009939.en: For example, if your essay focuses on types of clothing, there are a number of ways to sort this topic into categories.
college-writing-009939.zh: 例如，如果您的文章侧重于服装类型，有多种方法可以将此主题分类。

college-writing-009940.en: You could divide clothing by the function it serves: shirts and jackets (to cover the upper body); pants and skirts (for the lower body); and shoes and socks (for the feet).
college-writing-009940.zh: 您可以根据它所提供的功能划分衣服：衬衫和夹克（覆盖上半身）； 裤子和裙子（用于下半身）； 和鞋子和袜子（为脚）。

college-writing-009941.en: Or you could divide clothes according to the materials they are made from: animal products, plant products, and synthetic materials.
college-writing-009941.zh: 或者你可以根据它们制成的材料划分衣服：动物产品、植物产品和合成材料。

college-writing-009942.en: A more interesting, and potentially humorous, way to divide clothes is by fashion: clothes that are stylish, clothes that are going out of style, and clothes that are so unattractive that they never were in style.
college-writing-009942.zh: 一种更有趣、更有趣的分割衣服的方式是时尚：时尚的衣服，过时的衣服，以及如此没有吸引力的衣服，以至于他们从未有过时尚。

college-writing-009943.en: Notice that in all three of these cases, the broad topic of clothing has been divided into categories according to a particular principle (function, materials, and fashion).
college-writing-009943.zh: 请注意，在所有这三种情况下，服装的广泛主题都根据特定的原则（功能、材料和时尚）分为类别。

college-writing-009944.en: When you divide your topic for your essay, be sure to come up with your own division principle and make it clear to your readers.
college-writing-009944.zh: 当您为论文划分主题时，请务必提出您自己的划分原则，并让您的读者清楚。

college-writing-009946.en: Once you’ve selected your topic and figured out how to divide it, you will need to provide specific details so that readers fully understand the categories you created.
college-writing-009946.zh: 一旦您选择了主题并弄清楚了如何划分它，您将需要提供具体的细节，以便读者完全了解您创建的类别。

college-writing-009947.en: For the example about fashion above, you might classify plaid bell-bottom pants as part of the “going out of style” category, while blue jeans might belong in the “clothes that are stylish” group and a mustard-yellow velour jacket might fit in the “never stylish” group.
college-writing-009947.zh: 以上面的时尚为例，您可以将格子喇叭裤归类为“走出风格”类别的一部分，而蓝色牛仔裤可能属于“时尚服装”组，芥末黄色丝绒夹克可能属于“永远不会” 时尚”组。

college-writing-009948.en: Whatever divisions you establish, be sure to include enough details to make your division-classification method─your main point─clear to your readers.
college-writing-009948.zh: 无论您建立什么部门，请务必包含足够的细节，以使您的部门分类方法——您的主要观点——向您的读者清楚。

college-writing-009949.en: Equally important, keep your audience in mind.
college-writing-009949.zh: 同样重要的是，请牢记您的受众。

college-writing-009950.en: An audience of fashion-conscious young people, for instance, would probably have very different opinions about what is and isn’t stylish than an audience of middle-aged bankers.
college-writing-009950.zh: 例如，有时尚意识的年轻人的观众可能对什么是时尚的和不时尚的中年银行家的观众有着非常不同的看法。

college-writing-009951.en: Or an audience made up of the parents of middle-school students who are clamoring for “epic” clothes would have much more interest in clothing styles than the parents of students about to enter college.
college-writing-009951.zh: 或者由正在呼吁“史诗”服装的中学生家长组成的观众对服装风格的兴趣远远超过即将进入大学的学生的家长。

college-writing-009952.en: Development through Prewriting Julia, the writer of “Mall People,” believed from her observations that “people at malls” would make a good topic for an essay that emphasizes division-classification.
college-writing-009952.zh: 通过预写“购物中心人”的作者 Julia 的发展，他认为“商场里的人”将成为一篇强调分裂分类的文章的好话题。

college-writing-009953.en: But she did not immediately know how she wanted to group those people or what she wanted to say about them.
college-writing-009953.zh: 但她并不立即知道她想如何对这些人进行分组，或者她想对他们说些什么。

college-writing-009954.en: She decided to begin her prewriting by making a list of observations about mall shoppers.
college-writing-009954.zh: 她决定通过列出对购物中心购物者的观察来开始她的预写作。

college-writing-009955.en: Here is what she came up with:

college-writing-009958.en: Crowds around special displays—automobiles, kiddie rides
college-writing-009958.zh: 人群周围的特殊展示——汽车、儿童游乐设施

college-writing-009959.en: Older people walking in mall for exercise
college-writing-009959.zh: 走在商场锻炼的老年人

college-writing-009961.en: Women getting made over at makeup counter
college-writing-009961.zh: 女人在化妆柜台改头换面

college-writing-009963.en: Lots of people talking and laughing rather than shopping
college-writing-009963.zh: 很多人说话和笑而不是购物

college-writing-009964.en: Interviewers stopping shoppers to fill out questionnaires
college-writing-009964.zh: 采访者阻止购物者填写问卷

college-writing-009965.en: Kids hanging out, meeting each other

college-writing-009966.zh: 第360章 论文发展模式

college-writing-009967.en: As Julia reviewed her list, she concluded that the three largest groups of “mall people” were families with children, groups of teens, and dating couples.
college-writing-009967.zh: 当 Julia 回顾她的名单时，她得出的结论是，最大的三组“购物者”是有孩子的家庭、青少年群体和约会夫妇。

college-writing-009968.en: She decided to organize her essay around those three groups.
college-writing-009968.zh: 她决定围绕这三个群体组织她的论文。

college-writing-009969.en: To further flesh out her idea, she created a scratch outline that her essay would follow.
college-writing-009969.zh: 为了进一步充实她的想法，她创建了一个从她的论文将遵循的草案大纲。

college-writing-009970.en: Here is the scratch outline Julia prepared:
college-writing-009970.zh: 这是 Julia 准备的 Scratch Outline：

college-writing-009971.en: Mall offers inexpensive fun for several groups
college-writing-009971.zh: 商场为几个团体提供廉价的乐趣

college-writing-009984.en: Julia’s list and outline prepared her to write the first draft of her essay.
college-writing-009984.zh: 朱莉娅的名单和大纲让她准备写下她论文的初稿。

college-writing-009986.en: Malls aren’t only places to go shopping.
college-writing-009986.zh: 商场不仅仅是购物的地方。

college-writing-009987.en: They also offer free or at least cheap fun and activities for lots of people.
college-writing-009987.zh: 他们还为很多人提供免费或至少便宜的乐趣和活动。

college-writing-009988.en: Teenagers, dating couples, and families all like to visit the mall.
college-writing-009988.zh: 青少年、约会夫妇和家庭都喜欢参观购物中心。

college-writing-009989.en: Teenagers love to roam the mall in packs, like wolves.
college-writing-009989.zh: 青少年喜欢成群结队地在商场里漫游，就像狼一样。

college-writing-009990.en: They often dress alike, depending on the latest fashion.
college-writing-009990.zh: 他们经常穿着相似，这取决于最新的时尚。

college-writing-009991.en: They’re noisy and sometimes rude, and mall security officers sometimes kick them out of the building.
college-writing-009991.zh: 他们吵闹，有时粗鲁，商场保安有时会把他们踢出大楼。

college-writing-009992.en: Then they find somewhere else to go, maybe one of the warehouse-sized
college-writing-009992.zh: 然后他们找到其他地方去，也许是仓库大小的之一

college-writing-009996.en: Development through Revising After Julia completed her first draft, she put it aside.
college-writing-009996.zh: 在 Julia 完成她的初稿后，通过修订进行开发，她把它放在一边。

college-writing-009997.en: She knew from previous experience that she was a better critic of her own writing after she took a break from it.
college-writing-009997.zh: 她从以前的经验中知道，在她休息一下后，她是对自己写作的更好批评者。

college-writing-009998.en: The following morning, when Julia read over her first draft, she noticed several places where it could be improved.
college-writing-009998.zh: 第二天早上，当 Julia 阅读她的初稿时，她注意到了几个可以改进的地方。

college-writing-009999.en: Here are the observations she put in her writing journal:
college-writing-009999.zh: 以下是她在写作日记中发表的意见：

college-writing-010001.en: Those places are fun, but they tend to be more expensive than just “hanging out” at the mall.
college-writing-010001.zh: 这些地方很有趣，但它们往往比在商场“闲逛”更贵。

college-writing-010002.en: Teens are usually not as interested in shopping at the mall as they are in picking up members of the opposite sex and seeing their friends.
college-writing-010002.zh: 青少年通常对在商场购物的兴趣不如他们对接异性成员和见朋友的兴趣。

college-writing-010003.en: Dating couples also enjoy wandering around the mall.
college-writing-010003.zh: 约会夫妇还喜欢在商场周围闲逛。

college-writing-010004.en: They are easy to spot because they walk along holding hands and sometimes kissing.
college-writing-010004.zh: 它们很容易被发现，因为它们手牵着手走路，有时接吻。

college-writing-010005.en: They stare at diamond rings and wedding bands and shop for furniture together.
college-writing-010005.zh: 他们盯着钻石戒指和结婚戒指，一起购买家具。

college-writing-010006.en: Sometimes they have spats and one of them stomps off to sulk on a bench for a while.
college-writing-010006.zh: 有时他们会吐口水，其中一个会在长凳上闷闷不乐一会儿。

college-writing-010007.en: Little kids and their parents make up a big group of mall-goers.
college-writing-010007.zh: 小孩子和他们的父母组成了一大群商场顾客。

college-writing-010008.en: There is something for every member of the family there.
college-writing-010008.zh: 那里的每个家庭成员都有一些东西。

college-writing-010009.en: There are usually some special displays that interest the kids, and Mom and Dad can always find things they like to window-shop for.
college-writing-010009.zh: 通常有一些特殊的展示让孩子们感兴趣，爸爸妈妈总能找到他们喜欢橱窗的东西。

college-writing-010010.en: Another plus for the family is that there is inexpensive food, like burgers and pizza, available at the mall’s food court.
college-writing-010010.zh: 这个家庭的另一个优点是商场的美食广场有便宜的食物，比如汉堡和比萨饼。

college-writing-010011.en: • My first paragraph does present a thesis (malls offer inexpensive entertainment), and it
college-writing-010011.zh: • 我的第一段确实提出了一篇论文（购物中心提供廉价的娱乐），而且它

college-writing-010012.en: tells how I’m going to develop that thesis (by discussing three groups of people).
college-writing-010012.zh: 告诉我将如何开发该论文（通过讨论三组人）。

college-writing-010015.en: I think I could do a better job of drawing readers in by describing
college-writing-010015.zh: 我想我可以通过描述更好地吸引读者

college-writing-010017.en: • Some of the details in the essay aren’t necessary; they don’t support my main idea.
college-writing-010017.zh: • 论文中的一些细节不是必需的； 他们不支持我的主要想法。

college-writing-010019.en: instance, the stuff about teens being kicked out of the mall and about dating couples having
college-writing-010019.zh: 例如，关于青少年被赶出商场和约会夫妇的事情

college-writing-010020.en: fights doesn’t have anything to do with the entertainment malls provide.
college-writing-010020.zh: 战斗与娱乐中心提供的无关。

college-writing-010022.en: • Some of my statements that do support the main idea need more support.
college-writing-010022.zh: • 我的一些支持主要思想的陈述需要更多的支持。

college-writing-010024.en: when I say there are special displays that interest the kids in paragraph 4, I should give
college-writing-010024.zh: 当我在第 4 段中说孩子们感兴趣的特别展示时，我应该给

college-writing-010025.en: an example of such a display.

college-writing-010026.en: I should also back up the idea that many teens dress alike.
college-writing-010026.zh: 我还应该支持许多青少年穿着相似的想法。

college-writing-010027.en: With these observations in mind, Julia returned to her essay and revised it, producing the version that appears at the beginning of this chapter.
college-writing-010027.zh: 考虑到这些观察，朱莉娅回到她的文章并修改了它，制作了本章开头出现的版本。

college-writing-010028.zh: 第362章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010031.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-010031.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-010034.en: When I moved into a new house a few weeks ago, my books, as was natural, moved with me.
college-writing-010034.zh: 几周前，当我搬进新房子时，我的书本来很自然地和我一起搬家。

college-writing-010035.en: Strong, perspiring men shovelled them into packing-cases, and staggered with them to the van, cursing Caxton as they went.
college-writing-010035.zh: 强壮、出汗的人把它们铲进了包装箱里，然后跟着它们蹒跚地走到面包车上，边走边诅咒卡克斯顿。

college-writing-010036.en: On arrival at this end, they staggered with them into the room selected for my library, heaved off the lids of the cases, and awaited orders.
college-writing-010036.zh: 到达这里后，他们蹒跚着走进我的图书馆选择的房间，掀开箱子的盖子，等待命令。

college-writing-010037.en: The immediate need was for an emptier room.
college-writing-010037.zh: 迫切需要一个更空的房间。

college-writing-010038.en: Together we hurried the books into the new white shelves which awaited them, the order in which they stood being of no matter so long as they were off the floor.
college-writing-010038.zh: 我们一起把书赶到等待他们的新白色书架上，只要他们离开地板，他们所处的顺序就不变了。

college-writing-010039.en: Armful after armful was hastily stacked, the only pause being when (in the curious way in which these things happen) my own name suddenly caught the eye of the foreman.
college-writing-010039.zh: 一臂之力被匆忙堆积起来，唯一的停顿是（以奇怪的方式发生这些事情）我自己的名字突然引起了工头的注意。

college-writing-010040.en: “Did you write this one, sir?” he asked.
college-writing-010040.zh: “你写这一篇吗，先生？” 他问。

college-writing-010043.en: He glanced along the names of every armful after that, and appeared a little surprised at the number of books which I hadn’t written.
college-writing-010043.zh: 之后他扫了一眼每一臂的名字，对我没有写的书数量感到有些惊讶。

college-writing-010044.zh: 显然，这是一个随和的职业。

college-writing-010045.en: So we got the books up at last, and there they are still.
college-writing-010045.zh: 所以我们终于把书拿了起来，他们仍然在那里。

college-writing-010046.en: I told myself that when a wet afternoon came along I would arrange them properly.
college-writing-010046.zh: 我告诉自己，当一个潮湿的下午到来时，我会妥善安排它们。

college-writing-010047.en: When the wet afternoon came, I told myself that I would arrange them one of these fine morn-
college-writing-010047.zh: 当潮湿的下午到来时，我告诉自己，我会安排他们中的一个美好的早晨——

college-writing-010049.en: As they are now, I have to look along every shelf in the search for the book which I want.
college-writing-010049.zh: 就像他们现在一样，我必须在寻找我想要的书的每个书架上寻找。

college-writing-010050.en: To come to Keats is no guarantee that we are on the road to Shelley.
college-writing-010050.zh: 来到济慈并不能保证我们正在前往雪莱的路上。

college-writing-010051.en: Shelley, if he did not drop out on the way, is probably next to How to Be a Golfer Though Middle-aged.
college-writing-010051.zh: 雪莱，如果他没有在路上辍学，可能旁边是如何成为一名中年的高尔夫球手。

college-writing-010052.en: Having written as far as this, I had to get up and see where Shelley really was.
college-writing-010052.zh: 写到这一点之后，我不得不站起来看看雪莱到底在哪里。

college-writing-010053.en: It is worse than I thought.

college-writing-010054.en: He is between Geometrical Optics and Studies in New Zealand Scenery.
college-writing-010054.zh: 他介于几何光学和新西兰风景研究之间。

college-writing-010055.en: Ella Wheeler Wilcox, whom I find myself to be entertaining unawares, sits beside Anarchy or Order, which was apparently “sent in the hope that you will become a member of the Duty and Discipline Movement”─a vain hope, it would seem, for I have not yet
college-writing-010055.zh: 艾拉·惠勒·威尔科克斯（Ella Wheeler Wilcox），我发现自己在不知不觉中娱乐，他坐在无政府状态或秩序旁边，这显然是“希望你成为责任和纪律运动的一员”——似乎是徒劳的希望，因为我还没有

college-writing-010056.en: Think of a category of people, pets, or things in your life that mean a great deal.
college-writing-010056.zh: 想想你生活中意义重大的一类人、宠物或事物。

college-writing-010057.en: Create a scratch outline, with subcategories, for a division-classification essay on this topic.
college-writing-010057.zh: 为关于该主题的部门分类论文创建一个带有子类别的草稿大纲。

college-writing-010062.en: What I Found Out, by an English Governess, shares a corner with The Recreations of a Country Parson; they are followed by Villette and Baedeker’s Switzerland.
college-writing-010062.zh: 我在一位英国家庭教师中发现的与乡村牧师的娱乐活动有一个角落。 紧随其后的是 Villette 和 Baedeker 的瑞士。

college-writing-010063.en: Something will have to be done about it.

college-writing-010064.en: But I am wondering what is to be done.

college-writing-010065.en: If I gave you the impression that my books were precisely arranged in their old shelves, I misled you.
college-writing-010065.zh: 如果我给你的印象是我的书恰好放在他们的旧书架上，我误导了你。

college-writing-010066.en: They were arranged in the order known as “all anyhow.”
college-writing-010066.zh: 它们是按被称为“无论如何”的顺序排列的。

college-writing-010067.en: Possibly they were a little less “anyhow” than they are now, in that the volumes of any particular work were at least together, but that is all that can be claimed for them.
college-writing-010067.zh: 可能他们的“无论如何”比现在少一点，因为任何特定作品的数量至少都在一起了，但这就是他们可以声称的全部。

college-writing-010068.en: For years I put off the business of tidying them up, just as I am putting it off now.
college-writing-010068.zh: 多年来，我推迟了整理它们的业务，就像我现在推迟它一样。

college-writing-010069.en: It is not laziness; it is simply that I don’t know how to begin.
college-writing-010069.zh: 这不是懒惰； 只是我不知道如何开始。

college-writing-010070.en: Let us suppose that we decide to have all the poetry together.
college-writing-010070.zh: 假设我们决定将所有的诗歌放在一起。

college-writing-010072.en: But then Byron is eleven inches high (my tallest poet), and Beattie (my shortest) is just over four inches.
college-writing-010072.zh: 但拜伦有 11 英寸高（我最高的诗人），而 Beattie（我最矮的）只有 4 英寸多。

college-writing-010073.en: How foolish they will look standing side by side.
college-writing-010073.zh: 他们并肩站着看起来多么愚蠢。

college-writing-010074.en: Perhaps you don’t know Beattie, but I assure you that he was a poet.
college-writing-010074.zh: 也许你不认识比蒂，但我向你保证他是一位诗人。

college-writing-010075.zh: 他写了那些雄伟的台词：

college-writing-010076.en: The shepherd-swain of whom I mention made On Scotia’s mountains fed his little flock; The sickle, scythe or plough he never swayed─ An honest heart was almost all his stock.
college-writing-010076.zh: 我提到在斯科舍山上的牧羊人喂养了他的小群； 他从未摇过的镰刀、镰刀或犁——一颗诚实的心几乎是他所有的牲畜。

college-writing-010077.en: Of course, one would hardly expect a shepherd to sway a plough in the ordinary way, but Beattie was quite right to remind us that Edwin didn’t either.
college-writing-010077.zh: 当然，人们几乎不会指望一只牧羊人以普通的方式摇着一把犁，但比蒂提醒我们埃德温也没有。

college-writing-010078.en: Edwin was the name of the shepherd-swain.
college-writing-010078.zh: 埃德温是牧羊人的名字。

college-writing-010079.en: “And yet poor Edwin was no vulgar boy,” we are told a little further on in a line that should live.
college-writing-010079.zh: “然而可怜的埃德温不是粗俗的男孩，”我们被告知更进一步，应该活下去。

college-writing-010080.en: Well, having satisfied you that Beattie was really a poet, I can now return to my argument that an eleven-inch Byron cannot stand next to a four-inch Beattie, and be followed by an eight-inch Cowper, without making the shelf look silly.
college-writing-010080.zh: 好吧，如果你确信比蒂真的是一位诗人，我现在可以回到我的论点，即一个 11 英寸的拜伦不能站在一个 4 英寸的贝蒂旁边，后面跟着一个 8 英寸的考珀，不会让架子看起来很傻。

college-writing-010081.en: Yet how can I discard Beattie─ Beattie who wrote:
college-writing-010081.zh: 然而，我怎样才能丢弃 Beattie——Beattie 写道：

college-writing-010082.en: “And now the downy cheek and deepened voice Gave dignity to Edwin’s blooming prime.”
college-writing-010082.zh: “而现在，柔软的脸颊和加深的声音让埃德温盛开的巅峰时期赋予了尊严。”

college-writing-010084.en: If you arrange your books according to their contents you are sure to get an untidy shelf.
college-writing-010084.zh: 如果您根据它们的内容安排您的书籍，您一定会得到一个不整洁的书架。

college-writing-010085.en: If you arrange your books according to their size and colour you get an effective wall, but the poetically inclined visitor may lose sight of Beattie altogether.
college-writing-010085.zh: 如果您根据它们的大小和颜色排列书籍，您会得到一堵有效的墙，但诗意倾向的访客可能会完全忽略比蒂。

college-writing-010086.en: Before, then, we decide what to do about it, we must ask ourselves that very awkward question, “Why do we have books on our shelves at all?”
college-writing-010086.zh: 那么，在此之前，我们决定如何处理它，我们必须问自己一个非常尴尬的问题，“为什么我们的书架上有书？”

college-writing-010087.en: It is a most embarrassing question to answer.
college-writing-010087.zh: 这是一个最令人尴尬的问题。

college-writing-010088.en: Of course, you think that the proper answer (in your own case) is an indignant protest that you bought them in order to read them, and that you put them on your shelves in order that you could refer to them when necessary.
college-writing-010088.zh: 当然，您认为正确的答案（在您自己的情况下）是愤怒的抗议，即您购买它们是为了阅读它们，并将它们放在架子上，以便您可以在必要时参考它们。

college-writing-010089.en: A little reflection will show you what a stupid answer that is.
college-writing-010089.zh: 一点点反思会告诉你这是一个多么愚蠢的答案。

college-writing-010090.en: If you only want to read them, why are some of them bound in morocco and half-calf and other expensive coverings?
college-writing-010090.zh: 如果您只想阅读它们，为什么其中一些装在摩洛哥和半小牛和其他昂贵的覆盖物中？

college-writing-010091.en: Why did you buy a first edition when a hundredth edition was so much
college-writing-010091.zh: 当一百个版本这么多的时候，你为什么买第一版

college-writing-010092.zh: 第364章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010094.en: Why have you got half a dozen copies of the Rubaiyat?
college-writing-010094.zh: 为什么你有六份 Rubaiyat 副本？

college-writing-010095.en: What is the particular value of this other book that you treasure it so carefully?
college-writing-010095.zh: 你如此珍惜它的另一本书的特殊价值是什么？

college-writing-010096.en: Why, the fact that its pages are uncut.
college-writing-010096.zh: 为什么，它的页面未切割的事实。

college-writing-010097.en: If you cut the pages and read it, the value would go.
college-writing-010097.zh: 如果你剪掉页面并阅读它，价值就会消失。

college-writing-010098.en: So, then, your library is not just for reference.
college-writing-010098.zh: 因此，您的库不仅仅是供参考。

college-writing-010099.en: You know as well as I do that it furnishes your room; that it furnishes it more effectively than does paint or mahogany or china.
college-writing-010099.zh: 你和我一样清楚，它为你的房间布置； 它比油漆、桃花心木或中国更有效地提供它。

college-writing-010100.en: Of course, it is nice to have the books there, so that one can refer to them when one wishes.
college-writing-010100.zh: 当然，有书在那里是件好事，这样人们就可以在需要时参考它们。

college-writing-010101.en: One may be writing an article on sea-bathing, for instance, and have come to the sentence which begins: “In the well-remembered words of Coleridge, perhaps almost too familiar to be quoted”─and then one may have to look them up.
college-writing-010101.zh: 例如，人们可能正在写一篇关于海浴的文章，并以这样的句子为开头：“在柯勒律治的记忆中，也许几乎太熟悉而无法引用”——然后人们可能不得不查一下。

college-writing-010102.en: On these occasions a library is not only ornamental but useful.
college-writing-010102.zh: 在这些情况下，图书馆不仅是装饰性的，而且是有用的。

college-writing-010103.en: But do not let us be ashamed that we find it ornamental.
college-writing-010103.zh: 但不要让我们为我们发现它的观赏性而感到羞耻。

college-writing-010104.en: Indeed, the more I survey it, the more I feel that my library is sufficiently ornamental as it stands.
college-writing-010104.zh: 事实上，我越是调查它，我就越觉得我的图书馆是足够的装饰性。

college-writing-010105.en: Any reassembling of the books might spoil the colour-scheme.
college-writing-010105.zh: 任何重新组装书籍都可能破坏配色方案。

college-writing-010106.en: Baedeker’s Switzerland and Villette are both in red, a colour which is neatly caught up again, after an interlude in blue, by a volume of Browning and Jevons’ Elementary Logic.
college-writing-010106.zh: 贝德克的瑞士和维莱特都是红色的，这种颜色在蓝色插曲之后再次巧妙地被布朗宁和杰文斯的基本逻辑所吸引。

college-writing-010107.en: We had a woman here only yesterday who said, “How pretty your books look,” and I am inclined to think that that is good enough.
college-writing-010107.zh: 昨天我们有一个女人在这里说，“你的书看起来多么漂亮”，我倾向于认为这已经足够好了。

college-writing-010108.en: There is a careless rapture about them which I should lose if I started to arrange them methodically.
college-writing-010108.zh: 如果我开始有条不紊地安排它们，我应该会失去一种粗心的狂喜。

college-writing-010109.en: But perhaps I might risk this to the extent of getting all their heads the same way up.
college-writing-010109.zh: 但也许我可能会冒险以同样的方式让他们的头脑变得相同。

college-writing-010110.en: Yes, on one of these fine days (or wet nights) I shall take my library seriously in hand.
college-writing-010110.zh: 是的，在这些美好的日子（或潮湿的夜晚）之一，我将认真对待我的图书馆。

college-writing-010111.en: There are still one or two books which are the wrong way round.
college-writing-010111.zh: 仍然有一两本书是错误的。

college-writing-010112.en: I shall put them the right way round.
college-writing-010112.zh: 我会把它们放在正确的方向上。

college-writing-010114.en: 1. Which of the following statements best represents the main idea of the
college-writing-010114.zh: 1. 以下哪项陈述最能代表

college-writing-010116.en: a. Milne likes his library and wants to show it off to people.
college-writing-010116.zh: 一。 米尔恩喜欢他的图书馆，想向人们炫耀。

college-writing-010117.en: b. Milne recognizes that his library currently lacks any type of organization.
college-writing-010117.zh: B. 米尔恩认识到他的图书馆目前缺乏任何类型的组织。

college-writing-010118.en: c. Milne thinks that all libraries should be organized alphabetically.
college-writing-010118.zh: c.  Milne 认为所有库都应该按字母顺序排列。

college-writing-010119.en: d. Milne asserts that libraries are meant to furnish a room.
college-writing-010119.zh: D. 米尔恩断言，图书馆旨在布置一个房间。

college-writing-010120.en: 2. What is the topic sentence for paragraph 8?
college-writing-010120.zh: 2. 第 8 段的 主题句 是什么？

college-writing-010123.en: 3. Milne claims that a library furnishes a room better than what?
college-writing-010123.zh: 3. Milne 声称图书馆比什么更好？

college-writing-010126.en: 4. Milne makes a claim that people who buy books just to read them aren’t
college-writing-010126.zh: 4. 米尔恩声称，为了阅读而购买书籍的人不是

college-writing-010128.en: Which of the following does he NOT use as support for this claim?
college-writing-010128.zh: 他不使用以下哪项来支持这一主张？

college-writing-010129.en: a. Some books are bound in expensive coverings like morocco and half-calf.
college-writing-010129.zh: 一。 有些书被装在昂贵的覆盖物中，如摩洛哥和半小牛。

college-writing-010130.en: b. First editions are more expensive than a hundredth edition.
college-writing-010130.zh: B. 第一版比一百版贵。

college-writing-010131.en: c. Buying books and not opening them or “cutting” the pages.
college-writing-010131.zh: c.  购买书籍而不是打开它们或“剪切”页面。

college-writing-010132.en: d. Buying books to arrange in color-schemes in the library.
college-writing-010132.zh: D. 购买书籍以在图书馆的配色方案中排列。

college-writing-010133.en: 5. In paragraph 3, Milne states that his books were arranged in the order known
college-writing-010133.zh: 5. 在第 3 段中，Milne 指出他的书是按照已知的顺序排列的

college-writing-010135.en: 6. What three different ways does Milne suggest he could organize his library?
college-writing-010135.zh: 6. Milne 建议他可以组织他的图书馆的哪三种不同方式？

college-writing-010137.en: 7. Which method of organization does Milne use in his essay?
college-writing-010137.zh: 7. Milne 在他的论文中使用哪种组织方法？

college-writing-010140.en: 8. In paragraphs 4 and 5, Milne creates continuity through repetition.
college-writing-010140.zh: 8. 在第 4 段和第 5 段中，米尔恩通过重复创造了连续性。

college-writing-010142.en: major words or names does he repeat in these paragraphs?
college-writing-010142.zh: 他在这些段落中重复了主要词或名字吗？

college-writing-010144.en: 9. Which method best describes the introduction to “My Library”?
college-writing-010144.zh: 9. 哪种方法最能描述“我的图书馆”的介绍？

college-writing-010146.en: b. idea that it is the opposite of the one to be developed
college-writing-010146.zh: B. 认为它与要开发的一种相反

college-writing-010148.en: d. broad, general statement narrowing to thesis
college-writing-010148.zh: D. 宽泛的、一般性的陈述缩小到论文

college-writing-010149.en: 10. Milne ends his essay with a reference that looks back to paragraph 2.
college-writing-010149.zh: 10. Milne 以回顾第 2 段的参考文献结束了他的文章。

college-writing-010151.zh: 第366章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010152.en: Writing an Essay with Emphasis on Division-Classification
college-writing-010152.zh: 撰写一篇强调划分分类的论文

college-writing-010153.en: In this essay, you are to organize the music on your iPod, smartphone, or other music medium into at least three categories and explain how these categories
college-writing-010153.zh: 在这篇文章中，您将在您的 iPod、智能手机或其他音乐媒介上将音乐分为至少三类，并解释这些类别如何

college-writing-010155.en: You might have categories like “workouts” or “studying”; you might even have more specific categories like “music to listen to after breaking up with a guy.”
college-writing-010155.zh: 您可能有“锻炼”或“学习”等类别； 您甚至可能有更具体的类别，例如“与男人分手后要听的音乐”。

college-writing-010156.en: You will want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” and Chapter 9, “Narration,” to help you create support and details that will appeal to your reader.
college-writing-010156.zh: 您将需要查看第 8 章“描述”和第 9 章“叙述”，以帮助您创建吸引读者的支持和细节。

college-writing-010159.en: categories by type (sad, soul, jazz) or group (BTS, Apres, The Chicks) or by when you listen to the songs (with my parents, with friends, in the car).
college-writing-010159.zh: 按类型（悲伤、灵魂、爵士乐）或组（BTS、Apres、小鸡）或按类型（与我的父母、朋友一起、在车里）时的方式进行分类。

college-writing-010160.en: Whichever grouping principle you choose, be sure to come up with meaningful categories.
college-writing-010160.zh: 无论您选择哪种分组原则，请务必提出有意义的类别。

college-writing-010162.en: Decide on a thesis statement that will introduce your topic and claim.
college-writing-010162.zh: 决定一个 中心论点句 来介绍您的主题和主张。

college-writing-010164.zh: 可能的 中心论点句 如下：

college-writing-010165.en: My iPod is filled with thousands of songs that can be categorized to explain my moods.
college-writing-010165.zh: 我的 iPod 充满了数千首可以归类的歌曲，以解释我的心情。

college-writing-010166.en: My tablet is filled with songs that I listen to while I am with my parents, whenever I am alone, and when I am out with friends.
college-writing-010166.zh: 我的平板电脑里充满了我和父母在一起、每当我独自一人、和朋友出去的时候听的歌。

college-writing-010168.en: You may need to spend some extra time generating ideas to come up with
college-writing-010168.zh: 您可能需要花费一些额外的时间来产生想法来提出想法

college-writing-010169.zh: 对您的论文的额外支持。

college-writing-010170.en: You do not want to simply inventory the songs that are on your iPod; instead, you want to highlight one or two songs in each category, and explain why those songs are good examples for that category.
college-writing-010170.zh: 您不想简单地清点 iPod 上的歌曲； 相反，您想在每个类别中突出显示一两首歌曲，并解释为什么这些歌曲是该类别的好例子。

college-writing-010171.en: You may even want to incorporate a narrative with one or two songs in your essay as added support; gathering story ideas at this point will only help you as you draft your essay.
college-writing-010171.zh: 您甚至可能希望在您的文章中加入一两首歌曲的叙述作为额外的支持； 此时收集故事创意只会在您起草论文时对您有所帮助。

college-writing-010173.en: Now write the first draft of your essay.
college-writing-010173.zh: 现在写下你论文的初稿。

college-writing-010176.en: For at least ten minutes, look at the songs

college-writing-010177.en: you have on your iPod, smartphone, or tablet and group the songs into possible categories.
college-writing-010177.zh: 您可以在 iPod、智能手机或平板电脑上将歌曲分组到可能的类别中。

college-writing-010182.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-010182.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-010183.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-010183.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-010184.en: Keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter as you hear your own words, and ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-010184.zh: 当您听到自己的话时，请记住本章末尾的四个基础清单中的问题，并要求您的朋友也回复它们。

college-writing-010185.en: As you revise your essay, continue to refer to that checklist until you can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-010185.zh: 当您修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-010186.en: Many students find college to be more expensive than they expected, and as credit card companies continue to give cards away, more and more students are finding themselves deeper in debt than they need to be.
college-writing-010186.zh: 许多学生发现大学比他们预期的要贵，而且随着信用卡公司继续赠送卡片，越来越多的学生发现自己的债务比他们需要的还要深。

college-writing-010187.en: The best way to save money, or not overspend, is to create a budget that helps you keep track of your cash flow.
college-writing-010187.zh: 省钱或不超支的最佳方式是制定预算，帮助您跟踪现金流。

college-writing-010188.en: For this essay, you will need to classify common expenses that college students have and come up with a plan that helps students spend their money more wisely.
college-writing-010188.zh: 对于这篇文章，您需要对大学生的共同费用进行分类，并提出一个帮助学生更明智地花钱的计划。

college-writing-010189.en: You will want to review Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” and Chapter 16, “Argument,” to help you create an effective essay.
college-writing-010189.zh: 您将需要回顾第 10 章“示例”和第 16 章“论点”，以帮助您创建有效的论文。

college-writing-010192.en: First, you’ll need to classify typical student expenses.
college-writing-010192.zh: 首先，您需要对典型的学生费用进行分类。

college-writing-010194.en: them down by month or semester to help organize them.
college-writing-010194.zh: 他们按月或学期减少以帮助组织它们。

college-writing-010195.en: You should then divide these expenses into necessary and unnecessary.
college-writing-010195.zh: 然后，您应该将这些费用划分为必要和不必要的。

college-writing-010197.en: Once you have categorized students’ typical expenses, generate some ideas
college-writing-010197.zh: 一旦你对学生的典型费用进行了分类，就产生一些想法

college-writing-010198.en: that could help students save money.

college-writing-010199.en: You should provide ideas for savings in both categories.
college-writing-010199.zh: 您应该在这两个类别中提供节省的想法。

college-writing-010201.en: Create a thesis statement that introduces your topic and your proposal.
college-writing-010201.zh: 创建一个 中心论点句 来介绍您的主题和提案。

college-writing-010203.zh: 可能的 中心论点句 如下：

college-writing-010204.en: Students in college often go deeper into debt than they need to and should follow a simple plan to avoid this pitfall.
college-writing-010204.zh: 大学里的学生往往比他们需要的债务更深，并且应该遵循一个简单的计划来避免这种陷阱。

college-writing-010205.en: Students in college should organize and budget their expenses in order to avoid getting deeper in debt than necessary.
college-writing-010205.zh: 大学里的学生应该组织和预算他们的费用，以避免负债累累。

college-writing-010207.en: Now write the first draft of your essay.
college-writing-010207.zh: 现在写下你论文的初稿。

college-writing-010208.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-010208.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-010209.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-010209.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-010210.en: Keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist as you hear your own words, and ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-010210.zh: 当您听到自己的话时，请记住四个基准清单中的问题，并要求您的朋友也回复这些问题。

college-writing-010211.en: As you revise your essay, continue to refer to that checklist until you and your reader can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-010211.zh: 当您修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您和您的读者可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-010214.zh: 第368章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010215.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-010215.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-010216.en: In this essay that emphasizes division-classification, you will write with a specific purpose and for a specific audience.
college-writing-010216.zh: 在这篇强调划分分类的文章中，你将有特定的目的和特定的受众。

college-writing-010217.en: Imagine that your boss has asked you to prepare a section for the employee handbook.
college-writing-010217.zh: 想象一下，您的老板已要求您为员工手册准备一个部分。

college-writing-010218.en: The purpose of this section is to explain to new employees the three main types of clients they can expect to deal with and how to properly handle those clients.
college-writing-010218.zh: 本节的目的是向新员工解释他们可以期望与之打交道的三种主要类型的客户以及如何正确处理这些客户。

college-writing-010219.en: For instance, if you work at a salon and spa, you may explain there are three kinds of clients that you must regularly handle: the over-demanding customer, the environmentally conscious client, and the customer who never knows what they want.
college-writing-010219.zh: 例如，如果您在沙龙和水疗中心工作，您可以解释说您必须定期处理三种客户：要求过高的客户、具有环保意识的客户和永远不知道他们想要什么的客户。

college-writing-010220.en: Or maybe you work at a restaurant and the regular clients are business people, senior citizens, and families with small children.
college-writing-010220.zh: 或者，也许您在餐厅工作，普通客户是商务人士、老年人和有小孩的家庭。

college-writing-010221.en: Once you have identified the types, you will need to explain in detail how to effectively work with each specific group.
college-writing-010221.zh: 确定类型后，您将需要详细说明如何有效地与每个特定组合作。

college-writing-010222.en: You will want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” and Chapter 12, “Cause and Effect,” to help you create effective support for your essay.
college-writing-010222.zh: 您将需要查看第 8 章“描述”、第 10 章、“示例”和第 12 章“因果关系”，以帮助您为论文创造有效的支持。

college-writing-010225.zh: 部门分类清单：四个基地

college-writing-010227.en: Does my essay have a clearly stated thesis, including the topic and a dominant impression or principle of division?
college-writing-010227.zh: 我的文章是否有明确的论点，包括主题和分裂的主要印象或原则？

college-writing-010228.en: Does my essay describe the classifications in a clear, logical way?
college-writing-010228.zh: 我的文章是否以清晰、合乎逻辑的方式描述了分类？

college-writing-010229.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-010229.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-010231.en: Have I backed up my thesis with specific examples that support the divisions I am discussing?
college-writing-010231.zh: 我是否用支持我正在讨论的部门的具体例子来支持我的论文？

college-writing-010232.en: Is essential information missing that could help the reader understand my point?
college-writing-010232.zh: 是否缺少可以帮助读者理解我的观点的基本信息？

college-writing-010233.en: Are my support points detailed enough to create an interesting essay?
college-writing-010233.zh: 我的支持点是否足以创建一篇有趣的文章？

college-writing-010235.en: Is each one of the paragraphs in the body of my essay based on one of the categories I am describing?
college-writing-010235.zh: 我文章正文中的每一段都是基于我所描述的类别之一吗？

college-writing-010236.en: Do I have a concluding paragraph that provides a sense of completion to the essay?
college-writing-010236.zh: 我是否有一个结束的段落为论文提供了完成的感觉？

college-writing-010238.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-010238.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-010239.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-010239.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-010240.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-010240.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-010242.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-010242.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-010245.en: A. A., "My Library," in Not That It Matters.
college-writing-010245.zh: A.A.，“我的图书馆”，这并不重要。

college-writing-010246.en: New York: E. P. Dutton & Company.

college-writing-010247.en: Should cell phones be permitted in class?

college-writing-010248.en: Look at the photograph above and write an essay in which you argue for or against the use of cell phones in the classroom.
college-writing-010248.zh: 看看上面的照片，写一篇文章，你在教室里支持或反对使用手机。

college-writing-010249.en: Include at least three separate reasons that support your point of view.
college-writing-010249.zh: 至少包含三个支持您观点的独立原因。

college-writing-010250.zh: 爱丽儿·斯莱利/盖蒂图片社

college-writing-010251.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • develop an essay with emphasis on argument • write an essay with emphasis on argument • revise an essay with emphasis on argument
college-writing-010251.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何 • 撰写一篇强调论点的论文 • 写一篇强调论点的文章 • 修改一篇强调论证的文章

college-writing-010252.en: In addition, you will read and consider • two student essays that emphasize argument • one professional model essay that emphasizes argument
college-writing-010252.zh: 此外，您将阅读和考虑 • 两篇强调论点的学生论文 • 一篇强调论点的专业模型论文

college-writing-010254.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-010255.en: Do you know someone who enjoys a good argument?
college-writing-010255.zh: 你认识一个喜欢争论的人吗？

college-writing-010256.en: Such a person likes to challenge any sweeping statement we might make.
college-writing-010256.zh: 这样的人喜欢挑战我们可能做出的任何笼统的陈述。

college-writing-010257.en: For example, when we say something like “Ms. Lucci doesn’t grade fairly,” they come back with “Why do you say that? What are your reasons?”
college-writing-010257.zh: 例如，当我们说“Lucci 女士没有公平评分”之类的话时，他们会带着“你为什么这么说？你的原因是什么？”

college-writing-010258.en: Our questioner then listens carefully as we state our case, judging if we really do have solid evidence to support our point of view.
college-writing-010258.zh: 然后，当我们陈述我们的情况时，我们的提问者会仔细聆听，判断我们是否真的有确凿的证据来支持我们的观点。

college-writing-010259.en: We realize that saying, “Ms. Lucci just doesn’t, that’s all,” sounds weak and unconvincing, so we try to come up with stronger evidence to back up our statement.
college-writing-010259.zh: 我们意识到这句话，“Lucci 女士没有，仅此而已”听起来很虚弱和没有说服力，所以我们试图提出更有力的证据来支持我们的陈述。

college-writing-010260.en: Such a questioner may make us feel uncomfortable, but we may also feel grateful to them for helping us clarify our opinions.
college-writing-010260.zh: 这样的提问者可能会让我们感到不舒服，但我们也可能会感谢他们帮助我们澄清我们的意见。

college-writing-010263.en: The ability to put forth sound and compelling arguments is an important skill in everyday life.
college-writing-010263.zh: 提出声音和引人注目的论点的能力是日常生活中的一项重要技能。

college-writing-010264.en: You can use argument to make a point in a class discussion, persuade a friend to lend you money, or talk an employer into giving you a day off.
college-writing-010264.zh: 你可以用论证在课堂讨论中提出观点，说服朋友借钱给你，或者说服雇主给你休息一天。

college-writing-010265.en: Becoming skilled in clear, logical reasoning can also help you see through faulty arguments that others may make.
college-writing-010265.zh: 精通清晰、逻辑推理也可以帮助您看清其他人可能提出的错误论点。

college-writing-010266.en: You’ll become a better critic of advertisements, newspaper articles, political speeches, and the other persuasive appeals you see and hear every day.
college-writing-010266.zh: 您将成为您每天看到和听到的广告、报纸文章、政治演讲和其他有说服力的呼吁的更好批评者。

college-writing-010267.en: In this chapter, you will be asked to write an essay in which you defend a position with a series of solid reasons.
college-writing-010267.zh: 在本章中，您将被要求撰写一篇文章，在其中为您以一系列充分的理由捍卫一个立场。

college-writing-010268.en: In a general way, you have done the same thing─making a point and then supporting it─with all the essays in this book.
college-writing-010268.zh: 总的来说，你做了同样的事情——提出一个观点，然后用本书中的所有论文来支持它——它。

college-writing-010269.en: The difference here is that argument advances a controversial point, a point that at least some of your readers will not be inclined to accept.
college-writing-010269.zh: 这里的不同之处在于，论点提出了一个有争议的观点，这一点至少你的一些读者不会倾向于接受。

college-writing-010270.en: To prepare for this assignment, first read about five strategies you can use in advancing an argument.
college-writing-010270.zh: 为了准备这项作业，首先要了解可以用于推进论点的五种策略。

college-writing-010271.en: Then read the student essays and the model essay that follow and work through the questions that accompany the essays.
college-writing-010271.zh: 然后阅读学生论文和随后的模型论文，并解决随附随论文的问题。

college-writing-010273.en: Because argument assumes controversy, you have to work especially hard to convince readers of the validity of your position.
college-writing-010273.zh: 因为论证假设有争议，所以你必须特别努力地说服读者你的立场的有效性。

college-writing-010274.en: Here are five strategies you can use to help win over readers whose viewpoint may differ from yours.
college-writing-010274.zh: 以下是您可以使用的五种策略来帮助赢得与您观点可能不同的读者。

college-writing-010275.en: 1 Use Tactful, Courteous Language In an essay that emphasizes argument, you are attempting to persuade readers to accept your viewpoint.
college-writing-010275.zh: 1 在强调论证的文章中使用委婉、有礼貌的语言，您试图说服读者接受您的观点。

college-writing-010276.en: It is important, therefore, not to anger them by referring to them or their opinions in rude or belittling terms.
college-writing-010276.zh: 因此，重要的是，不要以粗鲁或贬低的方式提及他们或他们的意见来激怒他们。

college-writing-010277.en: Stay away from sweeping statements like “Everybody knows that . . .” or “People with any intelligence agree that. . . .”
college-writing-010277.zh: 远离像“每个人都知道……”这样的全面陈述。 或者“有任何情报的人都同意……”

college-writing-010278.en: Also, keep the focus on the issue you are discussing, not on the people involved in the debate.
college-writing-010278.zh: 此外，将重点放在您正在讨论的问题上，而不是参与辩论的人身上。

college-writing-010279.en: Don’t write, “My opponents say that orphanages cost less than foster care.”
college-writing-010279.zh: 不要写道，“我的反对者说孤儿院的成本低于寄养。”

college-writing-010280.en: Instead, write, “Supporters of orphanages say that orphanages cost less than foster care.”
college-writing-010280.zh: 相反，写道，“孤儿院的支持者说，孤儿院的成本低于寄养。”

college-writing-010281.en: Terms like my opponents imply that the argument is between you and anyone who disagrees with you.
college-writing-010281.zh: 像我的反对者这样的术语意味着争论是在你和任何不同意你的人之间。

college-writing-010282.en: By contrast, a term such as supporters of orphanages suggests that those who don’t agree with you are nevertheless open-minded people who are willing to consider differing opinions.
college-writing-010282.zh: 相比之下，诸如孤儿院支持者之类的术语表明，那些不同意你的人仍然是思想开放的人，他们愿意考虑不同的意见。

college-writing-010283.en: 2 Point Out Common Ground Another way to persuade readers to consider your opinion is to point out common ground─opinions that you share.
college-writing-010283.zh: 2 指出共同点 说服读者考虑您的意见的另一种方法是指出您分享的共同点。

college-writing-010284.en: Find points on which people on all sides of the
college-writing-010284.zh: 查找各个方面的人的点

college-writing-010285.zh: 第372章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010287.en: Perhaps you are arguing that there should be an 11 p.m. curfew for juveniles in your town.
college-writing-010287.zh: 也许你在争辩说应该有一个晚上 11 点。 你所在城镇的青少年宵禁。

college-writing-010288.en: Before going into detail about your proposal, remind readers who oppose such a curfew that you and they share certain goals: a safer city, a lower crime rate, and fewer gang-related tragedies.
college-writing-010288.zh: 在详细介绍您的提案之前，请提醒反对这种宵禁的读者，以至于您和他们有共同的目标：一个更安全的城市、更低的犯罪率和更少的与帮派有关的悲剧。

college-writing-010289.en: Readers will be more receptive to your idea once they have considered how you and they think alike.
college-writing-010289.zh: 一旦读者考虑了您和他们的想法如何，他们将更容易接受您的想法。

college-writing-010290.en: 3 Acknowledge Differing Viewpoints It is a mistake to simply ignore points of view that conflict with yours.
college-writing-010290.zh: 3 承认不同的观点 简单地忽略与您冲突的观点是错误的。

college-writing-010291.en: Acknowledging other viewpoints strengthens your position in several ways.
college-writing-010291.zh: 承认其他观点可以通过多种方式加强您的地位。

college-writing-010292.en: First, it helps you spot flaws in the opposing position─as well as in your own argument.
college-writing-010292.zh: 首先，它可以帮助你发现对立立场的缺陷——以及你自己的论点。

college-writing-010293.en: Second, and equally important, it gives the impression that you are an open-minded person, willing to look at an issue from all sides.
college-writing-010293.zh: 其次，同样重要的是，它给人的印象是你是一个思想开放的人，愿意从各个方面看待问题。

college-writing-010294.en: Readers will be more likely to consider your point of view if you indicate a willingness to consider theirs.
college-writing-010294.zh: 如果您表示愿意考虑他们的观点，读者将更有可能考虑您的观点。

college-writing-010295.en: At what point in your essay should you acknowledge opposing arguments?
college-writing-010295.zh: 在你的文章中，你应该承认反对的论点？

college-writing-010296.en: The earlier the better─ideally, in the introduction.

college-writing-010297.en: By quickly establishing that you recognize the other side’s position, you get your readers on board with you, ready to hear what else you have to say.
college-writing-010297.zh: 通过快速确定您认识到对方的立场，您可以让您的读者与您同行，准备好听听您还要说什么。

college-writing-010298.en: One effective technique is to cite the opposing viewpoint in your thesis statement.
college-writing-010298.zh: 一种有效的技术是在你的 中心论点句 中引用相反的观点。

college-writing-010299.en: You do this by dividing your thesis into two parts.
college-writing-010299.zh: 你通过将你的论文分成两部分来做到这一点。

college-writing-010300.en: In the first part, you acknowledge the other side’s point of view; in the second, you state your opinion, suggesting that yours is the stronger viewpoint.
college-writing-010300.zh: 第一部分，你承认对方的观点； 第二，你陈述你的意见，暗示你的观点是更强大的观点。

college-writing-010301.en: In the following example, the opposing viewpoint is underlined once; the writer’s own position is underlined twice:
college-writing-010301.zh: 在下面的示例中，对立的观点加下划线一次； 作者自己的立场有两次下划线：

college-writing-010302.en: Although some students believe that studying a foreign language is a waste of time, two years of foreign-language study should be required of all college graduates.
college-writing-010302.zh: 虽然有些学生认为学习外语是浪费时间，但所有大学毕业生都应该需要两年的外语学习。

college-writing-010303.en: For another example of a thesis that acknowledges an opposing viewpoint, look at this thesis statement, taken from the second student essay in this chapter, “Once Over Lightly: Local TV News”:
college-writing-010303.zh: 对于一个承认相反观点的论文的另一个例子，请看这本 中心论点句，摘自本章的第二篇学生论文，“Once Over Lightly: Local TV News”：

college-writing-010304.en: While local TV newscasts can provide a valuable community resource, too often such programs provide mere entertainment at the expense of solid news.
college-writing-010304.zh: 虽然当地电视新闻广播可以提供有价值的社区资源，但这些节目往往以牺牲可靠新闻为代价提供仅仅是娱乐。

college-writing-010305.en: Another effective technique is to use one or two sentences (separate from the thesis) in the introduction to acknowledge the alternative position.
college-writing-010305.zh: 另一种有效的技术是在引言中使用一两个句子（与论文分开）来承认替代立场。

college-writing-010306.en: Such sentences briefly state the “other side’s” argument.
college-writing-010306.zh: 这样的句子简要地陈述了“对方”的论点。

college-writing-010307.en: To see this technique at work, look at the introduction to the first student essay in this chapter, “Teenagers and Jobs,” noting the sentence “Many people argue that working can be a valuable experience for the young.”
college-writing-010307.zh: 要在工作中看到这种技术，请查看本章中第一篇学生论文的介绍“青少年和工作”，并指出“许多人认为工作对年轻人来说可能是一次宝贵的经验”这句话。

college-writing-010308.en: A third technique is to use a paragraph within the body of your essay to summarize opposing opinions in greater detail.
college-writing-010308.zh: 第三种技术是使用文章正文中的一段来更详细地总结反对意见。

college-writing-010309.en: To do this successfully, you must
college-writing-010309.zh: 要成功地做到这一点，你必须

college-writing-010311.en: spend some time researching those opposing arguments.
college-writing-010311.zh: 花一些时间研究那些相反的论点。

college-writing-010312.en: A fair, evenhanded summary of the other side’s ideas will help convince readers that you have looked at the issue from all angles before deciding where you stand.
college-writing-010312.zh: 对另一方想法的公平、公平的总结将有助于让读者相信您在决定您的立场之前已经从各个角度看待这个问题。

college-writing-010313.en: Imagine, for instance, that you are writing an essay arguing that the manufacture and sale of handguns should be outlawed.
college-writing-010313.zh: 例如，想象一下，您正在写一篇文章，认为手枪的制造和销售应该是非法的。

college-writing-010314.en: You would begin by doing some library research to find information on both sides of the issue, making sure to pay attention to material that argues against your viewpoint.
college-writing-010314.zh: 您将首先进行一些图书馆研究以查找问题双方的信息，确保关注与您的观点相反的材料。

college-writing-010315.en: You might also talk with local representatives of the National Rifle Association or other organizations that support gun ownership.
college-writing-010315.zh: 您还可以与全国步枪协会或其他支持枪支所有权的组织的当地代表交谈。

college-writing-010316.en: Having done your research, you would be in a good position to write a paragraph summarizing the opposing viewpoints.
college-writing-010316.zh: 完成您的研究后，您将能够撰写一段总结对立观点的段落。

college-writing-010317.en: In this paragraph, you might mention that many citizens believe that gun ownership is a right guaranteed by the Constitution and that gun owners fear that outlawing handguns would deprive law-abiding people of protection against gun-toting criminals.
college-writing-010317.zh: 在本段中，您可能会提到许多公民认为枪支所有权是宪法保障的一项权利，枪支拥有者担心取缔手枪会剥夺守法的人免受持枪罪犯的保护。

college-writing-010318.en: Once you had demonstrated that you understood opposing views, you would be in a stronger position to present your own point of view.
college-writing-010318.zh: 一旦你证明你理解了相反的观点，你将处于更强大的位置来展示自己的观点。

college-writing-010319.en: 4 When Appropriate, Grant the Merits of Differing Viewpoints Sometimes an opposing argument contains a point whose validity you cannot deny.
college-writing-010319.zh: 4 在适当的情况下，给予不同观点的优点 有时，一个相反的论点包含一个你不能否认其有效性的观点。

college-writing-010321.en: The strongest strategy is to admit that the point is a good one.
college-writing-010321.zh: 最有力的策略是承认这一点是好的。

college-writing-010322.en: You will lose credibility if you argue against something that clearly makes sense.
college-writing-010322.zh: 如果你反对明显有意义的事情，你将失去可信度。

college-writing-010323.en: Admit the merit of one aspect of the other argument while making it clear that you still believe your argument to be stronger overall.
college-writing-010323.zh: 承认另一个论点的一个方面的优点，同时明确表示你仍然相信你的论点总体上更强大。

college-writing-010324.en: Suppose that you were arguing against the use of computers in writing classrooms.
college-writing-010324.zh: 假设您反对在写作教室中使用计算机。

college-writing-010325.en: You might say, “Granted, students who are already accustomed to computers can use them to write papers more quickly and efficiently”─admitting that the other side has a valid point.
college-writing-010325.zh: 你可能会说，“当然，已经习惯计算机的学生可以用它们更快、更有效地写论文”——承认对方有一个有效的观点。

college-writing-010326.en: But you could quickly follow this admission with a statement making your own viewpoint clear: “But for students like me who write and think in longhand, a computer in the classroom is more a hindrance than a help; it would require too long a learning curve to be of any value to me.”
college-writing-010326.zh: 但是你可以很快地跟随这一承认，并用一个明确的观点来表达你自己的观点：“但对于像我这样用手写和思考的学生来说，课堂上的电脑与其说是帮助，不如说是一个障碍，而不是帮助；它需要太长的学习曲线才能对我有任何价值。”

college-writing-010327.en: 5 Rebut Differing Viewpoints Sometimes it may not be enough simply to acknowledge other points of view and present your own argument.
college-writing-010327.zh: 5 反驳不同的观点 有时，仅仅承认其他观点并提出自己的论点可能是不够的。

college-writing-010328.en: When you are dealing with an issue that your readers feel strongly about, you may need to rebut the opposing arguments.
college-writing-010328.zh: 当你处理一个你的读者强烈感受到的问题时，你可能需要反驳对立的论点。

college-writing-010329.en: To rebut means to point out problems with an opposing view, to show where an opponent’s argument breaks down.
college-writing-010329.zh: 反驳意味着用相反的观点指出问题，以显示对手的论点在哪里崩溃。

college-writing-010330.en: Imagine that you are writing an essay arguing that your college should use money intended to build a campus health and fitness center to upgrade the library
college-writing-010330.zh: 想象一下，您正在写一篇论文，认为您的大学应该使用旨在建立校园健康和健身中心的资金来升级图书馆

college-writing-010331.zh: 第374章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010333.en: From reading the school paper, you know that supporters of the center say it will help attract new students to the college.
college-writing-010333.zh: 通过阅读学校论文，您知道该中心的支持者表示，这将有助于吸引新生进入学院。

college-writing-010334.en: You rebut that point by citing a study conducted by the admissions office that shows that most students choose a college because they can afford it and because they like its academic programs and facilities.
college-writing-010334.zh: 你通过招生办公室进行的一项研究来反驳这一点，该研究表明大多数学生选择一所大学是因为他们负担得起，因为他们喜欢它的学术课程和设施。

college-writing-010335.en: You also emphasize that many students, already financially strapped, would have trouble paying the proposed fee for using the center.
college-writing-010335.zh: 您还强调，许多已经陷入财务困境的学生将难以支付使用该中心的建议费用。

college-writing-010336.en: A rebuttal can take two different forms: (1) You can first mention all the points raised by the other side and then present your counterargument to each of those points.
college-writing-010336.zh: 反驳可以采取两种不同的形式：（1）您可以首先提及对方提出的所有观点，然后将您的反驳呈现给每个点。

college-writing-010337.en: (2) You can present the first point raised by the opposition and rebut that point, then move on to the second opposing point and rebut that, and so on.
college-writing-010337.zh: (2) 你可以呈现对立提出的第一个点并反驳该点，然后继续到第二个对立点并反驳它，依此类推。

college-writing-010340.en: “The pressure for teenagers to work is great, and not just because of the economic plight in the world today. Much of it is peer pressure to have a little bit of freedom and independence, and to have their own spending money. The concern we have is when the part-time work becomes the primary focus.”
college-writing-010340.zh: “青少年工作的压力很大，不仅仅是因为当今世界的经济困境。大部分是同龄人的压力，需要有一点自由和独立，有自己的钱。我们担心的是兼职工作成为主要焦点。”

college-writing-010341.en: These are the words of Roxanne Bradshaw, educator and officer of the National Education Association.
college-writing-010341.zh: 这些是国家教育协会教育家和官员 Roxanne Bradshaw 的话。

college-writing-010342.en: Many people argue that working can be a valuable experience for the young.
college-writing-010342.zh: 许多人认为，工作对年轻人来说可能是一次宝贵的经历。

college-writing-010343.en: However, working more than about fifteen hours a week is harmful to adolescents because it reduces their involvement with school, encourages a materialistic and expensive lifestyle, and increases the chance of having problems with drugs and alcohol.
college-writing-010343.zh: 然而，每周工作超过 15 小时对青少年有害，因为这会减少他们对学校的参与，鼓励物质主义和昂贵的生活方式，并增加出现药物和酒精问题的机会。

college-writing-010344.en: Schoolwork and the benefits of extracurricular activities tend to go by the wayside when adolescents work long hours.
college-writing-010344.zh: 当青少年长时间工作时，学业和课外活动的好处往往会被搁置一旁。

college-writing-010345.en: As more and more teens have filled the numerous part-time jobs offered by fastfood restaurants and malls, teachers have faced increasing difficulties.
college-writing-010345.zh: 随着越来越多的青少年填补了快餐店和商场提供的众多兼职工作，教师面临越来越多的困难。

college-writing-010346.en: They must both keep the attention of tired pupils and give homework to students who simply don’t have time to do it.
college-writing-010346.zh: 他们必须保持疲惫的学生的注意力，并给没有时间做的学生做作业。

college-writing-010347.en: In addition, educators have noticed less involvement in the extracurricular activities that many consider a healthy influence on young people.
college-writing-010347.zh: 此外，教育工作者注意到对许多人认为对年轻人有健康影响的课外活动的参与较少。

college-writing-010348.en: School bands and athletic teams are losing players to work, and sports events are poorly attended by working students.
college-writing-010348.zh: 学校乐队和运动队正在失去球员上班，体育赛事的学生参加人数很少。

college-writing-010349.en: Those teens who try to do it all— homework, extracurricular activities, and work—may find themselves exhausted and prone to illness.
college-writing-010349.zh: 那些试图做这一切的青少年——家庭作业、课外活动和工作——可能会发现自己筋疲力尽，容易生病。

college-writing-010350.en: A recent newspaper story, for example, described a girl in Pennsylvania who suffered from extreme fatigue as a result of aiming for good grades, playing on two school athletic teams, and working thirty hours a week.
college-writing-010350.zh: 例如，最近的一篇报纸报道描述了宾夕法尼亚州的一个女孩，她因以良好的成绩、在两个学校的运动队中打球和每周工作 30 小时而感到极度疲劳。

college-writing-010353.en: Once Over Lightly: Local TV News
college-writing-010353.zh: 轻而易举：本地电视新闻

college-writing-010354.en: Unfortunately, local television newscasts are not a reliable source of news and don’t provide in-depth coverage and analysis of issues.
college-writing-010354.zh: 不幸的是，当地电视新闻广播不是可靠的新闻来源，也没有对问题进行深入的报道和分析。

college-writing-010355.en: While local TV newscasts can provide a valuable community resource, too often such programs provide mere entertainment at the expense of solid news.
college-writing-010355.zh: 虽然当地电视新闻广播可以提供有价值的社区资源，但这些节目往往以牺牲可靠新闻为代价提供仅仅是娱乐。

college-writing-010356.en: In their battle for high ratings, local programs emphasize news personalities at the expense of stories.
college-writing-010356.zh: 在他们争取高收视率的斗争中，当地节目以牺牲故事为代价强调新闻人物。

college-writing-010357.en: Visual appeal has a higher priority than actual news.
college-writing-010357.zh: 视觉吸引力比实际新闻具有更高的优先级。

college-writing-010358.en: And stories and reports are too brief and shallow.
college-writing-010358.zh: 故事和报道过于简短和肤浅。

college-writing-010359.en: Local TV newscasters are as much the subject of the news as are the stories they present.
college-writing-010359.zh: 当地电视新闻播音员和他们呈现的故事一样是新闻的主题。

college-writing-010360.en: Nowhere is this more obvious than in weather reports.
college-writing-010360.zh: 这在天气报告中最为明显。

college-writing-010361.en: Meteorologists spend valuable news time joking, drawing cartoons, chatting about weather fronts as “good guys” and “bad guys,” and dispensing weather trivia such as statistics about relative humidity and record highs and lows for the date.
college-writing-010361.zh: 气象学家花时间开玩笑，画卡通片，把天气前沿称为“好人”和“坏人”，并分发天气琐事，例如关于相对湿度的统计数据和日期的记录高点和低点。

college-writing-010362.en: Reporters, too, draw attention to themselves.
college-writing-010362.zh: 记者也引起了人们的注意。

college-writing-010363.en: Rather than just getting the story, the reporters are shown jumping into or getting out of helicopters to get the story.
college-writing-010363.zh: 记者们不只是了解故事，而是跳进或离开直升机来了解故事。

college-writing-010365.en: Another drawback of too much work is that it may promote materialism and an unrealistic lifestyle.
college-writing-010365.zh: 太多工作的另一个缺点是它可能促进物质主义和不切实际的生活方式。

college-writing-010366.en: Some parents claim that working helps teach adolescents the value of a dollar.
college-writing-010366.zh: 一些父母声称，工作有助于教青少年一美元的价值。

college-writing-010367.zh: 毫无疑问，这可能是真的。

college-writing-010368.en: It’s also true that some teens work to help out with the family budget or to save for college.
college-writing-010368.zh: 一些青少年努力帮助家庭预算或为大学存钱也是事实。

college-writing-010369.en: However, surveys have shown that the majority of working teens use their earnings to buy luxuries—nonessential electronic devices, clothing, even cars.
college-writing-010369.zh: 然而，调查显示，大多数在职青少年使用他们的收入购买奢侈品——非必要的电子设备、服装，甚至是汽车。

college-writing-010370.en: These young people, some of whom earn $500 or more a month, don’t worry about spending wisely—they can just about have it all.
college-writing-010370.zh: 这些年轻人，其中一些人每月赚取 500 美元或更多，他们不担心明智的支出——他们几乎可以拥有一切。

college-writing-010371.en: In many cases, experts point out, they are becoming accustomed to a lifestyle they won’t be able to afford several years down the road, when they no longer have parents paying for car insurance, food, lodging, and so on.
college-writing-010371.zh: 在许多情况下，专家指出，当他们不再有父母支付汽车保险、食物、住宿等费用时，他们已经习惯了几年后无法负担的生活方式。

college-writing-010372.en: At that point, they’ll be hard-pressed to pay for necessities as well as luxuries.
college-writing-010372.zh: 到那时，他们将很难支付必需品和奢侈品的费用。

college-writing-010373.en: Finally, teenagers who work a lot are more likely than others to get involved with alcohol and drugs.
college-writing-010373.zh: 最后，经常工作的青少年比其他人更有可能卷入酒精和毒品。

college-writing-010374.en: Teens who put in long hours may seek a quick release from stress, just like the adults who need to drink a couple of martinis after a hard day at work.
college-writing-010374.zh: 长时间工作的青少年可能会寻求快速从压力中解脱出来，就像在辛苦工作一天后需要喝几杯马提尼酒的成年人一样。

college-writing-010375.en: Stress is probably greater in our society today than it has been at any time in the past.
college-writing-010375.zh: 我们今天社会的压力可能比过去任何时候都要大。

college-writing-010376.en: Also, teens who have money are more likely to get involved with drugs.
college-writing-010376.zh: 此外，有钱的青少年更有可能卷入毒品。

college-writing-010377.en: Teenagers can enjoy the benefits of work while avoiding its drawbacks, simply by limiting their work hours during the school year.
college-writing-010377.zh: 青少年可以享受工作的好处，同时避免其缺点，只需在学年期间限制他们的工作时间。

college-writing-010378.en: As is often the case, a moderate approach will be the most healthy and rewarding.
college-writing-010378.zh: 通常情况下，适度的方法将是最健康和最有价值的。

college-writing-010380.zh: 第376章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010381.en: reporters interview crime victims or the residents of poor neighborhoods, the camera angle typically includes them and their reaction as well as their subjects.
college-writing-010381.zh: 记者采访了犯罪受害者或贫困社区的居民，镜头角度通常包括他们和他们的反应以及他们的主题。

college-writing-010382.en: When they report on a storm, they stand outside in the storm, their styled hair blowing, so we can admire how they “brave the elements.”
college-writing-010382.zh: 当他们报告暴风雨时，他们站在外面，他们风格的头发在吹，这样我们就可以欣赏他们如何“勇敢的元素”。

college-writing-010383.en: Then there are the news anchors, who are chosen as much for their looks as their skills.
college-writing-010383.zh: 然后是新闻主播，他们的外表和技能一样多。

college-writing-010384.en: They, too, dilute the news by putting their personalities at center stage.
college-writing-010384.zh: 他们也通过将自己的个性置于中心舞台来淡化新闻。

college-writing-010385.en: Often the selection of stories and the way they are presented are based on visual impact rather than news value.
college-writing-010385.zh: 通常，故事的选择及其呈现方式是基于视觉影响而不是新闻价值。

college-writing-010386.en: If a story is not accompanied by an interesting video, it is not likely to be shown on the local news.
college-writing-010386.zh: 如果一个故事没有附有有趣的视频，它不太可能在当地新闻中播放。

college-writing-010387.en: The result is an overemphasis on fires and car crashes and little attention to such important issues as the economy.
college-writing-010387.zh: 结果是过分强调火灾和车祸，而很少关注经济等重要问题。

college-writing-010388.en: A tractor-trailer spill on the highway slightly injures one person and inconveniences motorists for only an hour.
college-writing-010388.zh: 一辆拖拉机拖车在高速公路上溢出，轻微伤害了一个人，驾驶者的不便只持续了一个小时。

college-writing-010389.en: But because it provides dramatic pictures—the big truck on its side, its load spilled, emergency personnel running around, lots of flashing lights—it is given greater emphasis in the local newscast than a rise in local taxes, which has far more lasting effect on the viewer.
college-writing-010389.zh: 但因为它提供了戏剧性的画面——一辆大卡车，它的负荷溢出，应急人员四处奔波，大量闪光灯——在当地新闻广播中比增加地方税更受重视，这对观众产生了更持久的影响。

college-writing-010390.en: “If it bleeds, it leads” is the unofficial motto of many local news programs.
college-writing-010390.zh: “如果它流血，它会导致”是许多当地新闻节目的非官方座右铭。

college-writing-010391.en: A story that includes pictures of death and destruction, no matter how meaningless, is preferable on the local news to a solid, important story without flashy visuals.
college-writing-010391.zh: 一个包含死亡和毁灭图片的故事，无论多么毫无意义，在当地新闻中都比一个没有华丽视觉效果的坚实、重要的故事更可取。

college-writing-010392.en: The mania for visuals is so strong that local news programs will even slap irrelevant visuals onto an otherwise strong story.
college-writing-010392.zh: 视觉上的狂热是如此强烈，以至于当地新闻节目甚至会将无关紧要的视觉效果投射到一个原本强大的故事中。

college-writing-010393.en: A recent story on falling oil prices, for example, was accompanied by footage of a working oil well that drew attention away from the important economic information in the report.
college-writing-010393.zh: 例如，最近关于油价下跌的故事伴随着一座工作油井的镜头，该油井将注意力从报告中的重要经济信息上转移开来。

college-writing-010394.en: On the average, about half a minute is devoted to a story.
college-writing-010394.zh: 平均而言，大约半分钟是一个故事。

college-writing-010395.en: Clearly, stories that take less than half a minute are superficial.
college-writing-010395.zh: 显然，不到半分钟的故事是肤浅的。

college-writing-010396.en: Even the longest stories, which can take up to several minutes, are not accompanied by meaningful analysis.
college-writing-010396.zh: 即使是最长的故事，可能需要几分钟的时间，也没有进行有意义的分析。

college-writing-010397.en: Instead, the camera jumps from one location to another, and the newscaster simplifies and trivializes the issues.
college-writing-010397.zh: 相反，摄像机从一个位置跳到另一个位置，新闻播音员简化和琐碎问题。

college-writing-010398.en: For instance, one recent “in-depth” story about the homeless consisted of a glamorous reporter talking to a homeless person and asking him what should be done about the problem.
college-writing-010398.zh: 例如，最近一个关于无家可归者的“深入”故事包括一位迷人的记者与一个无家可归的人交谈，并询问他应该如何处理这个问题。

college-writing-010399.en: The poor man was in no condition to respond thoughtfully.
college-writing-010399.zh: 这个可怜的人没有任何条件，若有所思地回应。

college-writing-010400.en: The story then cut to an interview with a city bureaucrat who mechanically rambled on about the need for more government funding.
college-writing-010400.zh: 然后，故事切入了对一位城市官僚的采访，他机械地谈论需要更多的政府资金。

college-writing-010401.en: Is raising taxes the answer to every social problem?
college-writing-010401.zh: 提高税收是每个社会问题的答案吗？

college-writing-010402.en: There were also shots of homeless people sleeping in doorways and on top of heating vents, and there were interviews with people in the street, all of whom said that something should be done about the terrible problem of homelessness.
college-writing-010402.zh: 还有一些无家可归的人睡在门口和暖气通风口上的照片，街上的人都接受了采访，他们都说应该对无家可归的可怕问题采取一些措施。

college-writing-010403.en: There was, in all of this, no real exploration of the issue and no proposed solution.
college-writing-010403.zh: 在所有这些中，没有真正的探索问题，也没有提出的解决方案。

college-writing-010404.en: It was also apparent that the homeless were just the issue of the week.
college-writing-010404.zh: 很明显，无家可归者只是本周的问题。

college-writing-010405.en: After the week’s coverage was over, the topic was not mentioned again.
college-writing-010405.zh: 一周的报道结束后，这个话题没有再提及。

college-writing-010408.en: Because of the emphasis on newscasters’ personalities and on the visual impact of stories and the short time span for stories, local news shows provide little more than diversion.
college-writing-010408.zh: 由于强调新闻播音员的个性和故事的视觉影响以及故事的短时间跨度，当地新闻节目提供的只是转移注意力。

college-writing-010409.en: What viewers need instead is news that has real significance.
college-writing-010409.zh: 相反，观众需要的是具有真正意义的新闻。

college-writing-010410.en: Rather than being amused and entertained, we need to deal with complex issues and learn uncomfortable truths that will help us become more responsible consumers and citizens.
college-writing-010410.zh: 我们需要处理复杂的问题并学习令人不安的真相，而不是被逗乐和娱乐，这将帮助我们成为更负责任的消费者和公民。

college-writing-010436.en: Developing an Essay with Emphasis on Argument Considering Purpose and Audience When you write an essay that has an emphasis on argument, your main purpose is to convince readers that your particular view or opinion about a controversial issue or topic is correct.
college-writing-010436.zh: 撰写一篇强调论证的论文 考虑目的和受众 当您撰写一篇强调论证的文章时，您的主要目的是让读者相信您对有争议的问题或主题的特定观点或意见是正确的。

college-writing-010437.en: In addition, at times, you may have a second purpose for your essay: to persuade your audience to take some sort of action.
college-writing-010437.zh: 此外，有时，您的论文可能还有第二个目的：说服听众采取某种行动。

college-writing-010438.en: To convince readers, it is important to provide them with a clear main point and plenty of logical evidence to back it up.
college-writing-010438.zh: 为了说服读者，重要的是为他们提供明确的要点和大量的逻辑证据来支持它。

college-writing-010439.en: Say, for example, you want to argue that public schools should require students to wear uniforms.
college-writing-010439.zh: 例如，例如，您想争辩说公立学校应该要求学生穿制服。

college-writing-010440.en: In this case, you might do research to gather as much evidence as possible to support your point.
college-writing-010440.zh: 在这种情况下，您可能会进行研究以收集尽可能多的证据来支持您的观点。

college-writing-010441.en: You may check to see, for instance, if uniforms are cheaper than the alternative.
college-writing-010441.zh: 例如，您可以检查制服是否比替代品便宜。

college-writing-010442.en: Perhaps you could find out if schools with uniforms have a lower rate of violence than those without them.
college-writing-010442.zh: 也许您可以了解穿着制服的学校的暴力率是否低于没有校服的学校。

college-writing-010443.en: You may even look for studies to see if students’ academic performance improves when school uniforms are adopted.
college-writing-010443.zh: 您甚至可以寻找研究，看看学生的学习成绩是否在采用校服时有所改善。

college-writing-010444.en: As you search for evidence, be sure that it clearly links to your topic and supports the main point you are trying to get across to your audience.
college-writing-010444.zh: 当您搜索证据时，请确保它清楚地链接到您的主题并支持您试图传达给受众的主要观点。

college-writing-010445.en: While consideration of your audience is important for all essay forms, it is absolutely critical to the success of an essay that is persuasive in tone.
college-writing-010445.zh: 虽然考虑您的听众对所有论文形式都很重要，但对于一篇有说服力的论文的成功至关重要。

college-writing-010446.en: Depending on the main point you choose, your audience may be firmly opposed to your view or somewhat supportive of it.
college-writing-010446.zh: 根据您选择的主要观点，您的受众可能会强烈反对您的观点或对它的支持。

college-writing-010447.en: As you begin planning your essay, consider what
college-writing-010447.zh: 当你开始计划你的论文时，考虑一下什么

college-writing-010465.en: Development through Prewriting Before choosing a topic for her essay, Anna, the writer of “Teenagers and Jobs,” asked herself what controversial subject she was particularly well qualified to argue.
college-writing-010465.zh: 在为她的论文选择主题之前，“青少年和工作”的作者安娜在为她的论文选择主题之前通过预写的发展问自己，她特别有资格争论什么有争议的主题。

college-writing-010466.en: She wanted to select something she cared about, something she could sink her teeth into.
college-writing-010466.zh: 她想选择她关心的东西，她可以咬牙切齿的东西。

college-writing-010467.en: As a person who had been an active member of her high school community─she had worked on the newspaper, played basketball, and sung in a chorus─Anna first thought of writing about student apathy.
college-writing-010467.zh: 作为一个积极参与高中社区的人——她曾在报纸上工作、打篮球，并在合唱中演唱——安娜第一次想到写关于学生的冷漠。

college-writing-010468.en: It had always bothered her to see few students taking advantage of the opportunities available to them in school.
college-writing-010468.zh: 看到很少有学生利用学校可用的机会，她总是感到困扰。

college-writing-010469.en: But as she thought more about individual students she knew and their reasons for not getting more involved in school and extracurricular activities, she changed her opinion.
college-writing-010469.zh: 但随着她更多地思考她认识的个别学生以及他们没有更多地参与学校和课外活动的原因，她改变了自己的看法。

college-writing-010470.en: “I realized that ‘apathy’ was not really the problem,” she explained.
college-writing-010470.zh: “我意识到‘冷漠’并不是真正的问题，”她解释道。

college-writing-010471.en: “Many of them worked so much that they literally didn’t have time for school life.”
college-writing-010471.zh: “他们中的许多人都工作得如此之多，以至于他们实际上没有时间过学校生活。”

college-writing-010472.en: After narrowing her thesis to the idea of “teenagers and work,” Anna made a list of what she perceived as the bad points of students’ working too much:
college-writing-010472.zh: 在将她的论文缩小到“青少年和工作”的想法之后，安娜列出了她认为学生工作过多的缺点：

college-writing-010473.en: your audience already knows, and how it feels about the main point of your essay.
college-writing-010473.zh: 你的听众已经知道，以及对你论文的主要观点的感受。

college-writing-010474.en: Using the example above, for instance, ask yourself what opinion your audience holds about school uniforms.
college-writing-010474.zh: 例如，使用上面的例子，问问自己听众对校服有什么看法。

college-writing-010475.en: What are likely to be their objections to your argument?
college-writing-010475.zh: 他们对你的论点的反对意见可能是什么？

college-writing-010476.en: Why would people not support your main point?
college-writing-010476.zh: 为什么人们不支持你的主要观点？

college-writing-010477.en: What, if anything, are the merits of the opposing point of view?
college-writing-010477.zh: 如果有的话，对立观点的优点是什么？

college-writing-010478.en: In order to “get inside the head” of your opposition, you might even want to interview a few people you’re sure will disagree with you: say, for instance, a student with a very funky personal style who you know would dislike wearing a uniform.
college-writing-010478.zh: 为了“进入”你的反对派，你甚至可能想采访一些你肯定会不同意的人：比如说，一个你知道会不喜欢穿制服的学生。

college-writing-010479.en: By becoming aware of the points of view your audience might have, you will know how to proceed in researching your rebuttal to their arguments.
college-writing-010479.zh: 通过了解您的受众可能拥有的观点，您将知道如何继续研究您对他们的论点的反驳。

college-writing-010480.en: For more information on how to deal with opposing views in your essay, see the section in this chapter called, “Acknowledge Differing Viewpoints.”
college-writing-010480.zh: 有关如何处理文章中对立观点的更多信息，请参阅本章中的“承认不同观点”的部分。

college-writing-010481.en: By directly addressing your opposition, you add credibility to your argument and increase the chances that others will be convinced that your main point is valid.
college-writing-010481.zh: 通过直接解决您的反对意见，您可以为您的论点增加可信度，并增加其他人相信您的主要观点是有效的机会。
