college-writing-010515.en: Referring to this list, Anna wrote the following first draft of her essay.
college-writing-010515.zh: 参考这份清单，安娜写了她的论文的以下初稿。

college-writing-010517.en: Many people think that working is a valuable experience for young people.
college-writing-010517.zh: 许多人认为工作对年轻人来说是一次宝贵的经历。

college-writing-010518.en: But when teenagers have jobs, they are too likely to neglect their schoolwork, become overly materialistic, and get into trouble with drugs and alcohol.
college-writing-010518.zh: 但是当青少年有工作时，他们很可能会忽视自己的功课，变得过于物质化，并因毒品和酒精而陷入困境。

college-writing-010519.en: Schoolwork and the benefits of extracurricular activities tend to go by the wayside when adolescents work long hours.
college-writing-010519.zh: 当青少年长时间工作时，学业和课外活动的好处往往会被搁置一旁。

college-writing-010520.en: As more and more teens have taken jobs, teachers have faced increasing difficulties.
college-writing-010520.zh: 随着越来越多的青少年找到工作，教师面临着越来越多的困难。

college-writing-010521.en: They must both keep the attention of tired pupils and give homework to students who simply don’t have time to do it.
college-writing-010521.zh: 他们必须保持疲惫的学生的注意力，并给没有时间做的学生做作业。

college-writing-010522.en: In addition, educators have noticed less involvement in extracurricular activities.
college-writing-010522.zh: 此外，教育工作者注意到课外活动的参与较少。

college-writing-010523.en: School bands and athletic teams are losing players to work, and sports events are poorly attended by working students.
college-writing-010523.zh: 学校乐队和运动队正在失去球员上班，体育赛事的学生参加人数很少。

college-writing-010524.en: Those teens who try to do it all—homework, extracurricular activities, and work— may find themselves exhausted and burned out.
college-writing-010524.zh: 那些试图做这一切的青少年——家庭作业、课外活动和工作——可能会发现自己筋疲力尽，筋疲力尽。

college-writing-010525.en: Another drawback of too much work is that it may promote materialism and an unrealistic lifestyle.
college-writing-010525.zh: 太多工作的另一个缺点是它可能促进物质主义和不切实际的生活方式。

college-writing-010526.en: Most working teens use their earnings to buy luxuries.
college-writing-010526.zh: 大多数在职青少年用他们的收入来购买奢侈品。

college-writing-010527.en: These young people don’t worry about spending wisely—they can just about have it all.
college-writing-010527.zh: 这些年轻人不担心明智的消费——他们几乎可以拥有一切。

college-writing-010528.en: They are becoming accustomed to a lifestyle they won’t be able to afford several years down the road, when they have to support themselves.
college-writing-010528.zh: 当他们必须养活自己时，他们已经习惯了几年后无法负担得起的生活方式。

college-writing-010529.en: Finally, teenagers who work are more likely than others to get involved with alcohol and drugs.
college-writing-010529.zh: 最后，工作的青少年比其他人更有可能卷入酒精和毒品。

college-writing-010530.en: Teens who put in long hours may seek a quick release from stress, just like the adults who need to drink a couple of martinis after a hard day at work.
college-writing-010530.zh: 长时间工作的青少年可能会寻求快速从压力中解脱出来，就像在辛苦工作一天后需要喝几杯马提尼酒的成年人一样。

college-writing-010531.en: Also, teens who have money are more likely to get involved with drugs.
college-writing-010531.zh: 此外，有钱的青少年更有可能卷入毒品。

college-writing-010532.en: In short, teens and work just don’t mix.
college-writing-010532.zh: 简而言之，青少年和工作只是不混在一起。

college-writing-010533.en: Development through Revising Anna’s instructor had offered to look over students’ first drafts and suggest improvements for revision.
college-writing-010533.zh: 通过修订 Anna 的讲师的发展提出了查看学生的初稿并建议改进以进行修改。

college-writing-010534.en: Here is the note she wrote at the end of Anna’s work:
college-writing-010534.zh: 这是她在安娜作品结尾写的笔记：

college-writing-010536.en: While I think your thesis is overstated, it and each of your main topics are on the right track.
college-writing-010536.zh: 虽然我认为你的论文被夸大了，但它和你的每个主要主题都在正确的轨道上。

college-writing-010537.en: Here are some points to consider as you write your next draft:
college-writing-010537.zh: 在编写下一稿时，需要考虑以下几点：

college-writing-010538.en: • Many teenagers find working a limited number of hours a week to be a good experience.
college-writing-010538.zh: • 许多青少年认为每周工作时间有限，这是一次很好的体验。

college-writing-010539.en: I think it’s a mistake to state flatly that it’s always
college-writing-010539.zh: 我认为平淡地说它总是错误的

college-writing-010540.zh: 第382章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010541.en: a negative thing for teenagers to have jobs.
college-writing-010541.zh: 对青少年有工作的负面影响。

college-writing-010542.en: Think about acknowledging that there can be good points to students’ working part-time.
college-writing-010542.zh: 想想承认学生的兼职工作可能有好点。

college-writing-010543.en: • You do a pretty good job of supporting your first main point (“Schoolwork and the benefits of extracurricular activities tend to go by the wayside when adolescents work long hours”) by noting the effect of too much work on scholastic achievement and extracurricular activities.
college-writing-010543.zh: • 通过注意到过多工作对学术成就和课外活动的影响，您在支持您的第一个要点（“学业和课外活动的好处往往会在青少年长时间工作时倾向于顺理成章”）方面做得很好。

college-writing-010544.en: You less effectively support points 2 and 3 (“Another drawback of too much work is that it may promote materialism and an unrealistic lifestyle” and “Finally, teenagers who work are more likely than others to get involved with alcohol and drugs”).
college-writing-010544.zh: 你不那么有效地支持第 2 点和第 3 点（“太多工作的另一个缺点是它可能促进物质主义和不切实际的生活方式”和“最后，工作的青少年比其他人更有可能参与酒精和毒品的行为”）。

college-writing-010545.en: Show how teens become too materialistic; don’t just state that they do.
college-writing-010545.zh: 展示青少年如何变得过于物质主义； 不要只是说他们这样做。

college-writing-010546.en: And what evidence do you have that working teens use drugs and alcohol more than others?
college-writing-010546.zh: 你有什么证据表明，工作的青少年比其他人更多地使用毒品和酒精？

college-writing-010547.en: • Throughout the essay, can you come up with evidence beyond your own observations to support the idea that too much working is detrimental to teens?
college-writing-010547.zh: • 在整篇文章中，您能否提出超出您自己观察的证据来支持过多的工作对青少年有害的想法？

college-writing-010548.en: Look in the magazine indexes in the library and on the Internet for studies or stories that might support your thesis.
college-writing-010548.zh: 在图书馆和互联网上的杂志索引中查看可能支持您的论文的研究或故事。

college-writing-010549.en: I’ll look forward to seeing your final draft.
college-writing-010549.zh: 我期待着看到你的最终草案。

college-writing-010550.en: After considering her instructor’s comments, Anna wrote the version of “Teenagers and Jobs” that appears in the section “Student Essays to Consider” earlier in this chapter.
college-writing-010550.zh: 在考虑了她的导师的评论后，安娜写了本章前面“学生论文要考虑的学生论文”部分中出现的“青少年和乔布斯”版本。

college-writing-010551.en: Arguments can be made through visual images as well.
college-writing-010551.zh: 也可以通过视觉图像进行论证。

college-writing-010552.en: What visual argument is suggested by this photograph?
college-writing-010552.zh: 这张照片暗示了什么视觉论证？

college-writing-010557.zh: 一个 ee eae 小便

college-writing-010561.en: Then answer the questions and read the comments that follow.
college-writing-010561.zh: 然后回答问题并阅读下面的评论。

college-writing-010562.en: Essay on the Importance of Teaching Failure
college-writing-010562.zh: 教学失败的重要性论文

college-writing-010564.en: What can we conclude when undergraduates bemoan, “How did anyone ever come up with this stuff?”
college-writing-010564.zh: 当本科生哀叹时，我们可以得出什么结论：“怎么会有人想出这些东西？”

college-writing-010565.en: Although the students might feel confused or bedazzled, there’s one thing for certain: the instructor jumped over the requisite missteps that originally led to the discovery at hand.
college-writing-010565.zh: 虽然学生可能会感到困惑或眼花缭乱，但肯定有一件事：教练跳过了最初导致手头发现的必要失误。

college-writing-010566.en: This type of intellectual revisionism often depicts weighty concepts and conclusions as slick and sanitized, and, as a result, foreign and intangible.
college-writing-010566.zh: 这种类型的智力修正主义经常将重要的概念和结论描绘成光滑和消毒的，因此，是外来的和无形的。

college-writing-010567.en: In reality, every idea from every discipline is a human idea that comes from a natural, thoughtful, and (ideally) unending journey in which thinkers deeply understand the current state of knowledge, take a tiny step in a new direction, almost immediately hit a dead end, learn from that misstep, and, through iteration, inevitably move forward.
college-writing-010567.zh: 实际上，每个学科的每一个思想都是一个人的想法，它来自一个自然的、深思熟虑的、（理想的）无尽的旅程，在这个旅程中，思想者深刻地理解了当前的知识状态，朝着新的方向迈出了一小步，几乎立即遇到了死胡同，从这个错误中学习，并通过迭代， 不可避免地向前迈进。

college-writing-010568.en: That recipe for success is not just the secret formula for original scholarly discovery, but also for wise, everyday thinking for the entire population.
college-writing-010568.zh: 成功的秘诀不仅是原始学术发现的秘诀，也是整个人群的明智、日常思考的秘诀。

college-writing-010569.en: Hence, it is important to explicitly highlight how essential those dead ends and mistakes are─that is, to teach students the power of failure and how to fail effectively.
college-writing-010569.zh: 因此，重要的是要明确强调这些死胡同和错误的重要性——即教导学生失败的力量以及如何有效地失败。

college-writing-010570.en: Individuals need to embrace the realization that taking risks and failing are often the essential moves necessary to bring clarity, understanding, and innovation.
college-writing-010570.zh: 个人需要接受这样的认识，即冒险和失败通常是带来清晰、理解和创新所必需的必要举措。

college-writing-010571.en: By making a mistake, we are led to the pivotal question: “Why was that wrong?”
college-writing-010571.zh: 犯了一个错误，我们被引导到一个关键的问题：“为什么那是错误的？”

college-writing-010572.en: By answering this question, we are intentionally placing ourselves in a position to develop a new insight and to eventually succeed.
college-writing-010572.zh: 通过回答这个问题，我们故意将自己置于发展新见解并最终成功的位置。

college-writing-010573.en: But how do we foster such a critical habit of mind in our students─students who are hardwired to avoid failure at all costs?
college-writing-010573.zh: 但是，我们如何在学生中培养如此重要的思想习惯——这些学生天生就不惜一切代价避免失败？

college-writing-010575.en: For the last decade or so, I’ve put my students’ grades where my mouth is.
college-writing-010575.zh: 在过去十年左右的时间里，我把学生的成绩放在嘴边。

college-writing-010576.en: Instead of just touting the importance of failing, I now tell students that if they want to earn an A, they must fail regularly throughout the course of the semester─because 5 percent of their final grade is based on their “quality of failure.”
college-writing-010576.zh: 我现在告诉学生，如果他们想获得 A 的重要性，他们必须在整个学期期间定期失败——因为他们最终成绩的 5% 是基于他们的“失败质量”。

college-writing-010577.en: Would such a scheme provoke a change in attitude?
college-writing-010577.zh: 这样的计划会引起态度的改变吗？

college-writing-010578.en: Absolutely─with this grading practice in place, students gleefully take more risks and energetically engage in discussions.
college-writing-010578.zh: 绝对——有了这种评分实践，学生们兴高采烈地承担更多的风险，并积极参与讨论。

college-writing-010579.en: And when a student (say, Aaron) makes a mistake in class, he exclaims, “Oh well, my quality of failure grade today is really high.”
college-writing-010579.zh: 当一个学生（比如说，亚伦）在课堂上犯错时，他会大声说：“哦，好吧，我今天的失败质量真的很高。”

college-writing-010580.en: The class laughs and then quickly moves to the serious next step─answering: Why was that wrong?
college-writing-010580.zh: 全班笑了起来，然后迅速走到了严肃的下一步——回答：为什么错了？

college-writing-010581.en: It’s not enough to console an incorrect response with a nurturing, “Oh, Aaron, that’s not quite right, but we still think you’re the best!
college-writing-010581.zh: 仅仅用养育方式来安慰错误的回应是不够的，“哦，亚伦，这不太对劲，但我们仍然认为你是最棒的！

college-writing-010582.zh: 第384章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010584.en: Now, does anyone else have another guess?
college-writing-010584.zh: 现在，还有其他人猜测吗？

college-writing-010585.en: ’’ Instead, a mistake solicits either the enthusiastic yet honest response, “Congratulations, Aaron─that’s wrong! Now what lesson or insight is Aaron offering us?” or the class question, “What do you think? Is Aaron correct?”
college-writing-010585.zh: ’’”相反，一个错误会引起热情而诚实的回应，“恭喜，亚伦——那是错误的！现在亚伦给我们提供了什么教训或洞察力？” 或者课堂问题，“你怎么看？亚伦是对的吗？”

college-writing-010586.en: Either way, the students have to actively listen and then react, while Aaron sees his comment as an important element that allows the discussion to move forward.
college-writing-010586.zh: 无论哪种方式，学生都必须积极倾听然后做出反应，而亚伦将他的评论视为允许讨论向前推进的重要因素。

college-writing-010587.en: I often refer back again and again to someone’s previous mistake to celebrate just how significant it was.
college-writing-010587.zh: 我经常一次又一次地提到某人之前的错误，以庆祝它的重要性。

college-writing-010588.en: If we foster an environment in our classrooms in which failing is a natural and necessary component in making progress, then we allow our students to release their own genius and share their authentic ideas─even if (or especially when) those ideas aren’t quite polished or perfectly formed.
college-writing-010588.zh: 如果我们在课堂上营造一个失败是进步的自然和必要组成部分的环境，那么我们允许我们的学生释放他们自己的天才并分享他们的真实想法——即使（或者尤其是当）这些想法没有被完美地完善或完美形成。

college-writing-010589.en: After returning a graded assignment and reviewing the more challenging questions, I ask students to share their errors─and the class immediately comes to life: everyone wants to show off their mistakes as they now know they are offering valuable learning moments.
college-writing-010589.zh: 在返回评分作业并复习更具挑战性的问题后，我要求学生分享他们的错误——课堂立即变得生动：每个人都想炫耀自己的错误，因为他们现在知道他们正在提供有价值的学习时刻。

college-writing-010590.en: What’s more, in this receptive atmosphere, it’s actually fun to reveal those promising gems of an idea that turned out to be counterfeit.
college-writing-010590.zh: 更重要的是，在这种接受的氛围中，揭示那些被证明是假冒的想法的宝石实际上很有趣。

college-writing-010591.en: More recently, I’ve asked my students to intentionally fail─in the spirit of an industrial stress test.
college-writing-010591.zh: 最近，我要求我的学生故意失败——本着工业压力测试的精神。

college-writing-010592.en: I now require my students to write a first draft of an essay very quickly and poorly─long before its due date─and then have the students use that lousy draft as a starting point for the (hopefully lengthy) iterative process of revising and editing.
college-writing-010592.zh: 我现在要求我的学生在截止日期之前非常快和糟糕地写一篇论文的初稿——然后让学生使用那份糟糕的草稿作为（希望是冗长的）修改和编辑迭代过程的起点。

college-writing-010593.en: When the work is due, they must submit not only their final version, but also append their penultimate draft all marked up with their own red ink.
college-writing-010593.zh: 当作品到期时，他们不仅必须提交最终版本，还必须附上他们的倒数第二稿，全部用自己的红色墨水标记。

college-writing-010594.en: This strategy assures that they will produce at least one intermediate draft before the final version.
college-writing-010594.zh: 该策略确保他们将在最终版本之前至少产生一份中间草案。

college-writing-010595.en: Not surprisingly, the quality of their work improved dramatically.
college-writing-010595.zh: 毫不奇怪，他们的工作质量显着提高。

college-writing-010596.en: When I consult with or lead workshops for faculty and administrators, they are drawn to this principle of intentionally promoting failure, which inevitably leads to the question: How do you assess it?
college-writing-010596.zh: 当我为教师和管理人员咨询或领导研讨会时，他们会被这种故意促进失败的原则所吸引，这不可避免地会导致一个问题：你如何评估它？

college-writing-010597.en: The first time I tried my 5 percent “quality of failure,” I had no idea how to grade it.
college-writing-010597.zh: 当我第一次尝试我 5% 的“失败质量”时，我不知道如何给它评分。

college-writing-010598.en: But I practiced what I preached─taking a risk and being willing to fail in the noble cause of teaching students to think more effectively.
college-writing-010598.zh: 但我实践了我所宣扬的——冒险并愿意在教导学生更有效地思考的崇高事业中失败。

college-writing-010599.en: I passionately believe that assessment concerns should never squelch any creative pedagogical experiment.
college-writing-010599.zh: 我坚信评估问题永远不应该压制任何创造性的教学实验。

college-writing-010600.en: Try it today, and figure out how to measure it tomorrow.
college-writing-010600.zh: 今天试试，明天想办法测量它。

college-writing-010601.en: In the case of assessing “quality of failure,” at the end of the semester I ask my students to write a one-page reflective essay describing their productive failure in the course and how they have grown from those episodes (which might have occurred outside of class─including false starts and fruitful iterations).
college-writing-010601.zh: 在评估“失败质量”的情况下，在学期末，我要求我的学生写一篇一页反思性文章，描述他们在课程中的生产性失败以及它们是如何从这些事件中成长起来的（这可能发生在课堂之外——包括错误的开始和富有成果的迭代）。

college-writing-010602.en: They conclude their essay by providing their own grade on how they have evolved through failure and mistakes (from 0─meaning “I never failed” or “I learned nothing from failing” to 10─meaning “I created and understood in profound, new ways from my failed attempts”).
college-writing-010602.zh: 他们通过失败和错误（从 0 ——意思是“我从未失败”或“我从失败中学到任何东西”到 10——的意思是“我从失败的尝试中以深刻的新方式创造和理解”来结束论文，提供自己的成绩。）

college-writing-010603.en: I read their narratives, reflect on their class participation and willingness to take risks, and then usually award them the surprisingly honest and restrained grades they gave themselves.
college-writing-010603.zh: 我阅读了他们的叙述，反思了他们的阶级参与和冒险的意愿，然后通常会授予他们令人惊讶的诚实和克制的成绩。

college-writing-010604.en: To date, I’ve never had a student complain about their “quality of failure” grade.
college-writing-010604.zh: 迄今为止，我从未让学生抱怨过他们的“失败质量”等级。

college-writing-010606.en: To my skeptical colleagues who wonder if this grading scheme can be exploited as a loophole to reward unprepared students, I remind them that we should not create policies in the academy that police students, instead we should create policies that add pedagogical value and create educational opportunity.
college-writing-010606.zh: 对于那些怀疑这个评分方案是否可以作为奖励的漏洞来奖励学生的怀疑的同事，我提醒他们，我们不应该在学院中制定警察来警察学生的政策，而是应该制定增加教学价值和创造教育机会的政策。

college-writing-010607.en: And with respect to my grading failure practice, I found no such abuse at the three institutions in which I have employed it (Williams College, the University of Colorado at Boulder and Baylor University).
college-writing-010607.zh: 关于我的分级失败实践，我在我雇用它的三个机构（威廉姆斯学院、科罗拉多大学博尔德分校和贝勒大学）没有发现这种滥用行为。

college-writing-010608.en: On the contrary, if implemented correctly, you will see your students more engaged, more prepared, and more thoughtful in class discussions and in life.
college-writing-010608.zh: 相反，如果实施得当，你会看到你的学生在课堂讨论和生活中更加投入、更准备、更周到。

college-writing-010609.en: Beyond the subject matter contained in the thirty-two to forty-eight courses that typical undergraduates fleetingly encounter, our students’ education centers about the most important creative feat of their lives─the creation of themselves: Creating a mind enlivened by curiosity and the intellectual audacity to take risks and create new ideas, a mind that sees a world of unlimited possibilities.
college-writing-010609.zh: 除了典型的本科生短暂遇到的三十二至四十八门课程中所包含的主题之外，我们的学生的教育中心还关注他们生活中最重要的创造性壮举——创造一个充满好奇心和智力大胆的思想 冒险并创造新的想法，一个看到无限可能性的世界的思想。

college-writing-010610.en: So we as educators and scholars should constantly be asking ourselves: Have I taught my students how to successfully fail?
college-writing-010610.zh: 所以作为教育者和学者，我们应该不断地问自己：我是否教过我的学生如何成功地失败？

college-writing-010611.en: And if not, then: What am I waiting for?
college-writing-010611.zh: 如果不是，那么：我还在等什么？

college-writing-010613.en: 1. What is the thesis of Burger’s essay?
college-writing-010613.zh: 1. 汉堡论文的论文是什么？

college-writing-010614.en: If it is stated directly, locate the relevant
college-writing-010614.zh: 如果直接说明，请找到相关的

college-writing-010616.en: If it is implied, state the thesis in your own words.
college-writing-010616.zh: 如果有暗示，请用您自己的话说明论文。

college-writing-010617.en: 2. Which statement would best serve as a topic sentence for paragraphs 5 and 6?
college-writing-010617.zh: 2. 哪项陈述最适合作为第 5 段和第 6 段的 主题句？

college-writing-010618.en: a. Students should celebrate all failures in learning.
college-writing-010618.zh: 一。 学生应该庆祝所有的学习失败。

college-writing-010619.en: b. Helping students celebrate effective failure helps them learn.
college-writing-010619.zh: B. 帮助学生庆祝有效的失败有助于他们学习。

college-writing-010620.en: c. Teachers should publicize students’ failures to help them learn.
college-writing-010620.zh: c.  教师应该宣传学生的失败，以帮助他们学习。

college-writing-010621.en: d. Failure is part of education, so students just need to accept it.
college-writing-010621.zh: D. 失败是教育的一部分，所以学生只需要接受它。

college-writing-010622.en: 3. Which statement would best serve as a topic sentence for paragraph 10?
college-writing-010622.zh: 3. 哪项陈述最适合作为第 10 段的 主题句？

college-writing-010624.en: Students are required to grade themselves on their quality of failure, and
college-writing-010624.zh: 学生必须根据自己的失败质量进行评分，并且

college-writing-010625.en: their grades are usually honest and correct.
college-writing-010625.zh: 他们的成绩通常是诚实和正确的。

college-writing-010627.en: Students are required to grade themselves on their quality of failure, but
college-writing-010627.zh: 学生必须根据失败的质量对自己进行评分，但

college-writing-010696.en: Find an editorial in your local newspaper with which you either strongly agree or strongly disagree.
college-writing-010696.zh: 在您当地的报纸上找到您强烈同意或强烈反对的社论。

college-writing-010697.en: Write a letter to the editor responding to that editorial.

college-writing-010698.en: State why you agree or disagree with the position taken by the paper.
college-writing-010698.zh: 说明您同意或不同意论文所采取立场的原因。

college-writing-010699.en: Provide several paragraphs of supporting evidence for your position.
college-writing-010699.zh: 为您的职位提供几段 支撑论点的证据。

college-writing-010700.en: When you turn in the copy of your letter to your instructor, also turn in the editorial to which you are responding.
college-writing-010700.zh: 当您将信件的副本交给您的教师时，也请上交您正在回复的社论。

college-writing-010701.en: Your instructor may want you to send your letter to the newspaper, but you will want instructor feedback before doing so.
college-writing-010701.zh: 您的讲师可能希望您将信件发送到报纸，但在这样做之前，您会需要教师的反馈。

college-writing-010702.en: The topic of the editorial will determine the additional chapters you will need to review.
college-writing-010702.zh: 社论的主题将确定您需要查看的其他章节。

college-writing-010703.en: For instance, if the editorial focuses on an implied definition, you will need to review Chapter 14, “Definition,” but if the editorial focuses on the effects of a specific city project, you will need to review Chapter 12, “Cause and/or Effect.”
college-writing-010703.zh: 例如，如果编辑侧重于隐含定义，则需要复习第 14 章“定义”，但如果编辑侧重于特定城市项目的影响，则需要复习第 12 章“原因和/或效果”。

college-writing-010712.en: If you are writing to disagree with the article, you will want to pay special

college-writing-010713.en: attention to your tone, always keeping your words as respectful as possible.
college-writing-010713.zh: 注意你的语气，始终保持你的话尽可能尊重。

college-writing-010714.en: If you are writing to agree with the article, you should respectfully acknowledge the opposing point of view before stating your thesis.
college-writing-010714.zh: 如果你写信是为了同意这篇文章，你应该在陈述你的论文之前尊重对立的观点。

college-writing-010715.en: Often, an editorial is printed on the same page as another editorial or an op-ed piece that argues the opposite point; reading both articles will help you focus your introductory material to properly set up your reader.
college-writing-010715.zh: 通常，社论与另一篇社论或反对观点的专栏文章一起印刷在同一页上； 阅读这两篇文章将帮助您集中介绍性材料以正确设置您的读者。

college-writing-010717.en: As you organize your points, keep in mind that emphatic order (in which you
college-writing-010717.zh: 当你组织你的观点时，请记住强调秩序（你在其中

college-writing-010718.en: end with your most important reason) is often the most effective way to organize an argument.
college-writing-010718.zh: 以你最重要的理由结束）通常是组织争论的最有效方式。

college-writing-010719.en: Your reader is most likely to remember your final reason.
college-writing-010719.zh: 您的读者最有可能记住您的最终原因。

college-writing-010721.en: Proceed to write the first draft of your essay.

college-writing-010722.en: REVISING After you have completed the first draft of the paper, set it aside for a while if you can.
college-writing-010722.zh: 修改完成论文的初稿后，如果可以的话，将其搁置一段时间。

college-writing-010723.en: Then read the paper out loud to a friend or classmate whose judgment you respect.
college-writing-010723.zh: 然后大声朗读这篇论文给你尊重判断的朋友或同学。

college-writing-010724.en: Keep in mind the questions in the FOUR BASES Checklist at the end of this chapter as you hear your own words, and ask your friend to respond to them as well.
college-writing-010724.zh: 当您听到自己的话时，请记住本章末尾的四个基础清单中的问题，并要求您的朋友也回复它们。

college-writing-010725.en: As you revise your essay through additional drafts, continue to refer to that checklist until you and your reader can answer “yes” to each question.
college-writing-010725.zh: 当您通过其他草稿修改论文时，请继续参考该清单，直到您和您的读者可以对每个问题回答“是”。

college-writing-010727.zh: 通过利用你的推理能力和一般经验来支持和捍卫你的论点。

college-writing-010728.en: OPTION 1 For many years, junk food was available in school cafeterias and school vending machines across the nation.
college-writing-010728.zh: 选项 1 多年来，全国各地的学校食堂和学校自动售货机都提供垃圾食品。

college-writing-010729.en: For decades, school cafeteria menus did not encourage the best eating habits.
college-writing-010729.zh: 几十年来，学校食堂菜单并没有鼓励最好的饮食习惯。

college-writing-010730.en: A 2012 federal mandate changed the kinds of foods offered in public schools so that, for the large part, junk food was no longer available, and there was a strong emphasis on healthy eating, including fruits and vegetables.
college-writing-010730.zh: 2012 年的联邦授权改变了公立学校提供的食物种类，因此在很大程度上，垃圾食品不再可用，并且非常强调健康饮食，包括水果和蔬菜。

college-writing-010732.en: Schools are now practicing what they preach about the importance of healthy diets and it is commendable that they have stopped serving junk food.
college-writing-010732.zh: 学校现在正在实践他们所宣扬的健康饮食的重要性，值得称赞的是，他们已经停止提供垃圾食品。

college-writing-010733.en: OPTION 2 By the time many students reach high school, they have learned the basics in most subjects.
college-writing-010733.zh: 选项 2 当许多学生上高中时，他们已经学习了大多数科目的基础知识。

college-writing-010734.en: Some still have much to gain from the education that high schools
college-writing-010734.zh: 有些人仍然从高中的教育中获得很多好处

college-writing-010738.en: offer, but others might be better off spending the next four years in other ways.
college-writing-010738.zh: 提供，但其他人可能会在接下来的四年中以其他方式更好地度过。

college-writing-010739.en: For their benefit, high school attendance should be voluntary.
college-writing-010739.zh: 为了他们的利益，高中的出勤率应该是自愿的。

college-writing-010740.en: OPTION 3 Many of today’s young people are mainly concerned with prestigious careers, making money, and owning things.
college-writing-010740.zh: 选项 3 今天的许多年轻人主要关注享有盛誉的职业、赚钱和拥有东西。

college-writing-010741.en: It seems we no longer teach the benefits of spending time and money to help the community, the country, or the world.
college-writing-010741.zh: 似乎我们不再教花时间和金钱来帮助社区、国家或世界的好处。

college-writing-010742.en: Our country can strengthen these human values and improve the world by requiring young people to spend a year working in some type of community service.
college-writing-010742.zh: 我国可以通过要求年轻人花一年时间在某种类型的社区服务中工作来加强这些人的价值观并改善世界。

college-writing-010743.en: Protests and calls for activism are a cornerstone of American democracy.
college-writing-010743.zh: 抗议和呼吁激进主义是美国民主的基石。

college-writing-010745.en: Throughout history, people have publicly demonstrated for and against issues they feel passionately about.
college-writing-010745.zh: 纵观历史，人们公开展示支持和反对他们热衷的问题。

college-writing-010746.en: In 1963, thousands marched on Washington to protest the treatment of African Americans and demand equal civil rights.
college-writing-010746.zh: 1963 年，数千人向华盛顿游行，抗议非裔美国人的待遇并要求平等的公民权利。

college-writing-010747.en: In 1982, one million antinuclear protesters stood up against America’s development of nuclear weapons and called for an end to the cold war arms race.
college-writing-010747.zh: 1982 年，100 万反核抗议者站起来反对美国发展核武器，并呼吁结束冷战军备竞赛。

college-writing-010748.en: In 2016, the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe was joined by other tribes (or Native Nations), celebrities, and politicians to take a stand against the Dakota Access Pipeline to protect sacred land and water.
college-writing-010748.zh: 2016 年，其他部落（或土著国家）、名人和政治家也加入了立岩苏族部落，反对达科他州通道管道，以保护神圣的土地和水。

college-writing-010749.en: In 2020, Americans throughout the nation protested police brutality against Black Americans.
college-writing-010749.zh: 2020年，全国各地的美国人抗议警察对美国黑人的暴行。

college-writing-010750.en: Having strong convictions, however, doesn’t always mean that a person needs to participate in a protest or public demonstration.
college-writing-010750.zh: 然而，有强烈的信念并不总是意味着一个人需要参加抗议或公开示威。

college-writing-010751.en: Some arguments are much less controversial.
college-writing-010751.zh: 有些论点的争议要少得多。

college-writing-010752.en: For instance, students may feel that parking fees at their schools are too high or student housing is inadequate.
college-writing-010752.zh: 例如，学生可能会觉得他们学校的停车费太高或学生宿舍不够。

college-writing-010753.en: Other students may feel passionately about healthy food choices being more available to those in lower socioeconomic groups.
college-writing-010753.zh: 其他学生可能会对健康食品的选择充满热情，这些选择更适合社会经济较低的群体。

college-writing-010754.en: For this assignment, you are to think about issues you are most concerned about.
college-writing-010754.zh: 对于这项任务，您要考虑您最关心的问题。

college-writing-010755.en: Then, you should support and defend your argument by drawing on your reasoning ability, general experience, and any necessary research.
college-writing-010755.zh: 然后，你应该通过利用你的推理能力、一般经验和任何必要的研究来支持和捍卫你的论点。

college-writing-010756.en: You may want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” and Chapter 12, “Cause and/or Effect.”
college-writing-010756.zh: 您可能要复习第 8 章“描述”、第 10 章“例证”和第 12 章“原因和/或影响”。

college-writing-010757.en: If you need to incorporate research, you will want to review Part 3, “Researching, Writing, and Documenting.”
college-writing-010757.zh: 如果您需要纳入研究，您将需要回顾第 3 部分“研究、写作和记录”。

college-writing-010758.en: The following essay is an example written by a student who suffers from celiac disease.
college-writing-010758.zh: 下面的论文是一个患有乳糜泻的学生写的例子。

college-writing-010759.en: The writer argues that doctors need to be more proactive in diagnosing the disease, so those afflicted can manage it and heal.
college-writing-010759.zh: 作者认为，医生需要更加积极主动地诊断疾病，以便那些受苦的人能够治愈和治愈。

college-writing-010762.zh: yy tog 我们 4 usten yj ?

college-writing-010765.zh: 390 第二部分 论文发展模式

college-writing-010766.en: Celiac Disease Needs to Be Diagnosed to Be Controlled
college-writing-010766.zh: 乳糜泻需要被诊断以控制

college-writing-010767.en: It is estimated that one person in one hundred suffers from celiac disease, a genetic disorder that causes digestive problems.
college-writing-010767.zh: 据估计，百分之一的人患有乳糜泻，这是一种导致消化问题的遗传疾病。

college-writing-010768.en: These problems occur when gluten, a protein composite found in grains like wheat and barley, is ingested.
college-writing-010768.zh: 当小麦和大麦等谷物中发现的一种蛋白质复合物时，会出现这些问题。

college-writing-010769.en: The symptoms of celiac disease can range from irritability and abdominal pain to severe weight loss and fatigue.
college-writing-010769.zh: 乳糜泻的症状可以从烦躁和腹痛到严重的体重减轻和疲劳。

college-writing-010770.en: Also called celiac sprue, non-tropical sprue, gluten-sensitive enteropathy, and coeliac disease, the disease can cause serious damage that ranges from malnutrition to cancer.
college-writing-010770.zh: 该疾病也称为乳糜泻、非热带浇道、麸质敏感性肠病和乳糜泻，可造成严重的损害，从营养不良到癌症。

college-writing-010771.en: Doctors currently don’t know exactly what causes the disease, but they do understand that people who have the disease have an overreaction to gluten in food.
college-writing-010771.zh: 医生目前不知道究竟是什么导致了这种疾病，但他们确实明白患有这种疾病的人对食物中的麸质反应过度。

college-writing-010772.en: Doctors need to take this disease seriously and run tests to diagnose it, so those suffering from the disease can take control of their lives.
college-writing-010772.zh: 医生需要认真对待这种疾病并进行测试以诊断它，这样患有这种疾病的人就可以控制自己的生活。

college-writing-010773.en: Even though diagnosing celiac disease can be difficult because many of the symptoms are similar to other diseases like Crohn’s, anemia, or irritable bowel syndrome, it is important that doctors learn to properly diagnose their patients.
college-writing-010773.zh: 尽管诊断乳糜泻可能很困难，因为许多症状与克罗恩病、贫血或肠易激综合征等其他疾病相似，但重要的是医生学会正确诊断患者。

college-writing-010774.en: The obvious symptoms of celiac disease are abdominal pain and bloating.
college-writing-010774.zh: 乳糜泻的明显症状是腹痛和腹胀。

college-writing-010775.en: Other less obvious symptoms can be mouth blisters, joint irritation, and painful nerve damage.
college-writing-010775.zh: 其他不太明显的症状可能是口腔水疱、关节刺激和疼痛的神经损伤。

college-writing-010776.en: More serious symptoms include weight loss, stunted growth, and osteoporosis.
college-writing-010776.zh: 更严重的症状包括体重减轻、发育迟缓和骨质疏松症。

college-writing-010777.en: These symptoms result from what is physically occurring within the small intestine.
college-writing-010777.zh: 这些症状是由小肠内发生的物理发生的。

college-writing-010778.en: The small intestine is lined with tiny finger-like projections called villi; the villi are covered with microvilli.
college-writing-010778.zh: 小肠内衬有称为绒毛的微小手指状突起； 绒毛覆盖着微绒毛。

college-writing-010779.en: The villi and microvilli increase absorption of nutrients.
college-writing-010779.zh: 绒毛和微绒毛增加了营养的吸收。

college-writing-010780.en: Celiac disease destroys them and obstructs nutrient absorption.
college-writing-010780.zh: 乳糜泻会破坏它们并阻碍营养吸收。

college-writing-010781.en: Without the villi, nutrients like vitamins and protein are not absorbed and are quickly eliminated, often resulting in painful diarrhea.
college-writing-010781.zh: 没有绒毛，维生素和蛋白质等营养素不会被吸收，很快就会被消除，经常导致疼痛的腹泻。

college-writing-010782.en: Whether the symptoms are mild or severe, patients need doctors to help them figure out the cause, so they can get the proper treatment.
college-writing-010782.zh: 无论症状是轻微的还是严重的，患者都需要医生帮助他们找出原因，这样他们才能得到适当的治疗。

college-writing-010783.en: Proper diagnosis of celiac disease often requires several expensive tests and procedures.
college-writing-010783.zh: 正确诊断乳糜泻通常需要几次昂贵的测试和程序。

college-writing-010784.en: A blood test to screen for transglutaminase antibody (tTG) is the primary test used to screen for celiac.
college-writing-010784.zh: 筛选转谷氨酰胺酶抗体 (TTG) 的血液测试是用于筛选乳糜泻的主要测试。

college-writing-010785.en: Several other tests, like a total immunoglobulin A test or the anti-giadan antibody, may be ordered if the tTG test is positive for celiac disease.
college-writing-010785.zh: 如果 TTG 测试对乳糜泻呈阳性，可能会订购其他几项测试，例如全免疫球蛋白 A 测试或抗 Giadan 抗体。

college-writing-010786.en: These tests will be positive in celiac sufferers because their bodies see gluten as an enemy substance and produce elevated levels of antibodies to fight the substance.
college-writing-010786.zh: 这些测试将在腹腔患者中呈阳性，因为他们的身体将麸质视为敌方物质，并产生更高水平的抗体来对抗这种物质。

college-writing-010787.en: If blood tests are positive, doctors will often test a sample of the small intestine to check for damaged villi.
college-writing-010787.zh: 如果血液检查呈阳性，医生通常会测试小肠样本以检查是否受损的绒毛。

college-writing-010788.en: Some doctors may have patients swallow a camera pill to examine the entire small intestine.
college-writing-010788.zh: 一些医生可能让病人吞下相机药丸来检查整个小肠。

college-writing-010789.en: Even though the procedures can be expensive, diagnosis is the only way patients can be sure of the correct treatment, so it is vital that doctors run the needed tests.
college-writing-010789.zh: 尽管程序可能很昂贵，但诊断是患者确定正确治疗的唯一方法，因此医生进行所需的测试至关重要。

college-writing-010790.en: Unfortunately, there is currently no cure for celiac disease nor medicine to control it, so doctors need to educate their patients about how to control their symptoms.
college-writing-010790.zh: 不幸的是，目前没有治愈乳糜泻的治愈方法，也没有药物来控制它，因此医生需要教育他们的患者如何控制他们的症状。

college-writing-010791.en: Celiac disease can be effectively managed through a rigid diet; any foods that contain gluten must be
college-writing-010791.zh: 乳糜泻可以通过僵硬的饮食得到有效的管理； 任何含有麸质的食物都必须是

college-writing-010794.en: Writing for a Specific Purpose and Audience
college-writing-010794.zh: 为特定目的和受众写作

college-writing-010795.en: In this essay with emphasis on argument, you will write with a specific purpose and for a specific audience.
college-writing-010795.zh: 在这篇强调论证的文章中，你将有特定的目的和特定的受众。

college-writing-010796.en: The art of persuasion in the workplace is so important that many businesses bring in educational consultants to teach employees how, why, and when to be persuasive.
college-writing-010796.zh: 工作场所的说服艺术非常重要，以至于许多企业聘请教育顾问来教员工如何、为什么以及何时具有说服力。

college-writing-010797.en: Often these companies charge several thousands of dollars for their expertise; however, to save money, your boss has asked you to write an essay that will be given to all employees explaining the art of persuasion and why it is a necessary skill in your workplace.
college-writing-010797.zh: 这些公司通常会因其专业知识而收取数千美元的费用； 然而，为了省钱，你的老板要求你写一篇文章，将给所有员工解释说服的艺术以及为什么它是你工作场所的必要技能。

college-writing-010798.en: In order for employees to understand what they are being asked to do, you should incorporate an extended definition of what good persuasion is, and possibly contrast it with what good persuasion is not.
college-writing-010798.zh: 为了让员工了解他们被要求做什么，您应该包含对好的说服力是什么的扩展定义，并可能将其与良好的说服力所没有的对比。

college-writing-010799.en: You may also want to incorporate scenarios that demonstrate both good and bad examples to help your audience fully understand how and when to be persuasive.
college-writing-010799.zh: 您可能还希望结合展示好例子和坏例子的场景，以帮助您的听众充分了解如何以及何时具有说服力。

college-writing-010800.en: Perhaps you work at an advertising company.
college-writing-010800.zh: 也许你在一家广告公司工作。

college-writing-010801.en: One of your jobs is to acquire new client accounts, and persuading them to sign with you usually involves a key presentation.
college-writing-010801.zh: 您的工作之一是获取新的客户帐户，说服他们与您签署通常涉及关键演示文稿。

college-writing-010802.en: As the writer of this essay, you could give an example of one of your best presentations, explaining what was done correctly and why it worked.
college-writing-010802.zh: 作为这篇文章的作者，你可以举一个你最好的演示文稿之一的例子，解释什么是正确的，以及它为什么有效。

college-writing-010803.en: You could also give an example of one of your worst presentations, emphasizing what was done incorrectly.
college-writing-010803.zh: 你也可以举一个你最糟糕的演示文稿之一的例子，强调做错了什么。

college-writing-010804.en: You will want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” Chapter 11, “Process,” Chapter 13, “Comparison and/or Contrast,” and Chapter 14, “Definition,” to help create a strong, persuasive essay.
college-writing-010804.zh: 您将需要回顾第 8 章“描述”、第 11 章“过程”、第 13 章，“比较和/或对比”和第 14 章“定义”，以帮助撰写一篇强有力、有说服力的文章。

college-writing-010807.en: Such foods include barley, bulgur, durum, farina, graham flour, rye, semolina, spelt, triticale, and wheat.
college-writing-010807.zh: 此类食物包括大麦、鼓舞人心、硬粒小麦、法利纳、格雷厄姆面粉、黑麦、粗面粉、斯佩尔特、小麦和小麦。

college-writing-010808.en: Most gluten is found in food, but people diagnosed with celiac disease should also be aware of medicines, vitamins, and lip balms that may contain gluten.
college-writing-010808.zh: 大多数面筋存在于食物中，但被诊断患有乳糜泻的人也应该了解可能含有麸质的药物、维生素和润唇膏。

college-writing-010809.en: Once a person has started on a gluten-free diet, the body will begin to recover.
college-writing-010809.zh: 一旦一个人开始进行无麸质饮食，身体就会开始恢复。

college-writing-010810.en: The inflammation within the intestine will subside within several weeks.
college-writing-010810.zh: 肠道内的炎症将在几周内消退。

college-writing-010811.en: Full healing and regrowth of the villi may take as long as two to three years.
college-writing-010811.zh: 绒毛的完全愈合和再生可能需要长达两到三年的时间。

college-writing-010812.en: Trace amounts of gluten can be damaging, so it is important that once a person is diagnosed with celiac they avoid all forms of gluten.
college-writing-010812.zh: 微量的麸质可能会造成破坏，因此一旦一个人被诊断出患有乳糜泻，他们就避免了所有形式的麸质。

college-writing-010813.en: It is believed that as many as two million people are currently undiagnosed with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
college-writing-010813.zh: 据信，目前有高达两百万人尚未被诊断出患有乳糜泻或麸质敏感性疾病。

college-writing-010814.en: It is imperative that doctors understand this disease and do not disregard patients who complain of symptoms of the disease.
college-writing-010814.zh: 医生必须了解这种疾病，并且不要忽视抱怨该疾病症状的患者。

college-writing-010815.en: Since there is currently no medication to help heal patients, it is crucial that doctors diagnose patients before serious physical damage occurs and teach their patients how to manage the disease to avoid more damage.
college-writing-010815.zh: 由于目前没有药物可以帮助治愈患者，因此医生在严重的身体损伤发生之前诊断患者并教导他们的患者如何管理疾病以避免更多的损害是至关重要的。

college-writing-010816.zh: 第392章 论文发展模式

college-writing-010818.en: p. 383: Burger, Edward, “Essay on the Importance of Teaching Failure,” Inside Higher Ed, August 21, 2012.
college-writing-010818.zh: P. 383：Burger, Edward，“关于教学失败重要性的论文”，在 Higher Ed 中，2012 年 8 月 21 日。

college-writing-010822.en: Have I included a thesis statement that clearly asserts an argument?
college-writing-010822.zh: 我是否包含了一个明确断言论点的 中心论点句？

college-writing-010823.en: Does each paragraph in my essay have a clear topic sentence that goes back to the thesis?
college-writing-010823.zh: 我文章中的每个段落是否都有一个清晰的 主题句 可以追溯到论文？

college-writing-010824.en: Are there portions of the essay that do not support my thesis and therefore should be eliminated or rewritten?
college-writing-010824.zh: 文章中是否有部分不支持我的论文，因此应该被删除或重写？

college-writing-010826.en: Have I provided persuasive details to support my argument?
college-writing-010826.zh: 我是否提供了有说服力的细节来支持我的论点？

college-writing-010827.en: Have I included enough specific details to persuade my reader to agree with my argument?
college-writing-010827.zh: 我是否包含了足够的具体细节来说服我的读者同意我的论点？

college-writing-010829.en: Have I acknowledged the opposing point of view, to demonstrate I have considered other arguments?
college-writing-010829.zh: 我是否承认相反的观点，以证明我考虑过其他论点？

college-writing-010830.en: Have I provided a concluding paragraph to summarize my argument or to add a final persuasive touch?
college-writing-010830.zh: 我是否提供了一个结论段落来总结我的论点或添加最后的说服力？

college-writing-010832.en: Have I used a consistent point of view throughout my essay?
college-writing-010832.zh: 我在整个论文中都使用了一致的观点吗？

college-writing-010833.en: Have I used specific rather than general words?
college-writing-010833.zh: 我使用过特定的而不是一般的词吗？

college-writing-010834.en: Have I avoided wordiness and used concise wording?
college-writing-010834.zh: 我是否避免冗长并使用简洁的措辞？

college-writing-010836.en: Have I edited for spelling and other sentence skills errors, as listed in the checklist at the back of the book?
college-writing-010836.zh: 我是否编辑了书面清单中列出的拼写和其他句子技能错误？

college-writing-010838.en: Write an essay about an experience you have had researching for and writing a source-based essay.
college-writing-010838.zh: 写一篇关于你研究和撰写基于来源的论文的经历的文章。

college-writing-010839.en: What struggles and successes did you have?

college-writing-010840.en: What could have made the process better?
college-writing-010840.zh: 是什么让这个过程变得更好？

college-writing-010841.en: If you haven’t yet written a source-based essay, write an essay about any concerns you have about the process and any challenges you anticipate.
college-writing-010841.zh: 如果您还没有写一篇基于来源的文章，请写一篇关于您对流程和您预期的任何挑战的任何担忧的文章。

college-writing-010850.en: Write a letter to yourself exploring the difficulties you have had in the past navigating the Internet and your school library while trying to do research for a paper.
college-writing-010850.zh: 给自己写一封信，探索过去在互联网和学校图书馆中所遇到的困难，同时尝试研究论文。

college-writing-010852.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate how to • locate online sources efficiently • evaluate online sources • use the library in the context of the digital world
college-writing-010852.zh: 本章将解释和说明如何有效地定位在线资源 • 评估在线资源 • 在数字世界的背景下使用图书馆

college-writing-010854.en: Engaging in research means dealing with a lot of information from different sources.
college-writing-010854.zh: 从事研究意味着处理来自不同来源的大量信息。

college-writing-010855.en: One of the keys to good research is understanding how to navigate all the information that is available to you.
college-writing-010855.zh: 良好研究的关键之一是了解如何导航您可用的所有信息。

college-writing-010856.en: Students have the option of using:

college-writing-010857.en: C H A P T E R 17 17

college-writing-010867.en: Navigating all this information and choosing what type is best for the project at hand can be overwhelming.
college-writing-010867.zh: 浏览所有这些信息并选择最适合手头项目的类型可能会让人不知所措。

college-writing-010868.en: Figuring out which of the multitude of results are credible and trustworthy and will support the purpose of your paper can also be daunting.
college-writing-010868.zh: 弄清楚哪些结果中有哪些是可信和可信的，并且支持您的论文的目的也可能令人生畏。

college-writing-010869.en: Often, students begin their research by going online, which usually nets more results than are possible to evaluate.
college-writing-010869.zh: 通常，学生通过上网开始他们的研究，这通常会获得比可能评估的更多的结果。

college-writing-010870.en: This can cause both frustration and wasted time as students try to figure out where to start and what to read.
college-writing-010870.zh: 当学生试图弄清楚从哪里开始和阅读什么时，这可能会导致挫败感和浪费时间。

college-writing-010871.en: Especially when operating under a time crunch, students don’t always select the best resources for their papers.
college-writing-010871.zh: 尤其是在时间紧缩的情况下，学生并不总是为他们的论文选择最好的资源。

college-writing-010872.en: Knowing how to properly approach online research by using the right search engines and search terms and the right databases, as well as knowing how to find credible information, will save both time and frustration.
college-writing-010872.zh: 知道如何通过使用正确的搜索引擎和搜索词以及正确的数据库以及知道如何找到可靠的信息来正确进行在线研究将节省时间和挫败感。

college-writing-010873.en: While you will most likely do a majority of your research online, you want to keep all resource possibilities open.
college-writing-010873.zh: 虽然您很可能会在线进行大部分研究，但您希望保持所有资源的可能性。

college-writing-010874.en: You should always start with your college library, as it will provide you with the best sources.
college-writing-010874.zh: 您应该始终从您的大学图书馆开始，因为它将为您提供最好的资源。

college-writing-010875.en: Since, like most libraries, it has a variety of print, online, and media sources available, it can be challenging to navigate the resources in a college library.
college-writing-010875.zh: 由于与大多数图书馆一样，它拥有各种印刷、在线和媒体资源，因此在大学图书馆中浏览资源可能具有挑战性。

college-writing-010876.en: Even though these are “library sources,” you still have to understand how to evaluate and sift through your findings to find the best information for your needs.
college-writing-010876.zh: 即使这些是“图书馆来源”，您仍然必须了解如何评估和筛选您的发现，以找到适合您需求的最佳信息。

college-writing-010884.en: In addition, you will need to decide whether primary sources or secondary sources are best for your research.
college-writing-010884.zh: 此外，您需要确定主要来源或二级来源最适合您的研究。

college-writing-010885.en: Primary sources are original sources─documents like:
college-writing-010885.zh: 主要来源是原始来源——文档如：

college-writing-010892.zh: 396 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-010893.en: Although this chapter focuses on finding good sources for research, you should apply these same skills to any information you read, hear, or see on any media platform.
college-writing-010893.zh: 尽管本章侧重于寻找良好的研究来源，但您应该将这些相同的技能应用于您在任何媒体平台上阅读、听到或看到的任何信息。

college-writing-010894.en: You should be aware of two types of false information.
college-writing-010894.zh: 您应该了解两种类型的虚假信息。

college-writing-010895.en: Misinformation is information that is falsely presented as correct with or without intent to mislead.
college-writing-010895.zh: 错误信息是错误地呈现为正确或无意误导的信息。

college-writing-010896.en: Disinformation is false information that is deliberately disseminated to manipulate a narrative.
college-writing-010896.zh: 虚假信息是故意传播以操纵叙述的虚假信息。

college-writing-010897.en: Knowing how to critically evaluate sources, consult multiple sources, and understand source reliability will help you in both research and daily life.
college-writing-010897.zh: 了解如何批判性地评估来源、咨询多个来源并了解来源的可靠性将有助于您在研究和日常生活中。

college-writing-010902.en: • commentaries on a piece of research

college-writing-010903.en: Knowing how to identify the best and most appropriate sources for your work and how to use each source accurately will help you immeasurably in your research and significantly reduce the amount of time you’ll need to spend.
college-writing-010903.zh: 知道如何为您的工作确定最佳和最合适的来源以及如何准确使用每个来源将帮助您在研究中无可估量，并显着减少您需要花费的时间。

college-writing-010904.en: This chapter will introduce you to ways of managing and evaluating resources to help you efficiently research information that supports the purpose of each essay that you write.
college-writing-010904.zh: 本章将向您介绍管理和评估资源的方法，以帮助您有效地研究支持您撰写的每篇文章目的的信息。

college-writing-010905.en: Using Online Sources Effectively Locating Sources Efficiently When faced with a research paper assignment, students’ initial reaction is to go to Google, type in some terms and start reading the links in the order they appear.
college-writing-010905.zh: 使用在线资源 有效地定位资源 在面对研究论文作业时，学生的最初反应是去谷歌，输入一些术语并开始按照它们出现的顺序阅读链接。

college-writing-010906.en: Often, the first link students will see is Wikipedia, which seems to be full of information.
college-writing-010906.zh: 通常，学生将看到的第一个链接是维基百科，它似乎充满了信息。

college-writing-010907.en: However, the nature of Wikipedia─a site that can be edited by anyone─makes it unreliable as a source, regardless of its position in the list of results.
college-writing-010907.zh: 然而，维基百科的性质——一个可以被任何人编辑的网站——无论其在结果列表中的位置如何，它作为一个来源都不可靠。

college-writing-010908.en: Understanding that rank order doesn’t necessarily mean that site is the best choice should make students wary of beginning with a general Google search.
college-writing-010908.zh: 了解排名顺序并不一定意味着网站是最佳选择应该让学生对从一般的谷歌搜索开始持谨慎态度。

college-writing-010909.en: Another weakness of starting with Google is that this type of research can lead to an overwhelming number of results, which will take far too long to sort through.
college-writing-010909.zh: 从谷歌开始的另一个弱点是，这种类型的研究可能会导致大量的结果，这将花费太长时间来解决。

college-writing-010910.en: It can also take more time than necessary as students try to determine what search terms will deliver the best results.
college-writing-010910.zh: 当学生尝试确定哪些搜索词将提供最佳结果时，也可能需要更多的时间。

college-writing-010911.en: Since search engines go through a vast amount of information to find articles containing any of the words you have put into your search, knowing what search engine to use for information gathering, how best to search, and how to sift through the results is important for all researchers.
college-writing-010911.zh: 由于搜索引擎会通过大量的信息来查找包含您在搜索中投入的任何单词的文章，因此了解用于信息收集的搜索引擎、如何最好地搜索以及如何筛选结果对所有研究人员都很重要。

college-writing-010914.en: While most people think of Google when they look up information, it is not the only search engine option, and students should try different ones.
college-writing-010914.zh: 虽然大多数人在查找信息时会想到谷歌，但它不是唯一的搜索引擎选项，学生应该尝试不同的选择。

college-writing-010915.en: Meta search engines can produce more results because they get information from other search engines and are not confined to only one source of indexing.
college-writing-010915.zh: 元搜索引擎可以产生更多的结果，因为它们从其他搜索引擎中获取信息，并且不仅限于一种索引来源。

college-writing-010916.en: There are also specialized search engines that refine results to certain types of sources.
college-writing-010916.zh: 还有专门的搜索引擎可以将结果精化到某些类型的来源。

college-writing-010917.en: Being familiar with specialized search engines can save you time because these engines focus their searches in specific areas.
college-writing-010917.zh: 熟悉专门的搜索引擎可以节省您的时间，因为这些引擎将搜索集中在特定领域。

college-writing-010921.en: • Mamma (retrieves news, image, and videos with filter capability) • Symbaloo (can retrieve information from social networking sites like Twitter and image-sharing platforms like Instagram) • Turbo Scout (searches other meta search engines)
college-writing-010921.zh: • Mamma（检索具有过滤功能的新闻、图像和视频） • Symbaloo（可以从Twitter和Instagram等图像共享平台中检索信息） • Turbo Scout（搜索其他元搜索引擎）

college-writing-010923.en: • Google Scholar (searches scholarly articles) • WolframAlpha (creates data comparisons) • LivePlasma (searches books, movies, and music)
college-writing-010923.zh: • Google Scholar（搜索学术文章） • Wolframalpha（创建数据比较） • Liveplasma（搜索书籍、电影和音乐）

college-writing-010924.en: Using a specialized search engine like Google Scholar can narrow an initial search dramatically and can reduce the number of results by 97 percent.
college-writing-010924.zh: 使用像 Google Scholar 这样的专业搜索引擎可以显着缩小初始搜索范围，并且可以将结果数量减少 97%。

college-writing-010925.en: An additional benefit to using Google Scholar is that the results will all be from scholarly sources that have been evaluated by several people prior to their publication.
college-writing-010925.zh: 使用 Google Scholar 的另一个好处是，结果都将来自一些人在发表之前已经评估过的学术资源。

college-writing-010926.en: Like professionally published print sources, scholarly sources have to be approved by editors, peer reviewers, and publishers before they are accepted.
college-writing-010926.zh: 与专业出版的印刷来源一样，学术资源必须得到编辑、同行评审员和出版商的批准才能被接受。

college-writing-010927.en: You may not be able to get access to full-text copies of all the academic sources you find through your search, so you may need to use a database to access one, several, or all of the results you want to use.
college-writing-010927.zh: 您可能无法访问通过搜索找到的所有学术来源的全文副本，因此您可能需要使用数据库来访问您想要使用的一个、多个或所有结果。

college-writing-010928.en: Searching with Keywords and Boolean Operators
college-writing-010928.zh: 使用关键字和布尔运算符进行搜索

college-writing-010929.en: Being familiar with strong search terms (keywords) is also important when “Googling.”
college-writing-010929.zh: 在“谷歌搜索”时，熟悉强搜索词（关键字）也很重要。

college-writing-010930.en: If you want to do a paper on free college tuition, using Google will get you over 65 million results.
college-writing-010930.zh: 如果你想写一篇关于免费大学学费的论文，使用谷歌将获得超过 6500 万个结果。

college-writing-010931.en: However, if you narrow your search to debt-free college tuition debate, the results narrow to just over 450,000.
college-writing-010931.zh: 但是，如果您将搜索范围缩小到无债务的大学学费辩论，结果将缩小到刚刚超过 450,000。

college-writing-010933.en: Knowing how to best use keywords will help you save time.
college-writing-010933.zh: 了解如何最好地使用关键字将帮助您节省时间。

college-writing-010934.en: Keywords, like free college above, are the general terms that are entered into search engines.
college-writing-010934.zh: 关键字，如上面的免费大学，是输入搜索引擎的一般术语。

college-writing-010936.zh: 398 第 3 部分研究、写作和记录

college-writing-010937.en: keywords are typed into a search, documents with all those words will be included in the list of results.
college-writing-010937.zh: 关键字被输入到搜索中，所有这些单词的文档都将包含在结果列表中。

college-writing-010938.en: However, because all the words are included, no matter how insignificantly they have been used within the document, thousands, if not millions, of results will be returned.
college-writing-010938.zh: 但是，因为所有的单词都被包含在内，无论它们在文档中多么微不足道，都会返回数千甚至数百万个结果。

college-writing-010939.en: This is why you need to be as specific as possible.
college-writing-010939.zh: 这就是为什么你需要尽可能具体的原因。

college-writing-010940.en: Narrowing a search to debt-free college tuition debate will net fewer results because you have expanded all the specific words that must be contained in the document.
college-writing-010940.zh: 将搜索范围缩小到无债务的大学学费辩论将减少结果，因为您已经扩展了文档中必须包含的所有特定单词。

college-writing-010941.en: When searching with keywords, you will want to be aware of how synonyms and different phrases can affect not only the number of results, but also the quality of results.
college-writing-010941.zh: 使用关键字进行搜索时，您将希望了解同义词和不同短语如何不仅影响结果的数量，还会影响结果的质量。

college-writing-010942.en: For instance, if you started researching with the keywords free college you would get over one billion results because the words are all very broad.
college-writing-010942.zh: 例如，如果您开始使用关键字免费大学进行研究，您将获得超过 10 亿的结果，因为这些单词都非常广泛。

college-writing-010943.en: Knowing that you want to find information on either attending college for free or graduating without debt─debt-free─will help you find more relevant material.
college-writing-010943.zh: 知道您想免费上大学或在没有债务的情况下找到有关信息的信息（无债务）将帮助您找到更多相关的材料。

college-writing-010944.en: This same idea applies to the word debate in the search.
college-writing-010944.zh: 同样的想法也适用于搜索中的辩论一词。

college-writing-010945.en: If you change the word debate to argument, the number of results increases because the word argument has much broader meanings.
college-writing-010945.zh: 如果您将“辩论”一词改为论证，结果的数量会增加，因为“论证”一词具有更广泛的含义。

college-writing-010946.en: Be willing to try different, more specific, words as you search.
college-writing-010946.zh: 在搜索时愿意尝试不同的、更具体的单词。

college-writing-010948.en: Understanding Boolean operators can also help you narrow your searches.
college-writing-010948.zh: 了解布尔运算符还可以帮助您缩小搜索范围。

college-writing-010949.en: By adding quotation marks around words, using AND, OR, or NOT, you can quickly change your results.
college-writing-010949.zh: 通过在单词周围添加引号，使用和，或，或不，您可以快速更改结果。

college-writing-010950.en: In the earlier Google search, changing the phrase to debt-free and college causes the results to jump to seven million, but by changing the phrase to “debt-free AND college,” the results drop to just seven.
college-writing-010950.zh: 在早期的谷歌搜索中，将短语改为无债务和大学导致结果跃升至 700 万，但通过将短语改为“无债务和大学”，结果降至仅七。

college-writing-010951.en: Boolean operators can be used with any of the search engines.
college-writing-010951.zh: 布尔运算符可以与任何搜索引擎一起使用。

college-writing-010953.en: Databases, like JSTOR and Academic Search Elite, are services that offer you the ability to search and access periodicals and journals online.
college-writing-010953.zh: 数据库，如 JSTOR 和 Academic Search Elite，是为您提供在线搜索和访问期刊和期刊的能力的服务。

college-writing-010954.en: Most databases have to be accessed through a subscription service, so your library will be your best source.
college-writing-010954.zh: 大多数数据库必须通过订阅服务访问，因此您的库将是您的最佳来源。

college-writing-010955.en: However, if your library doesn’t subscribe to a certain database that you need to use, many offer individual subscriptions for reasonable fees.
college-writing-010955.zh: 但是，如果您的图书馆没有订阅您需要使用的某个数据库，许多人会以合理的费用提供个人订阅。

college-writing-010956.en: In this way you can, for example, read editions of The Harvard Review from the past thirty years.
college-writing-010956.zh: 例如，您可以通过这种方式阅读过去 30 年的《哈佛评论》的版本。

college-writing-010957.en: Common library databases will be discussed in more detail later in the chapter.
college-writing-010957.zh: 普通库数据库将在本章后面更详细地讨论。

college-writing-010958.en: Evaluating Online Sources Keep in mind that the quality and reliability of information you find on the Internet may vary widely, and it is your responsibility to learn how to discern valuable information from propaganda.
college-writing-010958.zh: 评估在线资源 记住，您在互联网上找到的信息的质量和可靠性可能会有很大差异，您有责任学习如何从宣传中辨别出有价值的信息。

college-writing-010959.en: Most reputable journals, news sources, and published books have editors and other staff members to verify information, thus giving you some assurance that care has been taken with the information.
college-writing-010959.zh: 大多数有信誉的期刊、新闻来源和出版的书籍都有编辑和其他工作人员来验证信息，从而让您确信已经对信息进行了谨慎处理。

college-writing-010960.en: Online, however, no such quality control exists.
college-writing-010960.zh: 然而，在线不存在这样的质量控制。

college-writing-010961.en: Anyone with a bit of computer know-how can create
college-writing-010961.zh: 任何有一点计算机知识的人都可以创建

college-writing-010963.en: a website, and it is very common for the information on sites to change overnight.
college-writing-010963.zh: 一个网站，网站上的信息在一夜之间发生变化是很常见的。

college-writing-010964.en: The designer of a website may be a Nobel Prize winner, a leading authority in a specialized field, a high school student, or a conspiracy theory zealot.
college-writing-010964.zh: 网站的设计师可以是诺贝尔奖获得者、专业领域的领军人物、高中生或阴谋论狂热者。

college-writing-010965.en: While the following information focuses on websites and other online sources, you should evaluate all your research (including print and media) in this manner to be sure you are using sources that are credible and support the purpose of your paper.
college-writing-010965.zh: 虽然以下信息侧重于网站和其他在线资源，但您应该以这种方式评估您的所有研究（包括印刷和媒体），以确保您使用的是可信的来源并支持您论文的目的。

college-writing-010966.en: Determining the Reliability of an Online Source
college-writing-010966.zh: 确定在线来源的可靠性

college-writing-010967.en: Be careful to look closely at any source in the following ways:
college-writing-010967.zh: 仔细观察任何源头的方式：

college-writing-010968.en: 1. Internet address: In a Web address (the Uniform Resource Locator or URL), the three letters following the “dot” are the domain.
college-writing-010968.zh: 1. Internet 地址：在网址（统一资源定位器或 URL）中，“点”后面的三个字母是域。

college-writing-010973.zh: org（非营利组织或有时营利性组织）。

college-writing-010974.en: A common misconception is that a website’s reliability can be determined by its domain.
college-writing-010974.zh: 一个常见的误解是网站的可靠性可以由其领域决定。

college-writing-010975.en: This is not the case, as almost anyone can get a Web address ending in .
college-writing-010975.zh: 情况并非如此，因为几乎任何人都可以获得以 . 结尾的网址。

college-writing-010978.en: org, or any of the other domains.

college-writing-010979.en: Therefore, it is important that you examine every website carefully, considering the four points that follow.
college-writing-010979.zh: 因此，考虑到以下四点，您仔细检查每个网站非常重要。

college-writing-010980.en: 2. Publisher or Sponsor: Who maintains the site?
college-writing-010980.zh: 2. 出版商或赞助商：谁维护网站？

college-writing-010981.zh: 组织/团体/个人有声望吗？

college-writing-010983.en: Remember, these don’t determine reliability, but they can help you find out who is responsible for the website.
college-writing-010983.zh: 请记住，这些并不能确定可靠性，但它们可以帮助您找出谁对网站负责。

college-writing-010984.en: The National Archives searchable database is a good resource for reliable information.
college-writing-010984.zh: 国家档案馆可搜索数据库是提供可靠信息的良好资源。

college-writing-010988.en: Research in the National Archives Catalog, Other Online Research Tools
college-writing-010988.zh: 国家档案馆目录和其他在线研究工具的研究

college-writing-010990.en: @ Research Your WH Research Cy Research a
college-writing-010990.zh: @研究您的 WH 研究 CY 研究

college-writing-010991.en: Ancestry Military Records \ Specific Topic Research Events
college-writing-010991.zh: 祖先军事记录 \ 特定主题研究活动

college-writing-010992.zh: 400 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-010993.en: 3. Author: What credentials does the author have (if any)?
college-writing-010993.zh: 3. 作者：作者有什么凭据（如果有的话）？

college-writing-010994.en: Has the author published other material on the topic?
college-writing-010994.zh: 作者是否发表了有关该主题的其他材料？

college-writing-010995.en: Is the author known to have a particular stance (bias) on this topic?
college-writing-010995.zh: 作者是否知道对这个主题有特定的立场（偏见）？

college-writing-010996.en: You may need to do some additional research through a Web search or library database search to find this information.
college-writing-010996.zh: 您可能需要通过网络搜索或图书馆数据库搜索进行一些额外的研究才能找到这些信息。

college-writing-010998.en: Check at the top or bottom of the document for copyright, publication, or revision dates.
college-writing-010998.zh: 在文档的顶部或底部检查版权、出版物或修订日期。

college-writing-010999.en: Knowing such dates will help you decide whether the material is current enough for your purposes.
college-writing-010999.zh: 了解此类日期将帮助您确定材料是否足以满足您的目的。

college-writing-011000.en: 5. Internal evidence: Does the author seem to proceed objectively─presenting all sides of a topic fairly before arguing their own views?
college-writing-011000.zh: 5. 内部证据：作者似乎在争论自己的观点之前公平地客观地展示了一个主题的各个方面？

college-writing-011001.en: Does the author produce solid, adequate support for those views?
college-writing-011001.zh: 作者是否为这些观点提供了坚实、充分的支持？

college-writing-011002.en: Results from a keyword search on Google using “free college tuition debate.”
college-writing-011002.zh: 使用“免费大学学费辩论”在谷歌上进行关键字搜索的结果。

college-writing-011030.en: Comparing Results from Different Search Engines
college-writing-011030.zh: 比较不同搜索引擎的结果

college-writing-011031.en: The two preceding images show the different results a student could expect when using Google versus Google Scholar.
college-writing-011031.zh: 前面的两张图片显示了学生在使用 Google Scholar 时可能期望的不同结果。

college-writing-011032.en: Although the same search terms were used, the results on Google Scholar were not only fewer, but they were also more focused and research based.
college-writing-011032.zh: 尽管使用了相同的搜索词，但 Google Scholar 上的结果不仅较少，而且它们也更加专注和基于研究。

college-writing-011033.en: Notice the difference in the number of results and types of results:
college-writing-011033.zh: 注意结果数量和结果类型的差异：

college-writing-011034.en: • In the first image, you can see that the first result is from the American Psychological Association, a well-known organization that works to advance the science of psychology.
college-writing-011034.zh: • 在第一张图片中，您可以看到第一个结果来自美国心理学会，该协会是一个致力于推进心理学科学的知名组织。

college-writing-011035.en: While it is a reputable source, you will still need to verify information you use from this site.
college-writing-011035.zh: 虽然它是一个有信誉的来源，但您仍然需要验证您从本网站使用的信息。

college-writing-011036.en: • The second result is a business-based website with information about tuition-free schools.
college-writing-011036.zh: • 第二个结果是一个基于商业的网站，提供有关免学费学校的信息。

college-writing-011037.en: A source like this will require you to read through the “about” section and verify the information.
college-writing-011037.zh: 像这样的来源将要求您阅读“关于”部分并验证信息。

college-writing-011038.en: For instance, this website claims that Alice Lloyd College is tuition-free; you could verify this by going directly to the college’s website.
college-writing-011038.zh: 例如，该网站声称爱丽丝劳埃德学院是免学费的； 您可以通过直接访问学院的网站来验证这一点。

college-writing-011039.en: Results from a keyword search on Google Scholar using “free college tuition debate.”
college-writing-011039.zh: 使用“免费大学学费辩论”在 Google Scholar 上进行关键字搜索的结果。

college-writing-011049.zh: 402 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011050.en: • The third result is an online political and intellectual journal.
college-writing-011050.zh: • 第三个结果是在线政治和智力期刊。

college-writing-011051.en: This site will also require you to read the “about” section to learn who publishes the site, who the authors are, and what organization is behind the site.
college-writing-011051.zh: 本网站还将要求您阅读“关于”部分以了解谁发布了该网站、作者是谁以及该网站背后的组织是什么。

college-writing-011052.en: Politically oriented websites will always have a strong bias, so it is very important that you spend time fact-checking before you use such a source as support.
college-writing-011052.zh: 以政治为导向的网站总是有强烈的偏见，因此在使用此类来源作为支持之前，花时间进行事实核查非常重要。

college-writing-011053.en: • The fourth result is from a popular news source.
college-writing-011053.zh: • 第四个结果来自流行的新闻来源。

college-writing-011054.en: While it is a well-known source, you will still need to spend time validating the information and checking any claims provided for bias.
college-writing-011054.zh: 虽然它是一个众所周知的来源，但您仍然需要花时间验证信息并检查为偏见提供的任何索赔。

college-writing-011055.en: • The fifth result is an organization, and the sixth result is a commercial news site.
college-writing-011055.zh: • 第五个结果是一个组织，第六个结果是商业新闻网站。

college-writing-011056.en: Both of these will require you to read the “about” sections, look at biases, and verify information the authors present.
college-writing-011056.zh: 这两个都需要您阅读“关于”部分，查看偏见，并验证作者提供的信息。

college-writing-011057.en: • In the second image, you can see all the results are from articles cited in other studies, based on research and published in specialized journals.
college-writing-011057.zh: • 在第二张图片中，您可以看到所有结果来自其他研究中引用的文章，这些文章基于研究并发表在专业期刊上。

college-writing-011058.en: These sources, while as potentially biased as organizations, do go through more steps in order to be published, so their credibility is already potentially stronger than the organizations and newspapers.
college-writing-011058.zh: 这些来源虽然像组织一样具有潜在偏见，但确实会采取更多步骤才能出版，因此它们的可信度已经可能比组织和报纸更强大。

college-writing-011059.en: You will still need to spend time analyzing the sources to determine how valuable they will be for your research, but you won’t need to spend as much time determining whether or not the sources are credible.
college-writing-011059.zh: 您仍然需要花时间分析资源以确定它们对您的研究的价值，但您不需要花太多时间来确定这些来源是否可信。

college-writing-011060.en: Using Critical Thinking to Examine Online Sources
college-writing-011060.zh: 使用批判性思维检查在线资源

college-writing-011061.en: Once you have determined whether or not a source is reliable, you then need to work through the material to determine how well it will support the purpose of your essay.
college-writing-011061.zh: 一旦你确定了一个来源是否可靠，你就需要通过材料来确定它在多大程度上支持你的论文目的。

college-writing-011062.en: You will first want to analyze the author’s argument, think about whether or not you have seen a similar opinion expressed elsewhere, and ask yourself if it endorses or counters the argument you are presenting (just because it counters your argument doesn’t mean you cannot use it).
college-writing-011062.zh: 您首先要分析作者的论点，想想您是否在其他地方看到过类似的观点，并问自己是否认可或反驳了您提出的论点（仅仅因为它与您的论点相反，并不意味着您不能使用它）。

college-writing-011063.en: As you look at the author’s argument, you want to think about whether or not the author’s support is valid and verifiable.
college-writing-011063.zh: 当您查看作者的论点时，您想考虑作者的支持是否有效且可验证。

college-writing-011064.en: Just because someone repeats something multiple times doesn’t make it true.
college-writing-011064.zh: 仅仅因为某人多次重复某事并不能使它成为现实。

college-writing-011065.en: Another good way to verify your source is to look at the sources the author has cited.
college-writing-011065.zh: 验证来源的另一个好方法是查看作者引用的来源。

college-writing-011066.en: If the author is citing obviously biased sites or fake news sites, no matter how good the argument sounds, it is most likely based on poor information.
college-writing-011066.zh: 如果作者引用明显有偏见的网站或假新闻网站，无论论点听起来多么好，它很可能是基于不良信息。

college-writing-011067.en: When you decide that the resource will work in your research, you will want to familiarize yourself with it by reading it several times and determining how you see it fitting into your paper.
college-writing-011067.zh: 当您决定该资源将在您的研究中起作用时，您将希望通过阅读几次并确定您如何看待它与您的论文来熟悉它。
