college-writing-011114.en: Using the Library in the Context of the Digital World
college-writing-011114.zh: 在数字世界的背景下使用图书馆

college-writing-011115.en: College libraries occupy both physical and virtual space.
college-writing-011115.zh: 大学图书馆占据物理空间和虚拟空间。

college-writing-011116.en: Getting familiar with both will benefit you well as you embark on your college journey.
college-writing-011116.zh: 当您踏上大学之旅时，熟悉两者都会对您有利。

college-writing-011117.en: The online resources can usually be accessed via your college library’s home page, which typically contains information that includes location, hours, catalog of holdings, and selected databases.
college-writing-011117.zh: 在线资源通常可以通过您的大学图书馆主页访问，该主页通常包含位置、小时数、馆藏目录和选定的数据库的信息。

college-writing-011118.en: Some library home pages include features like:
college-writing-011118.zh: 一些库主页包含以下功能：

college-writing-011119.zh: • 与图书管理员即时聊天

college-writing-011123.en: • lists of websites that librarians have found to be useful and credible
college-writing-011123.zh: • 图书馆员发现有用且可信的网站列表

college-writing-011124.en: Most students know that libraries’ physical buildings provide study space, computer workstations, and copying machines.
college-writing-011124.zh: 大多数学生都知道图书馆的物理建筑提供学习空间、计算机工作站和复印机。

college-writing-011125.en: You should also be aware of a library’s reading area, which contains recent copies of magazines and newspapers.
college-writing-011125.zh: 您还应该了解图书馆的阅读区，其中包含最近的杂志和报纸副本。

college-writing-011126.en: Other features that you will find in the library are listed here:
college-writing-011126.zh: 您将在库中找到的其他功能如下所示：

college-writing-011127.en: • rows of books that can be perused and checked out
college-writing-011127.zh: • 可以仔细阅读和签出的一排书籍

college-writing-011128.en: • DVDs and CDs that can be borrowed
college-writing-011128.zh: • 可以借用的 DVD 和 CD

college-writing-011129.en: • general reference materials that can be used in the library
college-writing-011129.zh: • 可用于库中的一般参考资料

college-writing-011130.en: • special materials that instructors put on reserve for specific class use
college-writing-011130.zh: • 教师为特定班级使用预留的特殊材料

college-writing-011131.en: You should become familiar with your library and expect to use most, if not all, of its features at some point in your college experience.
college-writing-011131.zh: 您应该熟悉您的图书馆，并期望在您的大学经历中的某个阶段使用它的大部分（如果不是全部）功能。

college-writing-011132.en: The more familiar you are with everything your library has to offer, the less time you will spend locating the information you need.
college-writing-011132.zh: 您对图书馆所提供的一切的熟悉程度越熟悉，您就越少花费时间查找所需的信息。

college-writing-011135.en: is an excellent way to start developing this familiarity and to help you navigate all the library has to offer.
college-writing-011135.zh: 是开始开发这种熟悉度并帮助您浏览所有库所提供的一切的绝佳方式。

college-writing-011136.en: After a brief discussion of the role of librarians, we will examine the various resources─both print and online─a library offers.
college-writing-011136.zh: 在简要讨论了图书馆员的作用后，我们将研究各种资源——印刷和在线——图书馆提供的各种资源。

college-writing-011137.en: Librarians The number one resource available to you through your college library is the college librarian.
college-writing-011137.zh: 图书馆员 通过您的大学图书馆获得的第一大资源是大学图书馆员。

college-writing-011138.en: Librarians help students and faculty with a variety of things.
college-writing-011138.zh: 图书馆员帮助学生和教师处理各种各样的事情。

college-writing-011139.en: Often, we think of librarians acquiring, sorting, and checking out books, and while college librarians do just that, they also provide many other services.
college-writing-011139.zh: 通常，我们会想到图书馆员获取、分类和检查书籍，而大学图书馆员这样做，但他们还提供许多其他服务。

college-writing-011140.en: They work closely with faculty to make sure students’ needs are being met, and they often set up subject guides or reserve materials that might be helpful for projects they know faculty are assigning.
college-writing-011140.zh: 他们与教师密切合作，以确保满足学生的需求，并且他们经常设置主题指南或保留可能有助于他们知道教师分配的项目的材料。

college-writing-011141.en: They are knowledgeable about the resources available to you and can quickly point you to the materials you need, often finding information for you in minutes rather than the hours or even days it might take you without assistance.
college-writing-011141.zh: 他们了解您可用的资源，并且可以快速向您指出您需要的材料，通常会在几分钟内为您找到信息，而不是在没有帮助的情况下为您提供的时间甚至几天。

college-writing-011142.en: Additionally, librarians often teach classes─in short sessions or sometimes over the course of a semester─about how to use the library and the library’s databases, how to conduct good research, and how to strengthen the skills you need to find, manage, and evaluate resources.
college-writing-011142.zh: 此外，图书馆员经常在短期或有时在一个学期的课程中教授课程——关于如何使用图书馆和图书馆的数据库、如何进行良好的研究以及如何加强您查找、管理和评估资源所需的技能。

college-writing-011143.zh: 参考资料 主要来源

college-writing-011144.en: Primary sources are original sources; they include conference presentations, dissertations, memoirs, photographs and paintings, speeches, works of literature, and government documents.
college-writing-011144.zh: 主要来源是原始来源； 它们包括会议演讲、论文、回忆录、照片和绘画、演讲、文学作品和政府文件。

college-writing-011145.en: Primary sources give students a direct connection to current and past events.
college-writing-011145.zh: 主要来源为学生提供了与当前和过去事件的直接联系。

college-writing-011146.en: By working directly with primary sources, students can create their own analyses of the original pieces without being influenced by others’ interpretations.
college-writing-011146.zh: 通过直接使用主要来源，学生可以创建自己对原始作品的分析，而不会受到他人解释的影响。

college-writing-011147.en: A good example of students’ work with primary sources is an assignment requiring the writing of a literary analysis or a rhetorical analysis.
college-writing-011147.zh: 学生使用主要来源工作的一个很好的例子是需要撰写文学分析或修辞分析的作业。

college-writing-011149.en: Secondary sources analyze, interpret, or comment on primary sources.
college-writing-011149.zh: 二级来源 分析、解释或评论主要来源。

college-writing-011150.en: Secondary sources include biographies, literature reviews, or articles written about primary sources.
college-writing-011150.zh: 次要来源包括传记、文献综述或撰写有关主要来源的文章。

college-writing-011151.en: While secondary sources are someone else’s interpretation and are often tainted by the prevailing social opinions, they can provide students with a wealth of information.
college-writing-011151.zh: 虽然次要来源是其他人的解释，并且经常受到流行的社会观点的影响，但它们可以为学生提供丰富的信息。

college-writing-011152.zh: 406 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011153.en: Using Both Primary and Secondary Sources Together
college-writing-011153.zh: 同时使用主要和次要来源

college-writing-011154.en: Often students will use secondary sources in conjunction with primary sources in order to create a full, clear picture of support.
college-writing-011154.zh: 通常，学生会将二级来源与主要来源结合使用，以创建完整、清晰的支持图景。

college-writing-011155.en: For instance, a student might be required to write an analysis of a Vincent van Gogh painting.
college-writing-011155.zh: 例如，学生可能需要写一篇文森特梵高画的分析。

college-writing-011156.en: They would first choose a painting that they find to be extremely interesting, and then analyze the piece themselves, focusing on any themes or techniques they are drawn to.
college-writing-011156.zh: 他们会首先选择一幅他们觉得非常有趣的画作，然后自己分析这幅画，专注于他们所吸引的任何主题或技术。

college-writing-011157.en: To add support and weight to their analysis, they could then locate articles from art critics in the early 1900s and early 2000s.
college-writing-011157.zh: 为了增加他们的分析支持和分量，他们可以找到 1900 年代初和 2000 年代初期艺术评论家的文章。

college-writing-011158.en: This would allow them to look at how van Gogh’s paintings were critiqued in different periods and compare these critiques to their own.
college-writing-011158.zh: 这将使他们能够看到梵高的画作如何在不同时期受到批评，并将这些批评与他们自己的批评进行比较。

college-writing-011160.en: General references include encyclopedias, world fact books, dictionaries, atlases, manuals, and so on.
college-writing-011160.zh: 一般参考文献包括百科全书、世界事实书籍、字典、地图集、手册等。

college-writing-011161.en: Most of these can be found online, but if you do want a print source, be aware that these are often for library use only, so you will want to be prepared to spend an hour or two in the library.
college-writing-011161.zh: 其中大部分可以在网上找到，但如果您确实想要一个打印源，请注意这些通常仅供图书馆使用，因此您需要准备在图书馆中度过一两个小时。

college-writing-011163.en: Many libraries will have certain books, periodicals, reports, videos, and journals that cannot be taken out of the library.
college-writing-011163.zh: 许多图书馆将拥有无法从图书馆中取出的某些书籍、期刊、报告、视频和期刊。

college-writing-011164.en: Instead, you will have to check out the material for a certain period, often two hours, and remain in the library while you read or view the material.
college-writing-011164.zh: 相反，您将不得不在一定时间内查看材料，通常是两个小时，并在阅读或查看材料时留在图书馆中。

college-writing-011165.en: It is common that professors will put such materials on reserve for students to use, but they will restrict the use to ensure all students have a chance to work with the material.
college-writing-011165.zh: 教授通常会将此类材料留给学生使用是很常见的，但他们会限制使用，以确保所有学生都有机会使用这些材料。

college-writing-011166.en: Library Catalog The library catalog, accessible both online and on-site, is your entry point to the holdings in your library.
college-writing-011166.zh: 图书馆目录 图书馆目录，可在线访问和现场访问，是您进入图书馆的入口点。

college-writing-011167.en: These holdings can include print books, eBooks, downloadable audio books, CDs, and DVDs.
college-writing-011167.zh: 这些馆藏可以包括印刷书籍、电子书、可下载的有声读物、CD 和 DVD。

college-writing-011168.en: Increasingly, more and more libraries have agreements with each other, so if a book or item isn’t available at your library, you may have the option of requesting it from another library.
college-writing-011168.zh: 越来越多的图书馆相互签订协议，因此如果您的图书馆没有一本书或物品，您可以选择从另一个图书馆请求它。

college-writing-011169.en: Your college library website and librarians should have this information readily available.
college-writing-011169.zh: 您的大学图书馆网站和图书馆员应随时获得这些信息。

college-writing-011171.en: There are numerous ways to find books using your library’s catalog.
college-writing-011171.zh: 使用图书馆的目录有很多方法可以找到书籍。

college-writing-011172.en: You can search by author, title, keyword(s), or subject.
college-writing-011172.zh: 您可以按作者、标题、关键字或主题进行搜索。

college-writing-011174.en: Author, Title, Keywords, or Subject If you are looking for a specific book or specific author, the easiest search would be an author or title search.
college-writing-011174.zh: 作者、标题、关键字或主题 如果您正在寻找特定的书籍或特定作者，最简单的搜索将是作者或标题搜索。

college-writing-011175.en: For example, suppose you want to see if the library has the book A Tribe Apart, by Patricia Hersch.
college-writing-011175.zh: 例如，假设您想查看图书馆是否有 Patricia Hersch 的书 A Tribe Apartment。

college-writing-011176.en: You could check for the book through:
college-writing-011176.zh: 您可以通过以下方式检查书籍：

college-writing-011177.en: 1. An author search, in which you would look under Hersch, Patricia.
college-writing-011177.zh: 1. 作者搜索，您可以在 Hersch, Patricia 下查看。

college-writing-011178.en: 2. A title search, in which you would look under Tribe Apart, A.
college-writing-011178.zh: 2. 标题搜索，您将在其中查看 Tribe 下的分开，a。

college-writing-011179.en: However, if you are looking for books on specific topics, a keyword or subject search is your better choice.
college-writing-011179.zh: 但是，如果您正在寻找有关特定主题的书籍，关键字或主题搜索是您更好的选择。

college-writing-011180.en: For example, if you are looking for a book about adolescent culture, you could check for a book through:
college-writing-011180.zh: 例如，如果您正在寻找一本关于青少年文化的书，您可以通过以下方式查看一本书：

college-writing-011182.en: In this case, since the subject of the book is adolescents, you could look under words like adolescent culture, codes, and values.
college-writing-011182.zh: 在这种情况下，由于这本书的主题是青少年，您可以查看青少年文化、代码和价值观等词。

college-writing-011183.en: Keyword searches are the most common way to begin research because the system will look for that term anywhere in the record.
college-writing-011183.zh: 关键字搜索是开始研究的最常见方式，因为系统会在记录中的任何地方寻找该术语。

college-writing-011184.en: Just as is true of the use of search engines, keyword searches are the easiest searches to employ when using online catalogs.
college-writing-011184.zh: 就像使用搜索引擎一样，关键字搜索是使用在线目录时最容易使用的搜索。

college-writing-011186.en: Subject searches use very limited and defined vocabulary.
college-writing-011186.zh: 主题搜索使用非常有限和明确的词汇。

college-writing-011187.en: While a good subject search can yield the best results, unless you know for sure what the subject search terms should be (in this case, “teenagers─United States”), subject searches should be done with the aid of a librarian.
college-writing-011187.zh: 虽然一个好的主题搜索可以产生最好的结果，除非你确定主题搜索词应该是什么（在这种情况下是“青少年——美国”），但主题搜索应该在图书管理员的帮助下进行。

college-writing-011188.en: Following is an example of an online catalog entry for Hersch’s book, A Tribe Apart.
college-writing-011188.zh: 以下是 Hersch 书《A Tribe Apart》的在线目录条目示例。

college-writing-011189.en: Note that in addition to giving you the publisher (Ballantine) and year of publication (1999), the entry also tells you the book’s physical location and its call number─each of which will help you find it in the library.
college-writing-011189.zh: 请注意，除了为您提供出版商（Ballantine）和出版年份（1999 年）外，该条目还告诉您这本书的物理位置及其呼叫号码——每个都将帮助您在图书馆中找到它。

college-writing-011190.en: If you need to request the book from another library, your library will have a specific spot (front desk, reference desk, etc.) where the book will be waiting upon delivery.
college-writing-011190.zh: 如果您需要从另一个图书馆申请这本书，您的图书馆将有一个特定的地点（前台、参考办公桌等），这本书将在交付时等待。

college-writing-011191.en: Summary Points: Using Keywords and Subject Searches
college-writing-011191.zh: 摘要点：使用关键字和主题搜索

college-writing-011192.en: • Searching by keyword allows for considerable flexibility of vocabulary and search parameters.
college-writing-011192.zh: • 按关键字搜索可以使词汇和搜索参数具有相当大的灵活性。

college-writing-011193.en: Keyword searches for books in a library catalog work much the same way as keyword searches in search engines.
college-writing-011193.zh: 图书馆目录中的关键字搜索与搜索引擎中的关键字搜索的工作方式大致相同。

college-writing-011194.en: • Searching by subject requires knowledge of very controlled vocabulary and search parameters.
college-writing-011194.zh: • 按主题搜索需要非常受控的词汇和搜索参数的知识。

college-writing-011195.en: It is best used with the aid of a librarian.
college-writing-011195.zh: 它最好在图书管理员的帮助下使用。

college-writing-011196.zh: 408 第 3 部分研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011197.en: An example of an online catalog entry.

college-writing-011221.en: Use your library’s catalog to answer the following questions.
college-writing-011221.zh: 使用图书馆的目录来回答以下问题。

college-writing-011222.en: 1. What is the title of one book by Anna Quindlen?
college-writing-011222.zh: 1. Anna Quindlen 的一本书的标题是什么？

college-writing-011223.en: 2. What is the title of one book by Gabriel Garcia Marquez?
college-writing-011223.zh: 2. Gabriel Garcia Marquez 的一本书的标题是什么？

college-writing-011224.en: 3. Who is the author of A Tree Grows in Brooklyn?
college-writing-011224.zh: 3. 布鲁克林一棵树的作者是谁？

college-writing-011227.en: 4. Who is the author of Seven Habits of Highly Effective People?
college-writing-011227.zh: 4. 《高效能人士的七个习惯》的作者是谁？

college-writing-011228.en: 5. List two books and their authors dealing with the subject of “adoption.”

college-writing-011267.en: Book Stacks The book stacks are the library shelves where books are arranged according to their call numbers.
college-writing-011267.zh: Book Stacks Book Stacks 是图书馆的书架，其中根据其呼叫编号排列书籍。

college-writing-011268.en: The call number, as distinctive as a Social Security number, always appears on the catalog entry for any book.
college-writing-011268.zh: 与社会安全号码一样独特的呼叫号码始终显示在任何书籍的目录条目中。

college-writing-011269.en: It is also printed on the spine of every book in the library.
college-writing-011269.zh: 它也印在图书馆每本书的脊椎上。

college-writing-011270.en: If your library has open stacks (ones that you are permitted to enter), there is a basic procedure to finding a book.
college-writing-011270.zh: 如果您的图书馆有开放的堆栈（您可以进入的堆栈），则有一个基本的查找书籍的程序。

college-writing-011271.en: Suppose you are looking for A Tribe Apart, which has the call number HQ796.H43 in the Library of Congress system.
college-writing-011271.zh: 假设您正在寻找一个分开的部落，它在国会图书馆系统中的电话号码为 HQ796.H43。

college-writing-011272.en: (Libraries using the Dewey decimal system have call letters made up entirely of numbers rather than letters and numbers. However, you use the same basic method to locate a book.)
college-writing-011272.zh: （使用杜威十进制系统的库的呼叫字母完全由数字而不是字母和数字组成。但是，您使用相同的基本方法来定位一本书。）

college-writing-011273.en: The first place you would look is the section that holds the H’s.
college-writing-011273.zh: 您首先要查看的是持有 H 的部分。

college-writing-011274.en: You would then want to look for the HQ’s, which will be listed alphabetically.
college-writing-011274.zh: 然后，您会想要查找将按字母顺序列出的总部。

college-writing-011275.en: Once you’ve located the section housing the HQ’s, you would then look for HQ796 and finally HQ796.H43.
college-writing-011275.zh: 找到总部所在的部分后，您将寻找 HQ796 和 HQ796.H43。

college-writing-011276.en: If your library has closed stacks (ones you are not permitted to enter), you will have to write down the title, author, and call number and have a reference librarian get the book for you.
college-writing-011276.zh: 如果您的图书馆有封闭的堆栈（您不允许进入的堆栈），您将必须写下标题、作者和电话号码，并让参考图书馆员为您获取这本书。

college-writing-011277.en: Periodicals Periodicals─magazines, journals, and newspapers─are available in both print and electronic form.
college-writing-011277.zh: 期刊 期刊 ——杂志、期刊和报纸——有印刷和电子形式。

college-writing-011278.en: They contain recent or very specialized information about a subject, which may not be available in a book.
college-writing-011278.zh: 它们包含有关某个主题的最近或非常专业的信息，这些信息可能在书中可能不可用。

college-writing-011279.en: Most libraries will have print copies of many of the magazines and journals students enjoy reading like Rolling Stone and People, and more scholarly sources like Economic Policy, Shakespeare Quarterly, and the Journal of the American Medical Association.
college-writing-011279.zh: 大多数图书馆都会有学生喜欢的许多杂志和期刊的印刷副本，如滚石和人物，以及更多的学术资源，如经济政策、莎士比亚季刊和美国医学协会杂志。

college-writing-011280.en: If the source isn’t available in print, check with your librarian to see if the resource is available online through one of the databases your college subscribes to.
college-writing-011280.zh: 如果来源无法提供，请与您的图书管理员联系，以查看该资源是否可通过您的大学订阅的数据库之一在线获得。

college-writing-011281.en: If not, the librarian may be able to secure it through an interlibrary loan or may be able to direct you to a nearby library that has that source either in print or electronic form.
college-writing-011281.zh: 如果没有，图书馆员可能能够通过馆际互借贷款获得它，或者可以将您引导到附近的图书馆，该图书馆以印刷或电子形式提供该来源。

college-writing-011282.en: Using Databases As mentioned earlier in this chapter, most college and public libraries now provide online computer-search services known as online databases or library subscription
college-writing-011282.zh: 使用本章前面提到的数据库，大多数大学和公共图书馆现在提供在线计算机搜索服务，称为在线数据库或图书馆订阅

college-writing-011285.en: Using any of these services, you will be able to type in keywords and quickly search many periodicals for articles on your subject.
college-writing-011285.zh: 使用任何这些服务，您将能够输入关键字并快速搜索许多期刊以获取有关您的主题的文章。

college-writing-011286.en: Some databases, such as General Science Index, are discipline-specific, but others, such as Academic Search Premier, are more general.
college-writing-011286.zh: 一些数据库，例如一般科学索引，是特定于学科的，但其他数据库，如学术搜索 Premier，则更一般。

college-writing-011287.en: The search process can vary depending on the database you are using.
college-writing-011287.zh: 搜索过程可能会因您使用的数据库而异。

college-writing-011288.en: As in searching the library catalog, your best choices are using an author or title search if you know the specific piece you are trying to locate or a keyword search if you are trying to gather information on a topic.
college-writing-011288.zh: 与搜索图书馆目录一样，如果您知道要查找的特定作品或试图收集有关某个主题的信息，则使用作者或标题搜索，或者使用关键字搜索。

college-writing-011289.en: Just as in a regular online search, using Boolean operators can help you narrow your results.
college-writing-011289.zh: 就像在定期在线搜索中一样，使用布尔运算符可以帮助您缩小结果的范围。

college-writing-011290.en: Use a subject search only if you know exactly what vocabulary to use.
college-writing-011290.zh: 仅当您确切知道要使用的词汇量时才使用主题搜索。

college-writing-011292.en: Often articles you find will be shown as “full text.”
college-writing-011292.zh: 您找到的文章通常会显示为“全文”。

college-writing-011293.en: That means that you can print out the entire article from your computer.
college-writing-011293.zh: 这意味着您可以从计算机中打印出整篇文章。

college-writing-011294.en: In other cases, only an abstract (summary) of the article will be available.
college-writing-011294.zh: 在其他情况下，只有文章的摘要（摘要）才可用。

college-writing-011295.en: However, abstracts are valuable too, for they allow you to determine whether the article is relevant to your research and whether you should continue searching for the full text.
college-writing-011295.zh: 但是，摘要也很有价值，因为它们可以让您确定文章是否与您的研究相关，以及您是否应该继续搜索全文。

college-writing-011296.en: Finally, database articles appear in html (hypertext markup language) or pdf (portable document format) format or in both.
college-writing-011296.zh: 最后，数据库文章以 HTML（超文本标记语言）或 PDF（便携式文档格式）格式或两者显示。

college-writing-011297.en: Articles in .html have been reformatted for publication on the Internet.
college-writing-011297.zh: .html 中的文章已重新格式化以在 Internet 上发布。

college-writing-011298.en: Those in .pdf are exact reproductions of a print document.
college-writing-011298.zh: .pdf 中的那些是打印文档的精确复制。

college-writing-011299.en: Note that some databases are among many compiled by the same provider.
college-writing-011299.zh: 请注意，某些数据库是同一提供商编译的许多数据库之一。

college-writing-011300.en: EBSCOhost, Infotrac, and ProQuest are such providers.
college-writing-011300.zh: ebscohost、infotrac 和 proquest 就是这样的提供商。

college-writing-011302.en: Following are a few online databases that have proven useful for new student researchers and are often available through college libraries.
college-writing-011302.zh: 以下是一些已被证明对新学生研究人员有用的在线数据库，并且通常可以通过大学图书馆获得。

college-writing-011303.en: (You should become familiar with your college’s offerings as not all databases are offered at all colleges.)
college-writing-011303.zh: （您应该熟悉您的大学的课程，因为并非所有大学都提供所有数据库。）

college-writing-011304.en: If you are unsure which databases will be most useful for your research, reference librarians are skilled and knowledgeable in exactly this area and can help you locate the best source of information.
college-writing-011304.zh: 如果您不确定哪些数据库对您的研究最有用，参考图书馆员在这方面是熟练和知识渊博的，可以帮助您找到最佳信息来源。

college-writing-011305.en: Academic Search Elite (EBSCO) covers a variety of disciplines and includes full-text articles and abstracts of articles from thousands of journals.
college-writing-011305.zh: Academy Search Elite (EBSCO) 涵盖各种学科，包括来自数千种期刊的全文文章和文章摘要。

college-writing-011306.en: American History Online (Facts on File Reference Suite) contains hundreds of primary source documents.
college-writing-011306.zh: American History Online（文件参考套件的事实）包含数百个主要源文档。

college-writing-011307.en: ERIC (Education Resources Information Center) makes available articles from professional journals, reports, and speeches having to do with education.
college-writing-011307.zh: ERIC（教育资源信息中心）从专业期刊、报告和与教育有关的演讲中提供文章。

college-writing-011308.en: JSTOR (Journal Storage) provides full-text articles found in back issues of journals in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences.
college-writing-011308.zh: JSTOR（Journal Storage）提供在人文、社会科学和自然科学期刊的背景中找到的全文文章。

college-writing-011309.en: Lexis-Nexis Academic Universe has full-text access to over 10,000 journals, covering local and world news, legal cases, and business.
college-writing-011309.zh: Lexis-Nexis Academic Universe 拥有超过 10,000 种期刊的全文访问权限，涵盖本地和世界新闻、法律案例和商业。

college-writing-011312.en: Science Online (Facts on File Reference Suite) contains thousands of diagrams, experiments, videos, biographies, and essays.

college-writing-011358.en: This chapter will explain • how to summarize an article • how to paraphrase an article • how to use a direct quotation
college-writing-011358.zh: 本章将解释 • 如何总结一篇文章 • 如何转述一篇文章 • 如何使用直接引用

college-writing-011359.en: C H A P T E R 18 18

college-writing-011361.en: Find an article in your school or local newspaper.
college-writing-011361.zh: 在您的学校或当地报纸上查找文章。

college-writing-011362.en: Choose one article and write a paragraph-length summary of that article.
college-writing-011362.zh: 选择一篇文章并写下该文章的段落长度摘要。

college-writing-011363.en: Then, using that same article, paraphrase one paragraph.
college-writing-011363.zh: 然后，使用同一篇文章，释义一段。

college-writing-011364.en: GM Visuals/Tetra Images, LLC/Alamy Stock Photo
college-writing-011364.zh: GM视觉/利乐图像，LLC/Alamy 库存照片

college-writing-011365.en: Most writing will require students to use information from outside sources.
college-writing-011365.zh: 大多数写作将要求学生使用来自外部来源的信息。

college-writing-011366.en: In order to properly incorporate information and avoid plagiarism, you will need to first understand the material you are reading, which may require you to do a second or third reading, take careful notes, and choose how to incorporate the information.
college-writing-011366.zh: 为了正确整合信息并避免抄袭，您需要首先了解您正在阅读的材料，这可能需要您进行第二次或第三次阅读，仔细记录并选择如何整合信息。

college-writing-011367.en: As a writer, you will need to decide whether or not to summarize or paraphrase the material or use a direct quotation.
college-writing-011367.zh: 作为作家，您需要决定是否总结或转述材料或使用直接引用。

college-writing-011368.en: The general rule is, if the author says it brilliantly, use the author’s words (quotation); if the author’s ideas are great, but you can rewrite it to better fit your essay, use paraphrase or summary.
college-writing-011368.zh: 一般的规则是，如果作者说得很出色，就使用作者的话（引文）； 如果作者的想法很好，但您可以重写它以更好地适合您的文章，使用释义或摘要。

college-writing-011372.en: If you fail to properly document information that you have incorporated into your essay and is not your own, you will be stealing.
college-writing-011372.zh: 如果您未能正确记录您在论文中包含的信息并且不是您自己的，那么您将被窃取。

college-writing-011373.en: The formal term is plagiarizing─ using someone else’s work as your own.
college-writing-011373.zh: 正式术语是抄袭——将别人的作品当作你自己的作品。

college-writing-011374.en: This is true whether you borrow a single image, idea, sentence, or entire essay.
college-writing-011374.zh: 无论您借用单个图像、想法、句子还是整篇文章，这都是正确的。

college-writing-011375.en: One example of plagiarism is turning in a friend’s paper (or a paper you purchased) as if it were your own.
college-writing-011375.zh: 抄袭的一个例子是把朋友的论文（或你购买的论文）当作你自己的。

college-writing-011376.en: Another example is copying an article found in a magazine, newspaper, journal, or on the Internet and turning it in as your own.
college-writing-011376.zh: 另一个例子是复制在杂志、报纸、期刊或互联网上找到的文章，并将其作为自己的方式交付。

college-writing-011377.en: By copying someone else’s work, you risk being failed or even expelled.
college-writing-011377.zh: 通过复制别人的作品，你有失败甚至被开除的风险。

college-writing-011378.en: Equally, plagiarism deprives you of what can be a most helpful learning and organization experience─researching and writing about a selected topic in detail.
college-writing-011378.zh: 同样，抄袭剥夺了您最有帮助的学习和组织体验——详细研究和撰写选定的主题。

college-writing-011379.en: Plagiarism presents a specific risk for each of the writing activities─ summarizing, paraphrasing, and using direct quotations─treated in this chapter.
college-writing-011379.zh: 抄袭对每项写作活动都存在特定的风险——总结、解释和使用直接引用——在本章中处理。

college-writing-011380.en: For that reason, within each major section, you will find a brief discussion that focuses on that activity and on what writers need to watch for specifically in order to avoid plagiarizing.
college-writing-011380.zh: 出于这个原因，在每个主要部分中，您将找到一个简短的讨论，重点关注该活动以及作家需要特别关注的内容，以避免抄袭。

college-writing-011382.en: At some point in a course, your instructor may ask you to write a summary of a book, an article, a TV show, or the like.
college-writing-011382.zh: 在课程中的某个时刻，您的讲师可能会要求您撰写书籍、文章、电视节目等的摘要。

college-writing-011383.en: In a summary (also referred to as a précis or an abstract), you reduce material in an original work to its main points and key support ing details.
college-writing-011383.zh: 在摘要（也称为概要或摘要）中，您将原创作品中的材料减少到其主要点和关键支持细节。

college-writing-011384.en: A summary may consist of a single word, a phrase, several sentences, or one or more paragraphs.
college-writing-011384.zh: 摘要可以由一个单词、一个短语、几个句子或一个或多个段落组成。

college-writing-011385.en: The length of any summary you prepare will depend on your instructor’s expectations and the length of the original work.
college-writing-011385.zh: 您准备的任何摘要的长度将取决于您的教师的期望和原始作品的长度。

college-writing-011386.en: Most often, you will be asked to write a summary consisting of one paragraph.
college-writing-011386.zh: 大多数情况下，您将被要求写出包含一个段落的摘要。

college-writing-011387.en: Summaries can be written as stand-alone pieces or incorporated into essays as detailed support.
college-writing-011387.zh: 摘要可以写成独立的文章，也可以作为详细的支持并入论文中。

college-writing-011388.en: Writing a summary brings together a number of important reading, study, and writing skills.
college-writing-011388.zh: 撰写总结汇集了许多重要的阅读、学习和写作技能。

college-writing-011389.en: To condense the original assigned material, you must preview, read, evaluate, organize, and perhaps outline it.
college-writing-011389.zh: 要浓缩原始分配的材料，您必须预览、阅读、评估、组织以及概述它。

college-writing-011390.en: Summarizing, then, can be a real aid to understanding; you must “get inside” the material and realize fully what is being said before you can reduce its meaning to a few words.
college-writing-011390.zh: 那么，总结可以真正帮助理解； 您必须“进入”材料并充分了解所说的内容，然后才能将其含义简化为几个词。

college-writing-011391.en: In this chapter, you will learn how to write summaries and para phrases and be given a brief introduction to using direct quotations.
college-writing-011391.zh: 在本章中，您将学习如何编写摘要和副词短语，并简要介绍使用直接引用。

college-writing-011392.en: (Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” will further explain how to incorporate quotations into your own writing.)
college-writing-011392.zh: （第 19 章，“写一篇基于来源的论文”，将进一步解释如何将引文纳入您自己的写作中。）

college-writing-011393.zh: 416 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011394.en: Avoiding Plagiarism in Summary Writing You need to be extra careful to avoid accidental plagiarism when writing a summary.
college-writing-011394.zh: 避免抄袭 总结写作时，您需要格外小心，以避免在撰写摘要时意外抄袭。

college-writing-011395.en: A helpful method is to make sure you fully understand the material first, and then to avoid consulting the original piece while writing your summary.
college-writing-011395.zh: 一种有用的方法是确保您首先完全理解材料，然后在编写摘要时避免查阅原始文章。

college-writing-011396.en: You can then inspect for plagiarism by checking your words and phrases against the original, making sure that the words used are your own and not the author’s.
college-writing-011396.zh: 然后，您可以通过检查您的单词和短语与原文进行检查，确保使用的单词是您自己的，而不是作者的。

college-writing-011397.en: You should also examine your sentence structure to confirm that you are not mimicking the author’s sentence structure and merely inserting a new word here and there.
college-writing-011397.zh: 您还应该检查您的句子结构，以确认您没有模仿作者的句子结构，而只是在这里和那里插入一个新单词。

college-writing-011398.en: Finally, you need to make sure you have credited the original source in your summary either by in-text citation or by crediting the author within the summary.
college-writing-011398.zh: 最后，您需要确保您已通过文本引用或在摘要中将作者归功于摘要中的原始来源。

college-writing-011399.en: How to Summarize an Article To write a summary of an article, follow the steps described below.
college-writing-011399.zh: 如何总结一篇文章 要写一篇文章的摘要，请按照以下步骤操作。

college-writing-011400.en: If the assigned material is a TV show or film, adapt the suggestions accordingly.
college-writing-011400.zh: 如果分配的材料是电视节目或电影，请相应地调整建议。

college-writing-011401.en: 1. Take a few minutes to preview the work.
college-writing-011401.zh: 1. 花几分钟时间预览作品。

college-writing-011402.en: You can preview an article in a magazine by taking a quick look at the following: a.
college-writing-011402.zh: 您可以通过快速查看以下内容在杂志中预览文章：

college-writing-011404.en: A title often summarizes what an article is about.
college-writing-011404.zh: 标题通常总结文章的内容。

college-writing-011406.en: the title for a minute and about how it may condense the meaning of the article.
college-writing-011406.zh: 一分钟的标题以及它如何浓缩文章的含义。

college-writing-011409.en: A subtitle, if given, is a short summary appearing under or
college-writing-011409.zh: 字幕（如果给出）是出现在以下或

college-writing-011411.en: For example, in a Newsweek article titled “Growing Old, Feeling Young,” the following caption appeared: “Not only are Americans living longer, they are staying active longer─and their worst enemy is not nature, but the myths and prejudices about grow ing old.”
college-writing-011411.zh: 例如，在新闻周刊的一篇题为“变老，感觉年轻”的文章中，出现了以下标题：“不仅美国人活得更久，而且他们的活跃时间更长——他们最大的敌人不是自然，而是关于变老的神话和偏见。”

college-writing-011412.en: In short, the subtitle, the caption, or any other words in large print under or next to the title often provide a quick insight into the meaning of an article.
college-writing-011412.zh: 简而言之，标题下方或旁边的大字体中的副标题、标题或任何其他单词通常可以快速了解文章的含义。

college-writing-011415.en: In the first several paragraphs, the

college-writing-011416.en: author may introduce you to the subject and state the purpose of the article.
college-writing-011416.zh: 作者可以向您介绍该主题并说明文章的目的。

college-writing-011417.en: In the last several paragraphs, the writer may present conclu sions or a summary.
college-writing-011417.zh: 在最后几段中，作者可能会提供结论或摘要。

college-writing-011418.en: The previews or summaries can give you a quick overview of what the entire article is about.
college-writing-011418.zh: 预览或摘要可以让您快速了解整篇文章的内容。

college-writing-011421.en: Note any heads or subheads that appear in the article.
college-writing-011421.zh: 注意文章中出现的任何头部或子标题。

college-writing-011422.en: They often provide clues to the article’s main points and give an imme diate sense of what each section is about.
college-writing-011422.zh: 它们经常为文章的主要观点提供线索，并立即了解每个部分的内容。

college-writing-011423.en: Look carefully at any pic tures, charts, or diagrams that accompany the article.
college-writing-011423.zh: 仔细查看文章随附的任何图片、图表或图表。

college-writing-011424.en: Page space in a magazine or journal is limited, and such visual aids are generally used only to illustrate important points in the article.
college-writing-011424.zh: 杂志或期刊中的页面空间是有限的，这种视觉辅助工具通常仅用于说明文章中的要点。

college-writing-011425.en: Note any words or phrases set off in italic type or boldface type; such words have probably been emphasized because they deal with important points in the article.
college-writing-011425.zh: 注意以斜体字或粗体字划定的任何单词或短语； 这些词可能已经被强调，因为它们涉及文章中的要点。

college-writing-011427.en: 2. Read the article for all you can understand the first time through.
college-writing-011427.zh: 2. 阅读所有您第一次可以理解的文章。

college-writing-011428.en: Do not slow down or turn back.

college-writing-011429.en: Check or otherwise mark main points and key supporting details.
college-writing-011429.zh: 检查或以其他方式标记主要点和键 支撑细节。

college-writing-011430.en: Pay special attention to all the items noted in the preview.
college-writing-011430.zh: 特别注意预览中注明的所有项目。

college-writing-011431.en: Also, look for definitions, examples, and enumerations (lists of items), which often indicate key ideas.
college-writing-011431.zh: 此外，查找通常指示关键思想的定义、示例和枚举（项目列表）。

college-writing-011432.en: You can also identify important points by turning any headings into questions and reading to find the answers to the questions.
college-writing-011432.zh: 您还可以通过将任何标题转换为问题并阅读以找到问题的答案来识别要点。

college-writing-011433.en: 3. Go back and reread more carefully the areas you have identified as most important.
college-writing-011433.zh: 3. 回去更仔细地重新阅读您确定为最重要的领域。

college-writing-011434.en: Also, focus on other key points you may have missed in your first reading.
college-writing-011434.zh: 此外，专注于您在第一次阅读时可能错过的其他关键点。

college-writing-011436.en: Concentrate on getting down the main ideas and the key supporting points.
college-writing-011436.zh: 专注于深入了解主要思想和关键支持点。

college-writing-011437.en: 5. Prepare the first draft of your summary, keeping these points in mind: a.
college-writing-011437.zh: 5. 准备摘要的初稿，牢记这些要点：

college-writing-011438.en: In the summary, identify the title and author of the work.
college-writing-011438.zh: 在摘要中，确定作品的标题和作者。

college-writing-011440.en: mary is not part of an essay, with in-text citation and a “Works Cited” page, then you should also include the date of publication and publica tion name.
college-writing-011440.zh: 玛丽不是论文的一部分，带有文本引用和“作品引用”页面，那么您还应该包括出版日期和出版物名称。

college-writing-011441.en: The two examples below show the difference in format.
college-writing-011441.zh: 下面的两个示例显示了格式的差异。

college-writing-011443.en: The first sentence of your summary should also be written as a
college-writing-011443.zh: 你的摘要的第一句话也应该写成

college-writing-011444.en: topic sentence and should contain the main idea or thesis of the original work in your own words.
college-writing-011444.zh: 主题句 并用你自己的话包含原作的主要思想或论点。

college-writing-011446.en: Do not write an overly detailed summary.
college-writing-011446.zh: 不要写一个过于详细的摘要。

college-writing-011448.en: pose of a summary is to reduce the original work to its main points and essential supporting details.
college-writing-011448.zh: 一个总结的姿势是将原作的主要点和必不可少的支撑细节 缩小到它的要点。

college-writing-011450.en: Express the main points and key supporting details in your own
college-writing-011450.zh: 表达自己的主要观点和关键 支撑细节

college-writing-011452.en: Do not imitate the style of the original work.

college-writing-011454.en: Never insert your own ideas or opinions into the summary.
college-writing-011454.zh: 切勿将您自己的想法或意见插入摘要中。

college-writing-011456.en: ful not to use loaded language.
college-writing-011456.zh: ful 不使用加载的语言。

college-writing-011457.en: For instance, saying “the author tries to support her claims with studies” or “the author supports her claims with weak information” implies an opinion of how well argued the original piece is.
college-writing-011457.zh: 例如，说“作者试图用研究来支持她的主张”或“作者用弱信息支持她的主张”意味着对原始文章的论证程度的看法。

college-writing-011458.en: A good summary, instead, would simply state, “the author supports her claims with studies.” f.
college-writing-011458.zh: 相反，一个好的总结会简单地说，“作者通过研究支持她的主张。” F.

college-writing-011459.en: Periodically refer to the author (by last name) or article to empha
college-writing-011459.zh: 定期引用作者（通过姓氏）或文章来强调

college-writing-011460.en: size that this is a summary.

college-writing-011461.en: As well, use signal words (argues, illustrates, asserts, observes, writes, reports) to remind readers that the ideas being presented are directly from the article.
college-writing-011461.zh: 同样，使用信号词（争论、说明、断言、观察、撰写、报告）来提醒读者所提出的想法直接来自文章。

college-writing-011463.en: Quote from the material only to illustrate key points.
college-writing-011463.zh: 仅从材料中引用以说明关键点。

college-writing-011466.en: A one-paragraph summary should not contain more than one quoted sentence or phrase.
college-writing-011466.zh: 一个单段摘要不应包含超过一个引用的句子或短语。

college-writing-011468.en: Preserve the balance and proportion of the original work.
college-writing-011468.zh: 保留原作的平衡和比例。

college-writing-011470.en: original devoted 70 percent of its space to one idea and only 30 per cent to another, your summary should reflect that emphasis.
college-writing-011470.zh: 最初将其 70% 的空间用于一个想法，而仅将 30% 用于另一个想法，您的摘要应该反映出这种重点。

college-writing-011474.zh: 在第 1 部分中解释了写作（统一、支持、连贯性和句子技能）。
