college-writing-011477.en: A Model Summary of an Article

college-writing-011478.en: Here is a model summary of a magazine article that would stand on its own:
college-writing-011478.zh: 这是一篇杂志文章的模型摘要，它可以独立存在：

college-writing-011479.en: Here is a model summary of a magazine article that is used in an essay containing a “Works Cited” page.
college-writing-011479.zh: 这是一篇包含“作品引用”页面的文章中使用的杂志文章的模型摘要。

college-writing-011480.en: Note that the publication information is not needed within the text, but it is available in the “Works Cited” entry.
college-writing-011480.zh: 请注意，文本中不需要出版信息，但在“作品引用”条目中提供。

college-writing-011481.en: If this is the first time you are citing the article, you need to reference the article’s title.
college-writing-011481.zh: 如果这是您第一次引用该文章，则需要引用该文章的标题。

college-writing-011482.en: However, if this is the second or subsequent time citing this article, you would refer only to the author’s last name, as in “Taubes continues to remark . . . ”
college-writing-011482.zh: 但是，如果这是第二次或后续引用这篇文章，您将仅引用作者的姓氏，如“Taubes 继续评论……”

college-writing-011483.en: In his article, “Why the Campaign to Stop America’s Obesity Crisis Keeps Failing,” Gary Taubes reports on the obesity epidemic and his beliefs that refined sugars are the cause of obesity.
college-writing-011483.zh: Gary Taubes 在他的文章“为何阻止美国肥胖危机的运动不断失败”的文章中报道了肥胖流行以及他认为精制糖是导致肥胖的原因。

college-writing-011484.en: He begins his article by citing information from the 1930s that demonstrates children had obesity problems even during the Depression.
college-writing-011484.zh: 他在文章开始时引用了 1930 年代的信息，这些信息表明即使在抑郁症期间儿童也有肥胖问题。

college-writing-011485.en: Taubes then points out that despite government recommendations, Americans’ dietary changes have not resulted in less obesity.
college-writing-011485.zh: 陶贝斯随后指出，尽管政府提出了建议，但美国人的饮食变化并没有导致肥胖减少。

college-writing-011486.en: He supports his claims about refined sugars and carbohydrates by detailing the science of fat cells, insulin, and the liver.
college-writing-011486.zh: 他通过详细说明脂肪细胞、胰岛素和肝脏的科学来支持他对精制糖和碳水化合物的说法。

college-writing-011487.en: He concludes with the assertion that the authorities like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health may need to rethink what they are telling Americans (32–36).
college-writing-011487.zh: 他最后断言，如疾病控制和预防中心和美国国立卫生研究院等当局可能需要重新思考他们告诉美国人的内容（32-36）。

college-writing-011488.en: In the article, “Why the Campaign to Stop America’s Obesity Crisis Keeps Failing,” originally printed in the May 2012 Newsweek, Gary Taubes reports on the obesity epidemic and his beliefs that refined sugars are the cause of obesity.
college-writing-011488.zh: Gary Taubes 报道了最初发表于 2012 年 5 月新闻周刊的“为什么阻止美国肥胖危机的运动不断失败”的文章中报道了肥胖流行病以及他认为精制糖是导致肥胖的原因的文章。

college-writing-011489.en: He begins his article by citing information from the 1930s that demonstrates children had obesity problems even during the Depression.
college-writing-011489.zh: 他在文章开始时引用了 1930 年代的信息，这些信息表明即使在抑郁症期间儿童也有肥胖问题。

college-writing-011490.en: Taubes then points out that despite government recommendations, Americans’ dietary changes have not resulted in less obesity.
college-writing-011490.zh: 陶贝斯随后指出，尽管政府提出了建议，但美国人的饮食变化并没有导致肥胖减少。

college-writing-011491.en: He supports his claims about refined sugars and carbohydrates by detailing the science of fat cells, insulin, and the liver.
college-writing-011491.zh: 他通过详细说明脂肪细胞、胰岛素和肝脏的科学来支持他对精制糖和碳水化合物的说法。

college-writing-011492.en: He concludes with the assertion that the authorities like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health may need to rethink what they are telling Americans (32–36).
college-writing-011492.zh: 他最后断言，如疾病控制和预防中心和美国国立卫生研究院等当局可能需要重新思考他们告诉美国人的内容（32-36）。

college-writing-011494.en: Write a summary of the following article, “Power Learning,” by Jerry Blythe.
college-writing-011494.zh: 写下 Jerry Blythe 的以下文章“Power Learning”的摘要。

college-writing-011495.en: Your topic sentence should introduce the name of the article, the main purpose/thesis of the article, and the publication information.
college-writing-011495.zh: 您的 主题句 应介绍文章的名称、文章的主要目的/论文以及出版信息。

college-writing-011496.en: The rest of your summary should include only factual information that expresses the main points of the article.
college-writing-011496.zh: 您摘要的其余部分应仅包含表达文章主要观点的事实信息。

college-writing-011497.en: Your concluding sentence should express the closing idea presented in the article.
college-writing-011497.zh: 你的结束语应该表达文章中提出的结束想法。

college-writing-011501.en: “Why the Campaign to Stop America’s Obesity Crisis
college-writing-011501.zh: “为什么要阻止美国的肥胖危机

college-writing-011505.en: Jill had not done as well in high school as she had hoped.
college-writing-011505.zh: 吉尔在高中的表现没有她希望的那么好。

college-writing-011506.en: Since college involved even more work, it was no surprise that she didn’t do better there.
college-writing-011506.zh: 由于大学涉及更多的工作，因此她没有在那里做得更好也就不足为奇了。

college-writing-011507.en: The reason for her so-so performance was not a lack of effort.
college-writing-011507.zh: 她马马虎虎的表现的原因不是缺乏努力。

college-writing-011508.en: She attended most of her classes and read her textbooks.
college-writing-011508.zh: 她参加了大部分课程并阅读了她的教科书。

college-writing-011509.en: And she never missed handing in any assignment, even though it often meant staying up late the night before homework was due.
college-writing-011509.zh: 而且她从来没有错过交任何任务，尽管这通常意味着在家庭作业到期前的深夜熬夜。

college-writing-011510.en: Still, she just got by in her classes.
college-writing-011510.zh: 尽管如此，她只是在她的课堂上过得去。

college-writing-011511.en: Before long, she came to the conclusion that she simply couldn’t do any better.
college-writing-011511.zh: 不久，她得出的结论是，她根本无法做得更好。

college-writing-011512.en: Then one day, one of her instructors said something to make her think otherwise.
college-writing-011512.zh: 然后有一天，她的一位导师说了一些让她不这么认为的话。

college-writing-011513.en: “You can probably build some sort of house by banging a few boards together,” he said.
college-writing-011513.zh: “你可能可以通过敲打几块木板来建造某种房子，”他说。

college-writing-011514.en: “But if you want a sturdy home, you’ll have to use the right techniques and tools. Building carefully takes work, but it gets better results. The same can be said of your education. There are no shortcuts, but there are some proven study skills that can really help. If you don’t use them, you may end up with a pretty flimsy education.”
college-writing-011514.zh: “但如果你想要一个坚固的家，你就必须使用正确的技术和工具。精心构建需要工作，但它会得到更好的结果。你的教育也可以这么说。没有捷径，但有一些经过验证的学习技能真的可以帮助你。如果你不使用它们，你 可能最终会得到相当脆弱的教育。”

college-writing-011515.en: Jill signed up for a study-skills course and found out a crucial fact— that learning how to learn is the key to success in school.
college-writing-011515.zh: 吉尔报名参加了学习技能课程，发现了一个关键事实——学习如何学习是学校成功的关键。

college-writing-011516.en: Certain dependable skills have made the difference between disappointment and success for generations of students.
college-writing-011516.zh: 某些可靠的技能为几代学生带来了失望和成功的区别。

college-writing-011517.en: These techniques won’t free you from work, but they will make your work far more productive.
college-writing-011517.zh: 这些技术不会让你从工作中解脱出来，但它们会让你的工作更有成效。

college-writing-011518.en: They include three important areas: time control, classroom note-taking, and textbook study.
college-writing-011518.zh: 它们包括三个重要领域：时间控制、课堂笔记和教科书学习。

college-writing-011520.en: Success in college depends on time control.
college-writing-011520.zh: 大学的成功取决于时间控制。

college-writing-011521.en: Time control means that you deliberately organize and plan your time, instead of letting it
college-writing-011521.zh: 时间控制意味着你故意组织和计划你的时间，而不是让它

college-writing-011523.zh: 420 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011525.en: Planning means that you should never be faced with an overdue term paper or a cram session the night before a test.
college-writing-011525.zh: 计划意味着您永远不应该在考试前一天晚上面对逾期的学期论文或补习班。

college-writing-011526.en: Three steps are involved in time control.
college-writing-011526.zh: 时间控制涉及三个步骤。

college-writing-011527.en: First, you should prepare a large monthly calendar.
college-writing-011527.zh: 首先，您应该准备一个大的月历。

college-writing-011528.en: Buy a calendar with a large white block around each date, or make one yourself.
college-writing-011528.zh: 在每个日期周围购买一个带有大白块的日历，或者自己制作一个。

college-writing-011529.en: At the beginning of the college semester, circle important dates on this calendar.
college-writing-011529.zh: 在大学学期开始时，在这个日历上圈出重要的日期。

college-writing-011530.en: Circle the days on which tests are scheduled; circle the days when papers are due.
college-writing-011530.zh: 圈出安排测试的日期； 圈出文件到期的日子。

college-writing-011531.en: This calendar can also be used to schedule study plans.
college-writing-011531.zh: 此日历也可用于安排学习计划。

college-writing-011532.en: At the beginning of the week, you can jot down your plans for each day.
college-writing-011532.zh: 在一周的开始，您可以记下您每天的计划。

college-writing-011533.en: An alternative method would be to make plans for each day the night before.
college-writing-011533.zh: 另一种方法是为前一天晚上的每一天制定计划。

college-writing-011534.en: On Tuesday night, for example, you might write down “Read Chapter 5 in psychology” in the Wednesday block.
college-writing-011534.zh: 例如，在周二晚上，您可能会在星期三的街区写下“阅读心理学中的第 5 章”。

college-writing-011535.en: Hang this calendar where you will see it every day—your kitchen, bedroom, even your bathroom!
college-writing-011535.zh: 把这个日历挂在你每天都能看到的地方——你的厨房、卧室，甚至你的浴室！

college-writing-011536.en: The second step in time control is to have a weekly study schedule for the semester—a chart that covers all the days of the week and all the waking hours in each day.
college-writing-011536.zh: 时间控制的第二步是有一个学期的每周学习时间表——一个图表，涵盖一周中的所有日子和每天醒着的所有时间。

college-writing-011537.en: Below is part of one student’s schedule:
college-writing-011537.zh: 以下是一名学生日程安排的一部分：

college-writing-011545.zh: 7:00 早餐 早餐 早餐 早餐

college-writing-011546.en: 8:00 Math STUDY Math STUDY Math Breakfast
college-writing-011546.zh: 8:00 数学学习 数学学习 数学早餐

college-writing-011547.en: 9:00 STUDY Biology STUDY Biology STUDY Job
college-writing-011547.zh: 9:00 研究生物学研究生物学研究工作

college-writing-011551.en: On your own schedule, fill in all the fixed hours in each day—hours for meals, classes, job (if any), and travel time.
college-writing-011551.zh: 根据您自己的时间表，填写每天的所有固定时间——膳食、课程、工作（如果有的话）和旅行时间。

college-writing-011552.en: Next, mark time blocks that you can realistically use for study each day.
college-writing-011552.zh: 接下来，标记您可以实际用于每天学习的时间块。

college-writing-011553.en: Depending on the number of courses you are taking and the demands of these courses, you may want to block off five, ten, or even twenty or more hours of study time a week.
college-writing-011553.zh: 根据您正在学习的课程数量和这些课程的要求，您可能希望每周停止 5、10 甚至 20 小时或更多小时的学习时间。

college-writing-011554.en: Keep in mind that you should not block off time that you do not truly intend to use for study.
college-writing-011554.zh: 请记住，您不应该阻止您不打算真正用于学习的时间。

college-writing-011555.en: Otherwise, your schedule will be a meaningless gimmick.
college-writing-011555.zh: 否则，您的日程安排将是一个毫无意义的噱头。

college-writing-011556.en: Also, remember that you should allow time for rest and relaxation.
college-writing-011556.zh: 另外，请记住，您应该留出时间休息和放松。

college-writing-011557.en: You will be happiest, and able to accomplish the most, when you have time for both work and play.
college-writing-011557.zh: 当您有时间工作和娱乐时，您将最快乐，并且能够完成最多的工作。

college-writing-011558.en: The third step in time control is to make a daily or weekly to-do list.
college-writing-011558.zh: 时间控制的第三步是制作每日或每周的待办事项清单。

college-writing-011559.en: This may be the most valuable time-control method you ever use.
college-writing-011559.zh: 这可能是您使用过的最有价值的时间控制方法。

college-writing-011560.en: On this list, write down the things you need to do for the following day or the following week.
college-writing-011560.zh: 在此列表中，写下您第二天或下周需要做的事情。

college-writing-011561.en: If you choose to write a weekly list, do it on Sunday
college-writing-011561.zh: 如果您选择写每周列表，请在周日进行

college-writing-011565.en: If you choose to write a daily list, do it the night before.
college-writing-011565.zh: 如果您选择编写每日列表，请在前一天晚上进行。

college-writing-011566.en: Here is part of one student’s daily list:
college-writing-011566.zh: 这是一名学生的每日列表的一部分：

college-writing-011569.zh: 2. 校对今天到期的英语付款人

college-writing-011570.en: 3. See Nikola about game on Friday
college-writing-011570.zh: 3. 周五见尼古拉关于比赛

college-writing-011572.en: 5. Read next chapter of psychology text
college-writing-011572.zh: 5. 阅读心理学文本的下一章

college-writing-011573.en: You may use a three-by-five-inch notepad or a small spiral-bound notebook for this list.
college-writing-011573.zh: 您可以为此列表使用 3 x 5 英寸的记事本或小螺旋装订笔记本。

college-writing-011574.en: Carry the list around with you during the day.

college-writing-011575.en: Always concentrate on doing the most important items first.
college-writing-011575.zh: 始终专注于做最重要的项目。

college-writing-011576.en: To make the best use of your time, mark high-priority items with an asterisk and give them precedence over low-priority items.
college-writing-011576.zh: 为了充分利用您的时间，用星号标记高优先级项目，并优先于低优先级项目。

college-writing-011577.en: For instance, you may find yourself wondering what to do after dinner on Thursday evening.
college-writing-011577.zh: 例如，您可能会发现自己想知道周四晚上晚餐后要做什么。

college-writing-011578.en: Among the items on your list are “Clean inside of car” and “Review chapter for math quiz.”
college-writing-011578.zh: 您列表中的项目包括“Clean Inside of Car”和“数学测验回顾章节”。

college-writing-011579.en: It is obviously more important for you to review your notes at this point; you can clean out the car some other time.
college-writing-011579.zh: 在这一点上复习你的笔记显然更重要； 你可以在其他时间清理汽车。

college-writing-011580.en: As you complete items on your to-do list, cross them out.
college-writing-011580.zh: 当您完成待办事项列表中的项目时，将它们划掉。

college-writing-011581.en: Do not worry about unfinished items.
college-writing-011581.zh: 不要担心未完成的物品。

college-writing-011583.en: You will still be accomplishing a great deal and making more effective use of your time.
college-writing-011583.zh: 您仍将完成大量工作并更有效地利用您的时间。

college-writing-011585.en: One of the most important single things you can do to perform well in a college course is to take effective class notes.
college-writing-011585.zh: 在大学课程中表现良好的最重要的单一事情之一就是做有效的课堂笔记。

college-writing-011586.en: The following hints should help you become a better note-taker.
college-writing-011586.zh: 以下提示应该可以帮助您成为更好的笔记本。

college-writing-011588.en: Your alternatives—reading the text, reading someone else’s notes, or both—cannot substitute for the class experience of hearing ideas in person as someone presents them to you.
college-writing-011588.zh: 您的替代方案——阅读文本、阅读其他人的笔记或两者兼而有之——无法代替在某人向您展示想法时亲自聆听想法的课堂体验。

college-writing-011589.en: Also, in class lectures and discussions, your instructor typically presents and develops the main ideas and facts of the course—the ones you will be expected to know on exams.
college-writing-011589.zh: 此外，在课堂讲座和讨论中，您的教师通常会展示和发展课程的主要思想和事实——您将在考试中了解到的。

college-writing-011590.en: Another valuable hint is to make use of abbreviations while taking notes.
college-writing-011590.zh: 另一个有价值的提示是在做笔记时使用缩写。

college-writing-011591.en: Using abbreviations saves time when you are trying to get down a great deal of information.
college-writing-011591.zh: 当您尝试获取大量信息时，使用缩写可以节省时间。

college-writing-011592.en: Abbreviate terms that recur frequently in a lecture and put a key to your abbreviations at the top of your notes.
college-writing-011592.zh: 缩写在讲座中经常出现的术语，并在笔记顶部放置缩写的关键。

college-writing-011593.en: For example, in sociology class, eth could stand for ethnocentrism; in a psychology class, STM could stand for short-term memory.
college-writing-011593.zh: 例如，在社会学课上，ETH 可以代表民族中心主义； 在心理学课程中，STM 可以代表短期记忆。

college-writing-011594.en: (When a lecture is over, you may want to go back and write out the terms you have abbreviated.)
college-writing-011594.zh: （当讲座结束时，您可能想回去写下您缩写的术语。）

college-writing-011595.en: Also, use e for example; def for definition; info for
college-writing-011595.zh: 另外，使用 E 为例； 定义的定义； 信息

college-writing-011597.zh: 422 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011598.en: information; + for and; and so on.

college-writing-011599.en: If you use the same abbreviations all the time, you will soon develop a kind of personal shorthand that makes taking notes much easier.
college-writing-011599.zh: 如果你一直使用相同的缩写，你很快就会发展出一种个人速记，让记笔记变得更加容易。

college-writing-011600.en: A third hint for taking notes is to be on the lookout for signals of importance.
college-writing-011600.zh: 做笔记的第三个提示是寻找重要的信号。

college-writing-011601.en: Write down whatever your instructor puts on the board.
college-writing-011601.zh: 写下你的教练放在黑板上的任何内容。

college-writing-011602.en: If he or she takes the time to put material on the board, it is probably important, and the chances are good that it will come up later on exams.
college-writing-011602.zh: 如果他或她花时间将材料放在板上，这可能很重要，并且很有可能它会在以后的考试中出现。

college-writing-011603.en: Always write down definitions and enumerations.

college-writing-011605.en: They are signaled in such ways as “The four steps in the process are . . .”; “There were three reasons for . . .”; “The two effects were . . .”; “Five characteristics of . . .”; and so on.
college-writing-011605.zh: 它们以“过程中的四个步骤是……”等方式发出信号。 “……有三个原因……”； “这两种影响是……”； “……的五个特征”； 等等。

college-writing-011606.en: In your notes, always number such enumerations (1, 2, 3, etc.).
college-writing-011606.zh: 在您的笔记中，请始终对此类枚举进行编号（1、2、3 等）。

college-writing-011607.en: They will help you understand relationships among ideas and organize the material of the lecture.
college-writing-011607.zh: 他们将帮助您了解想法之间的关系并组织讲座的材料。

college-writing-011608.en: Watch for emphasis words—words your instructor may use to indicate that something is important.
college-writing-011608.zh: 注意重点词——你的导师可能用来表示某事很重要的词。

college-writing-011609.en: Examples of such words are “This is an important reason . . .”; “A point that will keep coming up later . . .”; “The chief cause was . . .”; “The basic idea here is . . .”; and so on.
college-writing-011609.zh: 这些词的例子是“这是一个重要的原因……”； “以后会继续出现的一点……”； “主要原因是……”； “这里的基本思想是……”； 等等。

college-writing-011610.en: Always write down the important statements announced by these and other emphasis words.
college-writing-011610.zh: 总是写下这些和其他重点词宣布的重要陈述。

college-writing-011611.en: Finally, if your instructor repeats a point, you can assume that it is important.
college-writing-011611.zh: 最后，如果你的教练重复一个点，你可以假设它很重要。

college-writing-011612.en: You might put an R for repeated in the margin so that later you will know that your instructor stressed it.
college-writing-011612.zh: 您可以在页边空白处放置一个 R 进行重复，以便稍后您会知道您的教师会强调它。

college-writing-011613.en: Next, be sure to write down the instructor’s examples and mark them with an e.
college-writing-011613.zh: 接下来，请务必写下教师的示例并用 e 标记它们。

college-writing-011614.en: The examples help you understand abstract points.
college-writing-011614.zh: 这些示例可帮助您理解抽象点。

college-writing-011615.en: If you do not write them down, you are likely to forget them later, when they are needed to help make sense of an idea.
college-writing-011615.zh: 如果你不把它们写下来，你可能会在以后需要它们来帮助理解一个想法时忘记它们。

college-writing-011616.en: Also, be sure to write down the connections between ideas.
college-writing-011616.zh: 此外，请务必写下想法之间的联系。

college-writing-011617.en: Too many students merely copy terms the instructor puts on the board.
college-writing-011617.zh: 太多的学生只是复制教师放在板上的术语。

college-writing-011618.en: They forget that, as time passes, the details that serve as connecting bridges between ideas quickly fade.
college-writing-011618.zh: 他们忘记了，随着时间的推移，作为思想之间连接桥梁的细节很快就会消失。

college-writing-011619.en: You should, then, write down the relationships and connections in class.
college-writing-011619.zh: 然后，你应该在课堂上写下关系和联系。

college-writing-011620.en: That way you’ll have them to help tie together your notes later on.
college-writing-011620.zh: 这样，您将让它们稍后帮助将您的笔记联系在一起。

college-writing-011621.en: Review your notes as soon as possible after class.
college-writing-011621.zh: 上课后尽快查看您的笔记。

college-writing-011622.en: You must make them as clear as possible while they are fresh in your mind.
college-writing-011622.zh: 当它们在您的脑海中新鲜时，您必须使它们尽可能清晰。

college-writing-011623.en: A day later may be too late, because forgetting sets in very quickly.
college-writing-011623.zh: 一天后可能为时已晚，因为忘记很快就会出现。

college-writing-011624.en: Make sure that punctuation is clear, that all words are readable and correctly spelled, and that unfinished sentences are completed (or at least marked off so that you can check your notes with another student’s).
college-writing-011624.zh: 确保标点符号清晰，所有单词都是可读和拼写正确的，并且未完成的句子已完成（或至少标记为标记，以便您可以与其他学生的笔记一起检查）。

college-writing-011625.en: Add clarifying or connecting comments wherever necessary.
college-writing-011625.zh: 必要时添加澄清或连接评论。

college-writing-011626.en: Make sure that important ideas are clearly marked.
college-writing-011626.zh: 确保重要的想法被清楚地标记。

college-writing-011627.en: Improve the organization if necessary so that you can see at a glance main points and relationships among them.
college-writing-011627.zh: 必要时改进组织，以便您一目了然地看到它们之间的主要观点和关系。

college-writing-011628.en: Finally, try in general to get down a written record of each class.
college-writing-011628.zh: 最后，尝试一般地记录每个班级的书面记录。

college-writing-011629.en: You must do this because forgetting begins almost immediately.
college-writing-011629.zh: 您必须这样做，因为遗忘几乎立即开始。

college-writing-011630.en: Studies have shown that within two weeks you are likely to have forgotten 80 percent or more of what you have heard.
college-writing-011630.zh: 研究表明，在两周内，您可能已经忘记了 80% 或更多您所听到的内容。

college-writing-011631.en: And in four weeks you are lucky if 5 percent
college-writing-011631.zh: 如果 5%，你很幸运在四个星期内

college-writing-011635.en: This is so crucial that it bears repeating: To guard against the relentlessness of forgetting, it is absolutely essential that you write down what you hear in class.
college-writing-011635.zh: 这非常重要，以至于它需要重复：为了防止遗忘的无情，你写下你在课堂上听到的东西是绝对必要的。

college-writing-011636.en: Later you can concentrate on working to understand fully and to remember the ideas that have been presented in class.
college-writing-011636.zh: 稍后您可以专注于工作以充分理解并记住课堂上提出的想法。

college-writing-011637.en: And then, the more complete your notes are, the more you are likely to learn.
college-writing-011637.zh: 然后，你的笔记越完整，你就越有可能学到的东西。

college-writing-011639.en: In many college courses, success means being able to read and study a textbook skillfully.
college-writing-011639.zh: 在许多大学课程中，成功意味着能够熟练地阅读和学习教科书。

college-writing-011640.en: For many students, unfortunately, textbooks are heavy going.
college-writing-011640.zh: 不幸的是，对于许多学生来说，教科书是沉重的。

college-writing-011641.en: After an hour or two of study, the textbook material is as formless and as hard to understand as ever.
college-writing-011641.zh: 经过一两个小时的学习，教科书材料一如既往地无形且难以理解。

college-writing-011642.en: But there is a way to attack even the most difficult textbook and make sense of it.
college-writing-011642.zh: 但是有一种方法可以攻击最困难的教科书并理解它。

college-writing-011643.en: Use a sequence in which you preview a chapter, mark it, take notes on it, and then study the notes.
college-writing-011643.zh: 使用预览章节、标记它、在上面做笔记然后研究笔记的序列。

college-writing-011645.en: Previewing a selection is an important first step to understanding.
college-writing-011645.zh: 预览选择是理解的重要第一步。

college-writing-011646.en: Taking the time to preview a section or chapter can give you a bird’seye view of the way the material is organized.
college-writing-011646.zh: 花时间预览一个部分或章节可以让您鸟瞰材料的组织方式。

college-writing-011647.en: You will have a sense of where you are beginning, what you will cover, and where you will end.
college-writing-011647.zh: 你会知道你从哪里开始，你将涵盖什么，你将在哪里结束。

college-writing-011648.en: There are several steps in previewing a selection.

college-writing-011650.en: The title is the shortest possible summary of a selection and will often tell you the limits of the material you will cover.
college-writing-011650.zh: 标题是选区的最短总结，通常会告诉您您将涵盖的材料的限制。

college-writing-011651.en: For example, the title “FDR and the Supreme Court” tells you to expect a discussion of President Roosevelt’s dealings with the Court.
college-writing-011651.zh: 例如，“罗斯福和最高法院”的标题告诉您，期待对罗斯福总统与法院的交易进行讨论。

college-writing-011652.en: You know that you will probably not encounter any material dealing with FDR’s foreign policies or personal life.
college-writing-011652.zh: 您知道您可能不会遇到任何与罗斯福的外交政策或个人生活有关的材料。

college-writing-011653.en: Next, quickly read over the first and last paragraphs of the selection; these may contain important introductions to, and summaries of, the main ideas.
college-writing-011653.zh: 接下来，快速阅读选择的第一段和最后一段； 这些可能包含对主要思想的重要介绍和总结。

college-writing-011654.en: Then briefly examine the headings and subheadings in the selection.
college-writing-011654.zh: 然后简要检查选择中的标题和副标题。

college-writing-011655.en: Together, the headings and subheadings are a mini-outline of what you are reading.
college-writing-011655.zh: 标题和副标题一起是您正在阅读的内容的迷你大纲。

college-writing-011656.en: Headings are often main ideas or important concepts in capsule form; subheadings are breakdowns of ideas within main areas.
college-writing-011656.zh: 标题通常是胶囊形式的主要思想或重要概念； 副标题是主要领域内的想法细分。

college-writing-011657.en: Finally, read the first sentence of some paragraphs, look for words set off in boldface or italics, and look at pictures or diagrams.
college-writing-011657.zh: 最后，阅读一些段落的第一句话，寻找用粗体字或斜体表示的单词，并查看图片或图表。

college-writing-011658.en: After you have previewed a selection in this way, you should have a good general sense of the material to be read.
college-writing-011658.zh: 以这种方式预览选区后，您应该对要阅读的材料有一个很好的一般意义。

college-writing-011660.en: You should mark a textbook selection at the same time that you read it through carefully.
college-writing-011660.zh: 您应该在仔细阅读的同时标记教科书选择。

college-writing-011661.en: Use a felt-tip highlighter to shade material that seems important, or use a ballpoint pen and put symbols in the margin next to the material: stars, checks, or NB (nota bene, Latin for “note
college-writing-011661.zh: 使用毡尖荧光笔对看起来重要的材料进行遮蔽，或使用圆珠笔并在材料旁边的边距中放置符号：星星、支票或 NB（Nota Bene，拉丁文表示“注释”

college-writing-011663.zh: 424 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011665.en: What to mark is not as mysterious as some students believe.
college-writing-011665.zh: 标记什么并不像一些学生认为的那么神秘。

college-writing-011666.en: You should try to find main ideas by looking for clues: definitions and examples, enumerations, and emphasis words.
college-writing-011666.zh: 您应该尝试通过寻找线索来找到主要想法：定义和示例、枚举和强调词。

college-writing-011667.en: 1. Definitions and examples: Definitions are often among the most important ideas in a selection.
college-writing-011667.zh: 1. 定义和示例：定义通常是选择中最重要的想法之一。

college-writing-011668.en: They are particularly significant in introductory courses in almost any subject area, where much of your learning involves mastering the specialized vocabulary of that subject.
college-writing-011668.zh: 它们在几乎任何学科领域的入门课程中都特别重要，您的大部分学习都涉及掌握该学科的专业词汇。

college-writing-011669.en: In a sense, you are learning the “language” of psychology or business or whatever the subject might be.
college-writing-011669.zh: 从某种意义上说，您正在学习心理学或商业或任何主题的“语言”。

college-writing-011670.en: Most definitions are abstract, and so they usually are followed by one or more examples to help clarify their meaning.
college-writing-011670.zh: 大多数定义是抽象的，因此通常后面是一个或多个示例，以帮助阐明其含义。

college-writing-011671.en: Always mark off definitions and at least one example that makes a definition clear to you.
college-writing-011671.zh: 始终标记定义和至少一个让您清楚定义的示例。

college-writing-011672.en: In a psychology text, for example, we are told that “rationalization is an attempt to reduce anxiety by deciding that you have not really been frustrated.”
college-writing-011672.zh: 例如，在心理学文本中，我们被告知“理性化是一种通过确定你没有真正感到沮丧来减少焦虑的尝试。”

college-writing-011673.en: Several examples follow, among them: “A student, frustrated at doing poorly on an exam, convinces themself they weren’t given enough time to study.”
college-writing-011673.zh: 下面列出几个例子，其中一个是：“一名学生因为考试没考好而沮丧，于是说服自己，相信是别人没有给自己足够的复习时间。”

college-writing-011674.en: 2. Enumerations: Enumerations are lists of items (causes, reasons, types, and so on) that are numbered 1, 2, 3, . . . or that could easily be numbered.
college-writing-011674.zh: 2. 枚举：枚举是编号为 1、2、3、 的项目列表（原因、原因、类型等）。 。 。 或者可以很容易地编号。

college-writing-011675.en: They are often signaled by addition words.
college-writing-011675.zh: 它们通常由附加词表示。

college-writing-011676.en: Many of the paragraphs in this book, for instance, use words like First of all, Another, In addition, and Finally to signal items in a series.
college-writing-011676.zh: 例如，本书中的许多段落都使用第一个词，另一个，另外，最后用一个系列来表示项目。

college-writing-011677.en: Other textbooks also use this very common and effective organizational method.
college-writing-011677.zh: 其他教科书也使用这种非常常见和有效的组织方法。

college-writing-011678.en: 3. Emphasis words: Emphasis words tell you that an idea is important.
college-writing-011678.zh: 3. 强调词：强调词告诉你一个想法很重要。

college-writing-011679.en: Common emphasis words include phrases such as a major event, a key feature, the chief factor, important to note, above all, and most of all.
college-writing-011679.zh: 共同强调的词包括诸如重大事件、关键特征、主要因素、需要注意的重要因素等短语，最重要的是。

college-writing-011680.en: Here is an example: “The most significant contemporary use of marketing is its application to nonbusiness areas, such as political parties.”
college-writing-011680.zh: 举个例子：“当代最重要的营销用途是它在非商业领域的应用，例如政党。”

college-writing-011683.en: Go through the chapter a second time, rereading the most important parts.
college-writing-011683.zh: 第二次阅读本章，重读最重要的部分。

college-writing-011684.en: Try to write down the main ideas in a simple outline form.
college-writing-011684.zh: 尝试以简单的大纲形式写下主要思想。

college-writing-011685.en: For example, in taking notes on a psychology selection, you might write down the heading “Defense Mechanisms.”
college-writing-011685.zh: 例如，在对心理学选择进行笔记时，您可能会写下“防御机制”的标题。

college-writing-011686.en: Below the heading you would define them, number and describe each kind, and give an example of each.
college-writing-011686.zh: 在标题下方，您将定义它们，编号和描述每种类型，并给出每个类型的示例。

college-writing-011689.en: Definition: unconscious attempts to reduce anxiety
college-writing-011689.zh: 定义：无意识地尝试减少焦虑

college-writing-011694.en: (1) Rationalization: An attempt to reduce anxiety by deciding that you have not
college-writing-011694.zh: (1) 合理化：试图通过决定你没有

college-writing-011696.en: Example: An applicant who doesn’t get a job says they didn’t want the job in
college-writing-011696.zh: 示例：没有工作的申请人说他们不希望工作

college-writing-011698.en: (2) Projection: Projecting onto other people motives or thoughts of one’s own
college-writing-011698.zh: （2）投射：投射到他人的动机或自己的想法上

college-writing-011699.en: Example: A person who avoids horror movies because they find them
college-writing-011699.zh: 示例：一个人因为找到恐怖电影而避免使用恐怖电影

college-writing-011700.en: frightening assumes that everyone avoids horror movies for the same reason.
college-writing-011700.zh: 可怕的假设每个人出于同样的原因避免使用恐怖电影。

college-writing-011702.en: To study your notes, use repeated self-testing.
college-writing-011702.zh: 要研究您的笔记，请使用重复的自检。

college-writing-011703.en: For example, look at the heading “Defense Mechanisms” and say to yourself, “What are the kinds of defense mechanisms?”
college-writing-011703.zh: 例如，看看标题“防御机制”并对自己说：“什么是防御机制？”

college-writing-011704.en: When you can recite them, then say to yourself, “What is rationalization?” “What is an example of rationalization?”
college-writing-011704.zh: 当你可以背诵它们，然后对自己说：“什么是合理化？” “什么是合理化的例子？”

college-writing-011705.en: Then ask yourself, “What is projection?” “What is an example of projection?”
college-writing-011705.zh: 然后问自己：“什么是投影？” “投影的例子是什么？”

college-writing-011706.en: After you learn each section, review it, and then go on to the next section.
college-writing-011706.zh: 学习完每个部分后，查看它，然后继续下一节。

college-writing-011707.en: Do not simply read your notes; keep looking away and seeing if you can recite them to yourself.
college-writing-011707.zh: 不要简单地阅读您的笔记； 继续把目光移开，看看你是否可以自己背诵它们。

college-writing-011708.en: This self-testing is the key to effective learning.
college-writing-011708.zh: 这种自我测试是有效学习的关键。

college-writing-011710.en: Remember this sequence for dealing with a textbook: preview, mark, take notes, study the notes.
college-writing-011710.zh: 记住这个处理教科书的顺序：预览、标记、记笔记、学习笔记。

college-writing-011711.en: Approaching a textbook in this methodical way will give you very positive results.
college-writing-011711.zh: 以这种有条不紊的方式处理教科书会给你带来非常积极的结果。

college-writing-011712.en: You will no longer feel bogged down in a swamp of words, unable to figure out what you are supposed to know.
college-writing-011712.zh: 你将不再感到陷入一片沼泽，无法弄清楚你应该知道什么。

college-writing-011713.en: Instead, you will understand exactly what you have to do and how to go about doing it.
college-writing-011713.zh: 相反，您将准确了解您必须做什么以及如何去做。

college-writing-011715.en: Take a minute now to evaluate your own study habits.
college-writing-011715.zh: 现在花一点时间来评估你自己的学习习惯。

college-writing-011716.en: Do you practice many of the above skills to take effective classroom notes, control your time, and learn from your textbooks?
college-writing-011716.zh: 您是否练习了上述许多技能来进行有效的课堂笔记、控制您的时间并从教科书中学习？

college-writing-011718.en: The skills are not magic, but they are too valuable to ignore.
college-writing-011718.zh: 技能不是魔法，但它们太有价值了，不容忽视。

college-writing-011719.en: Use them carefully and consistently, and they will make academic success possible for you.
college-writing-011719.zh: 仔细和一致地使用它们，它们将使您的学术成功成为可能。

college-writing-011720.en: Try them, and you won’t need convincing.
college-writing-011720.zh: 试试它们，你不需要说服。

college-writing-011721.zh: 426 第 3 部分研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011722.en: Write a paragraph-length summary of a broadcast of the CBS television show 60 Minutes.
college-writing-011722.zh: 写下 CBS 电视节目播出的段落长度摘要 60 分钟。

college-writing-011723.en: In your first sentence, include the date of the show.
college-writing-011723.zh: 在你的第一句话中，包括节目的日期。

college-writing-011724.en: For example, “The January 3, 2021, broadcast of CBS’s 60 Minutes dealt with three subjects most people would find of interest. The first segment of the show centered on . . . ; the second segment examined . . . ; the final segment discussed. . . .”
college-writing-011724.zh: 例如，“2021年1月3日，CBS的《60分钟》播出了大多数人会感兴趣的三个主题。节目的第一部分以……为中心……；第二部分研究……讨论的最后一个部分。 ……”

college-writing-011725.en: Be sure to use parallel form in describing the three segments of the show.
college-writing-011725.zh: 描述这档节目的三个环节时，请使用平行结构。

college-writing-011726.en: Write a paragraph-length summary of a cover story of interest to you in a recent issue of a magazine like Sports Illustrated, Forbes, or Inked.
college-writing-011726.zh: 在《体育画报》、《福布斯》或《Inked》等杂志的最新一期杂志中，写下一段对您感兴趣的封面故事的段落总结。

college-writing-011728.en: In a paraphrase, you report the information in your own words and style without condensing it.
college-writing-011728.zh: 在改写时，你可以用自己的话和风格来表述信息，而不必进行压缩。

college-writing-011729.en: You should paraphrase when the original information is important, but you can write it more clearly in your own words.
college-writing-011729.zh: 当原始信息很重要时，你应该进行改写，但可以用自己的话写得更清晰。

college-writing-011730.en: In order to successfully paraphrase something, you should read the information, set it aside, and then try to explain what you just read in your own words and writing style.
college-writing-011730.zh: 为了成功进行意译，你应该先阅读相关信息，将其搁置一边，然后用自己的语言和写作风格来解释刚才所读的内容。

college-writing-011731.en: Since you are not condensing it, a paraphrase usually compares in length to the original work.
college-writing-011731.zh: 由于您没有浓缩它，因此释义通常会将长度与原始作品进行比较。

college-writing-011732.en: Unlike a summary, which can be created as a stand-alone paper, paraphrases are only used within a larger essay.
college-writing-011732.zh: 与可以作为独立论文创建的摘要不同，释义仅在较大的论文中使用。

college-writing-011733.en: Avoiding Plagiarism in Paraphrase Writing Students must be careful when paraphrasing in order to avoid plagiarism.
college-writing-011733.zh: 避免抄写写作中的学生在转述时必须小心，以避免抄袭。

college-writing-011734.en: As with summaries, if you don’t fully understand the information you have just read, you won’t be able to write a successful paraphrase.
college-writing-011734.zh: 与摘要一样，如果您不完全理解您刚刚阅读的信息，您将无法写出成功的释义。

college-writing-011735.en: You should preview, read, and eval uate the information before trying to write about it using your own words and writing style.
college-writing-011735.zh: 在尝试使用自己的文字和写作风格写下信息之前，您应该预览、阅读和评估信息。

college-writing-011736.en: Once you have completed your paraphrase, you should go back and inspect your words and sentence structure against those of the original.
college-writing-011736.zh: 一旦你完成了你的释义，你应该回去检查你的单词和句子结构。

college-writing-011737.en: This is particularly important because it is far easier to accidentally plagiarize when para phrasing if, as many students do, you try to take original sentences and just replace words here and there.
college-writing-011737.zh: 这一点尤其重要，因为在对照短语时，意外抄袭要容易得多，就像许多学生一样，如果您尝试使用原始句子并在这里和那里替换单词。

college-writing-011738.en: Simply changing one or two words from the original is not a paraphrase.
college-writing-011738.zh: 简单地从原文中更改一两个单词并不是释义。

college-writing-011739.en: This is still plagiarizing because you are plagiarizing the sentence structure and not writing it in your own words and voice.
college-writing-011739.zh: 这仍然是抄袭，因为你在抄袭句子结构，而不是用你自己的话和声音写出来。

college-writing-011740.en: Finally, just as with sum maries, you need to make sure you have credited the original source in your para phrase either by in-text citation or by crediting the author within the paraphrase.
college-writing-011740.zh: 最后，就像 Sum Maries 一样，您需要确保您已通过文本引用或在释义中将作者归功于您的 para 短语中的原始来源。

college-writing-011741.en: How to Paraphrase Information from an Article To paraphrase information from an article, follow steps 1 and 2 for “How to Summarize an Article,” then follow the steps below.
college-writing-011741.zh: 如何将文章中的信息翻译成文章中的转述信息，请按照“如何总结文章”的步骤 1 和 2 进行操作，然后按照以下步骤操作。

college-writing-011742.en: If the assigned material is a TV show or film, adapt the suggestions accordingly.
college-writing-011742.zh: 如果分配的材料是电视节目或电影，请相应地调整建议。

college-writing-011746.en: 1. Find and reread a paragraph or two that you have identified as important.
college-writing-011746.zh: 1. 查找并重读您认为重要的一两段。

college-writing-011748.en: Without looking at the original source and using your own words, write down what you have just read.
college-writing-011748.zh: 不看原始来源并使用自己的话，写下您刚刚阅读的内容。

college-writing-011749.en: One technique that helps many students to do this is to pretend they are telling some one about what they read.
college-writing-011749.zh: 帮助许多学生做到这一点的一种技术是假装他们正在告诉某人他们所读的内容。

college-writing-011750.en: 3. Compare your version with the original source.
college-writing-011750.zh: 3. 将您的版本与原始来源进行比较。

college-writing-011751.en: Using quotation marks, mark any words or phrases that are directly from the original source.
college-writing-011751.zh: 使用引号，标记任何直接来自原始来源的单词或短语。

college-writing-011752.en: Using a highlighter, mark any phrases that have a sentence structure that is similar to the original source or sound too much like that source.
college-writing-011752.zh: 使用荧光笔标记任何具有与原始来源相似的句子结构或声音过于该源的短语。

college-writing-011753.en: 4. Revise any sections that are structured closely to the original source.
college-writing-011753.zh: 4. 修改与原始来源密切相关的任何部分。

college-writing-011754.en: To do this, focus first on the areas you highlighted or put in quotation marks.
college-writing-011754.zh: 为此，请首先关注您突出显示或输入引号的区域。

college-writing-011755.en: Don’t just change a word here and there─instead, look at how you can completely rewrite and reorganize a sentence.
college-writing-011755.zh: 不要只是在这里和那里改变一个词——相反，看看如何完全重写和重组一个句子。

college-writing-011756.en: The paraphrase should use your voice, not the voice of the original author.
college-writing-011756.zh: 释义应该使用你的声音，而不是原作者的声音。

college-writing-011757.en: 5. At the bottom of your version, write down the source information, includ ing page number, so you can properly credit the information when you use it.
college-writing-011757.zh: 5. 在版本的底部，写下来源信息，包括页码，这样在使用时就能正确引用这些信息。

college-writing-011760.en: Note the sections that are too closely related to the original source.
college-writing-011760.zh: 注意与原始来源过于密切相关的部分。

college-writing-011761.en: The second one properly con veys the meaning of the passage without following the original sentence structure or using the original words.
college-writing-011761.zh: 第二个正确地表达了段落的含义，而不遵循原始句子结构或使用原始单词。

college-writing-011762.en: A scratch outline is an excellent sequel to the first four prewriting techniques.
college-writing-011762.zh: Scratch Outline 是前四种预写技术的绝佳续集。

college-writing-011763.en: A scratch outline often follows freewriting, questioning, listmaking, or diagramming; or it may gradually emerge in the midst of these strategies.
college-writing-011763.zh: 草图轮廓通常源于自由写作、提问、列表或图表绘制；也可能在这些策略的过程中逐渐显现出来。

college-writing-011764.en: In fact, trying to make a scratch outline is a good way to see if you need to do more prewriting.
college-writing-011764.zh: 实际上，尝试制作一个粗略的提纲是一种很好的方法，可以让你知道是否还需要进行更多的预写作工作。

college-writing-011765.en: If you cannot come up with a solid outline, then you know you need to do more prewriting to clarify your main point or its several kinds of support.
college-writing-011765.zh: 如果你无法制定出清晰的提纲，那么你就知道需要进行更多的预写作工作，以明确你的主要观点或其各种支撑点。

college-writing-011768.en: A scratch outline is a good follow-up to the first prewriting techniques.
college-writing-011768.zh: Scratch Outline 是对第一个预写技术的良好后续。

college-writing-011769.en: A scratch outline often follows diagramming, questioning, listmaking, or freewriting; or it may emerge in the middle of these strategies.
college-writing-011769.zh: 草稿大纲通常遵循图表、提问、列表制作或自由写作； 或者它可能出现在这些策略的中间。

college-writing-011770.en: In reality, making a scratch outline is the best way to see if you need to prewrite more.
college-writing-011770.zh: 实际上，划分大纲是查看是否需要预先编写更多内容的最佳方式。

college-writing-011771.en: If you cannot come up with a firm outline, then you know you need to do more prewriting to explain your claim and support.
college-writing-011771.zh: 如果你不能提出一个明确的大纲，那么你知道你需要做更多的预写来解释你的主张和支持。

college-writing-011773.zh: 428 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011774.en: Here are four sets of passages from the anthology of readings at the end of this book.
college-writing-011774.zh: 以下是本书末尾阅读选集的四组段落。

college-writing-011775.en: Each set begins with an original passage and an MLA formatted bib liographic entry demonstrating how a student would cite the use of such a passage in the Works Cited page.
college-writing-011775.zh: 每组都以原始段落和 MLA 格式的围兜文体条目开始，展示了学生将如何在引用的作品中引用此类段落的使用情况。

college-writing-011776.en: Each set is followed by two possible paraphrases of the passage.
college-writing-011776.zh: 每组后面是段落的两个可能的释义。

college-writing-011777.en: One is an acceptable paraphrase and the other is unacceptable in which the sentences and ideas too closely follow the original, using some of the same structure and same words as the original.
college-writing-011777.zh: 一种是可接受的释义，另一种是不可接受的，其中句子和想法过于紧跟原文，使用一些与原文相同的结构和相同的词语。

college-writing-011778.en: Identify the acceptable paraphrase with an A and the unacceptable paraphrase with a U.
college-writing-011778.zh: 用 A 识别可接受的释义，用 U 识别不可接受的释义。

college-writing-011779.en: SET 1: ORIGINAL PASSAGE During adolescence, Elkind says, kids are changing so much so fast (physically, mentally, and emotionally) that they become intensely self-centered.
college-writing-011779.zh: 第 1 组：在青春期，原始段落，孩子们的变化如此之快（身体上、精神上和情感上），以至于他们变得强烈以自我为中心。

college-writing-011780.en: It is literally difficult for them to remember that other individuals have their own lives, thoughts, and feelings, and that they are not focusing their attention on the adolescents.
college-writing-011780.zh: 他们很难记住其他人有自己的生活、想法和感受，并且他们没有将注意力集中在青少年身上。

college-writing-011781.en: According to Elkind, the adolescent is terrified of doing or saying something that will attract scorn or criticism.
college-writing-011781.zh: 根据埃尔金德的说法，青少年害怕做或说会引起蔑视或批评的事情。

college-writing-011782.en: As a result, we end up with the teenager whose life is “ruined” by an outbreak of acne; an adolescent who won’t leave the house on a bad hair day; or the teen who refuses to return to school after making an embarrassing slip during a speech.
college-writing-011782.zh: 结果，我们最终遇到了生活被痤疮爆发“毁掉”的少年； 一个不会在头发糟糕的日子离开家的青少年； 或者是在演讲中做出令人尴尬的失误后拒绝返回学校的青少年。

college-writing-011785.zh: 与阅读的大学写作技巧。

college-writing-011790.en: Elkind says, during adolescence, kids change so fast (physically,
college-writing-011790.zh: 埃尔金德说，在青春期，孩子们的变化如此之快（身体上，

college-writing-011791.en: mentally, and emotionally) that they become intensely selfcentered.
college-writing-011791.zh: 精神上和情感上）他们变得强烈以自我为中心。

college-writing-011792.en: It is hard for them to understand that other people have their own feelings, thoughts, and lives, and that they are not focused on the adolescents.
college-writing-011792.zh: 他们很难理解其他人有自己的感受、想法和生活，并且他们不关注青少年。

college-writing-011793.en: According to Elkind, adolescents are scared of doing or saying something that will attract negative attention.
college-writing-011793.zh: 根据 Elkind 的说法，青少年害怕做或说会引起负面关注的事情。

college-writing-011794.en: As a result, teenagers often think their lives are “ruined” by an outbreak of acne, won’t leave the house on a bad hair day, or refuse to go back to school after making an embarrassing mis take during a speech.
college-writing-011794.zh: 结果，青少年经常认为自己的生活因痤疮爆发而“毁掉”，不会在头发糟糕的日子离开家，或者在演讲中犯下令人尴尬的错误后拒绝回学校。

college-writing-011797.en: A scratch outline is a good technique to use after you have spent time prewriting with your chosen method.
college-writing-011797.zh: 在您花时间使用您选择的方法进行预写后，草稿轮廓是一种很好的技术。

college-writing-011798.en: By creating a scratch outline, you can see the holes in your argument and support, so you can figure out where you may need to do additional prewriting.
college-writing-011798.zh: 通过创建一个划分轮廓，您可以在论证和支持中看到漏洞，这样您就可以找出可能需要进行额外预写的地方。

college-writing-011799.en: The weaker your outline, the more obvious it is you need to spend more time prewriting.
college-writing-011799.zh: 你的轮廓越弱，你需要花更多的时间预写的时间就越明显。

college-writing-011804.en: According to Elkind, teens become so self-centered during adoles
college-writing-011804.zh: 根据 Elkind 的说法，青少年在 Adoles 期间变得如此以自我为中心

college-writing-011805.en: cence that they have a hard time looking outside of themselves and putting things into perspective.
college-writing-011805.zh: 认识到他们很难从自己的角度看待自己，并把事情放在眼里。

college-writing-011806.en: They struggle to recognize that other people are not focused on the adolescents’ experiences, but are instead dealing with their own lives.
college-writing-011806.zh: 他们很难认识到其他人不是专注于青少年的经历，而是在处理自己的生活。

college-writing-011807.en: Because teens are hyperfocused on themselves, this translates to small things like pimples or “bad hair” becoming overblown in importance, causing the teens to feel like their lives are ruined.
college-writing-011807.zh: 因为青少年过度专注于自己，这会转化为诸如粉刺或“坏头发”之类的小事变得被夸大，导致青少年觉得自己的生活被毁了。

college-writing-011808.en: SET 2: ORIGINAL PASSAGE Send a thank-you note.
college-writing-011808.zh: 第 2 组：原始段落 发送感谢信。

college-writing-011809.en: Once you’ve gotten past the interview, there is one more chance for you to make a fine impression.
college-writing-011809.zh: 一旦你通过了面试，你就有更多的机会给人留下美好的印象。

college-writing-011810.en: As soon as you can─certainly no more than one or two days after the interview─write a note of thanks.
college-writing-011810.zh: 面试结束后肯定不超过一两天——写一封感谢信。

college-writing-011811.en: In it, briefly remind the interviewer of when you came in and what job you applied for.
college-writing-011811.zh: 在其中，简要提醒面试官您何时进来以及您申请了什么工作。

college-writing-011812.en: As well as thanking the interviewer for seeing you, reaffirm your interest in the job and mention again why you think you are the best candidate for it.
college-writing-011812.zh: 除了感谢面试官见到你，重申你对这份工作的兴趣，并再次提及为什么你认为你是最好的候选人。

college-writing-011813.en: Make the note courteous, businesslike, and brief─just a paragraph or two.
college-writing-011813.zh: 把笔记做有礼貌、务实和简短——只是一两段。

college-writing-011814.en: If the interviewer is wavering between several equally qualified candidates, such a note could tip the scales in your favor.
college-writing-011814.zh: 如果面试官在几个同等合格的候选人之间摇摆不定，这样的音符可能会使你对你有利的规模倾斜。

college-writing-011816.en: “How to Do Well on a Job Interview.”

college-writing-011820.en: , authored by Zoé L. Albright and John Langan, The McGraw Hill Companies, 2022, pp. 278–281.
college-writing-011820.zh: ，佐伊·L. 奥尔布赖特和约翰·兰根撰写，麦格劳-希尔公司 2022 年出版，第 278–281 页。

college-writing-011822.en: After a job interview, you should consider sending a thank-you note
college-writing-011822.zh: 面试后，你应该考虑发送感谢信

college-writing-011823.en: to make one final positive impression.
college-writing-011823.zh: 给人留下最后的积极印象。

college-writing-011824.en: The note should be sent shortly after the interview, preferably the day of the interview or at the latest the next day.
college-writing-011824.zh: 笔记应在面试后不久发送，最好是面试当天或最迟在第二天发送。

college-writing-011825.en: Sending a note gives you the opportunity to remind the interviewer of your qualifications and desire to get the job, and it could be the difference between your getting the job and someone else getting it.
college-writing-011825.zh: 发送便条让您有机会提醒面试官您的资格和获得工作的愿望，这可能是您获得工作和其他人获得工作之间的区别。

college-writing-011828.en: There is one more chance for you to make

college-writing-011829.en: a fine impression once you’ve gotten past the interview.
college-writing-011829.zh: 经过面试后的良好印象。

college-writing-011830.en: As soon as you can, write a note of thanks.

college-writing-011831.en: In it, remind the interviewer of when you came in and what job you applied for, reaffirm your interest in the job, and mention again why you think you are the best candidate for it.
college-writing-011831.zh: 在其中，提醒面试官您何时进入以及您申请的工作，重申您对这份工作的兴趣，并再次提及您认为自己是最佳人选的原因。

college-writing-011832.en: Make the note kind, businesslike, and brief─just a paragraph or two.
college-writing-011832.zh: 使音符变得善良、务实和简短——只需一两段。

college-writing-011833.en: If the interviewer is wavering between several equally qualified candidates, such a note could help.
college-writing-011833.zh: 如果面试官在几个同样合格的候选人之间摇摆不定，这样的笔记可能会有所帮助。

college-writing-011834.zh: 430 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011835.en: SET 3: ORIGINAL PASSAGE The lecture system ultimately harms professors as well.
college-writing-011835.zh: 第 3 组：原始段落 讲座系统最终也会伤害教授。

college-writing-011836.en: It reduces feedback to a minimum, so that the lecturer can neither judge how well students understand the material nor benefit from their questions or comments.
college-writing-011836.zh: 它将反馈减少到最低限度，因此讲师既不能判断学生对材料的理解程度，也不能从他们的问题或评论中受益。

college-writing-011837.en: Questions that require the speaker to clarify obscure points and comments that challenge sloppily con structed arguments are indispensable to scholarship.
college-writing-011837.zh: 需要演讲者澄清晦涩难懂的观点和挑战那些草率构建论点的评论对于学术来说是必不可少的。

college-writing-011838.en: Without them, the liveliest mind can atrophy.
college-writing-011838.zh: 没有他们，最活泼的头脑可能会萎缩。

college-writing-011839.en: Undergraduates may not be able to make telling contributions very often, but lecturing insulates a professor even from the beginner’s naive question that could have triggered a fruitful line of thought.
college-writing-011839.zh: 本科生可能无法经常做出有说服力的贡献，但讲课即使是初学者的天真问题，也可能引发了一个富有成效的思路。

college-writing-011845.en: , authored by Zoé L. Albright and John Langan, The McGraw Hill Companies, 2022, pp. 699–702.
college-writing-011845.zh: ，佐伊·L. 奥尔布赖特和约翰·兰根撰写，麦格劳-希尔公司 2022 年出版，第 699–702 页。

college-writing-011847.en: Lectures, by nature, inhibit scholarly exchange.
college-writing-011847.zh: 讲座本质上抑制了学术交流。

college-writing-011849.en: seminates the material, and the student is expected to understand and digest it.
college-writing-011849.zh: 精炼材料，学生应该理解和消化它。

college-writing-011850.en: Very seldom is the student able to ask questions, which hurts not only the student, but the professor as well because they are unable to gauge how well students are understanding the material.
college-writing-011850.zh: 学生很少能提问，这不仅伤害了学生，而且也伤害了教授，因为他们无法衡量学生对材料的理解程度。

college-writing-011851.en: Without the exchange and discussion of ideas, or chal lenges to presented theories, opportunities for more in-depth knowledge and potential discovery is limited or missed.
college-writing-011851.zh: 如果没有思想的交流和讨论，或者对所提出的理论的挑战，更深入的知识和潜在发现的机会就会受到限制或错过。

college-writing-011853.en: Lectures hurt both the professor and student.
college-writing-011853.zh: 讲座伤害了教授和学生。

college-writing-011855.en: back, so the professor doesn’t know how well students understand the material and cannot profit from their questions.
college-writing-011855.zh: 回来，所以教授不知道学生对材料的理解程度如何，也无法从他们的问题中获利。

college-writing-011856.en: Students don’t get to ask the professor to explain unclear ideas or challenge argu ments, which are crucial to education.
college-writing-011856.zh: 学生无法要求教授解释不明确的想法或挑战论点，这对教育至关重要。

college-writing-011857.en: Without the ability to ques tion, students can get bored.
college-writing-011857.zh: 没有提问的能力，学生可能会感到无聊。

college-writing-011858.en: Undergraduates don’t contribute new information very often, but lectures guarantee that professors don’t hear naive questions.
college-writing-011858.zh: 本科生不经常提供新信息，但讲座保证教授不会听到天真的问题。

college-writing-011859.en: SET 4: ORIGINAL PASSAGE This was decades before gay characters on TV or in the movies had become commonplace.
college-writing-011859.zh: 第 4 集：原始段落 这是电视或电影中的同性恋角色变得司空见惯的几十年。

college-writing-011860.en: The words “gay marriage” would only have been heard in a punch line to a joke, and, in fact, most people still believed that homosexuality was a mental illness or a crime.
college-writing-011860.zh: “同性婚姻”这个词只能在笑话的妙语中被听到，事实上，大多数人仍然认为同性恋是一种精神疾病或犯罪。

college-writing-011861.en: In the town where I grew up, it was illegal to be gay─police used to stake out a little rundown cinderblock bar on the other side of the tracks where, supposedly, gay men gathered.
college-writing-011861.zh: 在我长大的小镇上，同性恋是违法的——警察过去在轨道的另一边放了一个破旧的煤渣块酒吧，据说是男同性恋者聚集在那里。

college-writing-011862.en: It was not uncommon for the police to rough up and handcuff men they saw coming out of this bar.
college-writing-011862.zh: 警察粗暴地站起来并给他们戴上手铐的人从这个酒吧里出来的情况并不少见。

college-writing-011863.en: Then they were thrown in the jail for the night for little or no real reason.
college-writing-011863.zh: 然后他们被关进监狱过夜，几乎没有真正的原因。

college-writing-011864.en: Most of the townspeople thought this was a good idea.
college-writing-011864.zh: 大多数市民认为这是个好主意。

college-writing-011868.zh: 与阅读的大学写作技巧。

college-writing-011872.en: This was before gay characters on TV had become commonplace.
college-writing-011872.zh: 这是在电视上的同性恋角色变得司空见惯之前。

college-writing-011873.en: The words “gay marriage” would only have been heard in a punch line to a joke.
college-writing-011873.zh: “同性婚姻”这个词只能在笑话的妙语中被听到。

college-writing-011874.en: Most people still believed that homosexuality was a crime.
college-writing-011874.zh: 大多数人仍然认为同性恋是犯罪。

college-writing-011875.en: In the town where I grew up, it was illegal to be gay and police arrested gay men through stake-outs at a specific bar.
college-writing-011875.zh: 在我长大的小镇上，成为同性恋者是违法的，警方通过在特定酒吧的赌注逮捕了男同性恋者。

college-writing-011876.en: It was not uncommon for the police to handcuff men they saw coming out of this bar.
college-writing-011876.zh: 警察给他们看到从这个酒吧里出来的男人戴上手铐的情况并不少见。

college-writing-011877.en: Then they were thrown in the jail for the night for little or no real reason.
college-writing-011877.zh: 然后他们被关进监狱过夜，几乎没有真正的原因。

college-writing-011878.en: Most people thought this was a good idea.
college-writing-011878.zh: 大多数人认为这是一个好主意。

college-writing-011880.en: In the author’s hometown, it was illegal to be gay.
college-writing-011880.zh: 在作者的家乡，同性恋是非法的。

college-writing-011882.en: were treated harshly by police and were often targeted and arrested for being suspected of being gay.
college-writing-011882.zh: 受到警方的严厉对待，并经常因涉嫌同性恋而被攻击和逮捕。

college-writing-011883.en: Because they weren’t aware of a different way of thinking, most of the community thought this treatment was ok.
college-writing-011883.zh: 因为他们没有意识到不同的思维方式，所以大多数社区认为这种治疗方法还可以。

college-writing-011884.en: At that time, gay people weren’t widely seen in the media, and if they were, they were usually treated as a joke or punch line instead of presented as normal.
college-writing-011884.zh: 当时，同性恋者在媒体上并没有被广泛看到，如果是的话，他们通常被视为笑话或妙语，而不是正常呈现。

college-writing-011885.en: Choose two non-consecutive paragraphs from the essay, “Power Learning,” you summarized in Activity 1 and write a paraphrase of each paragraph.
college-writing-011885.zh: 从文章“权力学习”中选择两个非连续的段落，您在活动 1 中总结并写下每个段落的释义。

college-writing-011886.en: Make sure you include the original paragraphs with your work.
college-writing-011886.zh: 确保您的作品中包含原始段落。

college-writing-011887.en: Choose a recent article from a journal like Popular Mechanics, Smithsonian, or Entrepreneur.
college-writing-011887.zh: 从大众力学、史密森尼或企业家等期刊中选择最近的一篇文章。

college-writing-011888.en: After reading the article, find a paragraph that could be poten tially useful in a research paper.
college-writing-011888.zh: 阅读完文章后，找到一个可能在研究论文中有用的段落。

college-writing-011889.en: Write the original paragraph; below the orig inal, paraphrase the paragraph.
college-writing-011889.zh: 写原段； 在原来的 inal 下方，释义段落。

college-writing-011890.en: Remember to follow the steps outlined earlier in the chapter.
college-writing-011890.zh: 请记住遵循本章前面概述的步骤。

college-writing-011892.en: Unlike a summary or paraphrase, a direct quotation must be written exactly as it appears in the original work.
college-writing-011892.zh: 与摘要或释义不同，直接引用必须与原始作品中出现的完全相同。

college-writing-011893.en: There are three ways that direct quotations are generally presented.
college-writing-011893.zh: 直接报价通常通过三种方式呈现。

college-writing-011894.en: For shorter passages, quotation marks are used.
college-writing-011894.zh: 对于较短的段落，使用引号。

college-writing-011895.en: For longer complete passages, the material is indented as a block of text and no quotation marks are used.
college-writing-011895.zh: 对于较长的完整段落，材料缩进为文本块，不使用引号。

college-writing-011896.en: (Each “Original Passage” in the preceding paraphrasing activity is an example of a direct quotation.)
college-writing-011896.zh: （前面的解释活动中的每个“原始段落”都是直接引用的一个例子。）

college-writing-011897.en: The same formatting applies to longer
college-writing-011897.zh: 相同的格式适用于较长的

college-writing-011900.zh: 432 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011901.en: passages with omitted material, but for these passages, ellipses are included to indicate the omitted text.
college-writing-011901.zh: 带有省略材料的段落，但对于这些段落，包括省略号以表示省略的文本。

college-writing-011902.en: Each of these categories is explained further and illustrated in the following sections.
college-writing-011902.zh: 这些类别中的每一个都将在以下部分中进一步解释并说明。

college-writing-011903.en: These examples have been taken from the “Power Learning” essay you worked with in Activity 1.
college-writing-011903.zh: 这些示例取自您在活动 1 中使用的“Power Learning”文章。

college-writing-011904.en: The paragraph location of each quotation is explained, so you can refer to the original essay and see the quotation in its original context.
college-writing-011904.zh: 说明每个引文的段落位置，因此您可以参考原文并在其原始上下文中查看引文。

college-writing-011905.en: Short Quotations If you want to include a brief sentence or two of direct text from an original source, you will use a short quotation.
college-writing-011905.zh: 简短的引文 如果您想包含来自原始来源的一句或两个直接文本的短语，您将使用简短的引用。

college-writing-011906.en: As you insert the quoted material into your own writing, a transition is usually needed.
college-writing-011906.zh: 当您将引用的材料插入您自己的写作中时，通常需要过渡。

college-writing-011908.en: Notice that in the second example, the writer builds the direct quote into a larger sentence and in so doing, places the letter “t” in brackets.
college-writing-011908.zh: 请注意，在第二个示例中，作者将直接引用构建到一个较大的句子中，这样就将字母“T”放在括号中。

college-writing-011909.en: This shows that the word was lowercased by the student and not by the author of the quotation.
college-writing-011909.zh: 这表明这个词是学生小写的，而不是引用的作者。

college-writing-011910.en: Blythe states, “Success in college depends on time control” (419).
college-writing-011910.zh: Blythe 说，“大学的成功取决于时间控制”（419）。

college-writing-011911.en: Blythe emphasizes there are three steps to good time control.
college-writing-011911.zh: Blythe 强调，良好的时间控制需要三个步骤。

college-writing-011912.en: He explains that “[t]he second step in time control is to have a weekly study schedule for the semester─a chart that covers all the days of the week and all the waking hours in each day” (420).
college-writing-011912.zh: 他解释说，“时间控制的第二步是每周有一个学期的学习时间表——一张图表，涵盖一周中的所有日子和每天的所有醒着时间”（420）。

college-writing-011913.en: Long Complete Quotations If you want to use a complete section that is longer than four lines, you should block the quotation, which means you’ll need to indent it by an extra five spaces to set it off from the rest of the essay.
college-writing-011913.zh: 长篇完整引用 如果您想使用长于四行的完整部分，您应该阻止引文，这意味着您需要额外缩进五个空格以将其与文章的其余部分引出。

college-writing-011914.en: (This will result in an indent of 1⁄2 inch from the left margin.)
college-writing-011914.zh: （这将导致距左边距 1⁄2 英寸的缩进。）

college-writing-011915.en: Block quotations do not use quotation marks.

college-writing-011916.en: In the example below, the first paragraph was written by a student as a lead-in to the direct quota tion from “Power Learning.”
college-writing-011916.zh: 在下面的例子中，第一段是学生写的，作为“权力学习”的直接配额的导入。

college-writing-011917.en: Notice how the quotation is set off by the extra indent.
college-writing-011917.zh: 注意额外的缩进是如何引出报价的。

college-writing-011918.en: In the essay, “Power Learning,” several strategies for successful studying are presented.
college-writing-011918.zh: 在论文“权力学习”中，提出了几种成功学习的策略。

college-writing-011919.en: In the section about note-taking, good attendance is stressed as the most important key to success:
college-writing-011919.zh: 在关于记笔记的部分中，良好的出勤率被强调为成功的最重要关键：

college-writing-011921.en: Your alternatives─reading the text, reading someone else’s notes, or both─cannot substitute for the class experience of hearing ideas in person as someone presents them to you.
college-writing-011921.zh: 你的替代方案——阅读文本、阅读别人的笔记或两者兼而有之——不能替代在某人向您展示想法时亲自听取想法的课堂体验。

college-writing-011922.en: Also, in class lectures and discussions, your instructor typically presents and devel ops the main ideas and facts of the course─the ones you will be expected to know on exams.
college-writing-011922.zh: 此外，在课堂讲座和讨论中，您的讲师通常会展示和开发课程的主要思想和事实——您将在考试中了解到的那些。

college-writing-011928.en: Quotations with Omitted Information If you are using a longer quotation that includes information unrelated to your topic, you may omit the irrelevant words as long as you don’t change the overall meaning.
college-writing-011928.zh: 带省略信息的报价 如果您使用的是包含与您的主题无关的信息的较长报价，只要您不改变整体含义，您就可以省略不相关的单词。

college-writing-011929.en: To show such an omission, use three spaced periods (known as ellipsis points) in place of the deleted words:
college-writing-011929.zh: 要显示这样的省略，请使用三个间隔的周期（称为省略号）代替删除的字：

college-writing-011930.en: The author offers three clear steps to good time control, “First, you should prepare a large monthly calendar . . . circle important dates on this calendar. Circle the days on which tests are scheduled; circle the days when papers are due” (Blythe 420).
college-writing-011930.zh: 作者提供了三个明确的时间控制步骤，“首先，你应该准备一个大的月历……在这个日历上圈出重要的日期。圈出安排测试的日期；圈出论文到期的日期”（Blythe 420）。

college-writing-011931.en: Note that in the following example there are four dots in the first line of the quotation─the first dot is the period at the end of the sentence.
college-writing-011931.zh: 请注意，在以下示例中，引文的第一行有四个点——第一个点是句子末尾的句点。

college-writing-011932.en: The author’s final step in time control focuses on lists.
college-writing-011932.zh: 作者在时间控制上的最后一步集中在列表上。

college-writing-011933.en: “The third step in time control is to make a daily or weekly to-do list. . . . On this list, write down the things you need to do for the following day or the following week” (Blythe 420).
college-writing-011933.zh: “时间控制的第三步是制作一个每日或每周的待办事项清单……在此列表中，写下您第二天或下周需要做的事情”（Blythe 420）。

college-writing-011934.en: Avoiding Plagiarism in Direct Quotations Unlike summaries and paraphrases─where accidental plagiarism can occur as students try to use their own words to report others’ words and ideas─there is less risk of plagiarism in the use of direct quotations.
college-writing-011934.zh: 避免在直接引语中抄袭 与摘要和释义不同——当学生试图用自己的话语来报告别人的话和想法时，可能会发生意外的抄袭……在使用直接引用时，抄袭的风险较小。

college-writing-011935.en: The key factor is to copy the exact words and punctuation and then enclose the text in quotation marks (or set it off as a block indent, if longer).
college-writing-011935.zh: 关键因素是复制确切的单词和标点符号，然后将文本用引号括起来（或者将其设置为块缩进，如果更长）。

college-writing-011936.en: However, if students forget to use quo tation marks or block indents and/or forget to credit the author, plagiarism can occur.
college-writing-011936.zh: 但是，如果学生忘记使用引号或阻止缩进和/或忘记归功于作者，则可能会发生抄袭。

college-writing-011937.en: Thus, it is critical for students to pay careful attention to their use of another author’s words throughout all their writing.
college-writing-011937.zh: 因此，学生在整个写作过程中都要仔细注意他们对另一个作者的文字的使用是至关重要的。

college-writing-011940.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate • how to plan and take notes for a source-based essay • how to incorporate sources in an essay • how to cite sources in an essay
college-writing-011940.zh: 本章将解释和说明 • 如何计划和记下基于来源的论文的笔记 • 如何在论文中整合资源 • 如何在论文中引用来源

college-writing-011941.en: This chapter also includes • a model literary analysis • a model rhetorical analysis
college-writing-011941.zh: 本章还包括 • 模型文学分析 • 模型修辞分析

college-writing-011942.en: C H A P T E R 19 19

college-writing-011944.en: To gain a sense of how to review a text, visit the New York Review of Books website at http://www.nybooks.com and choose a review to read.
college-writing-011944.zh: 要了解如何查看文本，请访问纽约书评网站 http://www.nybooks.com 并选择要阅读的评论。

college-writing-011945.en: Write a short paragraph explaining why you chose that review and what you’ve learned from it.
college-writing-011945.zh: 写一段简短的段落，解释你为什么选择那篇评论以及你从中学到了什么。

college-writing-011947.en: Each semester, you will probably be assigned at least one paper that will require you to use outside sources to support your argument.
college-writing-011947.zh: 每个学期，您可能会被分配至少一篇论文，要求您使用外部资源来支持您的论点。

college-writing-011948.en: Academic writing often calls for students to use different sources to support their arguments.
college-writing-011948.zh: 学术写作经常要求学生使用不同的来源来支持他们的论点。

college-writing-011949.en: For instance, a sociology class might require students to write a response to a chapter in their text, using information from that chapter as support.
college-writing-011949.zh: 例如，社会学课可能要求学生使用该章节中的信息作为支持来写下对章节的一章的回应。

college-writing-011950.en: Students in a history class may have to write a response to an essay written during the Civil War.
college-writing-011950.zh: 历史课上的学生可能不得不写一篇内战期间写的论文的回应。

college-writing-011951.en: While these assignments don’t necessarily demand research on the part of the student, they will require the student to use information from the original source as essay support.
college-writing-011951.zh: 虽然这些作业不一定需要学生的研究，但它们会要求学生使用来自原始来源的信息作为论文支持。

college-writing-011952.en: This information will need to be incorporated and cited properly.
college-writing-011952.zh: 此信息需要正确整合和引用。

college-writing-011957.zh: 第19章 撰写基于源的论文435

college-writing-011959.en: The purpose of a source-based essay is to thoroughly develop a limited topic that is neither too narrow nor too broad.
college-writing-011959.zh: 基于来源的论文的目的是彻底开发一个既不太狭窄也不太宽泛的有限主题。

college-writing-011960.en: You want your sources to focus on the development of that topic, not stray in multiple directions.
college-writing-011960.zh: 您希望您的来源专注于该主题的发展，而不是偏向多个方向。

college-writing-011961.en: When you are writing a source-based essay, you will need to read through and take notes on the material you plan to use to support your essay.
college-writing-011961.zh: 当您撰写基于来源的论文时，您需要通读并记录您计划用于支持您的论文的材料。

college-writing-011962.en: As you learned in Chapter 17, “Information Literacy,” finding the right information can often be the most difficult part of writing a source-based essay.
college-writing-011962.zh: 正如您在第 17 章“信息素养”中所学到的，找到正确的信息通常是撰写基于来源的文章中最困难的部分。

college-writing-011963.en: If you have been assigned a topic and have to locate your own sources, you should read over Chapter 17 before reading the rest of this chapter.
college-writing-011963.zh: 如果您被分配了一个主题并且必须找到自己的来源，您应该阅读本章的其余部分之前阅读第 17 章。

college-writing-011964.en: If you have been assigned a source to work with, you should be ready to create a scratch outline and begin taking notes.
college-writing-011964.zh: 如果您被分配了一个要使用的来源，您应该准备好创建一个划痕大纲并开始做笔记。

college-writing-011965.en: Preparing a Scratch Outline As you carefully read through the material you have gathered, think about the content and organization of your paper.
college-writing-011965.zh: 准备草稿大纲 当您仔细阅读您收集的材料时，请考虑论文的内容和组织。

college-writing-011966.en: Begin deciding what information you will present and how you will arrange it.
college-writing-011966.zh: 开始决定您将提供哪些信息以及您将如何安排。

college-writing-011967.en: Prepare a scratch outline that shows both the paper’s working thesis and the areas that support the thesis.
college-writing-011967.zh: 准备一份草稿大纲，展示论文的工作论文和支持论文的领域。

college-writing-011968.en: Try to include at least three areas, if not more, of support.
college-writing-011968.zh: 尝试包括至少三个领域，如果不是更多的话，支持。

college-writing-011969.en: Writing a source-based essay will require careful note-taking, proper integration of information, in-text citation, and a Works Cited page regardless of whether you are using one, two, or ten sources.
college-writing-011969.zh: 无论您使用的是一种、两个还是十种来源，撰写基于来源的论文都需要仔细记笔记、正确整合信息、文本引用和作品引用页面。

college-writing-011970.en: The following pages will explain how to properly incorporate and document your sources.
college-writing-011970.zh: 以下页面将解释如何正确合并和记录您的来源。

college-writing-011973.en: See Chapter 2 for further discussion about and additional models of scratch outlines.
college-writing-011973.zh: 有关 Scratch 轮廓的进一步讨论和其他模型，请参见第 2 章。

college-writing-011974.zh: 436 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-011975.en: Keeping Careful Notes With this tentative outline in mind, you can begin taking notes on the information that you expect to include in your paper.
college-writing-011975.zh: 仔细记注 考虑到这个试探性的大纲，您可以开始记录您希望包含在论文中的信息。

college-writing-011976.en: For each source, you will want to create a document or use note cards.
college-writing-011976.zh: 对于每个源，您都需要创建一个文档或使用记事卡。

college-writing-011977.en: Don’t use loose-leaf or notebook paper; doing so makes it harder to organize your notes as you prepare to draft your paper.
college-writing-011977.zh: 不要使用活页纸或笔记本纸； 这样做会使您在准备起草论文时更难整理笔记。

college-writing-011978.en: Notes should be in the form of direct quotations and summaries in your own words.
college-writing-011978.zh: 注释应以您自己的话直接引用和摘要的形式。

college-writing-011979.en: At times, you may also paraphrase.

college-writing-011980.en: Since most research involves condensing, you will probably summarize much more often than you will paraphrase.
college-writing-011980.zh: 由于大多数研究都涉及浓缩，因此您的总结可能比您所解释的要多得多。

college-writing-011981.en: Chapter 18 provides detailed information defining and differentiating these forms of writing.
college-writing-011981.zh: 第 18 章提供了定义和区分这些写作形式的详细信息。

college-writing-011982.en: When you create your notes, you want to make sure you include all relevant bibliographic information─title of source, author, page number, publication information.
college-writing-011982.zh: 创建笔记时，您要确保包含所有相关的书目信息——来源、作者、页码、出版信息的标题。

college-writing-011983.en: As you choose information that you think you are going to use, you should copy it word-for-word and enclose it within quotation marks.
college-writing-011983.zh: 当您选择您认为将要使用的信息时，您应该逐字复制它并将其包含在引号中。

college-writing-011984.en: If you want to paraphrase or summarize the information, you should write your paraphrase or summary with the page number and a notation stating what you have created.
college-writing-011984.zh: 如果您想转述或总结这些信息，您应该写下您的释义或摘要，并附有页码和说明您创建的内容的符号。

college-writing-011985.en: Always record the exact source and page from which you use information.
college-writing-011985.zh: 始终记录您使用信息的确切来源和页面。

college-writing-011986.en: In a source-based essay, you must document all information that is not common knowledge or not a matter of historical record.
college-writing-011986.zh: 在基于来源的论文中，您必须记录所有非常识或非历史记录问题的信息。

college-writing-011987.en: For example, the birth and death dates of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., are established facts and do not need documenting.
college-writing-011987.zh: 例如，Martin Luther King, Jr. 博士的出生和死亡日期是既定的事实，不需要记录。

college-writing-011988.en: On the other hand, the average number of hours worked in the United States this year compared with the average number worked in 1980 is a specialized fact and should be documented.
college-writing-011988.zh: 另一方面，与 1980 年的平均工作时间相比，今年在美国的平均工作小时数是一个特殊的事实，应该记录在案。

college-writing-011989.en: In addition, as you read several sources on a subject, you will develop a sense of what authors regard as generally shared, or common, information and what is more specialized information that requires documentation.
college-writing-011989.zh: 此外，当您阅读有关某个主题的几个来源时，您将了解作者认为一般共享或通用信息的哪些内容以及需要文档的更专业信息。

college-writing-011990.en: Notes can be taken in two different formats─note cards and documents.
college-writing-011990.zh: 笔记可以以两种不同的格式进行——笔记卡和文档。

college-writing-011991.en: Each format is discussed and illustrated below.
college-writing-011991.zh: 下面讨论和说明每种格式。

college-writing-011992.en: Taking Notes Using Note Cards When using note cards to take notes, students should include only one quotation, summary, or paraphrase per card.
college-writing-011992.zh: 使用记事卡做笔记 在使用记事卡做笔记时，学生应仅包含每张卡片的引语、摘要或释义。

college-writing-011995.en: A direct quotation must be written exactly as it appears in the original work.
college-writing-011995.zh: 直接引用必须与原始作品中出现的完全相同。

college-writing-011996.en: However, you may omit words that are not relevant to your point as long as you don’t change the meaning.
college-writing-011996.zh: 但是，只要您不改变含义，您就可以省略与您的观点无关的单词。

college-writing-011997.en: To show such an omission, use three spaced periods (known as ellipsis points) in place of the deleted words.
college-writing-011997.zh: 要显示这种省略，请使用三个间隔的周期（称为省略点）代替删除的单词。

college-writing-011998.en: Several examples of note cards with direct quotations follow.
college-writing-011998.zh: 下面是几个带有直接引用的记事卡的例子。

college-writing-011999.zh: 第19章 撰写基于源的论文437

college-writing-012000.zh: 奥尔科特，路易莎 M. 小女人。

college-writing-012002.en: “The dim, dusty-room, with the busts staring down from the tall bookcases, the cosey chairs, the globes, and best of all, the wilderness of books, in which she could wander where she liked, made the library a region of bliss to her. The moment Aunt March took her nap, or was busy with company, Jo hurried to this quiet place, and curling herself up in the easy-chair, devoured poetry, romance, history, travels, and pictures, like a regular book worm. But, like all happiness, it did not last long; for as sure as she had just reached the heart of the story, the sweetest verse of the song, or the most perilous adventure of her traveller, a shrill voice called, “Josy-phine! Josy-phine!” and she had to leave her paradise to wind yarn, wash the poodle or read Belsham’s Essays by the hour together.
college-writing-012002.zh: “昏暗、尘土飞扬的房间，半身像从高大的书柜、科西椅子、地球仪上看，最重要的是，书的荒野，她可以在她喜欢的地方漫步，让图书馆成为她幸福的地方。 马奇阿姨打了个盹，或者忙着陪伴，乔匆匆赶到这个安静的地方，把自己蜷缩在轻松的椅子里，被吞噬的诗歌、浪漫、历史、旅行和图片，就像一条普通的书虫一样。 因为她刚刚到达故事的核心，这首歌中最甜美的诗句，或者她旅行者最危险的冒险，一个尖锐的声音叫道：“Josy-Phine！ 乔西·芬！” 她不得不离开她的天堂去缠纱，洗个贵宾犬或按小时阅读贝尔沙姆的文章。

college-writing-012003.en: ” (This is a direct quotation found on page 40.)
college-writing-012003.zh: ”（这是第 40 页上的直接报价。）

college-writing-012005.en: Note with Direct Quotation and Ellipsis
college-writing-012005.zh: 注意直接引用和省略号

college-writing-012006.zh: 奥尔科特，路易莎 M. 小女人。

college-writing-012008.en: “The dim, dusty-room, with the busts staring down from the tall bookcases . . . and best of all, the wilderness of books, in which she could wander where she liked, made the library a region of bliss to her. The moment Aunt March took her nap, or was busy with company, Jo hurried to this quiet place, and . . . devoured poetry, romance, history, travels, and pictures, like a regular book worm. But, like all happiness, it did not last long . . . and she had to leave her paradise to wind yarn, wash the poodle or read Belsham’s Essays by the hour together.” (This is a direct quotation found on page 40.)
college-writing-012008.zh: “昏暗、尘土飞扬的房间，半身像从高大的书柜中向下看……最重要的是，书的荒野，她可以在她喜欢的地方漫步，使图书馆成为她的幸福之地。马奇阿姨带她的那一刻 小睡，或者忙着陪伴，乔匆匆赶到这个安静的地方，……吞噬诗歌、浪漫、历史、旅行和画像，就像一个普通的书虫一样，但是，就像所有的幸福一样，它并没有持续多久……她不得不离开她。 天堂风纱、洗涤贵宾犬或逐小时阅读贝尔沙姆的文章。” （这是第 40 页的直接报价。）

college-writing-012011.en: The Storied Life of A. J. Fikry.
college-writing-012011.zh: A. J. Fikry 的传奇生活。

college-writing-012066.en: Keep the following in mind as you take notes.

college-writing-012067.en: If you are using note cards:

college-writing-012068.en: • Write on only one side of each card.
college-writing-012068.zh: • 仅在每张卡片的一侧写字。

college-writing-012069.en: • Write only one kind of information, from one source, on any one card.
college-writing-012069.zh: • 在任何一张卡上只写一种来源的信息，一种来源。

college-writing-012070.en: • Identify the source and page number on every card.
college-writing-012070.zh: • 确定每张卡片上的来源和页码。

college-writing-012071.zh: • 确定您是否在每张卡片上都写了引文、摘要或释义。

college-writing-012073.zh: • 为每个源创建一个新文档。

college-writing-012074.en: • Identify the author, title, and publication information at the top of the document.
college-writing-012074.zh: • 识别文档顶部的作者、标题和出版物信息。

college-writing-012088.en: “The Lords of the Confederacy of the Five Nations shall be mentors of the people for all time. The thickness of their skin shall be seven spans─which is to say that they shall be proof against anger, offensive actions and criticism. Their hearts shall be full of peace and good will and their minds filled with a yearning for the welfare of the people of the Confederacy. college-writing-012096.en: “It is easy to see, that, in entering upon the duties of a slaveholder, some little experience is needed. Nature has done almost nothing to prepare men and women to be either slaves or slaveholders. Nothing but rigid training, long persisted in, can perfect the character of the one or the other. One cannot easily forget to love freedom; and it is as hard to cease to respect that natural love in our fellow creatures. On entering upon the career of a slaveholding mistress, Mrs. Auld was singularly deficient; nature, which fits nobody for such an office, had done less for her than any lady I had known. It was no easy matter to induce her to think and to feel that the curly-headed boy, who stood by her side, and even leaned on her lap; who was loved by little Tommy, and who loved little Tommy in turn; sustained to her only the relation of a chattel. I was more than that, and she felt me to be more than that. I could talk and sing; I could laugh and weep; I could reason and remember; I could love and hate. I was human, and she, dear lady, knew and felt me to be so. How could she, then, treat me as a brute, without a mighty struggle with all the noble powers of her own soul. That struggle came, and the will and power of the husband was victorious. Her noble soul was overthrown; but, he that overthrew it did not, himself, escape the consequences. He, not less than the other parties, was injured in his domestic peace by the fall.”
college-writing-012096.zh: “很容易看出，在履行奴隶主的职责时，需要一些小经验。大自然几乎没有为男人和女人做好准备，成为奴隶或奴隶主。只有严格的训练，长期坚持下去，才能完善其中一人的性格。不能轻易忘记 爱自由；在我们同胞中，也很难停止尊重这种自然的爱。在进入奴隶主人的职业生涯时，奥尔德夫人非常缺乏；与任何人都不适合从事这样的职务的大自然对她所做的事情比我的任何一位女士都少 知道，让她思考和感受那个站在她身边，甚至靠在她的腿上的卷头男孩，被小汤米所爱，又爱小汤米的人，只支持她的关系，这并非易事。 我不止于此，她觉得我不止于此。 我是人类，她，亲爱的女士，知道并感觉到我是这样的。 那么，她怎么能把我当作一个畜生，而不是与她自己灵魂的所有高尚力量进行激烈的斗争。 那场斗争来了，丈夫的意志和力量取得了胜利。 她高贵的灵魂被推翻； 但是，推翻它的人，他自己并没有逃避后果。 他不比其他各方少，在他的家庭和平中因堕落而受伤。”
