college-writing-012150.zh: ，佐伊·L. 奥尔布赖特和约翰·兰根撰写，麦格劳-希尔公司 2022 年出版，第 341–346 页。

college-writing-012152.en: Knowing how to write a good summary or paraphrase or copy a quotation isn’t enough.
college-writing-012152.zh: 知道如何写出好的摘要或释义或复制引文是不够的。

college-writing-012153.en: You have to know how to incorporate the information, so that it is seamless and part of your essay.
college-writing-012153.zh: 您必须知道如何整合这些信息，以便它是无缝的，并且是您论文的一部分。

college-writing-012154.en: There are several parts to a properly integrated quote, summary, or paraphrase.
college-writing-012154.zh: 正确集成的报价、摘要或释义有几个部分。

college-writing-012155.en: Introduction: The source needs to be introduced to the reader, so the reader understands why the upcoming information is important and is prepared for the information.
college-writing-012155.zh: 简介：需要向读者介绍来源，以便读者了解为什么即将发布的信息很重要并为信息做好准备。

college-writing-012156.en: Any time a new source is used, you must introduce the important information─author and credibility of the source used.
college-writing-012156.zh: 任何时候使用新来源，都必须介绍所使用的来源的重要信息——作者和可信度。

college-writing-012157.en: You should always refer to the author(s) by full name and title the first time; you can use the author(s)’ last name(s) each time after.
college-writing-012157.zh: 您应该第一次以全名和标题的形式引用作者； 之后，您可以每次使用作者的姓氏。

college-writing-012158.en: Never refer to an author by their first name only.
college-writing-012158.zh: 切勿仅使用作者的名字来引用作者的名字。

college-writing-012159.en: Quotation/Paraphrase/Summary: After you have introduced the source, you will need to transition into the exact words (quotation) or rewording (paraphrase/ summary) of the original source.
college-writing-012159.zh: 引用/释义/摘要：在您介绍了源代码后，您需要转换为原始来源的确切单词（引文）或重写（释义/摘要）。

college-writing-012160.en: You want to avoid statements like “the following quote says” or “a summary of the source is.”
college-writing-012160.zh: 您希望避免诸如“以下报价说”或“来源的摘要”之类的陈述。

college-writing-012161.en: Instead you should employ good transitional devices to link your ideas and to make a connection as to why you are using that piece of information.
college-writing-012161.zh: 相反，您应该使用良好的过渡设备来链接您的想法并与您使用该信息的原因建立联系。

college-writing-012162.en: See the following box for transition suggestions.
college-writing-012162.zh: 有关过渡建议，请参阅以下框。

college-writing-012163.en: Citation: Immediately following the information you used, you need to include a citation that shows where the information originated.
college-writing-012163.zh: 引文：在您使用的信息之后，您需要立即包含显示信息来源的引文。

college-writing-012164.en: Citations are explained in more detail later in the chapter.
college-writing-012164.zh: 引文将在本章后面更详细地解释。

college-writing-012165.en: Connection: Once you have incorporated the information, you want to continue to connect it to why you are using it.
college-writing-012165.zh: 连接：一旦您合并了信息，您希望继续将其连接到您使用它的原因。

college-writing-012166.en: Explain how the cited information supports the topic sentence of that paragraph or the thesis of your essay.
college-writing-012166.zh: 解释被引用的信息如何支持该段落的 主题句 或论文的论文。

college-writing-012167.en: By doing this, you develop the information more deeply, helping the reader to see your point.
college-writing-012167.zh: 通过这样做，您可以更深入地开发信息，帮助读者了解您的观点。

college-writing-012168.zh: 444 第 3 部分研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012169.en: An Example of How to Incorporate Source Material from Document Notes The following example demonstrates how to incorporate a direct quotation and a short summary.
college-writing-012169.zh: 如何从文档注释中合并源材料的示例 以下示例演示如何合并直接引用和简短摘要。

college-writing-012170.en: The student’s assignment was to react to the essay “from Self-Reliance” located in the anthology section, Part 5, of your text.
college-writing-012170.zh: 学生的作业是对位于您文本的选集第 5 部分中的“自力更生”的文章做出反应。

college-writing-012171.en: This student has chosen to keep their notes in a document instead of using note cards.
college-writing-012171.zh: 该学生选择将他们的笔记保存在文档中，而不是使用便条卡。

college-writing-012172.en: At the top of the document is the bibliographic entry.

college-writing-012173.en: The student has then included the two original quotations they have decided to use in their essay.
college-writing-012173.zh: 然后，该学生将他们决定在论文中使用的两个原始语录包括在内。

college-writing-012174.en: The first quotation also includes a summary as the student wasn’t sure if they were going to summarize this section or use a direct quotation.
college-writing-012174.zh: 第一个引用还包括一个摘要，因为学生不确定他们是否要总结本节或使用直接引用。

college-writing-012175.en: Keeping notes in this manner allows the student to keep their options open.
college-writing-012175.zh: 以这种方式记笔记可以让学生保持他们的选择开放。

college-writing-012194.en: , authored by Zoé L. Albright and John Langan, The McGraw Hill Companies, 2022, pp. 648–649.
college-writing-012194.zh: ，佐伊·L. 奥尔布赖特和约翰·兰根撰写，麦格劳-希尔公司 2022 年出版，第 648–649 页。

college-writing-012195.en: Original Quotation: “What I must do is all that concerns me, not what the people think. This rule, equally arduous in actual and in intellectual life, may serve for the whole distinction between greatness and meanness. It is the harder because you will always find those who think they know what is your duty better than you know it. It is easy in the world to live after the world’s opinion; it is easy in solitude to live after our own; but the great man is he who in the midst of the crowd keeps with perfect sweetness the independence of solitude . . .” (Emerson 649)
college-writing-012195.zh: 原文：“我必须做的是我所关心的一切，而不是人们的想法。这条规则，在现实和智力生活中同样艰巨，可能服务于伟大和卑鄙之间的整个区别。你总是会发现那些认为他们知道自己的责任比你更好的人 知道了，世上很容易生活在世界的意见之后；在我们自己的孤独中生活是很容易的；但伟大的人是他在人群中以完美的甜蜜来保持孤独的独立性的人。” 第649章

college-writing-012196.en: Summary: Emerson thinks we should ignore what others think even if it is hard.
college-writing-012196.zh: 总结：艾默生认为我们应该忽略别人的想法，即使这很困难。

college-writing-012197.en: It’s easy to follow your ideas if you don’t interact with others.
college-writing-012197.zh: 如果您不与他人互动，则很容易遵循您的想法。

college-writing-012198.en: It’s a better person who can follow his own ideas in society even if those ideas don’t follow society’s ideas (649).
college-writing-012198.zh: 即使这些想法不遵循社会的想法，它也是一个可以在社会中追随自己想法的更好的人（649）。

college-writing-012199.zh: 第19章 撰写基于源的论文445

college-writing-012200.en: Notice that the student’s notes are longer than what they wound up using in the final paragraph.
college-writing-012200.zh: 请注意，学生的笔记比他们在最后一段中使用的要长。

college-writing-012201.en: The first quotation in that paragraph is only a small portion of the original quote (second quotation on document).
college-writing-012201.zh: 该段落中的第一个引文只是原始报价的一小部分（文档上的第二个报价）。

college-writing-012202.en: Only the most important part of the quotation is used.
college-writing-012202.zh: 只使用报价中最重要的部分。

college-writing-012203.en: The second citation in the paragraph is a summary.
college-writing-012203.zh: 段落中的第二个引文是摘要。

college-writing-012204.en: Although the student could have tried to incorporate Emerson’s direct words, they were able to summarize the main points in their own words that better fit into the paragraph.
college-writing-012204.zh: 尽管学生本可以尝试将爱默生的直接词汇入进来，但他们能够用自己的话来总结更适合段落的主要观点。

college-writing-012205.en: While it is best to incorporate your research within your paragraph, it is sometimes necessary to use a quotation that is longer than four lines.
college-writing-012205.zh: 虽然最好将您的研究纳入您的段落，但有时需要使用超过四行的引文。

college-writing-012206.en: In this case, you will need to block your quotation.
college-writing-012206.zh: 在这种情况下，您将需要阻止您的报价。

college-writing-012207.en: However, you should use block quotations sparingly because they don’t often fit within the flow of your essay.
college-writing-012207.zh: 但是，您应该谨慎使用块引用，因为它们通常不适合您论文的流程。

college-writing-012209.en: Original quotation: “For nonconformity the world whips you with its displeasure. And therefore a man must know how to estimate a sour face. The by-standers look askance on him in the public street or in the friend’s parlor. If this aversion had its origin in contempt and resistance like his own he might well go home with a sad countenance . . .” (Emerson 649)
college-writing-012209.zh: 原文：“因为不符合你的不满，世界用不满来鞭打你。因此，一个人必须知道如何估计酸味的脸。旁观者在公共街道或朋友的客厅里对他不屑一顾。如果这种厌恶起源于蔑视 和他自己的抵抗力一样，他很可能带着悲伤的面容回家……” 第649章

college-writing-012210.en: Student’s Paragraph Using Short Quotation and Summary
college-writing-012210.zh: 学生的段落使用简短的报价和摘要

college-writing-012211.en: A person who seeks the accomplishment embodied by the American Dream must be ready to tear barriers and stand proudly above the masses.
college-writing-012211.zh: 一个寻求美国梦所体现的成就的人必须准备好撕毁障碍并自豪地站在群众之上。

college-writing-012212.en: A vast majority of the time when someone attempts to carve out a path in society, many critics and skeptics will attempt to deter that person from moving forward.
college-writing-012212.zh: 绝大多数时候，当有人试图在社会上开辟道路时，许多批评者和怀疑论者会试图阻止那个人前进。

college-writing-012213.en: According to Ralph Waldo Emerson, a noted American essayist from the 1800s, “[f]or nonconformity the world whips you with its displeasure” (649).
college-writing-012213.zh: 根据 1800 年代著名的美国散文家拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生 (Ralph Waldo Emerson) 的说法，“[f] 或不符合你的世界以其不满来鞭打你”（649）。

college-writing-012214.en: In the early 1980s, Steve Jobs had a revolutionary idea—that idea was to make computers easier to use by using a simple visual interface with a mouse.
college-writing-012214.zh: 在 1980 年代初期，史蒂夫·乔布斯有一个革命性的想法——这个想法是通过使用带有鼠标的简单可视化界面使计算机更容易使用。

college-writing-012215.en: Many dismissed the idea, and it was not initially successful.
college-writing-012215.zh: 许多人驳回了这个想法，但最初并没有成功。

college-writing-012216.en: Despite the critics, Jobs was not afraid to challenge the status quo and ignore the disbelievers; he went on to become one of the leaders of the computing world.
college-writing-012216.zh: 尽管受到批评，乔布斯并不害怕挑战现状并忽视不信道者。 他继续成为计算世界的领导者之一。

college-writing-012217.en: Those who dare to achieve the American Dream must be ready to wade through the sea of critics, and as Emerson asserts, ignore what others think or say of them, and no matter how hard it is, always speak their ideas (649).
college-writing-012217.zh: 那些敢于实现美国梦的人必须准备好在批评者的海洋中涉水，并且正如爱默生所断言的，忽略别人对他们的看法或所说的，无论多么困难，总是说出他们的想法（649）。

college-writing-012218.en: They must remain headstrong, dismiss the naysayers, and stray from the pack.
college-writing-012218.zh: 他们必须保持任性，解雇反对者，偏离人群。

college-writing-012219.en: Following is the paragraph that resulted from this student’s notes.
college-writing-012219.zh: 以下是本学生笔记产生的段落。

college-writing-012220.zh: 446 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012221.en: Citing Sources Format The model paper in this chapter shows acceptable formats for a research paper using the style recommended by the Modern Language Association (MLA).
college-writing-012221.zh: 引用来源格式 本章中的模型文件显示了使用现代语言协会推荐的风格的研究论文的可接受格式（MLA）。

college-writing-012222.en: Most English professors require this style.
college-writing-012222.zh: 大多数英语教授都需要这种风格。

college-writing-012223.en: However, if you are writing in another class, such as psychology, sociology, or one of the physical sciences, your instructor may require a different style.
college-writing-012223.zh: 但是，如果您在另一节课上写作，例如心理学、社会学或其中一门物理科学，您的教练可能需要不同的风格。

college-writing-012224.en: So, always check with your professor first.
college-writing-012224.zh: 所以，总是先和你的教授核实一下。

college-writing-012225.en: Documentation of Sources You must reveal the sources (books, articles, and so on) of borrowed information in your paper.
college-writing-012225.zh: 资料来源 您必须在论文中披露借用信息的来源（书籍、文章等）。

college-writing-012226.en: Whether you quote directly, or summarize ideas in your own words, you must acknowledge your sources.
college-writing-012226.zh: 无论您是直接引用还是用您自己的话总结想法，您都必须承认您的来源。

college-writing-012227.en: In the past, you may have used footnotes.
college-writing-012227.zh: 过去，您可能使用过脚注。

college-writing-012228.en: However, the MLA now requires a simpler form of documentation.
college-writing-012228.zh: 但是，MLA 现在需要更简单的文档形式。

college-writing-012229.en: Citations within a Paper When citing a source, you must mention the author’s name and the relevant page number.
college-writing-012229.zh: 论文中的引文 引用来源时，您必须提及作者的姓名和相关的页码。

college-writing-012230.en: The author’s name may appear either in the sentence you are writing or in parentheses following the sentence:
college-writing-012230.zh: 作者的姓名可能出现在您正在写的句子中，也可以出现在句子后面的括号中：

college-writing-012231.en: In The Way We Really Are, Stephanie Coontz writes, “Right up through the 1940s, ties of work, friendship, neighborhood, ethnicity, extended kin, and voluntary organizations were as important a source of identity for most Americans . . .” (37).
college-writing-012231.zh: 就我们的真实身份而言，斯蒂芬妮·康茨（Stephanie Coontz）写道：“直到 1940 年代，工作、友谊、邻里、种族、扩展亲属和志愿组织的联系对于大多数美国人来说也是身份的重要来源。” （37）。

college-writing-012232.zh: 学生的段落使用块引用

college-writing-012233.en: Keeping my priorities intact while in school has been more difficult than I thought.
college-writing-012233.zh: 在学校保持我的优先事项的完整性比我想象的要困难得多。

college-writing-012234.en: In Emerson’s essay “from Self-Reliance,” he asserts that society makes it difficult for a person to remain true to his or her own inner beliefs:
college-writing-012234.zh: 在艾默生的文章“来自自力更生”的文章中，他断言社会使一个人很难忠于自己的内在信念：

college-writing-012235.en: What I must do is all that concerns me, not what the people think.
college-writing-012235.zh: 我必须做的是所有让我关心的事情，而不是人们的想法。

college-writing-012236.en: This rule, equally arduous in actual and in intellectual life, may serve for the whole distinction between greatness and meanness.
college-writing-012236.zh: 这条规则在现实和智力生活中同样艰巨，可以用于整个伟大和卑鄙之间的区别。

college-writing-012237.en: It is the harder because you will always find those who think they know what is your duty better than you know it.
college-writing-012237.zh: 这更难，因为你总是会找到那些认为他们比你知道的更了解你的职责的人。

college-writing-012238.en: Knowing that even in the 1800s, society made it difficult for people to be true to their own selves, has made me realize that I’m not alone.
college-writing-012238.zh: 知道即使在 1800 年代，社会也让人们很难忠于自己，这让我意识到我并不孤单。

college-writing-012239.en: It has also made me more determined to keep my priorities straight and get the degree and career that I want, no matter what others may say.
college-writing-012239.zh: 这也让我更加坚定地保持我的优先事项并获得我想要的学位和职业，无论别人怎么说。

college-writing-012240.zh: 第19章 写一篇基于源的论文447

college-writing-012241.en: “Some . . . are looking for a way to reclaim family closeness in an increasingly fast-paced society. . . . Still others worry about unsavory influences in school—drugs, alcohol, sex, violence” (Kantrowitz and Wingert 66).
college-writing-012241.zh: “有些人……正在寻找一种方法，在一个节奏日益快的社会中恢复家庭亲密关系……还有一些人担心学校里的不良影响——毒品、酒精、性、暴力”（Kantrowitz 和 Wingert 66）。

college-writing-012242.en: There are several points to note about citations within the paper:
college-writing-012242.zh: 关于论文中的引文有几点需要注意：

college-writing-012243.en: • When the author’s name is provided in parentheses, only the last name is given.
college-writing-012243.zh: • 当在括号中提供作者姓名时，仅给出姓氏。

college-writing-012244.en: • There is no punctuation between the author’s name and the page number.
college-writing-012244.zh: • 作者姓名和页码之间没有标点符号。

college-writing-012245.en: • The parenthetical citation is placed after the borrowed material but before the period at the end of the sentence.
college-writing-012245.zh: • 括号引文位于借来的材料之后，但在句子结尾的句子之前。

college-writing-012246.en: • If you are using more than one work by the same author, include a shortened version of the title in the citation.
college-writing-012246.zh: • 如果您使用的是同一作者的不止一部作品，请在引文中包含标题的缩写版本。

college-writing-012247.en: For example, your citation for the quotation above would be (Coontz, Way We Really 39).
college-writing-012247.zh: 例如，您对上面引用的引用是（Coontz，Way we realing 39）。

college-writing-012248.en: Note that a comma appears between the author’s name and the title.
college-writing-012248.zh: 请注意，作者的姓名和标题之间会出现一个逗号。

college-writing-012250.en: in is used when citing a quotation from another source.
college-writing-012250.zh: 引用来自另一个来源的引用时使用 in。

college-writing-012251.en: For example, a quotation from Edward Wolff on page 2 of the paper was found in a book not by Wolff but by Sylvia Ann Hewlett and Cornel West.
college-writing-012251.zh: 例如，报纸第 2 页上的爱德华·沃尔夫 (Edward Wolff) 的引文是在一本不是 Wolff 的书中找到的，而是 Sylvia Ann Hewlett 和 Cornel West 的一本书。

college-writing-012253.en: Families have been feeling this loss of time for years but have been unable to describe it.
college-writing-012253.zh: 家庭多年来一直感受到这种时间的损失，但无法描述它。

college-writing-012254.en: The economist Edward Wolff explains the loss of time:
college-writing-012254.zh: 经济学家爱德华·沃尔夫解释了时间的损失：

college-writing-012255.en: Over a thirty-year time span, parental time has declined 13 percent.
college-writing-012255.zh: 在 30 年的时间跨度内，父母时间下降了 13%。

college-writing-012256.en: The time parents have available for their children has been squeezed by the rapid shift of mothers into the paid labor force, by escalating divorce rates and the subsequent abandonment of children by their fathers, and by an increase in the number of hours required on the job.
college-writing-012256.zh: 父母为孩子提供的时间因母亲的快速转变、离婚率的提高以及他们的父亲遗弃的孩子以及工作所需的小时数的增加而受到挤压。

college-writing-012257.en: The average worker is now at work 163 hours a year more than in 1969, which adds up to an extra month of work annually.
college-writing-012257.zh: 平均工人现在每年的工作时间比 1969 年多 163 小时，这增加了每年额外的一个月的工作。

college-writing-012258.zh: （在惠普和西部 48 中的 Qtd.）

college-writing-012259.en: Citations at the End of a Paper End your paper with a list of works cited that includes all the sources actually used in the paper.
college-writing-012259.zh: 在论文结尾处的引文结束了论文，并列出了引用的作品列表，其中包括论文中实际使用的所有来源。

college-writing-012260.en: (Don’t list other sources, no matter how many you have read.)
college-writing-012260.zh: （无论您阅读了多少内容，都不要列出其他来源。）

college-writing-012261.en: Look at the “Works Cited” page in the model research paper (in the next chapter) and note the following:
college-writing-012261.zh: 查看模型研究论文中的“作品引用”页面（在下一章中），并注意以下几点：

college-writing-012262.en: • The works-cited list begins on a new page, not on the last page of the paper’s text.
college-writing-012262.zh: • 作品被引用的列表从新页面开始，而不是在论文文本的最后一页上。

college-writing-012263.en: • Entries are organized alphabetically according to the authors’ last names.
college-writing-012263.zh: • 根据作者的姓氏按字母顺序组织条目。

college-writing-012265.en: • Entries are double-spaced, with no extra spaces between entries.
college-writing-012265.zh: • 条目是双倍行距的，条目之间没有额外的空格。

college-writing-012266.zh: 448 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012267.en: • After the first line of an entry, a half-inch indentation separates each additional line in that entry.
college-writing-012267.zh: • 在条目的第一行之后，半英寸的缩进将该条目中的每条附加行分开。

college-writing-012268.en: This arrangement is called a “hanging indent” in most formatting menus.
college-writing-012268.zh: 在大多数格式化菜单中，这种排列称为“悬挂缩进”。

college-writing-012269.en: • Italicize (do not underline) titles of books, periodicals, websites, and other independently published works.
college-writing-012269.zh: • 斜体化（不强调）书籍、期刊、网站和其他独立出版的作品的标题。

college-writing-012270.en: • Include a Digital Object Identifier or DOI (preferred, as it is permanently assigned to a source), a permalink, or a URL.
college-writing-012270.zh: • 包括数字对象标识符或 DOI（首选，因为它被永久分配给源）、固定链接或 URL。

college-writing-012271.en: Copy URLs in full from your browser.
college-writing-012271.zh: 从浏览器完整复制网址。

college-writing-012272.en: • If the date of publication includes a month, then abbreviate the month in your citation, except for the months of May, June, and July.
college-writing-012272.zh: • 如果出版日期包括一个月，那么在您的引文中缩写月份，5 月、6 月和 7 月的月份除外。

college-writing-012273.en: • When you are citing a Web page that has no publication date, you can include a date of access at the end of your citation.
college-writing-012273.zh: • 当您引用没有发布日期的网页时，您可以在引文结束时包含访问日期。

college-writing-012712.en: If you were to write a research essay on climate change, what would you focus on?
college-writing-012712.zh: 如果你要写一篇关于气候变化的研究论文，你会关注什么？

college-writing-012713.en: Climate change is too broad a topic to cover in one research paper.
college-writing-012713.zh: 气候变化是一个太广泛的主题，无法在一篇研究论文中涵盖。

college-writing-012714.en: You would need to select a more limited topic to write about, for example the effects of different types of farming on climate change.
college-writing-012714.zh: 您需要选择一个更有限的主题来写，例如不同类型的农业对气候变化的影响。

college-writing-012715.en: Looking at the above photographs, can you think of some other limited topics about climate change you might cover in a research paper?
college-writing-012715.zh: 看看上面的照片，你能想到一些你可能在研究论文中讨论的关于气候变化的其他有限话题吗？

college-writing-012717.en: This chapter will explain and illustrate • the major steps in writing a research paper: Step 1: Get started
college-writing-012717.zh: 本章将解释和说明 • 撰写研究论文的主要步骤： 第 1 步：开始

college-writing-012720.en: topic that you can readily research.
college-writing-012720.zh: 您可以随时研究的主题。

college-writing-012722.zh: 主题并明确您论文的目的。

college-writing-012724.en: and gather information on your limited topic.
college-writing-012724.zh: 并收集有关您有限主题的信息。

college-writing-012733.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-012737.en: Getting Started and Creating a Schedule

college-writing-012738.en: Writing a research essay will require you to be very organized in order to complete all the steps necessary in a timely fashion.
college-writing-012738.zh: 撰写研究论文将要求您非常有条理，以便及时完成所有必要的步骤。

college-writing-012739.en: Getting started is often the hardest part.
college-writing-012739.zh: 入门往往是最难的部分。

college-writing-012740.en: The inclination is that your paper isn’t due for several weeks, so there is no rush to begin.
college-writing-012740.zh: 倾向是你的论文有几个星期没有到期，所以没有急于开始。

college-writing-012741.en: This type of attitude can get you in trouble.
college-writing-012741.zh: 这种态度会让你陷入困境。

college-writing-012742.en: Instead, you should figure out your schedule and get started as soon as you have been assigned the paper.
college-writing-012742.zh: 相反，您应该弄清楚您的日程安排并在您被分配到论文后立即开始。

college-writing-012743.en: Creating an effective and realistic schedule is an important first step.
college-writing-012743.zh: 制定有效和现实的时间表是重要的第一步。

college-writing-012744.en: It is best to work backward from the date your paper is due.
college-writing-012744.zh: 最好从您的论文到期之日起倒退。

college-writing-012745.en: You should always build in more time than you think it will take and have a contingency plan that will allow you to handle unexpected interruptions and changes.
college-writing-012745.zh: 您应该始终建立比您想象的更多时间，并制定应急计划，让您处理意外的中断和变化。

college-writing-012746.en: At the end of this chapter is a model research essay that was written by a student, Jacob Lashley, for his English 101 class.
college-writing-012746.zh: 在本章的结尾是一篇由学生 Jacob Lashley 为他的英语 101 课写的模型研究论文。

college-writing-012747.en: His professor gave students three weeks to produce a rough draft with a due date of April 27, 2021, and a final draft due date of May 4, 2021.
college-writing-012747.zh: 他的教授给了学生三周的时间来制作草稿，截止日期为 2021 年 4 月 27 日，最终草稿截止日期为 2021 年 5 月 4 日。

college-writing-012748.en: Since Jacob knew time would be tight, he mapped out his schedule.
college-writing-012748.zh: 由于雅各布知道时间会很紧，他制定了他的日程安排。

college-writing-012749.en: First he filled in the due dates for the rough and final drafts.
college-writing-012749.zh: 首先，他填写了粗略和最终草稿的截止日期。

college-writing-012750.en: He then worked backward to create a timeline to keep on track.
college-writing-012750.zh: 然后，他向后工作以创建一个时间表以保持正轨。

college-writing-012751.en: He knew he would need as much time as possible to complete this task, so he built in quite a few weekend days.
college-writing-012751.zh: 他知道他需要尽可能多的时间来完成这项任务，所以他在几个周末的日子里都建成了。

college-writing-012752.en: A working version of his schedule is shown on the next page.
college-writing-012752.zh: 他的时间表的工作版本显示在下一页。

college-writing-012753.en: Writing a research essay will require many of the same skills as writing a sourcebased essay; however, it will also require good organization and time management.
college-writing-012753.zh: 撰写研究论文将需要许多与撰写基于源的论文相同的技能； 但是，它也需要良好的组织和时间管理。

college-writing-012754.en: Many students who are assigned research papers find themselves running out of time because they spend too many hours trying to gather research, reading the research, or changing the focus of their papers at the last minute.
college-writing-012754.zh: 许多被分配研究论文的学生发现自己的时间不多了，因为他们花了太多时间来收集研究、阅读研究或在最后一刻改变论文的重点。

college-writing-012755.en: This chapter will explain how to create a realistic schedule, organize your notes, and break down the writing of the essay into smaller, more manageable steps.
college-writing-012755.zh: 本章将解释如何创建一个现实的时间表，组织你的笔记，并将论文的写作分解成更小、更易于管理的步骤。

college-writing-012756.en: Selecting a Topic That You Can Readily Research
college-writing-012756.zh: 选择您可以随时研究的主题

college-writing-012757.en: Many professors will assign a topic, but if you need to select your own topic, you will want to add time in your research schedule to find one that interests you enough to work with for an extended period of time.
college-writing-012757.zh: 许多教授会分配一个主题，但如果您需要选择自己的主题，您将需要在您的研究时间表中添加时间，以找到您感兴趣的一个足够长的时间来使用。

college-writing-012758.en: Remember, if your professor has given you a list of topics to avoid, don’t waste your time trying to figure out a way to write about one of those topics.
college-writing-012758.zh: 请记住，如果您的教授给了您要避免的主题列表，请不要浪费时间试图找出写这些主题之一的方法。

college-writing-012759.en: To quickly find a topic that interests you and has enough material to work with, you should first consult your library resources.
college-writing-012759.zh: 要快速找到您感兴趣且有足够材料可供使用的主题，您应该首先咨询您的图书馆资源。

college-writing-012760.en: For example, if you initially choose the broad topic “climate change,” try to find at least three academic
college-writing-012760.zh: 例如，如果您最初选择广泛的主题“气候变化”，请尝试找到至少三个学术

college-writing-012761.zh: 462 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012763.en: These sources could be current science books or journal articles on climate change.
college-writing-012763.zh: 这些来源可能是当前有关气候变化的科学书籍或期刊文章。

college-writing-012764.en: For instance, when Jacob Lashley, author of the model research essay “Environmental Health,” visited his college library, he connected to EBSCOhost and typed “climate change” in the search box.
college-writing-012764.zh: 例如，当模型研究论文“环境健康”的作者 Jacob Lashley 访问他的大学图书馆时，他连接到 Ebscohost 并在搜索框中输入了“气候变化”。

college-writing-012765.en: In seconds, EBSCOhost came back with hundreds of hits─titles, publication information, and the complete text of articles about climate change.
college-writing-012765.zh: 在几秒钟内，Ebscohost 带着数百个热门歌曲回来了——标题、出版信息和关于气候变化的文章的全文。

college-writing-012766.en: If you decide you need more information and are planning to use the Internet, you don’t necessarily want to start with Google.
college-writing-012766.zh: 如果您决定需要更多信息并计划使用互联网，则不一定要从 Google 开始。

college-writing-012767.en: So many results will come back that you will not be able to work your way through them all in the time you have allotted for research.
college-writing-012767.zh: 如此多的结果会回来，以至于您将无法在您分配给研究的时间内完成所有这些工作。

college-writing-012768.en: As was discussed in Chapter 17, search engines like Google Scholar will enable you to search specific types of online sources.
college-writing-012768.zh: 正如第 17 章所讨论的，像 Google Scholar 这样的搜索引擎将使您能够搜索特定类型的在线资源。

college-writing-012769.en: This will prove a great time-saver for you as you gather your research.
college-writing-012769.zh: 当您收集您的研究时，这将证明您可以节省大量时间。

college-writing-012770.en: Limiting Your Topic and Making the Purpose of Your Paper Clear
college-writing-012770.zh: 限制您的主题并使论文的目的清晰

college-writing-012771.en: Like any paper that is source-based, a research essay should thoroughly develop a limited topic.
college-writing-012771.zh: 像任何基于来源的论文一样，研究论文应该彻底开发一个有限的主题。

college-writing-012772.en: Your paper’s length will determine how broad or narrow your topic will need to be.
college-writing-012772.zh: 您的论文长度将决定您的主题需要多宽或狭窄。

college-writing-012773.en: While a ten-page essay will allow you to address a broader topic than one that is four pages, you will still need to fully develop your argument and go beyond surface-level information.
college-writing-012773.zh: 虽然一篇十页的文章可以让您解决比四页更广泛的主题，但您仍然需要充分发展您的论点并超越表面层次的信息。

college-writing-012774.en: Therefore, as you read through books and

college-writing-012775.zh: 最终草案将于2021年5月4日到期

college-writing-012779.zh: 引用的作品 创建和选中

college-writing-012782.zh: 已创建和检查的参考书目

college-writing-012783.zh: 研究阅读和注释 2021年4月14日

college-writing-012790.en: articles, look for ways to limit your general topic.
college-writing-012790.zh: 文章，寻找限制您的一般主题的方法。

college-writing-012791.en: While you are doing this, you should also be thinking about your purpose─a working thesis─that will help you focus your essay.
college-writing-012791.zh: 在你这样做的时候，你也应该考虑你的目的——一个工作论文——它将帮助你集中你的论文。

college-writing-012792.en: One good way to do this is to question yourself as you are reading your material.
college-writing-012792.zh: 这样做的一种好方法是在阅读材料时质疑自己。

college-writing-012793.en: Consider what questions you find yourself asking as you read about the topic.
college-writing-012793.zh: 考虑您在阅读该主题时发现自己提出的问题。

college-writing-012794.en: Could one of these questions be turned into a working thesis?
college-writing-012794.zh: 可以将这些问题之一变成工作论文吗？

college-writing-012795.en: For instance, as Jacob read materials on the general topic “climate change,” he chose to limit his topic to ways in which the general population could make a positive impact on climate change.
college-writing-012795.zh: 例如，当 Jacob 阅读有关“气候变化”的一般主题的材料时，他选择将他的主题限制在一般人群可以对气候变化产生积极影响的方式上。

college-writing-012796.en: As he read, he found himself asking, “What are some of the causes of climate change?” and “What can people in developed countries do to offset climate change?”
college-writing-012796.zh: 当他读到时，他发现自己在问：“气候变化的一些原因是什么？” “发达国家的人可以做些什么来抵消气候变化？”

college-writing-012797.en: He then decided to limit his topic even further by focusing on the problem of food waste as a factor of climate change.
college-writing-012797.zh: 然后，他决定进一步限制他的主题，将食物浪费问题作为气候变化的一个因素。

college-writing-012798.en: A few other examples of limiting a research topic include:
college-writing-012798.zh: 限制研究主题的其他几个例子包括：

college-writing-012799.en: • narrowing the general topic “drug abuse” to “successful drug treatment programs for adolescents”
college-writing-012799.zh: • 将“药物滥用”的一般主题缩小到“成功的青少年药物治疗计划”

college-writing-012800.en: • or, refocusing a topic on conservation practices so that it is limited to controlling the overpopulation of deer in suburban areas.
college-writing-012800.zh: • 或者，将主题重新集中在保护实践上，使其仅限于控制郊区鹿群的人口过多。

college-writing-012801.en: Do not expect to limit your topic and make your purpose clear all at once.
college-writing-012801.zh: 不要期望限制您的主题并立即明确您的目的。

college-writing-012802.en: You may have to do quite a bit of reading as you work out a narrowed focus for your paper.
college-writing-012802.zh: 当你为你的论文设计一个狭窄的焦点时，你可能需要做很多阅读。

college-writing-012803.en: Note that many research essays have one of two general purposes: (1) to defend a point─for example, to provide evidence that elected officials should serve no more than a single term; or (2) to present information─for example, to discuss the effects of diet on heart disease.
college-writing-012803.zh: 请注意，许多研究论文有两个一般目的之一：（1）为一个观点辩护——例如，提供民选官员的任期不应超过一个任期的证据； 或 (2) 提供信息——例如，讨论饮食对心脏病的影响。

college-writing-012805.en: Once you have narrowed your topic, you should brainstorm what you already know about the topic.
college-writing-012805.zh: 一旦你缩小了你的主题，你应该集思广益你已经知道的关于这个话题的知识。

college-writing-012806.en: This will help you focus your research and save you time.
college-writing-012806.zh: 这将帮助您集中研究并节省时间。

college-writing-012807.en: For instance, as Jacob thought about his own lifestyle and how his habits contributed to climate change, he realized there were several changes he could make.
college-writing-012807.zh: 例如，当雅各布考虑自己的生活方式以及他的习惯如何导致气候变化时，他意识到他可以做出一些改变。

college-writing-012808.en: He spent time writing down things he knew he should be doing but wasn’t, and things he was doing but could be doing better.
college-writing-012808.zh: 他花时间写下他知道他应该做但没有做的事情，他正在做但可以做得更好的事情。

college-writing-012809.en: He also thought about how having an impact on climate change meant large-scale modifications in societal behavior, and how hard it might be to get people to make those changes.
college-writing-012809.zh: 他还考虑了对气候变化产生影响如何意味着社会行为的大规模修改，以及让人们做出这些改变的难度。

college-writing-012810.en: As he worked through his list, he realized that food waste was a large problem in developed economies and was something that the general population and industries could work together on to create positive change.
college-writing-012810.zh: 当他完成清单时，他意识到食物浪费是发达经济体的一个大问题，并且是普通民众和行业可以共同努力创造积极变革的问题。

college-writing-012811.en: Gathering Information on Your Limited Topic
college-writing-012811.zh: 收集有关您有限主题的信息

college-writing-012812.en: After limiting your topic and brainstorming what you already know, begin gathering relevant information.
college-writing-012812.zh: 在限制您的主题并集思广益之后，开始收集相关信息。

college-writing-012813.en: Remember that your time is limited, so you want to
college-writing-012813.zh: 记住你的时间是有限的，所以你想

college-writing-012814.zh: 464 第 3 部分研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012815.en: find the best sources in the shortest amount of time.
college-writing-012815.zh: 在最短的时间内找到最佳来源。

college-writing-012816.en: If you are having problems, a good resource is a reference librarian at your college who has the knowledge and skill set to point you in the right direction.
college-writing-012816.zh: 如果您有问题，一个好的资源是您大学的参考图书馆员，他有知识和技能，可以为您指明正确的方向。

college-writing-012817.en: A helpful way to proceed is to access your college library’s databases and catalog to find necessary resources.
college-writing-012817.zh: 一个有用的方法是访问大学图书馆的数据库和目录以找到必要的资源。

college-writing-012818.en: If you do find a book that you think will be relevant, you will want to request it as soon as possible so you have time to work with it.
college-writing-012818.zh: 如果您确实找到了一本您认为相关的书，您将希望尽快提出要求，以便您有时间使用它。

college-writing-012819.en: You will also want to start locating credible articles from the databases or the Internet.
college-writing-012819.zh: 您还需要开始从数据库或互联网中查找可靠的文章。

college-writing-012820.en: Don’t be tempted to save every article you find.
college-writing-012820.zh: 不要试图保存您找到的每篇文章。

college-writing-012821.en: Instead, as you locate articles, look at the subject headings in the catalog entry, skim the material, and save it or print it for further consideration only if you feel it will support your topic (or offer a good counterargument).
college-writing-012821.zh: 相反，当您找到文章时，请查看目录条目中的主题标题，浏览材料并保存或打印，仅当您觉得它会支持您的主题（或提供良好的反驳）时才进行进一步考虑。

college-writing-012822.en: Jacob had allotted only ten days to spend on research, so he used his first day to find potential articles.
college-writing-012822.zh: 雅各布只分配了十天的时间来研究，所以他用他的第一天来寻找潜在的文章。

college-writing-012823.en: As he skimmed through each article, he checked to see if it was general climate change information or related to food waste.
college-writing-012823.zh: 当他浏览每篇文章时，他检查了这是否是一般的气候变化信息或与食物浪费有关的信息。

college-writing-012824.en: If the article looked like it had potential, he quickly saved it to read for further consideration.
college-writing-012824.zh: 如果这篇文章看起来有潜力，他很快就把它保存下来以供进一步考虑。

college-writing-012825.en: Reading research material is not the same as reading a novel or magazine.
college-writing-012825.zh: 阅读研究材料与阅读小说或杂志不同。

college-writing-012826.en: Instead, you should read through the material once for an overview.
college-writing-012826.zh: 相反，您应该阅读一次材料以了解概述。

college-writing-012827.en: As you read through the first time, you will want to pay attention to any unfamiliar vocabulary, headings, and emphasized words.
college-writing-012827.zh: 当你第一次阅读时，你会想要关注任何不熟悉的词汇、标题和强调的单词。

college-writing-012828.en: During the second read, you should note areas that seem to work with your limited topic and create research questions to help you focus your essay.
college-writing-012828.zh: 在第二次阅读中，您应该注意似乎与您有限的主题相关的领域，并创建研究问题以帮助您集中论文。

college-writing-012829.en: Depending on your understanding, you may need a third read.
college-writing-012829.zh: 根据您的理解，您可能需要第三次阅读。

college-writing-012830.en: It is important that you allow yourself enough time to really focus on your research, but you don’t want to spend so much time on it that you run short on the time needed to outline, draft, and write your essay.
college-writing-012830.zh: 让自己有足够的时间真正专注于你的研究是很重要的，但你不想花太多时间在它上，以至于你会耗尽概述、起草和撰写论文所需的时间。

college-writing-012831.en: For instance, Jacob knew that he had limited his research time to ten days, so as he worked through his research, he continuously asked himself whether or not a particular source focused on his working thesis─ways that people can eliminate food waste to have an impact on climate change.
college-writing-012831.zh: 例如，雅各布知道他的研究时间限制在十天，所以在他完成他的研究时，他不断地问自己，一个特定的来源是否专注于他的工作论文——人们可以消除食物浪费以对气候变化产生影响的方法。

college-writing-012832.en: Knowing that he needed to address all sides of the issue, he didn’t automatically eliminate a source if it didn’t claim that food waste was a facet of climate change.
college-writing-012832.zh: 知道他需要解决问题的各个方面，如果没有声称食物浪费是气候变化的一个方面，他并没有自动消除来源。

college-writing-012833.en: He also knew that because he had a relatively brief amount of time to complete his research, any source that was unrelated to his limited topic should be set aside quickly so that he could move on to a new piece of research.
college-writing-012833.zh: 他也知道，因为他有相对较短的时间来完成他的研究，任何与他有限话题无关的来源都应该尽快搁置，这样他就可以继续进行一项新的研究。

college-writing-012834.en: Keeping Track of Your Sources and Taking Notes
college-writing-012834.zh: 跟踪您的来源并做笔记

college-writing-012835.en: As you are researching, you need to keep careful and thorough track of your sources.
college-writing-012835.zh: 在您研究的过程中，您需要仔细和彻底地跟踪您的来源。

college-writing-012836.en: As you learned in Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” doing this is important because you have to know where your information originates so
college-writing-012836.zh: 正如您在第 19 章“撰写基于来源的论文”中所学到的，这样做很重要，因为您必须知道您的信息的来源，因此

college-writing-012838.en: that you can cite it properly.

college-writing-012839.en: To keep track of your sources, you should create a working bibliography, a list of everything you have read and consulted.
college-writing-012839.zh: 为了跟踪您的来源，您应该创建一个有效的参考书目，列出您阅读和咨询的所有内容。

college-writing-012840.en: This should be formatted just as a “Works Cited” page is formatted.
college-writing-012840.zh: 这应该在“引用作品”页面的格式化时格式化。

college-writing-012841.en: If you printed any of your sources, you should staple documents to keep them organized, so the individual pages don’t get lost or mixed up.
college-writing-012841.zh: 如果您打印了任何来源，您应该将文档装订以保持它们井井有条，这样各个页面就不会丢失或混淆。

college-writing-012842.en: All print sources should be kept in a single folder that is dedicated to that writing assignment.
college-writing-012842.zh: 所有打印源都应保存在专用于该写作作业的单个文件夹中。

college-writing-012843.en: To keep electronic sources organized, save each source as a separate document, and store all sources in one folder that is dedicated to that writing assignment.
college-writing-012843.zh: 要使电子源井井有条，请将每个源保存为单独的文档，并将所有源存储在专用于该写作作业的一个文件夹中。

college-writing-012844.en: You will make use of your sources by creating a scratch outline and taking good notes in preparation for the writing of your essay.
college-writing-012844.zh: 您将通过创建草稿大纲并做好笔记来准备论文的写作，从而利用您的资源。

college-writing-012845.en: Chapter 19 provides detailed coverage of how to create a scratch outline and of the kinds of notes you should take.
college-writing-012845.zh: 第 19 章详细介绍了如何创建草稿大纲以及您应该做的各种笔记。

college-writing-012847.en: Many professors will require a research essay plan or a formal outline.
college-writing-012847.zh: 许多教授需要研究论文计划或正式大纲。

college-writing-012848.en: Both are extremely helpful as you write your essay, so even if your instructor doesn’t require an essay plan or a formal outline, you should consider creating one or both to help you focus your paper.
college-writing-012848.zh: 在您撰写论文时，两者都非常有帮助，因此即使您的教师不需要论文计划或正式大纲，您也应该考虑创建一个或两个以帮助您集中论文。

college-writing-012849.en: Both will build from your informal scratch outline, giving you a more thorough detailed road map.
college-writing-012849.zh: 两者都将根据您的非正式草稿大纲构建，为您提供更全面的详细路线图。

college-writing-012850.en: A detailed plan helps you figure out where your research will best fit into your essay before you even begin writing.
college-writing-012850.zh: 详细的计划可以帮助您在开始写作之前弄清楚您的研究最适合您的论文的位置。

college-writing-012851.en: Because a research essay plan includes the thesis statement and topic sentences, students can easily organize their research based upon the claims of each topic sentence.
college-writing-012851.zh: 由于研究论文计划包括中心论点句和主题句，因此学生可以根据每个主题句的主张轻松组织他们的研究。

college-writing-012852.en: Some students also find formal outlines to be helpful as a follow-up to a research essay plan because formal outlines include complete sentences and organize the information in a hierarchy.
college-writing-012852.zh: 一些学生还发现正式大纲可以作为研究论文计划的后续工作，因为正式的大纲包含完整的句子并以层次结构组织信息。

college-writing-012853.en: Formal outlines allow students to fully envision what their essay will look like.
college-writing-012853.zh: 正式的大纲允许学生充分想象他们的论文会是什么样子。

college-writing-012854.en: If you choose to create a formal outline, you can prepare either a topic outline (thesis plus supporting words and phrases) or a sentence outline (complete sentences).
college-writing-012854.zh: 如果您选择创建正式的大纲，您可以准备主题大纲（论文加上支持词和短语）或句子大纲（完整的句子）。

college-writing-012855.en: Formal outlines use roman numerals for first-level headings, capital letters for second-level headings, and Arabic numbers for third-level headings.
college-writing-012855.zh: 正式大纲使用罗马数字作为一级标题，大写字母表示二级标题，阿拉伯数字用于三级标题。

college-writing-012856.en: (See Chapter 2 for further discussion of formal outlines.)
college-writing-012856.zh: （有关正式大纲的进一步讨论，请参见第 2 章。）

college-writing-012857.en: After Jacob completed his scratch outline, he decided to use a research essay plan to help him organize his research.
college-writing-012857.zh: 雅各布完成了他的划痕大纲后，他决定使用研究论文计划来帮助他组织他的研究。

college-writing-012858.en: As he read through his notes, he determined where the information would best fit, and then he placed the quotes, paraphrases, and summaries under the topic sentences.
college-writing-012858.zh: 当他阅读他的笔记时，他确定了信息最适合的位置，然后他将引语、释义和摘要放在 主题句 下。

college-writing-012859.en: He included his citations just to make sure he didn’t accidentally forget to cite something when he began writing his essay.
college-writing-012859.zh: 他引用了他的引文，只是为了确保他在开始写论文时不会不小心忘记引用一些东西。

college-writing-012860.en: Working with such a plan offered him the chance to organize and reorganize his information and to start writing with a very clear purpose in mind.
college-writing-012860.zh: 制定这样的计划使他有机会组织和重组他的信息，并以非常明确的目的开始写作。

college-writing-012861.en: Jacob’s research essay plan also enabled him to work on his essay as the ideas developed.
college-writing-012861.zh: 雅各布的研究论文计划也使他能够随着想法的发展而撰写他的论文。

college-writing-012862.en: It wasn’t necessary for him to get his introduction completed before he could move on to the next paragraph, so he was able to avoid wasting time and
college-writing-012862.zh: 在他继续下一段之前，他没有必要完成他的介绍，这样他就可以避免浪费时间和

college-writing-012863.zh: 466 第 3 部分 研究、写作和记录

college-writing-012865.en: If he found himself stuck, he could move on to another point in the essay, then later go back to the area that was giving him difficulty.
college-writing-012865.zh: 如果他发现自己被卡住了，他可以继续文章中的另一个点，然后再回到给他带来困难的区域。

college-writing-012866.en: Once Jacob was finished with his rough draft, he created his Works Cited page.
college-writing-012866.zh: 雅各布完成他的草稿后，他创作了他的作品引用的页面。

college-writing-012867.en: To create a Works Cited page, go back to your working bibliography and check through your essay.
college-writing-012867.zh: 要创建作品引用页面，请返回您的工作参考书目并查看您的论文。

college-writing-012868.en: As you note a source that you used in your essay, check off that source on your bibliography.
college-writing-012868.zh: 当您注意到您在论文中使用的来源时，请在参考书目中检查该来源。

college-writing-012869.en: Once you have read through the essay and checked each source used, you can then refer to your notes to transfer the used sources into a Works Cited page.
college-writing-012869.zh: 一旦您阅读了论文并检查了使用的每个来源，您就可以参考您的笔记将使用的资源转移到引用的作品页面中。

college-writing-012870.en: This page will always be located at the end of your essay on a separate page.
college-writing-012870.zh: 此页面将始终位于文章末尾的单独页面上。

college-writing-012871.en: Throughout the process of writing your draft, your goal is to maintain unity and coherence and provide enough support to develop your thesis.
college-writing-012871.zh: 在撰写草稿的整个过程中，您的目标是保持统一和连贯性，并提供足够的支持来发展您的论文。

college-writing-012872.en: Before turning in your rough draft for peer or professor review, you should use the checklist at the back of this text to make sure that your essay follows all four bases of effective writing.
college-writing-012872.zh: 在上交同行或教授复习的草稿之前，您应该使用本文背面的清单，以确保您的文章遵循有效写作的所有四个基础。

college-writing-012874.en: Writing a research essay takes time and organization, and students should employ a good writing process and follow the steps laid out in this chapter.
college-writing-012874.zh: 撰写研究论文需要时间和组织，学生应该采用良好的写作过程并遵循本章中列出的步骤。

college-writing-012875.zh: 本节介绍 Jacob 的作品：他最初的草稿大纲、他的研究论文计划和他的完整书面论文，包括引用的作品。

college-writing-012880.zh: 在这个计划中，请注意雅各布在直接引用周围加了引号，以确保他在撰写论文时正确报告了他的信息。

college-writing-012882.zh: 当他组织他的研究时，他没有创造完整的句子，因为他专注于简单地组织他的想法。

college-writing-012883.en: He can make sure his sentences are complete as he writes his draft.
college-writing-012883.zh: 他可以在写草稿时确保他的句子是完整的。

college-writing-012884.en: By taking careful notes when he researched and carefully planning his essay development, Jacob ensured that he properly presented and cited his information to avoid possible plagiarism.
college-writing-012884.zh: 通过在研究和仔细规划他的论文开发时做仔细的记录，雅各布确保他正确呈现并引用了他的信息，以避免可能的抄袭。

college-writing-013342.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-013343.en: This chapter will explain two of the basic building blocks of English sentences: subjects and verbs.
college-writing-013343.zh: 本章将解释英语句子的两个基本组成部分：主语和动词。

college-writing-013345.en: auxiliary verbs: verbs that work with the main verb to make up the complete verb in a sentence; also called helping verbs.
college-writing-013345.zh: 辅助动词：与主动词一起使用以组成句子中完整动词的动词； 也称为帮助动词。

college-writing-013348.en: linking verbs: verbs that help describe a subject by connecting it to another word.
college-writing-013348.zh: 链接动词：通过将主语连接到另一个词来帮助描述主语的动词。

college-writing-013351.en: preposition: one of a group of words that precede a noun or pronoun and indicate direction, position, placement, duration, or another kind of connection to the other words in the sentence.
college-writing-013351.zh: 介词：名词或代词之前的一组单词中的一个，表示方向、位置、位置、持续时间或与句子中其他单词的其他类型的联系。

college-writing-013352.en: Examples: about, above, through, under, with.
college-writing-013352.zh: 示例：关于、上面、通过、下面、与。

college-writing-013353.en: subject: who or what a sentence speaks about; usually a noun or pronoun that acts, is acted upon, or is described.
college-writing-013353.zh: 主题：句子说的是谁或什么； 通常是作用、作用或描述的名词或代词。

college-writing-013356.en: verb: what the sentence says about the subject; a word that shows what a subject does or that helps describe the subject by linking it to an adjective.
college-writing-013356.zh: 动词：句子对主语的评价； 一个单词，它通过将主语与形容词联系起来来描述主语的作用或帮助描述主题。

college-writing-013359.en: Every sentence has a subject and a verb.
college-writing-013359.zh: 每个句子都有一个主语和一个动词。

college-writing-013360.en: Who or what the sentence speaks about is called the subject; what the sentence says about the subject is the verb.
college-writing-013360.zh: 句子说的是谁或什么被称为主语； 句子对主语的说法是动词。

college-writing-013361.en: In the following sentences, the subject is underlined once; the verb is underlined twice.
college-writing-013361.zh: 在以下句子中，主语被下划线一次； 动词加下划线两次。

college-writing-013364.en: Many people applied for the job.
college-writing-013364.zh: 许多人申请了这份工作。

college-writing-013366.zh: 第482章 第四部分句子技巧手册

college-writing-013367.en: A Simple Way to Find a Subject

college-writing-013368.en: If you ask who or what the sentence is about, your answer will be the subject.
college-writing-013368.zh: 如果你问这个句子是关于谁或什么的，你的答案将是主题。

college-writing-013369.en: Who is the first sentence about?

college-writing-013370.en: The boy What is the second sentence about?
college-writing-013370.zh: 男孩第二句话是关于什么的？

college-writing-013371.en: That fish Who is the third sentence about?
college-writing-013371.zh: 那条鱼是谁的第三句话？

college-writing-013372.en: Many people What is the fourth sentence about?
college-writing-013372.zh: 很多人的第四句是什么？

college-writing-013374.en: A Simple Way to Find a Verb

college-writing-013375.en: If you ask what the sentence says about the subject, your answer will be the verb.
college-writing-013375.zh: 如果你问句子对主语的含义，你的答案将是动词。

college-writing-013376.en: What does the first sentence say about the boy?
college-writing-013376.zh: 第一句话对男孩有什么看法？

college-writing-013378.en: What does the second sentence say about the fish?
college-writing-013378.zh: 第二句话对鱼有什么看法？

college-writing-013380.en: What does the third sentence say about the people?

college-writing-013382.en: What does the fourth sentence say about the show?
college-writing-013382.zh: 第四句话对节目有什么看法？

college-writing-013384.en: A second way to find the verb is to put I, you, we, he, she, it, or they in front of the word you think is a verb.
college-writing-013384.zh: 找到动词的第二种方法是将我、你、我们、他、她、它或它们放在你认为是动词的单词前面。

college-writing-013385.en: If the result makes sense, you have a verb.
college-writing-013385.zh: 如果结果有意义，你有一个动词。

college-writing-013386.en: For example, you could put he in front of cried in the first sentence, with the result, he cried, making sense.
college-writing-013386.zh: 例如，你可以把他放在第一句话的哭泣面前，结果，他哭了，有道理。

college-writing-013387.en: Thus, you know that cried is a verb.
college-writing-013387.zh: 因此，你知道哭泣是一个动词。

college-writing-013388.en: Also remember that most verbs show action.
college-writing-013388.zh: 还要记住，大多数动词都表现出动作。

college-writing-013389.en: In the sentences above, there are three action verbs: cried, smells, and applied.
college-writing-013389.zh: 在上面的句子中，有三个动作动词：哭泣、嗅觉和应用。

college-writing-013390.en: Other verbs, known as linking verbs, do not show action; they give information about the subject.
college-writing-013390.zh: 其他被称为链接动词的动词不显示动作； 他们提供有关该主题的信息。

college-writing-013391.en: In “The show is a documentary,” the linking verb is joins the subject (show) with a word that identifies or describes it (documentary).
college-writing-013391.zh: 在“节目是一部纪录片”中，链接动词 is 将主语（显示）与一个识别或描述它的词（文档）连接起来。

college-writing-013392.en: Other common linking verbs include am, are, was, were, feel, appear, and become.
college-writing-013392.zh: 其他常见的链接动词包括 am、are、ware、wares、weather、feel 、 exception 和 become。

college-writing-013556.en: This chapter will explain how to avoid the most common types of fragments.
college-writing-013556.zh: 本章将解释如何避免最常见的片段类型。

college-writing-013557.en: A fragment is a word group that lacks a subject or a verb and/or one that does not express a complete thought.
college-writing-013557.zh: 片段是缺少主语或动词和/或不表达完整思想的词组。

college-writing-013560.en: “Whenever,” a dependent word, cannot introduce a complete thought, so it cannot stand alone.
college-writing-013560.zh: “每当”，一个依赖的词，不能引入一个完整的思想，所以它不能独立存在。

college-writing-013562.en: Whenever I go to school, I take the bus.
college-writing-013562.zh: 每当我上学时，我就坐公共汽车。

college-writing-013563.en: The dependent word group is attached to a complete thought, so this is a full sentence.
college-writing-013563.zh: 依赖词组附加到一个完整的思想，所以这是一个完整的句子。

college-writing-013564.en: Every sentence must have a subject and a verb and must express a complete thought.
college-writing-013564.zh: 每个句子都必须有一个主语和一个动词，并且必须表达一个完整的思想。

college-writing-013565.en: A word group that lacks a subject or a verb and/or fails to express a complete thought is a fragment.
college-writing-013565.zh: 缺少主语或动词和/或未能表达完整思想的词组是片段。

college-writing-013566.en: Here are the most common types of fragments:
college-writing-013566.zh: 以下是最常见的片段类型：

college-writing-013572.en: Some word groups that begin with dependent words are fragments.
college-writing-013572.zh: 一些以依赖词开头的词组是片段。

college-writing-013573.en: When you start a sentence with a dependent word, be careful not to create a fragment.
college-writing-013573.zh: 当您以依赖单词开始句子时，请注意不要创建片段。

college-writing-013574.zh: 第490章 第四部分 句子技巧手册

college-writing-013576.en: after if, even if when, whenever although in order that where, wherever as since whether because that, so that which, whichever before unless while even though until who, whom, whose how what, whatever
college-writing-013576.zh: after：在……之后；if：如果；even if：即使；when：当……时；whenever：每当／无论何时；although：尽管；in order that：为了使；where：在……的地方；wherever：无论在哪里；as：当……时／因为；since：自从／因为；whether：是否；because：因为；that：引出从句的连接词；so that：以便／以致；which：哪一个／所指的事物；whichever：无论哪一个；before：在……之前；unless：除非；while：当……时／而；even though：即使／尽管；until：直到；who：谁（主格）；whom：谁（宾格）；whose：谁的；how：如何；what：什么／……的事物；whatever：无论什么。

college-writing-013577.en: Below, the word group beginning with after is a fragment:
college-writing-013577.zh: 下面，以after开头的单词组是一个片段：

college-writing-013578.zh: 在我兑现了我的薪水之后。

college-writing-013580.en: A dependent statement─one starting with a dependent word like after─cannot stand alone.
college-writing-013580.zh: 一个从属词开头的依赖性陈述——不能单独站立。

college-writing-013581.en: It depends on another statement to complete the thought.
college-writing-013581.zh: 这取决于另一个陈述来完成这个想法。

college-writing-013582.en: After I cashed my paycheck is a dependent statement.
college-writing-013582.zh: 在我兑现后，我的薪水是一份依赖报表。

college-writing-013584.en: We expect to find out, in the same sentence, what happened after the writer cashed the check.
college-writing-013584.zh: 我们希望在同一句话中找出作者兑现支票后发生的事情。

college-writing-013585.en: When a writer does not follow through and complete a thought, a fragment results.
college-writing-013585.zh: 当一个作家没有跟进并完成一个想法时，就会产生一个片段。

college-writing-013586.en: To correct the fragment, simply follow through and complete the thought:
college-writing-013586.zh: 要更正片段，只需遵循并完成想法：

college-writing-013587.en: After I cashed my paycheck, I treated myself to dinner.
college-writing-013587.zh: 在我兑现了我的薪水后，我请了自己吃晚饭。

college-writing-013588.en: Remember, then, that dependent statements by themselves are fragments.
college-writing-013588.zh: 那么，请记住，依赖性陈述本身就是片段。

college-writing-013589.en: They must be attached to a statement that makes sense standing alone.
college-writing-013589.zh: 他们必须依附于一个有意义的陈述。

college-writing-013590.en: Here are two other examples of dependent-word fragments:
college-writing-013590.zh: 以下是依赖词片段的其他两个示例：

college-writing-013593.en: The cat threw up the little rubber band.

college-writing-013595.en: Until I hear from you is a fragment; it does not make sense standing by itself.
college-writing-013595.zh: 直到我收到你的来信是一个片段； 自己站着没有意义。

college-writing-013596.en: We want to know in the same statement what until refers to.
college-writing-013596.zh: 我们想知道在同一个陈述中直到什么。

college-writing-013597.en: The writer must complete the thought.
college-writing-013597.zh: 作者必须完成这个想法。

college-writing-013598.en: Likewise, That it had swallowed recently is not in itself a complete thought.
college-writing-013598.zh: 同样，它最近吞下了它本身并不是一个完整的想法。

college-writing-013599.en: We want to know in the same statement what that refers to.
college-writing-013599.zh: 我们想在同一个陈述中知道它指的是什么。

college-writing-013600.en: Additional information about dependent words and phrases can be found in Chapter 5.
college-writing-013600.zh: 有关相关单词和短语的其他信息，请参见第 5 章。

college-writing-013601.en: In that chapter, dependent words are also referred to as subordinating words.
college-writing-013601.zh: 在那一章中，依赖词也被称为从属词。

college-writing-013602.en: How to Correct a Dependent-Word Fragment Often, you correct a dependent-word fragment by attaching it to the sentence that comes after it or to the one that comes before it.
college-writing-013602.zh: 如何更正一个依赖词片段 通常，您通过将依赖词片段附加到它之后的句子或它之前的句子中来纠正依赖词片段。

college-writing-013604.en: After I cashed my paycheck, I treated myself to dinner.
college-writing-013604.zh: 在我兑现了我的薪水后，我请了自己吃晚饭。

college-writing-013605.en: (The fragment has been attached to the sentence that comes after it.)
college-writing-013605.zh: （片段已附加到后面的句子上。）

college-writing-013606.en: The cat threw up the little rubber band that it had swallowed recently.
college-writing-013606.zh: 这只猫吐出了它最近吞下的小橡皮筋。

college-writing-013607.en: (The fragment has been attached to the sentence that comes before it.)
college-writing-013607.zh: （片段已附加到它之前的句子上。）

college-writing-013608.en: You can also connect a dependent-word fragment by removing the dependent word and rewriting the sentence:
college-writing-013608.zh: 您还可以通过删除依赖单词并重写句子来连接依赖单词片段：

college-writing-013609.en: I cashed my paycheck and then treated myself to dinner.
college-writing-013609.zh: 我兑现了我的薪水，然后请自己吃饭。

college-writing-013610.en: I will wait to hear from you.

college-writing-013612.en: Turn each of the following dependent-word groups into a sentence by adding a complete thought.
college-writing-013612.zh: 通过添加完整的想法将以下每个依赖词组转换为句子。

college-writing-013613.en: Use a comma after the dependent-word group if a dependent word starts the sentence.
college-writing-013613.zh: 如果从属单词开始句子，则在依赖词组后使用逗号。

college-writing-013616.zh: 在我成为素食主义者之前。

college-writing-013617.zh: 我的邻居在竞争中烧烤。

college-writing-013620.en: Before I became a vegetarian, I would eat fish four times a week.
college-writing-013620.zh: 在我成为素食主义者之前，我每周会吃四次鱼。

college-writing-013621.en: My neighbor who competitively barbeques has won several prizes.
college-writing-013621.zh: 我的竞争性烧烤邻居赢得了多个奖项。

college-writing-013623.en: Use a comma if a dependent-word group comes at the beginning of a sen-
college-writing-013623.zh: 如果从属词组出现在 sense 的开头，则使用逗号

college-writing-013624.en: tence, but not generally if it comes at the end of a sentence.
college-writing-013624.zh: tence，但一般情况下，如果它出现在句子的末尾。

college-writing-013625.en: Comma: After I cashed my paycheck, I treated myself to dinner.
college-writing-013625.zh: 逗号：兑现薪水后，我请自己吃饭。

college-writing-013626.en: No comma: I won’t leave the house until I hear from you.
college-writing-013626.zh: 没有逗号：在收到您的来信之前，我不会离开家。

college-writing-013628.en: Sometimes who, that, which, or where appear not at the very start but near
college-writing-013628.zh: 有时谁、那个、哪个或在哪里出现不是在开始时而是接近

college-writing-013629.en: the start of a word group.

college-writing-013631.en: I drove slowly past the old brick house.

college-writing-013632.en: The place where I grew up.

college-writing-013633.en: The place where I grew up is not a complete thought.
college-writing-013633.zh: 我长大的地方不是一个完整的想法。

college-writing-013634.en: We want to know in the same statement where was the place?
college-writing-013634.zh: 我们想知道在同一个陈述中那个地方在哪里？

college-writing-013635.en: To correct the fragment, attach it to the sentence that came before:
college-writing-013635.zh: 要更正片段，请将其附加到前面的句子：

college-writing-013636.en: I drove slowly past the old brick house, the place where I grew up.
college-writing-013636.zh: 我慢慢地经过旧砖房，我长大的地方。

college-writing-013638.zh: 第492章 第四部分句子技巧手册

college-writing-013639.en: 2. Although I had studied for several hours.
college-writing-013639.zh: 2. 虽然我已经学习了几个小时。

college-writing-013640.en: 3. Because I had just gotten paid.

college-writing-013643.en: Underline the dependent-word fragment in each item.
college-writing-013643.zh: 在每个项目中的依赖词片段下划线。

college-writing-013644.en: Then rewrite the items, correcting each fragment by attaching it to the sentence that comes before or the sentence that comes after it─whichever sounds more natural.
college-writing-013644.zh: 然后重写项目，将每个片段附加到前面的句子或后面的句子——以更自然的方式纠正每个片段。

college-writing-013645.en: Use a comma after the dependent-word group if it starts the sentence.
college-writing-013645.zh: 如果从依赖词组开始句子，则使用逗号。

college-writing-013646.en: 1. My cat flattens herself and tries to get out of the room.
college-writing-013646.zh: 1. 我的猫把自己压扁并试图离开房间。

college-writing-013647.en: Whenever I turn on the vacuum.

college-writing-013648.en: Apparently, she thinks something is coming to eat her.
college-writing-013648.zh: 显然，她认为有什么东西要吃她。

college-writing-013649.en: 2. Philadelphia was originally a Quaker colony.
college-writing-013649.zh: 2. 费城最初是一个贵格会殖民地。

college-writing-013650.en: That was founded by William Penn in 1681.

college-writing-013651.en: By 1777, it had become the capital of the new United States.
college-writing-013651.zh: 到 1777 年，它已成为新美国的首都。

college-writing-013652.en: 3. Sakinah is the manager of the new neighborhood garden.
college-writing-013652.zh: 3. Sakinah 是新社区花园的经理。

college-writing-013653.en: That was started to encourage people to grow their own food.
college-writing-013653.zh: 这开始鼓励人们种植自己的食物。

college-writing-013654.en: She has been making sure everyone is using only organic products.
college-writing-013654.zh: 她一直在确保每个人都只使用有机产品。

college-writing-013655.en: 4. Since Connor first began watching NOVA.
college-writing-013655.zh: 4. 自从康纳第一次开始观看 Nova。

college-writing-013656.en: He has been fascinated with space travel.
college-writing-013656.zh: 他一直对太空旅行着迷。

college-writing-013657.en: He has decided to become an astronaut.
college-writing-013657.zh: 他决定成为一名宇航员。

college-writing-013660.en: 5. Roman law was first recorded in 450 b.c. in what was known as the “twelve tablets.”
college-writing-013660.zh: 5. 罗马法首次记录于公元前 450 年。 在所谓的“十二个平板电脑”中。

college-writing-013662.en: Until the fall of the eastern Roman Empire nearly 2,000 years later.
college-writing-013662.zh: 直到近 2000 年后的东罗马帝国灭亡。

college-writing-013664.en: When an -ing word appears at or near the start of a word group, a fragment may result.
college-writing-013664.zh: 当单词出现在单词组的开头或附近时，可能会产生一个片段。

college-writing-013665.en: Such fragments often lack a subject and part of the verb.
college-writing-013665.zh: 这样的片段通常缺乏动词的主语和一部分。

college-writing-013666.en: In the items below, underline the word groups that contain -ing words.
college-writing-013666.zh: 在下面的项目中，在包含 -ing 单词的单词组中下划线。

college-writing-013668.en: 1. Enola walked all over the neighborhood yesterday.
college-writing-013668.zh: 1. Enola 昨天走遍了整个街区。

college-writing-013669.en: Trying to find her dog Bo.

college-writing-013670.en: Several people claimed they had seen him only hours before.
college-writing-013670.zh: 有几个人声称他们在几个小时前见过他。

college-writing-013671.en: 2. We sat back to watch the movie.

college-writing-013673.en: To our surprise, we clapped, cheered, and cried for the next two hours.
college-writing-013673.zh: 令我们惊讶的是，我们在接下来的两个小时里鼓掌、欢呼和哭泣。

college-writing-013675.en: It being the day before our wedding anniversary.
college-writing-013675.zh: 这是我们结婚纪念日的前一天。

college-writing-013676.en: I knew my wife would be surprised to receive a dozen heart-shaped balloons.
college-writing-013676.zh: 我知道我的妻子会惊讶地收到十几个心形气球。

college-writing-013677.en: People sometimes write -ing fragments because they think that the subject of one sentence will work for the next word group as well.
college-writing-013677.zh: 人们有时会写片段，因为他们认为一个句子的主题也适用于下一个单词组。

college-writing-013678.en: Thus, in item 1 the writer thinks that the subject Enola in the opening sentence will also serve as the subject for Trying to find her dog Bo.
college-writing-013678.zh: 因此，在第 1 项中，作者认为开头句子中的主题 enola 也将作为试图找到她的狗博的主题。

college-writing-013679.en: But the subject must be in the same sentence.
college-writing-013679.zh: 但主语必须在同一个句子中。

college-writing-013681.en: 1. Attach the fragment to the sentence that comes before it or to the sentence that comes after it, whichever makes sense.
college-writing-013681.zh: 1. 将片段附加到前面的句子或后面的句子上，以任何有意义的方式。

college-writing-013682.en: Item 1 could read, “Enola walked all over the neighborhood yesterday trying to find her dog Bo.”
college-writing-013682.zh: 第 1 项可以写道：“昨天，Enola 走遍了附近，试图找到她的狗博。”

college-writing-013683.en: 2. Add a subject and change the -ing verb part to the correct form of the verb.
college-writing-013683.zh: 2. 添加主语并将 -ing 动词部分更改为动词的正确形式。

college-writing-013684.en: Item 2 could read, “We didn’t expect anything special.”
college-writing-013684.zh: 第 2 项可以读到：“我们没想到有什么特别之处。”

college-writing-013685.en: 3. Change being to the correct form of the verb be (am, are, is, was, were).
college-writing-013685.zh: 3. 改变存在到动词 be (am, are, is, was, ware) 的正确形式。

college-writing-013686.en: Item 3 could read, “It was the day before our wedding anniversary.”
college-writing-013686.zh: 第3项可以是：“那是我们结婚纪念日的前一天。”

college-writing-013687.en: How to Correct to Fragments When to appears at or near the start of a word group, a fragment sometimes results:
college-writing-013687.zh: 如何在单词组的开头或附近出现碎片时更正片段，有时会产生一个片段：

college-writing-013688.en: At the Chinese restaurant, Jacy used chopsticks.

college-writing-013689.zh: 给他的约会留下深刻印象。

college-writing-013690.en: He spent one hour eating a small bowl of rice.
college-writing-013690.zh: 他花了一个小时吃一小碗米饭。

college-writing-013691.zh: 494 第四部分 句子技巧手册

college-writing-013692.en: The second word group is a fragment and can be corrected by adding it to the preceding sentence:
college-writing-013692.zh: 第二个单词组是一个片段，可以通过将其添加到前面的句子中进行校正：

college-writing-013693.en: At the Chinese restaurant, Jacy used chopsticks to impress his date.
college-writing-013693.zh: 在中餐厅，杰西用筷子给他的约会对象留下了深刻的印象。

college-writing-013694.en: Underline the -ing fragment in each of the following items.
college-writing-013694.zh: 在以下每个项目中的 -ing 片段下划线。

college-writing-013695.en: Then correct the item by using the method described in parentheses.
college-writing-013695.zh: 然后使用括号中描述的方法更正项目。

college-writing-013697.en: Including the Arctic Ocean and parts of Canada, the United States, and other countries.
college-writing-013697.zh: 包括北冰洋和部分加拿大、美国和其他国家。

college-writing-013698.en: The Arctic Circle is the area that surrounds the Earth’s North Pole.
college-writing-013698.zh: 北极圈是环绕地球北极的区域。

college-writing-013699.en: (Add the fragment to the sentence that comes after it.)
college-writing-013699.zh: （将片段添加到后面的句子中。）

college-writing-013700.en: 1. Ramses II ruled over Egypt from 1279 to 1212 b.c. Making his country stronger than ever before.
college-writing-013700.zh: 1. 拉美西斯二世在公元前 1279 年至 1212 年统治埃及。 让他的国家比以往任何时候都强大。

college-writing-013701.en: He was both ambitious and intelligent.

college-writing-013702.en: (Add the fragment to the preceding sentence.)

college-writing-013703.en: 2. A noisy fire truck suddenly raced down the street.
college-writing-013703.zh: 2. 一辆吵闹的消防车突然跑到街上。

college-writing-013704.en: Coming to a stop at my house.

college-writing-013705.en: My home security system had sent a false alarm.
college-writing-013705.zh: 我的家庭安全系统发出了误报。

college-writing-013706.en: (Correct the fragment by adding the subject it and changing coming to the proper form of the verb, came.)
college-writing-013706.zh: （通过添加主语 it 并改变来词的正确形式来纠正片段，来了。）

college-writing-013707.en: 3. I couldn’t find any books on Egyptian history in the library.
college-writing-013707.zh: 3. 我在图书馆找不到任何关于埃及历史的书籍。

college-writing-013708.en: They had all been checked out.

college-writing-013709.en: The reason for this being that a research paper had just been assigned to students in an ancient history class.
college-writing-013709.zh: 这样做的原因是刚刚为古代历史课上的学生分配了一篇研究论文。

college-writing-013710.en: (Correct the fragment by changing being to the proper form of the verb, was.)
college-writing-013710.zh: （通过将存在改变为动词的正确形式来纠正片段，是。）

college-writing-013711.en: Underline the -ing or to fragment in each item.
college-writing-013711.zh: 在每个项目中下划线或到碎片。

college-writing-013712.en: Then rewrite each item, correcting the fragment by using one of the three methods described above.
college-writing-013712.zh: 然后重写每个项目，使用上述三种方法之一来更正片段。

college-writing-013713.en: 1. Knowing she had not finished the book.
college-writing-013713.zh: 1. 知道她还没有读完这本书。

college-writing-013714.en: Madelyn was very nervous about going to class.
college-writing-013714.zh: 玛德琳对去上课很紧张。

college-writing-013715.en: She was sure the teacher was going to give a quiz.
college-writing-013715.zh: 她确信老师会做一个测验。

college-writing-013717.en: the Arctic Circle is the area that surrounds the Earth’s North Pole.
college-writing-013717.zh: 北极圈是环绕地球北极的区域。

college-writing-013719.en: Including the Arctic Ocean and parts of Canada, the United States, and other countries,
college-writing-013719.zh: 包括北冰洋和部分加拿大、美国和其他国家，

college-writing-013721.zh: 2. 我雇了一些青少年邻居。

college-writing-013722.en: To mow my lawn and weed the garden.
college-writing-013722.zh: 修剪我的草坪并除草花园。

college-writing-013723.en: They have been doing a great job.

college-writing-013724.en: 3. Searching for the right filament for his incandescent light bulb.
college-writing-013724.zh: 3. 为他的白炽灯泡寻找正确的灯丝。

college-writing-013725.en: Thomas Edison (1847–1931) found that a strip of carbonized bamboo could glow for 1,200 hours.
college-writing-013725.zh: 托马斯·爱迪生 (Thomas Edison) (1847–1931) 发现一条碳化竹条可以发光 1,200 小时。

college-writing-013726.en: 4. Estevo and Bryson have been friends since first grade.
college-writing-013726.zh: 4. Estevo 和 Bryson 从一年级开始就是朋友。

college-writing-013727.en: Graduating from high school this May.

college-writing-013728.en: 5. Sofia Vergara cofounded EBY with Renata Black.
college-writing-013728.zh: 5. Sofia Vergara 与 Renata Black 共同创立了 Eby。

college-writing-013729.en: Their company donates 10 percent of the profits to the Seven Bar Foundation.
college-writing-013729.zh: 他们的公司将利润的 10% 捐赠给七酒吧基金会。

college-writing-013730.en: Providing small business loans to women around the world.
college-writing-013730.zh: 为世界各地的女性提供小企业贷款。

college-writing-013732.en: Added-detail fragments lack a subject and a verb.
college-writing-013732.zh: 添加的细节片段缺少主语和动词。

college-writing-013733.en: They often begin with one of the following words:
college-writing-013733.zh: 它们通常以以下单词之一开头：

college-writing-013734.en: also especially except for example like including such as
college-writing-013734.zh: 特别是除了像包括这样的

college-writing-013735.en: Underline the one added-detail fragment in each of the following items:
college-writing-013735.zh: 在以下每个项目中的一个添加的细节片段下划线：

college-writing-013736.en: 1. Before a race, I eat starchy foods.
college-writing-013736.zh: 1. 比赛前，我吃淀粉类食物。

college-writing-013738.zh: 碳水化合物提供快速能量。

college-writing-013739.en: 2. Ana is taking a night course in auto mechanics.
college-writing-013739.zh: 2. Ana 正在参加汽车机械师的夜间课程。

college-writing-013741.en: She wants to save money on household repairs.
college-writing-013741.zh: 她想在家庭维修上省钱。

college-writing-013742.en: 3. My son keeps several pets in his room.
college-writing-013742.zh: 3. 我儿子在他的房间里养了几只宠物。

college-writing-013744.en: People often write added-detail fragments for much the same reason they write -ing fragments.
college-writing-013744.zh: 人们经常出于与编写片段的原因大致相同的原因编写附加细节片段。

college-writing-013745.en: They think the subject and verb in one sentence will serve for the next word group.
college-writing-013745.zh: 他们认为一个句子中的主语和动词将用于下一个单词组。

college-writing-013746.en: But the subject and verb must be in each word group.
college-writing-013746.zh: 但是主语和动词必须在每个单词组中。

college-writing-013747.zh: 496 第四部分 句子技巧手册

college-writing-013748.zh: 如何纠正添加的细节片段

college-writing-013749.en: 1. Attach the fragment to the complete thought that precedes it.
college-writing-013749.zh: 1. 将片段附加到它之前的完整思想上。

college-writing-013750.en: Item 1 could read “Before a race, I eat starchy foods such as bread and spaghetti.”
college-writing-013750.zh: 项目 1 可以读到“在比赛之前，我吃面包和意大利面等淀粉类食物。”

college-writing-013751.en: 2. Add a subject and a verb to the fragment to make it a complete sentence.
college-writing-013751.zh: 2. 在片段中添加一个主语和一个动词，使其成为一个完整的句子。

college-writing-013752.en: Item 2 could read “Ana is taking a night course in auto mechanics. Also, she is taking one in plumbing.”
college-writing-013752.zh: 项目2可以是“安娜正在参加汽车机械师的夜间课程。而且，她正在管道中学习。”

college-writing-013753.en: 3. Insert the fragment within the preceding sentence.
college-writing-013753.zh: 3. 在前面的句子中插入片段。

college-writing-013754.en: Item 3 could read “My son keeps several pets, including hamsters and mice, in his room.”
college-writing-013754.zh: 项目 3 可以写着“我的儿子在他的房间里养了几只宠物，包括仓鼠和老鼠。”

college-writing-013755.en: Underline the fragment in each of the following items.
college-writing-013755.zh: 在以下每个项目中的片段下划线。

college-writing-013984.en: In this text, the term “run-on” refers to both comma splices and fused sentences.

college-writing-013993.en: fused sentence: a run-on with no punctuation to mark the break between thoughts.

college-writing-013998.en: independent clause: a group of words having a subject and a verb that expresses a complete thought and is able to stand alone.
college-writing-013998.zh: 独立分句：一组单词，具有主语和动词，表达完整的思想，能够独立存在。

college-writing-014000.en: A run-on consists of two complete thoughts run together without adequate punctuation to signal the break between them.
college-writing-014000.zh: 一个连续的想法由两个完整的想法组成，没有足够的标点符号来表示它们之间的中断。

college-writing-014001.en: * There are two types of run-ons: fused sentences and comma splices.
college-writing-014001.zh: * 有两种类型的运行：无标点粘连句 和 逗号误接。

college-writing-014002.en: *Some instructors regard all run-ons as fused sentences.
college-writing-014002.zh: *一些教官将所有跑动视为 无标点粘连句。

college-writing-014003.en: But for many other instructors, and for our purposes in this book, the term run-on applies equally to fused sentences and comma splices.
college-writing-014003.zh: 但对于许多其他讲师，以及我们在本书中的目的，这个术语同样适用于 无标点粘连句 和 逗号误接。

college-writing-014004.en: The bottom line is that you do not want either fused sentences or comma splices in your writing.
college-writing-014004.zh: 最重要的是，您在写作中不希望 无标点粘连句 或 逗号误接。

college-writing-014005.en: Some instructors refer to each complete thought in a run-on as an independent clause.
college-writing-014005.zh: 一些讲师将每一个完整的想法称为 独立分句。

college-writing-014006.en: A clause is simply a group of words having a subject and a verb.
college-writing-014006.zh: 一个从句只是一组具有主语和动词的单词。

college-writing-014007.en: A clause may be independent (expressing a complete thought and able to stand alone) or dependent (not expressing a complete thought and not able to stand alone).
college-writing-014007.zh: 一个从句可以是独立的（表达一个完整的思想并能够独立存在）或依赖（不表达完整的思想，无法独立存在）。

college-writing-014008.en: Using this terminology, we’d say that a run-on is two independent clauses run together with no adequate sign given to mark the break between them.
college-writing-014008.zh: 使用这个术语，我们会说一个连续运行是两个 独立分句 一起运行，没有足够的符号来标记它们之间的中断。

college-writing-014009.en: Chapter 5, “The Fourth Step in Essay Writing,” demonstrates how to take simple sentences and make them compound or complex sentences without creating run-ons.
college-writing-014009.zh: 第 5 章，“论文写作的第四步”，演示了如何在不产生连续性的情况下采用简单的句子并使它们复合或复杂的句子。

college-writing-014019.zh: 两个完整的想法之间需要更强、更清晰的标记

college-writing-014291.en: This chapter will review the principal characteristics of regular and irregular verbs.
college-writing-014291.zh: 本章将回顾规则和不规则动词的主要特征。

college-writing-014293.en: irregular verb: a verb that has an irregular form in the past tense and past participle.
college-writing-014293.zh: 不规则动词：在过去时和过去分词中具有不规则形式的动词。

college-writing-014294.en: For example, choose becomes chose or chosen.
college-writing-014294.zh: 例如，选择变成选择或选择。

college-writing-014295.en: past participle: one of the principal parts of every verb; formed by adding -d or -ed to the present; used with the helping verbs have, has, or had, or with a form of be (with passive verbs).
college-writing-014295.zh: 过去分词：每个动词的主要部分之一； 通过向现在添加 -d 或 -ed 形成； 与帮助动词一起使用有、有或有或与某种形式的 be（被动动词）一起使用。

college-writing-014296.en: present participle: one of the principal parts of every verb; formed by adding -ing to the present.
college-writing-014296.zh: 现在分词：每个动词的主要部分之一； 通过向现在添加 -ing 形成。

college-writing-014297.en: principal parts of verbs: the four parts of every verb: present, past, past participle, and present participle.
college-writing-014297.zh: 动词的主要部分：每个动词的四个部分：现在、过去、过去分词和现在分词。

college-writing-014298.en: verb tense: the times shown by verbs: present, past, and future.
college-writing-014298.zh: 动词时态：动词显示的时间：现在、过去和未来。

college-writing-014299.en: Regular Verbs A Brief Review of Regular Verbs Every verb has four principal parts: present, past, past participle, and present participle.
college-writing-014299.zh: 常规动词 普通动词的简要回顾 每个动词都有四个主要部分：现在、过去、过去分词和现在分词。

college-writing-014300.en: These parts can be used to build all the verb tenses─ the times shown by verbs.
college-writing-014300.zh: 这些部分可用于构建所有动词时态——动词显示的时间。

college-writing-014301.en: Most verbs in English are regular.
college-writing-014301.zh: 英语中的大多数动词都是规则的。

college-writing-014302.en: The past and the past participle of regular verbs are formed by adding -d or -ed to the present.
college-writing-014302.zh: 正则动词的过去和过去分词是通过将 -d 或 -ed 添加到现在来形成的。

college-writing-014303.en: The past participle is the form of the verb used with the helping verbs have, has, or had (or some form of be with passive verbs).
college-writing-014303.zh: 过去分词是与助词一起使用的动词的形式（或某种形式的被动动词）。

college-writing-014304.en: The present participle is formed by adding -ing to the present.
college-writing-014304.zh: 当前分词是通过向现在添加 -ing 形成的。

college-writing-014305.en: For a more in-depth look at verb tense and helping verbs, refer to Chapters 25 and 26.

college-writing-014475.en: Subject–verb agreement is the correspondence in number between the subject and the verb of a sentence; plural subjects take plural verbs, and singular subjects take singular verbs.
college-writing-014475.zh: 主语-动词一致性是句子的主语和动词之间的对应关系； 复数主语取复数动词，单数主语取单数动词。

college-writing-014476.en: This chapter will review the necessity for subject–verb agreement.

college-writing-014486.en: Many indefinite pronouns (such as one, nobody, nothing, and each) take a singular verb; others, such as both or few, take plural verbs.
college-writing-014486.zh: 许多不定的代词（例如一个、无人、无、无，每个）采用单数动词； 其他人，例如两者或少，都采用复数动词。

college-writing-014487.en: A verb must agree with its subject in number.
college-writing-014487.zh: 动词必须在数量上与其主语一致。

college-writing-014488.en: A singular subject (one person or thing) takes a singular verb.
college-writing-014488.zh: 单数主语（一个人或事物）采用单数动词。

college-writing-014489.en: A plural subject (more than one person or thing) takes a plural verb.
college-writing-014489.zh: 复数主语（不止一个人或事物）采用复数动词。

college-writing-014490.en: Mistakes in subject–verb agreement are sometimes made in the following situations:
college-writing-014490.zh: 在以下情况下，有时会犯主语-动词一致性的错误：

college-writing-014491.en: 1. When words come between the subject and the verb
college-writing-014491.zh: 1. 当主语和动词之间出现单词时

college-writing-014492.zh: 2. 当动词出现在主语之前

college-writing-014495.en: Each of these situations is explained in this chapter.
college-writing-014495.zh: 本章将对这些情况中的每一种进行说明。

college-writing-014503.zh: 主语（fangs）是复数，所以动词（look）是复数。

college-writing-014504.zh: 主语和动词之间的词是介词短语：在狗的嘴里。

college-writing-014505.en: They do not affect subject–verb agreement.
college-writing-014505.zh: 它们不影响主语-动词一致性。

college-writing-014532.en: A verb agrees with its subject even when the verb comes before the subject.
college-writing-014532.zh: 即使动词出现在主语之前，动词也同意它的主语。

college-writing-014533.en: Words that may precede the subject include there, here, and, in questions, who, which, what, and where.
college-writing-014533.zh: 可能在主题之前的单词包括那里、这里和问题中，谁、哪个、什么和在哪里。

college-writing-014660.en: gerund: a verbal; the -ing form of the verb used as a noun.
