college-writing-014670.en: As mentioned in Chapter 24, the time that a verb shows is usually called tense.
college-writing-014670.zh: 如第 24 章所述，动词显示的时间通常称为时态。

college-writing-014671.en: The most common tenses are the simple present, past, and future.
college-writing-014671.zh: 最常见的时态是简单的现在、过去和未来。

college-writing-014672.en: In addition, nine other tenses enable us to express more specific ideas about time than the simple tenses do.
college-writing-014672.zh: 此外，与简单时态相比，其他九种时态使我们能够表达对时间的更具体的想法。

college-writing-014675.en: Past Ellen worked on her car.
college-writing-014675.zh: 过去艾伦在她的车上工作。

college-writing-014676.en: Future You will work on a new project next week.
college-writing-014676.zh: 未来你将在下周从事一个新项目。

college-writing-014680.en: Present perfect He has worked on his research paper for a month.
college-writing-014680.zh: Present Perfect 他在他的研究论文上工作了一个月。

college-writing-014681.en: They have worked out a compromise.

college-writing-014682.en: Note: The present perfect tense is used for an action that began in the past and continues in the present.
college-writing-014682.zh: 注意：现在完成时用于过去开始并继续到现在的动作。

college-writing-014683.en: Past perfect The nurse had worked two straight shifts.
college-writing-014683.zh: 过去的完美护士做了两个直系轮班。

college-writing-014684.en: Note: The past perfect tense is used for a past action that came before another past action.
college-writing-014684.zh: 注意：过去完成时用于另一个过去动作之前的过去动作。

college-writing-014685.en: Future perfect Next Monday, I will have worked here exactly two years.
college-writing-014685.zh: 未来完美 下周一，我将在这里工作了整整两年。

college-writing-014686.en: Present progressive I am working on my speech for the debate.
college-writing-014686.zh: 现在的进步人士我正在为辩论撰写演讲。

college-writing-014688.en: The toaster is not working properly.
college-writing-014688.zh: 烤面包机无法正常工作。

college-writing-014689.en: Past progressive He was working in the basement.
college-writing-014689.zh: 过去的进步他在地下室工作。

college-writing-014690.en: The contestants were working on their robot design.
college-writing-014690.zh: 参赛者正在研究他们的机器人设计。

college-writing-014691.en: Future progressive My son will be working in our store this summer.
college-writing-014691.zh: 未来进步我儿子将在今年夏天在我们的商店工作。

college-writing-014693.en: Adriel has been working late this week.
college-writing-014693.zh: 阿德里尔本周工作到很晚。

college-writing-014695.en: Until recently, I had been working nights.
college-writing-014695.zh: 直到最近，我一直在工作。

college-writing-014697.en: My mother will have been working as a nurse for forty-five years by the time she retires.
college-writing-014697.zh: 到她退休时，我的母亲已经做了四十五年的护士。

college-writing-014701.en: These common verbs can either stand alone or “help” other verbs.
college-writing-014701.zh: 这些普通动词可以单独站立，也可以“帮助”其他动词。

college-writing-014704.en: Here are examples of the helping verbs:
college-writing-014704.zh: 以下是帮助动词的示例：

college-writing-014705.en: USED ALONE USED AS HELPING VERBS I was angry.
college-writing-014705.zh: 单独用作帮助动词我很生气。

college-writing-014710.en: He did fail the previous test.
college-writing-014710.zh: 他确实没有通过上一个测试。

college-writing-014711.en: Nine helping verbs (traditionally known as modals, or modal auxiliaries) are always used in combination with other verbs.
college-writing-014711.zh: 九个帮助动词（传统上称为模态或模态助词）总是与其他动词结合使用。

college-writing-014712.en: Here are the nine verbs and a sentence example of each:
college-writing-014712.zh: 以下是每个动词的九个动词和一个句子示例：

college-writing-014713.en: can I can see the rainbow.

college-writing-014714.en: could I could not find a seat.

college-writing-014715.en: may The game may be postponed.

college-writing-014716.en: might Hannah might resent your advice.
college-writing-014716.zh: 可能汉娜可能会怨恨你的建议。

college-writing-014717.en: shall I shall see you tomorrow.

college-writing-014718.en: should He should get his car serviced.

college-writing-014719.en: will Luke will want to see you.

college-writing-014721.en: must You must visit us again.

college-writing-014722.en: Note from the examples that these verbs have only one form.
college-writing-014722.zh: 从例子中注意，这些动词只有一种形式。

college-writing-014723.en: They do not, for instance, add an -s when used with he, she, it, or any one person or thing.
college-writing-014723.zh: 例如，当与他、她、它或任何一个人或事物一起使用时，它们不会添加 -s。

college-writing-014726.en: Verbals are words formed from verbs.
college-writing-014726.zh: 动词是由动词组成的单词。

college-writing-014727.en: Verbals, like verbs, often express action.
college-writing-014727.zh: 像动词一样，动词经常表达动作。

college-writing-014728.en: They can add variety to your sentences and vigor to your writing style.
college-writing-014728.zh: 它们可以为您的句子增添多样性，并为您的写作风格增添活力。

college-writing-014729.en: The three kinds of verbals are infinitives, participles, and gerunds.
college-writing-014729.zh: 这三种语言是不定式、分词和动名词。

college-writing-014730.en: Additional information about infinitives can be found in Chapter 22.
college-writing-014730.zh: 有关不定式的其他信息，请参见第 22 章。

college-writing-014731.en: Additional information about participles and gerunds can be found in Chapters 22, 24, and 31.
college-writing-014731.zh: 有关分词和动名词的其他信息，请参见第 22、24 和 31 章。

college-writing-014734.en: Infinitive An infinitive is to plus the base form of the verb.
college-writing-014734.zh: 不定式不定式是加上动词的基本形式。

college-writing-014736.en: Lina hopes to write for a newspaper.

college-writing-014737.en: I asked the children to clean the kitchen.

college-writing-014738.en: Participle A participle is a verb form used as an adjective (a descriptive word).
college-writing-014738.zh: 分词 分词是用作形容词（描述性词）的动词形式。

college-writing-014740.en: The past participle ends in -ed or has an irregular ending.
college-writing-014740.zh: 过去分词以 -ed 结尾或具有不规则结尾。

college-writing-014741.en: Peering into the cracked mirror, the laughing clown waved to the reflection.
college-writing-014741.zh: 看着破裂的镜子，笑的小丑向倒影挥了挥手。

college-writing-014742.en: The astounded man stared at his winning lottery ticket.
college-writing-014742.zh: 震惊的男人盯着他中奖的彩票。

college-writing-014743.en: Swinging a sharp ax, the worker split the rotted beam.
college-writing-014743.zh: 挥舞一把锋利的斧头，工人将腐烂的光束分开。

college-writing-014744.en: Gerund A gerund is the -ing form of a verb used as a noun.
college-writing-014744.zh: Gerund A Gerund 是用作名词的动词的 -ing 形式。

college-writing-014746.en: Eating junk food is my diet downfall.
college-writing-014746.zh: 吃垃圾食品是我的饮食失败。

college-writing-014747.en: Through doodling, people express their inner feelings.
college-writing-014747.zh: 通过涂鸦，人们表达自己的内心感受。

college-writing-014762.en: This chapter will provide information on pronoun agreement and reference.
college-writing-014762.zh: 本章将提供有关代词协议和参考的信息。

college-writing-014764.en: Johan was annoyed when they failed his car for a faulty turn signal.
college-writing-014764.zh: 当他们因转向信号灯故障而让他的车失效时，约翰很生气。

college-writing-014765.en: In this case, “they” should be replaced by a specific noun, such as “the inspectors,” so the reader knows who the word “they” refers to.
college-writing-014765.zh: 在这种情况下，“他们”应该被一个特定的名词代替，例如“检查员”，以便读者知道“他们”这个词指的是谁。

college-writing-014767.en: Johan was annoyed when the inspectors failed his car for a faulty turn signal.
college-writing-014767.zh: 当检查员因转向信号灯故障而让他的车失效时，约翰很生气。

college-writing-014768.en: Now it is made clear that it was the inspectors who failed the car.
college-writing-014768.zh: 现在很清楚，是检查员让这辆车失效了。

college-writing-014770.en: indefinite pronouns: words that refer to people and things that are not named or are not specific.
college-writing-014770.zh: 无限代词：指代人和事物的词，没有命名或不是特定的。

college-writing-014771.en: Many indefinite pronouns take a singular verb; some take plural verbs; and others can take either a singular or a plural verb.
college-writing-014771.zh: 许多不定代词采用单数动词； 有些取复数动词； 其他人可以采用单数或复数动词。

college-writing-014772.en: nouns: words that name persons, places, or things.
college-writing-014772.zh: 名词：命名人、地方或事物的词。

college-writing-014773.en: pronouns: words that take the place of nouns.

college-writing-014774.en: Pronouns are shortcuts that keep you from unnecessarily repeating words in writing.
college-writing-014774.zh: 代词是一种快捷方式，可以防止您在书面中不必要地重复单词。

college-writing-014775.en: pronoun agreement: correspondence in number between the pronoun and the noun it replaces.
college-writing-014775.zh: 代词协议：代词和代名词代替的名词之间的对应关系。

college-writing-014776.en: Example: Students enrolled in the art class must prove that they can paint.
college-writing-014776.zh: 示例：参加艺术课的学生必须证明他们可以画画。

college-writing-014777.en: pronoun reference: the relationship between the pronoun and the noun in the sentence to which it refers.
college-writing-014777.zh: 代词引用：代词和名词在它所指的句子中的关系。

college-writing-014778.en: A sentence may be confusing if a pronoun appears to refer to more than one noun or does not appear to refer to any specific noun.
college-writing-014778.zh: 如果代词似乎指的是多个名词或似乎不指代任何特定名词，则句子可能会令人困惑。

college-writing-014779.en: Example: See above “Incorrect” and “Correct” example sentences.
college-writing-014779.zh: 示例：参见上面的“不正确”和“正确”的例句。

college-writing-014780.en: C H A P T E R Pronoun Agreement and Reference 27 27
college-writing-014780.zh: C h a p t e r 代词协议和参考文献 27 27

college-writing-014782.en: Nouns name persons, places, or things.
college-writing-014782.zh: 名词命名人、地方或事物。

college-writing-014783.en: Pronouns are words that take the place of nouns.

college-writing-014784.en: In fact, the word pronoun means “for a noun.”
college-writing-014784.zh: 事实上，代词这个词的意思是“名词”。

college-writing-014785.en: Pronouns are shortcuts that keep you from unnecessarily repeating words in writing.
college-writing-014785.zh: 代词是一种快捷方式，可以防止您在书面中不必要地重复单词。

college-writing-014786.en: Here are some examples of pronouns:
college-writing-014786.zh: 以下是一些代词的例子：

college-writing-014787.en: Eddie left his camera on the bus.
college-writing-014787.zh: 埃迪把他的相机留在了公共汽车上。

college-writing-014788.en: (His is a pronoun that takes the place of Eddie’s.)

college-writing-014789.en: Sandra drank the coffee even though it was cold.
college-writing-014789.zh: 桑德拉即使很冷，也喝了咖啡。

college-writing-014791.en: As I turned the newspaper’s damp pages, they disintegrated in my hands.
college-writing-014791.zh: 当我翻开报纸潮湿的页面时，它们在我手中瓦解了。

college-writing-014792.en: (They is a pronoun that takes the place of pages.)

college-writing-014793.en: This chapter presents rules that will help you avoid two common mistakes people make with pronouns.
college-writing-014793.zh: 本章介绍了可以帮助您避免人们使用代词的两个常见错误的规则。

college-writing-014795.en: 1. A pronoun must agree in number with the word or words it replaces.
college-writing-014795.zh: 1. 代词的数量必须与它所取代的单词或单词一致。

college-writing-014796.en: 2. A pronoun must refer clearly to the word it replaces.
college-writing-014796.zh: 2. 代词必须清楚地指代它所取代的词。

college-writing-014798.en: A pronoun must agree in number with the word or words it replaces.
college-writing-014798.zh: 代词必须与它所取代的单词或单词一致。

college-writing-014799.en: If the word a pronoun refers to is singular, the pronoun must be singular; if that word is plural, the pronoun must be plural.
college-writing-014799.zh: 如果一个代词指的是单数，代词必须是单数的； 如果这个词是复数，代词必须是复数。

college-writing-014800.en: (Note that the word a pronoun refers to is known as the antecedent.)
college-writing-014800.zh: （请注意，代词所指的单词称为先行词。）

college-writing-014801.en: Marie showed me her antique watch collection.
college-writing-014801.zh: 玛丽向我展示了她的古董手表系列。

college-writing-014802.en: Students enrolled in the art class must provide their own supplies.
college-writing-014802.zh: 参加艺术课的学生必须提供自己的用品。

college-writing-014803.en: In the first example, the pronoun her refers to the singular word Marie; in the second example, the pronoun their refers to the plural word Students.
college-writing-014803.zh: 在第一个例子中，代词她指的是单数单词 Marie； 在第二个例子中，代词是指复数词学生。

college-writing-014804.en: It’s important to note that language usage is evolving; the pronouns they/ them/their, once considered only plural, can be now be used as either singular or plural pronouns.
college-writing-014804.zh: 重要的是要注意语言使用正在发展。 他们/他们/他们/他们的代词，曾经被认为是复数，现在可以用作单数代词或复数代词。

college-writing-014805.en: Many people choose not to use he/she pronouns and instead choose to use they/them as non-gendered pronouns.
college-writing-014805.zh: 许多人选择不使用他/她的代词，而是选择将它们/它们用作非性别代词。

college-writing-014806.en: In the following example, their refers to one person, Lindz Amer, who uses they/them pronouns.
college-writing-014806.zh: 在下面的例子中，他们指的是一个人，Lindz Amer，他使用他们/他们的代词。

college-writing-014807.en: Lindz Amer hosts a phenomenal website and YouTube channel to tell their story and educate others.
college-writing-014807.zh: Lindz Amer 拥有一个非凡的网站和 YouTube 频道，讲述他们的故事并教育他人。

college-writing-014809.en: Write the appropriate pronoun (their, they, them, it) in the blank space in each of the following sentences.
college-writing-014809.zh: 在下列每个句子的空格中写下适当的代词（他们的、他们的、他们的）。

college-writing-014811.en: I opened the wet umbrella and put in the bathtub to dry.
college-writing-014811.zh: 我打开湿伞，放在浴缸里晾干。

college-writing-014812.en: 1. Kate and Omar left for the movies earlier than usual because knew the theater would be packed.
college-writing-014812.zh: 1. 凯特和奥马尔比平时更早去看电影，因为知道剧院会挤满人。

college-writing-014813.en: 2. The area around San Jose, California, produces fine wines, but is also the home of many high-tech companies.
college-writing-014813.zh: 2. 加利福尼亚州圣何塞周边地区生产优质葡萄酒，但也是许多高科技公司的所在地。

college-writing-014814.en: 3. Jiang and Takashi spent the entire holiday playing new video games.
college-writing-014814.zh: 3. 江和高石整个假期都在玩新的电子游戏。

college-writing-014815.en: 4. Many people immigrate to America to make a better life for families.
college-writing-014815.zh: 4. 许多人移民到美国，为家庭创造更好的生活。

college-writing-014816.en: 5. The salesperson said the store usually carried Birkenstocks, but hadn’t received any shipments in a while, so the stock was depleted.
college-writing-014816.zh: 5. 销售人员说，这家商店通常有 Birkenstocks，但有一段时间没有收到任何货物，因此库存耗尽。

college-writing-014817.en: 6. The young girl liked to read graphic novels because were filled with exciting adventures and intricate artwork.
college-writing-014817.zh: 6. 年轻女孩喜欢阅读图画小说，因为充满了激动人心的冒险和错综复杂的艺术品。

college-writing-014818.en: 7. The clothes were still damp, but I decided to fold anyway.
college-writing-014818.zh: 7. 衣服还是湿的，但我还是决定折叠起来。

college-writing-014819.en: 8. Tom said he enjoyed the play Les Misérables even though was a sad story filled with death.
college-writing-014819.zh: 8. 汤姆说他喜欢这部剧《悲惨世界》，尽管这是一个充满死亡的悲伤故事。

college-writing-014820.en: 9. Jabari’s grandparents renewed marriage vows at a huge fiftieth wedding anniversary celebration.
college-writing-014820.zh: 9. Jabari 的祖父母在一个盛大的 50 周年结婚纪念日庆祝活动中重新结婚。

college-writing-014821.en: 10. Samantha and Tom were walking quickly to algebra class, but I managed to catch up with .
college-writing-014821.zh: 10. Samantha 和 Tom 很快就去了代数课，但我设法赶上了 .

college-writing-014822.en: Indefinite Pronouns Indefinite pronouns follow slightly different rules from other pronouns.
college-writing-014822.zh: 不定代词 不定代词遵循与其他代词略有不同的规则。

college-writing-014823.en: They don’t always replace a specific noun nor do they always require an antecedent.
college-writing-014823.zh: 它们并不总是取代特定名词，也不总是需要先行词。

college-writing-014824.en: Some are considered singular, some are considered plural, and some can be either, depending on the context of the sentence.
college-writing-014824.zh: 有些被认为是单数的，有些被认为是复数，有些可以是，取决于句子的上下文。

college-writing-014827.en: Traditionally, writers used the masculine pronoun (he, him, his) to refer to people, regardless of gender.
college-writing-014827.zh: 传统上，作家使用男性代词（他、他、他的）来指代人，无论性别如何。

college-writing-014828.en: To become more inclusive, writers then began using he or she, him or her, and his or hers to avert an implied gender bias.
college-writing-014828.zh: 为了变得更具包容性，作家然后开始使用他或她、他或她和他或她的来避免隐含的性别偏见。

college-writing-014829.en: This construction was often awkward and wordy.
college-writing-014829.zh: 这种结构往往很尴尬和冗长。

college-writing-014830.en: As mentioned in the preceding section, language has evolved to become more inclusive and nonbiased, and the use of they, them, their has now become the preferred, clearer pronoun to use when referring to people if gender is unknown or irrelevant to the context or it is an individual's expressed choice.
college-writing-014830.zh: 如上一节所述，语言已经演变为更具包容性和无偏见性，如果性别与上下文不为或不相关，或是个人的表达，它们的使用现在已成为当提到人时使用的首选、更清晰的代词 选择。

college-writing-014833.en: If a pronoun in a sentence refers to one of these singular words, that pronoun should be singular.
college-writing-014833.zh: 如果句子中的代词指的是这些单数单词之一，则该代词应该是单数的。

college-writing-014834.en: In the examples that follow, each circled pronoun is singular because it refers to a singular indefinite pronoun.
college-writing-014834.zh: 在下面的例子中，每个带圈的代词都是单数的，因为它指的是一个单数的不定代词。

college-writing-014835.en: If there is a clear gender indication, as in these examples, it is acceptable to use he/him/his or she/her/hers as the singular pronoun.
college-writing-014835.zh: 如果有明确的性别指示，如在这些示例中，可以将他/他/他/她/她/她的/她/她的/她/她/她的/她的/她的/她的/她的/她的/她的/她的/她/她的人当作单数代词。

college-writing-014836.en: Somebody left her gym bag in the women’s locker room.
college-writing-014836.zh: 有人把她的健身包留在了女式更衣室里。

college-writing-014837.en: One of the boys on the soccer team said he would be an hour late.
college-writing-014837.zh: 足球队的一个男孩说他会迟到一个小时。

college-writing-014838.en: In the next example, there is no information about what type of club it is; thus, the use of their is appropriate as a neutral singular pronoun.
college-writing-014838.zh: 在下一个例子中，没有关于它是什么类型的俱乐部的信息； 因此，使用它们作为中性单数代词是合适的。

college-writing-014839.en: (However, if everyone in the club was a woman, the pronoun would be her.)
college-writing-014839.zh: （然而，如果俱乐部里的每个人都是女人，代词就是她。）

college-writing-014840.en: Everyone in the club must pay their dues next week.
college-writing-014840.zh: 俱乐部的每个人都必须在下周支付会费。

college-writing-014842.en: Everybody has their own opinion about the election.
college-writing-014842.zh: 每个人对选举都有自己的看法。

college-writing-014843.en: No one in the class remembered to bring their books.
college-writing-014843.zh: 班上没有人记得带他们的书。

college-writing-014844.en: Anybody who doesn’t have their ticket won’t get onto the plane.
college-writing-014844.zh: 任何没有票的人都不会上飞机。

college-writing-014845.en: Another option, which does not employ an indefinite pronoun, is to rewrite the sentence in plural form:
college-writing-014845.zh: 另一个不使用无限代词的选项是以复数形式重写句子：

college-writing-014846.en: Club members must pay their dues next week.
college-writing-014846.zh: 俱乐部会员必须在下周支付会费。

college-writing-014847.en: People have their own opinions about the election.
college-writing-014847.zh: 人们对选举有自己的看法。

college-writing-014848.en: No students in the class remembered to bring their books.
college-writing-014848.zh: 班上没有学生记得带他们的书。

college-writing-014849.en: Travelers who don’t have their tickets won’t get onto the plane.
college-writing-014849.zh: 没有机票的旅客不会上飞机。

college-writing-014850.zh: 被视为复数的常见不定代词

college-writing-014855.zh: 如果句子中的代词指的是这些复数单词之一，则该代词应该是复数。

college-writing-014862.zh: 如果句子中的代词指的是这些不定代词之一，则句子的上下文决定了是否应该使用单数代词或复数代词。

college-writing-014875.zh: 7. 今天有人把（他或她的）书留在教室里。

college-writing-014883.zh: 一个句子可能会令人困惑和不清楚，如果代词似乎指的是多个单词或不指代任何特定单词。

college-writing-014974.en: This chapter will describe some common types of pronouns:
college-writing-014974.zh: 本章将描述一些常见的代词类型：

college-writing-014975.en: • subject pronouns • object pronouns • possessive pronouns • demonstrative pronouns
college-writing-014975.zh: • 主语代词 • 宾语代词 • 所有格代词 • 指示代词

college-writing-014977.en: subject pronouns: pronouns that function as the subjects of verbs.
college-writing-014977.zh: 主语代词：作为动词主语的代词。

college-writing-014978.en: Example: They are all in the high school orchestra.
college-writing-014978.zh: 示例：他们都在高中管弦乐队。

college-writing-014979.en: object pronouns: pronouns that function as the objects of verbs or prepositions.
college-writing-014979.zh: 宾语代词：作为动词或介词的宾语的代词。

college-writing-014981.en: possessive pronouns: pronouns that show ownership or possession.
college-writing-014981.zh: 所有格代词：显示所有权或占有的代词。

college-writing-014983.en: demonstrative pronouns: pronouns that point to or single out a person or thing.
college-writing-014983.zh: 指示代词：指向或挑出一个人或事物的代词。

college-writing-014984.en: The four demonstrative pronouns are this, that, these, and those.
college-writing-014984.zh: 四个指示代词是这个、那个、这些和那些。

college-writing-014986.en: Most pronouns change their form depending on what place they occupy in a sentence.
college-writing-014986.zh: 大多数代词根据他们在句子中占据的位置而改变它们的形式。

college-writing-014987.en: In the box that follows is a list of subject and object pronouns.
college-writing-014987.zh: 在下面的框中是主语和宾语代词的列表。

college-writing-014988.en: Subject Pronouns Object Pronouns I me you you (no change) he him she her it it (no change) we us they them
college-writing-014988.zh: 主格与宾格：I → me（我）；you → you（你／你们，不变）；he → him（他）；she → her（她）；it → it（它，不变）；we → us（我们）；they → them（他们／她们／它们）。

college-writing-014990.en: Subject Pronouns Subject pronouns are subjects of verbs.
college-writing-014990.zh: 主语代词 主语代词是动词的主语。

college-writing-014991.en: He served as a soldier during the war in Iraq.
college-writing-014991.zh: 他在伊拉克战争期间担任士兵。

college-writing-014992.en: (He is the subject of the verb served.)

college-writing-014993.en: They are moving into our old apartment.
college-writing-014993.zh: 他们搬进我们的旧公寓。

college-writing-014994.en: (They is the subject of the verb are moving.)

college-writing-014995.en: We students should have a say in the decision.
college-writing-014995.zh: 我们学生应该对决定有发言权。

college-writing-014996.en: (We is the subject of the verb should have.)

college-writing-014997.en: Following are several rules for using subject pronouns─and several kinds of mistakes people sometimes make with subject pronouns.
college-writing-014997.zh: 以下是使用主语代词的几个规则——以及人们有时会在主语代词中犯的几种错误。

college-writing-014999.en: Use a subject pronoun when you have a compound subject (more than one subject).
college-writing-014999.zh: 当您有一个复合主语（不止一个科目）时，使用主语代词。

college-writing-015001.en: My brother and me are Billie Eilish fanatics.
college-writing-015001.zh: 我和我的兄弟是 Billie Eilish 的狂热分子。

college-writing-015002.en: My brother and I are Billie Eilish fanatics.
college-writing-015002.zh: 我和我的兄弟是 Billie Eilish 的狂热分子。

college-writing-015003.en: Him and me know the lyrics to all of Billie’s songs.
college-writing-015003.zh: 他和我都知道比莉所有歌曲的歌词。

college-writing-015004.en: He and I know the lyrics to all of Billie’s songs.
college-writing-015004.zh: 他和我都知道比莉所有歌曲的歌词。

college-writing-015006.en: Use a subject pronoun after forms of the verb be.
college-writing-015006.zh: 在动词 be 的形式之后使用主语代词。

college-writing-015007.en: Forms of be include am, are, is, was, were, has been, have been, and others.
college-writing-015007.zh: be 的形式包括 am、are、is、was、were、has been、have been 等。

college-writing-015008.en: It was I who left the light on.

college-writing-015009.en: It may be they in that car.
college-writing-015009.zh: 可能是他们在那辆车里。

college-writing-015011.en: The sentences above may sound strange and stilted to you because they are seldom used in conversation.
college-writing-015011.zh: 上面的句子对你来说可能听起来很奇怪和生硬，因为它们很少在谈话中使用。

college-writing-015012.en: When we speak with one another, forms such as “It was me,” “It may be them,” and “It is him” are widely accepted.
college-writing-015012.zh: 当我们彼此交谈时，诸如“是我”、“可能是它们”和“是他”之类的形式被广泛接受。

college-writing-015013.en: In formal writing, however, the grammatically correct forms are still preferred.
college-writing-015013.zh: 然而，在正式写作中，语法正确的形式仍然是首选。

college-writing-015015.en: If you are not sure what pronoun to use, try each pronoun by itself in the sentence.
college-writing-015015.zh: 如果您不确定要使用什么代词，请在句子中尝试每个代词。

college-writing-015016.en: The correct pronoun will be the one that sounds right.
college-writing-015016.zh: 正确的代词将是听起来正确的代名词。

college-writing-015017.en: For example, “Him knows the lyrics to all of Billie’s songs” does not sound right; “He knows the lyrics to all of Billie’s songs” does.
college-writing-015017.zh: 例如，“他知道比莉所有歌曲的歌词”听起来不对； “他知道比莉所有歌曲的歌词”。

college-writing-015021.en: Use subject pronouns after than or as.
college-writing-015021.zh: 之后使用主语代词 than 或 as。

college-writing-015022.en: The subject pronoun is used because a verb is understood after the pronoun.
college-writing-015022.zh: 使用主语代词是因为动词在代词之后被理解。

college-writing-015024.en: (The verb play is understood after I.)

college-writing-015025.en: Jenna is as bored as I (am).

college-writing-015026.en: (The verb am is understood after I.)
college-writing-015026.zh: （动词 am 在 i 之后被理解。）

college-writing-015027.en: We don’t need the money as much as they (do).
college-writing-015027.zh: 我们不需要像他们那样需要钱。

college-writing-015028.en: (The verb do is understood after they.)
college-writing-015028.zh: （动词 do 是在他们之后理解的。）

college-writing-015029.en: Object Pronouns Object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) are the objects of verbs or prepositions.
college-writing-015029.zh: 宾语代词 宾语代词（我、他、她、我们、他们）是动词或介词的宾语。

college-writing-015030.en: (Prepositions are connecting words like for, at, about, to, before, by, with, and of. See Chapter 23 for a list of prepositions.)
college-writing-015030.zh: （介词是连接词，如 for、at、about、to、before、by、with 和 of。请参阅第 23 章以获取介词列表。）

college-writing-015031.en: Notice that in each of the sentences below, the object pronoun directly follows the verb or preposition.
college-writing-015031.zh: 请注意，在下面的每个句子中，宾语代词直接跟随动词或介词。

college-writing-015032.en: Ali helped me. (Me is the object of the verb helped.) We took them to the college.
college-writing-015032.zh: 阿里帮助了我。 （我是动词帮助的宾语。）我们把他们带到了学院。

college-writing-015034.zh: 把孩子们留在我们身边。

college-writing-015035.en: (Us is the object of the preposition with.)

college-writing-015036.en: I got in line behind him.

college-writing-015037.en: (Him is the object of the preposition behind.)

college-writing-015038.en: People are sometimes uncertain about what pronoun to use when two objects follow a verb or a preposition and will sometimes incorrectly use a subject pronoun instead of an object pronoun.
college-writing-015038.zh: 当两个宾语跟随动词或介词时，人们有时不确定使用什么代词，有时会错误地使用主语代词而不是宾语代词。

college-writing-015040.en: You can avoid having to use a subject pronoun after be by simply rewording a sentence.
college-writing-015040.zh: 您可以通过简单地改写一个句子来避免在 be 之后使用主语代词。

college-writing-015054.zh: 她和林赛一起来看电影。

college-writing-015196.en: This chapter will describe the principal characteristics of adjectives and adverbs.
college-writing-015196.zh: 本章将描述形容词和副词的主要特征。

college-writing-015198.en: adjectives: words that describe nouns or pronouns.
college-writing-015198.zh: 形容词：描述名词或代词的词。

college-writing-015199.en: Example: Sofia is a wise economist.
college-writing-015199.zh: 示例：索菲亚是一位明智的经济学家。

college-writing-015200.en: adverbs: words that describe verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
college-writing-015200.zh: 副词：描述动词、形容词或其他副词的词。

college-writing-015201.en: Example: I walked quickly to the store.

college-writing-015202.zh: 形容词 什么是形容词？

college-writing-015203.en: Adjectives describe nouns (names of persons, places, or things) or pronouns.
college-writing-015203.zh: 形容词描述名词（人、地点或事物的名称）或代词。

college-writing-015204.zh: 索菲亚是一位明智的经济学家。

college-writing-015205.en: (The adjective wise describes the noun economist.)
college-writing-015205.zh: （形容词 wise 描述了名词经济学家。）

college-writing-015207.en: (The adjective funny describes the pronoun she.)
college-writing-015207.zh: （形容词搞笑描述了她的代词。）

college-writing-015208.en: I’ll carry the heavy bag of groceries.
college-writing-015208.zh: 我会背着沉重的杂货袋。

college-writing-015209.en: (The adjective heavy describes the noun bag.)

college-writing-015211.en: (The adjective torn describes the pronoun it.)
college-writing-015211.zh: （形容词 torn 描述了代词 it。）

college-writing-015212.en: Adjectives usually come before the word they describe (as in wise economist and heavy bag).
college-writing-015212.zh: 形容词通常出现在它们所描述的单词之前（如明智的经济学家和沉重的袋子）。

college-writing-015213.en: But they also come after forms of the verb be (is, are, was, were, and so on).
college-writing-015213.zh: 但它们也出现在动词 be (is, are, are, was, was, 等等) 的形式之后。

college-writing-015214.en: They also follow verbs such as look, appear, seem, become, sound, taste, and smell.
college-writing-015214.zh: 它们还跟随动词，例如看、出现、出现、变成、声音、味觉和嗅觉。

college-writing-015226.en: Using Adjectives to Compare Adjectives are often used to compare things or people.
college-writing-015226.zh: 使用形容词比较形容词通常用于比较事物或人。

college-writing-015227.en: Use the comparative form of the adjective if two people or things are being compared.
college-writing-015227.zh: 如果比较两个人或事物，请使用形容词的比较形式。

college-writing-015228.en: Use the superlative form of the adjective if three or more people or things are being compared.
college-writing-015228.zh: 如果比较三个或多个人或事物，请使用形容词的最高级形式。

college-writing-015229.en: For all one-syllable adjectives and some two-syllable adjectives, add -er when comparing two things and -est when comparing three or more things.
college-writing-015229.zh: 对于所有一音节的形容词和一些二音节的形容词，在比较两件事时加 -er 和 - 比较三个或更多的东西时。

college-writing-015230.en: Phil’s beard is longer than mine, but Noah’s is the longest.
college-writing-015230.zh: 菲尔的胡须比我的长，但诺亚的胡须最长。

college-writing-015231.en: Kana may be the quieter of the two sisters; but that’s not saying much, since they’re the loudest girls in school.
college-writing-015231.zh: 假名可能是两姐妹中较为安静的； 但这并没有说太多，因为她们是学校里最吵闹的女孩。

college-writing-015232.en: For some two-syllable adjectives and all longer adjectives, use more when comparing two things and most when comparing three or more things.
college-writing-015232.zh: 对于一些两个音节的形容词和所有较长的形容词，在比较两个或更多的东西时，比较两个东西时使用更多。

college-writing-015233.en: Liza Minnelli is more famous than her sister; but their mother, Judy Garland, is still the most famous member of the family.
college-writing-015233.zh: Liza Minnelli 比她的妹妹更有名； 但他们的母亲朱迪·加兰仍然是这个家庭中最著名的成员。

college-writing-015234.en: The red letters on the sign are more noticeable than the black ones, but the Day-Glo letters are the most noticeable.
college-writing-015234.zh: 标志上的红色字母比黑色字母更明显，但 Day-glo 字母最明显。

college-writing-015235.en: You can usually tell when to use more and most by the sound of a word.
college-writing-015235.zh: 您通常可以通过单词的声音来判断何时使用更多和最多。

college-writing-015236.en: For example, you can probably tell by its sound that “carefuller” would be too awkward to say and that more careful is thus correct.
college-writing-015236.zh: 例如，您可能可以从它的声音中看出“carefuller”会说太尴尬，因此更小心是正确的。

college-writing-015237.en: But there are many words for which both -er or -est and more or most are equally correct.
college-writing-015237.zh: 但是有很多单词 -er 或 -est 以及更多或大多数都同样正确。

college-writing-015238.en: For instance, either “a more fair rule” or “a fairer rule” is correct.
college-writing-015238.zh: 例如，“更公平的规则”或“更公平的规则”是正确的。

college-writing-015239.en: To form negative comparisons, use less and least.
college-writing-015239.zh: 要形成负面比较，请使用更少和最少。

college-writing-015240.en: During my first dance class, I felt less graceful than an injured elephant.
college-writing-015240.zh: 在我的第一堂舞蹈课上，我感觉不如受伤的大象那样优雅。

college-writing-015241.en: When the teacher came to our house to complain to my parents, I offered her the least comfortable chair in the room.
college-writing-015241.zh: 当老师来我们家抱怨我的父母时，我给了她房间里最不舒服的椅子。

college-writing-015242.en: Points to Remember about Comparing Point 1
college-writing-015242.zh: 关于比较点 1 的要点

college-writing-015243.en: Use only one form of comparison at a time.
college-writing-015243.zh: 一次只使用一种比较形式。

college-writing-015244.en: That is, do not use both an -er ending and more or both an -est ending and most:
college-writing-015244.zh: 也就是说，不要同时使用 -er 结尾和更多或同时使用 -est 结尾和大多数：

college-writing-015245.en: INCORRECT CORRECT My brother’s suitcase is always more heavier than my father’s.
college-writing-015245.zh: 不正确 更正我哥哥的手提箱总是比我父亲的要重。

college-writing-015246.en: My brother’s suitcase is always heavier than my father’s.

college-writing-015247.en: Get Out is still the most frighteningest movie I’ve ever seen.
college-writing-015247.zh: Get Out 仍然是我看过的最可怕的电影。

college-writing-015296.en: A Common Mistake with Adverbs and Adjectives People often mistakenly use an adjective instead of an adverb after a verb.

college-writing-015466.en: This chapter will describe dangling modifiers—descriptive words that open a sentence but do not describe what the author intended them to describe.
college-writing-015466.zh: 本章将描述 悬垂修饰语——打开句子但不描述作者意图描述的描述性词语。

college-writing-015468.en: While reading the newspaper, my dog sat with me on the steps.
college-writing-015468.zh: 在看报纸的时候，我的狗和我一起坐在台阶上。

college-writing-015469.en: The sentence misleadingly states that the dog was reading the newspaper.
college-writing-015469.zh: 这句话误导性地说这只狗正在看报纸。

college-writing-015471.en: While I was reading the newspaper, my dog sat with me on the steps.
college-writing-015471.zh: 当我看报纸时，我的狗和我一起坐在台阶上。

college-writing-015472.en: The sentence makes it clear that the subject “I” was reading the newspaper.
college-writing-015472.zh: 这句话清楚地表明，主题“我”正在阅读报纸。

college-writing-015473.zh: 识别和纠正 悬垂修饰语

college-writing-015474.en: A modifier that opens a sentence must be followed immediately by the word it is meant to describe.
college-writing-015474.zh: 打开句子的修饰语必须紧跟着它要描述的词。

college-writing-015475.en: Otherwise, the modifier is said to be dangling, and the sentence takes on an unintended meaning.
college-writing-015475.zh: 否则，修饰语被称为悬空，而句子具有意想不到的含义。

college-writing-015477.en: While reading the newspaper, my dog sat with me on the front steps.
college-writing-015477.zh: 在看报纸的时候，我的狗和我坐在前面的台阶上。

college-writing-015478.en: the unintended meaning is that the dog was reading the newspaper.
college-writing-015478.zh: 意想不到的意思是狗正在看报纸。

college-writing-015480.en: While reading the newspaper, I sat with my dog on the front steps.
college-writing-015480.zh: 在看报纸的时候，我和我的狗坐在前面的台阶上。

college-writing-015481.en: The dangling modifier could also be corrected by placing the subject within the opening word group:
college-writing-015481.zh: 悬垂修饰语也可以通过将主题置于开头词组中来进行纠正：

college-writing-015482.en: While I was reading the newspaper, my dog sat with me on the front steps.
college-writing-015482.zh: 当我在看报纸的时候，我的狗和我坐在前面的台阶上。

college-writing-015499.zh: 1. 将主题放在开头词组中：

college-writing-015501.zh: 2. 将主题放在开头词组后：

college-writing-015503.zh: 查看每个句子中的开头词，并询问谁或什么。

college-writing-015505.en: If it is not, provide the logical subject by using either method of correction described above.

college-writing-015882.en: This chapter will describe the two main uses of the apostrophe.
college-writing-015882.zh: 本章将描述撇号的两个主要用途。

college-writing-015883.en: The sentences below will introduce you to one of these uses—to show ownership or possession.
college-writing-015883.zh: 下面的句子将向您介绍这些用途之一——显示所有权或占有。

college-writing-015884.en: The other main use, to form contractions, is defined below.
college-writing-015884.zh: 形成收缩的另一个主要用途定义如下。

college-writing-015886.en: Because of the dogs constant barking, I could not sleep all night.
college-writing-015886.zh: 由于狗不断吠叫，我整晚都睡不着。

college-writing-015887.en: An apostrophe is needed before the s in dogs to show possession of the constant barking.
college-writing-015887.zh: 在狗的 s 之前需要一个撇号来表明拥有不断的吠叫。

college-writing-015889.en: Because of the dog’s constant barking, I could not sleep all night.
college-writing-015889.zh: 因为狗不断地吠叫，我整晚都睡不着。

college-writing-015890.en: With the apostrophe included it is clear that the dog is the possessor of the constant barking.
college-writing-015890.zh: 有了撇号，很明显这只狗是不断吠叫的拥有者。

college-writing-015892.en: apostrophe: a punctuation mark generally used in order to (1) show the omission of one or more letters in a contraction, and to (2) show ownership or possession.
college-writing-015892.zh: 撇号：通常用于（1）在缩写中省略一封或多封信的标点符号，以及（2）显示所有权或占有。

college-writing-015893.en: contraction: the combination of two words through omission of one or more letters and use of an apostrophe.
college-writing-015893.zh: 收缩：通过省略一个或多个字母和使用撇号来组合两个单词。

college-writing-015895.en: The two main uses of the apostrophe are
college-writing-015895.zh: 撇号的两个主要用途是

college-writing-015896.en: 1. To show the omission of one or more letters in a contraction
college-writing-015896.zh: 1. 显示在缩写中省略一封或多封信

college-writing-015899.en: A contraction is formed when two words are combined.
college-writing-015899.zh: 当两个词组合时形成收缩。

college-writing-015900.en: An apostrophe shows where letters are omitted.
college-writing-015900.zh: 撇号显示省略字母的位置。

college-writing-015901.en: have + not = haven’t (the o in not has been omitted) I + will = I’ll (the wi in will has been omitted)
college-writing-015901.zh: 有 + 不 = 没有（没有省略）我 + 将 = 我会（遗嘱中的 wi 被省略了）

college-writing-015902.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-015904.en: Following are some other common contractions:
college-writing-015904.zh: 以下是其他一些常见的收缩：

college-writing-015905.en: I + am = I’m it + is = it’s I + have = I’ve it + has = it’s I + had = I’d is + not = isn’t who + is = who’s could + not = couldn’t do + not = don’t I + would = I’d did + not = didn’t they + are = they’re
college-writing-015905.zh: I + AM = 我是它 + 是 = 是我 + 有 = 我有它 + 有 = 它是我 + 有 = 我是 + 不是 = 不是谁 + 是 = 谁可以 + 不能 = 不能做 + 不能做 + 没有 = 我做过 + 不 = 他们不是 + 是 = 他们是

college-writing-015906.zh: 我们 + 是 = 我们是

college-writing-015907.en: Will + not has an unusual contraction: won’t.
college-writing-015907.zh: will + not 有一个不寻常的收缩：不会。

college-writing-015915.en: Apostrophe to Show Ownership or Possession
college-writing-015915.zh: 证明所有权或占有的撇号

college-writing-015916.en: To show possession, we can use such words as belongs to, or possessed by.
college-writing-015916.zh: 为了表现出占有，我们可以使用属于或拥有的词。

college-writing-015917.en: the umbrella that belongs to Mark the toys possessed by children the aquatic center owned by the school district the gentleness of my father
college-writing-015917.zh: 属于孩子们的玩具的雨伞 学区拥有的水上中心 父亲的温柔

college-writing-015918.en: Even though contractions are common in everyday speech and in written dialogue, it is often best to avoid them in formal writing.
college-writing-015918.zh: 尽管收缩在日常演讲和书面对话中很常见，但在正式写作中通常最好避免它们。

college-writing-015921.en: But the apostrophe and s (if the word doesn’t end in s) is often the easiest way to do this.
college-writing-015921.zh: 但是撇号和 S（如果这个词没有以 S 结尾）通常是最简单的方法。

college-writing-015922.en: Mark’s umbrella the children’s toys the school district’s aquatic center my father’s gentleness
college-writing-015922.zh: 马克的雨伞 孩子们的玩具 学区的水生中心 我父亲的温柔

college-writing-015924.en: 1. The ’s goes with the owner or possessor (in the examples given, Mark, children, the school, my father).

college-writing-015925.en: What follows is the person or thing possessed (in the examples given, the umbrella, the toys, the aquatic center, gentleness).
college-writing-015925.zh: 以下是所拥有的人或物（在给出的例子中，雨伞、玩具、水生中心、温柔）。

college-writing-015926.en: 2. There should not be a break between the word and ’s.
college-writing-015926.zh: 2. 单词和's之间不应该有中断。

college-writing-015929.en: 3. An apostrophe and s are used to show possession with a singular word even if the word already ends in s: for example, Elias’s book (the book belonging to Elias).
college-writing-015929.zh: 3. 撇号和 s 用于用单数词来表示占有，即使这个词已经以 S 结尾：例如，以利亚的书（属于埃利亚斯的书）。

college-writing-016222.en: This chapter will describe the six main uses of the comma.
college-writing-016222.zh: 本章将描述逗号的六个主要用途。

college-writing-016223.en: The sentences below will introduce you to one of these uses—to set a direct quotation off from the rest of the sentence.
college-writing-016223.zh: 下面的句子将向您介绍这些用法之一——从句子的其余部分直接引用。

college-writing-016224.en: The other five main uses of the comma are included below.
college-writing-016224.zh: 逗号的其他五个主要用途如下。

college-writing-016226.en: The journalist pleaded “Just one more question.”
college-writing-016226.zh: 这位记者恳求“再说一个问题”。

college-writing-016227.en: A comma is needed to set the direct quotation off from the rest of the sentence.
college-writing-016227.zh: 需要一个逗号来设置句子其余部分的直接引号。

college-writing-016229.en: The journalist pleaded, “Just one more question.”
college-writing-016229.zh: 记者恳求道：“再问一个问题。”

college-writing-016230.en: With the comma included, the direct quotation is properly set off from the rest of the sentence.
college-writing-016230.zh: 包含逗号时，直接引用从句子的其余部分正确引出。

college-writing-016232.en: C H A P T E R

college-writing-016233.en: Six Main Uses of the Comma

college-writing-016234.en: Commas are used mainly as follows:

college-writing-016235.en: 1. To separate items in a series

college-writing-016237.en: 3. On both sides of words that interrupt the flow of thought in a sentence
college-writing-016237.zh: 3. 中断句子中思想流动的单词两面

college-writing-016238.en: 4. Between two complete thoughts connected by and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet
college-writing-016238.zh: 4. 在两个完整的思想之间，由 and、but、or、or、nor、so 连接

college-writing-016239.en: 5. To set off a direct quotation from the rest of a sentence
college-writing-016239.zh: 5. 引出句子其余部分的直接引用

college-writing-016241.en: You may find it helpful to remember that the comma often marks a slight pause or break in a sentence.
college-writing-016241.zh: 您可能会发现逗号通常会在句子中标记轻微的停顿或中断会有所帮助。

college-writing-016242.en: Read aloud the sentence examples given for each rule, and listen for the minor pauses or breaks that are signaled by commas.
college-writing-016242.zh: 大声朗读为每个规则给出的句子示例，并收听以逗号表示的小停顿或中断。

college-writing-016243.zh: 598 第四部分 句子技巧手册

college-writing-016244.en: Comma between Items in a Series Use commas to separate items in a series.
college-writing-016244.zh: 系列中项目之间的逗号使用逗号分隔系列中的项目。

college-writing-016245.en: The street vendor sold watches, necklaces, and earrings.
college-writing-016245.zh: 街头小贩出售手表、项链和耳环。

college-writing-016246.en: The pitcher adjusted his cap, pawed the ground, and peered over his shoulder.
college-writing-016246.zh: 投手调整了他的帽子，用爪子踩着地，凝视着他的肩膀。

college-writing-016247.en: The exercise instructor told us to inhale, exhale, and relax.
college-writing-016247.zh: 运动教练告诉我们吸气、呼气和放松。

college-writing-016248.en: Owen peered into the hot, still-smoking engine.
college-writing-016248.zh: 欧文凝视着炎热、仍然吸烟的引擎。

college-writing-016249.en: A. The final comma in a series is optional, but it is often used.
college-writing-016249.zh: A. 系列中的最终逗号是可选的，但经常使用。

college-writing-016251.en: comma in one series in an essay, use one in all the other series in the same essay.
college-writing-016251.zh: 在一篇文章中的一个系列中逗号，在同一篇文章中的所有其他系列中使用一个。

college-writing-016252.en: B. A comma is used between two descriptive words in a series only if and
college-writing-016252.zh: B. 仅当和序列中的两个描述性单词之间使用逗号

college-writing-016253.en: inserted between the words sounds natural.
college-writing-016253.zh: 插入单词之间听起来很自然。

college-writing-016255.en: Owen peered into the hot and still-smoking engine.
college-writing-016255.zh: 欧文凝视着炎热而仍然吸烟的引擎。

college-writing-016256.en: But notice in the following sentence that the descriptive words do not sound natural when and is inserted between them.
college-writing-016256.zh: 但请注意，在以下句子中，描述性单词在它们之间插入时听起来不自然。

college-writing-016257.en: In such cases, no comma is used.
college-writing-016257.zh: 在这种情况下，不使用逗号。

college-writing-016258.en: Micah wore a pale green tuxedo.
college-writing-016258.zh: Micah 穿着淡绿色的燕尾服。

college-writing-016259.en: (A pale and green tuxedo does not sound right, so no comma is used.)
college-writing-016259.zh: （淡绿色的燕尾服听起来不对，因此没有使用逗号。）

college-writing-016260.en: Place commas between items in a series.
college-writing-016260.zh: 在一个系列中的项目之间放置逗号。

college-writing-016261.en: 1. The American alligator lives in southern swamps streams lakes and other bodies of water.
college-writing-016261.zh: 1. 美国鳄鱼生活在南部沼泽溪流湖泊和其他水体中。

college-writing-016262.en: 2. Rudy stretched out on the swaying hammock popped open a frosty can of soda and balanced it carefully on his stomach.
college-writing-016262.zh: 2. 鲁迪在摇摇晃晃的吊床上伸了个懒腰，打开了一罐冰霜的苏打水，小心地在他的肚子上平衡了它。

college-writing-016263.en: 3. The children splashed through the warm deep swirling rainwater that flooded the street.
college-writing-016263.zh: 3. 孩子们在淹没街道的温暖的深水漩涡中溅起水花。

college-writing-016264.en: 4. The police officer’s warm brown eyes relaxed manner and pleasant smile made her easy to talk to.
college-writing-016264.zh: 4. 警官温暖的棕色眼睛放松的举止和愉快的笑容让她很容易交谈。

college-writing-016265.en: 5. The soft warm woolen blankets comforted us as we heard the cold north wind blow through the pines.
college-writing-016265.zh: 5. 当我们听到冰冷的北风吹过松树时，柔软温暖的羊毛毯让我们安慰。

college-writing-016266.en: Comma after Introductory Material Use a comma to set off introductory material.
college-writing-016266.zh: 介绍性材料后的逗号 用逗号引出介绍性材料。

college-writing-016267.en: Just in time, Leah applied the brakes and avoided a car accident.
college-writing-016267.zh: 正好，莉亚踩下了刹车，避免了车祸。

college-writing-016268.en: Muttering under his breath, Hassan reviewed the terms he had memorized.
college-writing-016268.zh: 哈桑低声喃喃，回顾了他记忆中的术语。

college-writing-016269.en: In a wolf pack, the dominant male holds his tail higher than the other pack members.
college-writing-016269.zh: 在狼群中，占主导地位的男性的尾巴比其他群组成员高。

college-writing-016272.zh: 在介绍性材料后放置逗号。

college-writing-016273.en: Once you have completed the activity, review your answers with a partner.
college-writing-016273.zh: 完成活动后，与合作伙伴一起查看您的答案。

college-writing-016274.en: 1. Although it cannot kill certain bacteria penicillin is still a useful antibiotic.
college-writing-016274.zh: 1.虽然它不能杀死某些细菌青霉素仍然是一种有用的抗生素。

college-writing-016275.en: 2. His heart pounding wildly Jesse opened the letter that would tell him whether he had been accepted to college.
college-writing-016275.zh: 2. 杰西疯狂地怦怦直跳，打开了这封信，告诉他他是否被大学录取了。

college-writing-016276.en: 3. Passing through fourteen states the Appalachian trail is over two thousand miles long.
college-writing-016276.zh: 3. 经过十四个州，阿巴拉契亚小径有两千多英里长。

college-writing-016277.en: 4. When the band hadn’t taken the stage forty-five minutes after the concert was supposed to begin the audience started shouting and stamping their feet.
college-writing-016277.zh: 4. 当乐队在音乐会应该开始四十五分钟后没有上台时，观众开始大喊大叫并跺脚。

college-writing-016278.en: 5. Along the side of the brook we noticed a newborn speckled fawn.
college-writing-016278.zh: 5. 在小溪的一侧，我们注意到一只新生的斑点小鹿。

college-writing-016279.en: Comma around Words That Interrupt the Flow of Thought Use a comma on both sides of words or phrases that interrupt the flow of thought in a sentence.
college-writing-016279.zh: 中断思想流的单词的逗号 在中断句子中的思想流动的单词或短语的两侧使用逗号。

college-writing-016280.en: The vinyl car seat, sticky from the heat, clung to my skin.
college-writing-016280.zh: 乙烯基汽车座椅，热得粘稠，粘在我的皮肤上。

college-writing-016281.en: Jake’s gaming system, which his wife got him as a birthday gift, occupies all his spare time.
college-writing-016281.zh: 杰克的游戏系统，他的妻子作为生日礼物送给他的，占据了他所有的业余时间。

college-writing-016282.en: The hallway, dingy and dark, was illuminated by a bare bulb.
college-writing-016282.zh: 走廊里昏暗而黑暗，被一个光秃秃的灯泡照亮。

college-writing-016283.en: Usually, by reading a sentence aloud, you can hear the words that interrupt the flow of thought.
college-writing-016283.zh: 通常，通过大声朗读句子，您可以听到中断思想流动的单词。

college-writing-016284.en: In cases where you are not sure if certain words are interrupters, remove them from the sentence.
college-writing-016284.zh: 如果您不确定某些单词是否是中断器，请将它们从句子中删除。

college-writing-016285.en: If it still makes sense without the words, you know that the words are interrupters and that the information they give is nonessential.
college-writing-016285.zh: 如果没有这些词仍然有意义，你就会知道这些词是打断者，而且它们提供的信息是非必要的。

college-writing-016286.en: Such nonessential or extra information is set off with commas.
college-writing-016286.zh: 这种非必要或额外的信息用逗号勾勒。

college-writing-016288.en: Sue Dodd, who goes to drumming class with me, was in a serious car accident.
college-writing-016288.zh: 和我一起去打鼓课的 Sue Dodd 发生了一场严重的车祸。

college-writing-016289.en: the words who goes to drumming class with me are extra information not needed to identify the subject of the sentence, Sue Dodd.
college-writing-016289.zh: 和我一起去打鼓课的词是识别句子主题的额外信息，Sue Dodd。

college-writing-016291.en: Although he had been first in the checkout line, Deion let an elderly woman go ahead of him.
college-writing-016291.zh: 虽然他在结账线上是第一位的，但戴恩还是让一位老妇人向他走来。

college-writing-016292.en: After the fire, we slogged through the ashes of the burned-out house.
college-writing-016292.zh: 大火过后，我们在烧毁的房子的灰烬中挣扎。

college-writing-016293.en: If the introductory material is brief, the comma is sometimes omitted.
college-writing-016293.zh: 如果介绍性材料是简短的，有时会省略逗号。

college-writing-016294.en: In the activities here, you should include the comma.
college-writing-016294.zh: 在此处的活动中，您应该包含逗号。

college-writing-016297.zh: 600 第四部分 句子技巧手册

college-writing-016299.en: Commas go around such nonessential information.
college-writing-016299.zh: 逗号绕过这些非必要的信息。

college-writing-016300.en: On the other hand, in the sentence

college-writing-016301.en: The woman who goes to drumming class with me was in a serious accident.
college-writing-016301.zh: 和我一起去打鼓课的女人发生了严重的事故。

college-writing-016302.en: the words who goes to drumming class with me supply essential information─ information needed for us to identify the woman being spoken of.
college-writing-016302.zh: 和我一起去打鼓课的话提供了重要的信息——我们需要识别被谈论的女人所需的信息。

college-writing-016303.en: If the words were removed from the sentence, we would no longer know exactly who was in the accident: “The woman was in a serious accident.”
college-writing-016303.zh: 如果从句子中删除这些词，我们将不再确切地知道是谁发生了事故：“这名妇女发生了严重的事故。”

college-writing-016305.en: Watership Down, a novel by Richard Adams, is the most thrilling adventure story I’ve ever read.
college-writing-016305.zh: Watership Down 是理查德·亚当斯 (Richard Adams) 的小说，是我读过的最激动人心的冒险故事。

college-writing-016306.en: Here the words a novel by Richard Adams could be left out, and we would still know the basic meaning of the sentence.
college-writing-016306.zh: 在这里，理查德·亚当斯的小说可能会被遗漏，我们仍然会知道这句话的基本含义。

college-writing-016307.en: Commas are placed around such nonessential material.
college-writing-016307.zh: 逗号放在这种非必要的材料周围。

college-writing-016309.en: Richard Adams’s novel Watership Down is the most thrilling adventure story I’ve ever read.
college-writing-016309.zh: 理查德·亚当斯的小说《Watership Down》是我读过的最激动人心的冒险故事。

college-writing-016310.en: the title of the novel is essential.
college-writing-016310.zh: 小说的标题是必不可少的。

college-writing-016311.en: Without it the sentence would read, “Richard Adams’s novel is the most thrilling adventure story I’ve ever read.”
college-writing-016311.zh: 没有它，这句话会写道：“理查德·亚当斯的小说是我读过的最激动人心的冒险故事。”

college-writing-016312.en: We would not know which of Richard Adams’s novels was so thrilling.
college-writing-016312.zh: 我们不知道理查德·亚当斯的哪些小说如此激动人心。

college-writing-016313.en: Commas are not used around the title, because it provides essential information.
college-writing-016313.zh: 标题不在标题周围使用，因为它提供了基本信息。

college-writing-016314.en: Most of the time you will be able to hear which words interrupt the flow of thought in a sentence and will not have to think about whether the words are essential or nonessential.
college-writing-016314.zh: 大多数时候，您将能够听到哪些单词中断了句子中的思想流，并且不必考虑这些单词是必不可少的还是非必要的。

college-writing-016315.en: Use commas to set off interrupting words.

college-writing-016316.en: 1. Two large pines located near my cabin were swaying in the cold winter wind.
college-writing-016316.zh: 1. 位于我小屋附近的两棵大松树在寒冷的冬风中摇曳。

college-writing-016317.en: 2. Hawaii which became the fiftieth state in 1959 is made up of eight major islands.
college-writing-016317.zh: 2. 1959 年成为第五十个州的夏威夷由八个主要岛屿组成。

college-writing-016318.en: 3. Nathan Bage an avid football fan watches college football on Saturdays and professional football on Sundays.
college-writing-016318.zh: 3. Nathan Bage 一位狂热的足球迷在周六观看大学橄榄球，周日观看职业足球比赛。

college-writing-016319.en: 4. The weather windy and wild created twenty-foot swells on the lake.
college-writing-016319.zh: 4. 大风和狂野的天气在湖上产生了 20 英尺的膨胀。

college-writing-016320.en: 5. A talented actress who has starred in many plays lives across the street.
college-writing-016320.zh: 5. 一位有才华的女演员，曾出演过街对面的许多戏剧生活。

college-writing-016321.en: Comma between Complete Thoughts Use a comma between two complete thoughts connected by and, but, for, or, nor, so, yet.
college-writing-016321.zh: 完整思想之间的逗号 在两个完整的思想之间使用逗号，但是，为，或，不，所以，所以。

college-writing-016322.en: Sam closed all the windows, but the predicted thunderstorm never arrived.
college-writing-016322.zh: 山姆关上了所有的窗户，但预计的雷暴从未到来。

college-writing-016323.en: I like wearing comfortable clothing, so I buy oversize shirts and sweaters.
college-writing-016323.zh: 我喜欢穿舒适的衣服，所以我买了超大号的衬衫和毛衣。

college-writing-016326.en: Riley attended The Culinary Institute of America, for she has a goal to become the best chef possible.
college-writing-016326.zh: 莱利就读于美国烹饪学院，因为她的目标是成为最好的厨师。

college-writing-016327.en: A. The comma is optional when the complete thoughts are short.
college-writing-016327.zh: A. 当完整的想法很短时，逗号是可选的。

college-writing-016328.en: The Ferris wheel started and Wilson closed his eyes.
college-writing-016328.zh: 摩天轮启动了，威尔逊闭上了眼睛。

college-writing-016329.en: Many people left but the band played on.
college-writing-016329.zh: 许多人离开了，但乐队继续演奏。

college-writing-016330.en: I made a wrong turn so I doubled back.
college-writing-016330.zh: 我做了一个错误的转弯，所以我加倍后退。

college-writing-016331.en: B. Be careful not to use a comma to separate two verbs that belong to one sub-
college-writing-016331.zh: B. 小心不要用逗号分隔属于一个子的两个动词

college-writing-016333.en: The comma is used only in sentences made up of two complete thoughts (two subjects and two verbs).
college-writing-016333.zh: 逗号仅用于由两个完整的想法（两个主语和两个动词）组成的句子中。

college-writing-016335.en: The doctor stared over his bifocals and lectured me about smoking.
college-writing-016335.zh: 医生盯着他的双焦点，向我讲授吸烟的知识。

college-writing-016336.en: there is only one subject (doctor) and a double verb (stared and lectured).
college-writing-016336.zh: 只有一个主语（医生）和一个双动词（盯着和讲课）。

college-writing-016339.en: Dean switched the lamp on and off and then tapped it with his fingers.
college-writing-016339.zh: 迪恩打开和关闭灯，然后用手指敲击它。

college-writing-016340.en: has only one subject (Dean) and a double verb (switched and tapped); therefore, no comma is needed.
college-writing-016340.zh: 只有一个主语（院长）和一个双动词（切换和敲击）； 因此，不需要逗号。

college-writing-016341.en: Place a comma before a joining word that connects two complete thoughts (two subjects and two verbs).
college-writing-016341.zh: 在连接两个完整想法（两个主语和两个动词）的连接词之前放置一个逗号。

college-writing-016342.en: Remember, do not place a comma within a sentence that has only one subject and a double verb.
college-writing-016342.zh: 请记住，不要在只有一个主语和一个双动词的句子中放置逗号。

college-writing-016343.en: Some items are correct as given.

college-writing-016344.en: For these items, write “Correct” at the end of the sentence.
college-writing-016344.zh: 对于这些项目，在句子的末尾写下“正确”。

college-writing-016345.zh: 1. 电视情景喜剧听起来很傻，但我把头从厨房里探了出来

college-writing-016347.zh: 2.在他出版他的第一部小说之前，去山上讲述，詹姆斯·鲍德温

college-writing-016349.en: 3. The fluffy frizzle chicken ran noisily around the coop for it was afraid of the
college-writing-016349.zh: 3. 蓬松的毛茸茸的鸡肉在鸡舍周围吵闹，因为它害怕

college-writing-016350.en: raccoon sitting outside the chicken wire.

college-writing-016351.en: 4. Orangutans are ideally suited for living in trees and they rarely climb down
college-writing-016351.zh: 4. 猩猩非常适合住在树上，它们很少爬下来

college-writing-016353.en: 5. Plastic surgery was developed to repair damaged tissue and it has helped
college-writing-016353.zh: 5. 整形手术是为了修复受损的组织而开发的，它有帮助

college-writing-016354.en: many war victims heal from injuries.
college-writing-016354.zh: 许多战争受害者从受伤中恢复过来。

college-writing-016355.en: 6. Allison was tired of summer reruns so she visited the town library to pick
college-writing-016355.zh: 6. 艾莉森厌倦了夏季重播，所以她参观了镇图书馆挑选

college-writing-016358.en: camera or you can visit a few stores’ websites to find it quickly.
college-writing-016358.zh: 相机或您可以访问一些商店的网站以快速找到它。

college-writing-016366.en: Comma with Direct Quotations Use a comma to set off a direct quotation from the rest of a sentence.
college-writing-016366.zh: 带有直接引号的逗号使用逗号来引出句子的其余部分的直接引号。

college-writing-016367.en: The carnival barker cried, “Step right up and win a prize!” “Be a good person to all around you,” the fortune cookie read.
college-writing-016367.zh: 狂欢巴克喊道：“站起来赢奖！” “做一个对你周围的好人，”幸运饼干写道。

college-writing-016369.en: “You’ll have to wait.” “For my first writing assignment,” said Scott, “I have to turn in a five-hundredword description of a stone.”
college-writing-016369.zh: “你得等。” “对于我的第一个写作作业，”斯科特说，“我必须上交五百字对一块石头的描述。”

college-writing-016371.en: Commas and periods at the end of a quotation go inside quotation marks.
college-writing-016371.zh: 报价结束时的逗号和句点进入引号内。

college-writing-016373.zh: 使用逗号来引出句子的其余部分的直接引用。

college-writing-016376.en: “How can I ever repay you for all you’ve done?”

college-writing-016377.zh: 3. 老师宣布“明天将是我们最后一天的国家考试”。

college-writing-016378.en: 4. “I know you did it” the detective accused the murderer “and I can prove it!”
college-writing-016378.zh: 4. “我知道你做到了” 侦探指控凶手“我可以证明！”

college-writing-016379.en: 5. “Please remember to watch the gap” the conductor warned.

college-writing-016380.en: Comma with Everyday Material Use a comma when a person is spoken to.
college-writing-016380.zh: 与日常材料通话时，与人交谈时使用逗号的逗号。

college-writing-016381.en: If you’re the last to leave, Nicholas, please switch off the lights.
college-writing-016381.zh: 如果你是最后一个离开的，尼古拉斯，请关掉灯。

college-writing-016382.zh: 迪伦，我认为我们走错了路。

college-writing-016383.en: Use a comma after the salutation of a friendly letter and after the salutation and closing of a friendly and a formal letter.
college-writing-016383.zh: 在友好的信的问候和友好和正式的信的致敬和结束后使用逗号。

college-writing-016389.zh: 除年数和街道号外，以四位数或更多的数字使用逗号。

college-writing-016390.zh: 2008 年，保险代理人卖给我一份 50,000 美元的定期人寿保险单。

college-writing-016391.en: Use commas in dates and in addresses as illustrated.
college-writing-016391.zh: 如图所示，在日期和地址中使用逗号。

college-writing-016392.zh: 1980 年 7 月 4 日，是我哥哥的生日。

college-writing-016393.zh: 布朗小学位于马萨诸塞州韦勒姆市牛奶街20号，02571。

college-writing-016395.zh: 在邮政编码之前没有使用逗号。

college-writing-016397.zh: 将逗号放在需要的地方。

college-writing-016758.en: This chapter will give you practice in avoiding slang, clichés, and pretentious words.
college-writing-016758.zh: 本章将为您提供避免俚语、陈词滥调和自命不凡的词语的练习。

college-writing-016760.en: cliché: an expression that has been worn out through constant use.
college-writing-016760.zh: 陈词滥调：通过不断使用而磨损的表达方式。

college-writing-016762.en: pretentious language: artificial or stilted expressions that more often obscure meaning than communicate it clearly.
college-writing-016762.zh: 自命不凡的语言：人为的或生硬的表达方式，往往掩盖了意义，而不是清晰地传达它。

college-writing-016763.en: Example: It was a splendid opportunity to obtain some slumber could be more simply expressed as It was a good chance to get some sleep.
college-writing-016763.zh: 示例：这是一个获得沉睡的绝佳机会，可以更简单地表达出来，因为这是一个睡觉的好机会。

college-writing-016764.en: slang: nonstandard language particular to a time and often to a specific locale; acceptable in everyday speech, slang should be avoided in formal contexts and, with few exceptions, in writing.
college-writing-016764.zh: 俚语：特定于时间的非标准语言，通常是特定的地区； 在日常演讲中可以接受，俚语应该在正式的环境中避免，除了少数例外，还要以书面形式避免。

college-writing-016765.en: Example: I’m going to have to sweat it out for the next couple of days until the test results are posted would be more appropriately expressed as I’m going to have to wait anxiously for the next couple of days until the test results are posted.
college-writing-016765.zh: 示例：在接下来的几天里，我将不得不出汗，直到发布测试结果会更恰当地表达，因为我将不得不焦急地等待接下来的几天，直到发布测试结果。

college-writing-016766.en: Choose your words carefully when you write.
college-writing-016766.zh: 写作时要仔细选择你的文字。

college-writing-016767.en: Always take the time to think about your word choices rather than simply use the first word that comes to mind.
college-writing-016767.zh: 总是花时间思考你的单词选择，而不是简单地使用想到的第一个词。

college-writing-016768.en: You want to develop the habit of selecting words that are precise and appropriate for your purpose.
college-writing-016768.zh: 您想养成选择精确且适合您目的的单词的习惯。

college-writing-016769.en: One way you can show sensitivity to language is by avoiding slang, clichés, and pretentious words.

college-writing-016772.en: However, slang is usually out of place in formal writing.
college-writing-016772.zh: 然而，俚语在正式写作中通常是格格不入的。

college-writing-016781.en: Slang expressions have a number of drawbacks.
college-writing-016781.zh: slang 表达式有许多缺点。

college-writing-016782.en: They go out of date quickly, they become tiresome if used excessively in writing, and they may communicate clearly to some readers but not to others.
college-writing-016782.zh: 它们很快就过时了，如果在写作中过度使用，它们会变得令人厌烦，它们可能会与一些读者清楚地交流，但不会与其他读者进行清晰的交流。

college-writing-016783.en: Also, the use of slang can be an evasion of the specific details that are often needed to make one’s meaning clear in writing.
college-writing-016783.zh: 此外，俚语的使用可能是对特定细节的回避，这些细节通常需要以书面形式明确一个人的意思。

college-writing-016784.en: For example, in “The movie really grossed me out,” the writer has not provided the specific details about the movie necessary for us to clearly understand the statement.
college-writing-016784.zh: 例如，在“这部电影真的让我很恶心”中，作者没有提供我们清楚理解陈述所需的电影的具体细节。

college-writing-016785.en: Was it acting, special effects, or violent scenes that the writer found so disgusting?
college-writing-016785.zh: 是作者觉得如此恶心的表演、特效还是暴力场景？

college-writing-016786.en: In general, then, you should avoid slang in your writing.
college-writing-016786.zh: 那么，一般来说，你应该避免写作中的俚语。

college-writing-016787.en: If you are in doubt about whether an expression is slang, it may help to check a recently published hardbound or electronic dictionary.
college-writing-016787.zh: 如果您对一个表达式是否是俚语有疑问，请检查最近出版的精装本或电子词典。

college-writing-016805.en: A cliché is an expression that has been worn out through constant use.
college-writing-016805.zh: 陈词滥调是一种通过不断使用而磨损的表达方式。

college-writing-016806.zh: 以下是一些典型的陈词滥调：

college-writing-016807.en: short but sweet at a loss for words drop in the bucket taking a big chance had a hard time of it took a turn for the worse word to the wise singing the blues it dawned on me in the nick of time sigh of relief too close for comfort too little, too late saw the light last but not least easier said than done work like a dog on top of the world all work and no play time and time again it goes without saying make ends meet
college-writing-016807.zh: short but sweet：简短而精彩；at a loss for words：一时语塞；drop in the bucket：杯水车薪；taking a big chance：冒很大的险；had a hard time of it：经历了一段艰难时期；took a turn for the worse：情况恶化；word to the wise：一句善意提醒；singing the blues：心情低落，诉说烦恼；it dawned on me：我恍然大悟；in the nick of time：千钧一发之际；sigh of relief：松了一口气；too close for comfort：近得让人不安；too little, too late：为时已晚，所做又太少；saw the light：终于明白；last but not least：最后一项同样重要；easier said than done：说起来容易，做起来难；work like a dog：拼命工作；on top of the world：欣喜若狂；all work and no play：只工作不娱乐；time and time again：一次又一次；it goes without saying：不言而喻；make ends meet：勉强维持收支平衡。

college-writing-016808.en: Clichés are common in speech but make your writing seem tired and stale.
college-writing-016808.zh: 陈词滥调在演讲中很常见，但会让你的写作显得疲惫和陈旧。

college-writing-016809.en: Also, they are often an evasion of the specific details that you must work to provide in your writing.
college-writing-016809.zh: 此外，它们通常是对您必须在写作中提供的具体细节的回避。

college-writing-016810.en: You should, then, avoid clichés and try to express your meaning in fresh, original ways.
college-writing-016810.zh: 那么，你应该避免陈词滥调，并尝试以新鲜、原创的方式表达你的意义。

college-writing-016812.en: Then substitute specific, fresh words for the trite expression.
college-writing-016812.zh: 然后用具体的、新鲜的词代替陈词滥调。

college-writing-016836.zh: 写一段简短的段落，描述你所度过的一天。

college-writing-016837.zh: 尝试将尽可能多的陈词滥调放入其中。

college-writing-016838.en: For example, “I got up at the crack of dawn, ready to take on the world. I grabbed a bite to eat. . . .”
college-writing-016838.zh: 比如，“我在黎明时分起床，准备迎接世界。我吃了一口吃的……”

college-writing-016843.en: Some people feel that they can improve their writing by using fancy, elevated words rather than simple, natural words.
college-writing-016843.zh: 有些人觉得他们可以通过使用花哨、高架的单词而不是简单、自然的单词来提高他们的写作能力。

college-writing-016844.en: They use artificial, stilted language that more often obscures their meaning than communicates it clearly.
college-writing-016844.zh: 他们使用人为的、生硬的语言，这些语言通常掩盖了它们的含义，而不是清楚地传达它。

college-writing-016845.en: This frequently occurs when students attempt to use a dictionary or thesaurus, but just pick words at random to replace the simpler words.
college-writing-016845.zh: 当学生尝试使用字典或词库时，通常会发生这种情况，但只是随机选择单词来代替更简单的单词。

college-writing-016846.en: Using college-level vocabulary is a way to improve your writing, but you must be careful in choosing words.
college-writing-016846.zh: 使用大学水平的词汇是提高写作的一种方式，但你在选择单词时必须小心。

college-writing-016847.en: Not only can certain choices sound artificial, but another problem may arise when words are chosen without enough thought.
college-writing-016847.zh: 不仅某些选择听起来是人为的，而且如果在没有足够思想的情况下选择单词，可能会出现另一个问题。

college-writing-016848.en: Because many words can act as nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs, using the wrong part of speech often leads to obscured meaning.
college-writing-016848.zh: 因为许多词可以充当名词、动词、形容词和副词，使用错误的词性部分往往会导致含义。
