college-writing-017392.en: The eighteen reading selections in Part 5 will help you find topics for writing.
college-writing-017392.zh: 第 5 部分中的 18 个阅读选择将帮助您找到写作主题。

college-writing-017393.en: (Note that there are also nine professional essays in Part 2.)
college-writing-017393.zh: （请注意，第 2 部分中也有九篇专业论文。）

college-writing-017394.en: These selections deal in various ways with interesting, often thought-provoking concerns or experiences of contemporary life.
college-writing-017394.zh: 这些选择以各种方式处理当代生活中有趣的、发人深省的关注或经历。

college-writing-017395.en: Subjects of the essays include the power of family and self; life goals; practical advice on surviving the first year of college; ways in which the Internet may be affecting our thinking; ways people change society; a comparison of academic writing and public writing; and the challenges of everyday life.
college-writing-017395.zh: 论文的主题包括家庭和自我的力量； 人生目标； 关于大学第一年生存的实用建议； 互联网可能影响我们思想的方式； 人们改变社会的方式； 学术写作和公开写作的比较； 以及日常生活的挑战。

college-writing-017396.en: The varied subjects should inspire lively class discussions as well as serious individual thought.
college-writing-017396.zh: 不同的主题应该激发生动的课堂讨论以及严肃的个人思考。

college-writing-017397.en: The selections should also provide a continuing source of high-interest material for a wide range of writing assignments.
college-writing-017397.zh: 选择还应为广泛的写作作业提供持续的高息材料来源。

college-writing-017398.en: The selections serve another purpose as well.

college-writing-017399.en: They will help develop reading skills, with direct benefits to you as a writer.
college-writing-017399.zh: 他们将帮助发展阅读技能，直接对您作为作家有利。

college-writing-017400.en: One benefit is that, through close reading, you will learn how to recognize the thesis in a selection and to identify and evaluate the supporting material that develops the thesis.
college-writing-017400.zh: 一个好处是，通过仔细阅读，您将学习如何在选拔中识别论文，并识别和评估开发论文的支持材料。

college-writing-017401.en: In your own writing, you will aim to achieve the same essential structure: an overall thesis followed by detailed, valid support for that thesis.
college-writing-017401.zh: 在你自己的写作中，你的目标是实现相同的基本结构：一个整体论文，然后是对该论文的详细、有效的支持。

college-writing-017402.en: A second benefit is that close reading will also help you explore a selection and its possibilities thoroughly.
college-writing-017402.zh: 第二个好处是仔细阅读还将帮助您彻底探索选择及其可能性。

college-writing-017403.en: The more you understand about what is said in a piece, the more ideas and feelings you may have about writing on an assigned topic or a related topic of your own.
college-writing-017403.zh: 您对一篇文章中所说的内容了解得越多，您对指定主题或相关主题的写作的想法和感受就越多。

college-writing-017404.en: A third benefit of close reading is that you will become more aware of authors’ stylistic devices─for example, their introductions and conclusions, their ways of presenting and developing a point, their use of transitions, and their choice of language to achieve a particular tone.
college-writing-017404.zh: 仔细阅读的第三个好处是，你将更加了解作者的风格手段——例如，他们的介绍和结论、他们呈现和发展一个点的方式、他们对过渡的使用以及他们选择的语言来实现特定的语气。

college-writing-017405.en: Recognizing these devices in other people’s writing will help you enlarge your own range of ideas and writing techniques.
college-writing-017405.zh: 在其他人的写作中识别这些设备将帮助您扩大自己的想法和写作技巧范围。

college-writing-017407.en: Each selection begins with a short overview that gives helpful background information as well as a brief idea of the topic of the reading.
college-writing-017407.zh: 每个选择都以简短的概述开始，该概述提供了有用的背景信息以及对阅读主题的简要了解。

college-writing-017408.en: The selection is followed by three sets of questions:

college-writing-017409.en: • First, ten “Reading Comprehension” questions help you measure your understanding of the material.
college-writing-017409.zh: • 首先，十个“阅读理解”问题可以帮助您衡量对材料的理解。

college-writing-017410.en: These questions involve several important reading skills: understanding vocabulary in context, recognizing a subject or topic, determining a thesis or main idea, identifying key supporting points, and making inferences.
college-writing-017410.zh: 这些问题涉及几个重要的阅读技巧：在上下文中理解词汇、识别主题或主题、确定论文或主要思想、确定关键支持点和做出推论。

college-writing-017411.en: Answering the questions will enable you and your
college-writing-017411.zh: 回答这些问题将使您和您的

college-writing-017414.en: instructor to quickly check your basic understanding of a selection.
college-writing-017414.zh: 教师快速检查您对选择的基本理解。

college-writing-017415.en: More significantly, as you move from one selection to the next, you will sharpen your reading skills as well as strengthen your thinking skills─two key factors in making you a better writer.
college-writing-017415.zh: 更重要的是，当您从一种选择转移到另一种选择时，您将提高您的阅读能力并增强您的思维能力——使您成为更好的作家的两个关键因素。

college-writing-017416.en: • Following the comprehension questions are four questions on “Structure and Technique” that focus on aspects of a writer’s craft, and four questions on “Critical Reading and Discussion” that involve you in reading carefully and thinking actively about a writer’s ideas.
college-writing-017416.zh: • 遵循理解问题的是四个关于“结构和技术”的问题，重点关注作家手艺的各个方面，以及四个关于“批判性阅读和讨论”的问题，这些问题涉及您仔细阅读和积极思考作家的想法。

college-writing-017417.en: Finally, several writing assignments accompany each selection.
college-writing-017417.zh: 最后，每个选择都伴随着几个写作作业。

college-writing-017418.en: The assignments range from personal narratives to expository and persuasive essays about issues in the world at large.
college-writing-017418.zh: 这些作业的范围从个人叙述到关于整个世界问题的说明性和有说服力的文章。

college-writing-017419.en: Many assignments provide detailed guidelines on how to proceed, including suggestions for prewriting and appropriate methods of development.
college-writing-017419.zh: 许多作业提供了有关如何进行的详细指南，包括预写建议和适当的开发方法。

college-writing-017420.en: When writing your essay responses to the readings, you will have opportunities to apply all the methods of development presented in Part 2 of this book.
college-writing-017420.zh: 在撰写对阅读材料的论文回复时，您将有机会应用本书第 2 部分中介绍的所有发展方法。

college-writing-017421.en: How to Read Well: Four General Steps
college-writing-017421.zh: 如何阅读：四个一般步骤

college-writing-017422.en: Skillful reading is an important part of becoming a skillful writer.
college-writing-017422.zh: 熟练的阅读是成为一名熟练作家的重要组成部分。

college-writing-017423.en: Following is a series of four steps that will make you a better reader─of the selections here and in your reading at large.
college-writing-017423.zh: 以下是一系列四个步骤，它们将使您更好地阅读这里和您的阅读中的选择。

college-writing-017424.en: 1. Concentrate as You Read To improve your concentration, follow these tips:
college-writing-017424.zh: 1. 在阅读时集中注意力 为了提高注意力，请遵循以下提示：

college-writing-017425.en: • First, read in a place where you can be quiet and alone.
college-writing-017425.zh: • 首先，在您可以安静和孤独的地方阅读。

college-writing-017426.en: Don’t choose a spot where there are a lot of distractions like TV, music, friends, or family.
college-writing-017426.zh: 不要选择一个有很多分心的地方，比如电视、音乐、朋友或家人。

college-writing-017427.en: • Next, sit upright when you read.

college-writing-017428.en: If your body is in a completely relaxed position, sprawled across a bed or nestled in an easy chair, your mind is also going to be completely relaxed.
college-writing-017428.zh: 如果你的身体处于完全放松的位置，躺在床上或依偎在安乐椅上，你的大脑也会完全放松。

college-writing-017429.en: The light muscular tension that comes from sitting in a straight chair promotes concentration and keeps your mind ready to work.
college-writing-017429.zh: 坐在直椅上的轻微肌肉张力促进了注意力，让您的大脑做好了工作的准备。

college-writing-017430.en: • Third, consider using your index finger (or a pen) as a pacer while you read.
college-writing-017430.zh: • 第三，在阅读时考虑使用食指（或笔）作为起搏器。

college-writing-017431.en: Lightly underline each line of print with your index finger as you read down a page.
college-writing-017431.zh: 当您阅读页面时，用食指轻轻下划线。

college-writing-017432.en: Hold your hand slightly above the page and move your finger at a speed that is a little too fast for comfort.
college-writing-017432.zh: 将手稍微放在页面上方，以有点太快的速度移动手指，无法舒适。

college-writing-017433.en: This pacing with your index finger, like sitting upright in a chair, creates a slight physical tension that will keep your body and mind focused and alert.
college-writing-017433.zh: 这种用食指的节奏，就像坐在椅子上一样，会产生轻微的身体紧张，让您的身体和精神保持专注和警觉。

college-writing-017434.zh: 644 第 5 部分 作者的阅读

college-writing-017435.en: 2. Skim Material Before You Read It In skimming, you spend about two minutes rapidly surveying a selection, looking for important points and skipping secondary material.
college-writing-017435.zh: 2. 略读材料 在您阅读时，您会花大约两分钟的时间快速调查一个选择，寻找要点并跳过次要材料。

college-writing-017437.en: • Begin by reading the overview that precedes the selection.
college-writing-017437.zh: • 首先阅读选择之前的概述。

college-writing-017438.en: • Then study the title of the selection for a few moments.
college-writing-017438.zh: • 然后研究选择的标题片刻。

college-writing-017439.en: A good title is the shortest possible summary of a selection; it often tells you in a single word or a few words what a selection is about.
college-writing-017439.zh: 一个好的标题是选择的最短可能的摘要； 它经常用一个词或几个词告诉你一个选择的内容。

college-writing-017440.en: For example, the title “The Professor Is a Dropout” suggests that you’re going to read about an intriguing, important aspect of someone’s work and life.
college-writing-017440.zh: 例如，“教授是一个辍学者”的标题表明你将阅读某人工作和生活中一个有趣、重要的方面。

college-writing-017441.en: • Next, form a question (or questions) based on the title.
college-writing-017441.zh: • 接下来，根据标题形成一个问题（或多个问题）。

college-writing-017442.en: For instance, for the selection titled “The Professor Is a Dropout,” you might ask, “What exactly did the professor drop out of? Did the professor drop out of teaching? Did the professor drop out of school? If so, how would that person become a professor?”
college-writing-017442.zh: 例如，对于题为“教授是一个辍学者”的选择，你可能会问：“教授到底是怎么掉了的？教授有没有辍学？教授是辍学了吗？如果是的话，那个人怎么会成为教授？”

college-writing-017443.en: Using a title to form questions is often a key to locating a writer’s thesis, your next concern in skimming.
college-writing-017443.zh: 使用标题来形成问题通常是定位作者论文的关键，这是您浏览的下一个问题。

college-writing-017444.en: • Read the first and last couple of paragraphs in the selection.
college-writing-017444.zh: • 阅读选择中的第一段和最后几段。

college-writing-017445.en: Very often a writer’s thesis, if it is directly stated, will appear in one of these places and will relate to the title.
college-writing-017445.zh: 很多时候，作者的论文，如果直接陈述的话，会出现在这些地方之一，并与标题有关。

college-writing-017446.en: For instance, in “The Certainty of Fear” the author says in her final paragraph that “[e]very stage of life brings them; while we may say goodbye to childish fears, there are always others in the wings, waiting to take their place.”
college-writing-017446.zh: 例如，在“恐惧的确定性”中，作者在她的最后一段中说：“生命的每一个阶段都会带来它们；虽然我们可以对幼稚的恐惧说再见，但总有其他人在等待着取代它们的位置。”

college-writing-017447.en: • Finally, look quickly at the rest of the selection for other clues to important points.
college-writing-017447.zh: • 最后，快速查看其余选择以获取重要点的其他线索。

college-writing-017448.en: Are there any subheads you can relate in some way to the title?
college-writing-017448.zh: 是否有任何子标题可以以某种方式与标题相关联？

college-writing-017449.en: Are there any words the author has decided to emphasize by setting them off in italic or boldface type?
college-writing-017449.zh: 作者有没有决定通过斜体或粗体字体来强调它们？

college-writing-017450.en: Are there any major lists of items signaled by words such as first, second, also, another, and so on?
college-writing-017450.zh: 是否有以第一、第二、第二、另一个等词表示的主要项目列表？

college-writing-017451.en: 3. Read the Selection Straight Through with a Pen in Hand Read the selection without slowing down or turning back; just aim to understand as much as you can the first time through.
college-writing-017451.zh: 3. 用笔直接阅读选择 阅读选择，不要放慢速度或回头； 只是为了在第一次通过时尽可能多地理解。

college-writing-017452.en: Write a check or star beside answers to basic questions you formed from the title and beside other ideas that seem important.
college-writing-017452.zh: 在您从标题中形成的基本问题以及其他看起来很重要的想法的答案旁边写支票或星号。

college-writing-017453.en: Number lists of important points: 1, 2, 3, and so on.

college-writing-017455.en: Write question marks in the margins next to passages that are unclear and that you will want to reread.
college-writing-017455.zh: 在不清楚的段落旁边的页边空白处写下问号，并且您会想要重读。

college-writing-017456.en: 4. Work with the Material Go back and reread passages that were not clear the first time through.
college-writing-017456.zh: 4. 使用材料返回并重读第一次不清楚的段落。

college-writing-017457.en: Look up words that block your understanding of ideas and write their meanings in the
college-writing-017457.zh: 查找阻碍您对想法的理解的单词并将其含义写在

college-writing-017459.en: Also, reread carefully the areas you identified as most important; doing so will enlarge your understanding of the material.
college-writing-017459.zh: 此外，请仔细阅读您确定为最重要的领域； 这样做将扩大您对材料的理解。

college-writing-017460.en: Now that you have a sense of the whole, prepare a short written outline of the selection by answering these questions:
college-writing-017460.zh: 既然您对整体有了了解，请通过回答以下问题来准备一份简短的书面选拔大纲：

college-writing-017462.en: • What key points support the thesis?

college-writing-017463.en: • What seem to be other important ideas in the selection?
college-writing-017463.zh: • 选择中的其他重要想法似乎是什么？

college-writing-017464.en: By working with the material in this way, you will significantly increase your understanding of a selection.
college-writing-017464.zh: 通过以这种方式使用材料，您将显着增加对选择的理解。

college-writing-017465.en: Effective reading, just like effective writing, does not happen all at once.
college-writing-017465.zh: 有效的阅读，就像有效的写作一样，不会同时发生。

college-writing-017466.en: Rather, it must be worked on.

college-writing-017467.en: Often you begin with a general impression of what something means, and then, by working at it, you move to a deeper level of understanding.
college-writing-017467.zh: 通常，您从对某事的含义的一般印象开始，然后，通过工作，您可以进入更深层次的理解。

college-writing-017468.en: How to Answer the Comprehension Questions: Specific Hints
college-writing-017468.zh: 如何回答理解问题：具体提示

college-writing-017469.en: The ten reading comprehension questions that follow each selection involve several important reading skills:
college-writing-017469.zh: 每个选择之后的十个阅读理解问题涉及几个重要的阅读技能：

college-writing-017471.en: • summarizing the selection in a title

college-writing-017473.zh: • 识别钥匙 支撑细节

college-writing-017475.en: The following hints will help you apply each of these reading skills:
college-writing-017475.zh: 以下提示将帮助您应用这些阅读技能：

college-writing-017477.en: To decide on the meaning of an unfamiliar word, consider its context.
college-writing-017477.zh: 要决定一个不熟悉的词的含义，请考虑它的上下文。

college-writing-017478.en: Ask yourself, “Are there any clues in the sentence that suggest what this word means?”
college-writing-017478.zh: 问问自己：“句子中有没有暗示这个词的意思的线索？”

college-writing-017480.en: Remember that the title should accurately describe the entire selection.
college-writing-017480.zh: 请记住，标题应准确描述整个选择。

college-writing-017481.en: It should be neither too broad nor too narrow for the material in the selection.
college-writing-017481.zh: 对于选择中的材料，它应该既不太宽也不太窄。

college-writing-017482.en: It should answer the question “What is this about?” as specifically as possible.
college-writing-017482.zh: 它应该回答“这是关于什么的？”这个问题。 尽可能具体。

college-writing-017483.en: Note that you may at times find it easier to answer the title question after the main-idea question.
college-writing-017483.zh: 请注意，您有时可能会发现在主思想问题之后更容易回答标题问题。

college-writing-017485.en: Choose the statement that you think best expresses the main idea─also known as the central point, or thesis─of the entire selection.
college-writing-017485.zh: 选择你认为最能表达你认为最能表达的主要思想的陈述——也称为中心点，或整个选择的论点。

college-writing-017486.en: Remember that the title will often help you focus on the main idea.
college-writing-017486.zh: 请记住，标题通常会帮助您专注于主要思想。

college-writing-017487.en: Then ask yourself, “Does most of the material in the selection support this statement?”
college-writing-017487.zh: 然后问自己，“选拔中的大部分材料是否支持这种说法？”

college-writing-017488.en: If you can answer yes, you have found the thesis.
college-writing-017488.zh: 如果你能回答是，你就找到了论文。

college-writing-017490.zh: 646 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-017492.en: If you were asked to give a two-minute summary of a selection, the key, or major, details are the ones you would include in that summary.
college-writing-017492.zh: 如果您被要求对选择、关键或主要内容进行两分钟的总结，则详细信息是您将在该摘要中包含的详细信息。

college-writing-017493.en: To determine the key details, ask yourself, “What are the major supporting points for the thesis?”
college-writing-017493.zh: 要确定关键细节，问问自己：“论文的主要支持点是什么？”

college-writing-017495.en: Answer these questions by drawing on the evidence presented in the selection and your own common sense.
college-writing-017495.zh: 通过利用选择和您自己的常识中提供的证据来回答这些问题。

college-writing-017496.en: Ask yourself, “What reasonable judgments can I make on the basis of the information in the selection?”
college-writing-017496.zh: 问问自己：“我可以根据选择中的信息做出哪些合理的判断？”

college-writing-017497.en: The readings in Part 5 are categorized according to three main themes: Building Self-Awareness; Education and Learning; and Challenging Societal Values.
college-writing-017497.zh: 第 5 部分中的读数根据三个主要主题分类：建立自我意识； 教育和学习； 和具有挑战性的社会价值观。

college-writing-017498.en: Additionally, these readings represent how authors use a variety of rhetorical modes within their essays to support their points.
college-writing-017498.zh: 此外，这些读物代表了作者如何在论文中使用各种修辞模式来支持他们的观点。

college-writing-017499.en: A complete list of these readings, grouped by rhetorical mode, is provided at the front of this book.
college-writing-017499.zh: 本书正面提供了按修辞模式分组的这些读物的完整列表。

college-writing-017500.en: It is titled “Readings Listed by Rhetorical Mode” and directly follows the Table of Contents.
college-writing-017500.zh: 它的标题是“按修辞模式列出的读数”，直接跟随目录。

college-writing-017501.en: Note that that list includes the Part 2 essays as well.
college-writing-017501.zh: 请注意，该列表还包括第 2 部分论文。

college-writing-017506.zh: 来自自力更生的拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生 648

college-writing-017507.en: I Became Her Target Roger Wilkins 653
college-writing-017507.zh: 我成了她的目标罗杰威尔金斯 653

college-writing-017508.en: Stepping into the Light Tanya Savory 660

college-writing-017509.en: The Certainty of Fear Audra Kendall 669
college-writing-017509.zh: 恐惧的确定性 奥德拉·肯德尔 669

college-writing-017510.en: 100 Years of The Secret Garden Gretchen Holbrook Gerzina 676
college-writing-017510.zh: 100年的秘密花园格雷琴霍尔布鲁克格尔齐纳676

college-writing-017511.zh: 648 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-017512.en: There is a time in every man’s education when he arrives at the conviction that envy is ignorance; that imitation is suicide; that he must take himself for better for worse as his portion; that though the wide universe is full of good, no kernel of nourishing corn can come to him but through his toil bestowed on that plot of ground which is given to him to till .
college-writing-017512.zh: 每个人的教育中都有一段时间，他确信嫉妒是无知； 模仿是自杀； 他必须把自己当作更坏的部分； 尽管广阔的宇宙充满了美好，但没有任何滋养玉米的核心可以来到他身边，而是通过他的辛劳所赐给他的那块土地。

college-writing-017513.en: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
college-writing-017513.zh: 相信自己：每一颗心都在那根铁弦上振动。

college-writing-017514.en: Accept the place the divine providence has found for you, the society of your contemporaries, the connection of events.
college-writing-017514.zh: 接受神圣为你找到的地方，你同时代人的社会，事件的联系。

college-writing-017515.en: Great men have always done so, and confided themselves childlike to the genius of their age, betraying their perception that the absolutely trustworthy was seated at their heart, working through their hands, predominating in all their being .
college-writing-017515.zh: 伟大的人总是这样做，并向他们这个时代的天才倾诉自己，背叛了他们认为绝对值得信赖的人坐在他们的心里，通过他们的手工作，在他们的所有存在中占主导地位的看法。

college-writing-017516.en: Whoso would be a man, must be a nonconformist.
college-writing-017516.zh: 谁会是一个人，必须是一个不墨守成规的人。

college-writing-017517.en: He who would gather immortal palms must not be hindered by the name of goodness, but must explore if it be goodness.
college-writing-017517.zh: 收集不朽的手掌的人不能以善良的名义阻碍，而必须探索是否是善的。

college-writing-017518.en: Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
college-writing-017518.zh: 没有什么是神圣的，只有你自己思想的完整性。

college-writing-017519.en: Absolve you to yourself, and you shall have the suffrage of the world.
college-writing-017519.zh: 将你赦免，你将拥有世界的选举权。

college-writing-017520.en: I remember an answer which when quite young I was prompted to make to a valued adviser, who was wont to importune me with the dear old doctrines of the church.
college-writing-017520.zh: 我记得一个答案，当我很小的时候，我被提示向一位尊贵的顾问提出一个答案，他习惯于让我了解教会的老教义。

college-writing-017521.en: On my saying, “What have I to do with the sacredness of traditions, if I live wholly from within?” my friend suggested,─“But these impulses may be from below, not from above.”
college-writing-017521.zh: 在我的话中，“如果我完全从内部生活，我与传统的神圣性有什么关系？” 我的朋友建议，“但这些冲动可能来自下面，而不是来自上面。”

college-writing-017522.en: I replied, “They do not seem to me to be such; but if I am the Devil’s child, I will live then from the Devil.”
college-writing-017522.zh: 我回答说：“在我看来，他们不是这样的；但如果我是魔鬼的孩子，我将从魔鬼那里活着。”

college-writing-017523.en: No law can be sacred to me but that of my nature.
college-writing-017523.zh: 除了我的本性，没有任何法律对我来说是神圣的。

college-writing-017524.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson was born on May 25, 1803, in Boston, Massachusetts.
college-writing-017524.zh: 拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生于 1803 年 5 月 25 日出生于马萨诸塞州波士顿。

college-writing-017525.en: He is known as an essayist, poet, and the “philosophical voice of the nine-
college-writing-017525.zh: 他被称为散文家、诗人和“九人的哲学声音”

college-writing-017527.en: ” He graduated from Harvard Divinity School and

college-writing-017528.en: was ordained as a minister, but resigned after the death of his first wife.

college-writing-017529.en: After his marriage to his second wife, Emerson settled into a life of reading,

college-writing-017539.en: Good and bad are but names very readily transferable to that or this; the only right is what is after my constitution, the only wrong what is against it .

college-writing-017541.en: This rule, equally arduous in actual and in intellectual life, may serve for the whole distinction between greatness and meanness.

college-writing-017542.en: It is the harder because you will always find those who think they know what is your duty better than you know it.

college-writing-017543.en: It is easy in the world to live after the world’s opinion; it is easy in solitude to live after our own; but the great man is he who in the midst of the crowd keeps with perfect sweetness the independence of solitude .

college-writing-017544.en: For nonconformity the world whips you with its displeasure.

college-writing-017545.en: And therefore a man must know how to estimate a sour face.

college-writing-017546.en: The by-standers look askance on him in the public street or in the friend’s parlor.

college-writing-017547.en: If this aversion had its origin in contempt and resistance like his own he might well go home with a sad countenance; but the sour faces of the multitude, like their sweet faces, have no deep cause, but are put on and off as the wind blows and a newspaper direct .

college-writing-017548.en: The other terror that scares us from self-trust is our consistency; a reverence for our past act or word, because the eyes of others have no other data for computing our orbit than our past acts, and we are loath to disappoint them .
college-writing-017548.zh: 另一个让我们害怕自信的恐惧是我们的一致性； 对我们过去的行为或言语的崇敬，因为他人的眼睛除了我们过去的行为之外没有其他数据可以计算我们的轨道，我们不愿让他们失望。

college-writing-017549.en: A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds, adored by little statesmen and philosophers and divines.
college-writing-017549.zh: 一个愚蠢的一致性是小思想的大地精，受到小政治家、哲学家和神灵的崇拜。

college-writing-017550.en: With consistency a great soul has simply nothing to do.
college-writing-017550.zh: 凭借一致性，一个伟大的灵魂根本无事可做。

college-writing-017552.en: Speak what you think now in hard words, and tomorrow speak what tomorrow thinks in hard words again, though it contradict every thing you said today.
college-writing-017552.zh: 用严厉的语言说出你现在的想法，明天再用严厉的语言说出明天的想法，尽管这与你今天所说的每一件事相矛盾。

college-writing-017553.en: ─“Ah, so you shall be sure to be misunderstood.”─Is it so bad, then, to be misunderstood?

college-writing-017649.en: Respond to Emerson’s essay and his central idea that all people have the potential to be great, if they trust themselves.
college-writing-017649.zh: 回应爱默生的文章和他的中心思想，即所有人都有可能成为伟大的人，如果他们相信自己的话。

college-writing-017653.en: Emerson mentions several accomplished men in his essay.
college-writing-017653.zh: 爱默生在他的文章中提到了几个有成就的人。

college-writing-017654.en: Choose one of the men mentioned, research about his life, and then explain how he fits the statement at the end of the essay: “To be great is to be misunderstood.”
college-writing-017654.zh: 选择其中一位提到的人，研究他的生活，然后解释他如何符合文章结尾的陈述：“伟大就是被误解。”

college-writing-017655.en: Alternately, choose a person who has lived since Emerson’s time who fits the statement and is known for their accomplishments.
college-writing-017655.zh: 或者，选择一个符合爱默生的时代生活的人，他以自己的成就而闻名。

college-writing-017657.en: The promise of the American Dream prevails, but many people think it is a right, not an earned privilege.
college-writing-017657.zh: 美国梦的承诺盛行，但许多人认为这是一种权利，而不是一种获得的特权。

college-writing-017658.en: Most people who have achieved the American Dream have worked hard and haven’t simply waited for someone to hand them the prize.
college-writing-017658.zh: 大多数实现美国梦的人都在努力工作，而不是简单地等待有人将奖品交给他们。

college-writing-017659.en: People like Steve Jobs and Larry Page started out working long hours in a garage or dorm room, taking risks when necessary (often with unexpected consequences), and pushed themselves to achieve.
college-writing-017659.zh: 像史蒂夫·乔布斯和拉里·佩奇这样的人开始在车库或宿舍里长时间工作，在必要时冒险（通常会带来意想不到的后果），并推动自己实现。

college-writing-017660.en: Write an essay in which you use the principles laid out in Self-Reliance as a guide for achieving the dream.
college-writing-017660.zh: 写一篇文章，你使用自力更生的原则作为实现梦想的指南。

college-writing-017661.en: You may want to incorporate examples of people who have demonstrated these principles as extra support.
college-writing-017661.zh: 您可能希望将展示这些原则的人作为额外支持的例子。

college-writing-017670.en: My favorite teacher’s name was “Deadeye” Bean.
college-writing-017670.zh: 我最喜欢的老师的名字是“deadeye”豆。

college-writing-017672.en: She taught American history to eighth-graders in the junior high section of Creston, the high school that served the north end of Grand Rapids, Michigan.
college-writing-017672.zh: 她在克雷斯顿的初中部分向八年级学生教授美国历史，这是一所为密歇根州大急流城北端服务的高中。

college-writing-017674.en: Franklin D. Roosevelt was president; American troops were battling their way across France; Joe DiMaggio was still in the service; the Montgomery bus boycott was more than a decade away, and I was a twelve-year-old black newcomer in a school that was otherwise all white.
college-writing-017674.zh: 富兰克林·D·罗斯福是总统； 美国军队正在法国穿越； 乔·迪马乔还在服役。 蒙哥马利巴士抵制距离已经有十多年了，而我是一所学校的 12 岁黑人新人，原本是白人。

college-writing-017675.en: My mother, who had been a widow in New York, had married my stepfather, a Grand Rapids physician, the year before, and he had bought the best house he could afford for his new family.
college-writing-017675.zh: 我的母亲曾在纽约做过寡妇，一年前他嫁给了我的继父，一位大急流城的医生，他为他的新家庭买了最好的房子。

college-writing-017676.en: The problem for our new neighbors was that their neighborhood had previously been pristine1 (in their terms) and that they were ignorant about black people.
college-writing-017676.zh: 我们的新邻居的问题是他们的邻居以前是原始的（就他们而言），他们对黑人一无所知。

college-writing-017677.en: The prevailing wisdom in the neighborhood was that we were spoiling it and that we ought to go back where we belonged (or alternatively, ought not intrude where we were not wanted).
college-writing-017677.zh: 附近的普遍智慧是我们正在破坏它，我们应该回到我们所属的地方（或者，不应该闯入我们不想要的地方）。

college-writing-017678.en: There was a lot of angry talk among the adults, but nothing much came of it.
college-writing-017678.zh: 成年人之间有很多愤怒的谈话，但没有任何结果。

college-writing-017679.en: But some of the kids, those first few weeks, were quite nasty.
college-writing-017679.zh: 但有些孩子，最初的几周，非常讨厌。

college-writing-017680.en: They threw stones at me, chased me home when I was on foot and spat on my bike seat when I was in class.
college-writing-017680.zh: 他们向我扔石头，在我步行时追着我回家，在我上课的时候在我的自行车座椅上吐口水。

college-writing-017681.en: For a time, I was a pretty lonely, friendless and sometimes
college-writing-017681.zh: 有一段时间，我很孤独，没有朋友，有时

college-writing-017682.en: Any newcomer in school often has an awkward time breaking the ice with classmates.
college-writing-017682.zh: 学校里的任何新人经常和同学们一起度过一段尴尬的时光。

college-writing-017683.en: For Roger Wilkins, being the only Black student in his new school made the situation considerably worse.
college-writing-017683.zh: 对于罗杰·威尔金斯来说，作为他新学校里唯一的黑人学生，情况要严重得多。

college-writing-017684.en: He could easily have become the focus of the other students’ prejudice and fear.
college-writing-017684.zh: 他很容易成为其他学生偏见和恐惧的焦点。

college-writing-017685.en: Instead, help came in the form of a teacher who quickly made it clear how she saw him—as a class member with something to contribute.
college-writing-017685.zh: 相反，帮助以一位老师的形式出现，她很快就清楚地表明了她是如何看待他的——作为一名有贡献的班员。

college-writing-017693.en: I was just transplanted from Harlem, and here in Grand Rapids, the dominant culture was speaking to me insistently.
college-writing-017693.zh: 我刚从哈林区移植，在大急流城，占主导地位的文化一直在对我说话。

college-writing-017694.en: I can see now that those youngsters were bullying and culturally disadvantaged.
college-writing-017694.zh: 我现在可以看到那些年轻人是欺凌和文化不利的人。

college-writing-017695.en: I knew then that they were bigoted, but the culture spoke to me more powerfully than my mind and I felt ashamed for being different─a nonstandard person.
college-writing-017695.zh: 那时我知道他们是偏执的，但文化对我的影响比我的想法更强大，我为自己与众不同而感到羞耻——一个不标准的人。

college-writing-017696.en: I now know that Dorothy Bean understood most of that and deplored it.
college-writing-017696.zh: 我现在知道 Dorothy Bean 明白其中的大部分内容并遗憾。

college-writing-017697.en: So things began to change when I walked into her classroom.
college-writing-017697.zh: 所以当我走进她的教室时，情况开始发生变化。

college-writing-017698.en: She was a pleasant-looking single woman, who looked old and wrinkled to me at the time, but who was probably about forty.
college-writing-017698.zh: 她是一个看起来很愉快的单身女人，当时在我看来很老，皱巴巴的，但她大概四十岁左右。

college-writing-017699.en: Whereas my other teachers approached the problem of easing in their new black pupil by ignoring him for the first few weeks, Miss Bean went right at me.
college-writing-017699.zh: 虽然我的其他老师在最初的几周里忽略了他的新黑人学生的宽松问题，但 Bean 小姐直接冲向我。

college-writing-017700.en: On the morning after having read our first assignment, she asked me the first question.
college-writing-017700.zh: 在阅读了我们的第一个作业后的第二天早上，她问了我第一个问题。

college-writing-017701.en: I later came to know that in Grand Rapids, she was viewed as a very liberal person who believed, among other things, that Negroes were equal.
college-writing-017701.zh: 后来我才知道，在大急流城，她被视为一个非常自由的人，除其他外，她认为黑人是平等的。

college-writing-017702.en: I gulped and answered her question and the follow-up.
college-writing-017702.zh: 我吞下并回答了她的问题和后续行动。

college-writing-017703.en: They weren’t brilliant answers, but they did establish the facts that I had read the assignment and that I could speak English.
college-writing-017703.zh: 他们不是很好的答案，但他们确实确定了我读过作业并且我会说英语的事实。

college-writing-017704.en: Later in the hour, when one of my classmates had bungled an answer, Miss Bean came back to me with a question that required me to clean up the girl’s mess and established me as a smart person.
college-writing-017704.zh: 一个小时后，当我的一个同学搞砸了一个答案时，比恩小姐带着一个问题回到我身边，要求我清理女孩的烂摊子，让我成为一个聪明的人。

college-writing-017705.en: Thus, the teacher began to give me human dimensions, though not perfect ones for an eighth-grader.
college-writing-017705.zh: 因此，老师开始给我人性化的维度，但对于八年级的学生来说并不完美。

college-writing-017706.en: It was somewhat better to be an incipient2 teacher’s pet than merely a dark presence in the back of the room onto whose silent form my classmates could fit all the stereotypes they carried in their heads.
college-writing-017706.zh: 做一个初学者的宠物比仅仅在房间后面的黑暗存在要好一些，我的同学们可以适应他们脑海中的所有刻板印象。

college-writing-017707.en: A few days later, Miss Bean became the first teacher ever to require me to think.
college-writing-017707.zh: 几天后，豆小姐成为了第一位要求我思考的老师。

college-writing-017708.en: She asked my opinion about something Jefferson had done.
college-writing-017708.zh: 她问我对杰斐逊所做的事情的看法。

college-writing-017709.en: In those days, all my opinions were derivative.3
college-writing-017709.zh: 在那些日子里，我所有的意见都是衍生的。3

college-writing-017710.en: I was for Roosevelt because my parents were, and I was for the Yankees because my older buddy from Harlem was a Yankee fan.
college-writing-017710.zh: 我支持罗斯福，因为我的父母是，而我是洋基队的，因为我来自哈莱姆的老朋友是洋基队的球迷。

college-writing-017711.en: Besides, we didn’t have opinions about historical figures like Jefferson.
college-writing-017711.zh: 此外，我们对杰斐逊等历史人物没有意见。

college-writing-017712.en: Like our high school building or old Mayor Welch, he just was.
college-writing-017712.zh: 就像我们的高中大楼或老市长韦尔奇一样，他只是。

college-writing-017713.en: After I had stared at her for a few seconds, she said: “Well, should he have bought Louisiana or not?”
college-writing-017713.zh: 在我盯着她看了几秒钟后，她说：“好吧，他应该买路易斯安那州还是不买？”

college-writing-017716.en: What kind of question was that, I groused silently.
college-writing-017716.zh: 那是什么样的问题，我默默地抱怨道。

college-writing-017718.en: Day after day, she kept doing that to me, and my answers became stronger and more confident.
college-writing-017718.zh: 日复一日，她一直对我这样做，我的答案变得更强大、更自信。

college-writing-017719.en: She was the first teacher to give me the sense that thinking was part of education and that I could form opinions that had some value.
college-writing-017719.zh: 她是第一个让我觉得思考是教育的一部分的老师，我可以形成一些有价值的意见。

college-writing-017720.en: Her final service to me came on a day when my mind was wandering and I was idly digging my pencil into the writing surface on the arm of my chair.
college-writing-017720.zh: 她最后一次为我服务是在我的思绪飘忽不定的那一天，我正忙着把铅笔挖到椅子扶手上的书写表面上。

college-writing-017721.en: Miss Bean impulsively threw a hunk of gum eraser at me.
college-writing-017721.zh: 豆小姐冲动地向我扔了一大块口香糖橡皮擦。

college-writing-017722.zh: 被惊人的机会，它击中了

college-writing-017726.en: my hand and sent the pencil flying.
college-writing-017726.zh: 我的手和铅笔飞了起来。

college-writing-017727.en: She gasped, and I crept mortified after my pencil as the class roared.
college-writing-017727.zh: 她喘着粗气，当全班咆哮时，我在我的铅笔后感到羞愧。

college-writing-017729.en: Afterward, kids came up to me to laugh about “Old Deadeye Bean.”
college-writing-017729.zh: 之后，孩子们来找我笑“老死眼豆”。

college-writing-017730.en: The incident became a legend, and I, a part of that story, became a person to talk to.
college-writing-017730.zh: 这一事件成为了一个传奇，而我，这个故事的一部分，成为了一个可以交谈的人。

college-writing-017731.en: So that’s how I became just another kid in school and Dorothy Bean became “Old Deadeye.”
college-writing-017731.zh: 所以这就是我成为学校的另一个孩子的原因，多萝西·比恩变成了“老死人”。

college-writing-017733.zh: 1. 这个词在“但最初的几周里，有些孩子很遗憾

college-writing-017784.zh: 对八年级学生来说是完美的”（第 6 段），威尔金斯所指的不完美是他的

college-writing-017790.zh: 一。 知道这件事会成为他的破冰船。

college-writing-017797.zh: 威尔金斯在他的大部分文章中使用？

college-writing-017799.en: 2. Which kind of transition signal─addition, time, or space─does Wilkins use
college-writing-017799.zh: 2. 什么样的过渡信号——加、时间、空间——威尔金斯使用

college-writing-017800.zh: 将他的论文从一项活动顺利转移到另一项活动？

college-writing-017801.en: Find at least four different words that are examples of this signal.
college-writing-017801.zh: 找到至少四个作为此信号示例的不同单词。

college-writing-017802.en: 3. In the first paragraph, Wilkins chooses to provide some historical background
college-writing-017802.zh: 3. 在第一段中，威尔金斯选择提供一些历史背景

college-writing-017804.zh: 你认为他为什么选择那里提到的具体细节？

college-writing-017808.en: Before reading this essay, what did you think the title “I Became Her Target” might refer to?
college-writing-017808.zh: 在阅读这篇文章之前，您认为“我成为她的目标”的标题可能指的是什么？

college-writing-017809.en: What additional meanings do you think Wilkins intended?
college-writing-017809.zh: 您认为威尔金斯的意图是什么？

college-writing-017811.en: 1. What does Wilkins mean by the term nonstandard person (paragraph 3)?
college-writing-017811.zh: 1. 威尔金斯所说的非标准人（第 3 段）是什么意思？

college-writing-017813.en: you think he later felt more like a “standard” person?
college-writing-017813.zh: 你认为他后来感觉更像一个“标准”的人？

college-writing-017815.en: 2. Wilkins mentions several ways Miss Bean treated him differently from the
college-writing-017815.zh: 2. Wilkins 提到了 Bean 小姐对他的不同待遇的几种方式

college-writing-017816.en: way he was treated by the other teachers at Creston.
college-writing-017816.zh: 克雷斯顿的其他老师对待他的方式。

college-writing-017817.en: How did her approach differ from theirs?
college-writing-017817.zh: 她的方法与他们的方法有何不同？

college-writing-017818.en: What does this approach reveal about Miss Bean─as a teacher and as a person?
college-writing-017818.zh: 这种方法揭示了比恩小姐作为一个老师和一个人的什么？

college-writing-017819.en: 3. Wilkins says that initially he was Miss Bean’s “incipient teacher’s pet” (paragraph
college-writing-017819.zh: 3. 威尔金斯说他最初是比恩小姐的“初级老师的宠物”（段落）

college-writing-017820.en: But how did Miss Bean’s behavior toward him go beyond mere favoritism?
college-writing-017820.zh: 但比恩小姐对他的行为是如何超越单纯的偏袒呢？

college-writing-017821.en: In what way did her treatment of Wilkins affect how his peers regarded him?
college-writing-017821.zh: 她对威尔金斯的处理方式对他的同龄人如何看待他有何影响？

college-writing-017822.en: 4. In paragraph 7, Wilkins says, “Miss Bean became the first teacher ever to
college-writing-017822.zh: 4. 在第 7 段中，威尔金斯说：“豆小姐成为有史以来第一位

college-writing-017824.en: ” Before Miss Bean’s class, what do you suspect Wilkins─ and his classmates─were being taught to do in school?
college-writing-017824.zh: ”在比恩小姐上课之前，你怀疑威尔金斯——和他的同学们——在学校被教导要做什么？

college-writing-017825.en: Describe a teacher who gave you “the sense that thinking was part of education.”
college-writing-017825.zh: 描述一位给你的老师“认为思维是教育的一部分”。

college-writing-017826.en: In your opinion, what can teachers do to get students to think?
college-writing-017826.zh: 在您看来，教师可以做些什么来让学生思考？

college-writing-017829.en: Dorothy Bean, Wilkins’s favorite teacher, obviously had an important influence on him in more ways than one.
college-writing-017829.zh: 威尔金斯最喜欢的老师多萝西·比恩显然对他的影响不止一种。

college-writing-017830.en: She helped him become accepted by the other students, she strengthened his self-image, and she helped him learn to think for himself.
college-writing-017830.zh: 她帮助他被其他学生接受，她加强了他的自我形象，并帮助他学会了自己思考。

college-writing-017831.en: Write an essay on one of your favorite teachers and the ways that person influenced you.
college-writing-017831.zh: 写一篇关于你最喜欢的老师以及那个人影响你的方式的文章。

college-writing-017833.en: Like Wilkins, dramatize specific incidents to show how this teacher affected you.
college-writing-017833.zh: 像威尔金斯一样，将特定事件戏剧化，以展示这位老师对您的影响。

college-writing-017834.en: Provide whatever background is necessary to put the teacher’s influence into perspective.
college-writing-017834.zh: 提供任何必要的背景，以将教师的影响力转化为视角。

college-writing-017835.en: Your thesis will be a general statement that summarizes the teacher’s impact on your life, such as this one: “Mrs. Croson, my sixth-grade teacher, helped me in ways that strengthened all of the rest of my education.”
college-writing-017835.zh: 你的论文将是一个总结老师对你生活的影响的一般性陈述，例如：“克罗森夫人，我的六年级老师，以加强我所有其他教育的方式帮助了我。”

college-writing-017836.en: Then go on in your introduction to list three specific ways the teacher influenced you.
college-writing-017836.zh: 然后继续你的介绍，列出老师影响你的三种具体方式。

college-writing-017837.en: An example of such a plan of development is “She gave me confidence and taught me the joys of reading and writing.”
college-writing-017837.zh: 这样的展开提纲的一个例子是“她给了我信心，教会了我阅读和写作的乐趣。”

college-writing-017838.en: Alternatively, write an essay on three of your favorite teachers.
college-writing-017838.zh: 或者，写一篇关于你最喜欢的三位老师的文章。

college-writing-017839.en: Your thesis might be about the characteristics the three teachers shared or how they influenced you.
college-writing-017839.zh: 你的论文可能是关于三位老师的共同特征或他们如何影响你的。

college-writing-017841.en: Wilkins suggests that the students in his new school misjudged him because at first they saw him only as a stereotype, a stranger with no particular personal characteristics.
college-writing-017841.zh: 威尔金斯认为，他新学校的学生误判了他，因为起初他们只是将他视为刻板印象，一个没有特别个人特征的陌生人。

college-writing-017842.en: Perhaps we are all subject to prejudging people, if not because of their race, then for another reason.
college-writing-017842.zh: 也许我们都受到预先判断的人的影响，如果不是因为他们的种族，那么出于另一个原因。

college-writing-017843.en: Did a person who made a good impression on you ever turn out to be boring and mean?
college-writing-017843.zh: 一个给你留下好印象的人有没有变得无聊和刻薄？

college-writing-017844.en: Did a boss you thought was overly strict ever turn out to be supportive and teach you a lot?
college-writing-017844.zh: 你认为过于严格的老板有没有成为支持并教你很多东西的老板？

college-writing-017845.en: Write an essay about someone who was really quite different from what you initially thought they would be.
college-writing-017845.zh: 写一篇关于与您最初认为的完全不同的人的文章。

college-writing-017846.en: You may wish to consider the following characteristics, which often lead people to prejudge each other:
college-writing-017846.zh: 您可能希望考虑以下特征，这些特征通常会导致人们相互预先判断：

college-writing-017854.en: Begin your essay by explaining in vivid detail your first impression and what caused it.
college-writing-017854.zh: 通过生动地详细解释您的第一印象以及导致它的原因来开始您的论文。

college-writing-017855.en: Then go on to narrate some experiences you had with the person and how these experiences changed your mind about them.
college-writing-017855.zh: 然后继续讲述你与这个人的一些经历，以及这些经历如何改变了你对他们的看法。

college-writing-017856.en: Alternatively, write about an individual or individuals who have prejudged you.
college-writing-017856.zh: 或者，写下预先判断您的个人或个人。

college-writing-017857.en: Explain what those people thought of you and why, and describe how they treated you.
college-writing-017857.zh: 解释那些人对你的看法以及为什么，并描述他们如何对待你。

college-writing-017858.en: If they came to change their minds, explain why and how your relationship changed.
college-writing-017858.zh: 如果他们开始改变主意，请解释你们的关系为什么以及如何改变。

college-writing-017862.en: Write an essay in which you contrast your best teacher and your worst teacher.
college-writing-017862.zh: 写一篇文章，将你最好的老师和最差的老师对比。

college-writing-017863.en: Make a list of the qualities that made one teacher excellent and the other ineffective or worse.
college-writing-017863.zh: 列出使一位教师变得出色而另一位教师无效或更糟的品质。

college-writing-017864.en: Focus on three pairs of contrasting qualities, using either a one-side-at-atime or a point-by-point method of development (see Chapter 13, “Comparison and/ or Contrast”).
college-writing-017864.zh: 专注于三对对比品质，使用一边或逐点的发展方法（参见第 13 章“比较和/或对比”）。

college-writing-017865.en: Following are some elements of teaching to consider as you plan your essay:
college-writing-017865.zh: 以下是您在计划论文时要考虑的一些教学要素：

college-writing-017866.en: grasp of the subject ability to communicate ability to motivate interest in students classroom presentation sense of humor
college-writing-017866.zh: 掌握学科 沟通能力 激发学生兴趣 课堂表现 幽默感

college-writing-017867.en: In addition, consider what you or other students learned or did not learn, such as the following:
college-writing-017867.zh: 此外，请考虑您或其他学生学到或未学到的内容，例如：

college-writing-017868.en: subject matter ways to learn ways to think self-confidence methods of cooperation
college-writing-017868.zh: 主题 学习思维方式的方法 合作的方式 合作的方式

college-writing-017870.en: One night in April when I was barely seven years old, my mother told me to put on my Sunday dress─Dad was taking the family to a church across town.
college-writing-017870.zh: 四月的一个晚上，当我才七岁的时候，我妈妈告诉我穿上我的周日礼服——爸爸正带着家人去镇上的一座教堂。

college-writing-017871.en: None of this made sense to me.
college-writing-017871.zh: 这对我来说没有任何意义。

college-writing-017872.en: After all, it was a Thursday, it was nearly bedtime, and our church was right next door.
college-writing-017872.zh: 毕竟，那是一个星期四，快到睡觉时间了，我们的教堂就在隔壁。

college-writing-017873.en: Dad was the minister, so all we did was walk across a parking lot to get to church.
college-writing-017873.zh: 爸爸是牧师，所以我们所做的只是走过一个停车场去教堂。

college-writing-017874.en: Why were we going across town?
college-writing-017874.zh: 我们为什么要穿越城镇？

college-writing-017875.en: After what seemed like an endless drive, we were winding slowly through a neighborhood I’d never seen before.
college-writing-017875.zh: 在看似无休止的车程之后，我们慢慢地蜿蜒穿过一个我从未见过的社区。

college-writing-017876.en: Suddenly we were in front of a big wooden building with no windows.
college-writing-017876.zh: 突然，我们在一座没有窗户的大木屋前。

college-writing-017877.en: Streams of people were pouring in, all of them quiet and many of them hugging or holding hands.
college-writing-017877.zh: 人群涌入，所有人都安静下来，其中许多人拥抱或牵手。

college-writing-017878.en: When our family walked into the church, many people turned to stare at us for a moment─nearly everyone in the church was Black, and we were white.
college-writing-017878.zh: 当我们的家人走进教堂时，许多人转身盯着我们看了一会儿——几乎教堂里的每个人都是黑人，我们是白人。

college-writing-017879.en: But then a friend of my father’s, a young Black minister, rushed over to greet us and led us to a pew.
college-writing-017879.zh: 但随后我父亲的一个朋友，一位年轻的黑人部长，冲过来迎接我们，把我们带到了长椅上。

college-writing-017880.en: Throughout that evening, the tall Black woman sitting next to me turned to smile at me again and again even though there were tears in her eyes.
college-writing-017880.zh: 整个晚上，坐在我旁边的那个高大的黑人女人转身对我微笑，即使她的眼里含着泪水。

college-writing-017881.en: I was amazed by her hat full of flowers and even some bird feathers, so I smiled back.
college-writing-017881.zh: 我对她满是鲜花甚至一些鸟羽毛的帽子感到惊讶，所以我回以微笑。

college-writing-017882.en: No one wore hats like that in our church.
college-writing-017882.zh: 在我们的教会里，没有人戴着这样的帽子。

college-writing-017883.en: I gazed at her hat until I became drowsy and drifted in and out of sleep, occasionally waking up to hear voices joined in song.
college-writing-017883.zh: 我凝视着她的帽子，直到我昏昏欲睡，在睡梦中进进出出，偶尔醒来听到歌曲中加入的声音。

college-writing-017884.en: Many songs were sung that night that I knew, but at the end of the service everyone joined hands and sang a slow, moving song that I’d never heard before: We shall overcome, we shall overcome, we shall overcome some day.
college-writing-017884.zh: 那天晚上我知道唱了很多歌，但在服务结束时，每个人都拉手，唱了一首我以前从未听过的缓慢而动人的歌曲：我们将克服，我们将克服，我们将克服某一天。

college-writing-017885.en: . . . The tall woman next to me put one arm around me and lifted the other into the air, tears streaming down her face.
college-writing-017885.zh: 。 。 。 我旁边的高个女人用一只手臂搂着我，把另一只手举到空中，泪水顺着她的脸流下来。

college-writing-017886.en: It was April 4th, 1968, and Martin Luther King Jr. had been shot and killed just five hours earlier.
college-writing-017886.zh: 那是 1968 年 4 月 4 日，小马丁·路德·金在五个小时前被枪杀。

college-writing-017887.en: What would you do if you were convinced that people would reject, even despise you if they knew who you really were?
college-writing-017887.zh: 如果你确信人们会拒绝，甚至鄙视你，如果他们知道你的真实身份，你会怎么做？

college-writing-017888.en: Would you dare to be yourself and risk their condemnation?
college-writing-017888.zh: 你敢做你自己，冒着他们的谴责吗？

college-writing-017889.en: Or would you do your best to conform to their expectations?
college-writing-017889.zh: 或者你会尽力满足他们的期望？

college-writing-017890.en: In this selection, Tanya Savory tells how she came to terms with her identity as a gay woman.
college-writing-017890.zh: 在这个选择中，Tanya Savory 讲述了她是如何接受自己作为同性恋女性的身份的。

college-writing-017891.en: In doing so, she draws a parallel between fair treatment for gays and the civil rights struggles of her youth.
college-writing-017891.zh: 在这样做的过程中，她将公平对待同性恋与她年轻时的民权斗争相提并论。

college-writing-017896.en: When I was a senior in high school, I sat on the front porch with my dad one warm South Carolina afternoon and asked him about that night.
college-writing-017896.zh: 当我上高中的时候，我和父亲坐在前廊的一个温暖的南卡罗来纳州下午，向他询问了那天晚上的情况。

college-writing-017898.en: I asked “Afraid? Of what?” my dad asked, giving me a kind of funny look.
college-writing-017898.zh: 我问“害怕吗？什么？” 我爸爸问，给了我一种有趣的表情。

college-writing-017899.en: “Well, you know,” I said awkwardly, “afraid of the kind of white people who hate Blacks. What if they had found out that we were at that service that night? Weren’t you afraid of what they might think or do?”
college-writing-017899.zh: “好吧，你知道，”我尴尬地说，“害怕那些讨厌黑人的白人。如果他们发现我们那天晚上在那场服务，你不怕他们怎么想或做什么吗？”

college-writing-017900.en: My dad stared at me for a long moment before he answered.
college-writing-017900.zh: 我爸爸盯着我看了很久，才回答。

college-writing-017901.en: “Your mother and I have never been afraid of what bigots think of us. And we certainly weren’t going to be bullied into hiding the way we felt just because some racists thought we were wrong.”
college-writing-017901.zh: “你的母亲和我从不害怕偏执狂对我们的看法。我们当然不会因为一些种族主义者认为我们错了而被欺负隐藏我们的感受。”

college-writing-017902.en: “Yeah, but when everyone found out, you lost a lot of friends. Even Aunt Jo still doesn’t speak to you,” I pointed out.
college-writing-017902.zh: “是的，但是当大家发现之后，你失去了很多朋友。即使是乔阿姨仍然不和你说话，”我指出。

college-writing-017903.en: “Not a lot of friends─a few. But that’s a small price to pay to be true to yourself. I’m sorry to lose some friends, but I’d be sorrier to be living my life according to how other people think I should live it.”
college-writing-017903.zh: “不是很多朋友——有几个。但是要付出真诚的自己，这是一个很小的代价。我很遗憾失去一些朋友，但我会很遗憾按照别人认为我应该生活的方式过我的生活。”

college-writing-017904.en: “Really? I asked. “You really think that?” “Yes. I really know that,” my dad answered.
college-writing-017904.zh: “真的吗？我问道：“你真的这么想吗？” “是的。 我真的知道这一点，”我父亲回答。

college-writing-017905.en: That night I lay awake for hours thinking about what my dad had said.
college-writing-017905.zh: 那天晚上，我睡了好几个小时，想着我爸爸说的话。

college-writing-017906.en: I knew he was right, but I was 100 percent afraid to be true to myself.
college-writing-017906.zh: 我知道他是对的，但我 100% 害怕做真实的自己。

college-writing-017907.en: I was in a small town in the South in 1978, and I was afraid, very afraid, that I was someone that even open-minded people would despise.
college-writing-017907.zh: 1978年我在南方的一个小镇，我很害怕，我很害怕，即使是思想开放的人也会鄙视的人。

college-writing-017908.en: Someone who, if I were true to myself, would be laughed at, abandoned by my friends, and worse.
college-writing-017908.zh: 如果我忠于自己，会被我的朋友们嘲笑，被朋友抛弃，甚至更糟。

college-writing-017909.en: Someone whose own mother and father might turn against her.
college-writing-017909.zh: 一个自己的父母可能会反对她的人。

college-writing-017910.en: I was afraid I was gay.

college-writing-017911.en: This was decades before gay characters on TV or in the movies had become commonplace.
college-writing-017911.zh: 这是在电视或电影中的同性恋角色变得司空见惯的几十年前。

college-writing-017912.en: The words “gay marriage” would only have been heard in a punch line to a joke, and, in fact, most people still believed that homosexuality was a mental illness or a crime.
college-writing-017912.zh: “同性婚姻”这个词只能在笑话的妙语中被听到，事实上，大多数人仍然认为同性恋是一种精神疾病或犯罪。

college-writing-017913.en: In the town where I grew up, it was illegal to be gay─police used to stake out a little rundown cinderblock bar on the other side of the tracks where, supposedly, gay men gathered.
college-writing-017913.zh: 在我长大的小镇上，同性恋是违法的——警察过去在轨道的另一边放了一个破旧的煤渣块酒吧，据说是男同性恋者聚集在那里。

college-writing-017914.en: It was not uncommon for the police to rough up and handcuff men they saw coming out of this bar.
college-writing-017914.zh: 警察粗暴地站起来并给他们戴上手铐的人从这个酒吧里出来的情况并不少见。

college-writing-017915.en: Then they were thrown in the jail for the night for little or no real reason.
college-writing-017915.zh: 然后他们被关进监狱过夜，几乎没有真正的原因。

college-writing-017916.en: Most of the townspeople thought this was a good idea.
college-writing-017916.zh: 大多数市民认为这是个好主意。

college-writing-017917.en: Every day in the halls at school, I would wonder and worry if my classmates could tell by looking at me. I pretty much looked and acted like any other seventeen-year-old girl.
college-writing-017917.zh: 每天在学校的大厅里，我都会想知道和担心我的同学能不能通过看着我来判断。 我几乎看起来和表现得像任何其他 17 岁的女孩。

college-writing-017918.en: I passed notes in geometry, wore too much mascara, and worried about what I would wear to the prom in April.
college-writing-017918.zh: 我通过几何学的笔记，涂了太多睫毛膏，担心我会在四月的舞会上穿什么。

college-writing-017919.en: And like most of my friends, I had a boyfriend that I loved.
college-writing-017919.zh: 和我的大多数朋友一样，我有一个我爱的男朋友。

college-writing-017920.en: But something had begun to creep into my consciousness about a year earlier─something like the slightest pinprick of light that had grown just a bit brighter every day until I was sure that everyone could see it like a spotlight on me: I didn’t love my boyfriend, Mark, the same way I loved my best friend, Karla.
college-writing-017920.zh: 但大约一年前，我的意识开始蔓延到我的意识中——就像最轻微的光线一样，每天都变得更亮一点，直到我确信每个人都能看到它就像聚光灯：我不爱我的男朋友，马克，就像我爱我最好的一样 朋友，卡拉。

college-writing-017921.en: I loved her more─I was in love with her.

college-writing-017922.en: Midway through my senior year in high school, I became so afraid and confused about how I felt that I simply made the choice to stop being friends with Karla.
college-writing-017922.zh: 在我高中四年级的中途，我变得如此害怕和困惑，因为我觉得我只是选择停止与卡拉成为朋友。

college-writing-017923.en: The way I saw it, if I turned off the spotlight, no one would be able to see the real me.
college-writing-017923.zh: 在我看来，如果我关掉聚光灯，没有人能看到真正的我。

college-writing-017924.zh: 662 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-017925.en: In the darkness, it was easier to hide.

college-writing-017926.en: I made new friends that I didn’t really care too much about.
college-writing-017926.zh: 我结交了我不太关心的新朋友。

college-writing-017927.en: I lost interest in anything that was special or unique about me, not wanting to draw attention to who I was.
college-writing-017927.zh: 我对任何关于我的特别或独特的事物失去了兴趣，不想引起人们对我是谁的关注。

college-writing-017928.en: I went entirely overboard in my devotion to Mark, even suggesting that we get married as soon as we graduated from high school.
college-writing-017928.zh: 我对马克的投入完全过火了，甚至建议我们一高中毕业就结婚。

college-writing-017929.en: College and my future no longer mattered to me.
college-writing-017929.zh: 大学和我的未来对我来说不再重要。

college-writing-017930.en: All that mattered was escaping the light, the fear of who I really was.
college-writing-017930.zh: 重要的是逃避光，对我真正的恐惧的恐惧。

college-writing-017931.en: It didn’t matter that I was confused and miserable as long as I was hidden.
college-writing-017931.zh: 只要我被隐藏起来，我感到困惑和痛苦并不重要。

college-writing-017932.en: Strange as it may sound today, I was actually relieved when, one Sunday morning, I came across a short and angry article in a Christian magazine that insisted that homosexuality was a sin and that it was a choice.
college-writing-017932.zh: 今天听起来很奇怪，当我在一个星期天早上，在一本基督教杂志上看到一篇简短而愤怒的文章时，我真的松了一口气，坚持同性恋是一种罪过，这是一种选择。

college-writing-017933.en: Apparently, all one had to do was change his or her mind about who they loved, choose to hate that kind of love, and everything would be okay.
college-writing-017933.zh: 显然，所要做的就是改变他或她对他们所爱的人的看法，选择讨厌那种爱，一切都会好起来的。

college-writing-017934.en: Supposedly it was as simple as deciding not to rob a bank or choosing not to eat too much pie.
college-writing-017934.zh: 据说这很简单，就像决定不抢银行或选择不吃太多馅饼一样简单。

college-writing-017935.en: Choose heterosexuality and you get heaven.
college-writing-017935.zh: 选择异性恋，你就会得到天堂。

college-writing-017937.en: I had made the right choice!

college-writing-017938.en: In a burst of satisfaction, I decided to tell my father everything I had been through and how I had made the right decision.
college-writing-017938.zh: 一阵满足，我决定告诉我父亲我所经历的一切，以及我如何做出正确的决定。

college-writing-017939.en: After all, he was a minister.

college-writing-017940.en: Surely he’d be proud of me.
college-writing-017940.zh: 他肯定会为我感到骄傲。

college-writing-017942.en: “Is your decision based on who you really are or who you want people to think you are?” was my dad’s first question.
college-writing-017942.zh: “你的决定是基于你的真实身份还是你希望人们认为你是谁？” 是我父亲的第一个问题。

college-writing-017944.en: This was not how I had expected my father to respond at all.
college-writing-017944.zh: 这不是我期望父亲做出回应的方式。

college-writing-017945.en: No one I knew had ever said anything about it being okay to be gay.
college-writing-017945.zh: 我认识的没有人说过可以成为同性恋者。

college-writing-017946.en: In fact, no one ever talked about it at all except to make fun of it.
college-writing-017946.zh: 事实上，除了取笑它之外，没有人谈论过它。

college-writing-017947.en: I paused for a long time before answering.
college-writing-017947.zh: 我停顿了很长时间才回答。

college-writing-017948.en: Finally, I quietly said, “I’m not sure.”
college-writing-017948.zh: 最后，我悄悄地说：“我不确定。”

college-writing-017949.en: I don’t remember what else was said, but my father hugged me.
college-writing-017949.zh: 我不记得还说了什么，但我父亲拥抱了我。

college-writing-017950.en: And that was a great turning point, a great source of light in my life.
college-writing-017950.zh: 这是一个伟大的转折点，是我生命中的重要光源。

college-writing-017951.en: Decades later, I look back on that year as a strange, murky time full of confusion about myself and about the world around me.
college-writing-017951.zh: 几十年后，我把那一年回顾为一个奇怪的、模糊的时期，对自己和周围的世界充满了困惑。

college-writing-017952.en: Luckily, I had parents who, though they worried about how the world around me would treat me, did not try to change me.
college-writing-017952.zh: 幸运的是，我的父母虽然担心我周围的世界会如何对待我，但他们并没有试图改变我。

college-writing-017953.en: They never once suggested that there was anything “wrong” with me.
college-writing-017953.zh: 他们从来没有说过我有什么“错误”的地方。

college-writing-017954.en: But most of the gay people I know who grew up in that same era were not so lucky: One friend tells a story of his seventy-five-year-old grandmother chasing him down the street with a shotgun when she found out he was gay.
college-writing-017954.zh: 但我认识的大多数在同一个时代长大的同性恋者都没有那么幸运：一位朋友讲述了他 75 岁的祖母在发现他是同性恋时在街上追着他的故事。

college-writing-017955.en: “She thought I’d be better off dead,” he explained.
college-writing-017955.zh: “她认为我死后会更好，”他解释道。

college-writing-017957.en: Another friend describes how her parents changed the locks on the doors, leaving a note that simply read, “Don’t come back.”
college-writing-017957.zh: 另一位朋友描述了她的父母如何更换门上的锁，留下一张便条，上面写着“不要回来”。

college-writing-017958.en: Perhaps worst of all was a friend whose own family boycotted his funeral when he died of AIDS.
college-writing-017958.zh: 也许最糟糕的是一个朋友，当他死于艾滋病时，他的家人抵制了他的葬礼。

college-writing-017959.en: It’s hard to imagine where that kind of hate comes from.
college-writing-017959.zh: 很难想象这种仇恨是从哪里来的。

college-writing-017960.en: What is it about love between two people of the same sex that creates such anger and hostility?
college-writing-017960.zh: 两个同性的人之间的爱情是什么引起了如此愤怒和敌意？

college-writing-017961.en: Some people, like my friend’s seventy-five-year-old grandmother, have an uninformed idea of what gay people are like.
college-writing-017961.zh: 有些人，比如我朋友 75 岁的祖母，对同性恋者是什么样的人有一个不知情的想法。

college-writing-017962.en: They believe all the ridiculous stereotypes that they’ve read about or seen on TV or in the movies.
college-writing-017962.zh: 他们相信他们在电视或电影中读到或看到的所有荒谬的刻板印象。

college-writing-017965.en: them─and fear is always one step away from hate.
college-writing-017965.zh: 他们——恐惧总是远离仇恨的一步。

college-writing-017966.en: To them, gay people are a big group of creepy and weird outcasts full of prissy men who wear dresses and angry women who look like lumberjacks.
college-writing-017966.zh: 对他们来说，同性恋者是一大群令人毛骨悚然和怪异的弃儿，到处都是穿裙子的脾气暴躁的男人和看起来像伐木工人的愤怒女人。

college-writing-017967.en: In reality, of course, gay people are no different from anyone else.
college-writing-017967.zh: 当然，实际上，同性恋者与其他人没有什么不同。

college-writing-017968.en: We work in the same jobs, eat the same foods, have the same worries, and experience the same joys and sorrows as any other human beings.
college-writing-017968.zh: 我们从事相同的工作，吃同样的食物，有同样的担忧，并经历与任何其他人一样的欢乐和悲伤。

college-writing-017969.en: Other people, like the parents who locked their daughter out of their house, feel that it is immoral─that it is just plain wrong for two people of the same sex to fall in love.
college-writing-017969.zh: 其他人，比如把女儿锁在家里的父母，觉得两个同性的人坠入爱河是不道德的。

college-writing-017970.en: They feel that it is best to just lock it out and hope it goes away.
college-writing-017970.zh: 他们觉得最好把它锁在外面，希望它消失。

college-writing-017971.en: This, in fact, was the same way many people felt about Black and white people falling in love years ago.
college-writing-017971.zh: 事实上，这与许多人几年前对黑人和白人坠入爱河的感受一样。

college-writing-017972.en: It just seemed wrong and it made people feel uneasy.
college-writing-017972.zh: 这似乎是错误的，它让人们感到不安。

college-writing-017973.en: They didn’t want to have to see it or think about it.
college-writing-017973.zh: 他们不想看到它或考虑它。

college-writing-017974.en: So until 1948, it was against the law in the United States for interracial couples to marry.
college-writing-017974.zh: 因此，直到 1948 年，异族夫妇结婚在美国是违法的。

college-writing-017975.en: But laws designed to keep people from loving one another and labeling something “immoral” just because it makes some people uncomfortable are always bad ideas.
college-writing-017975.zh: 但旨在阻止人们彼此相爱并仅仅因为它让一些人感到不舒服而将“不道德”标记为“不道德”的法律总是坏主意。

college-writing-017976.en: Still other people, like the family that refused to attend their own son’s funeral, claim that God doesn’t approve of homosexuality.
college-writing-017976.zh: 还有一些人，比如拒绝参加自己儿子葬礼的家人，声称上帝不赞成同性恋。

college-writing-017977.en: Like the author of the article I had read so many years ago, they feel it’s a sin.
college-writing-017977.zh: 就像我多年前读过的文章的作者一样，他们觉得这是一种罪过。

college-writing-017978.en: There is rarely any argument one can present that can change the minds of people who point to the Bible as their reason for disliking, even hating, gay people.
college-writing-017978.zh: 很少有人可以提出任何论点可以改变那些指向圣经的人的想法，因为他们不喜欢甚至讨厌的同性恋者。

college-writing-017979.en: But using religion to justify the way we can mistreat other people, however, is nothing new.
college-writing-017979.zh: 然而，使用宗教来证明我们虐待他人的方式是正当的，这并不是什么新鲜事。

college-writing-017980.en: In the past, the Bible has been used to justify slavery, segregation, and even denying women the right to vote.
college-writing-017980.zh: 过去，圣经一直被用来为奴隶制、种族隔离，甚至剥夺妇女的投票权。

college-writing-017981.en: As the daughter of a minister, all of this seems strange to me.
college-writing-017981.zh: 作为部长的女儿，这一切对我来说似乎很奇怪。

college-writing-017982.en: Like my father, I would like to think that religion is better suited to promoting love─not hate.
college-writing-017982.zh: 像我父亲一样，我想认为宗教更适合促进爱——而不是恨。

college-writing-017983.zh: 幸运的是，事情正在发生变化。

college-writing-017984.en: It is definitely not the same dark and mysterious world for a young gay person that it was when I was seventeen.
college-writing-017984.zh: 对于一个年轻的同性恋者来说，这绝对不是我十七岁时的黑暗和神秘世界。

college-writing-017985.en: Being gay is actually discussed, and it is no longer considered cool or socially acceptable to make fun of gay people or tell jokes about them.
college-writing-017985.zh: 实际上是同性恋是讨论的，取笑同性恋者或讲笑话不再被认为是很酷或社会上可以接受的。

college-writing-017986.en: And the majority of Americans say that they think homosexuals should be accepted the same as anyone else.
college-writing-017986.zh: 大多数美国人说他们认为同性恋者应该和其他人一样被接受。

college-writing-017987.en: It is no longer unusual to hear about gay actors, singers, athletes, ministers, teachers, firefighters, senators, or even a gay wizard in Harry Potter!
college-writing-017987.zh: 听到同性恋演员、歌手、运动员、牧师、教师、消防员、参议员甚至哈利波特中的同性恋巫师的消息已经不寻常了！

college-writing-017988.en: Even so, there is a long road ahead.
college-writing-017988.zh: 即便如此，前方还有很长的路。

college-writing-017989.en: In many states it is still legal to fire an employee simply because he or she is gay.
college-writing-017989.zh: 在许多州，仅仅因为他或她是同性恋而解雇员工仍然是合法的。

college-writing-017990.en: And nearly every day there are acts of violence directed at gay people who refuse to hide who they are.
college-writing-017990.zh: 几乎每天都有针对拒绝隐藏自己的同性恋者的暴力行为。

college-writing-017991.en: But somewhere in the future, there will certainly come a day when no one has to worry about “coming out” any longer because no one will really care one way or the other about sexual orientation.
college-writing-017991.zh: 但在未来的某个地方，肯定会有一天没有人再担心“出来”，因为没有人会真正关心性取向。

college-writing-017993.en: As it is, gay people rarely spend their time focusing on the fact that they are gay, regardless of how big a deal the media likes to make of a celebrity or politician who has suddenly come out.
college-writing-017993.zh: 事实上，同性恋者很少把时间花在他们是同性恋的事实上，不管媒体喜欢对突然出现的名人或政治家有多大意义。

college-writing-017994.en: As talk show host Ellen Degeneres once explained, “I never think about being gay, you know? I’m just living my life . . . I don’t wake up every morning and say, ‘I’m gay!’” Like any minority, gay people are not looking for special recognition─just fair treatment and the same rights everyone has that make it possible just to live one’s life.
college-writing-017994.zh: 正如脱口秀主持人艾伦·德杰尼勒斯曾经解释说的那样，“我从没想过成为同性恋，你知道吗？我只是过着我的生活……我不会每天早上醒来说，‘我是同性恋！’”像任何少数人一样，同性恋者不是在寻找特别的东西 承认——只是公平对待和每个人所拥有的相同权利，这使得人们可以过上自己的生活。

college-writing-017995.zh: 664 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-017997.en: Not long ago, I read a story that made me very angry.
college-writing-017997.zh: 不久前，我读了一个让我非常生气的故事。

college-writing-017998.en: In a small town in the Midwest, an elderly woman named Sarah had just lost her partner of forty-two years, Laura, to leukemia.
college-writing-017998.zh: 在中西部的一个小镇，一位名叫莎拉的老妇人刚刚失去了她 42 岁的伴侣劳拉，因白血病而失去了她的伴侣。

college-writing-017999.en: As Laura lay dying in the hospital, Sarah pleaded with the hospital staff to allow her to see Laura, but the staff refused─only family was allowed in the rooms of critical patients.
college-writing-017999.zh: 当劳拉在医院去世时，莎拉恳求医院工作人员允许她见劳拉，但工作人员拒绝了——只有家人被允许进入重症患者的房间。

college-writing-018001.en: Laura died alone, and Sarah never got to tell her goodbye.
college-writing-018001.zh: 劳拉一个人死了，莎拉从来没有和她说再见。

college-writing-018002.en: Within a couple days of Laura’s death, Laura’s only surviving relative, a nephew who hadn’t seen his great-aunt in twenty years, came to claim possession of the home Sarah and Laura had shared for decades.
college-writing-018002.zh: 在劳拉去世的几天内，劳拉唯一幸存的亲戚，一个二十年未见他姑姑的侄子，声称拥有莎拉和劳拉几十年来共享的家。

college-writing-018003.en: The home was in Laura’s name, so now the law said it belonged to the nephew.
college-writing-018003.zh: 这所房子以劳拉的名义，所以现在法律说它属于侄子。

college-writing-018004.en: Additionally, the nephew was happy to be legally entitled to all of the home’s possessions and all of the money in his aunt’s savings.
college-writing-018004.zh: 此外，侄子很高兴在法律上有权获得他姑姑的所有财产和所有钱。

college-writing-018005.en: Sarah was left with nothing─no laws protected her because no laws recognized her relationship with Laura.
college-writing-018005.zh: 莎拉一无所有——没有法律保护她，因为没有法律承认她与劳拉的关系。

college-writing-018006.en: Legally, Sarah and Laura were no more than strangers to one another.
college-writing-018006.zh: 从法律上讲，莎拉和劳拉对彼此来说不过是陌生人。

college-writing-018007.en: Sarah would spend her remaining years in a rundown facility for penniless elderly people.
college-writing-018007.zh: 莎拉将在一个破旧的设施中度过余生，为身无分文的老人服务。

college-writing-018008.en: And, legally, Sarah could even have been denied the right to attend her partner’s funeral if the nephew hadn’t wanted her there.
college-writing-018008.zh: 而且，从法律上讲，如果侄子不希望她在那里，莎拉甚至可能被剥夺了参加她伴侣葬礼的权利。

college-writing-018009.en: However, the nephew had no interest in attending the service once he secured the deed to the house.
college-writing-018009.zh: 然而，侄子一旦把契约拿到了房子，就没有兴趣参加这项服务。

college-writing-018010.en: On a cold April morning, Sarah and a handful of friends gathered at Laura’s gravesite.
college-writing-018010.zh: 在一个寒冷的四月早晨，莎拉和几个朋友聚集在劳拉的墓地。

college-writing-018011.en: But just as the service began, shouts were heard.
college-writing-018011.zh: 但就在服务开始时，听到了喊叫声。

college-writing-018012.en: Ten members of an anti-gay hate group had gathered across the road from the rural cemetery.
college-writing-018012.zh: 一个反同性恋仇恨组织的十名成员聚集在马路对面的农村墓地。

college-writing-018013.en: Somehow, they had gotten wind of the fact that a gay person was about to be buried.
college-writing-018013.zh: 不知何故，他们得到了一个同性恋者即将被埋葬的事实。

college-writing-018014.en: Standing in a line and holding signs with slogans such as “Fags Burn in Hell” and “God Hates Homos,” the group shouted cruel and angry comments throughout the funeral service.
college-writing-018014.zh: 这群人排成一列，举着标语，如“Fags Burns in Hell”和“God Hates Homos”，在葬礼上大喊残忍和愤怒的评论。

college-writing-018015.en: Legally, they had the right to do this.
college-writing-018015.zh: 在法律上，他们有权这样做。

college-writing-018016.en: As I read this story and looked at the pictures of the faces of those holding the signs and yelling, I felt hate.
college-writing-018016.zh: 当我读到这个故事，看着那些拿着标志和大喊大叫的人的照片时，我感到讨厌。

college-writing-018017.en: I felt like jumping in my car and driving nonstop to that little town and giving them a dose of their own darkness.
college-writing-018017.zh: 我想跳上我的车，不停地开车到那个小镇，给他们一剂自己的黑暗。

college-writing-018018.en: I wanted to pay them back for all the despair their kind of hatred brought to gay teens who were, like I had once been, lost and confused.
college-writing-018018.zh: 我想偿还他们给同性恋青少年带来的所有绝望，他们就像我曾经迷失和困惑一样。

college-writing-018019.en: I wanted to spew venom right back at this group.
college-writing-018019.zh: 我想马上把毒液喷回这个群体。

college-writing-018020.en: But then, near the end of the story, a comment by the elderly woman, Sarah, stopped me in my tracks.
college-writing-018020.zh: 但随后，在故事快结束时，老妇人莎拉的评论让我停下了脚步。

college-writing-018021.en: Reporters, who had crassly rushed to the scene, asked Sarah how she felt about the group picketing across the street.
college-writing-018021.zh: 记者们粗暴地赶到现场，问莎拉她对街对面纠察队的感受如何。

college-writing-018022.en: “Well,” she had said, “I’m sorry they feel that way. But it won’t do no good to hate them back.”
college-writing-018022.zh: “好吧，”她说，“我很抱歉他们有这种感觉。但讨厌他们是没有好处的。”

college-writing-018023.en: And suddenly, Sarah’s words were like a light─a light that seemed to shine all the way back to nearly forty years ago.
college-writing-018023.zh: 突然间，莎拉的话就像一道光——一道似乎一直照耀到四十年前的光。

college-writing-018024.en: To a night in April amidst a group of mourners who chose to sing and hold hands in response to hate and violence.
college-writing-018024.zh: 到四月的一个晚上，一群哀悼者选择唱歌和牵手来应对仇恨和暴力。

college-writing-018025.en: A group that was certainly angry and weary of being treated unfairly.
college-writing-018025.zh: 一个肯定对不公平对待的愤怒和厌倦的群体。

college-writing-018028.en: somewhere during that evening, the young Black minister who had led us to a seat must have reminded the congregation of the wisdom of Dr. King’s teachings that love would ultimately overcome hate and that light would always overcome darkness.
college-writing-018028.zh: 在那个晚上的某个地方，带领我们到座位的年轻黑人牧师一定提醒了会众金博士的教义的智慧，即爱最终会克服仇恨，光明总能战胜黑暗。
