college-writing-018119.zh: 写一篇关于你生活中对你产生积极影响的人的文章。

college-writing-018120.en: Provide whatever background is necessary to put the person’s influence into perspective.
college-writing-018120.zh: 提供任何必要的背景，以将人的影响力转化为视角。

college-writing-018121.en: Your thesis will be a general statement that summarizes the person’s impact on your life, such as this one: “_______ helped me in ways that affected my life.”
college-writing-018121.zh: 你的论文将是一个一般性的陈述，总结了这个人对你生活的影响，例如：“_______________以影响我生活的方式帮助了我。”

college-writing-018122.en: Then go on in your introduction to list three specific ways that person influenced you.
college-writing-018122.zh: 然后继续你的介绍，列出那个人影响你的三种具体方式。

college-writing-018123.en: An example of such a plan of development is, “He (she/they) helped me to believe in myself, showed me that it was important to listen to others, and taught me the value of hard work.”
college-writing-018123.zh: 这样的展开提纲的一个例子是，“他（她/他们）帮助我相信自己，向我表明倾听他人的声音很重要，并教会了我努力工作的价值。”

college-writing-018124.zh: 668 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-018126.en: Savory was outraged by the picketers who appeared at Laura’s funeral.
college-writing-018126.zh: 出现在劳拉葬礼上的纠察队员激怒了萨沃里。

college-writing-018127.en: Although most of us have probably not experienced this level of hatred, we’ve all seen or heard about situations that have awakened our sense of injustice.
college-writing-018127.zh: 尽管我们大多数人可能没有经历过这种程度的仇恨，但我们都看到或听说过唤醒我们不公正感的情况。

college-writing-018128.en: Write an essay about three situations you’ve experienced or learned about that awakened your sense of injustice.
college-writing-018128.zh: 写一篇关于你经历或了解到的三种情况的文章，这些情况唤醒了你的不公正感。

college-writing-018129.en: In your essay, devote each supporting paragraph to one such anecdote, describing the incident in detail and your response to it.
college-writing-018129.zh: 在你的文章中，将每个支持段落都用于这样的轶事，详细描述事件和您对它的回应。

college-writing-018130.en: Like Savory, the incident you describe could be something you read about or saw on TV.
college-writing-018130.zh: 就像 Savory 一样，您描述的事件可能是您在电视上阅读或看到的内容。

college-writing-018131.en: If you wish, you may suggest ways in which similar incidents might be avoided.
college-writing-018131.zh: 如果您愿意，您可以建议可以避免类似事件的方式。

college-writing-018132.en: Your thesis for the essay might be similar to the following:
college-writing-018132.zh: 您的论文论文可能类似于以下内容：

college-writing-018133.en: In my life, three incidents in particular have awakened my sense of injustice.
college-writing-018133.zh: 在我的生活中，尤其是三件事唤醒了我的不公正感。

college-writing-018135.en: Although, as Savory points out, LGBTQ people are now more accepted by society than they once were, the question of same-sex marriage is still a controversial topic.
college-writing-018135.zh: 尽管，正如 Savory 指出的那样，LGBTQ 人现在比以前更被社会接受，但同性婚姻的问题仍然是一个有争议的话题。

college-writing-018136.en: Write an essay that takes as its thesis one of the following statements:
college-writing-018136.zh: 写一篇论文，以以下陈述之一为论文：

college-writing-018137.en: The Supreme Court made the right decision in 2015 to legalize same-sex marriage.
college-writing-018137.zh: 最高法院在 2015 年做出了正确的决定，将同性婚姻合法化。

college-writing-018138.en: The word marriage should apply only to a union between a man and a woman.
college-writing-018138.zh: 婚姻这个词应该只适用于男人和女人之间的结合。

college-writing-018139.en: Support your thesis with several points, each developed in its own paragraph.
college-writing-018139.zh: 用几点支持你的论文，每个点都在自己的段落中开发。

college-writing-018140.en: Before you begin, you may wish to research arguments for and against same-sex marriage on the Internet.
college-writing-018140.zh: 在开始之前，您可能希望在互联网上研究支持和反对同性婚姻的论点。

college-writing-018141.en: To access the Internet, use a search engine such as Google (www. google.com) and refer to Chapter 17, “Information Literacy.”
college-writing-018141.zh: 要访问互联网，请使用谷歌 (www.google.com) 等搜索引擎，并参考第 17 章“信息素养”。

college-writing-018143.en: I had all the usual childhood fears.
college-writing-018143.zh: 我有所有通常的童年恐惧。

college-writing-018144.en: I couldn’t go to sleep unless the light in my bedroom closet was on.
college-writing-018144.zh: 除非我卧室壁橱里的灯亮着，否则我无法入睡。

college-writing-018145.en: I dreaded that someday when my mother was distracted, Crazy Betty (our local small-town oddball) would grab me in the grocery store.
college-writing-018145.zh: 我害怕有一天我妈妈分心了，疯狂的贝蒂（我们当地的小镇怪人）会在杂货店抓住我。

college-writing-018146.en: On the hottest summer nights, my feet had to be wrapped tightly in my bedsheets; if one of them hung bare over the side of the bed, who knew what might grab it in its cold, slimy claw?
college-writing-018146.zh: 在最热的夏夜，我的脚不得不紧紧地裹在床单上； 如果其中一个赤裸地挂在床边，谁知道什么可以抓住它冰冷、粘糊糊的爪子？

college-writing-018147.en: But all other frights paled before the Great Fear, the Titanic of my childhood terrors.
college-writing-018147.zh: 但在我童年恐惧的泰坦尼克号之前，所有其他的恐惧都相形见绌。

college-writing-018148.en: That fear─and I admit, I feel a tightening in my stomach typing the words even today─was that something would happen to Monk-Monk.
college-writing-018148.zh: 那种恐惧——我承认，即使在今天，我的胃里也感到一种收紧的词——是和尚、和尚会发生什么事。

college-writing-018149.en: Looking at Monk-Monk today, you wouldn’t see what I see.
college-writing-018149.zh: 今天看着和尚，你不会看到我看到的。

college-writing-018150.en: You’d see a torn, discolored sock monkey, very much past his prime, stuffing leaking from his stumpy tail, holes on his sock-body inexpertly stitched up with thread that doesn’t match.
college-writing-018150.zh: 你会看到一只撕裂的、变色的袜子猴子，已经过了他的巅峰期，塞满了从他粗短的尾巴里漏出来的东西，他的袜子上的洞没有用不匹配的线缝合。

college-writing-018151.en: I see my dearest childhood friend, my companion of a thousand nights.
college-writing-018151.zh: 我看到了我最亲爱的儿时朋友，我的一千夜之伴。

college-writing-018152.en: When I was only two and very ill, an aunt made him for me and delivered him to the hospital.
college-writing-018152.zh: 当我只有两岁且病得很重的时候，一位姑姑为我安排了他，并将他送到了医院。

college-writing-018153.en: I bonded with him fiercely and rarely let him out of my sight.
college-writing-018153.zh: 我与他凶狠地联系在一起，很少让他离开我的视线。

college-writing-018154.en: When no one else was around, Monk-Monk played endless games with me, soaked up my tears, and listened to my secrets.
college-writing-018154.zh: 当周围没有其他人的时候，和尚和我一起玩无尽的游戏，浸湿了我的眼泪，听了我的秘密。

college-writing-018155.en: And then Uncle Ken came to visit.

college-writing-018156.en: I didn’t know Uncle Ken well, and I didn’t like him very much.
college-writing-018156.zh: 我不太了解肯叔叔，我也不太喜欢他。

college-writing-018157.en: I had the feeling he didn’t really like me, either.
college-writing-018157.zh: 我有一种感觉，他也不喜欢我。

college-writing-018158.en: He clearly thought it was pretty silly that a big first-grader was dragging a sock monkey around, and he teased me by saying he thought he’d take Monk-Monk home to Ohio with him.
college-writing-018158.zh: 他显然认为一个大一年级学生拖着一只袜子猴子到处乱跑是很愚蠢的，他取笑我说他认为他会把和尚带回家到俄亥俄州。

college-writing-018159.zh: 我更紧紧地抓住了和尚。

college-writing-018160.en: I was at school a few days later when Uncle Ken left.
college-writing-018160.zh: 几天后，当肯叔叔离开时，我在学校。

college-writing-018161.en: When I came home, I couldn’t find Monk-Monk anywhere.
college-writing-018161.zh: 回到家，我找不到任何地方的僧侣。

college-writing-018162.en: I can hardly describe the depths of my panic.
college-writing-018162.zh: 我几乎无法描述我的恐慌的深度。

college-writing-018163.en: I don’t think I cried; my terror was beyond that.
college-writing-018163.zh: 我不认为我哭了； 我的恐惧远不止于此。

college-writing-018168.en: Were your fears different five years ago?
college-writing-018168.zh: 五年前你的恐惧有什么不同吗？

college-writing-018169.en: Will they change as you grow older?
college-writing-018169.zh: 随着年龄的增长，它们会改变吗？

college-writing-018170.en: In this selection, Audra Kendall shows us that every stage of life brings its own fears—and that all fears revolve around the threat of loss.
college-writing-018170.zh: 在这个选择中，奥德拉·肯德尔向我们展示了生命的每个阶段都会带来自己的恐惧——所有的恐惧都围绕着失去的威胁。

college-writing-018171.en: Do your fears fit the pattern?

college-writing-018175.en: raced like a wild animal in a tiny cage.
college-writing-018175.zh: 在一个小笼子里像野生动物一样比赛。

college-writing-018177.en: What had Uncle Ken done to him?

college-writing-018178.en: Was he safe somewhere, or had Uncle Ken (and this thought made my heart nearly stop) thrown him out the car window?
college-writing-018178.zh: 他在某个地方安全吗，还是让肯叔叔（这个想法让我的心几乎停止了）把他扔出了车窗？

college-writing-018179.en: Was Monk-Monk lying in a weedy strip along the interstate, lonely and cold, never to be loved again?
college-writing-018179.zh: 和尚是躺在州际公路的杂草地带上，孤独而寒冷，再也不会被爱吗？

college-writing-018180.en: When we found Monk-Monk wedged behind the sofa (could Uncle Ken really have been mean enough to do that? I never found out), I was limp with relief.
college-writing-018180.zh: 当我们发现和尚被塞在沙发后面时（肯叔叔真的有足够的意思吗？我从来没有发现），我松了一口气。

college-writing-018181.en: For days afterwards I was shaken, crying at the least provocation.
college-writing-018181.zh: 之后的几天我都被震动了，至少哭了起来。

college-writing-018182.en: As far as I can remember, that near-loss of Monk-Monk was my first encounter with real, deep-down fear.
college-writing-018182.zh: 据我所知，那个近乎失去的僧侣是我第一次遇到真正的、内心深处的恐惧。

college-writing-018183.en: I felt the threatened loss of something precious to me.
college-writing-018183.zh: 我感到对我来说珍贵的东西受到了威胁的损失。

college-writing-018184.en: And that, I think, is the essence of fear─the threat of loss.
college-writing-018184.zh: 我认为，这就是恐惧的本质——失去的威胁。

college-writing-018185.en: Small children fear the loss of a favorite toy.
college-writing-018185.zh: 小孩害怕失去最喜欢的玩具。

college-writing-018186.en: The fears of adolescents are different.
college-writing-018186.zh: 青少年的恐惧是不同的。

college-writing-018187.en: Above almost anything, adolescents fear losing their cool─looking “stupid.”
college-writing-018187.zh: 最重要的是，青少年害怕失去冷静——看起来“愚蠢”。

college-writing-018188.en: They will risk almost anything in order to maintain the illusion that they are cool, composed and in control.
college-writing-018188.zh: 他们几乎会冒任何风险，以保持他们冷静、镇定和控制的错觉。

college-writing-018189.en: Let me give you an example.

college-writing-018190.en: A friend of mine had the opportunity to work in Florence, Italy, for a few months.
college-writing-018190.zh: 我的一个朋友有机会在意大利佛罗伦萨工作了几个月。

college-writing-018191.en: While he was gone, he arranged for his two teenage sons to visit him for a week.
college-writing-018191.zh: 当他离开时，他安排他的两个十几岁的儿子拜访他一个星期。

college-writing-018192.en: The excited boys arrived at the airport and checked in.
college-writing-018192.zh: 兴奋的男孩们到达机场并办理了登机手续。

college-writing-018193.en: After sitting down to wait for their flight, one nudged the other.
college-writing-018193.zh: 坐下来等待他们的飞行后，一只推了另一只。

college-writing-018194.en: “Look at the tickets,” he told his brother.

college-writing-018196.en: Indeed, the tickets did not list Florence as the destination.
college-writing-018196.zh: 事实上，门票并没有将佛罗伦萨列为目的地。

college-writing-018198.en: Now, it so happens that Firenze is the Italian name for Florence, so everything was fine.
college-writing-018198.zh: 现在，佛罗伦萨是佛罗伦萨的意大利名字，所以一切都很好。

college-writing-018199.en: But the boys didn’t know that.
college-writing-018199.zh: 但男孩们并不知道这一点。

college-writing-018200.en: They thought that through some error, they were being put on the wrong plane for the wrong destination.
college-writing-018200.zh: 他们认为通过一些错误，他们被放在错误的飞机上，因为错误的目的地。

college-writing-018203.en: At the appointed time, they unhappily boarded the plane for Firenze, sat down, and worried silently for six hours that they were going to end up in, oh, maybe South America.
college-writing-018203.zh: 在约定的时间，他们不幸登上了佛罗伦萨的飞机，坐下，默默地担心了六个小时，他们将最终到达，哦，也许是南美。

college-writing-018206.en: But the thought of admitting to a ticket agent that they didn’t know what “Firenze” meant was more terrifying than the prospect of being dumped, alone, in a strange city on an unknown continent.
college-writing-018206.zh: 但是，一想到要向售票员承认他们不知道“佛罗伦萨”的含义，就比在一个陌生的大陆上一个陌生的城市被倾倒的前景更可怕。

college-writing-018207.en: The fear of being conspicuous does not usually land teenagers on jet airplanes bound for unknown destinations.
college-writing-018207.zh: 对引人注目的恐惧通常不会降落在飞往未知目的地的喷气式飞机上。

college-writing-018208.en: But for many adolescents, it rules their daily lives.
college-writing-018208.zh: 但对于许多青少年来说，它支配着他们的日常生活。

college-writing-018209.en: Such fear is rooted in the enormous self-consciousness that afflicts many adolescents.
college-writing-018209.zh: 这种恐惧植根于困扰许多青少年的巨大自我意识。

college-writing-018210.en: Psychologist David Elkind has come up with what he calls the “Imaginary Audience Theory” to help explain this period of life.
college-writing-018210.zh: 心理学家大卫·埃尔金德（David Elkind）提出了他所谓的“想象观众理论”来帮助解释这一生。

college-writing-018211.en: During adolescence, Elkind says, kids are changing so much so fast (physically, mentally, and emotionally) that they become intensely self-centered.
college-writing-018211.zh: 埃尔金德说，在青春期，孩子们的变化如此之快（身体上、精神上和情感上），以至于他们变得强烈以自我为中心。

college-writing-018212.en: It is literally difficult for them to remember that other individuals have their own lives, thoughts, and feelings, and that they are not focusing their attention on the adolescents.
college-writing-018212.zh: 他们很难记住其他人有自己的生活、想法和感受，并且他们没有将注意力集中在青少年身上。

college-writing-018213.en: According to Elkind, the adolescent feels as though he or she is on an enormous stage before a watchful audience that is noticing every aspect of his or her behavior.
college-writing-018213.zh: 根据埃尔金德的说法，青少年感觉好像他或她在一个巨大的舞台上，在一个警惕的观众面前，他们注意到了他或她行为的各个方面。

college-writing-018214.en: As a result, the adolescent is terrified of doing or saying something that will attract scorn or criticism.
college-writing-018214.zh: 结果，青少年害怕做或说会引起蔑视或批评的事情。

college-writing-018215.en: As a result, we end up with the teenager
college-writing-018215.zh: 结果，我们最终得到了少年

college-writing-018217.en: whose life is “ruined” by an outbreak of acne; an adolescent who won’t leave the house on a bad hair day, or the teen who refuses to return to school after making an embarrassing slip during a speech.
college-writing-018217.zh: 其生命因痤疮爆发而“毁坏”； 一个不会在头发糟糕的日子里离开家的青少年，或者在演讲中做出令人尴尬的失误后拒绝返回学校的青少年。

college-writing-018218.en: In general, typical adolescent fears don’t do great harm.
college-writing-018218.zh: 一般来说，典型的青少年恐惧不会造成很大的伤害。

college-writing-018219.en: Kids mature and eventually realize a moment’s embarrassment isn’t that big a deal, and that, in fact, most people aren’t paying much attention to them at all.
college-writing-018219.zh: 孩子们成熟了，最终意识到片刻的尴尬没什么大不了的，事实上，大多数人根本没有太关注他们。

college-writing-018220.en: But the fear of being conspicuous can have serious, even tragic results.
college-writing-018220.zh: 但对显眼的恐惧可能会产生严重的、甚至是悲剧性的结果。

college-writing-018221.en: Adolescents can be so fearful of being criticized that they sometimes go along with the crowd when it is in their best interests not to.
college-writing-018221.zh: 青少年可能会如此害怕被批评，以至于他们有时会在符合他们最大利益的情况下与人群一起去。

college-writing-018222.en: Teens get into cars with obviously intoxicated drivers; they go along with the crowd on a shoplifting expedition; they engage in risky sexual behavior, etc., in large part because they are afraid to speak up and risk the scorn of the “audience.”
college-writing-018222.zh: 青少年带着明显醉酒的司机上车； 他们与人群一起入店行窃探险； 他们从事危险的性行为等，很大程度上是因为他们害怕说出来并冒着“受众”的轻蔑风险。

college-writing-018223.en: In midlife, we generally become more confident and less obsessed with what others are thinking of us.
college-writing-018223.zh: 在中年时，我们通常会变得更加自信，对别人对我们的看法更少痴迷。

college-writing-018224.en: But underneath that veneer of confidence, a new kind of fear grips many middle-aged people.
college-writing-018224.zh: 但在这种自信的外表之下，一种新的恐惧笼罩着许多中年人。

college-writing-018225.en: That fear has been expressed in timeless fashion by the Italian poet Dante in his famous poem The Inferno: “In the middle of the road, I found myself in a dark wood, with no clear path through.”
college-writing-018225.zh: 意大利诗人但丁在他的著名诗《地狱》中以永恒的方式表达了这种恐惧：

college-writing-018227.en: As people enter middle age, they face the unsettling fact that their lives are halfway over.
college-writing-018227.zh: 随着人们进入中年，他们面临着令人不安的事实，即他们的生活已经过去了一半。

college-writing-018228.en: They are no longer youngsters, looking ahead at decades filled with unlimited potential.
college-writing-018228.zh: 他们不再是年轻人，展望未来充满无限潜力的几十年。

college-writing-018229.en: In looking back at what they have accomplished, many people feel unsatisfied.
college-writing-018229.zh: 回顾他们所取得的成就，许多人感到不满意。

college-writing-018230.en: They may not have achieved the career success they had hoped for.
college-writing-018230.zh: 他们可能没有取得他们希望的职业成功。

college-writing-018231.en: They fear they do not have time to reach goals that they had once dreamed of.
college-writing-018231.zh: 他们担心自己没有时间去实现他们曾经梦想的目标。

college-writing-018232.en: They become critical of their own aging bodies.
college-writing-018232.zh: 他们对自己老化的身体变得批评。

college-writing-018233.en: As their parents die and their children grow up and leave home, they feel adrift, no longer certain of their roles in life.
college-writing-018233.zh: 当他们的父母死去，他们的孩子长大并离开家时，他们感到漂泊，不再确定自己在生活中的角色。

college-writing-018234.en: Frightening thoughts press in: “My life is heading downhill. I’m running out of time.”
college-writing-018234.zh: 可怕的想法写进来：“我的人生正在走下坡路。我的时间不多了。”

college-writing-018235.en: The result of all this inner turmoil is what is often termed a midlife crisis.
college-writing-018235.zh: 所有这些内心动荡的结果是通常被称为中年危机的结果。

college-writing-018236.en: Movies and sitcoms often present such a crisis in tragicomic style: the middle-aged guy dumps his wife, dyes his hair, buys a sports car, and begins romancing a woman young enough to be his daughter.
college-writing-018236.zh: 电影和情景喜剧经常以悲剧风格呈现出这样的危机：中年人甩掉妻子，染发，买一辆跑车，并开始与一个足够年轻的女人成为他的女儿。

college-writing-018237.en: The middle-aged woman gets liposuction and a facelift and has an affair with a young personal trainer.
college-writing-018237.zh: 中年妇女接受吸脂和整容，并与一位年轻的私人教练有染。

college-writing-018238.en: There is plenty of evidence that such behavior does occur.
college-writing-018238.zh: 有很多证据表明这种行为确实发生了。

college-writing-018239.en: Many long-term marriages break up as a result of one or both partners’ midlife crisis.
college-writing-018239.zh: 许多长期婚姻因伴侣的中年危机而破裂。

college-writing-018240.en: The panicky feelings that can result from thinking “Is this all there is?” can make even a formerly happy marriage seem suffocating.
college-writing-018240.zh: 想着“这就是一切吗？”可能产生的恐慌情绪。 甚至可以让以前幸福的婚姻显得令人窒息。

college-writing-018241.en: However, most midlife crises do not have such dramatic results.
college-writing-018241.zh: 然而，大多数中年危机并没有产生如此戏剧性的结果。

college-writing-018242.en: More typically, the midlife crisis is a time of inner exploration, of reconsidering one’s priorities.
college-writing-018242.zh: 更常见的是，中年危机是内在探索的时期，是重新考虑自己的优先事项。

college-writing-018243.en: It may involve a period of depression, but, fortunately, most people emerge from a midlife crisis feeling relatively satisfied.
college-writing-018243.zh: 它可能涉及一段时间的抑郁症，但幸运的是，大多数人从中年危机中脱颖而出，感到相对满意。

college-writing-018244.en: They come to terms with the idea that youth and its promise are behind them, and learn to appreciate the perhaps quieter joys of mature life.
college-writing-018244.zh: 他们接受了青年及其承诺在他们身后的想法，并学会欣赏成熟生活中可能更安静的快乐。

college-writing-018245.en: Those joys and a sense of certainty about life’s priorities often carry over into the elderly years.
college-writing-018245.zh: 那些快乐和对生活优先事项的确定感常常会延续到老年人的岁月里。

college-writing-018246.en: Senior citizens’ self-knowledge often allows them to state their opinions and explore new interests in a way they did not feel free to in their younger years.
college-writing-018246.zh: 老年人的自我认识常常允许他们以他们年轻时没有自由的方式表达自己的意见和探索新的兴趣。

college-writing-018247.zh: 672 第 5 部分 作家读物

college-writing-018248.en: But along with the relief from self-consciousness comes another set of fears for the elderly.
college-writing-018248.zh: 但伴随着从自我意识中解脱出来的另一套老年人的恐惧。

college-writing-018249.en: Those fears center around the increasing frailty of the body and the accompanying loss of independence.
college-writing-018249.zh: 这些恐惧集中在身体越来越脆弱和随之而来的独立性丧失方面。

college-writing-018250.en: Some years ago, a television ad featured an elderly woman saying, “Help! I’ve fallen and I can’t get up.”
college-writing-018250.zh: 几年前，一则电视广告中有一位老妇人说：“救命！我摔倒了，我起不来了。”

college-writing-018251.en: The ad became the punch line of many jokes, but the message was serious.
college-writing-018251.zh: 广告成为许多笑话的妙语，但信息很严肃。

college-writing-018252.en: Many elderly people report falling as their greatest fear.
college-writing-018252.zh: 许多老年人报告跌倒是他们最大的恐惧。

college-writing-018253.en: They are not simply concerned with the injury they might suffer.
college-writing-018253.zh: 他们不仅仅关心他们可能遭受的伤害。

college-writing-018254.en: They worry that a fall might lead to being institutionalized, a step that many elderly people fear deeply.
college-writing-018254.zh: 他们担心跌倒可能会导致制度化，这是许多老年人深感恐惧的一步。

college-writing-018255.en: After a lifetime of independence and, often, of taking care of others, they dread the idea of being helpless, even a burden to their families.
college-writing-018255.zh: 在一生的独立之后，经常照顾他人，他们害怕无助的想法，甚至是对家人的负担。

college-writing-018256.en: As a result, many elderly people─especially after having suffered a fall or another injury─become increasingly reluctant to go out into the world to try new things and keep up with friends.
college-writing-018256.zh: 结果，很多老人——特别是在摔倒或受伤后——变得越来越不愿意去世界上尝试新事物，跟上朋友的步伐。

college-writing-018257.en: Afraid of being hurt, they become hermit-like, staying within the confines of their homes.
college-writing-018257.zh: 害怕受到伤害，他们变得像隐士一样，呆在家里。

college-writing-018258.en: Ironically, this isolation and lack of exercise can actually hasten the dreaded loss of independence.
college-writing-018258.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，这种孤立和缺乏锻炼实际上可以加速可怕的独立性丧失。

college-writing-018259.en: Mental and physical activity are both key elements in keeping elderly people in good health.
college-writing-018259.zh: 心理和身体活动都是保持老年人健康的关键要素。

college-writing-018260.en: Benjamin Franklin once wrote, “In this world nothing is certain but death and taxes.”
college-writing-018260.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林曾写道：“在这个世界上，除了死亡和税收，没有什么是确定的。”

college-writing-018261.zh: 富兰克林可能补充说，“和恐惧”。

college-writing-018262.en: Every stage of life brings them; while we may say goodbye to childish fears, there are always others in the wings, waiting to take their place.
college-writing-018262.zh: 生命的每个阶段都带来了他们； 虽然我们可能会与幼稚的恐惧说再见，但总有其他人在等待取代他们的位置。

college-writing-018263.en: By being aware of them, we can keep their dark shadows from adversely affecting our lives.
college-writing-018263.zh: 通过了解它们，我们可以防止它们的黑暗阴影对我们的生活产生不利影响。

college-writing-018266.zh: 被称为中年危机”（第 19 段）的意思

college-writing-018366.en: Write an essay about a frightening incident that occurred during your childhood.
college-writing-018366.zh: 写一篇关于你童年时期发生的可怕事件的文章。

college-writing-018367.en: Begin by providing some background information about yourself.
college-writing-018367.zh: 首先提供一些关于你自己的背景信息。

college-writing-018368.en: How old were you when this incident occurred?
college-writing-018368.zh: 这起事件发生时你几岁？

college-writing-018370.en: Was another person involved besides you?
college-writing-018370.zh: 除了你，还有另一个人参与吗？

college-writing-018371.en: Was this incident something you had feared might happen, or did it happen unexpectedly?
college-writing-018371.zh: 这个事件是你担心可能发生的事情，还是它出乎意料地发生了？

college-writing-018372.en: Then organize your supporting paragraphs into two or three time phases.
college-writing-018372.zh: 然后将您的支持段落分成两个或三个时间阶段。

college-writing-018373.zh: 首先，您可能想回顾关于叙事论文的第 9 章。

college-writing-018374.zh: 你可以通过总结这件事对童年恐惧的一般意义来结束你的文章。

college-writing-018375.en: Alternatively, write an essay in which you describe in detail three of your childhood fears.
college-writing-018375.zh: 或者，写一篇文章，你详细描述了你童年的三个恐惧。

college-writing-018376.zh: 你的论文的论文可能类似于：

college-writing-018377.en: Like Audra Kendall in “The Certainty of Fear,” I had my own childhood fears.
college-writing-018377.zh: 就像“恐惧的确定性”中的奥德拉·肯德尔一样，我有自己的童年恐惧。

college-writing-018379.en: Kendall writes about fears that characterize different life stages.
college-writing-018379.zh: 肯德尔写了描述不同人生阶段的恐惧。

college-writing-018380.en: Think of some people you know of different ages.
college-writing-018380.zh: 想想你认识的不同年龄的一些人。

college-writing-018381.en: Then write an essay about three of them who exhibit fears characteristic of their age group.
college-writing-018381.zh: 然后写一篇关于他们三个表现出他们年龄组的恐惧特征的文章。

college-writing-018382.en: The thesis of your essay might be similar to this:
college-writing-018382.zh: 你的论文的论文可能类似于：

college-writing-018383.en: It is clear to me that my little brother Ben, my thirteen-year-old cousin Ted, and my grandmother Rose have fears that are specific to their age group.
college-writing-018383.zh: 我很清楚，我的弟弟本、我 13 岁的表弟泰德和我的祖母罗斯对他们的年龄组有特定的恐惧。

college-writing-018384.en: A supporting paragraph about a little brother, for instance, might begin, “Since I’m often around him, I’ve come to realize that my little brother Ben has some typical childhood fears.”
college-writing-018384.zh: 例如，关于一个弟弟的支持段落可能会以“因为我经常在他身边，我开始意识到我的弟弟本有一些典型的童年恐惧”开始。

college-writing-018386.en: Often the things we fear never happen, such as the fear the teens in the selection had of landing someplace other than in Florence, Italy.
college-writing-018386.zh: 通常我们担心的事情永远不会发生，例如在选择中的青少年害怕降落在意大利佛罗伦萨以外的某个地方。

college-writing-018387.zh: 写一篇文章，将你对三个不同场合可能发生的事情的恐惧与实际发生的事情进行对比。

college-writing-018393.en: “With regard to The Secret Garden,” Frances Hodgson Burnett wrote to her English publisher in October 1910, “do you realize that it is not a novel, but a childs [sic] story though it is gravely beginning life as an important illustrated serial in a magazine for adults. . . . It is an innocent thriller of a story to which grown ups listen spell bound to my keen delight.”
college-writing-018393.zh: “关于秘密花园，”弗朗西斯·霍奇森·伯内特（Frances Hodgson Burnett）在 1910 年 10 月写信给她的英国出版商，“你是否意识到这不是一部小说，而是一个儿童 [原文如此] 的故事，尽管它是成人杂志中重要的插图连续剧的开始。 .这是一部无辜的惊悚片，成年人听着我强烈的喜悦。”

college-writing-018394.en: The “thriller of a story” made its first appearance that fall in The American Magazine, but appeared as an actual book a year later.
college-writing-018394.zh: “故事的惊悚片”在美国杂志上首次亮相，但一年后作为一本真正的书出现。

college-writing-018395.en: Now, as the novel is celebrated during its centennial year, it’s fascinating to go back and see the modest beginning of a book that is repeatedly cited as one of the most influential and beloved children’s books of all time.
college-writing-018395.zh: 现在，正如这部小说在其百年纪念年庆祝的那样，回顾一本被一再引用为有史以来最有影响力和最受喜爱的儿童读物的书的谦虚开始是令人着迷的。

college-writing-018396.en: Yet Burnett would be astonished today to learn that she is known primarily as a writer for children, when the majority of her fifty-three novels and thirteen produced plays were for adults.
college-writing-018396.zh: 然而，伯内特今天会惊讶地得知她主要被称为儿童作家，而她的 53 部小说和 13 部作品中的大部分是为成年人制作的。

college-writing-018397.en: When Burnett sat down to write the story of an orphaned girl sent from India to the Yorkshire moors, where she helps herself and others find redemption and health by reviving a forgotten garden, she composed it not in the north of England but in her new home on Long Island.
college-writing-018397.zh: 当伯内特坐下来写一个从印度送往约克郡荒野的孤儿女孩的故事时，她通过复兴一个被遗忘的花园来帮助自己和其他人找到救赎和健康，她不是在英格兰北部而是在她位于长岛的新家中创作的。

college-writing-018398.en: Born in 1849 and raised in Manchester, England, into a middle class family, she moved as a teenager to Tennessee when her widowed mother decided they should emigrate at the end of the Civil War.
college-writing-018398.zh: 出生于 1849 年，在英国曼彻斯特长大，在内战结束时，她的丧偶母亲决定移民到田纳西州，十几岁时搬到了田纳西州。

college-writing-018399.en: Although they were poor, Burnett was delighted at giving up the grit and smoke of a factory city for the stunning landscapes of eastern Tennessee.
college-writing-018399.zh: 尽管他们很穷，但伯内特很高兴为田纳西州东部的壮丽景观放弃了工厂城市的勇气和烟雾。

college-writing-018401.en: Gretchen Holbrook Gerzina holds a Ph.D. from Stanford University and
college-writing-018401.zh: Gretchen Holbrook Gerzina 拥有博士学位。 来自斯坦福大学和

college-writing-018402.en: has taught at Vassar College and Barnard College, Columbia University.
college-writing-018402.zh: 曾在哥伦比亚大学瓦萨学院和巴纳德学院任教。

college-writing-018403.en: In this essay, Dr. Gerzina discusses the life of Frances Hodgson Burnett
college-writing-018403.zh: 在这篇文章中，格尔齐纳博士讨论了弗朗西斯·霍奇森·伯内特的生平

college-writing-018404.en: and what influenced her to write The Secret Garden.
college-writing-018404.zh: 以及是什么影响了她写《秘密花园》。

college-writing-018406.zh: 格雷琴·霍尔布鲁克·格尔齐纳

college-writing-018408.zh: Gretchen Holbrook Gerzina/英联邦荣誉学院

college-writing-018410.en: she soon began to publish her romantic stories in some of the most popular magazines, eventually becoming hugely famous when she published her sixth novel, Little Lord Fauntleroy, in 1886.
college-writing-018410.zh: 她很快就开始在一些最受欢迎的杂志上发表她的浪漫故事，最终在她出版了她的第六部小说《小王子》（Little Lord Fauntleroy）后，在 1886 年出版了她的浪漫故事。

college-writing-018411.en: From the first her work had never been turned down by any publisher, but with Fauntleroy she became, and remained, the highest paid woman writer of her time, churning out books and stories with great regularity.
college-writing-018411.zh: 从一开始，她的作品从未被任何出版商拒绝，但随着 Fauntleroy 的创作，她成为并仍然是她那个时代收入最高的女作家，非常规律地制作书籍和故事。

college-writing-018412.en: Despite the enormous success of Fauntleroy, and later of A Little Princess, most of her novels and plays were not for a juvenile audience.
college-writing-018412.zh: 尽管 Fauntleroy 以及后来的小公主取得了巨大的成功，但她的大部分小说和戏剧都不是为少年观众准备的。

college-writing-018413.en: By this time a married mother of two living in Washington, DC, she capitalized on her English background in most of her work.
college-writing-018413.zh: 到了这个时候，她是一个住在华盛顿特区的两个孩子的已婚母亲，她在大部分工作中利用了自己的英语背景。

college-writing-018414.en: Over the years, England remained an active and important part of her life.
college-writing-018414.zh: 多年来，英格兰仍然是她生活中积极而重要的一部分。

college-writing-018415.en: She crossed the Atlantic no fewer than thirty-three times over her lifetime, often living abroad for a year or two at a time.
college-writing-018415.zh: 她一生中穿越大西洋不少于三十三次，经常一次在国外生活一两年。

college-writing-018416.en: At the same time, she maintained homes in Washington, and later in New York, and doted upon her very American sons, even when her marriage to their father broke down and through some surprisingly long absences from them.
college-writing-018416.zh: 与此同时，她在华盛顿和后来的纽约维持家园，并宠爱她的美国儿子，即使她与父亲的婚姻破裂，以及他们的一些令人惊讶的长期缺席。

college-writing-018417.en: Two life-changing events contributed to the genesis of The Secret Garden, which was written late in her life.
college-writing-018417.zh: 两个改变生活的事件促成了她生命晚期写的秘密花园的起源。

college-writing-018418.en: The first was the death of her sixteen-year-old son Lionel, who became increasingly ill in Washington while she was living away.
college-writing-018418.zh: 第一个是她 16 岁的儿子莱昂内尔去世，她在华盛顿住得越来越重病。

college-writing-018419.en: Her husband, Dr. Swan Burnett, wrote her urgent letters about their son’s failing health, but it was not until the diagnosis turned out to be tuberculosis that she rushed home to take Lionel on a desperate circuit of European spas.
college-writing-018419.zh: 她的丈夫 Swan Burnett 博士写了她关于他们儿子健康状况不佳的紧急信件，但直到诊断结果证明是肺结核，她才赶回家把莱昂内尔带回了一个绝望的欧洲水疗中心。

college-writing-018420.en: When he died in her arms in Paris at the end of 1890, she was completely devastated.
college-writing-018420.zh: 1890 年底，当他在巴黎死在她的怀里时，她被彻底摧毁了。

college-writing-018421.en: For years she threw herself into starting and supporting a clubhouse for boys in London, and in spoiling her remaining son, Vivian.
college-writing-018421.zh: 多年来，她全身心地投入到伦敦男孩的俱乐部会所，并宠坏了她剩下的儿子薇薇安。

college-writing-018422.en: The second loss was that of her beloved home Maytham Hall in Kent, in southern England, which she had leased for ten years.
college-writing-018422.zh: 第二次损失是她在英格兰南部肯特的心爱的家梅瑟姆大厅，她租了十年。

college-writing-018423.en: In1908 the leaseholder decided to sell the grand house, and Burnett was forced to leave the home where she had spent the happiest months of each year, after shedding her abusive second husband.
college-writing-018423.zh: 1908 年，承租人决定卖掉这座大房子，伯内特在摆脱了虐待她的第二任丈夫后被迫离开了她度过了每年最快乐几个月的房子。

college-writing-018424.en: There she cultivated extensive gardens, held parties, and tamed a robin as she wrote outdoors at a table in a sheltered garden.
college-writing-018424.zh: 在那里，她种植了广阔的花园，举办了派对，并在户外的避风花园的桌子上写下了一只知更鸟。

college-writing-018425.en: Both the robin and the gardens made their way into The Secret Garden.
college-writing-018425.zh: 罗宾和花园都进入了秘密花园。

college-writing-018426.en: With the loss of Maytham Hall, Burnett returned to America where she built adjoining houses for herself and her sister Edith, and for Vivian and his family in Plandome, on Long Island.
college-writing-018426.zh: 随着梅瑟姆·霍尔的丧失，伯内特回到了美国，在那里她为自己和姐姐伊迪丝以及在长岛的普兰多姆为薇薇安和他的家人建造了毗邻的房屋。

college-writing-018427.en: She returned for several long sojourns to England, and spent her winters with Edith in Bermuda.
college-writing-018427.zh: 她回到英国度过了几个漫长的旅程，并在百慕大与伊迪丝一起度过了她的冬天。

college-writing-018428.en: In both Bermuda and Plandome she threw herself into gardening, with the help of gardeners, designing extensive gardens that produced award-winning blooms.
college-writing-018428.zh: 在百慕大和普兰多姆，她在园丁的帮助下投入到园艺中，设计了广泛的花园，这些花园产生了屡获殊荣的花朵。

college-writing-018429.en: Roses were her favorite, and her trademark, just as they were for Lilias Craven in The Secret Garden.
college-writing-018429.zh: 玫瑰是她的最爱，也是她的标志，就像它们在秘密花园里为莉莉亚斯克雷文一样。

college-writing-018430.en: Every year Burnett published a book in time for the Christmas market, and in 1910 she found herself intrigued by the thought of a sallow and unlikeable little girl, her disabled cousin, and a strong nature-loving boy and his benevolent mother.
college-writing-018430.zh: 伯内特每年都会出版一本《及时为圣诞市场》出版的书，1910 年，她发现自己对一个蜡黄和不可爱的小女孩、她残疾的表弟、一个热爱大自然的男孩和他仁慈的母亲的想法很感兴趣。

college-writing-018431.en: Always taken with her own writing─she often declared that they “came” to her rather than being invented, and she could sometimes be found reading her own books on a stairway, with evident pleasure─she wrote to her publisher that “I love it myself.
college-writing-018431.zh: 总是带着她自己的写作——她经常宣称他们“来到”她而不是被发明，有时可以发现她在楼梯上阅读她自己的书，显然很高兴——她写信给她的出版商说：“我自己喜欢它。

college-writing-018433.zh: 678 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-018434.en: garden in it whose locked door is hidden by ivy and whose key has been buried for ten years.
college-writing-018434.zh: 花园里的花园被常春藤藏起来，钥匙被埋了十年。

college-writing-018435.en: It contains also a sort of Faun who charms wild creatures and tame ones and there is a moorland cottage woman who is a sort of Madonna with twelve children─a warm bosomed, sane, wise, simple Mother thing.
college-writing-018435.zh: 它还包含一种迷人的野生动物和驯服的动物，还有一个有十二个孩子的摩尔兰小屋的女人——一个温暖的、理智的、简单的、简单的母亲的东西。

college-writing-018436.en: Burnett loved the combination of the gothic and the natural worlds, and the ability of children to understand and appreciate them in everyday life.
college-writing-018436.zh: 伯内特喜欢哥特式和自然世界的结合，以及孩子们在日常生活中理解和欣赏它们的能力。

college-writing-018437.en: In this new story, she was able, whether she recognized it or not, to recover from her two enormous losses.
college-writing-018437.zh: 在这个新故事中，无论她是否认出，她都能够从她的两次巨大损失中恢复过来。

college-writing-018438.en: Unlike her son Lionel, Colin Craven is restored to health at the end of the novel.
college-writing-018438.zh: 与她的儿子莱昂内尔不同，科林·克雷文在小说的结尾恢复了健康。

college-writing-018439.en: And unlike Maytham Hall, the gardens at Misselthwaite Manor continually bloomed.
college-writing-018439.zh: 与梅瑟姆大厅不同，米塞尔斯韦特庄园的花园不断开花。

college-writing-018440.en: When Burnett died in 1924, her friends helped erect a memorial to her in Central Park, consisting of a fountain surrounded by gardens and reading benches.
college-writing-018440.zh: 当伯内特于 1924 年去世时，她的朋友们帮助她在中央公园为她竖立了一座纪念碑，那里有一个被花园和阅读长椅包围的喷泉。

college-writing-018441.en: Their prescient choice of The Secret Garden for the fountain sculpture surprised the public, for it was, at the time, one of her lesser known and appreciated books, but they knew these were things that were close to the author’s heart.
college-writing-018441.zh: 他们有先见之明的秘密花园作为喷泉雕塑的选择让公众感到惊讶，因为在当时，这是她鲜为人知和欣赏的一本书，但他们知道这些是作者心目中的东西。

college-writing-018442.en: Although it sold well enough at first, The Secret Garden lapsed into a kind of near oblivion for many decades.
college-writing-018442.zh: 虽然起初它卖得足够好，但几十年来，秘密花园变成了一种近乎被遗忘的东西。

college-writing-018443.en: Critics ignored or disparaged it, even at a time when children’s literature began receiving more and more critical and scholarly attention.
college-writing-018443.zh: 即使在儿童文学开始受到越来越多的批评和学术关注的时候，批评者也忽略或贬低了它。

college-writing-018444.en: It was the children, along with librarians, who saved it, passing on the book to readers and friends, and creating a special place in their hearts for the story.
college-writing-018444.zh: 是孩子们和图书馆员一起拯救了它，将这本书传递给读者和朋友，并在他们心中为故事创造了一个特殊的位置。

college-writing-018445.en: By the 1960s, its fortunes began to revive, and when the book went out of copyright in 1986, dozens of illustrators and publishers rushed to reproduce it.
college-writing-018445.zh: 到 1960 年代，它的命运开始复苏，当这本书在 1986 年失去版权时，数十名插画家和出版商急于复制它。

college-writing-018446.en: As we celebrate 100 years of The Secret Garden, the book has never been more popular or influential.
college-writing-018446.zh: 当我们庆祝秘密花园 100 周年时，这本书从未像现在这样流行或有影响力。

college-writing-018447.en: Whole shelves in bookstores carry its many editions, and it has been translated into nearly every known language.
college-writing-018447.zh: 书店的整个书架上都有许多版本，它已被翻译成几乎所有已知的语言。

college-writing-018448.en: Children around the world continue to love the story of the children, who with the help of nature and positive thinking, bring the world back to life.
college-writing-018448.zh: 世界各地的孩子们继续爱着孩子们的故事，他们在大自然和积极思考的帮助下，让世界复活。

college-writing-018449.en: As Burnett said to a friend, “I know quite well that it is one of my best finds.”
college-writing-018449.zh: 正如伯内特对一位朋友所说，“我很清楚这是我最好的发现之一。”

college-writing-018450.en: Children and adults one hundred years later, still agree.
college-writing-018450.zh: 一百年后的儿童和成人，仍然同意。

college-writing-018524.zh: 1. 在第 4 段中，提交人声称伯内特宠爱她的儿子。

college-writing-018526.en: graphs 4 and 5; do you feel Burnett was a doting mother?
college-writing-018526.zh: 图 4 和图 5； 你觉得伯内特是一个溺爱的母亲吗？

college-writing-018528.en: 2. In paragraph 9, the author states, “Burnett loved the combination of the
college-writing-018528.zh: 2. 在第 9 段中，作者指出，“伯内特喜欢将

college-writing-018529.en: gothic and the natural worlds, and the ability of children to understand and appreciate them in everyday life.
college-writing-018529.zh: 哥特式和自然世界，以及儿童在日常生活中理解和欣赏它们的能力。

college-writing-018530.en: ” Do you agree or disagree with the author’s opinion?
college-writing-018530.zh: “你同意还是不同意作者的意见？

college-writing-018532.en: 3. The author claims that “children, along with librarians” saved The Secret
college-writing-018532.zh: 3. 作者声称“孩子们和图书馆员”保住了这个秘密

college-writing-018533.en: Garden by “passing on the book to readers and friends, and creating a special place in their hearts for the story.”
college-writing-018533.zh: “把书传给读者和朋友，在他们心中创造一个特殊的地方，为故事创造一个特殊的地方”。

college-writing-018534.en: Can you think of other books that have had similar fates?
college-writing-018534.zh: 你能想到其他命运相似的书吗？

college-writing-018535.en: 4. In 1986, The Secret Garden went out of copyright.

college-writing-018538.en: would illustrators and publishers be interested in something going out of copyright?
college-writing-018538.zh: 插画家和出版商会对超出版权的东西感兴趣吗？

college-writing-018542.en: The book The Secret Garden is about a neglected garden that is brought back to life with love and attention.
college-writing-018542.zh: 《秘密花园》一书是关于一个被忽视的花园，它被爱和关注带回了生活。

college-writing-018543.en: The garden is a metaphor for people; when people are neglected or forgotten, they wither away.
college-writing-018543.zh: 花园是人们的隐喻； 当人们被忽视或遗忘时，他们就会枯萎。

college-writing-018544.en: Using this idea of metaphor, write an essay in which you discuss a time you felt neglected, but someone stepped in and helped you blossom.
college-writing-018544.zh: 用这个隐喻的想法，写一篇文章，你讨论一个你感到被忽视的时间，但有人介入并帮助你开花。

college-writing-018545.en: You might focus on a teacher who helped you personally or academically; a family member who helped you find your talents; or a coach who helped you achieve goals others didn’t think you would reach.
college-writing-018545.zh: 您可能会专注于帮助您个人或学术的老师； 帮助您找到才能的家庭成员； 或者帮助您实现其他人认为您无法达到的目标的教练。

college-writing-018547.en: Write an essay in which you discuss the merits of one of your favorite children’s (or young adult’s) books and why it should be celebrated as The Secret Garden has been.
college-writing-018547.zh: 写一篇文章，讨论你最喜欢的儿童（或年轻人）书籍的优点，以及为什么应该像秘密花园一样庆祝它。

college-writing-018548.en: Your essay should focus on the strengths of the book, why it is significant enough to its genre, and why others should read it.
college-writing-018548.zh: 你的文章应该关注这本书的优势，为什么它对它的体裁足够重要，以及为什么其他人应该阅读它。

college-writing-018550.en: Urban gardening has become a widespread phenomenon over the past decade.
college-writing-018550.zh: 在过去的十年里，城市园艺已成为一种普遍的现象。

college-writing-018551.en: Gardens have been popping up everywhere─windowsills and decks, rooftops, abandoned city lots, and even in the back of truck beds.
college-writing-018551.zh: 花园到处都出现了——窗台和甲板、屋顶、废弃的城市地段，甚至在卡车床的后面。

college-writing-018552.en: Many cities have begun urban gardens to help bring fresh fruits and vegetables to people who have normally been unable to acquire or afford these foods.
college-writing-018552.zh: 许多城市已经开始了城市花园，以帮助通常无法获得或负担这些食物的人提供新鲜的水果和蔬菜。

college-writing-018553.en: In this essay, you are to research the affordability and availability of fresh fruits and vegetables in your town or city.
college-writing-018553.zh: 在这篇文章中，您将研究您所在城镇或城市的新鲜水果和蔬菜的可负担性和可用性。

college-writing-018554.en: Does your city have farmers’ markets?
college-writing-018554.zh: 你的城市有农贸市场吗？

college-writing-018556.en: Do you have any food deserts (areas where it is difficult to purchase fresh food)?
college-writing-018556.zh: 您是否有任何食物沙漠（难以购买新鲜食品的地区）？

college-writing-018557.en: Once you have learned about what your city or town has to offer, create a plan that will increase the availability of affordable fresh food to the citizens of your community.
college-writing-018557.zh: 一旦您了解了您的城市或城镇所提供的服务，请制定一个计划，以增加您所在社区公民的负担得起的新鲜食品的可用性。

college-writing-018558.en: This plan may include locating abandoned or untended lots and getting a community volunteer program together to begin prepping the soil; partnering with local nurseries; and/or working with local colleges and universities.
college-writing-018558.zh: 该计划可能包括找到废弃或无人照料的地段，并召集社区志愿者计划开始准备土壤； 与当地托儿所合作； 和/或与当地学院和大学合作。

college-writing-018559.en: Once you have created a plan, you will want to write your essay as if you are presenting it to your city council.
college-writing-018559.zh: 一旦你制定了一个计划，你就会想写你的论文，就像你把它提交给你的市议会一样。

college-writing-018560.en: This means that you will need to develop a formal argument that will include an explanation of the process (how it will be created and how people will access the food) and answer potential questions about costs, workers, and logistics.
college-writing-018560.zh: 这意味着您需要制定一个正式的论点，其中包括对过程的解释（将如何创建以及人们将如何获得食物）并回答有关成本、工人和物流的潜在问题。

college-writing-018563.en: Colleges Must Confront Structural Racism Kevin V. Collymore 683
college-writing-018563.zh: 大学必须面对结构性种族主义 Kevin V. Collymore 683

college-writing-018564.en: How to Make It in College, Now That You’re Here Brian O’Keeney 690
college-writing-018564.zh: 如何在大学里成功，既然你在这里 Brian O'Keeney 690

college-writing-018568.zh: 谷歌是在让我们变得愚蠢吗？

college-writing-018570.en: The Quiet Struggle of College Students with Kids Gillian B. White 725
college-writing-018570.zh: 有孩子的大学生的安静斗争 Gillian B. White 725

college-writing-018571.en: What Academics Misunderstand about ‘Public Writing’ Irina Dumitrescu 733
college-writing-018571.zh: 学者对“公开写作”的误解 伊琳娜·杜米特雷斯库 733

college-writing-018574.en: The protest movement spurred by the killing of George Floyd aims to dismantle not only instances of overt racism and violence but also institutional racism in every sector of American life.
college-writing-018574.zh: 由乔治·弗洛伊德（George Floyd）杀害引发的抗议运动不仅旨在消除美国生活的每个部门的公开种族主义和暴力事件，还要消除制度性的种族主义。

college-writing-018575.en: Higher education will not be immune from this reckoning.
college-writing-018575.zh: 高等教育将无法免于这种清算。

college-writing-018576.en: Whether colleges end up operating in person, online, or in a hybrid format this fall, they will have to confront structural racism head-on.
college-writing-018576.zh: 无论大学最终在今年秋天以个人、在线还是混合形式最终运营，它们都将不得不正面面对结构性种族主义。

college-writing-018577.en: For students, who have made clear their dissatisfaction with the status quo, empty gestures from administrators will not be enough.
college-writing-018577.zh: 对于那些已经明确表示对现状不满的学生来说，管理人员的空洞姿态是不够的。

college-writing-018578.zh: 他们将要求有意义的改变。

college-writing-018579.en: They will demand leadership that is proactive, not reactive.
college-writing-018579.zh: 他们将要求主动而不是被动的领导。

college-writing-018580.en: Here are some concrete steps colleges can take to combat structural racism in higher education:
college-writing-018580.zh: 以下是大学可以采取的一些具体步骤来对抗高等教育中的结构性种族主义：

college-writing-018581.en: Require implicit-bias training for anyone involved in admissions.
college-writing-018581.zh: 需要对参与招生的任何人进行隐式偏见培训。

college-writing-018582.en: Admissions workers are the gatekeepers of institutions.
college-writing-018582.zh: 招生工作人员是机构的看门人。

college-writing-018583.en: They must understand the importance of their role, as well as the biases they bring to it.
college-writing-018583.zh: 他们必须了解他们的角色的重要性，以及他们给它带来的偏见。

college-writing-018584.en: All application readers should undergo training to recognize their unconscious biases before every admissions cycle.
college-writing-018584.zh: 所有应用程序读者都应该在每个录取周期之前接受培训，以识别他们的无意识偏见。

college-writing-018585.en: In her decision upholding affirmative action at Harvard University, Judge Allison D. Burroughs advised implicit-bias training for its admissions team.
college-writing-018585.zh: 在哈佛大学支持平权行动的决定中，艾莉森·D·伯勒斯法官为其招生团队提供了隐性偏见的建议。

college-writing-018586.en: This valuable and necessary intervention should be adopted at all colleges, even when a federal judge doesn’t recommend it.
college-writing-018586.zh: 即使联邦法官不建议，也应在所有大学采用这种有价值且必要的干预措施。

college-writing-018587.en: Kevin V. Collymore received his M.A. in higher education and student affairs from New York University.
college-writing-018587.zh: Kevin V. Collymore 在纽约大学获得高等教育和学生事务硕士学位。

college-writing-018588.en: In this essay, in which he analyzes what colleges should be doing to stop structural racism, he writes from his current perspective as the Assistant Director of Advisement and Student Services at New York University.
college-writing-018588.zh: 在这篇文章中，他分析了大学应该采取哪些措施来阻止结构性种族主义，他从目前的角度写作，担任纽约大学的顾问和学生服务助理主任。

college-writing-018589.zh: 大学必须面对结构性种族歧视

college-writing-018590.en: Here are steps they should take now
college-writing-018590.zh: 这是他们现在应该采取的步骤

college-writing-018594.zh: 684 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-018595.en: Guarantee financial aid beyond the first year.
college-writing-018595.zh: 保证第一年以后的经济援助。

college-writing-018596.en: Stop front-loading financial-aid packages to lure first-generation and underrepresented students to your institution.
college-writing-018596.zh: 停止前置的经济援助计划，以吸引第一代和代表性不足的学生来到您的机构。

college-writing-018597.en: This includes the practice of offering merit-aid scholarships with preconditions for continued funding beyond the first year.
college-writing-018597.zh: 这包括在第一年之后继续提供资助奖学金的做法，并提供持续资金的先决条件。

college-writing-018598.en: A bachelor’s degree is a key way for this population to improve not only their lives but also the lives of their immediate families.
college-writing-018598.zh: 学士学位不仅是这些人群改善生活的关键途径，也是改善直系亲属生活的关键途径。

college-writing-018599.en: If students are increasingly burdened by the stress of making payments, it can affect their academic performance, including their ability to stay enrolled.
college-writing-018599.zh: 如果学生越来越多地承受支付的压力，它会影响他们的学习成绩，包括他们的入学能力。

college-writing-018600.en: Those who do manage to graduate are likely to become disaffected alumni.
college-writing-018600.zh: 那些成功毕业的人很可能会成为心怀不满的校友。

college-writing-018601.en: Require de-escalation training for public-safety officers.
college-writing-018601.zh: 需要对公共安全人员进行降级培训。

college-writing-018602.en: The physical safety and well-being of students are core responsibilities of all colleges.
college-writing-018602.zh: 学生的人身安全和福祉是所有大学的核心职责。

college-writing-018603.en: Public-safety officers should be required to undergo racial-bias and de-escalation training annually.
college-writing-018603.zh: 应要求公共安全官员每年接受种族偏见和降级培训。

college-writing-018604.en: Further, public-safety administrators should make an effort to participate in student town halls and student-government meetings to build trust.
college-writing-018604.zh: 此外，公共安全管理人员应努力参加学生市政厅和学生政府会议以建立信任。

college-writing-018605.en: Students shouldn’t hear from the campus police only during a crisis.
college-writing-018605.zh: 学生不应仅在危机期间收到校园警察的消息。

college-writing-018606.en: At Barnard College, for example, a community-safety group is “charged with discussing broad issues related to campus safety, including concerns about racial and other forms of bias and their consequences.”
college-writing-018606.zh: 例如，在巴纳德学院，一个社区安全小组“负责讨论与校园安全相关的广泛问题，包括对种族和其他形式的偏见及其后果的担忧。”

college-writing-018607.zh: 采取透明的学生抗议政策。

college-writing-018608.en: At public colleges, students are guaranteed their constitutional right to free assembly.
college-writing-018608.zh: 在公立大学，学生获得自由集会的宪法权利。

college-writing-018609.en: At private institutions, there should be a well-defined process to allow students to organize on campus.
college-writing-018609.zh: 在私立机构，应该有一个明确的流程，让学生可以在校园里组织起来。

college-writing-018610.en: Make all processes for student protest transparent and accessible.
college-writing-018610.zh: 使学生抗议的所有流程透明且可访问。

college-writing-018611.en: At Middlebury College and the University of Southern California, for example, student-demonstration policies are embodied in student handbooks, and a single student or a recognized student club can request event space on campus for a demonstration.
college-writing-018611.zh: 例如，在米德尔伯里学院和南加州大学，学生手册中体现了学生示范政策，单个学生或认可的学生俱乐部可以要求校园内的活动空间进行演示。

college-writing-018612.en: This differs from many private institutions, where demonstrations require a sponsoring department or group, a policy that can discourage and suppress enthusiasm.
college-writing-018612.zh: 这与许多私人机构不同，其中示威需要赞助部门或团体，这是一种可以阻止和抑制热情的政策。

college-writing-018613.en: Conduct a campuswide review of building and school names.
college-writing-018613.zh: 对建筑和学校名称进行校园范围的审查。

college-writing-018614.en: Colleges have existed in America since colonial times.
college-writing-018614.zh: 自殖民时代以来，美国就存在着大学。

college-writing-018615.en: The names on all buildings should be examined for potential links to the country’s dark history of slavery, Jim Crow, and white supremacy.
college-writing-018615.zh: 应检查所有建筑物上的名称，以寻找与该国奴隶制的黑暗历史、吉姆克劳和白人至上的潜在联系。

college-writing-018616.en: Princeton University’s recent announcement that it will remove Woodrow Wilson’s name from its public-policy school is a reminder that reviews should not be limited to Confederate names.
college-writing-018616.zh: 普林斯顿大学最近宣布将从其公共政策学校中删除伍德罗威尔逊的名字，提醒人们，评论不应仅限于同盟名称。

college-writing-018617.en: Colleges are better off using an independent third party to investigate and provide recommendations.
college-writing-018617.zh: 大学最好使用独立的第三方来调查和提供建议。

college-writing-018618.en: It’s not easy to tell a benefactor that his or her money is not welcome at your institution, especially if the benefactor is a trustee or someone else with close ties to the college.
college-writing-018618.zh: 告诉恩人他或她的钱在您的机构不受欢迎是不容易的，特别是如果恩人是受托人或与学院有密切联系的其他人。

college-writing-018619.en: Using a third party makes the decision easier.
college-writing-018619.zh: 使用第三方使决定更容易。

college-writing-018620.zh: 惩罚校园内的种族定性。

college-writing-018621.en: Just as we’ve seen in the larger society, students of color have been forced to engage with campus safety officers or the local police because employees or other students reported them as suspicious.
college-writing-018621.zh: 正如我们在更大的社会中看到的那样，有色人种学生被迫与校园安全官员或当地警察接触，因为员工或其他学生报告他们很可疑。

college-writing-018624.en: Race-based calls to public safety should be an infraction punishable under the rules governing student and employment conduct.
college-writing-018624.zh: 基于种族的公共安全呼吁应根据学生和就业行为的规则受到惩罚。

college-writing-018625.en: Create a strategic plan to hire a diverse faculty and staff.
college-writing-018625.zh: 制定战略计划以聘用多元化的教职员工。

college-writing-018626.en: Recruiting to hire a more diverse work force should not be limited to the equal-employment-opportunity statement in a job ad or an additional statement on the value of diversity.
college-writing-018626.zh: 招聘雇用更多样化的员工队伍不应仅限于求职广告中的平等就业机会声明或关于多样性价值的附加声明。

college-writing-018627.en: Institutions must think creatively about and invest money in hiring and retaining full-time professors and administrators of color.
college-writing-018627.zh: 机构必须创造性地思考和投入资金来雇用和留住有色人种的全职教授和管理人员。

college-writing-018628.en: Administrators should ask themselves the following: Have we developed a faculty pipeline to recruit, hire, retain, and tenure full-time faculty of color?
college-writing-018628.zh: 管理员应该问自己以下问题：我们是否开发了一条教师管道来招聘、聘用、保留和终身有色人种教师？

college-writing-018629.en: Does campus leadership resemble the student body?
college-writing-018629.zh: 校园领导像学生群体吗？

college-writing-018630.en: How diverse is our faculty-tenure committee?
college-writing-018630.zh: 我们的教师任期委员会有多多样化？

college-writing-018631.en: Should the chief diversity officer be a standing member of the tenure committee?
college-writing-018631.zh: 首席多元化官应该是任期委员会的常任成员吗？

college-writing-018632.en: How often are professional-development opportunities given to administrators of color compared with their white counterparts?
college-writing-018632.zh: 与白人同行相比，有色人种管理员的专业发展机会多久给予一次？

college-writing-018634.en: After a disturbing national or local event, leaders often urge students by email to take advantage of the college’s health and wellness services.
college-writing-018634.zh: 在令人不安的国家或地方活动结束后，领导者经常通过电子邮件敦促学生利用学院的健康和保健服务。

college-writing-018635.en: But how diverse is that staff at your institution?
college-writing-018635.zh: 但是，您所在机构的员工有多多样化？

college-writing-018636.en: If your college is like most, the answer is “not very.”
college-writing-018636.zh: 如果你的大学是最像的，答案是“不是很”。

college-writing-018637.en: For too long, we have asked minority students to enter a health and wellness space staffed by professionals who do not resemble them.
college-writing-018637.zh: 长期以来，我们一直要求少数族裔学生进入一个由与他们不同的专业人士组成的健康和保健空间。

college-writing-018638.en: Hire diverse psychologists, physicians, nurses, social workers, and nutritionists on your campus.
college-writing-018638.zh: 在您的校园内聘请不同的心理学家、医生、护士、社会工作者和营养师。

college-writing-018639.en: Expand the scope of your chief diversity officer.
college-writing-018639.zh: 扩大您的首席多元化官的范围。

college-writing-018640.en: If your campus does not have a chief diversity officer, now is a good time to hire one.
college-writing-018640.zh: 如果您的校园没有首席多元化官，那么现在是聘请一位的好时机。

college-writing-018641.en: If your campus already has one, take a closer look at the role.
college-writing-018641.zh: 如果你的校园已经有了，请仔细看看这个角色。

college-writing-018643.en: Is there an office dedicated to the work of inclusion?
college-writing-018643.zh: 是否有专门从事包容性工作的办公室？

college-writing-018644.en: Will the officer’s work also encompass faculty development?
college-writing-018644.zh: 军官的工作还包括教师发展吗？

college-writing-018647.en: Speak often about race, privilege, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
college-writing-018647.zh: 经常谈论种族、特权、多样性、公平和包容。

college-writing-018648.en: The model and philosophy of proactive advising should not be limited to academic advising.
college-writing-018648.zh: 主动咨询的模式和哲学不应仅限于学术咨询。

college-writing-018649.en: It can be applied across campus.
