college-writing-018785.zh: 690 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-018786.en: Today is your first day on campus.
college-writing-018786.zh: 今天是你在校园的第一天。

college-writing-018787.en: You were a high school senior three months ago.
college-writing-018787.zh: 三个月前，你是一名高中生。

college-writing-018788.en: Or maybe you’ve been at home with your children for the last ten years.
college-writing-018788.zh: 或者，也许你在过去的十年里一直和你的孩子在家。

college-writing-018789.en: Or maybe you work full time and you’re coming to school to start the process that leads to a better job.
college-writing-018789.zh: 或者，也许你全职工作，你来学校开始这个过程，从而带来更好的工作。

college-writing-018790.en: Whatever your background is, you’re probably not too concerned today with staying in college.
college-writing-018790.zh: 不管你的背景是什么，你今天可能不太关心留在大学里。

college-writing-018791.en: After all, you just got over the hurdle (and the paperwork) of applying to this place and organizing your life so that you could attend.
college-writing-018791.zh: 毕竟，你刚刚克服了申请这个地方并组织你的生活以便你可以参加的障碍（和文书工作）。

college-writing-018792.en: And today, you’re confused and tired.
college-writing-018792.zh: 而今天，你感到困惑和疲倦。

college-writing-018793.en: Everything is a hassle, from finding the classrooms to standing in line at the bookstore.
college-writing-018793.zh: 一切都很麻烦，从找到教室到在书店排队。

college-writing-018794.zh: 但无论如何，请阅读我的建议。

college-writing-018795.en: And if you don’t read it today, clip and save this article.
college-writing-018795.zh: 如果您今天不阅读它，请剪辑并保存这篇文章。

college-writing-018796.en: You might want to look at it a little further down the road.
college-writing-018796.zh: 你可能想再往下看一点。

college-writing-018797.en: By the way, if this isn’t your very first day, don’t skip this article.
college-writing-018797.zh: 顺便说一句，如果这不是您的第一天，请不要跳过这篇文章。

college-writing-018798.en: Maybe you haven’t been doing as well in your studies as you’d hoped.
college-writing-018798.zh: 也许你在学习中的表现没有你希望的那么好。

college-writing-018799.en: Or perhaps you’ve had problems juggling your work schedule, your class schedule, and your social life.
college-writing-018799.zh: 或者，您可能在兼顾您的工作时间表、您的课程表和社交生活方面遇到了问题。

college-writing-018800.zh: 如果是这样，请继续阅读。

college-writing-018801.en: You’re about to get the inside story on making it in college.
college-writing-018801.zh: 你即将了解在大学里取得成功的内幕。

college-writing-018802.en: On the basis of my own experience as a final-year student, and after dozens of interviews with successful students, I’ve worked out a no-fail system for coping with college.
college-writing-018802.zh: 根据我自己作为最后一年学生的经验，在对成功的学生进行了数十次采访后，我制定了一个应对大学的无失败系统。

college-writing-018803.en: These are the inside tips every student needs to do well in school.
college-writing-018803.zh: 这些是每个学生在学校取得好成绩所需的内部技巧。

college-writing-018804.en: I’ve put myself in your place, and I’m going to answer the questions that will cross (or have already crossed) your mind during your stay here.
college-writing-018804.zh: 我已经把自己放在了你的位置上，我将回答你在这里逗留期间会跨过（或已经跨越）你的想法的问题。

college-writing-018805.en: The author of this selection presents a compact guide to being a successful student.
college-writing-018805.zh: 本次选拔的作者为成功的学生提供了一份紧凑的指南。

college-writing-018806.en: He will show you how to pass tests, how to avoid becoming a student zombie, how to find time to fit in everything you want to do, and how to deal with personal problems while keeping up with your studies.
college-writing-018806.zh: 他将向您展示如何通过考试，如何避免成为学生僵尸，如何找到时间适应您想做的一切，以及如何在跟上学习的同时处理个人问题。

college-writing-018807.en: These and other helpful tips have been culled from the author’s own experience and his candid interviews with fellow students.
college-writing-018807.zh: 这些和其他有用的提示是从作者自己的经验和他对同学的坦率采访中挑选出来的。

college-writing-018808.en: How to Make It in College, Now That You’re Here
college-writing-018808.zh: 如何在大学里成功，既然你在这里

college-writing-018812.en: What’s the Secret of Getting Good Grades?
college-writing-018812.zh: 取得好成绩的秘诀是什么？

college-writing-018813.en: It all comes down to getting those grades, doesn’t it?
college-writing-018813.zh: 这一切都归结为获得这些成绩，不是吗？

college-writing-018814.en: After all, you came here for some reason, and you’re going to need passing grades to get the credits or degree you want.
college-writing-018814.zh: 毕竟，您出于某种原因来到这里，您需要及格成绩才能获得您想要的学分或学位。

college-writing-018815.en: Many of us never did much studying in high school; most of the learning we did took place in the classroom.
college-writing-018815.zh: 我们中的许多人在高中时从未做过太多的学习。 我们所做的大部分学习都是在课堂上进行的。

college-writing-018816.en: College, however, is a lot different.
college-writing-018816.zh: 然而，大学有很大的不同。

college-writing-018817.en: You’re really on your own when it comes to passing courses.
college-writing-018817.zh: 当谈到通过课程时，你真的是靠自己的。

college-writing-018818.en: In fact, sometimes you’ll feel as if nobody cares if you make it or not.
college-writing-018818.zh: 事实上，有时你会觉得没有人在乎你是否成功。

college-writing-018819.en: Therefore, you’ve got to figure out a study system that gets results.
college-writing-018819.zh: 因此，您必须找出一个获得结果的研究系统。

college-writing-018820.en: Sooner or later, you’ll be alone with those books.
college-writing-018820.zh: 迟早，你会独自阅读这些书。

college-writing-018821.en: After that, you’ll be sitting in a classroom with an exam sheet on your desk.
college-writing-018821.zh: 之后，您将坐在教室里，桌子上放着一张考试表。

college-writing-018822.en: Whether you stare at that exam with a queasy stomach or whip through it fairly confidently depends on your study techniques.
college-writing-018822.zh: 无论您是用恶心的胃或相当自信地通过它来盯着考试，都取决于您的学习技巧。

college-writing-018823.en: Most of the successful students I talked to agreed that the following eight study tips deliver solid results.
college-writing-018823.zh: 我与之交谈的大多数成功学生都同意以下八个学习技巧提供了可靠的结果。

college-writing-018825.en: Those students you see “studying” in the cafeteria or game room aren’t learning much.
college-writing-018825.zh: 你看到的那些在自助餐厅或游戏室“学习”的学生并没有学到太多东西。

college-writing-018826.en: You just can’t learn when you’re distracted by people and noise.
college-writing-018826.zh: 当你被人和噪音分心时，你无法学习。

college-writing-018827.en: Even the library can be a bad place to study if you constantly find yourself watching the clouds outside or the students walking through the stacks.
college-writing-018827.zh: 如果您经常发现自己在看外面的云或穿过堆栈的学生，即使是图书馆也可能是一个不好的学习场所。

college-writing-018828.en: It takes guts to sit, alone, in a quiet place in order to study.
college-writing-018828.zh: 为了学习，独自坐在一个安静的地方需要勇气。

college-writing-018829.en: But you have to do it.

college-writing-018830.en: Find a room at home or a spot in the library that’s relatively quiet─and boring.
college-writing-018830.zh: 在家中找一个房间或图书馆的一个相对安静和无聊的地方。

college-writing-018831.en: When you sit there, you won’t have much to do except study.
college-writing-018831.zh: 当你坐在那里时，除了学习之外，你没有什么可做的。

college-writing-018832.en: 2. Get into a Study Frame of Mind.

college-writing-018833.en: When you sit down, do it with the attitude that you’re going to get this studying done.
college-writing-018833.zh: 当你坐下时，以你将完成这项研究的态度来做这件事。

college-writing-018834.en: You’re not going to doodle in your notebook or make a list for the supermarket.
college-writing-018834.zh: 你不会在你的笔记本上涂鸦，也不会为超市列出清单。

college-writing-018835.en: Decide that you are going to study and learn now, so that you can move on to more interesting things as soon as possible.
college-writing-018835.zh: 决定你现在要学习和学习，这样你就可以尽快转向更有趣的事情。

college-writing-018837.en: If you sweat out a block of study time, and do a good job on it, treat yourself.
college-writing-018837.zh: 如果你在学习时间中出汗并做好工作，请善待自己。

college-writing-018839.en: You can “psych” yourself up for studying by promising to reward yourself afterward.
college-writing-018839.zh: 您可以通过承诺之后奖励自己来“心理”自己学习。

college-writing-018840.en: A present for yourself can be anything from a favorite TV show to a relaxing bath to a dish of double chocolate ice cream.
college-writing-018840.zh: 送给自己的礼物可以是任何东西，从最喜欢的电视节目到放松的浴缸，再到一盘双巧克力冰淇淋。

college-writing-018842.en: Lots of students sit down with an assignment like “Read chapter five, pages 125–150” and do just that.
college-writing-018842.zh: 许多学生坐下来完成诸如“阅读第五章，第 125-150 页”之类的作业，然后就这样做了。

college-writing-018843.en: They turn to page 125 and start to read.
college-writing-018843.zh: 他们翻到第 125 页并开始阅读。

college-writing-018844.en: After a while, they find that they have no idea what they just read.
college-writing-018844.zh: 过了一会儿，他们发现他们不知道他们刚刚读了什么。

college-writing-018845.en: For the last ten minutes, they’ve been thinking about their five-year-old or what they’re going to eat for dinner.
college-writing-018845.zh: 在过去的十分钟里，他们一直在想着他们五岁的孩子，或者他们晚餐要吃什么。

college-writing-018846.en: Eventually, they plod through all the pages but don’t remember much afterward.
college-writing-018846.zh: 最终，他们浏览了所有的页面，但后来不太记得了。

college-writing-018847.en: In order to prevent this problem, skim the textbook chapter first.
college-writing-018847.zh: 为了防止这个问题，先浏览教科书章节。

college-writing-018848.en: This means: look at the title, the subtitles, the headings, the pictures, the first and last paragraphs.
college-writing-018848.zh: 这意味着：查看标题、字幕、标题、图片、第一段和最后一段。

college-writing-018849.en: Try to find out what the person who wrote the book had in mind when he or she organized the chapter.
college-writing-018849.zh: 试着找出写这本书的人在组织本章时的想法。

college-writing-018850.en: What was important enough to set off as a title or in bold type?
college-writing-018850.zh: 什么是作为标题或粗体类型的重要到足以启动？

college-writing-018851.en: After skimming, you should be able to explain to yourself what the main points of the chapter are.
college-writing-018851.zh: 略读后，您应该能够向自己解释本章的要点是什么。

college-writing-018852.en: Unless you’re the kind of person who would step into an empty elevator shaft without looking first, you’ll soon discover the value of skimming.
college-writing-018852.zh: 除非你是那种不先看就踏入空电梯井的人，否则你很快就会发现掠夺的价值。

college-writing-018853.zh: 692 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-018854.en: 5. Take Notes on What You’re Studying.
college-writing-018854.zh: 5. 记下你正在学习的内容。

college-writing-018855.en: This sounds like a hassle, but it works.
college-writing-018855.zh: 这听起来很麻烦，但它确实有效。

college-writing-018856.en: Go back over the material after you’ve read it, and jot down key words and phrases in the margins.
college-writing-018856.zh: 阅读完材料后，请回顾一下，并在页边空白中记下关键词和短语。

college-writing-018857.en: When you review the chapter for a test, you’ll have handy little things like “definition of rationalization” or “example of assimilation” in the margins.
college-writing-018857.zh: 当您查看本章进行测试时，您会在页边空白处有一些方便的小东西，例如“合理化的定义”或“同化的例子”。

college-writing-018858.en: If the material is especially tough, organize a separate sheet of notes.
college-writing-018858.zh: 如果材料特别坚韧，请单独组织一张纸条。

college-writing-018859.en: Write down definitions, examples, lists, and main ideas.
college-writing-018859.zh: 写下定义、示例、列表和主要想法。

college-writing-018860.en: The idea is to have a single sheet that boils the entire chapter down to a digestible lump.
college-writing-018860.zh: 这个想法是有一张纸，可以将整个章节归结为一个可消化的肿块。

college-writing-018861.en: 6. Review After You’ve Read and Taken Notes.

college-writing-018862.en: Some people swear that talking to yourself works.
college-writing-018862.zh: 有些人发誓，自言自语是有效的。

college-writing-018863.en: Tell yourself about the most important points in the chapter.
college-writing-018863.zh: 告诉自己本章中最重要的要点。

college-writing-018864.en: Once you’ve said them out loud, they seem to stick better in your mind.
college-writing-018864.zh: 一旦你大声说出来，它们似乎会更好地在你的脑海中粘住。

college-writing-018865.en: If you can’t talk to yourself about the material after reading it, that’s a sure sign you don’t really know it.
college-writing-018865.zh: 如果您在阅读后无法自言自语，那肯定是您并不真正了解的迹象。

college-writing-018867.en: This may sound contradictory, but give up when you’ve had enough.
college-writing-018867.zh: 这听起来可能是矛盾的，但是当你受够了就放弃了。

college-writing-018868.en: You should try to make it through at least an hour, though.
college-writing-018868.zh: 不过，您应该尝试至少度过一个小时。

college-writing-018869.en: Ten minutes here and there are useless.
college-writing-018869.zh: 这里和那里十分钟都是无用的。

college-writing-018870.en: When your head starts to pound and your eyes develop spidery red lines, quit.
college-writing-018870.zh: 当你的头开始怦怦直跳，你的眼睛长出蜘蛛般的红线时，退出。

college-writing-018871.en: You won’t do much learning when you’re exhausted.
college-writing-018871.zh: 当你筋疲力尽时，你不会做太多的学习。

college-writing-018872.en: 8. Take a College Skills Course If You Need It.
college-writing-018872.zh: 8. 如果需要，参加大学技能课程。

college-writing-018873.en: Don’t hesitate or feel embarrassed about enrolling in a study skills course.
college-writing-018873.zh: 不要犹豫或对参加学习技能课程感到尴尬。

college-writing-018874.en: Many students say they wouldn’t have made it without one.
college-writing-018874.zh: 许多学生说没有一个就不会成功。

college-writing-018875.en: How Can I Keep Up with All My Responsibilities without Going Crazy?
college-writing-018875.zh: 我怎样才能在不发疯的情况下跟上我所有的责任？

college-writing-018879.en: You’ve got a husband, wife, boyfriend, girlfriend, child.
college-writing-018879.zh: 你有一个丈夫、妻子、男朋友、女朋友、孩子。

college-writing-018881.en: How are you possibly going to cover all the bases in your life and maintain your sanity?
college-writing-018881.zh: 你将如何覆盖你生活中的所有基础并保持你的理智？

college-writing-018882.en: This is one of the toughest problems students face.
college-writing-018882.zh: 这是学生面临的最棘手的问题之一。

college-writing-018883.en: Even if they start the semester with the best of intentions, they eventually find themselves tearing their hair out trying to do everything they’re supposed to do.
college-writing-018883.zh: 即使他们以最好的意图开始这个学期，他们最终还是发现自己在努力做他们应该做的一切。

college-writing-018884.en: Believe it or not, though, it is possible to meet all your responsibilities.
college-writing-018884.zh: 不管你信不信，有可能履行你的所有责任。

college-writing-018885.en: And you don’t have to turn into a hermit or give up your loved ones to do it.
college-writing-018885.zh: 而且你不必变成隐士或放弃你所爱的人去做。

college-writing-018886.en: The secret here is to organize your time.
college-writing-018886.zh: 这里的秘诀是组织你的时间。

college-writing-018887.en: But don’t just sit around half the semester planning to get everything together soon.
college-writing-018887.zh: 但不要只坐大约一半的学期，计划尽快把所有东西都整理好。

college-writing-018888.en: Before you know it, you’ll be confronted with midterms, papers, family, and work all at once.
college-writing-018888.zh: 在不知不觉中，您将同时面临期中、论文、家庭和工作。

college-writing-018889.en: Don’t let yourself reach that breaking point.
college-writing-018889.zh: 不要让自己达到那个临界点。

college-writing-018892.en: Get one of those calendars with big blocks around the dates.
college-writing-018892.zh: 获取日期周围有大块的这些日历之一。

college-writing-018893.en: Give yourself an overview of the whole term by marking down the due dates for papers and projects.
college-writing-018893.zh: 通过标记论文和项目的截止日期来概述整个学期。

college-writing-018895.en: This way those days don’t sneak up on you unexpectedly.
college-writing-018895.zh: 这样，那些日子不会意外地偷偷靠近你。

college-writing-018897.en: Sit down during the first few days of this semester and make up a sheet listing the days and hours of the week.
college-writing-018897.zh: 在本学期的前几天坐下来，编制一张清单，列出一周中的天数和时间。

college-writing-018898.en: Fill in your work and class hours first.
college-writing-018898.zh: 首先填写您的工作和上课时间。

college-writing-018899.en: Then try to block out some study hours.
college-writing-018899.zh: 然后尝试阻止一些学习时间。

college-writing-018900.en: It’s better to study a little every day

college-writing-018902.en: than to create a huge once-or-twice-a-week marathon session.
college-writing-018902.zh: 而不是创建一个每周一次或两次的大型马拉松赛。

college-writing-018903.en: Schedule study hours for your hardest classes for the times when you feel most energetic.
college-writing-018903.zh: 为您最难的课程安排学习时间，让您在感到最有活力的时候。

college-writing-018904.en: For example, I battled my tax law textbook in the mornings; when I looked at it after 7:00 p.m., I might as well have been reading Chinese.
college-writing-018904.zh: 例如，我在早上与我的税法教科书作斗争； 当我在晚上 7:00 之后看它时，我还不如一直在读中文。

college-writing-018905.en: The usual proportion, by the way, is one hour of study time for every class hour.
college-writing-018905.zh: 顺便说一句，通常的比例是每节课一小时的学习时间。

college-writing-018906.en: In case you’re one of those people who get carried away, remember to leave blocks of free time, too.
college-writing-018906.zh: 如果您是那些被冲昏头脑的人之一，请记住留下空闲时间。

college-writing-018907.en: You won’t be any good to yourself or anyone else if you don’t relax and pack in the studying once in a while.
college-writing-018907.zh: 如果你不放松并偶尔打包学习，你对自己或其他任何人都不会有任何好处。

college-writing-018909.en: This is the secret that, more than any other, got me through college.
college-writing-018909.zh: 这是一个秘密，比其他任何人都更能让我读完大学。

college-writing-018910.en: Once a week (or every day if you want to), write a list of what you have to do.
college-writing-018910.zh: 每周一次（或者如果你愿意的话每天），写下你必须做的事情的清单。

college-writing-018911.en: Write down everything from “write English paper” to “buy cold cuts for lunch.”
college-writing-018911.zh: 写下从“写英文纸”到“买冷盘作为午餐”的所有内容。

college-writing-018912.en: The best thing about a “to do” list is that it seems to tame all those stray “I have to” thoughts that nag at your mind.
college-writing-018912.zh: 关于“做”清单的最好的事情是，它似乎驯服了所有那些困扰着你的流浪“我必须”的想法。

college-writing-018913.en: Just making the list seems to make the tasks “doable.”
college-writing-018913.zh: 仅仅列出列表似乎使任务“可行”。

college-writing-018914.en: After you finish something on the list, cross it off.
college-writing-018914.zh: 完成列表中的某些内容后，将其划掉。

college-writing-018915.en: Don’t be compulsive about finishing everything; you’re not Superman or Wonder Woman.
college-writing-018915.zh: 不要强迫完成所有事情； 你不是超人或神奇女侠。

college-writing-018916.en: Get the important things done first.

college-writing-018917.en: The secondary things you don’t finish can simply be moved to your next “to do” list.
college-writing-018917.zh: 您没有完成的次要事情可以简单地移至您的下一个“待办事项”列表。

college-writing-018918.en: What Can I Do If Personal Problems Get in the Way of My Studies?
college-writing-018918.zh: 如果个人问题妨碍了我的学习，我该怎么办？

college-writing-018919.en: One student, Roger, told me this story:
college-writing-018919.zh: 一位学生罗杰告诉我这个故事：

college-writing-018920.en: Everything was going OK for me until the middle of the spring semester.
college-writing-018920.zh: 直到春季学期中期，我的一切都很好。

college-writing-018921.en: I went through a terrible time when I broke up with my girlfriend and started seeing her best friend.
college-writing-018921.zh: 当我和女朋友分手并开始见到她最好的朋友时，我经历了一段糟糕的时光。

college-writing-018922.en: I was trying to deal with my ex-girlfriend’s hurt and anger, my new girlfriend’s guilt, and my own worries and anxieties at the same time.
college-writing-018922.zh: 我试图处理前女友的伤害和愤怒，我的新女友的内疚，以及我自己的担忧和焦虑。

college-writing-018923.en: In addition to this, my mother was sick and on a medication that made her really irritable.
college-writing-018923.zh: 除此之外，我妈妈病了，服用的药物让她非常烦躁。

college-writing-018924.en: I hated to go home because the atmosphere was so uncomfortable.
college-writing-018924.zh: 我讨厌回家，因为气氛太不舒服了。

college-writing-018925.en: Soon, I started missing classes because I couldn’t deal with the academic pressures as well as my own personal problems.
college-writing-018925.zh: 很快，我开始缺课，因为我无法处理学术压力以及我自己的个人问题。

college-writing-018926.en: It seemed easier to hang around my girlfriend’s apartment than to face all my problems at home and at school.
college-writing-018926.zh: 在我女朋友的公寓里闲逛似乎比在家里和学校里面对我所有的问题都容易。

college-writing-018927.zh: 另一名学生玛丽安告诉我：

college-writing-018928.en: I’d been married for eight years and the relationship wasn’t going too well.
college-writing-018928.zh: 我结婚八年了，这段关系不太顺利。

college-writing-018929.en: I saw the handwriting on the wall, and I decided to prepare for the future.
college-writing-018929.zh: 我看到墙上的字迹，我决定为未来做准备。

college-writing-018930.en: I enrolled in college, because I knew I’d need a decent job to support myself.
college-writing-018930.zh: 我上大学了，因为我知道我需要一份体面的工作来养活自己。

college-writing-018931.en: Well, my husband had a fit because I was going to school.
college-writing-018931.zh: 好吧，我丈夫很适合，因为我要去上学。

college-writing-018932.en: We were arguing a lot anyway, and he made it almost impossible for me to study at home.
college-writing-018932.zh: 无论如何，我们争论了很多，他让我几乎不可能在家学习。

college-writing-018933.en: I think he was angry and almost jealous because I was drawing away from him.
college-writing-018933.zh: 我认为他很生气，几乎嫉妒，因为我正在远离他。

college-writing-018934.en: It got so bad that I thought about quitting college for a while.
college-writing-018934.zh: 它变得如此糟糕，以至于我想了一段时间就退学了。

college-writing-018935.en: I wasn’t getting any support at home, and it was just too hard to go on.
college-writing-018935.zh: 我在家里没有得到任何支持，而且太难继续了。

college-writing-018936.zh: 694 第 5 部分 作家读物

college-writing-018937.en: Personal troubles like these are overwhelming when you’re going through them.
college-writing-018937.zh: 当您经历这些问题时，像这样的个人麻烦是压倒性的。

college-writing-018938.en: School seems like the least important thing in your life.
college-writing-018938.zh: 学校似乎是你生命中最不重要的事情。

college-writing-018939.en: The two students above are perfect examples of this.
college-writing-018939.zh: 上面的两个学生就是这方面的完美例子。

college-writing-018940.en: But if you think about it, quitting or failing school would be the worst thing for these two students.
college-writing-018940.zh: 但如果你想一想，退学或失败对这两个学生来说将是最糟糕的事情。

college-writing-018941.en: Roger’s problems, at least with his girlfriends, would simmer down eventually, and then he’d regret having left school.
college-writing-018941.zh: 罗杰的问题，至少和他的女朋友在一起，最终会慢慢低落，然后他会后悔离开学校。

college-writing-018942.en: Marian had to finish college if she wanted to be able to live independently.
college-writing-018942.zh: 如果玛丽安想要能够独立生活，她必须完成大学学业。

college-writing-018943.en: Sometimes, you’ve just got to hang tough.
college-writing-018943.zh: 有时，你只需要坚持下去。

college-writing-018944.en: But what do you do while you’re trying to live through a lousy time?
college-writing-018944.zh: 但是当你试图度过一个糟糕的时期时，你会做什么？

college-writing-018945.en: First of all, do something difficult.
college-writing-018945.zh: 首先，做一些困难的事情。

college-writing-018946.en: Ask yourself, honestly, if you’re exaggerating small problems as an excuse to avoid classes and studying.
college-writing-018946.zh: 老实说，问问自己，如果你夸大小问题作为避免上课和学习的借口。

college-writing-018947.en: It takes strength to admit this, but there’s no sense in kidding yourself.
college-writing-018947.zh: 承认这一点需要力量，但自欺欺人是没有意义的。

college-writing-018948.en: If your problems are serious, and real, try to make some human contacts at school.
college-writing-018948.zh: 如果您的问题很严重且真实，请尝试在学校进行一些人际交往。

college-writing-018949.en: Lots of students hide inside a miserable shell made of their own troubles and feel isolated and lonely.
college-writing-018949.zh: 许多学生躲在一个悲惨的外壳里，他们自己的麻烦和感到孤立和孤独。

college-writing-018950.en: Believe me, there are plenty of students with problems.
college-writing-018950.zh: 相信我，有很多学生有问题。

college-writing-018951.en: Not everyone is getting A’s and having a fabulous social and home life at the same time.
college-writing-018951.zh: 不是每个人都获得了 A 并同时拥有美妙的社交和家庭生活。

college-writing-018952.en: As you go through the term, you’ll pick up some vibrations about the students in your classes.
college-writing-018952.zh: 在你读完这个学期时，你会在课堂上学到一些关于学生的振动。

college-writing-018953.en: Perhaps someone strikes you as a compatible person.
college-writing-018953.zh: 也许有人认为你是一个兼容的人。

college-writing-018954.en: Why not speak to that person after class?
college-writing-018954.zh: 为什么不在课后和那个人说话？

college-writing-018955.en: Share a cup of coffee in the cafeteria or walk to the parking lot together.
college-writing-018955.zh: 在自助餐厅分享一杯咖啡或一起步行到停车场。

college-writing-018956.en: You’re not looking for a best friend or the love of your life.
college-writing-018956.zh: 你不是在寻找最好的朋友或你生命中的挚爱。

college-writing-018957.en: You just want to build a little network of support for yourself.
college-writing-018957.zh: 你只是想为自己建立一个小支持网络。

college-writing-018958.en: Sharing your difficulties, questions, and complaints with a friendly person on campus can make a world of difference in how you feel.
college-writing-018958.zh: 与校园内友好的人分享您的困难、问题和抱怨可以让您的感受与世界有很大不同。

college-writing-018959.en: Finally, if your problems are overwhelming, get some professional help.
college-writing-018959.zh: 最后，如果您的问题是压倒性的，请寻求专业帮助。

college-writing-018960.en: Why do you think colleges spend countless dollars on counseling departments and campus psychiatric services?
college-writing-018960.zh: 为什么你认为大学在咨询部门和校园精神病服务上花费无数美元？

college-writing-018961.en: More than ever, students all over the country are taking advantage of the help offered by support groups and therapy sessions.
college-writing-018961.zh: 比以往任何时候，全国各地的学生都在利用支持小组和治疗课程提供的帮助。

college-writing-018962.en: There’s no shame attached to asking for help, either; in fact, almost 40 percent of college students (according to one survey) will use counseling services during their time in school.
college-writing-018962.zh: 寻求帮助也没有什么可耻的。 事实上，近 40% 的大学生（根据一项调查）会在学校期间使用咨询服务。

college-writing-018963.en: Just walk into a student center or counseling office and ask for an appointment.
college-writing-018963.zh: 只需走进学生中心或咨询办公室并预约。

college-writing-018964.en: You wouldn’t think twice about asking a dentist to help you get rid of your toothache.
college-writing-018964.zh: 您不会三思而后行地要求牙医帮助您摆脱牙痛。

college-writing-018965.en: Counselors are paid─and want─to help you with your problems.
college-writing-018965.zh: 辅导员有报酬——并希望——帮助您解决问题。

college-writing-018966.en: Why Do Some People Make It and Some Drop Out?
college-writing-018966.zh: 为什么有些人会成功，有些人会退出？

college-writing-018967.en: Anyone who spends at least one semester in college notices that some students give up on their classes.
college-writing-018967.zh: 任何至少在大学度过一个学期的人都会注意到有些学生放弃了他们的课程。

college-writing-018968.en: The person who sits behind you in accounting, for example, begins to miss a lot of class meetings and eventually vanishes.
college-writing-018968.zh: 例如，在你身后坐在你身后的人开始错过很多班级会议并最终消失。

college-writing-018969.en: Or another student comes to class without the assignment, doodles in a notebook during the lecture, and leaves during the break.
college-writing-018969.zh: 或者另一个学生没有作业来上课，在讲座期间在笔记本上涂鸦，在休息时离开。

college-writing-018970.en: What’s the difference between students like this and the ones who succeed in school?
college-writing-018970.zh: 像这样的学生和那些在学校取得成功的学生有什么区别？

college-writing-018971.en: My survey may be nonscientific, but everyone I asked said the same thing: attitude.
college-writing-018971.zh: 我的调查可能是不科学的，但我问的每个人都说同样的话：态度。

college-writing-018972.en: A positive attitude is the key to everything else─good study habits, smart time scheduling, and coping with personal difficulties.
college-writing-018972.zh: 积极的态度是其他一切的关键——良好的学习习惯、聪明的时间安排和应对个人困难。

college-writing-018975.en: Well, for one thing, it means avoiding the zombie syndrome.
college-writing-018975.zh: 好吧，一方面，这意味着避免僵尸综合症。

college-writing-018976.en: It means not only showing up for your classes, but also doing something while you’re there.
college-writing-018976.zh: 这意味着不仅出现在您的课程中，而且还意味着您在那里的时候做一些事情。

college-writing-018979.en: Ask a question if you want to.

college-writing-018980.en: Don’t just walk into a class, put your mind in neutral, and drift away to never-never land.
college-writing-018980.zh: 不要只是走进一个班级，把你的思想放在中立的地方，然后飘到永远不会降落的地方。

college-writing-018981.en: Having a positive attitude goes deeper than this, though.
college-writing-018981.zh: 不过，积极的态度比这更深。

college-writing-018982.en: It means being mature about college as an institution.
college-writing-018982.zh: 这意味着关于大学作为一所机构的成熟。

college-writing-018983.en: Too many students approach college classes like six-year-olds who expect first grade to be as much fun as Sesame Street.
college-writing-018983.zh: 太多的学生像六岁的孩子一样接近大学课程，他们希望一年级和芝麻街一样有趣。

college-writing-018984.en: First grade, as we all know, isn’t as much fun as Sesame Street.
college-writing-018984.zh: 众所周知，一年级没有芝麻街那么有趣。

college-writing-018985.en: And college classes can sometimes be downright dull.
college-writing-018985.zh: 大学课程有时可能是彻头彻尾的乏味。

college-writing-018986.en: If you let a boring class discourage you so much that you want to leave school, you’ll lose in the long run.
college-writing-018986.zh: 如果你让一个无聊的课程让你如此沮丧，以至于你想离开学校，从长远来看，你会输。

college-writing-018988.en: You want a degree, or a certificate, or a career.
college-writing-018988.zh: 您想要学位、证书或职业。

college-writing-018989.en: If you have to, you can make it through a less-than-interesting class in order to achieve what you want.
college-writing-018989.zh: 如果你必须这样做，你可以通过一个不那么有趣的课程来实现你想要的。

college-writing-018990.en: Get whatever you can out of every class.
college-writing-018990.zh: 从每节课中得到你能得到的任何东西。

college-writing-018991.en: But if you simply can’t stand a certain class, be determined to fulfill its requirements and be done with it once and for all.
college-writing-018991.zh: 但是，如果您根本无法忍受某个阶级，请决心满足其要求并一劳永逸地完成它。

college-writing-018992.en: After the initial high of starting school, you have to settle in for the long haul.
college-writing-018992.zh: 在开始上学的最初高点之后，您必须长期安顿下来。

college-writing-018993.en: If you follow the advice here, you’ll be prepared to face the academic crunch.
college-writing-018993.zh: 如果您遵循此处的建议，您将准备好面对学术紧缩。

college-writing-018994.en: You’ll also live through the semester without giving up your family, your job, or Monday Night Football.
college-writing-018994.zh: 您还可以在不放弃家人、工作或周一晚上足球的情况下度过整个学期。

college-writing-018995.en: Finally, going to college can be an exciting time.
college-writing-018995.zh: 最后，上大学可能是一个激动人心的时刻。

college-writing-018997.en: And when you learn things, the world becomes a more interesting place.
college-writing-018997.zh: 当你学习东西时，世界变得更有趣。

college-writing-018999.en: 1. The word queasy in “with a queasy stomach” (paragraph 3) means
college-writing-018999.zh: 1.“胃不舒服”中的“恶心”一词（第 3 段）是指

college-writing-019004.en: 2. The word tactics in “try these three tactics” (paragraph 14) means
college-writing-019004.zh: 2. “试用这三种策略”中的“战术”一词（第 14 段）是指

college-writing-019009.en: 3. Which of the following would be a good alternative title for this selection?
college-writing-019009.zh: 3. 以下哪一项是此选择的一个很好的替代标题？

college-writing-019010.en: a. Your First Day on Campus
college-writing-019010.zh: 一。 您在校园的第一天

college-writing-019012.en: c. How to Budget Your Time
college-writing-019012.zh: c.  如何预算你的时间

college-writing-019013.en: d. The Benefits of College Skills Courses
college-writing-019013.zh: D. 大学技能课程的好处

college-writing-019014.zh: 696 第 5 部分 作家读物

college-writing-019015.en: 4. Which sentence expresses the main idea of the selection?
college-writing-019015.zh: 4. 哪个句子表达了选择的主要思想？

college-writing-019016.en: a. In high school, most of us did little homework.
college-writing-019016.zh: 一。 在高中时，我们大多数人都很少做功课。

college-writing-019017.en: b. You should give yourself rewards for studying well.
college-writing-019017.zh: B. 你应该给自己奖励学习的回报。

college-writing-019018.en: c. Sometimes personal problems interfere with studying.
college-writing-019018.zh: c.  有时个人问题会干扰学习。

college-writing-019019.en: d. You can succeed in college by following certain guidelines.
college-writing-019019.zh: D. 您可以通过遵循某些准则在大学取得成功。

college-writing-019020.en: 5. According to the author, “making it” in college means
college-writing-019020.zh: 5.根据作者的说法，在大学里“做”是指

college-writing-019021.en: a. studying whenever you have any free time.
college-writing-019021.zh: 一。 只要有空闲时间就可以学习。

college-writing-019022.en: b. getting a degree by barely passing your courses.
college-writing-019022.zh: B. 勉强通过你的课程获得学位。

college-writing-019023.en: c. quitting school until you solve your personal problems.
college-writing-019023.zh: c.  退学，直到你解决你的个人问题。

college-writing-019024.en: d. getting good grades without making your life miserable.
college-writing-019024.zh: D. 在不让你的生活变得悲惨的情况下取得好成绩。

college-writing-019025.en: 6. If your personal problems seem overwhelming, you should
college-writing-019025.zh: 6.如果你的个人问题看起来压倒性的，你应该

college-writing-019026.en: a. drop out for a while.

college-writing-019027.zh: B. 把它们夸大给老师。

college-writing-019029.en: d. get help from a professional.
college-writing-019029.zh: D. 向专业人士寻求帮助。

college-writing-019030.en: 7. Which of the following is not described by the author as a means of time control?
college-writing-019030.zh: 7. 以下哪一项没有被作者描述为时间控制的手段？

college-writing-019035.en: 8. We can infer that the writer of this essay
college-writing-019035.zh: 8.我们可以推断这篇文章的作者

college-writing-019036.en: a. cares about college students and their success.
college-writing-019036.zh: 一。 关心大学生和他们的成功。

college-writing-019040.en: 9. From the selection we can conclude that
college-writing-019040.zh: 9. 从选择中我们可以得出结论

college-writing-019041.en: a. college textbooks are very expensive.
college-writing-019041.zh: 一。 大学教科书非常昂贵。

college-writing-019042.en: b. it is a good practice to write notes in your textbook.
college-writing-019042.zh: B. 在教科书中写笔记是一个很好的做法。

college-writing-019043.en: c. taking notes on your reading takes too much time.
college-writing-019043.zh: c.  为您的阅读做笔记需要太多时间。

college-writing-019044.en: d. a student should never mark up an expensive book.
college-writing-019044.zh: D. 学生永远不应该标记一本昂贵的书。

college-writing-019046.en: a. fewer people than before are attending college.
college-writing-019046.zh: 一。 上大学的人比以前少了。

college-writing-019047.en: b. most college students experience no problems during their first year.
college-writing-019047.zh: B. 大多数大学生在第一年就没有任何问题。

college-writing-019049.en: c. all college students experience overwhelming problems.
college-writing-019049.zh: c.  所有大学生都会遇到压倒性的问题。

college-writing-019050.en: d. coping with college is difficult.

college-writing-019052.en: 1. O’Keeney uses a highly structured format in his essay.
college-writing-019052.zh: 1. O'Keeney 在他的文章中使用了高度结构化的格式。

college-writing-019055.en: Why do you think O’Keeney structured his essay in this way?
college-writing-019055.zh: 为什么你认为奥基尼以这种方式构建他的文章？

college-writing-019056.en: 2. Does the author clearly state his thesis?
college-writing-019056.zh: 2. 作者是否清楚地陈述了他的论文？

college-writing-019057.en: If so, where is it stated, and how?
college-writing-019057.zh: 如果是这样，它在哪里说明，如何说明？

college-writing-019058.en: 3. What method of introduction does the author use in the section on personal
college-writing-019058.zh: 3. 作者在个人部分中使用的介绍方法是什么

college-writing-019060.en: What is the value of using this method?
college-writing-019060.zh: 使用这种方法有什么价值？

college-writing-019061.en: 4. In his essay, O’Keeney addresses his audience in the second person─using
college-writing-019061.zh: 4. 在他的文章中，奥基尼用第二人称向他的听众讲话——

college-writing-019063.en: How does such a technique advance his main point?
college-writing-019063.zh: 这样的技术如何提升他的主要观点？

college-writing-019065.en: 1. What, according to O’Keeney, is the secret of getting good grades?
college-writing-019065.zh: 1. 根据奥基尼的说法，取得好成绩的秘诀是什么？

college-writing-019067.en: used any of O’Keeney’s study methods?
college-writing-019067.zh: 使用奥基尼的任何研究方法？

college-writing-019068.en: If so, how useful do you think they have been for you?
college-writing-019068.zh: 如果是这样，您认为它们对您有多大用处？

college-writing-019069.en: Are there any that you haven’t used but might try?
college-writing-019069.zh: 有没有你没有使用过但可以尝试的？

college-writing-019071.en: 2. What does O’Keeney recommend students do to manage their time and
college-writing-019071.zh: 2. 奥基尼建议学生如何管理他们的时间和

college-writing-019073.en: Which of these suggestions are you most likely to use?
college-writing-019073.zh: 您最有可能使用以下哪些建议？

college-writing-019074.en: Which are you least likely to use?

college-writing-019076.en: 3. What is the secret the author says got him through college?
college-writing-019076.zh: 3. 作者说的秘密是什么让他上大学？

college-writing-019078.en: think is the most helpful or important suggestion the author makes in the selection?
college-writing-019078.zh: 认为作者在选择中提出的最有帮助或最重要的建议是什么？

college-writing-019080.en: 4. Do you agree with the author that Roger and Marian should stay in school?
college-writing-019080.zh: 4. 你同意作者罗杰和玛丽安应该留在学校的观点吗？

college-writing-019081.en: Are there any situations in which it would be better for students to quit school or leave, at least temporarily?
college-writing-019081.zh: 有没有什么情况下，学生最好是辍学或离开，至少是暂时的？

college-writing-019082.en: Explain, giving examples to support your answer.
college-writing-019082.zh: 解释，举例来支持你的答案。

college-writing-019085.en: Write an essay similar to the one you’ve just read that explains how to succeed in some other field─for example, a job, a sport, marriage, child rearing.
college-writing-019085.zh: 写一篇类似于你刚刚读过的文章，解释了如何在其他领域取得成功——例如，一份工作、一项运动、婚姻、抚养孩子。

college-writing-019086.en: First, brainstorm three or four problem areas a newcomer to this experience might encounter.
college-writing-019086.zh: 首先，集思广益，新来者可能会遇到的三个或四个问题领域。

college-writing-019087.en: Then, under each area you have listed, jot down some helpful hints and techniques
college-writing-019087.zh: 然后，在您列出的每个区域下，记下一些有用的提示和技巧

college-writing-019091.en: For example, a paper on “How to Succeed as a Restaurant Server” might describe the following problem areas:
college-writing-019091.zh: 例如，一篇关于“如何作为餐厅服务器成功”的论文可能会描述以下问题领域：

college-writing-019092.en: developing a good memory learning to do tasks quickly coping with troublesome customers
college-writing-019092.zh: 培养良好的记忆力 学习快速应对麻烦的客户

college-writing-019093.en: Each supporting paragraph in this paper would discuss specific techniques for dealing with these problems.
college-writing-019093.zh: 本文中的每个支持段落都将讨论处理这些问题的具体技术。

college-writing-019094.en: Be sure that the advice you give is detailed and specific enough to really help a person in such a situation.
college-writing-019094.zh: 确保您提供的建议足够详细和具体，以真正帮助处于这种情况的人。

college-writing-019095.en: You may find it helpful to look over the essays in Chapter 11.
college-writing-019095.zh: 您可能会发现查看第 11 章中的文章很有帮助。

college-writing-019097.en: Write a letter to Roger or Marian, giving advice on how to deal with the personal problem mentioned in the article.
college-writing-019097.zh: 写信给罗杰或玛丽安，就如何处理文章中提到的个人问题提供建议。

college-writing-019098.zh: 您可能会推荐以下内容：

college-writing-019099.zh: 在学校建立其他联系人。

college-writing-019102.en: (Where? What should this person be told?)
college-writing-019102.zh: （在哪里？应该告诉这个人什么？）

college-writing-019103.en: Realize that the problem is not so serious.
college-writing-019103.zh: 意识到问题并没有那么严重。

college-writing-019105.en: In your introductory paragraph, explain why you are writing the letter.
college-writing-019105.zh: 在你的介绍性段落中，解释你写这封信的原因。

college-writing-019106.en: Include a thesis statement that says what plan of action you are recommending.
college-writing-019106.zh: 包括一个 中心论点句，说明您推荐的行动计划。

college-writing-019107.en: Then, in the rest of the paper, explain the plan of action in detail.
college-writing-019107.zh: 然后，在论文的其余部分，详细解释行动计划。

college-writing-019109.en: Write an essay contrasting college as you thought it would be with college as it is.
college-writing-019109.zh: 写一篇对比大学的论文，因为你认为它会像大学一样。

college-writing-019110.en: You can organize the essay by focusing on three specific things that are different from what you expected.
college-writing-019110.zh: 您可以通过关注与您预期不同的三个特定事物来组织论文。

college-writing-019111.en: Or you can cover three areas of difference.
college-writing-019111.zh: 或者你可以覆盖三个不同的领域。

college-writing-019112.en: For instance, you may decide to contrast your expectations about (1) a college dorm room, (2) your roommate, and (3) dining-hall food with reality.
college-writing-019112.zh: 例如，您可能决定将您对（1）大学宿舍、（2）室友和（3）食堂食品与现实的期望进行对比。

college-writing-019113.en: Or you could contrast your expectations about (1) fellow students, (2) college professors, and (3) college courses with reality.
college-writing-019113.zh: 或者，您可以将您对（1）同学、（2）大学教授和（3）大学课程的期望与现实进行对比。

college-writing-019114.en: Refer to the section in Chapter 13 on methods of developing comparison or contrast essays to review point-by-point and one-side-at-a-time development.
college-writing-019114.zh: 请参阅第 13 章中关于开发比较或对比论文的方法以逐点和一次一侧开发的方法的部分。

college-writing-019115.en: Be sure to make an outline of your essay before you begin to write.
college-writing-019115.zh: 在开始写作之前，请务必对您的论文进行大纲。

college-writing-019117.en: A former teacher of mine, Robert A. Fowkes of New York University, likes to tell the story of a class he took in Old Welsh while studying in Germany during the 1930s.
college-writing-019117.zh: 我的前任老师，纽约大学的罗伯特·A·福克斯 (Robert A. Fowkes)，喜欢讲述他在 1930 年代在德国学习时在老威尔士上课的故事。

college-writing-019118.en: On the first day the professor strode up to the podium, shuffled his notes, coughed, and began, “Guten Tag, Meinen Damen und Herren” (“Good day, ladies and gentlemen”).
college-writing-019118.zh: 第一天，教授走上讲台，洗了他的笔记，咳嗽了一声，然后开始说：“Guten tag, Meinen damen und Herren”（“晚安，女士们，先生们”）。

college-writing-019119.zh: 福克斯不安地环顾四周。

college-writing-019120.en: He was the only student in the course.
college-writing-019120.zh: 他是该课程中唯一的学生。

college-writing-019121.en: Toward the middle of the semester, Fowkes fell ill and missed a class.
college-writing-019121.zh: 到了学期的中期，福克斯病倒了，错过了一节课。

college-writing-019122.en: When he returned, the professor nodded vaguely and, to Fowkes’s astonishment, began to deliver not the next lecture in the sequence but the one after.
college-writing-019122.zh: 当他回来时，教授含糊地点点头，令福克斯惊讶的是，他开始讲授的不是下一个讲座，而是之后的讲座。

college-writing-019123.en: Had he, in fact, lectured to an empty hall in the absence of his solitary student?
college-writing-019123.zh: 事实上，他是否在他孤独的学生不在的情况下在一个空荡荡的大厅里讲课？

college-writing-019124.zh: 福克斯认为这是完全可能的。

college-writing-019125.en: Today, American colleges and universities (originally modeled on German ones) are under strong attack from many quarters.
college-writing-019125.zh: 今天，美国学院和大学（最初以德国大学为蓝本）正受到许多方面的强烈攻击。

college-writing-019126.en: Teachers, it is charged, are not doing a good job of teaching, and students are not doing a good job of learning.
college-writing-019126.zh: 老师们，是收费的，教学做得不好，学生也做得不好。

college-writing-019127.en: American businesses and industries suffer from unenterprising, uncreative executives educated not to think for themselves but to mouth outdated truisms1 the rest of the world has long discarded.
college-writing-019127.zh: 美国的企业和行业遭受着缺乏进取心的、没有创造力的高管，他们被教育不为自己思考，而是说出过时的老生常谈 1 世界其他地方早已被抛弃。

college-writing-019128.en: College graduates lack both basic skills and general
college-writing-019128.zh: 大学毕业生缺乏基本技能和一般技能

college-writing-019129.en: College students are doodling in their notebooks or gazing off into space as their instructor lectures for fifty minutes.
college-writing-019129.zh: 大学生在他们的笔记本上涂鸦或凝视着他们的导师讲座五十分钟。

college-writing-019130.en: What is wrong with this picture?

college-writing-019131.en: Many would say that what is wrong is the students.
college-writing-019131.zh: 许多人会说，问题是学生。

college-writing-019132.en: However, the educator and author David Daniels would say that the lecture itself is the problem.
college-writing-019132.zh: 然而，教育家和作家大卫丹尼尔斯会说讲座本身就是问题所在。

college-writing-019133.en: As you read this article, see if you agree with Daniels’s analysis of lectures and their place in a college education.
college-writing-019133.zh: 在阅读本文时，看看您是否同意丹尼尔斯对讲座的分析及其在大学教育中的地位。

college-writing-019143.en: Studies are conducted and reports are issued on the status of higher education, but any changes that result either are largely cosmetic or make a bad situation worse.
college-writing-019143.zh: 对高等教育状况进行了研究，并发布了有关高等教育状况的报告，但任何结果要么在很大程度上是化妆品，要么使糟糕的情况变得更糟。

college-writing-019144.en: One aspect of American education too seldom challenged is the lecture system.
college-writing-019144.zh: 美国教育中很少受到挑战的一个方面是讲座系统。

college-writing-019145.en: Professors continue to lecture and students to take notes much as they did in the thirteenth century, when books were so scarce and expensive that few students could own them.
college-writing-019145.zh: 教授们继续讲课，学生们像在 13 世纪那样做笔记，当时书籍如此稀缺且昂贵，以至于很少有学生能够拥有它们。

college-writing-019146.en: The time is long overdue for us to abandon the lecture system and turn to methods that really work.
college-writing-019146.zh: 我们放弃讲座系统并转向真正有效的方法的时间早就应该了。

college-writing-019147.en: To understand the inadequacy of the present system, it is enough to follow a single imaginary first-year student─let’s call her Mary─through a term of lectures on, say, introductory psychology (although any other subject would do as well).
college-writing-019147.zh: 要了解当前系统的不足，足以跟随一个想象中的一年级学生——让我们称她为玛丽——通过一个关于介绍性心理学的讲座（尽管任何其他学科也可以）。

college-writing-019148.en: She arrives on the first day and looks around the huge lecture hall, taken a little aback to see how large the class is.
college-writing-019148.zh: 她第一天到了，环顾了巨大的演讲厅，有点吃惊地看看班级有多大。

college-writing-019149.en: Once the hundred or more students enrolled in the course discover that the professor never takes attendance (how can he?─calling the roll would take far too much time), the class shrinks to a less imposing size.
college-writing-019149.zh: 一旦参加该课程的数百名或更多学生发现教授从不参加（他怎么会打电话？

college-writing-019150.en: Some days Mary sits in the front row, from where she can watch the professor read from a stack of yellowed notes that seem nearly as old as he is.
college-writing-019150.zh: 有时候，玛丽坐在前排，在那里她可以看到教授从一堆看似年老的泛黄笔记中读到。

college-writing-019151.en: She is bored by the lectures, and so are most of the other students, to judge by the way they are nodding off or doodling in their notebooks.
college-writing-019151.zh: 她对讲座感到厌烦，其他大多数学生也是如此，以他们在笔记本上打瞌睡或涂鸦的方式来判断。

college-writing-019152.en: Gradually she realizes the professor is as bored as his audience.
college-writing-019152.zh: 渐渐地，她意识到教授和他的听众一样无聊。

college-writing-019153.en: At the end of each lecture he asks, “Are there any questions?” in a tone of voice that makes it plain he would much rather there weren’t.
college-writing-019153.zh: 在每一次讲座结束时，他都会问：“有什么问题吗？” 用一种说清楚的语气，他宁愿没有。

college-writing-019154.en: He needn’t worry─the students are as relieved as he is that the class is over.
college-writing-019154.zh: 他不用担心——学生们和他一样松了一口气，因为课堂结束了。

college-writing-019155.en: Mary knows very well she should read an assignment before every lecture.
college-writing-019155.zh: 玛丽很清楚她应该在每次讲座前阅读作业。

college-writing-019156.en: However, as the professor gives no quizzes and asks no questions, she soon realizes she needn’t prepare.
college-writing-019156.zh: 然而，由于教授不做任何测验，也没有问任何问题，她很快意识到她不需要做准备。

college-writing-019157.en: At the end of the term she catches up by skimming her notes and memorizing a list of facts and dates.
college-writing-019157.zh: 在学期结束时，她通过浏览她的笔记和记住一系列事实和日期来赶上。

college-writing-019158.en: After the final exam, she promptly forgets much of what she has memorized.
college-writing-019158.zh: 期末考试后，她立即忘记了她所记忆的大部分内容。

college-writing-019159.en: Some of her fellow students, disappointed at the impersonality of it all, drop out of college altogether.
college-writing-019159.zh: 她的一些同学对这一切的非人格感到失望，完全辍学了。

college-writing-019160.en: Others, like Mary, stick it out, grow resigned to the system and await better days when, as juniors and seniors, they will attend smaller classes and at last get the kind of personal attention real learning requires.
college-writing-019160.zh: 其他人，比如玛丽，坚持下去，逐渐屈服于系统，等待更好的日子，作为大三和老年人，他们将参加较小的课程，并最终获得真正的学习所需的个人关注。

college-writing-019161.en: I admit this picture is overdrawn─most universities supplement lecture courses with discussion groups, usually led by graduate students; and some classes, such as first-year English, are always relatively small.
college-writing-019161.zh: 我承认这张照片透支了——大多数大学用讨论组补充讲座课程，通常由研究生领导； 有些课程，例如一年级英语，总是相对较小。

college-writing-019162.en: Nevertheless, far too many courses rely principally or entirely on lectures, an arrangement much loved by faculty and administrators but scarcely designed to benefit the students.
college-writing-019162.zh: 然而，太多的课程主要或完全依赖于讲座，这种安排深受教师和管理人员的喜爱，但几乎没有旨在使学生受益。

college-writing-019163.en: One problem with lectures is that listening intelligently is hard work.
college-writing-019163.zh: 讲座的问题之一是智能聆听是一项艰苦的工作。

college-writing-019164.en: Reading the same material in a textbook is a more efficient way to learn because students can proceed as slowly as they need to until the subject matter becomes clear to them.
college-writing-019164.zh: 在教科书中阅读相同的材料是一种更有效的学习方式，因为学生可以根据需要慢慢进行，直到主题变得清晰为止。

college-writing-019165.en: Even simply paying attention is very difficult; people can listen at a rate of four hundred to six hundred words a minute, while the most impassioned2 professor talks at scarcely a third of that speed.
college-writing-019165.zh: 即使只是简单地注意也是非常困难的； 人们可以以每分钟四百到六百个字的速度聆听，而最热情的2教授以几乎不到三分之一的速度说话。

college-writing-019169.en: This time lag between speech and comprehension leads to daydreaming.
college-writing-019169.zh: 言语和理解之间的时间滞后导致了白日梦。

college-writing-019170.en: Many students believe years of watching television have sabotaged their attention span, but their real problem is that listening attentively is much harder than they think.
college-writing-019170.zh: 许多学生认为，多年看电视已经破坏了他们的注意力，但他们真正的问题是，专心聆听比他们想象的要难得多。

college-writing-019171.en: Worse still, attending lectures is passive learning, at least for inexperienced listeners.
college-writing-019171.zh: 更糟糕的是，参加讲座是被动学习，至少对于没有经验的听众来说是这样。

college-writing-019172.en: Active learning, in which students write essays or perform experiments and then have their work evaluated by an instructor, is far more beneficial for those who have not yet fully learned how to learn.
college-writing-019172.zh: 主动学习，学生写论文或进行实验，然后让教师对他们的工作进行评估，对尚未完全学习如何学习的人更有益。

college-writing-019173.en: While it’s true that techniques of active listening, such as trying to anticipate the speaker’s next point or taking notes selectively, can enhance the value of a lecture, few students possess such skills at the beginning of their college careers.
college-writing-019173.zh: 虽然积极倾听的技术，例如试图预测演讲者的下一个观点或有选择地做笔记，可以提高讲座的价值，但很少有学生在大学生涯的开始就拥有这种技能。

college-writing-019174.en: More commonly, students try to write everything down and even bring tape recorders to class in a clumsy effort to capture every word.
college-writing-019174.zh: 更常见的是，学生们试图把所有的东西都写下来，甚至把录音机带到课堂上，笨拙地捕捉每一个字。

college-writing-019175.en: Students need to question their professors and to have their ideas taken seriously.
college-writing-019175.zh: 学生需要质疑他们的教授，并认真对待他们的想法。

college-writing-019176.en: Only then will they develop the analytical skills required to think intelligently and creatively.
college-writing-019176.zh: 只有这样，他们才会培养智能和创造性思考所需的分析技能。

college-writing-019177.en: Most students learn best by engaging in frequent and even heated debate, not by scribbling down a professor’s often unsatisfactory summary of complicated issues.
college-writing-019177.zh: 大多数学生通过频繁甚至激烈的辩论来学习最好，而不是写下教授对复杂问题的经常不满意的总结。

college-writing-019178.en: They need small discussion classes that demand the common labors of teacher and students rather than classes in which one person, however learned, propounds his or her own ideas.
college-writing-019178.zh: 他们需要小型讨论班，这些课程需要教师和学生的共同劳动，而不是一个人在其中提出自己的想法的课程。

college-writing-019179.en: The lecture system ultimately harms professors as well.
college-writing-019179.zh: 讲座系统最终也会伤害教授。

college-writing-019180.en: It reduces feedback to a minimum, so that the lecturer can neither judge how well students understand the material nor benefit from their questions or comments.
college-writing-019180.zh: 它将反馈减少到最低限度，因此讲师既不能判断学生对材料的理解程度，也不能从他们的问题或评论中受益。

college-writing-019181.en: Questions that require the speaker to clarify obscure points and comments that challenge sloppily constructed arguments are indispensable to scholarship.
college-writing-019181.zh: 需要演讲者澄清晦涩难懂的观点和挑战那些草率构建的论点的评论对于学术来说是必不可少的。

college-writing-019182.en: Without them, the liveliest mind can atrophy.
college-writing-019182.zh: 没有他们，最活泼的头脑可能会萎缩。

college-writing-019183.en: Undergraduates may not be able to make telling contributions very often, but lecturing insulates a professor even from the beginner’s naive question that could have triggered a fruitful line of thought.
college-writing-019183.zh: 本科生可能无法经常做出有说服力的贡献，但讲课即使是初学者的天真问题，也可能引发了一个富有成效的思路。

college-writing-019184.en: If lectures make so little sense, why have they been allowed to continue?
college-writing-019184.zh: 如果讲座没有意义，为什么允许他们继续？

college-writing-019186.en: They can cram far more students into a lecture hall than into a discussion class, and for many administrators that is almost the end of the story.
college-writing-019186.zh: 他们可以将更多的学生塞进演讲厅而不是讨论课，对于许多管理人员来说，这几乎是故事的结尾。

college-writing-019187.en: But the truth is that faculty members, and even students, conspire with them to keep the lecture system alive and well.
college-writing-019187.zh: 但事实是，教职员工，甚至学生都与他们密谋，以保持讲座系统的活力和良好状态。

college-writing-019188.en: Lectures are easier on everyone than debates.
college-writing-019188.zh: 每个人的讲座都比辩论更容易。

college-writing-019189.en: Professors can pretend to teach by lecturing just as students can pretend to learn by attending lectures, with no one the wiser, including the participants.
college-writing-019189.zh: 教授可以假装讲课，就像学生可以通过参加讲座假装学习一样，没有一个更聪明的人，包括参与者。

college-writing-019190.en: Moreover, if lectures afford some students an opportunity to sit back and let the professor run the show, they offer some professors an irresistible forum for showing off.
college-writing-019190.zh: 此外，如果讲座让一些学生有机会坐下来让教授主持节目，他们会为一些教授提供一个令人无法抗拒的炫耀论坛。

college-writing-019191.en: In a classroom where everyone contributes, students are less able to hide and professors less tempted to engage in intellectual exhibitionism.
college-writing-019191.zh: 在每个人都做出贡献的课堂上，学生无法隐藏，而教授则不太愿意从事智力暴露狂。

college-writing-019192.en: Smaller classes in which students are required to involve themselves in discussion put an end to students’ passivity.
college-writing-019192.zh: 要求学生参与讨论的较小课程结束了学生的被动性。

college-writing-019193.en: Students become actively involved when forced to question their own ideas as well as their instructor’s.
college-writing-019193.zh: 当被迫质疑自己的想法以及他们的老师的想法时，学生会变得积极参与。

college-writing-019194.en: Their listening skills improve dramatically in the excitement of intellectual give-and-take with their instructors and
college-writing-019194.zh: 他们的听力技巧在与教师的智力让步和学习的兴奋中显着提高

college-writing-019197.en: Such interchanges help professors do their job better because they allow them to discover who knows what─before final exams, not after.
college-writing-019197.zh: 这种互换可以帮助教授更好地完成工作，因为它们可以让他们发现谁知道什么——在期末考试之前，而不是之后。

college-writing-019198.en: When exams are given in this type of course, they can require analysis and synthesis from the students, not empty memorization.
college-writing-019198.zh: 当在这类课程中进行考试时，它们可能需要学生的分析和综合，而不是空记忆。

college-writing-019199.en: Classes like this require energy, imagination, and commitment from professors, all of which can be exhausting.
college-writing-019199.zh: 像这样的课程需要教授的精力、想象力和承诺，所有这些都可能会让人筋疲力尽。

college-writing-019200.en: But they compel students to share responsibility for their own intellectual growth.
college-writing-019200.zh: 但他们迫使学生分担自己的智力成长责任。

college-writing-019201.en: Lectures will never entirely disappear from the university scene both because they seem to be economically necessary and because they spring from a long tradition in a setting that values tradition for its own sake.
college-writing-019201.zh: 讲座永远不会完全从大学场景中消失，因为它们似乎在经济上是必要的，而且因为它们源于一个长久的传统，在一个重视传统的环境中。

college-writing-019202.en: But the lectures too frequently come at the wrong end of the students’ educational careers─during the first two years, when they most need close, even individual, instruction.
college-writing-019202.zh: 但讲座过于频繁地出现在学生教育生涯的错误一端——在前两年，当他们最需要亲密的教学时，甚至是个人的教学。

college-writing-019203.en: If lecture classes were restricted to junior and senior undergraduates and to graduate students, who are less in need of scholarly nurturing and more able to prepare work on their own, they would be far less destructive of students’ interests and enthusiasms than the present system.
college-writing-019203.zh: 如果讲座课程仅限于初中和高年级本科生以及研究生，他们不太需要学术培育，更有能力自己准备工作，那么他们对学生的兴趣和热情的破坏性远低于目前的制度。

college-writing-019204.en: After all, students must learn to listen before they can listen to learn.
college-writing-019204.zh: 毕竟，学生必须先学会听才能听。

college-writing-019206.en: 1. The word enhance in “techniques of active listening . . . can enhance the value
college-writing-019206.zh: 1.“积极倾听技术”中的“增强”一词可以增强价值

college-writing-019212.en: 2. The word atrophy in “Without [questions and comments], the liveliest mind
college-writing-019212.zh: 2.“没有[问题和评论]，最活泼的头脑中的萎缩”一词

college-writing-019213.zh: 可以萎缩”（第 12 段）是指

college-writing-019218.en: 3. Which of the following would be a good alternative title for this selection?
college-writing-019218.zh: 3. 以下哪一项是此选择的一个很好的替代标题？

college-writing-019219.en: a. How to Benefit from Lecture Classes
college-writing-019219.zh: 一。 如何从讲座课程中受益

college-writing-019220.en: b. The Necessity of Classroom Lecturing
college-writing-019220.zh: B. 课堂讲课的必要性

college-writing-019222.en: d. College Lectures: An Inspirational Tradition
college-writing-019222.zh: D. 大学讲座：鼓舞人心的传统

college-writing-019224.en: 4. Which sentence best expresses the main idea of the selection?
college-writing-019224.zh: 4. 哪句话最能表达选择的主要思想？

college-writing-019225.en: a. American colleges and universities are being attacked from many sides.
college-writing-019225.zh: 一。 美国的学院和大学正受到多方面的攻击。

college-writing-019226.en: b. Colleges and universities should offer interactive, not lecture, classes to
college-writing-019226.zh: B. 学院和大学应提供互动而不是讲座，课程

college-writing-019228.en: c. College graduates lack basic skills and general culture.
college-writing-019228.zh: c.  大学毕业生缺乏基本技能和一般文化。

college-writing-019229.en: d. American colleges and universities are modeled on German ones.

college-writing-019296.en: opportunities for asking questions opportunities for discussions quality of feedback from the instructor

college-writing-019299.en: You will then have the basis for a thesis statement and three supporting topic sentences.
