college-writing-019300.en: An example of a thesis statement for this essay is
college-writing-019300.zh: 这篇文章的中心论点句的一个例子是

college-writing-019301.en: Because of the different approaches to students’ questions, class discussion, and feedback from the instructor in grading papers, I learned a lot more in my first-year English class than in my business lecture class.
college-writing-019301.zh: 由于学生的问题、课堂讨论和教师在评分论文中的反馈方法不同，我在第一年的英语课上学到的东西比在我的商务讲座课上学到的要多得多。

college-writing-019302.en: That thesis statement could be shortened to
college-writing-019302.zh: 中心论点句 可以缩短为

college-writing-019303.en: I learned a lot more in my first-year English class than in my business lecture class.
college-writing-019303.zh: 我在一年级英语课上学到的东西比在商务讲座课上学到的要多得多。

college-writing-019304.en: The three supporting points for this thesis statement are about
college-writing-019304.zh: 本中心论点句的三个支持点是关于

college-writing-019305.en: different approaches to students’ questions, class discussion, and personal feedback on assignments.
college-writing-019305.zh: 学生问题的不同方法、课堂讨论和对作业的个人反馈。

college-writing-019306.en: Change each of the points listed above into a sentence, and you have your three topic sentences.
college-writing-019306.zh: 将上面列出的每个点更改为一个句子，您就有了您的三个 主题句。

college-writing-019307.en: A topic sentence based on the last point above might be “While my English instructor gave me a lot of useful feedback on my assignments, my business instructor put only a grade on papers.”
college-writing-019307.zh: 基于上述最后一点的 主题句 可能是“虽然我的英语教练给了我很多关于我的作业的有用反馈，但我的商务教练只在论文上给出了一个成绩。”

college-writing-019308.en: Use specific details from your experience to develop your supporting paragraphs.
college-writing-019308.zh: 使用您经验中的具体细节来开发您的支持段落。

college-writing-019310.en: In this selection, Daniels has given some disadvantages of lectures.
college-writing-019310.zh: 在这个选择中，丹尼尔斯给出了一些讲座的缺点。

college-writing-019311.en: Write an essay on the advantages of lectures.
college-writing-019311.zh: 写一篇关于讲座优势的文章。

college-writing-019312.en: To support your points, use examples from your personal experience and the experiences of others.
college-writing-019312.zh: 为了支持您的观点，请使用您的个人经验和他人的经验中的示例。

college-writing-019313.en: Begin by jotting down a list of advantages.

college-writing-019314.en: Then choose the advantages you have the most to say about and develop those in your essay.
college-writing-019314.zh: 然后选择你最能说的优势，并在你的论文中发展这些优势。

college-writing-019316.en: Which teachers or instructors have you had who were not in a rut, who conducted classes that made you glad to learn?
college-writing-019316.zh: 你有哪些老师或教师没有陷入困境，他们上课让你很高兴学习？

college-writing-019317.en: Write a description of your idea of a very good teacher or instructor.
college-writing-019317.zh: 写下你对一个非常好的老师或导师的想法的描述。

college-writing-019318.en: Your description may be of someone who actually taught you, or it may be of a fictional person who combines all the traits you have enjoyed (or missed) in your teachers and instructors through the years.
college-writing-019318.zh: 你的描述可能是一个真正教过你的人，或者它可能是一个虚构的人，它结合了你多年来在老师和导师中所享有的所有特征（或错过）。

college-writing-019319.en: Be sure to include plenty of specific examples of classroom activities and their effects on students.
college-writing-019319.zh: 一定要包括大量课堂活动的具体例子及其对学生的影响。

college-writing-019320.en: Here are a few aspects of teaching that you may wish to use in your description:
college-writing-019320.zh: 以下是您可能希望在描述中使用的几个教学方面：

college-writing-019321.en: mastery of subject matter ability to excite students about subject types of activities used
college-writing-019321.zh: 掌握主题 能够激发学生对所用活动的学科类型的能力

college-writing-019323.en: This is an exciting time for our brains.
college-writing-019323.zh: 这对我们的大脑来说是一个激动人心的时刻。

college-writing-019324.en: More and more research is showing that our brains change constantly with learning and experience and that this takes place throughout our lives.
college-writing-019324.zh: 越来越多的研究表明，我们的大脑会随着学习和经验而不断变化，这发生在我们的生活中。

college-writing-019325.en: Does this have implications for students’ motivation and learning?
college-writing-019325.zh: 这对学生的动机和学习有影响吗？

college-writing-019327.en: In my research in collaboration with my graduate students, we have shown that what students believe about their brains─whether they see their intelligence as something that’s fixed or something that can grow and change─has profound effects on their motivation, learning, and school achievement (Dweck, 2006).
college-writing-019327.zh: 在我与研究生合作的研究中，我们已经表明，学生对他们大脑的信仰——无论他们认为自己的智力是固定的还是可以成长和改变的东西——对他们的动机、学习和学校成就有着深远的影响（Dweck，2006）。

college-writing-019328.en: These different beliefs, or mindsets, create different psychological worlds: one in which students are afraid of challenges and devastated by setbacks, and one in which students relish challenges and are resilient in the face of setbacks.
college-writing-019328.zh: 这些不同的信念或心态创造了不同的心理世界：学生害怕挑战和受挫折的破坏，以及学生喜欢挑战并在面对挫折时具有韧性的一种。

college-writing-019330.en: How are the mindsets communicated to students?
college-writing-019330.zh: 心态是如何传达给学生的？

college-writing-019331.en: And, most important, can they be changed?
college-writing-019331.zh: 而且，最重要的是，它们可以改变吗？

college-writing-019332.en: As we answer these questions, you will understand why so many students do not achieve to their potential, why so many bright students stop working when school becomes challenging, and why stereotypes have such profound effects on students’ achievement.
college-writing-019332.zh: 当我们回答这些问题时，您将了解为什么这么多学生没有发挥自己的潜力，为什么有这么多聪明的学生在学校变得具有挑战性时停止工作，以及为什么刻板印象对学生的成绩产生如此深远的影响。

college-writing-019333.en: You will also learn how praise can have a negative effect on students’ mindsets, harming their motivation to learn.
college-writing-019333.zh: 您还将了解表扬如何对学生的心态产生负面影响，从而损害他们的学习动力。

college-writing-019334.en: Carol S. Dweck earned her Ph.D. in Social and Developmental Psychol-
college-writing-019334.zh: Carol S. Dweck 获得了博士学位。 在社会和发展心理

college-writing-019335.en: ogy from Yale University and is the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professor
college-writing-019335.zh: 来自耶鲁大学的 OGY，是刘易斯和弗吉尼亚伊顿教授

college-writing-019336.zh: 斯坦福大学心理学博士。

college-writing-019337.zh: 这篇文章解释了她最近的

college-writing-019344.en: Mindsets and Achievement Many students believe that intelligence is fixed, that each person has a certain amount and that’s that.
college-writing-019344.zh: 心态和成就 许多学生认为智力是固定的，每个人都有一定的数量，就是这样。

college-writing-019345.en: We call this a fixed mindset, and, as you will see, students with this mindset worry about how much of this fixed intelligence they possess.
college-writing-019345.zh: 我们称之为固定心态，正如您将看到的，具有这种心态的学生担心他们拥有多少这种固定的智力。

college-writing-019346.en: A fixed mindset makes challenges threatening for students (because they believe that their fixed ability may not be up to the task) and it makes mistakes and failures demoralizing (because they believe that such setbacks reflect badly on their level of fixed intelligence).
college-writing-019346.zh: 固定的心态使挑战对学生构成威胁（因为他们认为他们的固定能力可能无法胜任），并且会使错误和失败变得士气低落（因为他们认为这种挫折会严重反映他们的固定智力水平）。

college-writing-019347.en: Other students believe that intelligence is something that can be cultivated through effort and education.
college-writing-019347.zh: 其他学生认为智力是可以通过努力和教育培养的东西。

college-writing-019348.en: They don’t necessarily believe that everyone has the same abilities or that anyone can be as smart as Einstein, but they do believe that everyone can improve their abilities.
college-writing-019348.zh: 他们不一定相信每个人都有相同的能力，或者任何人都可以像爱因斯坦一样聪明，但他们确实相信每个人都可以提高自己的能力。

college-writing-019349.en: And they understand that even Einstein wasn’t Einstein until he put in years of focused hard work.
college-writing-019349.zh: 他们明白，即使爱因斯坦也不是爱因斯坦，直到他投入了多年的专注努力。

college-writing-019350.en: In short, students with this growth mindset believe that intelligence is a potential that can be realized through learning.
college-writing-019350.zh: 简而言之，具有这种成长心态的学生相信智力是一种可以通过学习实现的潜力。

college-writing-019351.en: As a result, confronting challenges, profiting from mistakes, and persevering in the face of setbacks become ways of getting smarter.
college-writing-019351.zh: 因此，面对挑战，从错误中获利，在挫折中坚持不懈，成为变得更聪明的方式。

college-writing-019352.en: To understand the different worlds these mindsets create, we followed several hundred students across a difficult school transition─the transition to seventh grade.
college-writing-019352.zh: 为了了解这些心态所创造的不同世界，我们跟随数百名学生经历了艰难的学校过渡——过渡到七年级。

college-writing-019353.en: This is when the academic work often gets much harder, the grading gets stricter, and the school environment gets less personalized with students moving from class to class.
college-writing-019353.zh: 这是学术工作经常变得更加困难的时候，评分变得更严格，学校环境变得越来越个性化，学生从一个班到另一个班级。

college-writing-019354.en: As the students entered seventh grade, we measured their mindsets (along with a number of other things) and then we monitored their grades over the next two years.
college-writing-019354.zh: 当学生进入七年级时，我们测量了他们的心态（以及其他一些事情），然后我们在接下来的两年里监测了他们的成绩。

college-writing-019355.en: The first thing we found was that students with different mindsets cared about different things in school.
college-writing-019355.zh: 我们发现的第一件事是不同心态的学生在学校关心不同的事情。

college-writing-019356.en: Those with a growth mindset were much more interested in learning than in just looking smart in school.
college-writing-019356.zh: 那些有成长心态的人对学习比在学校看起来更聪明更感兴趣。

college-writing-019357.en: This was not the case for students with a fixed mindset.
college-writing-019357.zh: 对于有固定心态的学生来说，情况并非如此。

college-writing-019358.en: In fact, in many of our studies with students from preschool age to college age, we find that students with a fixed mindset care so much about how smart they will appear that they often reject learning opportunities─even ones that are critical to their success (Cimpian, et al., 2007; Hong, et al., 1999; Nussbaum and Dweck, 2008; Mangels, et al., 2006).
college-writing-019358.zh: 事实上，在我们对从学龄前到大学年龄的学生的许多研究中，我们发现具有固定心态的学生非常关心他们的聪明程度，以至于他们经常拒绝学习机会——即使是对他们成功至关重要的学习机会（Cimpian 等人，2007；Hong， 等人，1999；努斯鲍姆和德韦克，2008；曼格尔斯等人，2006）。

college-writing-019359.en: Next, we found that students with the two mindsets had radically different beliefs about effort.
college-writing-019359.zh: 接下来，我们发现有两种心态的学生对努力有截然不同的信念。

college-writing-019360.en: Those with a growth mindset had a very straightforward (and correct) idea of effort─the idea that the harder you work, the more your ability will grow and that even geniuses have had to work hard for their accomplishments.
college-writing-019360.zh: 那些有成长心态的人有一个非常直接（和正确）的努力的想法——你越努力，你的能力就越大，即使是天才们也必须努力为自己的成就而努力工作。

college-writing-019361.en: In contrast, the students with the fixed mindset believed that if you worked hard it meant that you didn’t have ability, and that things would just come naturally to you if you did.
college-writing-019361.zh: 相比之下，有固定心态的学生认为，如果你努力工作，这意味着你没有能力，如果你这样做，事情就会自然而然地发生在你身上。

college-writing-019362.en: This means that every time something is hard for them and requires effort, it’s both a threat and a bind.
college-writing-019362.zh: 这意味着每次事情对他们来说都是困难的并且需要努力时，这既是一种威胁，也是一种束缚。

college-writing-019363.en: If they work hard at it that means that they aren’t good at it, but if they don’t work hard they won’t do well.
college-writing-019363.zh: 如果他们努力工作，这意味着他们不擅长，但如果他们不努力，他们就不会做得很好。

college-writing-019364.en: Clearly, since just about every worthwhile pursuit involves effort over a long period of time, this is a potentially crippling belief, not only in school but also in life.
college-writing-019364.zh: 显然，由于几乎每一个有价值的追求都涉及很长一段时间的努力，这可能是一种可能严重的信念，不仅在学校里，而且在生活中也是如此。

college-writing-019366.en: Students with different mindsets also had very different reactions to setbacks.
college-writing-019366.zh: 不同心态的学生对挫折的反应也非常不同。

college-writing-019367.en: Those with growth mindsets reported that, after a setback in school, they would simply study more or study differently the next time.
college-writing-019367.zh: 那些有成长心态的人报告说，在学校经历了挫折之后，他们只会在下次学习更多或以不同的方式学习。

college-writing-019368.en: But those with fixed mindsets were more likely to say that they would feel dumb, study less the next time, and seriously consider cheating.
college-writing-019368.zh: 但那些有固定心态的人更有可能说他们会感到愚蠢，下次学习少，并认真考虑作弊。

college-writing-019369.en: If you feel dumb─permanently dumb─in an academic area, there is no good way to bounce back and be successful in the future.
college-writing-019369.zh: 如果你在学术领域感到愚蠢——永远愚蠢——没有什么好方法可以反弹并在未来取得成功。

college-writing-019370.en: In a growth mindset, however, you can make a plan of positive action that can remedy a deficiency (Hong, et al., 1999; Nussbaum and Dweck, 2008; Heyman, et al., 1992).
college-writing-019370.zh: 然而，在成长心态中，您可以制定积极行动的计划，以弥补不足（Hong 等人，1999；Nussbaum 和 Dweck，2008；Heyman 等人，1992）。

college-writing-019371.en: Finally, when we looked at the math grades they went on to earn, we found that the students with a growth mindset had pulled ahead.
college-writing-019371.zh: 最后，当我们查看他们继续获得的数学成绩时，我们发现具有成长心态的学生已经领先。

college-writing-019372.en: Although both groups had started seventh grade with equivalent achievement test scores, a growth mindset quickly propelled students ahead of their fixed-mindset peers, and this gap only increased over the two years of the study.
college-writing-019372.zh: 尽管两组都在七年级开始时获得了同等的成绩测试分数，但成长心态迅速推动学生领先于固定心态同龄人，而这种差距在研究的两年内只会增加。

college-writing-019373.en: In short, the belief that intelligence is fixed dampened students’ motivation to learn, made them afraid of effort, and made them want to quit after a setback.
college-writing-019373.zh: 简而言之，智力是固定的信念抑制了学生的学习动力，使他们害怕努力，让他们在挫折后想要退出。

college-writing-019374.en: This is why so many bright students stop working when school becomes hard.
college-writing-019374.zh: 这就是为什么有这么多聪明的学生在学校变得艰难时停止工作的原因。

college-writing-019375.en: Many bright students find grade school easy and coast to success early on.
college-writing-019375.zh: 许多聪明的学生发现小学很容易，而且很早就成功了。

college-writing-019376.en: But later on, when they are challenged, they struggle.
college-writing-019376.zh: 但后来，当他们受到挑战时，他们会挣扎。

college-writing-019377.en: They don’t want to make mistakes and feel dumb─and, most of all, they don’t want to work hard and feel dumb.
college-writing-019377.zh: 他们不想犯错误，感到愚蠢——最重要的是，他们不想努力工作和感到愚蠢。

college-writing-019379.en: It is the belief that intelligence can be developed that opens students to a love of learning, a belief in the power of effort and constructive, determined reactions to setbacks.
college-writing-019379.zh: 人们相信智力可以发展，使学生对学习的热爱、对努力的力量和对挫折的建设性、坚定的反应的信念。

college-writing-019380.en: How Do Students Learn These Mindsets?
college-writing-019380.zh: 学生如何学习这些心态？

college-writing-019381.en: In the 1990s, parents and schools decided that the most important thing for kids to have was self-esteem.
college-writing-019381.zh: 在 1990 年代，家长和学校认为孩子们最重要的事情是自尊。

college-writing-019382.en: If children felt good about themselves, people believed, they would be set for life.
college-writing-019382.zh: 人们相信，如果孩子们对自己感觉良好，他们就会为生活做好准备。

college-writing-019383.en: In some quarters, self-esteem in math seemed to become more important than knowing math, and self-esteem in English seemed to become more important than reading and writing.
college-writing-019383.zh: 在某些方面，数学上的自尊似乎比了解数学更重要，而英语中的自尊似乎变得比阅读和写作更重要。

college-writing-019384.en: But the biggest mistake was the belief that you could simply hand children self-esteem by telling them how smart and talented they are.
college-writing-019384.zh: 但最大的错误是相信你可以通过告诉他们他们有多聪明和有才华来简单地让孩子们自尊。

college-writing-019385.en: Even though this is such an intuitively appealing idea, and even though it was exceedingly well-intentioned, I believe it has had disastrous effects.
college-writing-019385.zh: 尽管这是一个非常吸引人的想法，尽管它的意图非常好，但我相信它产生了灾难性的影响。

college-writing-019386.en: In the 1990s, we took a poll among parents and found that almost 85 percent endorsed the notion that it was necessary to praise their children’s abilities to give them confidence and help them achieve.
college-writing-019386.zh: 在 1990 年代，我们对父母进行了一项民意调查，发现近 85% 的人赞同这样一种观点，即必须赞扬孩子给予他们信心和帮助他们取得成就的能力。

college-writing-019387.en: Their children are now in the workforce and we are told that young workers cannot last through the day without being propped up by praise, rewards, and recognition.
college-writing-019387.zh: 他们的孩子现在在劳动力中，我们被告知，年轻的工人不能在没有得到赞美、奖励和认可的支持下持续一天。

college-writing-019388.en: Coaches are asking me where all the coachable athletes have gone.
college-writing-019388.zh: 教练问我所有可教练的运动员都去了哪里。

college-writing-019389.en: Parents ask me why their children won’t work hard in school.
college-writing-019389.zh: 父母问我为什么他们的孩子不在学校努力工作。

college-writing-019391.en: Could all of this come from well-meant praise?
college-writing-019391.zh: 所有这些都来自善意的赞美吗？

college-writing-019392.en: Well, we were suspicious of the praise movement at the time.
college-writing-019392.zh: 好吧，我们当时对赞美运动持怀疑态度。

college-writing-019393.en: We had already seen in our research that it was the most vulnerable children who were already obsessed with their intelligence and chronically worried about how smart they were.
college-writing-019393.zh: 我们已经在研究中看到，最脆弱的孩子已经沉迷于他们的智力，并长期担心他们有多聪明。

college-writing-019394.en: What if praising intelligence made all children concerned about their intelligence?
college-writing-019394.zh: 如果称赞智慧让所有孩子都担心自己的智力怎么办？

college-writing-019395.en: This kind of praise might tell them that having high intelligence and talent is the most important thing and is what makes you valuable.
college-writing-019395.zh: 这种赞美可能会告诉他们，拥有高智慧和才能是最重要的事情，也是让你有价值的东西。

college-writing-019396.en: It might tell them that intelligence is just something you have and not something you develop.
college-writing-019396.zh: 它可能会告诉他们，智力只是你拥有的东西，而不是你发展的东西。

college-writing-019397.en: It might deny the role of effort and dedication in achievement.
college-writing-019397.zh: 它可能否认努力和奉献在成就中的作用。

college-writing-019398.en: In short, it might promote a fixed mindset with all of its vulnerabilities.
college-writing-019398.zh: 简而言之，它可能会促进一种具有所有脆弱性的固定心态。

college-writing-019399.en: The wonderful thing about research is that you can put questions like this to the test─and we did (Kamins and Dweck, 1999; Mueller and Dweck, 1998).
college-writing-019399.zh: 研究的美妙之处在于，您可以对这样的问题进行测试——我们做到了（Kamins 和 Dweck，1999；Mueller 和 Dweck，1998）。

college-writing-019400.en: We gave two groups of children problems from an IQ test, and we praised them.
college-writing-019400.zh: 我们在智商测试中给了两组儿童问题，我们称赞他们。

college-writing-019401.en: We praised the children in one group for their intelligence, telling them, “Wow, that’s a really good score. You must be smart at this.”
college-writing-019401.zh: 我们赞扬了一组中的孩子们的智慧，告诉他们：“哇，这是一个非常好的分数。你一定很聪明。”

college-writing-019402.en: We praised the children in another group for their effort: “Wow, that’s a really good score. You must have worked really hard.”
college-writing-019402.zh: 我们赞扬了另一组的孩子们的努力：“哇，这真是个好成绩。你一定很努力的。”

college-writing-019403.en: That’s all we did, but the results were dramatic.
college-writing-019403.zh: 这就是我们所做的一切，但结果是戏剧性的。

college-writing-019404.en: We did studies like this with children of different ages and ethnicities from around the country, and the results were the same.
college-writing-019404.zh: 我们对来自全国各地的不同年龄和种族的孩子进行了这样的研究，结果是一样的。

college-writing-019405.en: Here is what happened with fifth graders.
college-writing-019405.zh: 这是五年级学生发生的事情。

college-writing-019406.en: The children praised for their intelligence did not want to learn.
college-writing-019406.zh: 孩子们称赞他们的智慧不想学习。

college-writing-019407.en: When we offered them a challenging task that they could learn from, the majority opted for an easier one, one on which they could avoid making mistakes.
college-writing-019407.zh: 当我们为他们提供一项他们可以学习的具有挑战性的任务时，大多数人选择了一项更简单的任务，他们可以避免犯错误。

college-writing-019408.en: The children praised for their effort wanted the task they could learn from.
college-writing-019408.zh: 孩子们称赞他们的努力想要他们可以学习的任务。

college-writing-019409.en: The children praised for their intelligence lost their confidence as soon as the problems got more difficult.
college-writing-019409.zh: 一旦问题变得更加困难，孩子们的智慧就失去了信心。

college-writing-019410.en: Now, as a group, they thought they weren’t smart.
college-writing-019410.zh: 现在，作为一个群体，他们认为他们并不聪明。

college-writing-019411.en: They also lost their enjoyment, and, as a result, their performance plummeted.
college-writing-019411.zh: 他们也失去了乐趣，因此，他们的表现暴跌。

college-writing-019412.en: On the other hand, those praised for effort maintained their confidence, their motivation, and their performance.
college-writing-019412.zh: 另一方面，那些因努力而受到称赞的人保持了他们的信心、动力和表现。

college-writing-019413.en: Actually, their performance improved over time such that, by the end, they were performing substantially better than the intelligence-praised children on this IQ test.
college-writing-019413.zh: 实际上，它们的性能随着时间的推移而提高，以至于最终，他们在这个智商测试中的表现要好于智力赞美的孩子。

college-writing-019414.en: Finally, the children who were praised for their intelligence lied about their scores more often than the children who were praised for their effort.
college-writing-019414.zh: 最后，那些因智慧而受到称赞的孩子比那些因努力而受到称赞的孩子更常撒谎。

college-writing-019415.en: We asked children to write something (anonymously) about their experience to a child in another school and we left a little space for them to report their scores.
college-writing-019415.zh: 我们要求孩子们（匿名地）写一些关于他们在另一所学校的孩子的经历，我们为他们留了一点空间来报告他们的分数。

college-writing-019416.en: Almost 40 percent of the intelligence-praised children elevated their scores, whereas only 12 or 13 percent of children in the other group did so.
college-writing-019416.zh: 近 40% 的智力评价儿童提高了他们的分数，而另一组中只有 12% 或 13% 的儿童这样做。

college-writing-019417.en: To me this suggests that, after students are praised for their intelligence, it’s too humiliating for them to admit mistakes.
college-writing-019417.zh: 对我来说，这表明，在学生因智慧而受到称赞之后，他们承认错误太丢人了。

college-writing-019418.en: The results were so striking that we repeated the study five times just to be sure, and each time roughly the same things happened.
college-writing-019418.zh: 结果是如此惊人，以至于我们为了确定地重复了五次研究，每次大致相同的事情发生了。

college-writing-019419.en: Intelligence praise, compared to effort (or “process”) praise, put children into a fixed mindset.
college-writing-019419.zh: 智力表扬，比起努力（或“过程”）的赞美，把孩子置于固定的心态中。

college-writing-019422.en: of giving them confidence, it made them fragile, so much so that a brush with difficulty erased their confidence, their enjoyment, and their good performance, and made them ashamed of their work.
college-writing-019422.zh: 给他们信心，这让他们变得脆弱，以至于困难重重的刷子抹去了他们的信心、享受和良好的表现，让他们为自己的工作感到羞耻。

college-writing-019423.en: This can hardly be the self-esteem that parents and educators have been aiming for.
college-writing-019423.zh: 这很难成为父母和教育工作者一直在追求的自尊。

college-writing-019424.en: Often, when children stop working in school, parents deal with this by reassuring their children how smart they are.
college-writing-019424.zh: 通常，当孩子们停止在学校工作时，父母会通过向孩子保证他们有多聪明来处理这个问题。

college-writing-019425.en: We can now see that this simply fans the flames.
college-writing-019425.zh: 我们现在可以看到这只是煽动火焰。

college-writing-019426.en: It confirms the fixed mindset and makes kids all the more certain that they don’t want to try something difficult─something that could lose them their parents’ high regard.
college-writing-019426.zh: 它证实了固定的心态，让孩子们更加确定他们不想尝试一些困难的事情——这可能会失去他们父母的高度重视。

college-writing-019427.en: How should we praise our students?
college-writing-019427.zh: 我们应该如何赞美我们的学生？

college-writing-019428.zh: 我们应该如何让他们放心？

college-writing-019429.en: By focusing them on the process they engaged in─their effort, their strategies, their concentration, their perseverance, or their improvement.
college-writing-019429.zh: 通过将他们专注于他们参与的过程——他们的努力、他们的策略、他们的专注、他们的毅力或他们的进步。

college-writing-019430.en: “You really stuck to that until you got it. That’s wonderful!” “It was a hard project, but you did it one step at a time and it turned out great!”
college-writing-019430.zh: “在你得到它之前，你真的坚持了下来。这太棒了！” “这是一个艰难的项目，但你一次一步就完成了，结果很好！”

college-writing-019431.en: “I like how you chose the tough problems to solve. You’re really going to stretch yourself and learn new things.”
college-writing-019431.zh: “我喜欢你选择解决难题的方式。你真的要伸展自己，学习新事物。”

college-writing-019432.en: “I know that school used to be a snap for you. What a waste that was. Now you really have an opportunity to develop your abilities.”
college-writing-019432.zh: “我知道那所学校曾经对你来说是一件容易的事。那太浪费了。现在你真的有机会发展自己的能力。”

college-writing-019433.en: Brainology Can a growth mindset be taught directly to kids?
college-writing-019433.zh: 大脑学 可以直接向孩子教授成长心态吗？

college-writing-019434.en: If it can be taught, will it enhance their motivation and grades?
college-writing-019434.zh: 如果可以教，它会增强他们的动力和成绩吗？

college-writing-019435.en: We set out to answer this question by creating a growth mindset workshop (Blackwell, et al., 2007).
college-writing-019435.zh: 我们着手创建一个成长心态研讨会来回答这个问题（Blackwell 等人，2007 年）。

college-writing-019436.en: We took seventh graders and divided them into two groups.
college-writing-019436.zh: 我们把七年级的学生分成了两组。

college-writing-019437.en: Both groups got an eight-session workshop full of great study skills, but the “growth mindset group” also got lessons in the growth mindset─what it was and how to apply it to their schoolwork.
college-writing-019437.zh: 两个小组都有一个八节课的研讨会，充满了很好的学习技能，但“成长心态小组”也在成长心态上得到了教训——它是什么以及如何将其应用到他们的学业中。

college-writing-019438.en: Those lessons began with an article called “You Can Grow Your Intelligence: New Research Shows the Brain Can Be Developed Like a Muscle.”
college-writing-019438.zh: 这些教训始于一篇名为“你可以提高你的智力：新的研究表明大脑可以像肌肉一样发展”的文章。

college-writing-019439.en: Students were mesmerized by this article and its message.
college-writing-019439.zh: 学生被这篇文章及其信息迷住了。

college-writing-019440.en: They loved the idea that the growth of their brains was in their hands.
college-writing-019440.zh: 他们喜欢大脑的成长掌握在他们手中的想法。

college-writing-019441.en: This article and the lessons that followed changed the terms of engagement for students.
college-writing-019441.zh: 本文和随后的课程改变了学生的参与条款。

college-writing-019442.en: Many students had seen school as a place where they performed and were judged, but now they understood that they had an active role to play in the development of their minds.
college-writing-019442.zh: 许多学生将学校视为他们表演和评判的地方，但现在他们明白他们在思想的发展中发挥了积极的作用。

college-writing-019443.en: They got to work, and by the end of the semester the growth-mindset group showed a significant increase in their math grades.
college-writing-019443.zh: 他们开始工作，到学期结束时，成长心态小组的数学成绩显着增加。

college-writing-019444.en: The control group─the group that had gotten eight sessions of study skills─showed no improvement and continued to decline.
college-writing-019444.zh: 对照组——获得了八节学习技能的组——没有改善，继续下降。

college-writing-019445.en: Even though they had learned many useful study skills, they did not have the motivation to put them into practice.
college-writing-019445.zh: 尽管他们学到了许多有用的学习技能，但他们没有动力将它们付诸实践。

college-writing-019446.en: The teachers, who didn’t even know there were two different groups, singled out students in the growth-mindset group as showing clear changes in their
college-writing-019446.zh: 那些甚至不知道有两个不同群体的老师们，他们在成长心态组中单独列出了学生，他们的学生表现出明显的变化

college-writing-019449.en: They reported that these students were now far more engaged with their schoolwork and were putting considerably more effort into their classroom learning, homework, and studying.
college-writing-019449.zh: 他们报告说，这些学生现在对他们的学业工作更加投入，并且在课堂学习、家庭作业和学习方面付出了更多的努力。

college-writing-019450.en: Joshua Aronson, Catherine Good, and their colleagues had similar findings (Aronson, Fried, and Good, 2002; Good, Aronson, and Inzlicht, 2003).
college-writing-019450.zh: Joshua Aronson、Catherine Good 和他们的同事也有类似的发现（Aronson、Fried 和 Good，2002；Good、Aronson 和 Inzlicht，2003）。

college-writing-019451.en: Their studies and ours also found that negatively stereotyped students (such as girls in math, or African-American and Hispanic students in math and verbal areas) showed substantial benefits from being in a growth-mindset workshop.
college-writing-019451.zh: 他们和我们的研究还发现，负面刻板印象的学生（例如数学中的女孩，或数学和语言领域的非裔美国人和西班牙裔学生）显示出参加成长心态研讨会的巨大好处。

college-writing-019452.zh: 刻板印象通常是固定心态标签。

college-writing-019453.en: They imply that the trait or ability in question is fixed and that some groups have it and others don’t.
college-writing-019453.zh: 他们暗示所讨论的特征或能力是固定的，有些群体有，而另一些群体则没有。

college-writing-019454.en: Much of the harm that stereotypes do comes from the fixed-mindset message they send.
college-writing-019454.zh: 刻板印象造成的大部分伤害来自他们发送的固定心态信息。

college-writing-019455.en: The growth mindset, while not denying that performance differences might exist, portrays abilities as acquirable and sends a particularly encouraging message to students who have been negatively stereotyped─one that they respond to with renewed motivation and engagement.
college-writing-019455.zh: 成长心态虽然不否认可能存在绩效差异，但将能力描绘为可获取的，并向那些被负面刻板印象的学生传达了一个特别令人鼓舞的信息——他们以新的动力和参与度回应。

college-writing-019456.en: Inspired by these positive findings, we started to think about how we could make a growth mindset workshop more widely available.
college-writing-019456.zh: 受这些积极发现的启发，我们开始思考如何使成长型思维方式更广泛地使用。

college-writing-019457.en: To do this, we have begun to develop a computer-based program called “Brainology.”
college-writing-019457.zh: 为此，我们已经开始开发一个名为“大脑学”的基于计算机的程序。

college-writing-019458.en: In six computer modules, students learn about the brain and how to make it work better.
college-writing-019458.zh: 在六个计算机模块中，学生了解大脑以及如何使其更好地工作。

college-writing-019459.en: They follow two hip teens through their school day, learn how to confront and solve schoolwork problems, and create study plans.
college-writing-019459.zh: 他们跟随两个时髦的青少年上学，学习如何面对和解决学业问题，并制定学习计划。

college-writing-019460.en: They visit a state-of-the-art virtual brain lab, do brain experiments, and find out such things as how the brain changes with learning─how it grows new connections every time students learn something new.
college-writing-019460.zh: 他们参观了一个最先进的虚拟大脑实验室，进行大脑实验，并找出大脑如何随着学习而变化的事情——每次学生学习新事物时，它如何建立新的联系。

college-writing-019461.en: They also learn how to use this idea in their schoolwork by putting their study skills to work to make themselves smarter.
college-writing-019461.zh: 他们还通过将自己的学习技能投入到工作中，让自己变得更聪明，学习如何在学业中使用这个想法。

college-writing-019462.en: We pilot-tested Brainology in twenty New York City schools.
college-writing-019462.zh: 我们在纽约市的 20 所学校进行了试点测试的大脑学。

college-writing-019463.en: Virtually all of the students loved it and reported (anonymously) the ways in which they changed their ideas about learning and changed their learning and study habits.
college-writing-019463.zh: 几乎所有的学生都喜欢它，并（匿名地）报告了他们改变学习观念的方式，改变了他们的学习和学习习惯。

college-writing-019464.en: Here are some things they said in response to the question, “Did you change your mind about anything?”

college-writing-019466.en: Yes . . . I imagine neurons making connections in my brain and I feel like I am learning something.
college-writing-019466.zh: 是的。 。 。 我想象神经元在我的大脑中建立联系，我觉得我正在学习一些东西。

college-writing-019468.en: I always picture them when I’m in school.

college-writing-019469.en: Teachers also reported changes in their students, saying that they had become more active and eager learners: “They offer to practice, study, take notes, or pay attention to ensure that connections will be made.”
college-writing-019469.zh: 老师们还报告了学生的变化，说他们变得更加积极和热心的学习者：“他们提供练习、学习、记笔记或注意确保联系。”

college-writing-019472.en: In our society, we seem to worship talent─and we often portray it as a gift.
college-writing-019472.zh: 在我们的社会中，我们似乎崇拜天赋——我们经常将其描绘成一种礼物。

college-writing-019473.en: Now we can see that this is not motivating to our students.
college-writing-019473.zh: 现在我们可以看到，这对我们的学生没有任何动力。

college-writing-019474.en: Those who think they have this gift expect to sit there with it and be successful.
college-writing-019474.zh: 那些认为他们有这份天赋的人希望与它坐在那里并取得成功。

college-writing-019475.en: When they aren’t successful, they get defensive and demoralized, and often opt out.

college-writing-019477.en: We need to correct the harmful idea that people simply have gifts that transport them to success, and to teach our students that no matter how smart or talented someone is─be it Einstein, Mozart, or Michael Jordan─no one succeeds in a big way without enormous amounts of dedication and effort.
college-writing-019477.zh: 我们需要纠正一个有害的观点，即人们只是拥有将他们带入成功的天赋，并教导我们的学生，无论某人多么聪明或有才华——无论是爱因斯坦、莫扎特还是迈克尔·乔丹——没有人会在没有大量奉献的情况下取得巨大成功和 努力。

college-writing-019478.en: It is through effort that people build their abilities and realize their potential.
college-writing-019478.zh: 正是通过努力，人们才能建立自己的能力并发挥自己的潜力。

college-writing-019479.en: More and more research is showing there is one thing that sets the great successes apart from their equally talented peers─how hard they’ve worked (Ericsson, et al., 2006).

college-writing-019480.en: Next time you’re tempted to praise your students’ intelligence or talent, restrain yourself.
college-writing-019480.zh: 下次你想赞美学生的智力或才能时，要克制自己。

college-writing-019481.en: Instead, teach them how much fun a challenging task is, how interesting and informative errors are, and how great it is to struggle with something and make progress.

college-writing-019482.zh: 最重要的是，告诉他们，通过接受挑战、犯错误和付出努力，他们让自己变得更聪明。

college-writing-019638.zh: “戴夫，停下。停下，好吗？停下，戴夫。你会停下来吗，戴夫？”

college-writing-019639.en: So the supercomputer HAL pleads with the implacable astronaut Dave Bowman in a famous and weirdly poignant scene toward the end of Stanley Kubrick’s 2001: A Space Odyssey.
college-writing-019639.zh: 因此，在斯坦利·库布里克 2001 年的《太空漫游》结束时，超级计算机 HAL 在一个著名且怪异的凄美场景中恳求无能的宇航员戴夫·鲍曼 (Dave Bowman)。

college-writing-019640.en: Bowman, having nearly been sent to a deep-space death by the malfunctioning machine, is calmly, coldly disconnecting the memory circuits that control its artificial “brain.” “Dave, my mind is going,” HAL says, forlornly.
college-writing-019640.zh: 鲍曼几乎被故障机器送入深空死亡，他冷静地，冷静地断开了控制其人工“大脑”的记忆电路。 “戴夫，我的思绪在走，”哈尔孤单地说。

college-writing-019641.en: “I can feel it. I can feel it.”

college-writing-019643.en: Over the past few years I’ve had an uncomfortable sense that someone, or something, has been tinkering with my brain, remapping the neural circuitry, reprogramming the memory.
college-writing-019643.zh: 在过去的几年里，我有一种不舒服的感觉，有人或某事一直在修补我的大脑，重新映射神经回路，重新编程记忆。

college-writing-019644.en: My mind isn’t going─so far as I can tell─but it’s changing.
college-writing-019644.zh: 我的思绪没有去——据我所知——但它正在改变。

college-writing-019645.en: I’m not thinking the way I used to think.
college-writing-019645.zh: 我不是在想我以前的想法。

college-writing-019646.en: I can feel it most strongly when I’m reading.
college-writing-019646.zh: 当我阅读时，我能感觉到最强烈的感觉。

college-writing-019647.en: Immersing myself in a book or a lengthy article used to be easy.
college-writing-019647.zh: 沉浸在一本书或一篇长篇文章中过去很容易。

college-writing-019648.en: My mind would get caught up in the narrative or the turns of the argument, and I’d spend hours strolling through long stretches of prose.
college-writing-019648.zh: 我的思绪会陷入叙述或争论的转折中，我会花几个小时在漫长的散文中漫步。

college-writing-019650.en: Now my concentration often starts to drift after two or three pages.
college-writing-019650.zh: 现在我的注意力经常在两三页后开始漂移。

college-writing-019651.en: I get fidgety, lose the thread, begin looking for something else to do.
college-writing-019651.zh: 我变得烦躁，失去了线索，开始寻找其他事情要做。

college-writing-019652.en: I feel as if I’m always dragging my wayward brain back to the text.
college-writing-019652.zh: 我觉得我总是把我任性的大脑拖回文本。

college-writing-019653.en: The deep reading that used to come naturally has become a struggle.
college-writing-019653.zh: 过去自然而然的深入阅读变成了一场斗争。

college-writing-019654.en: Nicholas Carr is a well-known author who writes about society, culture,
college-writing-019654.zh: 尼古拉斯·卡尔（Nicholas Carr）是一位著名的作家，他撰写了有关社会、文化的文章。

college-writing-019656.en: This passage was originally published in The Atlantic
college-writing-019656.zh: 这篇文章最初发表在大西洋

college-writing-019657.en: and then revised to become the first chapter in his book The Shallows:
college-writing-019657.zh: 然后修改为他的书《浅滩》的第一章：

college-writing-019658.en: What the Internet Is Doing to Our Brains.
college-writing-019658.zh: 互联网对我们的大脑做了什么。

college-writing-019659.zh: 谷歌是在让我们变得愚蠢吗？

college-writing-019663.en: *This essay is abridged from the original.
college-writing-019663.zh: *这篇文章是从原文中删节的。

college-writing-019667.en: I think I know what’s going on.
college-writing-019667.zh: 我想我知道发生了什么。

college-writing-019668.en: For more than a decade now, I’ve been spending a lot of time online, searching and surfing and sometimes adding to the great databases of the Internet.
college-writing-019668.zh: 十多年来，我一直在上网、搜索和冲浪，有时还会添加到互联网的伟大数据库中。

college-writing-019669.en: The Web has been a godsend to me as a writer.
college-writing-019669.zh: 作为作家，网络对我来说是天赐之物。

college-writing-019670.en: Research that once required days in the stacks or periodical rooms of libraries can now be done in minutes.
college-writing-019670.zh: 曾经在图书馆堆栈或定期房间中需要几天的研究现在可以在几分钟内完成。

college-writing-019671.en: A few Google searches, some quick clicks on hyperlinks, and I’ve got the telltale fact or pithy quote I was after.
college-writing-019671.zh: 一些谷歌搜索，一些超链接的快速点击，我得到了我所追求的事实或精辟的报价。

college-writing-019672.en: Even when I’m not working, I’m as likely as not to be foraging in the Web’s info-thickets, reading and writing e-mails, scanning headlines and blog posts, watching videos and listening to podcasts, or just tripping from link to link to link.
college-writing-019672.zh: 即使我不工作，我也很可能不会在网络的信息中觅食、阅读和撰写电子邮件、扫描标题和博客文章、观看视频和收听播客，或者只是从链接到链接到链接。

college-writing-019673.en: (Unlike footnotes, to which they’re sometimes likened, hyperlinks don’t merely point to related works; they propel you toward them.)
college-writing-019673.zh: （与有时被比作的脚注不同，超链接不仅仅指向相关作品；它们将您推向它们。）

college-writing-019674.en: For me, as for others, the Net is becoming a universal medium, the conduit for most of the information that flows through my eyes and ears and into my mind.
college-writing-019674.zh: 对我来说，对于其他人来说，网络正在成为一种普遍的媒介，是流经我的眼睛和耳朵并进入我脑海的大部分信息的管道。

college-writing-019675.en: The advantages of having immediate access to such an incredibly rich store of information are many, and they’ve been widely described and duly applauded.
college-writing-019675.zh: 立即访问如此丰富的信息存储的优势很多，它们已被广泛描述和适当的称赞。

college-writing-019676.en: “The perfect recall of silicon memory,” Wired’s Clive Thompson has written, “can be an enormous boon to thinking.”
college-writing-019676.zh: “对硅记忆的完美回忆，”《连线》的克莱夫·汤普森写道，“可以成为思考的巨大福音。”

college-writing-019677.en: But that boon comes at a price.
college-writing-019677.zh: 但这个恩惠是有代价的。

college-writing-019678.en: As the media theorist Marshall McLuhan pointed out in the 1960s, media are not just passive channels of information.
college-writing-019678.zh: 正如媒体理论家马歇尔·麦克卢汉在 1960 年代所指出的那样，媒体不仅仅是被动的信息渠道。

college-writing-019679.en: They supply the stuff of thought, but they also shape the process of thought.
college-writing-019679.zh: 他们提供思想的东西，但它们也塑造了思想的过程。

college-writing-019680.en: And what the Net seems to be doing is chipping away my capacity for concentration and contemplation.
college-writing-019680.zh: 网络似乎正在削弱我专注和沉思的能力。

college-writing-019681.en: My mind now expects to take in information the way the Net distributes it: in a swiftly moving stream of particles.
college-writing-019681.zh: 我的思想现在希望以网络的方式来吸收信息：在快速移动的粒子流中。

college-writing-019682.en: Once I was a scuba diver in the sea of words.
college-writing-019682.zh: 曾经我是文字海中的水肺潜水员。

college-writing-019683.en: Now I zip along the surface like a guy on a Jet Ski.
college-writing-019683.zh: 现在我像喷气式滑雪上的人一样沿着表面拉链。

college-writing-019685.en: When I mention my troubles with reading to friends and acquaintances─literary types, most of them─many say they’re having similar experiences.
college-writing-019685.zh: 当我提到我在读给朋友和熟人读书时遇到的麻烦——他们中的大多数人——许多人说他们也有类似的经历。

college-writing-019686.en: The more they use the Web, the more they have to fight to stay focused on long pieces of writing.
college-writing-019686.zh: 他们使用网络的次数越多，他们就越需要专注于长篇文章。

college-writing-019687.en: Some of the bloggers I follow have also begun mentioning the phenomenon.
college-writing-019687.zh: 我关注的一些博主也开始提到这种现象。

college-writing-019688.en: Scott Karp, who writes a blog about online media, recently confessed that he has stopped reading books altogether.
college-writing-019688.zh: 撰写有关在线媒体博客的斯科特·卡普最近承认，他已经完全停止阅读书籍。

college-writing-019689.en: “I was a lit major in college, and used to be [a] voracious book reader,” he wrote.
college-writing-019689.zh: “我在大学时是一个灯火通明的专业，曾经是一个贪婪的书读者，”他写道。

college-writing-019691.en: He speculates on the answer: “What if I do all my reading on the web not so much because the way I read has changed, i.e. I’m just seeking convenience, but because the way I THINK has changed?”
college-writing-019691.zh: 他推测答案：“如果我在网上读完所有的阅读方式，不是因为我的阅读方式发生了变化，即我只是在寻求便利，而是因为我认为的方式发生了变化，该怎么办？”

college-writing-019692.en: Bruce Friedman, who blogs regularly about the use of computers in medicine, also has described how the Internet has altered his mental habits.
college-writing-019692.zh: 布鲁斯·弗里德曼（Bruce Friedman）经常在博客上使用计算机在医学中使用，他还描述了互联网如何改变了他的心理习惯。

college-writing-019693.en: “I now have almost totally lost the ability to read and absorb a longish article on the web or in print,” he wrote earlier this year.
college-writing-019693.zh: “我现在几乎完全失去了在网络或印刷品上阅读和吸收长篇文章的能力，”他今年早些时候写道。

college-writing-019694.en: A pathologist who has long been on the faculty of the University of Michigan Medical School, Friedman elaborated on his comment in a telephone conversation with me.
college-writing-019694.zh: 作为一名长期在密歇根大学医学院任教的病理学家，弗里德曼在与我的电话交谈中详细阐述了他的评论。

college-writing-019695.en: His thinking, he said, has taken on a “staccato” quality, reflecting the way he quickly scans short passages of text from many sources online.
college-writing-019695.zh: 他说，他的想法具有“断断续续”的品质，反映了他在网上快速扫描许多来源的短文的方式。

college-writing-019696.en: “I can’t read War and Peace anymore,” he admitted.
college-writing-019696.zh: “我不能再读《战争与和平》了，”他承认。

college-writing-019697.en: “I’ve lost the ability to do that. Even a blog post of more than three or four paragraphs is too much to absorb. I skim it.”
college-writing-019697.zh: “我已经失去了这样做的能力。即使是超过三四段的博客文章也无法吸收。我略读它。”

college-writing-019699.zh: 仅凭轶事并不能证明太多。

college-writing-019700.en: And we still await the long-term neurological and psychological experiments that will provide a definitive picture of how Internet use affects cognition.
college-writing-019700.zh: 我们仍在等待长期的神经和心理实验，这些实验将提供互联网使用如何影响认知的最终画面。

college-writing-019701.en: But a recently published study of online research habits, conducted by scholars from University College London, suggests that we may well be in the midst of a sea change in the way we read and think.
college-writing-019701.zh: 但最近发表的一项关于在线研究习惯的研究，由伦敦大学学院的学者进行，表明我们很可能正处于阅读和思考方式的巨大变化之中。

college-writing-019702.en: As part of the five-year research program, the scholars examined computer logs documenting the behavior of visitors to two popular research sites, one operated by the British Library and one by a U.K. educational consortium, that provide access to journal articles, e-books, and other sources of written information.
college-writing-019702.zh: 作为五年研究计划的一部分，学者们检查了记录访问者行为的两个热门研究地点的计算机日志，一个由大英图书馆运营，一个由英国教育联盟提供，这些网站提供对期刊文章、电子书和其他书面信息来源的访问权限。

college-writing-019703.en: They found that people using the sites exhibited “a form of skimming activity,” hopping from one source to another and rarely returning to any source they’d already visited.
college-writing-019703.zh: 他们发现使用这些网站的人表现出“一种掠夺活动”，从一个来源跳到另一个来源，很少返回他们已经访问过的任何来源。

college-writing-019704.en: They typically read no more than one or two pages of an article or book before they would “bounce” out to another site.
college-writing-019704.zh: 他们通常在“反弹”到另一个网站之前阅读的文章或书籍不超过一两页。

college-writing-019705.en: Sometimes they’d save a long article, but there’s no evidence that they ever went back and actually read it.
college-writing-019705.zh: 有时他们会保存一篇长篇文章，但没有证据表明他们曾经回去并真正阅读过它。

college-writing-019706.en: The authors of the study report:

college-writing-019707.en: It is clear that users are not reading online in the traditional sense; indeed there are signs that new forms of “reading” are emerging as users “power browse” horizontally through titles, contents pages and abstracts going for quick wins.
college-writing-019707.zh: 很明显，用户不是传统意义上的在线阅读； 确实，有迹象表明，随着用户通过标题、内容页面和摘要以快速获胜的方式“水平浏览”，新形式的“阅读”正在出现。

college-writing-019708.en: It almost seems that they go online to avoid reading in the traditional sense.
college-writing-019708.zh: 似乎他们上网是为了避免传统意义上的阅读。

college-writing-019709.en: Thanks to the ubiquity of text on the Internet, not to mention the popularity of text-messaging on cell phones, we may well be reading more today than we did in the 1970s or 1980s, when television was our medium of choice.
college-writing-019709.zh: 由于互联网上无处不在的文字，更不用说手机上短信的流行，我们今天的阅读量可能比 1970 年代或 1980 年代更多，当时电视是我们的首选媒体。

college-writing-019710.en: But it’s a different kind of reading, and behind it lies a different kind of thinking─perhaps even a new sense of the self.
college-writing-019710.zh: 但它是一种不同的阅读方式，背后隐藏着一种不同的思维——甚至可能是一种新的自我意识。

college-writing-019711.en: “We are not only what we read,” says Maryanne Wolf, a developmental psychologist at Tufts University and the author of Proust and the Squid: The Story and Science of the Reading Brain.
college-writing-019711.zh: “我们不仅是我们读到的，”塔夫茨大学的发育心理学家、普鲁斯特与鱿鱼的作者玛丽安妮·沃尔夫说：《阅读大脑的故事和科学》。

college-writing-019713.en: Wolf worries that the style of reading promoted by the Net, a style that puts “efficiency” and “immediacy” above all else, may be weakening our capacity for the kind of deep reading that emerged when an earlier technology, the printing press, made long and complex works of prose commonplace.
college-writing-019713.zh: 沃尔夫担心网络推广的阅读风格，一种将“效率”和“即时性”置于一切之上的风格，可能会削弱我们在早期技术、印刷机、长而复杂的散文作品中出现的深度阅读能力。

college-writing-019714.en: When we read online, she says, we tend to become “mere decoders of information.”
college-writing-019714.zh: 她说，当我们在网上阅读时，我们往往会成为“信息解码器”。

college-writing-019715.en: Our ability to interpret text, to make the rich mental connections that form when we read deeply and without distraction, remains largely disengaged.
college-writing-019715.zh: 当我们深入阅读并且不分心地阅读时，我们解释文本的能力，建立丰富的心理联系，在很大程度上仍然是脱节的。

college-writing-019716.en: Reading, explains Wolf, is not an instinctive skill for human beings.
college-writing-019716.zh: 沃尔夫解释说，阅读并不是人类的本能技能。

college-writing-019717.en: It’s not etched into our genes the way speech is.
college-writing-019717.zh: 它不像语音那样被蚀刻到我们的基因中。

college-writing-019718.en: We have to teach our minds how to translate the symbolic characters we see into the language we understand.
college-writing-019718.zh: 我们必须教导我们的思想如何将我们看到的符号字符翻译成我们所理解的语言。

college-writing-019719.en: And the media or other technologies we use in learning and practicing the craft of reading play an important part in shaping the neural circuits inside our brains.
college-writing-019719.zh: 我们在学习和练习阅读技巧方面使用的媒体或其他技术在塑造大脑中的神经回路方面发挥着重要作用。

college-writing-019720.en: Experiments demonstrate that readers of ideograms, such as the Chinese, develop a mental circuitry for reading that is very different from the circuitry found in those of us whose written language employs an alphabet.
college-writing-019720.zh: 实验表明，象形文字的读者，如中国人，开发了一种与我们这些书面语言使用字母表的电路非常不同的心理电路。

college-writing-019721.en: The variations extend across many regions of the brain, including those that govern such essential cognitive functions as memory and the interpretation of visual and auditory stimuli.
college-writing-019721.zh: 这些变异延伸到大脑的许多区域，包括控制记忆等基本认知功能的区域，以及对视觉和听觉刺激的解释。

college-writing-019724.en: We can expect as well that the circuits woven by our use of the Net will be different from those woven by our reading of books and other printed works. . . .
college-writing-019724.zh: 我们也可以期待，我们使用网络编织的电路将与我们阅读书籍和其他印刷作品所编织的电路不同。 。 。 。

college-writing-019725.en: In Google’s world, the world we enter when we go online, there’s little place for the fuzziness of contemplation.
college-writing-019725.zh: 在谷歌的世界里，我们上网时进入的世界，沉思的模糊性几乎没有地方。

college-writing-019726.en: Ambiguity is not an opening for insight but a bug to be fixed.
college-writing-019726.zh: 歧义不是洞察力的开放，而是要修复的错误。

college-writing-019727.en: The human brain is just an outdated computer that needs a faster processor and a bigger hard drive.
college-writing-019727.zh: 人脑只是一台过时的计算机，需要更快的处理器和更大的硬盘驱动器。

college-writing-019728.en: The idea that our minds should operate as high-speed data-processing machines is not only built into the workings of the Internet, it is the network’s reigning business model as well.
college-writing-019728.zh: 我们的思想应该作为高速数据处理机器运行的想法不仅内置于互联网的工作中，它也是网络的统治商业模式。

college-writing-019729.en: The faster we surf across the Web─the more links we click and pages we view─the more opportunities Google and other companies gain to collect information about us and to feed us advertisements.
college-writing-019729.zh: 我们在网络上浏览的速度越快——我们点击的链接和查看的页面就越多——谷歌和其他公司获得的机会就越多，可以收集有关我们的信息并为我们提供广告。

college-writing-019730.en: Most of the proprietors of the commercial Internet have a financial stake in collecting the crumbs of data we leave behind as we flit from link to link─the more crumbs, the better.
college-writing-019730.zh: 大多数商业互联网的所有者在收集我们留下的数据碎屑时拥有财务利益，因为我们从一个链接到另一个链接——越多的面包屑越好。

college-writing-019731.en: The last thing these companies want is to encourage leisurely reading or slow, concentrated thought.
college-writing-019731.zh: 这些公司最不想做的就是鼓励悠闲阅读或缓慢、集中的思考。

college-writing-019732.en: It’s in their economic interest to drive us to distraction.
college-writing-019732.zh: 驱使我们分心符合他们的经济利益。

college-writing-019733.zh: 也许我只是一个忧心忡忡的人。

college-writing-019734.en: Just as there’s a tendency to glorify technological progress, there’s a countertendency to expect the worst of every new tool or machine.
college-writing-019734.zh: 正如有一种美化技术进步的倾向一样，每一种新工具或机器中的最坏情况都有一种相反的趋势。

college-writing-019735.en: In Plato’s Phaedrus, Socrates bemoaned the development of writing.
college-writing-019735.zh: 在柏拉图的《费德鲁斯》中，苏格拉底哀叹写作的发展。

college-writing-019736.en: He feared that, as people came to rely on the written word as a substitute for the knowledge they used to carry inside their heads, they would, in the words of one of the dialogue’s characters, “cease to exercise their memory and become forgetful.”
college-writing-019736.zh: 他担心，当人们开始依靠书面文字来代替他们过去常常将脑袋里的知识作为替代品时，他们会用对话人物之一的话说，“停止运用他们的记忆，变得健忘”。

college-writing-019737.en: And because they would be able to “receive a quantity of information without proper instruction,” they would “be thought very knowledgeable when they are for the most part quite ignorant.”
college-writing-019737.zh: 因为他们能够“在没有适当指导的情况下接收一定数量的信息”，所以他们“在大部分情况下都非常无知时会被认为是非常有知识的”。

college-writing-019738.en: They would be “filled with the conceit of wisdom instead of real wisdom.”
college-writing-019738.zh: 他们将“充满智慧而不是真正的智慧”。

college-writing-019739.en: Socrates wasn’t wrong─the new technology did often have the effects he feared─but he was shortsighted.
college-writing-019739.zh: 苏格拉底并没有错——新技术经常产生他担心的影响——但他是短视的。

college-writing-019740.en: He couldn’t foresee the many ways that writing and reading would serve to spread information, spur fresh ideas, and expand human knowledge (if not wisdom).
college-writing-019740.zh: 他无法预见写作和阅读在传播信息、激发新思想和扩展人类知识（如果不是智慧的话）方面的作用方式。

college-writing-019741.en: The arrival of Gutenberg’s printing press, in the 15th century, set off another round of teeth gnashing.
college-writing-019741.zh: 15世纪古腾堡印刷机的到来，又一轮牙齿咬牙切齿。

college-writing-019742.en: The Italian humanist Hieronimo Squarciafico worried that the easy availability of books would lead to intellectual laziness, making men “less studious” and weakening their minds.
college-writing-019742.zh: 意大利人文主义者 Hieronimo Squarciafico 担心书籍的容易获得会导致智力上的懒惰，使男人“不那么好学”并削弱他们的思想。

college-writing-019743.en: Others argued that cheaply printed books and broadsheets would undermine religious authority, demean the work of scholars and scribes, and spread sedition and debauchery.
college-writing-019743.zh: 其他人则认为，廉价印刷的书籍和大报会破坏宗教权威，贬低学者和文士的工作，并传播煽动和放荡。

college-writing-019744.en: As New York University professor Clay Shirky notes, “Most of the arguments made against the printing press were correct, even prescient.”
college-writing-019744.zh: 正如纽约大学 Clay Shirky 教授所指出的，“针对印刷机的大多数论点都是正确的，甚至是有先见之明的。”

college-writing-019745.en: But, again, the doomsayers were unable to imagine the myriad blessings that the printed word would deliver.
college-writing-019745.zh: 但是，再一次，末日预言者无法想象印刷的文字会带来无数的祝福。

college-writing-019746.en: So, yes, you should be skeptical of my skepticism.
college-writing-019746.zh: 所以，是的，你应该对我的怀疑态度持怀疑态度。

college-writing-019747.en: Perhaps those who dismiss critics of the Internet as Luddites or nostalgists will be proved correct, and from our hyperactive, data-stoked minds will spring a golden age of intellectual discovery and universal wisdom.
college-writing-019747.zh: 也许那些将互联网批评者视为卢德主义者或怀旧主义者的人会被证明是正确的，而从我们过度活跃、数据激发的思想中，将出现智力发现和普遍智慧的黄金时代。

college-writing-019748.en: Then again, the Net isn’t the alphabet, and although
college-writing-019748.zh: 再说一次，网络不是字母，虽然

college-writing-019750.en: it may replace the printing press, it produces something altogether different.
college-writing-019750.zh: 它可能会取代印刷机，它会产生完全不同的东西。

college-writing-019751.en: The kind of deep reading that a sequence of printed pages promotes is valuable not just for the knowledge we acquire from the author’s words but for the intellectual vibrations those words set off within our own minds.
college-writing-019751.zh: 一系列印刷页面所促进的深度阅读不仅对我们从作者的话语中获得的知识有价值，而且对于这些词语在我们自己的脑海中引发的智力振动是有价值的。

college-writing-019752.en: In the quiet spaces opened up by the sustained, undistracted reading of a book, or by any other act of contemplation, for that matter, we make our own associations, draw our own inferences and analogies, foster our own ideas.
college-writing-019752.zh: 在持续、不分心的阅读一本书或任何其他沉思行为所开辟的安静空间中，就此而言，我们建立自己的联想，得出自己的推论和类比，培养我们自己的想法。

college-writing-019753.en: Deep reading, as Maryanne Wolf argues, is indistinguishable from deep thinking.
college-writing-019753.zh: 正如玛丽安妮·沃尔夫（Maryanne Wolf）所论证的那样，深入阅读与深刻的思考是无法区分的。

college-writing-019754.en: If we lose those quiet spaces, or fill them up with “content,” we will sacrifice something important not only in our selves but in our culture.
college-writing-019754.zh: 如果我们失去了那些安静的空间，或者用“内容”填满它们，我们将牺牲一些重要的东西，不仅在我们自己，而且在我们的文化中。

college-writing-019755.en: In a recent essay, the playwright Richard Foreman eloquently described what’s at stake:
college-writing-019755.zh: 在最近的一篇文章中，剧作家理查德·福尔曼雄辩地描述了什么是危险的：

college-writing-019756.en: I come from a tradition of Western culture, in which the ideal (my ideal) was the complex, dense and “cathedral-like” structure of the highly educated and articulate personality─a man or woman who carried inside themselves a personally constructed and unique version of the entire heritage of the West.
college-writing-019756.zh: 我来自西方文化的传统，其中理想（我的理想）是受过高等教育和口齿伶俐的人格的复杂、密集和“大教堂式”结构——一个男人或女人，一个男人或女人，一个男人或女人，一个个人构建和独特的版本，是整个西方遗产的独特版本。

college-writing-019757.en: [But now] I see within us all (myself included) the replacement of complex inner density with a new kind of self─evolving under the pressure of information overload and the technology of the “instantly available.”
college-writing-019757.zh: [但现在]我看到我们所有人（包括我自己）在信息过载的压力下用一种新的自我替代复杂的内部密度和“即时可用”的技术。

college-writing-019758.en: As we are drained of our “inner repertory of dense cultural inheritance,” Foreman concluded, we risk turning into “‘pancake people’─spread wide and thin as we connect with that vast network of information accessed by the mere touch of a button.”
college-writing-019758.zh: 福尔曼总结说，当我们耗尽了“密集的文化遗产的内部剧目”时，我们有可能变成“煎饼人”——当我们与只需按一下按钮访问的庞大信息网络联系起来时，就会变得广泛而稀薄。

college-writing-019759.en: I’m haunted by that scene in 2001.

college-writing-019760.en: What makes it so poignant, and so weird, is the computer’s emotional response to the disassembly of its mind: its despair as one circuit after another goes dark, its childlike pleading with the astronaut─“I can feel it. I can feel it. I’m afraid”─and its final reversion to what can only be called a state of innocence.
college-writing-019760.zh: 是什么让它如此凄美，又如此奇怪，是计算机对它的心灵分解的情感反应：它的绝望一层一层地变暗，它对宇航员的孩子般的恳求——“我能感觉到。我能感觉到它。 害怕”——它的最终回归只能被称为纯真状态。

college-writing-019761.en: HAL’s outpouring of feeling contrasts with the emotionlessness that characterizes the human figures in the film, who go about their business with an almost robotic efficiency.
college-writing-019761.zh: 哈尔的感情与电影中人物人物的无情感形成鲜明对比，他们以几乎机器人的效率开展业务。

college-writing-019762.en: Their thoughts and actions feel scripted, as if they’re following the steps of an algorithm.
college-writing-019762.zh: 他们的想法和行为感觉像是在遵循算法的步骤。

college-writing-019763.en: In the world of 2001, people have become so machinelike that the most human character turns out to be a machine.
college-writing-019763.zh: 在 2001 年的世界里，人们变得如此机器化，以至于最人性化的角色变成了一台机器。

college-writing-019764.en: That’s the essence of Kubrick’s dark prophecy: as we come to rely on computers to mediate our understanding of the world, it is our own intelligence that flattens into artificial intelligence.
college-writing-019764.zh: 这就是库布里克黑暗预言的精髓：当我们依靠计算机来调解我们对世界的理解时，我们自己的智能才会变为人工智能。

college-writing-019883.zh: 例如，如果您一直在研究瑜伽

college-writing-019885.zh: 724 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-019886.en: gear and an ad for a company you had never even heard of popped up, would this be more or less worrisome than ads from actual sites you had visited?
college-writing-019886.zh: 为您从未听说过的公司弹出的装备和广告，这会比您访问过的实际网站的广告或多或少令人担忧吗？

college-writing-019887.en: The rest of your paper should then discuss why or why not this type of data gathering is acceptable; whether or not you feel it violates privacy; and whether or not regulations should be put into place.
college-writing-019887.zh: 然后，您论文的其余部分应该讨论为什么或为什么不可以接受这种类型的数据收集； 您是否觉得它侵犯了隐私； 以及是否应制定法规。

college-writing-019888.en: You will want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” and Chapter 16, “Argument,” to help you write a strong essay.
college-writing-019888.zh: 你会想回顾第 8 章“描述”和第 16 章“论点”，以帮助你写一篇强有力的文章。

college-writing-019890.en: For this essay, you are going to profile someone who regularly works on computers.
college-writing-019890.zh: 对于这篇文章，您将介绍经常在计算机上工作的人。

college-writing-019891.en: Your profile should focus on what this person thinks about computers, data gathering, and the effects computer use has on people, so you will want to ask guiding questions such as the following.
college-writing-019891.zh: 您的个人资料应关注此人对计算机、数据收集和计算机使用对人的影响的看法，因此您需要提出指导性问题，例如以下内容。

college-writing-019892.en: Make sure you ask for explanations and any clarifications you need to write a lengthy profile.
college-writing-019892.zh: 确保您要求解释和编写冗长的个人资料所需的任何说明。

college-writing-019893.en: • How often do you use a computer?
college-writing-019893.zh: • 您多久使用一次计算机？

college-writing-019894.en: What types of things do you do on a computer?
college-writing-019894.zh: 你在电脑上做什么类型的事情？

college-writing-019895.en: • What are the sites you most often visit?
college-writing-019895.zh: • 您最常访问的网站是什么？

college-writing-019896.en: • Whenever you search for information using Google, the company collects, stores, and analyzes your data.
college-writing-019896.zh: • 每当您使用 Google 搜索信息时，公司都会收集、存储和分析您的数据。

college-writing-019897.en: This data is used for targeted ads, among other things.
college-writing-019897.zh: 此数据用于有针对性的广告等。

college-writing-019898.en: How do you feel about this type of data gathering?
college-writing-019898.zh: 您如何看待这种类型的数据收集？

college-writing-019899.en: • Do you feel data gathering is a violation of privacy?
college-writing-019899.zh: • 您是否认为收集数据是对隐私的侵犯？

college-writing-019901.en: • Have you noticed the targeted ads on any of the sites you are visiting?
college-writing-019901.zh: • 您是否注意到您正在访问的任何网站上的目标广告？

college-writing-019902.en: • Do you think computers have affected our health or our brains?
college-writing-019902.zh: • 您认为计算机是否影响了我们的健康或大脑？

college-writing-019904.en: • Do you think computers are becoming dangerous, like HAL in 2001: A Space Odyssey?
college-writing-019904.zh: • 您认为计算机是否变得危险，例如 2001 年的 HAL：太空漫游？

college-writing-019905.en: Once you have asked all your questions, you will need to create a thesis that introduces the person you are profiling and the main claim you will support
college-writing-019905.zh: 一旦您提出了所有问题，您将需要创建一篇论文，介绍您要分析的人以及您将支持的主要主张

college-writing-019907.en: The following sample thesis statements should help you develop your own thesis:
college-writing-019907.zh: 以下示例 中心论点句 应该可以帮助您开发自己的论文：

college-writing-019908.zh: • 虽然我的妈妈简·史密斯经常在电脑上工作，但她担心我们过于依赖它们。

college-writing-019909.en: • My dad, Allan Jones, believes that Google’s data gathering has made his life online much better.
college-writing-019909.zh: • 我的父亲艾伦·琼斯 (Allan Jones) 认为，谷歌的数据收集让他的在线生活变得更好。

college-writing-019916.en: The Quiet Struggle of College Students with Kids
college-writing-019916.zh: 有孩子的大学生的安静斗争

college-writing-019918.en: More than one-quarter of American undergraduates have dependent children, but affordable, on-campus childcare is still hard to find.
college-writing-019918.zh: 超过四分之一的美国本科生有受抚养的孩子，但仍然很难找到负担得起的校内托儿服务。

college-writing-019919.en: In 2001, Michelle Marie enrolled at Oregon State University.
college-writing-019919.zh: 2001 年，Michelle Marie 就读于俄勒冈州立大学。

college-writing-019920.en: After two years of community college, and then another two years at home taking care of her baby, Marie was ready to complete her bachelor’s degree.
college-writing-019920.zh: 经过两年的社区大学学习，然后在家照顾她的孩子两年后，玛丽准备完成她的学士学位。

college-writing-019921.en: But that meant she’d need to find someone to watch her daughter, who was nearly two years old, and both resources and information were scarce.
college-writing-019921.zh: 但这意味着她需要找人看她快两岁的女儿，资源和信息都很稀缺。

college-writing-019922.en: “At the time nobody was asking me if I was a student parent. Nobody was saying, ‘Hey, we’re aware that you’re a member of a population that is perhaps not served by the services and resources that are available,’”
college-writing-019922.zh: “当时没有人问我是否是学生家长。没有人说，‘嘿，我们知道你是可能无法获得的服务和资源所服务的人群中的一员，’”

college-writing-019924.en: “I felt like I had to set aside my parent status in order to be a student.”
college-writing-019924.zh: “我觉得为了成为一名学生，我必须搁置父母的身份。”

college-writing-019925.en: Marie was lucky; a nearby aunt was able to provide childcare until her daughter was old enough for kindergarten.
college-writing-019925.zh: 玛丽很幸运； 附近的一位阿姨能够提供托儿服务，直到她的女儿长大到可以幼儿园。

college-writing-019926.en: Without her aunt’s help, Marie says she’s not sure how, or if, she could have juggled both school and a young child.
college-writing-019926.zh: 没有她姑姑的帮助，玛丽说她不确定如何，或者是否可以兼顾学校和一个年幼的孩子。

college-writing-019927.en: Now, nearly 15 years later, she’s working on her Ph.D. and participating in student-parent advocacy on campus, in hopes of creating a better experience for others who will follow in her footsteps.
college-writing-019927.zh: 现在，将近 15 年后，她正在攻读博士学位。 并在校园内参与学生家长的宣传，希望为追随她脚步的其他人创造更好的体验。

college-writing-019928.en: But Marie says things haven’t improved all that much.
college-writing-019928.zh: 但玛丽说，情况并没有太大改善。

college-writing-019929.en: “Childcare is actually even less available on campus, and more expensive than it was then,” she says.
college-writing-019929.zh: “在校园里，托儿服务实际上更少，而且比当时更昂贵，”她说。

college-writing-019930.zh: “学生父母仍然是一个看不见的人群。”

college-writing-019931.en: Gillian B. White received her B.A. Economics and Political Science degree from Columbia University and her M.S. Journalism degree from Northwestern.
college-writing-019931.zh: Gillian B. White 获得了学士学位。 哥伦比亚大学经济学和政治学学位和她的硕士学位 西北大学的新闻学学位。

college-writing-019932.en: She is a freelance writer and a Senior Associate Editor for The Atlantic.
college-writing-019932.zh: 她是大西洋的自由撰稿人和高级副主编。

college-writing-019933.en: In this article, she highlights some of the challenges college students who are parents face.
college-writing-019933.zh: 在本文中，她重点介绍了家长面临的一些挑战。

college-writing-019936.zh: 726 第 5 部分 作家读物

college-writing-019937.en: According to a 2014 study from the Institute for Women’s Policy Research, 4.8 million college students were parents of dependent children in 2011, the most recent year for which data is available─that’s about 26 percent of all college undergraduates.
college-writing-019937.zh: 根据妇女政策研究所 2014 年的一项研究，2011 年有 480 万大学生是受抚养儿童的父母，这是最近一年的数据——约占所有大学本科生的 26%。

college-writing-019938.en: The vast majority of these students, 71 percent, are women.
college-writing-019938.zh: 这些学生中的绝大多数，71%，是女性。

college-writing-019939.en: But while the number of enrolled students who have children has grown (increasing by 50 percent between 1995 and 2011, according to IWPR), the availability of childcare on campuses hasn’t.
college-writing-019939.zh: 但是，尽管根据 IWPR 的数据，尽管 1995 年至 2011 年间，有孩子的注册学生人数有所增长（在 1995 年至 2011 年间增加了 50%），但校园内的托儿服务却没有。

college-writing-019940.en: In fact, the number of overall childcare facilities available at public colleges (where more than 60 percent of students with children enroll) has decreased over the past decade or so.
college-writing-019940.zh: 事实上，在过去十年左右的时间里，公立大学的整体托儿设施（超过 60% 的有儿童入学人数）的整体托儿设施数量有所减少。

college-writing-019941.en: In 2002, 54 percent of public, four-year colleges had on-campus childcare; by 2013 that number had dropped to 51 percent.
college-writing-019941.zh: 2002 年，54% 的公立四年制大学拥有校内托儿服务； 到 2013 年，这一数字已降至 51%。

college-writing-019942.en: For public, two-year colleges, those figures declined from 52 percent to 46 percent during the same period.
college-writing-019942.zh: 对于公立的两年制大学，同期这些数字从 52% 下降到 46%。

college-writing-019944.en: Number of Parents Enrolled in College, 1995-2011

college-writing-019945.en: The reasons behind the declining availability in childcare are varied, potentially a mix of both budget constraints and academic culture, says Barbara Gault, the executive director at IWPR.
college-writing-019945.zh: IWPR 执行董事 Barbara Gault 说，儿童保育可用性下降的原因多种多样，可能包含预算限制和学术文化。

college-writing-019946.en: “It’s taking a long time for institutions of higher education to undergo a culture shift that reflects the changing demographics, and to begin to view themselves as organizations that are family-friendly─not just for faculty, but for students,” she says.
college-writing-019946.zh: “高等教育机构需要很长时间才能经历反映人口结构变化的文化转变，并开始将自己视为对家庭友好的组织——不仅对教师，而且对学生来说，”她说。

college-writing-019947.en: It might also be true that these types of facilities aren’t yet considered a financial priority.
college-writing-019947.zh: 这些类型的设施尚未被视为财务优先事项也可能是正确的。

college-writing-019948.en: “Institutions are looking desperately for places to cut. Because there’s so little awareness of the prevalence of students with children I think it often ends up looking like something that’s an extra rather than something that’s essential,” Gault says.
college-writing-019948.zh: “机构正在拼命寻找可以削减的地方。因为人们对学生和孩子的流行程度的认识太少了，我认为它通常最终看起来像是一种额外的东西，而不是必不可少的东西，”Gault 说。

college-writing-019949.en: Graduate student Kimberly Lewis is a soon-to-be parent who is currently wrestling with the lack of both funds and childcare programs as she anticipates the arrival of a child in February.
college-writing-019949.zh: 研究生金伯利·刘易斯 (Kimberly Lewis) 是一位即将成为家长的父母，她目前正在为缺乏资金和儿童保育计划而苦苦挣扎，因为她预计二月份将有一个孩子的到来。

college-writing-019950.en: While she’s excited, she’s also a bit nervous.
college-writing-019950.zh: 虽然她很兴奋，但她也有点紧张。

college-writing-019951.en: Lewis works as a graduate assistant at Western Illinois University in Macomb.
college-writing-019951.zh: 刘易斯在马科姆的西伊利诺伊大学担任研究生助理。

college-writing-019952.en: In exchange she receives a stipend that helps cover her expenses while she furthers her education.
college-writing-019952.zh: 作为交换，她获得了一份津贴，以帮助支付她的费用，同时她继续接受教育。

college-writing-019953.en: She also receives assistance from SNAP and WIC in order to make ends meet each month.
college-writing-019953.zh: 她还从 Snap 和 WIC 获得帮助，以维持每个月的生计。

college-writing-019954.en: But when it comes to finding help for childcare, so that she can head back to work and school after the baby, Lewis can’t seem to find a solution.
college-writing-019954.zh: 但是，当谈到为儿童保育寻求帮助，以便她可以在婴儿之后重返工作和上学时，刘易斯似乎无法找到解决方案。

college-writing-019956.en: She says that she looked into childcare on campus, but that the facility wouldn’t hold a spot open for her until March, when her child will be old enough to finally start daycare.
college-writing-019956.zh: 她说她在校园里调查了托儿所，但直到三月份她的孩子长大到可以最终开始托儿所，该设施才会为她开放。

college-writing-019957.en: And then a nearby Early Head Start program bumped her to the wait-list after originally confirming her registration.
college-writing-019957.zh: 然后，在最初确认她的注册后，附近的一个早期启蒙计划将她撞到了候补名单。

college-writing-019958.en: “They told me, ‘Hey, you’re pretty poor, you qualify for Early Head Start,’” she said.
college-writing-019958.zh: “他们告诉我，‘嘿，你很穷，你有资格提早开始，’”她说。

college-writing-019959.en: But then two weeks later they called to say that she had been moved to the wait-list and her child’s spot was no longer confirmed.
college-writing-019959.zh: 但两周后，他们打电话说她已经被转移到候补名单上，她孩子的位置不再得到证实。

college-writing-019960.en: She says that the daycare facility cited the fact that enrollment was need-based, not first-come, first-served, but that they told a friend of hers the opposite.
college-writing-019960.zh: 她说，日托机构引用了这样一个事实，即注册是基于需求的，不是先到先得的，而是他们告诉她的一个朋友的相反。

college-writing-019961.en: Plus, Lewis says, she does in fact need the help.
college-writing-019961.zh: 另外，刘易斯说，她确实需要帮助。

college-writing-019962.en: If she can’t arrange childcare, she’ll lose her graduate-assistant job and along with it her $800 monthly stipend and tuition assistance.
college-writing-019962.zh: 如果她不能安排托儿服务，她将失去她的研究生助理工作，以及她每月 800 美元的津贴和学费援助。

college-writing-019963.en: If she can’t find a solution by the time she has to go back to work, after the school’s 2015 spring break, she’s considered going into debt in order to fund both her studies and the cost of childcare.
college-writing-019963.zh: 如果她在 2015 年春假后无法找到解决方案，她必须在学校的 2015 年春假之后找到解决方案，以资助她的学习和儿童保育费用。

college-writing-019964.en: It’s a solution that other student-parents have had to rely on while in school.
college-writing-019964.zh: 这是其他学生父母在学校期间不得不依赖的解决方案。

college-writing-019965.en: Andrea Fitch turned to loans while she pursued her bachelor’s almost five years ago.
college-writing-019965.zh: Andrea Fitch 在近五年前攻读学士学位时转向贷款。

college-writing-019966.en: She managed to earn scholarships or grant money for nearly all of her education expenses while she studied at Colorado State University.
college-writing-019966.zh: 在科罗拉多州立大学学习期间，她几乎所有的教育费用都获得了奖学金或拨款。

college-writing-019967.en: She says she looked into the daycare on-site, but “it was still charging $40 a day, per kid─and there was a wait-list because a lot of the children at that facility were from faculty and staff.”
college-writing-019967.zh: 她说她在现场调查了托儿所，但“每个孩子仍然每天收费 40 美元——而且有一个候补名单，因为该设施的很多孩子都来自教职员工。”

college-writing-019968.en: Fitch says that she also looked into subsidies for childcare, but at the time, Colorado’s Child Care Assistance Program was frozen, leaving little financial help available.
college-writing-019968.zh: 惠誉说，她还研究了儿童保育补贴，但当时科罗拉多州的托儿援助计划被冻结，几乎没有经济帮助。

college-writing-019969.en: In the end, she took out nearly $30,000 in loans in order to pay for in-home childcare while she earned her degree.
college-writing-019969.zh: 最后，她获得了近 30,000 美元的贷款，以便在获得学位的同时支付家庭托儿服务。

college-writing-019970.en: “I felt like it was my only option for creating a next step,” she said.
college-writing-019970.zh: “我觉得这是我创造下一步的唯一选择，”她说。

college-writing-019972.en: Average Undergraduate Debt One Year After Graduation
college-writing-019972.zh: 毕业一年后的平均本科债务

college-writing-019973.zh: 所有学生 男性 女性 独立

college-writing-019974.en: Students Students without Children Students with Children
college-writing-019974.zh: 学生 无儿童 学生 有孩子的学生

college-writing-019975.en: Students who have kids tend to have higher student-loan debt than their childless peers, according to IWPR.
college-writing-019975.zh: 根据 IWPR 的说法，有孩子的学生往往比没有孩子的同龄人有更高的学生贷款债务。

college-writing-019976.en: That’s particularly problematic given the fact
college-writing-019976.zh: 鉴于事实，这尤其成问题

college-writing-019977.zh: 728 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-019978.en: that these parents are also more likely to have low-incomes than their fellow students.
college-writing-019978.zh: 这些家长也比同学更有可能拥有低收入。

college-writing-019979.en: That makes subsidies, like the federal funds that support childcare at colleges, particularly important.
college-writing-019979.zh: 这使得补贴，例如支持大学托儿服务的联邦资金，尤其重要。

college-writing-019980.en: But some of those services have also been reduced.
college-writing-019980.zh: 但其中一些服务也减少了。

college-writing-019981.en: In 2013 around $14.9 million was allocated to the Child Care Access Means Parents in School program, which provides funding for on-campus childcare services.
college-writing-019981.zh: 2013 年，约 1490 万美元用于儿童保育服务，该计划为校内托儿服务提供资金。

college-writing-019982.en: That’s a far cry from the funding that was allocated in 2001, when $25 million was made available for such programs.
college-writing-019982.zh: 这与 2001 年分配的资金相去甚远，当时为此类计划提供了 2500 万美元。

college-writing-019983.en: And in many states, programs that offer funding for student-parents are facing frozen funds, require a certain number of work hours per week, or inflict limits on total school hours, making subsidies more difficult to qualify for and imposing more stringent schedules on those who do receive funds, according to IWPR’s research.
college-writing-019983.zh: 在许多州，为学生父母提供资金的项目面临冻结资金，每周需要一定数量的工作时间，或限制总上学时间，使补贴更难获得资格，并对确实获得资金的人施加更严格的时间表。 IWPR的研究。

college-writing-019984.en: So why is on-campus childcare so important?
college-writing-019984.zh: 那么为什么校内托儿服务如此重要呢？

college-writing-019985.en: Well, it’s partially because it could help more parents graduate, allowing them to secure better jobs and provide a more stable home for themselves and their children.
college-writing-019985.zh: 嗯，这部分是因为它可以帮助更多的父母毕业，让他们获得更好的工作，并为自己和孩子提供更稳定的家。

college-writing-019986.en: According to IWPR, parents with dependent children drop out of college at a higher rate than any other demographic, with only 33 percent of students with children obtaining a degree or certificate within six years.
college-writing-019986.zh: 根据 IWPR 的说法，有受抚养子女的父母以高于任何其他人群的比例辍学，只有 33% 的有孩子的学生在六年内获得学位或证书。

college-writing-019987.en: Placing these facilities on-campus not only simplifies daily routines for parents, allowing them to spend less time (and money) commuting from home, to daycare to school, and back again, but also gives them peace-of-mind while at school, since they could easily reach their children in case of emergency.

college-writing-020133.en: Public writing can be a touchy subject.
college-writing-020133.zh: 公开写作可能是一个敏感的话题。

college-writing-020134.en: From one perspective, we are living in a golden age of public intellectualism.
college-writing-020134.zh: 从一个角度来看，我们生活在一个公共知识主义的黄金时代。

college-writing-020135.en: Today’s scholars have numerous ways to reach a broad audience─from online magazines hungry for fresh takes on the topics of the day to print magazines looking for authoritative essays.
college-writing-020135.zh: 今天的学者有多种方式可以接触到广泛的受众——从渴望对当天主题的新主题到印刷杂志寻找权威论文的在线杂志。

college-writing-020136.en: Writing coaches and programs such as the OpEd Project offer training in how to pitch to general-interest publications, while grant agencies in Europe and North America increasingly require recipients to communicate with the public.
college-writing-020136.zh: 写作教练和项目（如 Oped Project）提供有关如何向一般利益出版物推销的培训，而欧洲和北美的资助机构越来越要求接受者与公众进行沟通。

college-writing-020137.en: To some scholars, public writing has even started to seem like yet another skill they are expected to master to stay competitive.
college-writing-020137.zh: 对于一些学者来说，公开写作甚至开始看起来像是他们应该掌握的另一项技能，以保持竞争力。

college-writing-020138.en: At the same time, academics often approach newspapers, magazines, and websites with assumptions drawn from the outlets we’re used to writing for: scholarly journals and, since the early 2000s, the blogs that flourish as a faster, more casual medium of scholarly exchange.
college-writing-020138.zh: 与此同时，学者们常常以来自我们习惯写作的渠道的假设来处理报纸、杂志和网站：学术期刊，以及自2000年代初期，这些博客作为一种更快、更随意的学术交流媒介而蓬勃发展。

college-writing-020139.en: Trying to write for the public can mean a series of unpleasant surprises about what happens to our work at every stage of editing and publication.
college-writing-020139.zh: 试图为公众写作可能意味着一系列令人不快的惊喜，我们的工作在编辑和出版的每个阶段都会发生什么。

college-writing-020140.zh: Irina Dumitrescu 获得了博士学位。 耶鲁大学英语专业。

college-writing-020141.en: She has taught at Columbia University and Southern Methodist University and is currently a professor of English medieval studies at the University of Bonn.
