college-writing-020142.zh: 学者对“公开写作”的误解

college-writing-020143.en: Popular writing should be as rigorous as scholarship—but much easier to read
college-writing-020143.zh: 大众写作应该和学术一样严格——但更容易阅读

college-writing-020147.zh: 734 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-020148.en: Even as readers, however, scholars tend to misunderstand how public writing─ or as the public would call it, “writing”─works, what it’s for, and what makes it good.
college-writing-020148.zh: 然而，即使读者，学者们也倾向于误解公共写作——或者公众所说的，“写作”——有效，它的用途，以及什么是好的。

college-writing-020149.en: The result is both unnecessary frustration for academics making that first foray into newspapers and online outlets, and misplaced indignation among certain scholars who think their colleagues’ public essays should read just like scholarship.
college-writing-020149.zh: 结果是对首次涉足报纸和在线媒体的学者来说，这既是不必要的挫败感，也是在某些学者中错位的愤慨，他们认为他们的同事的公开论文应该读起来就像学术一样。

college-writing-020150.en: In more than a decade of writing essays and reviews for the public, both in my academic wheelhouse and outside of it, I have gathered a number of lessons that I offer here to spare other freelance writers some pain and annoyance.
college-writing-020150.zh: 在为公众撰写论文和评论的十多年中，无论是在我的学术驾驶室还是在它之外，我都在这里收集了一些课程，以免其他自由撰稿人的痛苦和烦恼。

college-writing-020151.en: My comments are specifically about the process of writing─sometimes with a contract, and preferably for pay─for editors at established print and online publications aimed at a general audience.
college-writing-020151.zh: 我的评论专门是关于写作的过程——有时是有合同的，最好是付费——在针对普通受众的既定印刷和在线出版物中编辑。

college-writing-020153.en: As a scholar, you are used to having an enormous amount of say over your writing and how it is presented.
college-writing-020153.zh: 作为一名学者，您习惯于对您的写作及其呈现方式有大量的发言权。

college-writing-020154.en: It may not always feel that way, particularly when you are responding to Reader B and revising that article for the fifth time.
college-writing-020154.zh: 它可能并不总是有这种感觉，尤其是当您响应读者 B 并第五次修改该文章时。

college-writing-020155.en: Yet the final work represents your vision.
college-writing-020155.zh: 然而，最后的作品代表了你的愿景。

college-writing-020156.en: The moment you write for general-interest outlets, however, you are subject to their editorial vision.
college-writing-020156.zh: 然而，当你为一般利益网点写作的那一刻，你就受制于他们的编辑愿景。

college-writing-020157.en: What that means in practical terms: Headlines, illustrations, and publication dates are decided for you.
college-writing-020157.zh: 这实际上意味着什么：标题、插图和出版日期是为您决定的。

college-writing-020158.en: Sometimes the headline will misrepresent the article it accompanies, or exaggerate your message to attract clicks.
college-writing-020158.zh: 有时，标题会歪曲其附带的文章，或夸大您的信息以吸引点击。

college-writing-020159.en: Readers angered by the headline tend to direct their rage at you, the writer.
college-writing-020159.zh: 被标题激怒的读者倾向于将他们的愤怒指向你，作者。

college-writing-020160.en: In some cases, you will see the draft headline during the editing process, but it can still change after that point.
college-writing-020160.zh: 在某些情况下，您会在编辑过程中看到草稿标题，但在此之后仍可能发生变化。

college-writing-020161.en: All of the above holds for art, too, which can range from subtly inaccurate to deeply offensive.
college-writing-020161.zh: 以上所有内容也适用于艺术，从巧妙的不准确到严重的冒犯性。

college-writing-020162.en: The worst headlines usually appear online, but the good news is that you can sometimes persuade the editors at online outlets to change a particularly egregious headline.
college-writing-020162.zh: 最糟糕的头条新闻通常会出现在网上，但好消息是你有时可以说服在线媒体的编辑改变一个特别令人震惊的标题。

college-writing-020163.en: Much the same goes for the publication date.

college-writing-020164.en: Unless a piece is pegged to a quickly developing news event, it’s likely to go into a publication queue and appear anywhere from weeks to months later.
college-writing-020164.zh: 除非一篇文章与快速发展的新闻事件挂钩，否则它很可能会进入出版物队列并在数周到数月后出现。

college-writing-020165.en: That can be challenging for writers impatient to see their work appear.
college-writing-020165.zh: 对于迫不及待地看到他们的作品出现的作家来说，这可能具有挑战性。

college-writing-020166.en: Even when an outlet gives you a publication date, it can be delayed without notice, either due to more pressing pieces or because the editors saved it for use with other articles on the same theme.
college-writing-020166.zh: 即使当一个分店给你一个出版日期，它也可能会在没有通知的情况下推迟，无论是因为更紧迫的作品，还是因为编辑保存了它以供与同一主题的其他文章一起使用。

college-writing-020167.en: In one case, I had a book review appear online as announced, but in print a month later.
college-writing-020167.zh: 在一个案例中，我在网上发布了一篇书评，但在一个月后出版。

college-writing-020168.en: Meanwhile, readers used to the fast publishing potential of Medium or personal blogs might wrongly assume that a newly published essay reflects your current thinking, when, in fact, it may only reflect how you viewed the matter six months ago.
college-writing-020168.zh: 同时，习惯于中媒体或个人博客的快速出版潜力的读者可能会错误地认为新发表的文章反映了您当前的想法，而事实上，它可能只反映了您在六个月前如何看待此事。

college-writing-020169.en: Just as work in scholarly journals suffers from a time lag, so does much popular writing.
college-writing-020169.zh: 正如学术期刊上的工作存在时间滞后一样，许多流行的写作也是如此。

college-writing-020170.en: Even once your essay has been published, you may be surprised to find it syndicated to other outlets or translated into foreign languages─all without your knowledge or permission.
college-writing-020170.zh: 即使您的论文发表后，您也可能会惊讶地发现它与其他渠道联合或翻译成外语——所有这些都没有您的知识或许可。

college-writing-020171.en: In some cases you will receive a permission request and a fee for the reprint, but in others you will not even be informed.
college-writing-020171.zh: 在某些情况下，您会收到许可请求和转载费用，但在其他情况下，您甚至不会被告知。

college-writing-020173.en: Before you allow your work to be published by a particular venue, ask your editor to spell out the copyright arrangement (since it’s not always clear in the outlet’s “terms and conditions”).
college-writing-020173.zh: 在您允许您的作品由特定场地出版之前，请让您的编辑说明版权安排（因为在出口的“条款和条件”中并不总是清楚）。

college-writing-020174.en: If the terms don’t include nonexclusive reprint rights, you can sometimes negotiate for that.
college-writing-020174.zh: 如果这些条款不包括非排他性重印版权，您有时可以为此进行谈判。

college-writing-020175.en: Check the publication to make sure it fits your ethics, but know that the moment you agree to sell the rights, you have limited say over how your work will be presented.
college-writing-020175.zh: 查看出版物以确保它符合您的道德规范，但要知道在您同意出售这些权利的那一刻，您对您的作品将如何呈现的发言有限。

college-writing-020177.en: Editors for general-interest publications usually like to play an active role in shaping articles, to an extent that can be bracing for scholars used to solitary writing.
college-writing-020177.zh: 一般利益出版物的编辑通常喜欢在文章的塑造中发挥积极作用，在一定程度上可以为习惯于单独写作的学者做好准备。

college-writing-020178.en: With a few exceptions, such as op-eds and literary essays, you will usually land assignments with a pitch outlining the story you plan to tell and how you will go about it.
college-writing-020178.zh: 除了一些例外，例如专栏和文学论文，您通常会通过宣传您计划讲述的故事以及您将如何进行的宣传来完成任务。

college-writing-020179.en: Most editors prefer a pitch to a draft, as it allows them input at an early stage of the work.
college-writing-020179.zh: 大多数编辑更喜欢推销而不是草稿，因为它允许他们在工作的早期阶段进行输入。

college-writing-020180.en: Once a draft is done, the fun really begins.
college-writing-020180.zh: 草稿完成后，乐趣才真正开始。

college-writing-020181.en: Some editors make only general comments or tiny changes, while others revise the text intensively.
college-writing-020181.zh: 一些编辑器只进行一般性评论或微小的更改，而另一些编辑则会对文本进行深入的修改。

college-writing-020182.en: We academics tend to be precious about our prose.
college-writing-020182.zh: 我们学者往往对我们的散文很珍贵。

college-writing-020183.en: It can be hard to receive a draft in which the editor has mercilessly slashed our darling paragraphs, rewritten our brilliant sentences, and inserted her own writing.
college-writing-020183.zh: 很难收到编辑无情地砍掉我们亲爱的段落、重写我们精彩的句子并插入自己的文字的草稿。

college-writing-020184.en: Viewing writing as a collaborative endeavor has been one of the most difficult lessons I have had to learn as a crossover writer.
college-writing-020184.zh: 将写作视为一项合作努力一直是我作为跨界作家必须学习的最困难的课程之一。

college-writing-020185.en: Once I learned not to be so prickly about what happened to my prose, however, I began to see the bright side.
college-writing-020185.zh: 然而，一旦我学会了不要对我的散文发生的事情如此挑剔，我就开始看到光明的一面。

college-writing-020186.en: If you have a hands-on editor, you can ask for advice early in the process, and worry less about providing a perfect draft─the editor will work with you to improve it.
college-writing-020186.zh: 如果您有动手编辑，您可以在此过程的早期寻求建议，而不必担心提供完美的草稿——编辑将与您一起改进它。

college-writing-020187.en: I knew I had reached a new point in my freelancing education when I received page proofs from a new publication and marveled that the editors had not changed a word.
college-writing-020187.zh: 当我收到来自新出版物的页面校样时，我知道我的自由职业教育已经达到了一个新的阶段，并惊叹编辑们没有改变一个词。

college-writing-020188.en: Later, when I compared the proofs to my original draft, I realized that every single sentence had been rewritten.
college-writing-020188.zh: 后来，当我将证明与我的原始草稿进行比较时，我意识到每一句话都被改写了。

college-writing-020190.en: Much has been written about bad academic prose, and I do not need to repeat it here.
college-writing-020190.zh: 关于糟糕的学术散文已经写了很多，我不需要在这里重复一遍。

college-writing-020191.en: Even good academic prose, however, is ill suited to a general audience.
college-writing-020191.zh: 然而，即使是好的学术散文也不适合普通观众。

college-writing-020192.en: The habits we learn in writing scholarship serve us poorly in popular writing.
college-writing-020192.zh: 我们在写作学术中学到的习惯在流行写作中对我们很有帮助。

college-writing-020193.en: Graduate school teaches us to craft our prose defensively─to ward off possible attacks from colleagues.
college-writing-020193.zh: 研究生院教我们防御性地制作散文——以抵御同事可能的攻击。

college-writing-020194.en: We shy away from strong claims, watering down every sentence with “perhaps” or “one could say.”
college-writing-020194.zh: 我们回避强烈的主张，用“也许”或“可以说”来淡化每一句话。

college-writing-020195.en: In the worst cases, we make our prose completely impenetrable, figuring that if our critics can’t understand what we’re saying, they won’t be able to tear it down.
college-writing-020195.zh: 在最坏的情况下，我们让我们的散文完全无法理解，认为如果我们的批评者无法理解我们在说什么，他们将无法将其拆除。

college-writing-020196.en: But the qualities that make scholarly writing unassailable turn off general readers.
college-writing-020196.zh: 但是使学术写作无懈可击的品质让普通读者望而却步。

college-writing-020197.en: One of our key defenses is citation, which is what makes it so unsettling to write something without footnotes─particularly if the essay is related to our research.
college-writing-020197.zh: 我们的主要防御之一是引文，这就是为什么写一些没有脚注的东西如此令人不安——特别是如果这篇文章与我们的研究有关。

college-writing-020198.en: A public-facing piece will not cite all of its sources.
college-writing-020198.zh: 面向公众的文章不会引用其所有来源。

college-writing-020199.zh: 它可能不会引用任何内容。

college-writing-020200.en: I have seen that prompt consternation among colleagues, who grumble that the foundational work of Professor X wasn’t mentioned in that (enviable) New
college-writing-020200.zh: 我在同事中看到了迅速的惊愕，他们抱怨X教授的基础工作没有被提及（令人羡慕的）新

college-writing-020201.zh: 736 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-020202.en: Yorker feature written by Professor Z. But the public does not want to read about Professor X’s contributions.
college-writing-020202.zh: Yorker 由 Z 教授撰写的专题片。但公众不想阅读 X 教授的贡献。

college-writing-020203.en: Readers of your general-interest essay don’t expect in-text citations of everything you read that went into writing it.
college-writing-020203.zh: 您的一般兴趣文章的读者不期望您阅读的所有内容中的文本引用用于撰写它。

college-writing-020205.en: Public writing has a different ethos from scholarly prose.
college-writing-020205.zh: 公共写作与学术散文有着不同的精神。

college-writing-020206.en: We write scholarship to establish our credentials in a field, to lay stake to original claims, and to build a name for ourselves in the profession.
college-writing-020206.zh: 我们写奖学金是为了在一个领域建立我们的证书，为最初的主张奠定赌注，并在这个行业中为自己树立一个名字。

college-writing-020207.en: For general-interest writing, however, you should follow Horace’s advice for poetry: Aim to instruct or delight─ideally, do both.
college-writing-020207.zh: 然而，对于一般利益写作，你应该遵循霍勒斯的诗歌建议：旨在指导或高兴——理想情况下，两者都做。

college-writing-020208.en: Tell your readers a story, and give them the basic information they need to take it in.
college-writing-020208.zh: 告诉读者一个故事，并给他们提供他们需要的基本信息。

college-writing-020209.en: Avoid jargon for the most part, but teach your readers a key term when it will help them understand your topic better.
college-writing-020209.zh: 在大多数情况下避免行话，但在帮助他们更好地理解您的主题时教您的读者一个关键术语。

college-writing-020210.en: One genre that can be confusing in this respect is book reviews.
college-writing-020210.zh: 在这方面可能令人困惑的一种类型是书评。

college-writing-020211.en: They are an easy entry point into public writing, as they draw on skills that scholars already have.
college-writing-020211.zh: 它们是公开写作的一个简单的切入点，因为它们利用了学者们已经拥有的技能。

college-writing-020212.en: But the point of writing a book review for the public is not to show how clever you are or what typos you have caught in the text.
college-writing-020212.zh: 但为公众撰写书评的目的不是为了表明您有多聪明，或者您在文本中捕捉到了什么错别字。

college-writing-020213.en: Rather, it is to help readers decide if they want to buy the book, and to offer them insights and information to enjoy even if they choose not to.
college-writing-020213.zh: 相反，它是为了帮助读者决定是否要购买这本书，并为他们提供即使他们选择不购买的见解和信息。

college-writing-020214.en: To be fair, the most useful book reviews in academic journals do that, too, in their own register, but general publications usually are more interested in the experience of the reader than in the egos of the reviewer or the author whose work is being reviewed.
college-writing-020214.zh: 公平地说，学术期刊中最有用的书评也在他们自己的名册上这样做，但一般出版物通常对读者的经验更感兴趣，而不是审稿人的自我或正在审查的作者的自我。

college-writing-020215.en: This also means that if your book is the one being reviewed in a mainstream publication, you may be dismayed to find the “review” is an independent essay using your book as a hook.
college-writing-020215.zh: 这也意味着，如果您的书是在主流出版物中审查的书，您可能会沮丧地发现“评论”是一篇独立的文章，使用您的书作为钩子。

college-writing-020218.en: Academics sometimes make the mistake of thinking that their standards do not need to be particularly high when writing for the public.
college-writing-020218.zh: 学者们有时会错误地认为他们的标准在为公众写作时不需要特别高。

college-writing-020219.en: Even though you will not be writing with the precision of scholarly prose or citing every source, you should still strive to be as accurate and careful as you would be in your scholarly publications, especially if you are drawing on your specialization.
college-writing-020219.zh: 即使您不会以学术散文的精确性或引用每个来源的方式写作，但您仍然应该努力做到像在学术出版物中一样准确和谨慎，特别是如果您正在利用您的专业化。

college-writing-020220.en: A few mainstream publications still have fact-checking departments, but, in general, assume you bear full responsibility for ensuring the truth of what you write.
college-writing-020220.zh: 一些主流出版物仍然有事实核查部门，但总的来说，假设您对确保您所写内容的真实性负有全部责任。

college-writing-020221.en: You owe the public an even higher standard of rigor than you do your colleagues, since the public is more likely to trust your credentials and has less access to your sources.
college-writing-020221.zh: 你欠公众的标准比你的同事更高，因为公众更有可能信任你的凭据，而且对你的来源的访问权限更少。

college-writing-020222.en: If you get proofs before publication, check them carefully to make sure that no inaccuracies have slipped in.
college-writing-020222.zh: 如果您在发布前获得证明，请仔细检查以确保没有任何不准确之处发生。

college-writing-020223.en: The uncomfortable reality is that─while crossover work counts for little in the way of raises or promotions in academe─it can still hurt your reputation if you do a sloppy job.
college-writing-020223.zh: 令人不安的现实是——虽然跨界工作在学术界的加薪或晋升方式中很少，但如果你做得很草率，它仍然会损害你的声誉。

college-writing-020224.en: Given all of those warnings, why write for the public at all?
college-writing-020224.zh: 鉴于所有这些警告，为什么要为公众写作？

college-writing-020225.en: There are strategic reasons, such as raising your visibility or showing the relevance of your research.
college-writing-020225.zh: 有战略原因，例如提高您的知名度或展示您的研究的相关性。

college-writing-020226.en: It is also satisfying to reach readers who are curious about your field, but do not have the training necessary to appreciate your scholarship.
college-writing-020226.zh: 吸引对您所在领域感到好奇但没有获得欣赏您的奖学金所需的培训的读者也很满意。

college-writing-020227.en: As a public scholar, you have the freedom to write about topics beyond
college-writing-020227.zh: 作为一名公共学者，您可以自由地撰写超出主题的主题

college-writing-020229.en: your area of specialization, which in turn can enrich your research and teaching.
college-writing-020229.zh: 您的专业领域，反过来又可以丰富您的研究和教学。

college-writing-020230.en: Finally, many of the qualities that make for good public essays─clarity, conviction, style─can improve your scholarly writing too.
college-writing-020230.zh: 最后，许多造作优秀公共论文的品质——清晰、信念、风格——也可以提高你的学术写作。

college-writing-020232.en: 1. The word subject in “you are subject to their editorial vision” (paragraph 6)
college-writing-020232.zh: 1. “你受其编辑愿景”中的“主语”（第 6 段）

college-writing-020238.en: 2. The word egregious in “persuade the editors at online outlets to change a

college-writing-020239.zh: 特别令人震惊的标题”（第 7 段）的意思

college-writing-020240.zh: 一。 可以容忍和次要。

college-writing-020243.zh: D. 非凡而值得注意的。

college-writing-020244.en: 3. The word pegged in “unless a piece is pegged to a quickly developing news
college-writing-020244.zh: 3. “除非一件作品与快速发展的新闻挂钩，否则

college-writing-020246.en: a. estimated to be of a certain value.
college-writing-020246.zh: 一。 估计有一定的价值。

college-writing-020247.en: b. expected to be something based on a stereotype.
college-writing-020247.zh: B. 预计是基于刻板印象的东西。

college-writing-020248.en: c. identified, labeled, classified, or assigned.
college-writing-020248.zh: c.  已识别、标记、分类或分配。

college-writing-020249.en: d. attached to a certain variable as a measure of value.
college-writing-020249.zh: D. 附加到某个变量作为值的衡量标准。

college-writing-020250.en: 4. Which of the following would be a good alternative title for the selection?
college-writing-020250.zh: 4. 以下哪一项是选择的一个很好的替代标题？

college-writing-020251.en: a. Two Different Types of Writing
college-writing-020251.zh: 一。 两种不同类型的写作

college-writing-020252.zh: B. 不同的流派，不同的规则

college-writing-020253.zh: c.  编辑如何进行修改

college-writing-020255.en: 5. Which sentence best expresses the main idea of the selection?
college-writing-020255.zh: 5. 哪句话最能表达选择的主要思想？

college-writing-020257.en: There is a place for academic writers in public writing, but the writers
college-writing-020257.zh: 公共写作中有学术作家的位置，但作家

college-writing-020258.en: need to recognize different rules and constraints.
college-writing-020258.zh: 需要识别不同的规则和约束。

college-writing-020260.en: Academic writing is more important than public writing, and
college-writing-020260.zh: 学术写作比公开写作更重要，而且

college-writing-020261.en: academic writers should not lower themselves to writing general-interest pieces.
college-writing-020261.zh: 学术作家不应该降低自己写一般利益的文章。

college-writing-020264.en: Academic writers should have control over what they write and shouldn’t
college-writing-020264.zh: 学术作家应该控制他们所写的和不应该

college-writing-020371.en: Guadalupe Quintanilla is an assistant professor at the University of Houston.
college-writing-020371.zh: Guadalupe Quintanilla 是休斯顿大学的助理教授。

college-writing-020372.en: She is president of her own communications company.
college-writing-020372.zh: 她是她自己的通信公司的总裁。

college-writing-020373.en: She trains law enforcement officers all over the country.
college-writing-020373.zh: 她在全国各地培训执法人员。

college-writing-020374.en: She was nominated to serve as the U.S. Attorney General.
college-writing-020374.zh: 她被提名担任美国司法部长。

college-writing-020375.en: She’s been a representative to the United Nations.
college-writing-020375.zh: 她一直是联合国的代表。

college-writing-020376.en: That’s a pretty impressive string of accomplishments.
college-writing-020376.zh: 这是一系列令人印象深刻的成就。

college-writing-020377.en: It’s all the more impressive when you consider this: “Lupe” Quintanilla is a first-grade dropout.
college-writing-020377.zh: 考虑到这一点，这更加令人印象深刻：“Lupe”Quintanilla 是一级辍学者。

college-writing-020378.en: Her school records state that she is retarded, that her IQ is so low she can’t learn much of anything.
college-writing-020378.zh: 她的学校记录显示，她智障，她的智商太低了，什么都学不到。

college-writing-020379.en: How did Lupe Quintanilla, “retarded” nonlearner, become Dr. Quintanilla, respected educator?
college-writing-020379.zh: “迟钝”的非学习者 Lupe Quintanilla 是如何成为受人尊敬的教育家 Quintanilla 博士的？

college-writing-020380.en: Her remarkable journey began in the town of Nogales, Mexico, just below the Arizona border.
college-writing-020380.zh: 她非凡的旅程始于墨西哥的诺加莱斯镇，就在亚利桑那州边境的下方。

college-writing-020381.en: That’s where Lupe first lived with her grandparents.
college-writing-020381.zh: 这就是卢佩第一次和她的祖父母住在一起的地方。

college-writing-020383.en: Then an uncle who had just finished medical school made her grandparents a generous offer.
college-writing-020383.zh: 然后一位刚刚完成医学院的叔叔向她的祖父母提供了慷慨的提议。

college-writing-020384.en: If they wanted to live with him, he would support the family as he began his medical practice.
college-writing-020384.zh: 如果他们想和他住在一起，他会在他开始医疗实践时支持这个家庭。

college-writing-020385.en: Lupe, her grandparents, and her uncle all moved hundreds of miles to a town in southern Mexico that didn’t even have paved roads, let alone any schools.
college-writing-020385.zh: 卢佩、她的祖父母和她的叔叔都搬到了数百英里的墨西哥南部，那里的小镇甚至没有铺路，更不用说任何学校了。

college-writing-020386.en: There, Lupe grew up helping her grandfather run his little pharmacy and her grandmother keep house.
college-writing-020386.zh: 在那里，卢佩从小就帮助她的祖父经营他的小药房和她的祖母保管处。

college-writing-020389.en: After being mistakenly labeled “retarded”* and humiliated into dropping
college-writing-020389.zh: 在被错误地标记为“迟钝”*并被羞辱地被标记为丢弃后

college-writing-020390.en: out of first grade, Lupe Quintanilla knew she wanted nothing more to
college-writing-020390.zh: 一年级的时候，Lupe Quintanilla 知道她不想再

college-writing-020392.en: Life as a wife and mother would satisfy her—
college-writing-020392.zh: 妻子和母亲的生活会满足她——

college-writing-020393.en: and it did, until she saw her own children being pushed aside as “slow
college-writing-020393.zh: 确实如此，直到她看到自己的孩子被推到一边

college-writing-020395.en: ” Driven to help them succeed, Lupe took steps that dramat-
college-writing-020395.zh: ”为了帮助他们成功，卢佩采取了戏剧性的步骤——

college-writing-020401.en: *When the professor was young, the word “retarded” was often used to label anyone who was seen as having cognitive and mental limitations.
college-writing-020401.zh: *当教授年轻时，“智障”这个词经常被用来标记任何被视为有认知和精神限制的人。

college-writing-020402.en: That word is no longer accepted as appropriate; however, in this piece, it is used to emphasize the negativity of the word.
college-writing-020402.zh: 该词不再被酌情接受； 然而，在这篇文章中，它被用来强调这个词的消极性。

college-writing-020403.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 743

college-writing-020405.en: “Oh, my grandfather was stern, authoritarian, as Mexican culture demanded, but they were also very kind to me.”
college-writing-020405.zh: “哦，我的祖父是严厉的，专制的，正如墨西哥文化所要求的那样，但他们对我也很友善。”

college-writing-020406.en: When the chores were done, her grandfather taught Lupe to read and write Spanish and do basic arithmetic.
college-writing-020406.zh: 做家务后，她的祖父教卢佩读写西班牙语和做基本的算术。

college-writing-020407.en: When Lupe was twelve, her grandfather became blind.
college-writing-020407.zh: 卢佩十二岁时，她的祖父失明了。

college-writing-020408.en: The family left Mexico and went to Brownsville, Texas, with the hope that doctors there could restore his sight.
college-writing-020408.zh: 这家人离开墨西哥，前往德克萨斯州的布朗斯维尔，希望那里的医生能够恢复他的视力。

college-writing-020409.en: Once they arrived in Brownsville, Lupe was enrolled in school.
college-writing-020409.zh: 他们到达布朗斯维尔后，卢佩就被学校注册了。

college-writing-020410.en: Although she understood no English, she was given an IQ test in that language.
college-writing-020410.zh: 虽然她不懂英语，但她接受了这种语言的智商测试。

college-writing-020411.en: Not surprisingly, she didn’t do very well.
college-writing-020411.zh: 毫不奇怪，她做得不是很好。

college-writing-020412.zh: 卢佩甚至记得她的分数。

college-writing-020413.en: “I scored a sixty-four, which classified me as seriously retarded, not even teachable,” she said.
college-writing-020413.zh: “我打了 64 分，这将我归类为严重智障，甚至无法教，”她说。

college-writing-020414.en: “I was put into first grade with a class of six-year-olds. My duties were to take the little kids to the bathroom and to cut out pictures.”
college-writing-020414.zh: “我和一班六岁的孩子一起上一年级。我的职责是带小孩去洗手间，剪下照片。”

college-writing-020415.en: The classroom activities were a total mystery to Lupe─they were all conducted in English.
college-writing-020415.zh: 课堂活动对 Lupe 来说是一个完全的谜——它们都是用英语进行的。

college-writing-020416.en: And she was humiliated by the other children, who teased her for being “so much older and so much dumber” than they were.
college-writing-020416.zh: 她被其他孩子羞辱了，他们取笑她“比他们老得多，又笨得多”。

college-writing-020417.en: After four months in first grade, an incident occurred that Lupe still does not fully understand.
college-writing-020417.zh: 一年级的四个月后，发生了卢佩仍然不完全理解的事件。

college-writing-020418.en: As she stood in the doorway of the classroom waiting to escort a little girl to the bathroom, a man approached her.
college-writing-020418.zh: 当她站在教室门口等着护送一个小女孩到浴室时，一个男人走近她。

college-writing-020419.en: He asked her, in Spanish, how to find the principal’s office.
college-writing-020419.zh: 他用西班牙语问她如何找到校长的办公室。

college-writing-020421.en: “Finally someone in this school had spoken to me with words I could understand, in the language of my soul, the language of my grandmother,” she said.
college-writing-020421.zh: “终于，这所学校的某个人用我灵魂的语言和我祖母的语言对我说话，”她说。

college-writing-020422.en: Eagerly, she answered his question in Spanish.
college-writing-020422.zh: 急切地，她用西班牙语回答了他的问题。

college-writing-020423.en: Instantly her teacher swooped down on her, grabbing her arm and scolding her.
college-writing-020423.zh: 她的老师立刻扑向她，抓住她的胳膊，骂她。

college-writing-020424.en: She pulled Lupe along to the principal’s office.
college-writing-020424.zh: 她把卢佩拉到校长办公室。

college-writing-020425.en: There, the teacher and the principal both shouted at her, obviously very angry.
college-writing-020425.zh: 在那里，老师和校长都冲她大喊，显然很生气。

college-writing-020426.en: Lupe was frightened and embarrassed, but also bewildered.
college-writing-020426.zh: 卢佩既害怕又尴尬，但也感到困惑。

college-writing-020427.en: She didn’t understand a word they were saying.
college-writing-020427.zh: 她说的一个字都听不懂。

college-writing-020428.en: “Why were they so angry? I don’t know,” said Lupe.
college-writing-020428.zh: “他们为什么这么生气？我不知道，”卢佩说。

college-writing-020429.en: “Was it because I spoke Spanish at school? Or that I spoke to the man at all? I really don’t know. All I know is how humiliated I was.”
college-writing-020429.zh: “是因为我在学校说西班牙语吗？还是我和那个人说话了？我真的不知道。我所知道的就是我有多丢人。”

college-writing-020430.en: When she got home that day, she cried miserably, begging her grandfather not to make her return to school.
college-writing-020430.zh: 那天她回到家时，她悲惨地哭了，恳求她的祖父不要让她回到学校。

college-writing-020432.en: From that time on, Lupe stayed at home, serving as her blind grandfather’s “eyes.”
college-writing-020432.zh: 从那时起，卢佩呆在家里，作为她盲人祖父的“眼睛”。

college-writing-020433.en: She was a fluent reader in Spanish, and the older man loved to have her read newspapers, poetry, and novels aloud to him for hours.
college-writing-020433.zh: 她是一个流利的西班牙语读者，年长的男人喜欢让她读报纸、诗歌和小说几个小时。

college-writing-020434.en: Lupe’s own love of reading flourished during these years.
college-writing-020434.zh: 卢佩自己对阅读的热爱在这些年里蓬勃发展。

college-writing-020435.en: Her vocabulary was enriched and her imagination fired by the novels she read─novels which she learned later were classics of Spanish literature.
college-writing-020435.zh: 她的词汇丰富了，她读到的小说激发了她的想象力——她后来学到的小说是西班牙文学的经典。

college-writing-020436.en: She read Don Quixote, the famous story of the noble, impractical knight who fought against windmills.
college-writing-020436.zh: 她读了堂吉诃德，这是一个与风车作战的高贵、不切实际的骑士的著名故事。

college-writing-020437.en: She read thrilling accounts of the Mexican revolution.
college-writing-020437.zh: 她读了关于墨西哥革命的惊险报道。

college-writing-020438.en: She read La Prensa, the local Spanish-language paper, and Selecciones, the Spanish-language version of Reader’s Digest.
college-writing-020438.zh: 她阅读了当地的西班牙语论文 La Prensa 和 Selecciones，这是读者文摘的西班牙语版本。

college-writing-020439.en: When she was just sixteen, Lupe married a young Mexican-American dental technician.
college-writing-020439.zh: 在她 16 岁的时候，Lupe 嫁给了一位年轻的墨西哥裔美国牙科技师。

college-writing-020440.en: Within five years, she had given birth to her three children, Victor, Mario, and Martha.
college-writing-020440.zh: 五年之内，她生下了她的三个孩子，维克多、马里奥和玛莎。

college-writing-020441.en: Lupe’s grandparents lived with the young family.
college-writing-020441.zh: 卢佩的祖父母和这个年轻的家庭住在一起。

college-writing-020442.en: Lupe was quite happy with her life.
college-writing-020442.zh: 卢佩对她的生活非常满意。

college-writing-020443.en: “I cooked, sewed, cleaned, and cared for everybody,”
college-writing-020443.zh: “我做饭、缝纫、清洁和照顾每个人，”

college-writing-020444.zh: 744 第 5 部分 作家的读物

college-writing-020446.en: “I listened to my grandmother when she told me what made a good wife. In the morning I would actually put on my husband’s shoes and tie the laces─anything to make his life easier. Living with my grandparents for so long, I was one generation behind in my ideas of what a woman could do and be.”
college-writing-020446.zh: “当我的祖母告诉我什么造就了一个好妻子时，我听了她的声音。早上我真的会穿上我丈夫的鞋子，系好鞋带……任何能让他的生活更轻松的东西……和我的祖父母一起生活这么久，我的想法落后了一代人 女人可以做和成为。”

college-writing-020447.en: Lupe’s contentment ended when her children started school.
college-writing-020447.zh: 当她的孩子们开始上学时，卢佩的满足感就结束了。

college-writing-020448.en: When they brought home their report cards, she struggled to understand them.
college-writing-020448.zh: 当他们把成绩单带回家时，她很难理解它们。

college-writing-020449.en: She could read enough English to know that what they said was not good.
college-writing-020449.zh: 她可以读到足够多的英语，知道他们说的不好。

college-writing-020450.en: Her children had been put into a group called “Yellow Birds.”
college-writing-020450.zh: 她的孩子们被分成了一个叫做“黄鸟”的团体。

college-writing-020451.en: It was a group for slow learners.
college-writing-020451.zh: 这是一个适合缓慢学习者的团体。

college-writing-020452.en: At night in bed, Lupe cried and blamed herself.
college-writing-020452.zh: 晚上在床上，卢佩哭着责备自己。

college-writing-020453.en: It was obvious─not only was she retarded, but her children had taken after her.
college-writing-020453.zh: 很明显——她不仅被智障了，而且她的孩子们已经追上了她。

college-writing-020454.en: Now they, too, would never be able to learn like other children.
college-writing-020454.zh: 现在他们也永远无法像其他孩子一样学习。

college-writing-020455.en: But in time, a thought began to break through Lupe’s despair: Her children didn’t seem like slow learners to her.
college-writing-020455.zh: 但随着时间的推移，一个想法开始打破了卢佩的绝望：她的孩子对她来说似乎不像是慢学者。

college-writing-020456.en: At home, they learned everything she taught them, quickly and easily.
college-writing-020456.zh: 在家里，他们快速轻松地学到了她教给他们的一切。

college-writing-020457.en: She read to them constantly, from the books that she herself had loved as a child.
college-writing-020457.zh: 她不断地读给他们听，她自己小时候喜欢的书。

college-writing-020458.en: Aesop’s Fables and stories from 1,001 Arabian Nights were family favorites.
college-writing-020458.zh: 伊索的寓言和 1,001 个阿拉伯之夜的故事是家庭的最爱。

college-writing-020459.en: The children filled the house with the sounds of the songs, prayers, games, and rhymes they had learned from their parents and grandparents.
college-writing-020459.zh: 孩子们从他们的父母和祖父母那里学到的歌曲、祈祷、游戏和押韵的声音充满了房子。

college-writing-020460.en: They were smart children, eager to learn.
college-writing-020460.zh: 他们是聪明的孩子，渴望学习。

college-writing-020461.zh: 他们很快学会了西班牙语。

college-writing-020462.en: A radical idea began to form in Lupe’s mind.
college-writing-020462.zh: 卢佩的脑海中开始形成一个激进的想法。

college-writing-020463.en: Maybe the school was wrong about her children.
college-writing-020463.zh: 也许学校对她的孩子是错误的。

college-writing-020464.en: And if the school system could be wrong about her children─maybe it had been wrong about her, too.
college-writing-020464.zh: 如果学校系统可能对她的孩子有误——也许她也错了。

college-writing-020465.en: Lupe visited her children’s school, a daring action for her.
college-writing-020465.zh: Lupe 参观了她孩子的学校，这对她来说是一个大胆的行动。

college-writing-020466.en: “Many Hispanic parents would not dream of going to the classroom,” she said.
college-writing-020466.zh: “许多西班牙裔父母不会梦想去教室，”她说。

college-writing-020467.en: “In Hispanic culture, the teacher is regarded as a third parent, as an ultimate authority. To question her would seem most disrespectful, as though you were saying that she didn’t know her job.”
college-writing-020467.zh: “在西班牙文化中，老师被认为是第三位家长，是终极权威。质疑她似乎是最不尊重的，就好像你说她不知道自己的工作。”

college-writing-020468.en: That was one reason Lupe’s grandparents had not interfered when Lupe was classified as retarded.
college-writing-020468.zh: 这是卢佩的祖父母在卢佩被归类为智障时没有干涉的原因之一。

college-writing-020469.en: “Anglo teachers often misunderstand Hispanic parents, believing that they aren’t concerned about their children’s education because they don’t come visit the schools,” Lupe said.
college-writing-020469.zh: “Anglo 教师经常误解西班牙裔父母，认为他们不关心孩子的教育，因为他们不来参观这些学校，”Lupe 说。

college-writing-020470.en: “It’s not a lack of concern at all. It’s a mark of respect for the teacher’s authority.”
college-writing-020470.zh: “这根本不是缺乏担忧。这是对教师权威的尊重的标志。”

college-writing-020471.en: At her children’s school, Lupe spoke to three different teachers.
college-writing-020471.zh: 在她孩子的学校，Lupe 与三位不同的老师进行了交谈。

college-writing-020472.en: Two of them told her the same thing: “Your children are just slow. Sorry, but they can’t learn.”
college-writing-020472.zh: 其中两个告诉她同样的事情：“你的孩子很慢。对不起，但他们不能学习。”

college-writing-020473.en: A third offered a glimmer of hope.
college-writing-020473.zh: 三分之一提供了一丝希望。

college-writing-020474.en: He said, “They don’t know how to function in English. It’s possible that if you spoke English at home they would be able to do better.”
college-writing-020474.zh: 他说：“他们不知道如何用英语运作。如果你在家说英语，他们可能会做得更好。”

college-writing-020476.en: “Where can I learn English?” she asked.
college-writing-020476.zh: “我在哪里可以学英语？” 她问。

college-writing-020478.en: At that time there were no local English-language programs for adults.
college-writing-020478.zh: 当时没有当地的成人英语课程。

college-writing-020479.en: Finally he suggested that Lupe visit the local high school.
college-writing-020479.zh: 最后他建议卢佩去当地的高中。

college-writing-020480.en: Maybe she would be permitted to sit in the back of a classroom and pick up some English that way.
college-writing-020480.zh: 也许她会被允许坐在教室的后面，这样学习一些英语。

college-writing-020481.en: Lupe made an appointment with a counselor at the high school.
college-writing-020481.zh: Lupe 与高中的一名辅导员预约。

college-writing-020482.en: But when the two women met, the counselor shook her head.
college-writing-020482.zh: 但当两个女人见面时，辅导员摇了摇头。

college-writing-020483.en: “Your test scores show that you are retarded,” she told Lupe.
college-writing-020483.zh: “你的考试成绩表明你是智障，”她告诉 Lupe。

college-writing-020484.en: “You’d just be taking space in the classroom away from someone who could learn.”
college-writing-020484.zh: “你只是在教室里从一个可以学习的人身上腾出空间。”

college-writing-020485.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 745

college-writing-020486.en: Lupe’s next stop was the hospital where she had served for years as a volunteer.
college-writing-020486.zh: Lupe 的下一站是她多年来一直担任志愿者的医院。

college-writing-020487.en: Could she sit in on some of the nursing classes held there?
college-writing-020487.zh: 她可以参加那里举行的一些护理课程吗？

college-writing-020488.en: No, she was told, not without a diploma.
college-writing-020488.zh: 不，她被告知，并非没有文凭。

college-writing-020489.en: Still undeterred, she went on to Texas Southmost College in Brownsville.
college-writing-020489.zh: 仍然没有被吓倒，她去了布朗斯维尔的德克萨斯州最南端学院。

college-writing-020490.en: Could she sit in on a class?

college-writing-020491.zh: 没有； 没有高中文凭。

college-writing-020492.en: Finally she went to the telephone company, where she knew operators were being trained.
college-writing-020492.zh: 最后她去了电话公司，在那里她知道接线员正在接受培训。

college-writing-020493.en: Could she listen in on the classes?

college-writing-020494.en: No, only high-school graduates were permitted.

college-writing-020495.en: That day, leaving the telephone company, Lupe felt she had hit bottom.
college-writing-020495.zh: 那天，离开电话公司，卢佩觉得她已经触底了。

college-writing-020496.en: She had been terrified in the first place to try to find an English class.
college-writing-020496.zh: 她一开始就害怕找到英语课。

college-writing-020497.en: Meeting with rejection after rejection nearly destroyed what little self-confidence she had.
college-writing-020497.zh: 一次又一次的拒绝几乎摧毁了她所拥有的一点自信。

college-writing-020498.en: She walked home in the rain, crying.

college-writing-020499.en: “I felt like a big barrier had fallen across my path,” she said.
college-writing-020499.zh: “我觉得我的道路上像一道大障碍物倒下了，”她说。

college-writing-020500.en: “I couldn’t go over it; I couldn’t go under it; I couldn’t go around it.”
college-writing-020500.zh: “我无法越过它；我无法进入它下面；我无法绕过它。”

college-writing-020501.en: But the next day Lupe woke with fresh determination.
college-writing-020501.zh: 但第二天，卢佩带着新的决心醒来。

college-writing-020502.en: “I was motivated by love of my kids,” she said.
college-writing-020502.zh: “我被孩子们的爱所激励，”她说。

college-writing-020504.en: She got up; made breakfast for her kids, husband, and grandparents; saw her children and husband off for the day; and started out again.
college-writing-020504.zh: 她起身； 为她的孩子、丈夫和祖父母做了早餐； 为她的孩子和丈夫送去了一天； 并重新开始。

college-writing-020505.en: “I remember walking to the bus stop, past a dog that always scared me to death, and heading back to the college. The lady I spoke to said, ‘I told you, we can’t do anything for you without a high-school degree.’ But as I left the building, I went up to the first Spanish-speaking student I saw. His name was Gabito. I said, ‘Who really makes the decisions around here?’ He said, ‘The registrar.’”
college-writing-020505.zh: “我记得走到公交车站，经过一只总是把我吓死的狗，然后回到学院。与我交谈过的那位女士说，‘我告诉过你，没有高中学位，我们什么都做不了。’但当我离开大楼时，我走到了第一个 我看到的是西班牙语的学生。

college-writing-020506.en: Since she hadn’t had any luck in the office building, Lupe decided to take a more direct approach.
college-writing-020506.zh: 由于她在办公楼里没有任何运气，所以卢佩决定采取更直接的方法。

college-writing-020507.en: She asked Gabito to point out the registrar’s car in the parking lot.
college-writing-020507.zh: 她让加比托在停车场指出登记员的车。

college-writing-020508.en: For the next two hours she waited beside it until its owner showed up.
college-writing-020508.zh: 在接下来的两个小时里，她一直在它旁边等到它的主人出现。

college-writing-020509.en: Impressed by Lupe’s persistence, the registrar listened to her story.
college-writing-020509.zh: Lupe 的毅力给人留下了深刻的印象，注册商听了她的故事。

college-writing-020510.en: But instead of giving her permission to sit in on a class and learn more English, he insisted that she sign up for a full college load.
college-writing-020510.zh: 但他没有允许她允许她参加课堂学习更多的英语，而是坚持要求她报名参加大学的全部工作。

college-writing-020511.en: Before she knew it, she was enrolled in four classes: basic math, basic English, psychology, and typing.
college-writing-020511.zh: 在她知道之前，她就读了四门课：基础数学、英语基础、心理学和打字。

college-writing-020512.en: The registrar’s parting words to her were, “Don’t come back if you don’t make it through.”
college-writing-020512.zh: 登记员对她说的离别的话是：“如果你没有通过，就不要回来。”

college-writing-020513.en: With that “encouragement,” Lupe began a semester that was part nightmare, part dream come true.
college-writing-020513.zh: 带着“鼓励”，卢佩开始了一个学期，这一部分是噩梦，一部分是梦想成真。

college-writing-020514.en: Every day she got her husband and children off to school, took the bus to campus, came home to make lunch for her husband and grandparents, went back to campus, and was home in time to greet Victor, Mario, and Martha when they got home from school.
college-writing-020514.zh: 每天她让丈夫和孩子上学，乘公共汽车去校园，回家为丈夫和祖父母做午餐，回到校园，回到校园，及时回家迎接维克多、马里奥和玛莎放学回家。

college-writing-020515.en: In the evenings she cooked, cleaned, did laundry, and got the children to bed.
college-writing-020515.zh: 晚上她做饭、打扫卫生、洗衣服，让孩子们上床睡觉。

college-writing-020516.en: Then she would study, often until three in the morning.
college-writing-020516.zh: 然后她会学习，经常到凌晨三点。

college-writing-020517.en: “Sometimes in class I would feel sick with the stress of it,” she said.
college-writing-020517.zh: “有时在课堂上我会因为压力而感到恶心，”她说。

college-writing-020518.en: “I’d go to the bathroom and talk to myself in the mirror. Sometimes I’d say, ‘What are you doing here? Why don’t you go home and watch I Love Lucy?’”
college-writing-020518.zh: “我会去洗手间，对着镜子自言自语。有时我会说，‘你在这里做什么？你为什么不回家看我爱露西？’”

college-writing-020520.en: Instead, she studied furiously, using her Spanish-English dictionary, constantly making lists of new words she wanted to understand.
college-writing-020520.zh: 相反，她用她的西班牙语-英语词典疯狂地学习，不断列出她想理解的新单词。

college-writing-020521.en: “I still do that today,” she said.

college-writing-020522.en: “When I come across a word I don’t

college-writing-020523.zh: 746 第 5 部分 作家的阅读

college-writing-020524.en: know, I write it down, look it up, and write sentences using it until I own that word.
college-writing-020524.zh: 知道，我把它写下来，查一下，用它写句子，直到我拥有那个词。

college-writing-020525.en: Although so much of the language and subject matter was new to Lupe, one part of the college experience was not.
college-writing-020525.zh: 尽管很多语言和主题对 Lupe 来说都是新的，但大学经历的一部分不是。

college-writing-020526.en: That was the key skill of reading, a skill Lupe possessed.
college-writing-020526.zh: 那是阅读的关键技能，是卢佩拥有的技能。

college-writing-020527.en: As she struggled with English, she found the reading speed, comprehension, and vocabulary that she had developed in Spanish carrying over into her new language.
college-writing-020527.zh: 当她在英语中挣扎时，她发现了她在西班牙语中发展起来的阅读速度、理解力和词汇量，延续到她的新语言中。

college-writing-020528.en: “Reading,” she said, “reading was the vehicle. Although I didn’t know it at the time, when I was a girl learning to love to read, I was laying the foundation for academic success.”
college-writing-020528.zh: “读书，”她说，“读书是载体。当时我不知道，当我还是个学着爱读书的女孩时，我正在为学业成功奠定基础。”

college-writing-020529.en: She gives credit, too, to her Hispanic fellow students.
college-writing-020529.zh: 她也赞扬她的西班牙裔同学。

college-writing-020530.en: “At first, they didn’t know what to make of me. They were eighteen years old, and at that time it was very unfashionable for an older person to be in college. But once they decided I wasn’t a ‘plant’ from the administration, they were my greatest help.”
college-writing-020530.zh: “起初，他们不知道该怎么看我。他们已经十八岁了，当时一个年长的人上大学是非常不合时宜的。但一旦他们决定我不是政府的‘植物’，他们就是我最大的帮助。”

college-writing-020531.en: The younger students spent hours helping Lupe, explaining unfamiliar words and terms, coaching her, and answering her questions.
college-writing-020531.zh: 年轻的学生花了几个小时帮助 Lupe，解释不熟悉的单词和术语，指导她，回答她的问题。

college-writing-020532.en: That first semester passed in a fog of exhaustion.
college-writing-020532.zh: 第一学期在疲惫的迷雾中过去了。

college-writing-020533.en: Many mornings Lupe doubted she could get out of bed, much less care for her family and tackle her classes.
college-writing-020533.zh: 许多早晨，Lupe 怀疑她能否起床，更不用说照顾她的家人并解决她的课程了。

college-writing-020534.en: But when she thought of her children and what was at stake for them, she forced herself on.
college-writing-020534.zh: 但当她想到她的孩子以及对他们来说危在旦夕的事情时，她强迫自己继续前进。

college-writing-020535.en: She remembers well what those days were like.
college-writing-020535.zh: 她清楚地记得那些日子是什么样的。

college-writing-020536.en: “Just a day at a time. That was all I could think about. I could make myself get up one more day, study one more day, cook and clean one more day. And those days eventually turned into a semester.”
college-writing-020536.zh: “一次一天。这就是我能想到的。我可以让自己再起床一天，再学习一天，再做饭，再打扫一天。那些日子最终变成了一个学期。”

college-writing-020537.en: To her own amazement perhaps as much as anyone’s, Lupe discovered that she was far from retarded.
college-writing-020537.zh: 令她惊奇的是，卢佩可能和任何人一样，发现她远非迟钝。

college-writing-020538.en: Although she sweated blood over many assignments, she completed them.
college-writing-020538.zh: 尽管她在许多任务中流血，但她完成了。

college-writing-020539.en: She turned them in on time.

college-writing-020540.en: And, remarkably, she made the dean’s list her very first semester.
college-writing-020540.zh: 而且，值得注意的是，她在第一学期就将院长名单列为她的名单。

college-writing-020541.en: After that, there was no stopping Lupe Quintanilla.
college-writing-020541.zh: 在那之后，没有停止 Lupe Quintanilla。

college-writing-020542.en: She soon realized that the associate’s degree offered by Texas Southmost College would not satisfy her.
college-writing-020542.zh: 她很快意识到德克萨斯州最南端学院提供的副学士学位不会让她满意。

college-writing-020543.en: Continuing her Monday, Wednesday, and Friday schedule at Southmost, she enrolled for Tuesday and Thursday courses at Pan American University, a school 140 miles from Brownsville.
college-writing-020543.zh: 继续她在最南端的周一、周三和周五日程安排，她在距离布朗斯维尔 140 英里的学校泛美大学参加了周二和周四的课程。

college-writing-020544.en: Within three years, she had earned both her junior college degree and a bachelor’s degree in biology.
college-writing-020544.zh: 三年之内，她获得了大专学位和生物学学士学位。

college-writing-020545.en: She then won a fellowship that took her to graduate school at the University of Houston, where she earned a master’s degree in Spanish literature.
college-writing-020545.zh: 然后，她获得了休斯顿大学研究生院的奖学金，在那里她获得了西班牙文学硕士学位。

college-writing-020546.en: When she graduated, the university offered her a job as director of the Mexican-American studies program.
college-writing-020546.zh: 当她毕业时，该大学为她提供了一份墨西哥裔美国人研究项目主任的工作。

college-writing-020547.en: While in that position, she earned a doctoral degree in education.
college-writing-020547.zh: 在担任该职位期间，她获得了教育博士学位。

college-writing-020548.en: How did she do it all?

college-writing-020550.en: “I hardly know. When I think back to those years, it seems like a life that someone else lived.”
college-writing-020550.zh: “我几乎不知道。回想起那些年，这似乎是别人的生活。”

college-writing-020551.en: It was a rich and exciting but also very challenging period for Lupe and her family.
college-writing-020551.zh: 对于 Lupe 和她的家人来说，这是一个丰富而令人兴奋但也非常具有挑战性的时期。

college-writing-020552.en: On the one hand, Lupe was motivated by the desire to set an example for her children, to prove to them that they could succeed in the English-speaking academic world.
college-writing-020552.zh: 一方面，Lupe 的动机是为她的孩子树立榜样，向他们证明他们可以在说英语的学术界取得成功。

college-writing-020553.en: On the other hand, she worried about neglecting her family.
college-writing-020553.zh: 另一方面，她担心忽视家人。

college-writing-020554.en: She tried hard to attend important activities, such as parents’ meetings at school and her children’s sporting events.
college-writing-020554.zh: 她努力参加重要的活动，例如学校的家长会议和孩子的体育赛事。

college-writing-020555.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 747

college-writing-020556.en: But things didn’t always work out.
college-writing-020556.zh: 但事情并不总是成功的。

college-writing-020557.en: Lupe still remembers attending a baseball game that her older son, Victor, was playing in.
college-writing-020557.zh: Lupe 仍然记得参加过她的大儿子 Victor 正在参加的一场棒球比赛。

college-writing-020558.en: When Victor came to bat, he hit a home run.
college-writing-020558.zh: 当维克多来击球时，他击出了本垒打。

college-writing-020559.en: But as the crowd cheered and Victor glanced proudly over at his mother in the stands, he saw she was studying a textbook.
college-writing-020559.zh: 但当人群欢呼起来，维克多自豪地瞥了一眼看台上的母亲时，他看到她正在学习一本教科书。

college-writing-020560.en: “I hadn’t seen the home run,” Lupe admitted.
college-writing-020560.zh: “我没有看到本垒打，”卢佩承认。

college-writing-020561.en: “That sort of thing was hard for everyone to take.”
college-writing-020561.zh: “这种事情对每个人来说都很难接受。”

college-writing-020562.en: Although Lupe worried that her children would resent her busy schedule, she also saw her success reflected in them as they blossomed in school.
college-writing-020562.zh: 虽然卢佩担心她的孩子会怨恨她繁忙的日程，但她也看到她的成功反映在他们在学校开花的时候。

college-writing-020563.en: She forced herself to speak English at home, and their language skills improved quickly.
college-writing-020563.zh: 她强迫自己在家说英语，他们的语言能力很快提高了。

college-writing-020564.en: She read to them in English instead of Spanish─gulping down her pride as their pronunciation became better than hers and they began correcting her.
college-writing-020564.zh: 她用英语读给他们听，而不是西班牙语——因为他们的发音变得比她的好，他们开始纠正她，低下了她的骄傲。

college-writing-020565.en: (Once the children were in high school and fluent in English, Lupe switched back to Spanish at home, so that the children would be fully comfortable in both languages.) “I saw the change in them almost immediately,” she said.
college-writing-020565.zh: （一旦孩子们上了高中并且流利了英语，Lupe 在家中改回西班牙语，这样孩子们就可以完全适应两种语言。）“我几乎立即看到了他们的变化，”她说。

college-writing-020566.en: “After I helped them with their homework, they would see me pulling out my own books and going to work. In the morning, I would show them the papers I had written. As I gained confidence, so did they.”
college-writing-020566.zh: “在我帮他们做作业后，他们会看到我拿出自己的书去上班。早上，我会向他们展示我写的文件。当我获得信心时，他们也一样。”

college-writing-020567.en: By the next year, the children had been promoted out of the Yellow Birds.
college-writing-020567.zh: 到第二年，孩子们已经从黄色的鸟类中升职了。

college-writing-020568.en: Even though Victor, Mario, and Martha all did well academically, Lupe realized she could not assume that they would face no more obstacles in school.
college-writing-020568.zh: 尽管维克多、马里奥和玛莎在学业上都表现出色，但卢佩意识到她不能假设他们不会在学校面临更多的障碍。

college-writing-020569.en: When Mario was in high school, for instance, he wanted to sign up for a debate class.
college-writing-020569.zh: 例如，当马里奥上高中时，他想报名参加辩论课。

college-writing-020570.en: Instead, he was assigned to woodworking.

college-writing-020571.en: She visited the school to ask why.

college-writing-020572.en: Mario’s teacher told her, “He’s good with his hands. He’ll be a great carpenter, and that’s a good thing for a Mexican to be.”
college-writing-020572.zh: 马里奥的老师告诉她：“他的手很好。他会成为一个伟大的木匠，这对墨西哥人来说是件好事。”

college-writing-020573.en: Controlling her temper, Lupe responded, “I’m glad you think he’s good with his hands. He’ll be a great physician someday, and he is going to be in the debate class.”
college-writing-020573.zh: 卢佩控制着她的脾气，回答说：“我很高兴你认为他的手很好。他总有一天会成为一名出色的医生，他将参加辩论课。”

college-writing-020574.en: Today, Lupe Quintanilla teaches at the University of Houston, where she has developed several dozen courses concerning Hispanic literature and culture.
college-writing-020574.zh: 今天，Lupe Quintanilla 在休斯顿大学任教，在那里她开发了几十门关于西班牙语文学和文化的课程。

college-writing-020575.en: Her cross-cultural training for law enforcement officers, which helps bring police and firefighters and local Hispanic communities closer together, is renowned throughout the country.
college-writing-020575.zh: 她对执法人员的跨文化培训，帮助警察和消防员以及当地的西班牙裔社区更紧密地联系在一起，在全国享有盛誉。

college-writing-020576.en: Former President Ronald Reagan named her to a national board that keeps the White House informed of new programs in law enforcement.
college-writing-020576.zh: 前总统罗纳德·里根将她任命为国家委员会，该委员会让白宫了解执法部门的新计划。

college-writing-020577.en: She has received numerous awards for teaching excellence, and there is even a scholarship named in her honor.
college-writing-020577.zh: 她因卓越教学而获得无数奖项，甚至还有一项以她的荣誉命名的奖学金。

college-writing-020578.en: Her name appears in the Hispanic Hall of Fame, and she has been co-chair of the White House Commission on Hispanic Education.
college-writing-020578.zh: 她的名字出现在西班牙裔名人堂中，她一直是白宫西班牙教育委员会的联合主席。

college-writing-020579.en: The love of reading that her grandfather instilled in Lupe is still alive.
college-writing-020579.zh: 她的祖父灌输给卢佩的阅读爱情仍然活着。

college-writing-020580.en: She thinks of him every year when she introduces to her students one of his favorite poets, Amado Nervo.
college-writing-020580.zh: 当她向她的学生介绍他最喜欢的诗人之一阿马多·内尔沃时，她每年都会想起他。

college-writing-020581.en: She requires them to memorize these lines from one of Nervo’s poems: “When I got to the end of my long journey in life, I realized that I was the architect of my own destiny.”
college-writing-020581.zh: 她要求他们从内尔沃的一首诗中记住这些台词：

college-writing-020582.en: Of these lines, Lupe says, “That is something that I deeply believe, and I want my students to learn it before the end of their long journey. We create our own destiny.”
college-writing-020582.zh: 卢佩说：“这是我深信的东西，我希望我的学生在漫长的旅程结束之前学习它。我们创造了自己的命运。”

college-writing-020583.en: Her love of reading and learning has helped Lupe create a distinguished destiny.
college-writing-020583.zh: 她对阅读和学习的热爱帮助卢佩创造了一个杰出的命运。

college-writing-020584.en: But none of the honors she has received means more to her than the success
college-writing-020584.zh: 但她所获得的荣誉对她来说没有比成功更重要的了

college-writing-020701.en: Write an essay that takes as its thesis one of the following statements:

college-writing-020708.en: Choose a person you know who, in your opinion, has done a fine job of taking charge of their own destiny.
college-writing-020708.zh: 选择一个你认识的人，在你看来，他在掌控自己的命运方面做得很好。

college-writing-020709.en: Write an essay about this person.
college-writing-020709.zh: 写一篇关于这个人的文章。

college-writing-020710.en: You might describe three areas of life in which the person has taken control.
college-writing-020710.zh: 您可以描述该人已经控制的生活的三个领域。

college-writing-020711.en: Alternatively, you might narrate three incidents from the person’s life that illustrate their admirable self-determination.
college-writing-020711.zh: 或者，您可能会讲述该人生活中的三件事，这些事件说明了他们令人钦佩的自决。

college-writing-020713.en: Lupe had to struggle in order to balance her school responsibilities with her duties as a wife and mother.

college-writing-020714.zh: 写一篇文章，在其中确定您需要兼顾作为学生的生活的各个方面。

college-writing-020715.zh: 它们可能包括工作、配偶或重要其他人、孩子、家政职责、宠物、课外活动、困难的生活环境或其他任何对您的学业构成挑战的事情。

college-writing-020716.zh: 提供生动的、现实生活中的说明，说明这些责任中的每一个有时与您的学习相冲突。

college-writing-020719.en: There are two stages in a name for people of color.
college-writing-020719.zh: 有色人种的名字有两个阶段。

college-writing-020720.en: First, it begins when you change your name to fit the mouths of others.
college-writing-020720.zh: 首先，当您更改姓名以适应他人的嘴巴时，它就开始了。

college-writing-020721.en: It’s easier to let people pronounce your name the way they want to instead of the immigrant dialect it’s supposed to be said in.
college-writing-020721.zh: 让人们以他们想要的方式表达你的名字更容易，而不是它应该说的移民方言。

college-writing-020722.en: It’s easier, simpler and it allows you to shed a bit of your identity to fit in.
college-writing-020722.zh: 它更容易、更简单，它可以让你摆脱一些你的身份以适应。

college-writing-020723.en: You may not look like everyone, but simplifying your name will make you stand out less.
college-writing-020723.zh: 你可能看起来不像每个人，但简化你的名字会让你脱颖而出。

college-writing-020724.en: The second stage comes years later.

college-writing-020725.en: When you’ve grown a little and you understand the power of names, the importance of the culture and heritage you were given.
college-writing-020725.zh: 当你成长了一点，你了解名字的力量，你被赋予的文化和遗产的重要性。

college-writing-020726.zh: 你的名字就是你的身份。

college-writing-020727.en: It encompasses who you are, so why would you change that to make it easier for someone else?
college-writing-020727.zh: 它包括你是谁，那么你为什么要改变它以使别人更容易呢？

college-writing-020729.en: So when Republican Sen. David Perdue mocked Senator and Vice Presidential nominee Kamala Harris’s name by saying “Ka-MAL-a, Ka-MAL-a or Kamala, Kamala, Ka-mala, -mala, -mala, I don’t know, whatever,” at a rally in Georgia, not only was it disrespectful to a highly qualified colleague, but it also brought up a conversation about how people of color have faced years of microaggressive behavior for simply having names.
college-writing-020729.zh: 因此，当共和党参议员大卫·珀杜（David Perdue）嘲笑参议员和副总统候选人卡马拉·哈里斯（Kamala Harris）的名字时说：“Ka-mal-a、Ka-mal-a 或 Kamala、Kamala、Ka-mala、-mala、-mala，我不知道， 无论如何，”在佐治亚州的一次集会上，这不仅对高素质的同事不尊重，而且还引发了一场关于有色人种如何因简单地拥有名字而面临微观攻击行为的对话。

college-writing-020730.en: His team later stated that Perdue “simply mispronounced” Harris’s name and it “didn’t mean anything.”
college-writing-020730.zh: 他的团队后来表示，Perdue“简单地误读了”哈里斯的名字，“没有任何意义”。

college-writing-020731.en: Harris and Perdue have served in the Senate for three
college-writing-020731.zh: 哈里斯和珀杜曾在参议院任职三人

college-writing-020732.en: Duaa Israr graduated in 2021 from DePaul University in Illinois, where
college-writing-020732.zh: Duaa Israr于2021年毕业于伊利诺伊州的德保罗大学

college-writing-020733.en: she double-majored in journalism and political science.
college-writing-020733.zh: 她在新闻和政治学方面拥有双学位。

college-writing-020735.en: that she wrote for her college newspaper, Israr explores the impor-
college-writing-020735.zh: 她为她的大学报纸写的，Israr 探索了

college-writing-020736.en: tance of a person’s name and the significance of its proper
college-writing-020736.zh: 一个人的名字及其正确的意义

college-writing-020738.en: Purposefully Mispronouncing Kamala Harris’s Name Is Racist, Plain and Simple
college-writing-020738.zh: 故意误读卡马拉哈里斯的名字是种族主义、简单明了

college-writing-020742.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 753

college-writing-020743.en: years together and they serve on the budget committee.
college-writing-020743.zh: 一起多年，他们在预算委员会任职。

college-writing-020744.en: It wasn’t a simple mistake when you’ve known a person for multiple years, it was willfully ignorant.
college-writing-020744.zh: 当你认识一个人多年时，这不是一个简单的错误，它是故意无知的。

college-writing-020745.en: “The first time someone mispronounces a name, there’s a pass. Maybe they’re unfamiliar with the name or they sincerely can’t pronounce it, that’s one thing. But when someone mispronounces it consistently because they don’t want to bother, it’s highly problematic, demeaning, personal and intolerable,” said DePaul Professor of Political Science Christina Rivers.
college-writing-020745.zh: “第一次有人说出一个名字，有一个通行证。也许他们不熟悉这个名字，或者他们真诚地说不出来，这是一回事。但是当有人因为不想打扰而始终误读它时， 这是高度成问题的、贬低的、个人的和无法忍受的，”德保罗政治学教授克里斯蒂娜·里弗斯说。

college-writing-020746.zh: 说白了，珀杜是种族主义者。

college-writing-020747.en: The mispronunciation of a name is not a minuscule topic that can be brushed off as an honest mistake.
college-writing-020747.zh: 一个名字的错误发音不是一个微不足道的话题，可以被认为是一个诚实的错误。

college-writing-020748.en: Not for people who have been brushed off their entire lives.
college-writing-020748.zh: 不适合那些一生都被剥夺的人。

college-writing-020749.en: For people of color, our names prevent us from getting interviews, let alone offers, jobs and promotions.
college-writing-020749.zh: 对于有色人种，我们的名字阻止我们接受采访，更不用说提供、工作和晋升了。

college-writing-020750.en: The concept that our names are not “white-sounding” is just another obstacle that places us behind our white counterparts.
college-writing-020750.zh: 我们的名字不是“听起来白人”的概念只是让我们落后于白人同行的另一个障碍。

college-writing-020751.en: This isn’t the first incident of Harris’s name being mocked.
college-writing-020751.zh: 这不是哈里斯的名字被嘲笑的第一起事件。

college-writing-020752.en: When Harris was announced as Joe Biden’s running mate, Fox News Host Tucker Carlson proceeded to mispronounce Harris’s name multiple times until Democratic political consultant Richard Goodstein corrected Carlson, calling the action “the bare minimum.”
college-writing-020752.zh: 当哈里斯被宣布为乔·拜登的竞选伙伴时，福克斯新闻的主持人塔克·卡尔森多次误读哈里斯的名字，直到民主党政治顾问理查德·古德斯坦更正了卡尔森，称这项行动是“最低限度的”。

college-writing-020753.en: Carlson responded with “so what?” “To me, this indicates his disrespect for the Senator who might be the VP of the country. Not only that, but I do think that it’s an indicator that to him, everything including people’s identity must be modified to fit his heritage, the way he speaks. It’s not like her name has a letter or a combination of letters that are difficult to articulate,” said DePaul Islamic Studies professor Ahmed Hashim.
college-writing-020753.zh: 卡尔森回答说：“那又怎样？” “对我来说，这表明他不尊重可能是国家副总裁的参议员。不仅如此，我认为这表明对他来说，包括人们身份在内的一切都必须修改以适应他的传统，他说话的方式。 难以表达的信件或信件组合，”德保罗伊斯兰研究教授艾哈迈德·哈希姆说。

college-writing-020754.en: But the mispronunciation behind Harris’s name goes beyond just a form of racism.
college-writing-020754.zh: 但哈里斯名字背后的发音错误不仅仅是一种种族主义。

college-writing-020755.en: It also has to do with her being a female in politics.
college-writing-020755.zh: 这也与她在政治上成为女性有关。

college-writing-020756.en: Over the past year, we’ve seen an increase in blatant disrespect and violence towards women in politics and how they have been treated by their male coworkers.
college-writing-020756.zh: 在过去的一年里，我们看到对政治中女性的公然不尊重和暴力增加，以及她们的男性同事对待她们的方式。

college-writing-020757.en: From President Trump stating that Sen. Ilhan Omar was an al-Qaeda sympathizer to Rep. Ted Yoho calling Sen. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez a “f***ing bitch,” to even the plot to kidnap Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, women in politics have been criticized for simply existing.
college-writing-020757.zh: 特朗普总统说参议员伊尔汉·奥马尔是基地组织对众议员泰德·约霍称参议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯的“他妈的婊子”的同情者，甚至是绑架州长格雷琴·惠特默的阴谋， 政治上的女性因简单存在而受到批评。

college-writing-020758.en: The focus on Harris’s name is partly because she’s a woman of color in a position of power, and her name makes her an easy target to point out to people that she’s different.
college-writing-020758.zh: 对哈里斯名字的关注部分是因为她是一个有色人种的女人，她的名字很容易成为向人们指出她与众不同的目标。

college-writing-020759.en: She doesn’t fit the mold of what a politician looks like.
college-writing-020759.zh: 她不符合政治家的样子。

college-writing-020760.en: She’s not white, and she’s not a man.
college-writing-020760.zh: 她不是白人，也不是男人。

college-writing-020761.en: “Her name is something, repeating it like this. It’s used like a smoke screen, dismissing someone because they are an immigrant. She’s an immigrant, she’s Black, but people can’t go there. They can’t attack her publicly for that. There’s a concept called the neutrality of a name. It’s the intentional concentration on her name that’s coded for the objection to who she is as a woman of color,” Rivers said.
college-writing-020761.zh: “她的名字是这样的。 姓名。正是故意集中在她的名字上，以反对她作为有色女性的反对意见，”里弗斯说。

college-writing-020763.en: In Islam, it’s the basis for all acts of worship.
college-writing-020763.zh: 在伊斯兰教中，它是所有敬拜行为的基础。

college-writing-020764.en: The action of cupping your hands, closing your eyes and asking God for what you need.
college-writing-020764.zh: 举起双手，闭上眼睛，向上帝祈求你需要什么的动作。

college-writing-020765.en: It’s calling on a superior being, Allah, for help.
college-writing-020765.zh: 它呼吁一个优越的存在，真主，寻求帮助。

college-writing-020766.zh: 简而言之，二人组就是祈祷。

college-writing-020768.zh: 我的名字透露出我是一个有色人种的女人，写着关于政治的文章。

college-writing-020769.en: My name makes me an easy target for those who would like to use it to deny me a job, attack me for my religion and remind others that I’m different.
college-writing-020769.zh: 我的名字使我成为那些想要用它来拒绝我的工作、攻击我的宗教并提醒其他人我与众不同的人的容易目标。

college-writing-020770.en: But, there’s also a chance that my name comes across to people─to women─who look like me.
college-writing-020770.zh: 但是，我的名字也有可能出现在人们身上——那些看起来像我的女人——那些看起来像我的女人。

college-writing-020911.zh: 758 第 5 部分 作家阅读

college-writing-020912.en: I believe in the importance of nonsense.
college-writing-020912.zh: 我相信胡说八道的重要性。

college-writing-020913.en: More specifically, that a little bit of nonsense in life is very valuable.
college-writing-020913.zh: 更具体地说，生活中的一点点胡说八道是非常有价值的。

college-writing-020914.en: Nonsense, in this case, being internet memes.
college-writing-020914.zh: 胡说八道，在这种情况下，是互联网模因。

college-writing-020915.en: Usually, I’m quick to criticize the internet.
college-writing-020915.zh: 通常，我很快就会批评互联网。

college-writing-020916.en: I have dedicated a significant amount of time to blaming it for many of our generation’s social conflicts.
college-writing-020916.zh: 我花了大量时间将我们这一代的许多社会冲突归咎于它。

college-writing-020917.en: And honestly, contemplating social media and the web at large frequently leads me down a path of existential desperation.
college-writing-020917.zh: 老实说，考虑社交媒体和网络经常让我走上一条存在主义的绝望之路。

college-writing-020918.en: But memes are, for me, an exception.
college-writing-020918.zh: 但对我来说，模因是一个例外。

college-writing-020919.en: They are deceivingly relevant and their function is more profound than their shallow perceptions afford them.
college-writing-020919.zh: 它们具有欺骗性的相关性，并且它们的功能比他们的肤浅观念提供给他们更深刻。

college-writing-020920.en: Of course, not all memes are funny, many are pointless, and offensive ones are unacceptable.
college-writing-020920.zh: 当然，不是所有的模因都很有趣，很多都是毫无意义的，攻击性的是不可接受的。

college-writing-020921.en: But the concept of a meme is significant.

college-writing-020922.en: It is an authentic, unfiltered expression rarely seen elsewhere online.
college-writing-020922.zh: 这是一种真实的、未经过滤的表达方式，在网上很少见。

college-writing-020923.en: It is a sign of humanity, something we often try to erase from our virtual selves.
college-writing-020923.zh: 这是人类的标志，我们经常试图从虚拟自我中抹去。

college-writing-020924.en: Evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins coined the term “meme” in his 1976 book “The Selfish Gene,” where he defines it as “a unit of cultural transmission.”
college-writing-020924.zh: 进化生物学家理查德·道金斯（Richard Dawkins）在他1976年的《自私基因》一书中创造了“meme”一词，他将其定义为“文化传播的一个单位”。

college-writing-020925.en: From the Greek word “mimema,” meaning “imitated,” memes are contingent on imitating relevant cultural patterns.
college-writing-020925.zh: 从希腊语“mimema”的意思是“模仿”，模因是模仿相关的文化模式。

college-writing-020926.en: Dawkins considers memes to be cultural genes─they have heredity, undergo replication, and require fitness to survive.
college-writing-020926.zh: 道金斯认为模因是文化基因——它们具有遗传性，经历复制，需要适应性才能生存。

college-writing-020927.en: His analogy, while so unfortunately untimely, explains meme fitness in terms of virus: ideas worth passing on are contagious.
college-writing-020927.zh: 他的类比，虽然不幸的是不合时宜，但用病毒解释了 Meme Fitness：值得传递的想法具有传染性。

college-writing-020928.en: The fittest, most contagious memes allow us to feel and relate to others.
college-writing-020928.zh: 最适合、最具传染性的表情包让我们感受并与他人建立联系。

college-writing-020929.en: Their images─the face of Sulley from “Monsters, Inc.” superimposed onto Mike Wazowski’s, Kermit the Frog drinking tea, or Baby Yoda─are so detached from reality, that we feel free to laugh at their captions because there is distance between us and them.
college-writing-020929.zh: 他们的图像——来自“Monsters, Inc.”的 Sulley 的脸 叠加在 Mike Wazowski 的，Kermit the Frog 喝茶或 Baby Yoda——与现实如此分离，我们可以随意嘲笑他们的标题，因为我们和他们之间有距离。

college-writing-020930.en: Serena G. Pellegrino is a philosophy major at Harvard University.
college-writing-020930.zh: Serena G. Pellegrino 是哈佛大学的哲学专业。

college-writing-020932.en: article, in which she discusses the phenomenon of memes, was pub-
college-writing-020932.zh: 她在其中讨论了模因现象的文章是发布

college-writing-020933.en: lished in the university newspaper, The Harvard Crimson.
college-writing-020933.zh: 发表在大学报纸《哈佛深红》中。

college-writing-020934.en: Memes and the Art of Nonsense
college-writing-020934.zh: 模因和胡说八道的艺术

college-writing-020938.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 759

college-writing-020940.zh: 没有感到暴露，我们会同情。

college-writing-020941.en: But memes are so refreshing because they remind us to take ourselves less seriously.
college-writing-020941.zh: 但表情包是如此令人耳目一新，因为它们提醒我们不要认真对待自己。

college-writing-020942.en: When an online audience is constantly watching and judging, they render our every action a performance─an evaluation of self.
college-writing-020942.zh: 当在线观众不断地观看和评判时，他们的每一个动作都变成了一种表演——对自我的评价。

college-writing-020943.en: So choosing what information to disclose and how we should look on our profiles is in itself an act.
college-writing-020943.zh: 因此，选择要披露的信息以及我们应该如何看待我们的个人资料本身就是一种行为。

college-writing-020944.en: Who we so carefully portray is a character.
college-writing-020944.zh: 我们如此仔细地描绘的是一个角色。

college-writing-020945.en: However, memes are a break in character─a sigh of relief when we’re off stage.
college-writing-020945.zh: 然而，模因是性格的中断——当我们离开舞台时，我松了一口气。

college-writing-020946.en: Through memes’ ridiculousness, we acknowledge the show can’t go on forever.
college-writing-020946.zh: 通过模因的荒谬，我们承认这个节目不能永远持续下去。

college-writing-020947.en: We’re flawed and our flaws can be funny.
college-writing-020947.zh: 我们有缺陷，我们的缺陷可能很有趣。

college-writing-020948.en: We take off our masks to laugh at the fact that we can be a mess.
college-writing-020948.zh: 我们摘下口罩，嘲笑我们可能一团糟的事实。

college-writing-020949.en: Sometimes, relating to a comic of a dog sitting in flames drinking coffee insisting “this is fine” can be therapeutic.
college-writing-020949.zh: 有时，与坐在火焰中喝咖啡的狗的漫画有关，坚持“这很好”可能是治疗性的。

college-writing-020950.en: This critique through parody is no novelty.
college-writing-020950.zh: 这种通过模仿的批评并不新鲜。

college-writing-020951.en: In the early 1700s, Italian playwright Carlo Goldoni innovated the theatre* scene and revitalized “commedia dell’arte,” a then-declining dramatic art form, to realize a vision proving quite meme-like.
college-writing-020951.zh: 在 1700 年代初期，意大利剧作家卡洛·戈尔多尼（Carlo Goldoni）创新了剧院*场景，并重振了当时衰退的戏剧艺术形式“Commedia Dell'Arte”，以实现一个非常像模因的愿景。

college-writing-020952.en: Just as memes unveil a more authentic emotional and human experience, Goldoni eliminated the use of masks and replaced stock characters with more realistic personalities.
college-writing-020952.zh: 就像模因揭示了更真实的情感和人性体验一样，Goldoni 消除了使用面具的使用，并以更真实的个性取代了普通角色。

college-writing-020953.en: And like our trove of recycled meme images, Goldoni created a fixed set of these personalities.
college-writing-020953.zh: 就像我们的可回收模因图像宝库一样，Goldoni 创造了一组固定的这些个性。

college-writing-020954.en: Their scripted jokes were scattered into improvised acting, functioning much like captions we apply according to context.
college-writing-020954.zh: 他们的剧本笑话被分散到即兴表演中，功能很像我们根据上下文应用的标题。

college-writing-020955.en: In addition to emotional release, Goldoni’s dramatic arts offered cultural commentary and political criticism.
college-writing-020955.zh: 除了情感释放外，戈尔多尼的戏剧艺术还提供了文化评论和政治批评。

college-writing-020956.en: His productions were popular for their transgressive humour*, actors often speaking in Italian dialects to criticize the different regions of Italy.
college-writing-020956.zh: 他的作品因其越界的幽默*而广受欢迎，演员经常用意大利方言来批评意大利的不同地区。

college-writing-020957.en: And we see much the same online, memes calling out the odd idiosyncrasies of different states or disagreeing with our government.
college-writing-020957.zh: 我们在网上看到的几乎相同，模因呼唤不同州的奇怪特质或不同意我们的政府。

college-writing-020958.en: Especially in the COVID era, we are in constant disagreement with laws, politicians, and each other.
college-writing-020958.zh: 尤其是在COVID时代，我们一直与法律、政治家和彼此分歧。

college-writing-020959.en: As Goldoni’s productions did so many years ago, memes give us grounds to transgress.
college-writing-020959.zh: 正如 Goldoni 的作品多年前所做的那样，模因让我们有理由违反。

college-writing-020960.en: In the guise of ridiculousness, we can push the boundaries and express contentious opinions without direct, explicit confrontation.
college-writing-020960.zh: 以荒谬的名义，我们可以突破界限，表达有争议的意见，而无需直接、明确的对抗。

college-writing-020961.en: After all, where else would we be able to overlay a “Karen” wig onto Donald Trump’s hair?
college-writing-020961.zh: 毕竟，我们还能在哪里将“凯伦”假发覆盖在唐纳德特朗普的头发上？

college-writing-020962.en: Yet the real beauty of Goldoni’s art and the world of memes is their ability to pantomime and portray the world as it is.
college-writing-020962.zh: 然而，戈尔多尼的艺术和模因世界的真正美是他们能够哑剧和描绘世界的能力。

college-writing-020963.en: As viewers, we enjoy watching scenarios in which we can see ourselves─joyful, tragic, awkward, or hopeless as they may be.
college-writing-020963.zh: 作为观众，我们喜欢观看我们可以看到自己的场景——他们可能会快乐、悲惨、尴尬或绝望。

college-writing-020964.zh: 客观地体验可以帮助我们处理。

college-writing-020965.en: It takes the edge off the lives we live so seriously.
college-writing-020965.zh: 它消除了我们如此认真地生活的生活。

college-writing-020966.en: But while history repeats itself to a large extent, it evolves, too.
college-writing-020966.zh: 但是，虽然历史在很大程度上重演，但它也在发展。

college-writing-020967.en: Memes are far more abstract than people playing parts on stage.
college-writing-020967.zh: 模因比在舞台上扮演角色的人要抽象得多。

college-writing-020968.en: That we can feel seen by seeming gibberish may go to show just how critical of ourselves we have become; we don’t like it when things get too real.
college-writing-020968.zh: 看起来像胡言乱语的我们可以感觉到，可以表明我们已经变得多么批评自己； 我们不喜欢事情变得太真实。

college-writing-020969.en: Our solution, then, is both escape and catharsis.
college-writing-020969.zh: 那么，我们的解决方案是逃逸和宣泄。

college-writing-021106.en: Fresh lemonade is my drink of choice.
college-writing-021106.zh: 新鲜柠檬水是我的首选饮品。

college-writing-021107.en: In my small Kentucky town, beautiful black, brown, and white girls set up their lemonade stands and practice the art of money making─it’s business.
college-writing-021107.zh: 在我的肯塔基州小镇，美丽的黑人、棕色和白人女孩建立了她们的柠檬水摊，实践了赚钱的艺术——这是生意。

college-writing-021108.en: As a grown black woman who believes in the manifesto “Girl, get your money straight” my first response to Beyoncé’s visual album, Lemonade, was WOW─this is the business of capitalist money-making at its best.
college-writing-021108.zh: 作为一个相信宣言“女孩，让你的钱直截了当”的成年黑人女性，我对碧昂丝的视觉专辑《柠檬水》的第一反应是哇——这是资本主义赚钱的最佳方式。

college-writing-021109.en: Viewers who like to suggest Lemonade was created solely or primarily for black female audiences are missing the point.
college-writing-021109.zh: 喜欢推荐柠檬水的观众完全或主要为黑人女性观众创造了这一点。

college-writing-021110.en: Commodities, irrespective of their subject matter, are made, produced, and marketed to entice any and all consumers.
college-writing-021110.zh: 商品，无论其主题如何，都是制造、生产和销售的，以吸引任何和所有消费者。

college-writing-021111.en: Beyoncé’s audience is the world and that world of business and money-making has no color.
college-writing-021111.zh: 碧昂丝的观众就是世界，商业和赚钱的世界没有色彩。

college-writing-021112.en: What makes this production─this commodity─daring is its subject matter.
college-writing-021112.zh: 是什么造就了这个产品——这种商品——大胆是它的主题。

college-writing-021113.en: Obviously Lemonade positively exploits images of black female bodies─placing them at the center, making them the norm.
college-writing-021113.zh: 显然，Lemonade 积极利用了黑人女性身体的图像——将它们放在中心，使它们成为常态。

college-writing-021114.en: In this visual narrative, there are diverse representations (black female bodies come in all sizes, shapes, and textures with all manner of big hair).
college-writing-021114.zh: 在这种视觉叙事中，有不同的表现形式（黑人女性的身体有各种大小、形状和纹理，有着各种各样的大头发）。

college-writing-021115.en: Portraits of ordinary everyday black women are spotlighted, poised as though they are royalty.
college-writing-021115.zh: 普通黑人女性的肖像被聚焦，像皇室一样沉着。

college-writing-021116.en: The unnamed, unidentified mothers of murdered young black males are each given pride of place.
college-writing-021116.zh: 被谋杀的年轻黑人男性的不知名的、身份不明的母亲都被赋予了骄傲。

college-writing-021117.en: Real-life images of ordinary, overweight not dressed up bodies are placed within a visual backdrop that includes stylized, choreographed, fashion plate fantasy representations.
college-writing-021117.zh: 普通的、超重的没有装扮的身体的真实图像被放置在一个视觉背景中，其中包括风格化、精心设计的时尚板块幻想表现。

college-writing-021118.en: Despite all the glamorous showcasing of Deep South antebellum fashion, when the show begins Beyoncé as star appears in sporty casual clothing, the controversial hoodie.
college-writing-021118.zh: 尽管南方战前时尚的所有迷人展示，当该节目开始时，碧昂丝作为明星出现在运动休闲服装中，备受争议的连帽衫。

college-writing-021119.en: Concurrently, the scantily-clothed dancing image of athlete Serena
college-writing-021119.zh: 与此同时，运动员塞雷娜的衣着暴露的舞蹈形象
