college-writing-021132.en: (Speaking of commodification, in the real-life frame Beyoncé’s new line of sportswear, Ivy Park, is in the process of being marketed right now.)
college-writing-021132.zh: （说到商品化，在现实生活中，碧昂丝的新运动装系列，常春藤公园，目前正在推销中。）

college-writing-021133.en: Lemonade offers viewers a visual extravaganza─a display of black female bodies that transgresses all boundaries.
college-writing-021133.zh: 柠檬水为观众提供了一场视觉盛宴——展示了跨越所有界限的黑人女性身体。

college-writing-021134.en: It’s all about the body, and the body as commodity.
college-writing-021134.zh: 这一切都与身体有关，身体作为商品。

college-writing-021135.en: This is certainly not radical or revolutionary.
college-writing-021135.zh: 这当然不是激进或革命性的。

college-writing-021136.en: From slavery to the present day, black female bodies, clothed and unclothed, have been bought and sold.
college-writing-021136.zh: 从奴隶制到现在，黑人女性的尸体，穿着衣服，没有衣服，被买卖。

college-writing-021137.en: What makes this commodification different in Lemonade is intent; its purpose is to seduce, celebrate, and delight─to challenge the ongoing present day devaluation and dehumanization of the black female body.
college-writing-021137.zh: 柠檬水中这种商品化的不同之处在于意图； 其目的是引诱、庆祝和愉悦——挑战黑人女性身体持续的贬低和非人性化。

college-writing-021138.en: Throughout Lemonade the black female body is utterly-aestheticized─its beauty a powerful in your face confrontation.
college-writing-021138.zh: 在整个柠檬水中，黑人女性的身体是完全美学的——它的美丽在你的脸上对抗。

college-writing-021140.en: Images like these were first seen in Julie Dash’s groundbreaking film Daughters of the Dust shot by the brilliant cinematographer Arthur Jafa.
college-writing-021140.zh: 像这样的图像首次出现在朱莉·达什（Julie Dash）的开创性电影《尘埃》中，由出色的电影摄影师亚瑟·贾法（Arthur Jafa）拍摄。

college-writing-021141.en: Many of the black and white still images of women and nature are reminiscent of the transformative and innovative contemporary photography of Carrie Mae Weems.
college-writing-021141.zh: 许多女性和自然的黑白静止图像让人想起 Carrie Mae Weems 的变革和创新当代摄影。

college-writing-021142.en: She has continually offered decolonized radical revisioning of the black female body.
college-writing-021142.zh: 她不断地为黑人女性身体提供非殖民化的激进修正。

college-writing-021143.en: It is the broad scope of Lemonade’s visual landscape that makes it so distinctive─the construction of a powerfully symbolic black female sisterhood that resists invisibility, that refuses to be silent.
college-writing-021143.zh: 正是柠檬水的视觉景观的广泛范围使其如此与众不同——构建了一个强大的象征性的黑人女性姐妹会，抵抗隐形，拒绝保持沉默。

college-writing-021144.en: This in and of itself is no small feat─it shifts the gaze of white mainstream culture.
college-writing-021144.zh: 这本身就是不小的壮举——它改变了白人主流文化的凝视。

college-writing-021145.en: It challenges us all to look anew, to radically revision how we see the black female body.
college-writing-021145.zh: 它挑战我们所有人重新审视，从根本上修改我们如何看待黑人女性的身体。

college-writing-021146.en: However, this radical repositioning of black female images does not truly overshadow or change conventional sexist constructions of black female identity.
college-writing-021146.zh: 然而，这种对黑人女性形象的彻底重新定位并没有真正掩盖或改变黑人女性身份的传统性别歧视结构。

college-writing-021147.en: Even though Beyoncé and her creative collaborators daringly offer multi dimensional images of black female life, much of the album stays within a conventional stereotypical framework, where the black woman is always a victim.
college-writing-021147.zh: 尽管碧昂丝和她的创意合作者大胆地提供了黑人女性生活的多维图像，但这张专辑的大部分内容都保留在一个传统的刻板印象框架中，黑人女性始终是受害者。

college-writing-021148.en: Although based on the real-life experience of Beyoncé, Lemonade is a fantasy fictional narrative with Beyoncé starring as the lead character.
college-writing-021148.zh: 虽然基于碧昂丝的现实生活经历，但柠檬水是一个幻想虚构的叙事，碧昂丝饰演主角。

college-writing-021149.en: This work begins with a story of pain and betrayal highlighting the trauma it produces.
college-writing-021149.zh: 这项工作以痛苦和背叛的故事开始，突出了它造成的创伤。

college-writing-021150.en: The story is as old as the ballad of “Frankie and Johnny” (“he was my man alright, but he done me wrong”).
college-writing-021150.zh: 这个故事和“弗兰基和约翰尼”的歌谣一样古老（“他是我的人，好吧，但他做错了”）。

college-writing-021151.en: Like the fictional Frankie, Beyoncé’s character responds to her man’s betrayal with rage.
college-writing-021151.zh: 就像虚构的弗兰基一样，碧昂丝的角色以愤怒的方式回应了她男人的背叛。

college-writing-021153.en: And even though the father in the song “Daddy’s Lessons” gives her a rifle warning her about men, she does not shoot her man.
college-writing-021153.zh: 尽管歌曲“爸爸的课程”中的父亲给了她一把步枪，警告她关于男人的事情，但她并没有开枪打死她的男人。

college-writing-021154.en: She dons a magnificently designed golden yellow gown, boldly struts through the street with baseball bat in hand, randomly smashing cars.
college-writing-021154.zh: 她穿着一件设计精美的金黄色长袍，大胆地昂首阔步地在街上昂首阔步，手里拿着棒球棒，随意砸汽车。

college-writing-021155.en: In this scene, the goddess-like character of Beyoncé is sexualized along with her acts of emotional violence, like Wagner’s “Ride of the Valkyries” she destroys with no shame.
college-writing-021155.zh: 在这个场景中，碧昂丝的女神般的角色随着她的情感暴力行为而被性化，就像瓦格纳的“女武神之骑”一样，她毫不掩饰地摧毁了她。

college-writing-021156.en: Among the many mixed messages embedded in Lemonade is this celebration of rage.
college-writing-021156.zh: 在柠檬水中嵌入的众多混合信息中，这种愤怒的庆祝活动。

college-writing-021157.en: Smug and smiling in her golden garb, Beyoncé is the embodiment of a fantastical female power, which is just that─pure fantasy.
college-writing-021157.zh: 碧昂丝在她的金色外衣上沾沾自喜地自鸣得意，微笑着，是一种幻想女性力量的化身，这就是纯粹的幻想。

college-writing-021158.en: Images of female violence undercut a central message embedded in Lemonade that violence in all its forms, especially the violence of lies and betrayal, hurts.
college-writing-021158.zh: 女性暴力的图像削弱了柠檬水中嵌入的中心信息，即各种形式的暴力，尤其是对谎言和背叛的暴力，都会造成伤害。

college-writing-021160.en: Contrary to misguided notions of gender equality, women do not and will not seize power and create self-love and self-esteem through violent acts.
college-writing-021160.zh: 与被误导的性别平等观念相反，妇女不会也不会通过暴力行为夺取权力，创造自爱和自尊。

college-writing-021161.en: Female violence is no more liberatory than male violence.
college-writing-021161.zh: 女性暴力并不比男性暴力更自由。

college-writing-021162.en: And when violence is made to look sexy and eroticized, as in the Lemonade sexy-dress street scene, it does not serve to undercut the prevailing cultural sentiment that it is acceptable to use violence to reinforce domination, especially in relations between men and women.
college-writing-021162.zh: 当暴力看起来性感和色情化时，就像在柠檬水性感的街头场景中一样，它并没有削弱普遍的文化情绪，即使用暴力来加强统治是可以接受的，尤其是在男女之间的关系中。

college-writing-021163.en: Violence does not create positive change.
college-writing-021163.zh: 暴力不会产生积极的变化。

college-writing-021164.en: Even though Beyoncé and her creative collaborators make use of the powerful voice and words of Malcolm X to emphasize the lack of respect for black womanhood, simply showcasing beautiful black bodies does not create a just culture of optimal well being where black females can become fully self-actualized and be truly respected.
college-writing-021164.zh: 尽管碧昂丝和她的创意合作者利用马尔科姆 X 的强有力的声音和话语来强调对黑人女性的缺乏尊重，但简单地展示美丽的黑人身体并不能创造出一种公正的最佳健康文化，让黑人女性可以完全自我实现并真正成为现实 受人尊敬。

college-writing-021165.en: Honoring the self, loving our bodies, is an appropriate stage in the construction of healthy self-esteem.
college-writing-021165.zh: 尊重自我，爱我们的身体，是建立健康自尊的适当阶段。

college-writing-021166.en: This aspect of Lemonade is affirming.
college-writing-021166.zh: 柠檬水的这方面是肯定的。

college-writing-021167.en: Certainly, to witness Miss Hattie, the 90-year-old grandmother of Jay Z, give her personal testimony that she has survived by taking the lemons life handed her and making lemonade is awesome.
college-writing-021167.zh: 当然，见证 Jay Z 的 90 岁祖母哈蒂小姐的个人见证，证明她通过夺走柠檬的生命并制作柠檬水而幸存下来。

college-writing-021168.en: All the references to honoring our ancestors and elders in Lemonade inspire.
college-writing-021168.zh: 在柠檬水中尊重我们的祖先和长辈的所有参考都激发了灵感。

college-writing-021169.en: However, concluding this narrative of hurt and betrayal with caring images of family and home do not serve as adequate ways to reconcile and heal trauma.
college-writing-021169.zh: 然而，用家庭和家庭的关怀形象来结束这种伤害和背叛的叙述并不能作为调和和治愈创伤的充分方式。

college-writing-021170.en: Concurrently, in the world of art-making, a black female creator as powerfully placed as Beyoncé can both create images and present viewers with her own interpretation of what those images mean.
college-writing-021170.zh: 与此同时，在艺术创作的世界中，像碧昂丝这样强大的黑人女性创作者既可以创造图像，也可以向观众展示她自己对这些图像的含义的解释。

college-writing-021171.en: However, her interpretation cannot stand as truth.
college-writing-021171.zh: 然而，她的解释不能像真理一样。

college-writing-021172.en: For example, Beyoncé uses her non-fictional voice and persona to claim feminism, even to claim, as she does in a recent issue of Elle magazine, “to give clarity to the true meaning” of the term, but her construction of feminism cannot be trusted.
college-writing-021172.zh: 例如，碧昂丝用她非虚构的声音和角色来声称女权主义，甚至像她在最近一期的《ELLE》杂志中所做的那样，“要清楚地说明这个词的真正含义”，但她对女权主义的建构是不可信的。

college-writing-021173.en: Her vision of feminism does not call for an end to patriarchal domination.
college-writing-021173.zh: 她对女权主义的看法并不要求结束父权统治。

college-writing-021174.en: It’s all about insisting on equal rights for men and women.
college-writing-021174.zh: 这一切都是为了坚持男女平等的权利。

college-writing-021175.en: In the world of fantasy feminism, there are no class, sex, and race hierarchies that breakdown simplified categories of women and men, no call to challenge and change systems of domination, no emphasis on intersectionality.
college-writing-021175.zh: 在幻想女权主义的世界里，没有阶级、性别和种族等级制度来分解女性和男性的简化类别，没有呼吁挑战和改变统治系统，不强调交叉性。

college-writing-021176.en: In such a simplified worldview, women gaining the freedom to be like men can be seen as powerful.
college-writing-021176.zh: 在这样一个简化的世界观中，获得像男人一样自由的女性可以被视为强大。

college-writing-021177.en: But it is a false construction of power as so many men, especially black men, do not possess actual power.
college-writing-021177.zh: 但这是一种虚假的权力结构，因为许多人，尤其是黑人，没有实际的权力。

college-writing-021178.en: And indeed, it is clear that black male cruelty and violence towards black women is a direct outcome of patriarchal exploitation and oppression.
college-writing-021178.zh: 事实上，很明显，黑人男性对黑人女性的残忍和暴力是父权剥削和压迫的直接结果。

college-writing-021179.en: In her fictive world, Beyoncé can name black female pain, poignantly articulated by the passionate poetry of Somali-British poet Warsan Shire, and move through stages evoked by printed words: Intuition, Denial, Forgiveness, Hope, Reconciliation.
college-writing-021179.zh: 在她的虚构世界中，碧昂丝可以说出黑人女性的痛苦，被索马里-英国诗人华桑·希尔的激情诗意所表达，并通过印刷文字所唤起的阶段：直觉、否认、宽恕、希望， 和解。

college-writing-021180.en: In this fictive world, black female emotional pain can be exposed and revealed.
college-writing-021180.zh: 在这个虚构的世界里，黑人女性的情感痛苦可以被揭露和揭示。

college-writing-021181.en: It can be given voice: this is a vital and essential stage of freedom struggle, but it does not bring exploitation and domination to an end.
college-writing-021181.zh: 可以发出声音：这是自由斗争的重要和重要阶段，但它并没有结束剥削和统治。

college-writing-021183.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 767

college-writing-021184.en: how hard women in relationships with patriarchal men work for change, forgive, and reconcile, men must do the work of inner and outer transformation if emotional violence against black females is to end.
college-writing-021184.zh: 女性与父权男性的关系如何努力实现变革、宽恕和和解，如果对黑人女性的情感暴力要结束，男性必须完成内在和外在转变的工作。

college-writing-021185.en: We see no hint of this in Lemonade.
college-writing-021185.zh: 我们在柠檬水中没有看到这一点的迹象。

college-writing-021186.en: If change is not mutual then black female emotional hurt can be voiced, but the reality of men inflicting emotional pain will still continue (can we really trust the caring images of Jay Z which conclude this narrative).
college-writing-021186.zh: 如果改变不是相互的，那么可以表达黑人女性的情感伤害，但男性造成情感痛苦的现实仍将继续（我们真的可以相信 Jay Z 的关怀形象，结束了这个叙述）。

college-writing-021187.en: It is only as black women and all women resist patriarchal romanticization of domination in relationships can a healthy self-love emerge that allows every black female, and all females, to refuse to be a victim.
college-writing-021187.zh: 只有黑人女性和所有女性都抵制父权制的人际关系中统治的浪漫化，才能出现一种健康的自爱，让每个黑人女性和所有女性都拒绝成为受害者。

college-writing-021188.en: Ultimately Lemonade glamorizes a world of gendered cultural paradox and contradiction.
college-writing-021188.zh: 最终，柠檬水美化了一个充满性别的文化悖论和矛盾的世界。

college-writing-021190.en: As Beyoncé proudly proclaims in the powerful anthem “Freedom”: “I had my ups and downs, but I always find the inner-strength to pull myself up.”
college-writing-021190.zh: 正如碧昂丝在强有力的国歌中自豪地宣称的“自由”：“我有起有落，但我总能找到内在的力量来振作起来。”

college-writing-021191.en: To truly be free, we must choose beyond simply surviving adversity, we must dare to create lives of sustained optimal well-being and joy.
college-writing-021191.zh: 要真正自由，我们必须选择超越简单的逆境，我们必须敢于创造持续的最佳幸福和快乐的生活。

college-writing-021192.en: In that world, the making and drinking of lemonade will be a fresh and zestful delight, a real-life mixture of the bitter and the sweet, and not a measure of our capacity to endure pain, but rather a celebration of our moving beyond pain.
college-writing-021192.zh: 在那个世界里，柠檬水的制作和饮用将是一种新鲜而热情的喜悦，是苦味和甜味的现实生活混合，而不是衡量我们忍受痛苦的能力，而是庆祝我们超越痛苦。

college-writing-021283.en: Most people need music in their lives because it speaks to them in a multitude of ways.
college-writing-021283.zh: 大多数人在生活中需要音乐，因为它以多种方式与他们交谈。

college-writing-021284.en: We each have our favorite artists and favorite songs.
college-writing-021284.zh: 我们每个人都有我们最喜欢的艺术家和最喜欢的歌曲。

college-writing-021285.en: For this assignment, you are to choose one of the following assignments.
college-writing-021285.zh: 对于此作业，您将选择以下作业之一。

college-writing-021287.en: You will need to explain who the artist is, what the album is, and why it is your favorite.
college-writing-021287.zh: 你需要解释艺术家是谁，这张专辑是什么，以及为什么它是你最喜欢的。

college-writing-021288.en: • Write about your three favorite songs.

college-writing-021289.en: You will need to describe the artist behind each song and explain why that song is one of your favorites.

college-writing-021291.en: In this analysis of Beyoncé’s Lemonade, the author explores themes she sees woven throughout the album.
college-writing-021291.zh: 在对碧昂丝柠檬水的分析中，作者探索了她在整张专辑中看到的主题。

college-writing-021292.en: Most artists’ albums are like essays─multiple songs that work together to support the thesis of the album.
college-writing-021292.zh: 大多数艺术家的专辑都像散文——多首歌曲共同支持这张专辑的论点。

college-writing-021293.en: For this assignment, you are to pick one of your favorite albums and analyze its themes and messages.
college-writing-021293.zh: 对于这项任务，您将选择您最喜欢的专辑之一并分析其主题和信息。

college-writing-021294.zh: 您可能想回顾第 19 章“撰写基于来源的论文”中的修辞分析样本文章，以了解如何保持分析语气。

college-writing-021295.en: You will also need to review Chapter 8, “Description,” to help you create such strong descriptions in your paper that even someone unfamiliar with the album will be able to understand your point.
college-writing-021295.zh: 您还需要查看第 8 章“描述”，以帮助您在论文中创建如此强烈的描述，即使不熟悉这张专辑的人也能理解您的观点。

college-writing-021297.zh: 当作者讨论碧昂丝专辑的特定部分时，她专注于视频中的角色粉碎汽车和“毁灭无耻”的特定场景。

college-writing-021298.en: Do you think this is a radical idea in the twenty-first century?

college-writing-021300.en: What does it mean for marginalized people to destroy with no shame, and has shame played a part in their struggles?
college-writing-021300.zh: 被边缘化的人毫不羞耻地摧毁，羞耻是否在他们的斗争中发挥了作用，这意味着什么？

college-writing-021301.zh: 对于此作业，您将只关注一个问题，并使用历史或当前事件的支持来回答该问题。

college-writing-021302.en: This will require you to read Chapter 17, “Information Literacy,” Chapter 18, “Summarizing and Paraphrasing,” and Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” so you can properly integrate the information you find in your research.

college-writing-021304.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 771

college-writing-021305.en: These days, American colleges are eager to boast about their number of women enrollees, their percentage of ethnic minorities, even their ratio of low-income students.
college-writing-021305.zh: 如今，美国大学渴望吹嘘她们的女性参保人数、少数民族的比例，甚至是她们的低收入学生比例。

college-writing-021306.en: They’re very proud of their inclusiveness and outreach.
college-writing-021306.zh: 他们为自己的包容性和外展感到自豪。

college-writing-021307.en: But many colleges are mum when it comes to the students on their campuses with criminal records.
college-writing-021307.zh: 但是，当涉及到有犯罪记录的校园里的学生时，许多大学都是妈妈。

college-writing-021308.en: To be fair, it’s a very delicate issue, one that requires reassuring students and parents that safety has not been compromised while also ensuring that some students with records are not singled out or treated differently.
college-writing-021308.zh: 公平地说，这是一个非常微妙的问题，它需要让学生和家长放心，安全没有受到损害，同时还要确保一些有记录的学生不会被单独挑选或对待。

college-writing-021309.en: Finding that balance has proved elusive for some colleges, but others have successfully untangled the complexities created by this increasingly common phenomenon.
college-writing-021309.zh: 对于一些大学来说，发现这种平衡已被证明是难以捉摸的，但其他大学已经成功地解除了这种日益普遍的现象造成的复杂性。

college-writing-021310.en: At hundreds of colleges, students have to disclose any criminal history during the admissions process and may be prescreened by a special committee.
college-writing-021310.zh: 在数百所大学，学生必须在录取过程中披露任何犯罪记录，并且可能会被一个特别委员会预先筛选。

college-writing-021311.en: A quick online search yields multiple websites─like the one at the University of Colorado, Boulder─with guidelines for admissions for students with criminal records.
college-writing-021311.zh: 快速的在线搜索产生了多个网站——比如科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的一个网站——为有犯罪记录的学生提供入学指南。

college-writing-021312.en: At some schools, a formerly incarcerated student’s movements on campus and his or her access to facilities may be restricted.
college-writing-021312.zh: 在一些学校，以前被监禁的学生在校园内的活动和他或她使用设施的机会可能会受到限制。

college-writing-021313.en: At a number of colleges and universities, students who have committed certain crimes may be jointly monitored by campus authorities and state officials.
college-writing-021313.zh: 在一些学院和大学，犯有某些罪行的学生可能会受到校园当局和国家官员的共同监督。

college-writing-021314.en: The measures are set up based on state requirements, school policy, and the institution’s comfort level.
college-writing-021314.zh: 这些措施是根据国家要求、学校政策和机构的舒适度设置的。

college-writing-021315.en: Juleyka Lantigua-Williams is a writer, editor, and journalist who has had articles appear in the Chicago Tribune, L.A. Times, JET, and The Atlantic.
college-writing-021315.zh: Julleyka Lantigua-Williams 是一位作家、编辑和记者，他曾在《芝加哥论坛报》、洛杉矶时报、喷气机和大西洋上发表过文章。

college-writing-021316.en: She received her B.A. from Skidmore College and her M.S. in Journalism from Boston University.
college-writing-021316.zh: 她获得了学士学位。 来自斯基德莫尔学院和她的硕士学位 波士顿大学新闻学专业。

college-writing-021317.en: When a Classmate Is a Former Inmate

college-writing-021318.zh: 朱利卡·兰蒂瓜-威廉姆斯

college-writing-021322.en: “It’s just incredibly stigmatizing,” said Emily NaPier, the director of justice strategies at the Center for Community Alternatives, which conducts research in this area.
college-writing-021322.zh: “这只是令人难以置信的污名化，”社区替代中心司法战略主任艾米丽·纳皮尔 (Emily Napier) 说，该中心在该领域进行研究。

college-writing-021323.en: She said that some students with records complain that some schools “don’t allow them to live on campus housing,” “some have a probation period,” and others “have some level of tracking and surveillance regarding their grades.”
college-writing-021323.zh: 她说，一些有记录的学生抱怨有些学校“不允许他们住在校园住房”，“有些有试用期”，而另一些人则“对他们的成绩有一定程度的跟踪和监控”。

college-writing-021324.en: NaPier added that the center is also aware of schools that require students with criminal records “to sign a declaration that they will only come to campus for classes and will not participate in any extracurricular activity on campus, that they will not linger on campus, that they will not be on campus for any other reason other than classes.”
college-writing-021324.zh: Napier 补充说，该中心还知道学校要求有犯罪记录的学生“签署声明，他们只会来校园上课，不会参加校园内的任何课外活动，他们不会在校园内徘徊，他们不会因为课堂以外的任何其他原因而在校园内。”

college-writing-021325.en: That used to be the case at Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis.
college-writing-021325.zh: 印第安纳大学普渡大学印第安纳波利斯大学曾经是这种情况。

college-writing-021326.en: For students who had answered “yes” to an application question asking if they had a criminal history, their admissions letter informed them that they could enroll in school, but they couldn’t live on campus.
college-writing-021326.zh: 对于那些回答“是”的申请问题，询问他们是否有犯罪记录的学生，他们的招生信通知他们可以上学，但他们不能住在校园里。

college-writing-021327.en: However, the school recently removed the measure after it expanded the use of the background question to applications that are given to high-schoolers, which could have meant that “freshmen would not be able to live on campus housing,” said Pamela Brown, IUPUI’s associate director of undergraduate admissions for operations.
college-writing-021327.zh: 然而，学校最近取消了这项措施，因为它将背景问题的使用范围扩展到了高中生的申请，这可能意味着“大一新生无法住在校园住房中，”IUPUI 的本科招生副主任帕梅拉·布朗说。

college-writing-021328.en: She said the school regularly modifies its policies as conflicts come up.
college-writing-021328.zh: 她说，随着冲突的出现，学校会定期修改政策。

college-writing-021329.en: “It just didn’t make sense to exclude them from campus housing,” she said.
college-writing-021329.zh: “将他们排除在校园住房之外是没有意义的，”她说。

college-writing-021330.en: Now, the incoming fall 2016 class will be the first to be allowed to live on campus no matter their backgrounds.
college-writing-021330.zh: 现在，即将到来的 2016 年秋季班级将成为第一个被允许在校园生活的课程，无论他们的背景如何。

college-writing-021331.en: But, in some instances, there are situations that are entirely out of a school’s control.
college-writing-021331.zh: 但是，在某些情况下，有些情况完全超出了学校的控制范围。

college-writing-021332.en: Students with criminal records who want to apply for certain professional programs often hit dead-ends.
college-writing-021332.zh: 想要申请某些专业课程的有犯罪记录的学生经常陷入困境。

college-writing-021333.en: “People are not rejected solely based on having a criminal record but can end up being excluded from certain academic programs that do not allow those with criminal histories to work in the field,” said Jason Ebbeling, executive director of the Student Success Center at Connecticut State Colleges & Universities.
college-writing-021333.zh: 康涅狄格州立大学和大学学生成功中心的执行主任杰森·埃伯林说：“人们不会仅仅因为有犯罪记录而被拒绝，而是最终可能被排除在某些不允许有犯罪历史的人的学术课程之外。”

college-writing-021334.en: Due to licensure requirements or clinical-rotation guidelines, future teachers, nurses, and others who might work in sensitive areas are not allowed to have past criminal histories.
college-writing-021334.zh: 由于许可要求或临床轮换指南，未来的教师、护士和其他可能在敏感地区工作的人不得有过去的犯罪历史。

college-writing-021335.en: “Why is someone in a classroom with a record more dangerous than someone sitting next to me in a movie theater or a restaurant?” asked Barmak Nassirian during my conversation with him.
college-writing-021335.zh: “为什么有记录在教室里的人比坐在我旁边的电影院或餐厅里的人更危险？” 在我与 Barmak Nassirian 的谈话中问道。

college-writing-021336.en: Nassirian has worked in higher education for 25 years and is the director of policy analysis at the American Association of State Colleges and Universities.
college-writing-021336.zh: Nassirian 在高等教育领域工作了 25 年，是美国州立大学和大学协会的政策分析主任。

college-writing-021337.en: “People do have a responsibility for maintaining safe campuses, I don’t dismiss that.”
college-writing-021337.zh: “人们确实有责任维护安全的校园，我不会忽视这一点。”

college-writing-021338.en: But he fervently opposes asking students to divulge the information, considering it as part of admissions, and subsequently monitoring students once on campus.
college-writing-021338.zh: 但他强烈反对要求学生透露信息，将其视为招生的一部分，并随后在校园内监控学生一次。

college-writing-021339.en: “We essentially condemn people to a life of underemployment and poverty if we deny them the one medicine that actually cures criminal behavior: education.”
college-writing-021339.zh: “如果我们拒绝一种真正治愈犯罪行为的药物，我们基本上会谴责人们的就业不足和贫困的生活：教育。”

college-writing-021340.en: “We have a number of students that do have a criminal background,” Ebbeling said.
college-writing-021340.zh: “我们有一些确实有犯罪背景的学生，”埃伯林说。

college-writing-021341.en: “We work at the community-college level with people that have been sex offenders and people who have other convictions.”
college-writing-021341.zh: “我们在社区大学层面与性犯罪者和有其他信念的人一起工作。”

college-writing-021343.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 773

college-writing-021344.en: criminal backgrounds and felony convictions at its universities but not at its community colleges.
college-writing-021344.zh: 其大学的犯罪背景和重罪定罪，但不在其社区学院。

college-writing-021345.en: Some cases don’t necessarily even require a background question.
college-writing-021345.zh: 有些情况甚至不一定需要背景问题。

college-writing-021346.en: “We have a very formalized process for sex offenders: The state has a registry for sex offenders; deans of students at the community-college level meet with students to discuss behavioral expectations; in fact, we place a hold on their account until the meeting happens,” Ebbeling said.
college-writing-021346.zh: “我们对性犯罪者有一个非常正式的程序：该州有一个性犯罪者登记处；社区学院级别的学生院长与学生会面，讨论行为期望；事实上，我们保留了他们的账户，直到会议发生，”埃伯林说。

college-writing-021347.en: “We start from a place where they are given the opportunities any other students are given until there are any behavioral disruptions,” he said.
college-writing-021347.zh: “我们从一个地方开始，让他们有机会获得任何其他学生的机会，直到有任何行为中断，”他说。

college-writing-021348.en: But he also explained that for the sexual-assault registry, there are state requirements that Connecticut schools must comply with and of course they must collaborate with state agencies on any pending investigations.
college-writing-021348.zh: 但他也解释说，对于性侵犯登记处，康涅狄格州的学校必须遵守州的要求，当然它们必须与州机构合作进行任何未决的调查。

college-writing-021349.en: College administrators, according to several of the experts I spoke to, try to put in place as many mechanisms and safety precautions as possible to reinforce how safe their campuses are, especially for the peace of mind of prospective families.
college-writing-021349.zh: 根据我采访过的几位专家的说法，大学管理人员试图尽可能多地采取机制和安全预防措施，以加强他们的校园的安全性，特别是为了让未来的家庭安心。

college-writing-021350.en: And yet, there are no statistically valid relationships between asking about criminal histories, the ratio of such students on campus, and the incidences of campus crime.
college-writing-021350.zh: 然而，在询问犯罪历史、校园内此类学生的比例和校园犯罪率之间没有统计学上有效的关系。

college-writing-021351.en: One glaring example of this is sexual assault, one of the most common campus crimes.
college-writing-021351.zh: 一个明显的例子是性侵犯，这是最常见的校园犯罪之一。

college-writing-021352.en: Walter DeKeseredy, a professor of sociology and the director of the Research Center on Violence at West Virginia University, has spent over 30 years conducting research on violence against women, but he is best known for his work on sexual assault on college campuses.
college-writing-021352.zh: Walter Dekeseredy 是社会学教授和西弗吉尼亚大学暴力研究中心主任，他花了 30 多年的时间对暴力侵害妇女行为进行研究，但他最出名的是他在大学校园性侵犯方面的工作。

college-writing-021353.en: He sees no merit in efforts to identify and monitor students with prior criminal records on campus.
college-writing-021353.zh: 他认为在校园内识别和监控有犯罪记录的学生方面没有任何价值。

college-writing-021354.en: “Two of the high-risk groups on campus are fraternity brothers and men who are in combative sports─football, hockey, and lacrosse,” DeKeseredy said.
college-writing-021354.zh: “校园里的两个高风险群体是兄弟会兄弟和从事好斗运动的人——足球、曲棍球和曲棍球，”Dekeseredy 说。

college-writing-021355.en: “We have the data. They are among the highest-risk men on campus for committing sexual assault. You have a subculture that promotes and rewards a hyper masculine masculinity.”
college-writing-021355.zh: “我们有数据。他们是校园内遭受性侵犯风险最高的男性之一。你有一种促进和奖励超男性化男性气质的亚文化。”

college-writing-021356.en: Another researcher believes there are other important factors at play.
college-writing-021356.zh: 另一位研究人员认为还有其他重要因素在起作用。

college-writing-021357.en: “The issue of race and class are primary, and they get focused on young black men, but it’s really young white men who created the problem,” said Natalie Sokoloff, professor emerita of sociology at John Jay College of Criminal Justice.
college-writing-021357.zh: “种族和阶级的问题是主要问题，他们的重点是年轻的黑人男性，但造成这个问题的是真正的年轻白人，”约翰杰伊刑事司法学院社会学荣誉教授娜塔莉·索科洛夫 (Natalie Sokoloff) 说。

college-writing-021358.en: So even though in the United States black men are more likely to have a record and thus more likely to be under scrutiny by collegiate safety policies, it is actually white men who commit the majority of serious crimes, like sexual assault, on campus.
college-writing-021358.zh: 因此，尽管在美国，黑人男性更有可能拥有记录，因此更有可能受到大学安全政策的审查，但实际上是白人在校园内犯下了大多数严重的罪行，例如性侵犯。

college-writing-021359.en: “What we try to highlight is that these kinds of practices really are a de facto form of race-based discrimination . . . They undermine the goal of higher education, restrict access, and result in less diverse applicant pools. It’s so counterproductive.”
college-writing-021359.zh: “我们试图强调的是，这些做法实际上是基于种族的歧视的一种事实形式……它们破坏了高等教育的目标，限制了准入，并导致了减少多样化的申请人池。这会适得其反。”

college-writing-021360.en: One measure that has emerged from the growing awareness of crimes on campus is the practice of signaling in students’ transcripts when disciplinary action has been taken against them.
college-writing-021360.zh: 对校园犯罪意识日益增强的一种措施是在对学生的成绩单采取纪律处分时发出信号的做法。

college-writing-021361.en: In most instances, schools do this of their own volition, but in several states, it is the law.

college-writing-021362.en: One university has even started tracking states and colleges that annotate transcripts.

college-writing-021363.en: “An issue that pops up is perpetrators of sexual violence who leave campus just ahead of the sheriff, who quietly transfer before any evidence is gathered against them,” Nassirian said, referring to troublemaking students who voluntarily leave school before any disciplinary or legal measures have been taken against them─only to later transfer into a new college with a fresh start.

college-writing-021366.en: “There is a real risk, and real pressure, to annotate the transcript with any instances of disciplinary actions to warn the future institution about the student.”
college-writing-021366.zh: “有一个真正的风险和真正的压力，要在成绩单上注释任何纪律处分，以警告未来的机构关于学生的事情。”

college-writing-021367.en: A student could in theory simply not admit to a criminal background and circumvent all of the hassle and stigma─but hiding it can have severe consequences.
college-writing-021367.zh: 理论上，学生可以根本不承认犯罪背景并规避所有的麻烦和污名——但隐藏起来可能会产生严重的后果。

college-writing-021368.en: In Connecticut’s state-university system, it “could be grounds for dismissal if the student does not self-identify in [the] admissions process, and there’s an issue later on,” according to Ebbeling.

college-writing-021370.en: “It could be grounds for disciplinary action or dismissal if it were discovered later on,” said Paul Seegert, U.W.’s director of admissions.

college-writing-021497.en: As a young child, Marc Talusan was enthralled with the music of Lea Salonga upon first listen, connecting with Salonga’s lyric “I am the girl with golden hair.”
college-writing-021497.zh: 小时候，马克·塔卢森（Marc Talusan）在第一次聆听时被Lea Salonga的音乐迷住了，与Salonga的歌词“我是金发的女孩”相联系。

college-writing-021498.en: Writes Talusan: “But by the time she sang, “What a joy! What a life! What a chance!” a few moments later, I had already returned to my own body, the body of a boy in the Philippines who just happened to have her hair.
college-writing-021498.zh: 塔卢森写道：“但当她唱歌时，“多么快乐！ 什么生活！ 什么机会！” 片刻之后，我已经回到了自己的身体，菲律宾一个男孩的身体恰好有她的头发。

college-writing-021499.en: My future may hold riches, but I would not live it as a beautiful woman.
college-writing-021499.zh: 我的未来可能拥有财富，但我不会像一个美丽的女人一样生活。

college-writing-021500.en: What Talusan did receive, throughout a childhood in the Philippines, was positive affirmation based upon the white skin-tone and blonde hair that came with Talusan’s albinism.
college-writing-021500.zh: 在菲律宾的整个童年时期，塔卢森确实得到了基于塔卢森白化病的白色肤色和金发的积极肯定。

college-writing-021501.en: Talusan’s grandmother would always say: “‘Those other kids aren’t white like you,’” writes Talusan.
college-writing-021501.zh: Talusan 的祖母总是说：“‘其他孩子不像你那样白人，’”塔卢森写道。

college-writing-021502.en: “And when she said white, puti, I could tell she also meant beautiful, intelligent, better, more special.”
college-writing-021502.zh: “当她说白人时，普蒂，我可以看出她的意思也是美丽、聪明、更好、更特别。”

college-writing-021503.en: Everywhere the young Talusan went, from grocery shopping to a bus ride to visit family, Talusan was met with positive affirmation because of this whiteness.
college-writing-021503.zh: 年轻的塔卢森（Talusan）所到之处，从杂货店购物到乘坐公共汽车去探亲，Talusan 得到了积极的肯定，因为这种白度。

college-writing-021504.en: This deification of whiteness in a culture in which whiteness is alien speaks to the immense power of the narrative of white supremacy that anchored Western colonization.
college-writing-021504.zh: 在白人是陌生的文化中，白度的这种神化说明了锚定西方殖民化的白人至上性叙事的巨大力量。

college-writing-021505.en: Yet, the same white body that makes Talusan so desirable at home─the same body, when migrated to the United States, the land of whiteness─is faced with the lack of desirability based on race; indeed, a meditation on this forms much of the opening section of the memoir, itself anchored in a reunion event for Harvard’s queer alumni.
college-writing-021505.zh: 然而，同样的白人身体，使塔卢森在家中如此受欢迎——同样的身体，当移居美国时，白度之地——面临着缺乏基于种族的渴望； 事实上，对这一点的沉思形成了回忆录的大部分开头部分，它本身就锚定在哈佛的酷儿校友的重聚活动中。

college-writing-021521.en: Here, Talusan interrogates “how our looks determined our place in the gay pecking order and how our lack of attractiveness had so much to do with our race and femininity,” before noting that Talusan and the other person of color at the reunion, Kit Clark, a queer black man, “both occupied liminal spaces in our white-dominated Harvard gay society” due to race.
college-writing-021521.zh: 在这里，Talusan 审问了“我们的外表如何决定了我们在同性恋啄食顺序中的位置，以及我们缺乏吸引力如何与我们的种族和女性气质有很大关系”，然后注意到塔卢森和另一个有色人种重聚，克拉克，一个酷儿 黑人，由于种族，“这两个人都占据了我们白人占主导的哈佛同性恋社会中的阈限空间”。

college-writing-021522.en: In Fairest’s carefully nuanced and detailed analysis, Talusan articulates the ways in which people of color create solidarity when there are only one or two non-white individuals in these elite, predominantly white spaces of privilege.
college-writing-021522.zh: 在 Fairest 精心细致和详细的分析中，Talusan 阐明了当这些精英（以白人为主）的特权空间中只有一两个非白人个人时，有色人种创造团结的方式。

college-writing-021523.en: At times, this solidarity is in simply seeing each other─in un-erasing the erasure whiteness creates.
college-writing-021523.zh: 有时，这种团结在于简单地看到对方——在消除白度造成的擦除中。

college-writing-021524.en: Writes Talusan movingly of the importance of Kit Clark’s queer POC presence in that elite, white LGBTQ space:
college-writing-021524.zh: Talusan 感人地写道 Kit Clark 的酷儿 POC 在那个精英的白色 LGBTQ 空间中的重要性：

college-writing-021525.en: “He recognized me as an albino Asian when everyone else thought I was white; he could tell my workout regimen was cover for a femininity I obscured because it was not attractive.”
college-writing-021525.zh: “当其他人都认为我是白人时，他认出我是一个白化亚洲人；他可以说我的锻炼方案是对我所掩盖的女性气质的掩护，因为它没有吸引力。”

college-writing-021526.en: And yet Talusan, despite constant positive affirmation because of “fair” skin and hair, while still known as Marc Talusan, always felt something was missing.
college-writing-021526.zh: 然而，尽管由于“公平”的皮肤和头发而不断得到积极的肯定，但塔卢森虽然仍然被称为马克·塔卢森（Marc Talusan），但总是觉得缺少了一些东西。

college-writing-021527.en: Although Talusan had had a lifelong understanding of queerness, it would not be until years later and a chance meeting with a student’s trans friend that Talusan would realize life could be lived as Meredith Talusan instead: “Me, a child from a Philippine province, descendant of peasant farmers, son of derelict immigrants.”
college-writing-021527.zh: 尽管塔卢森对酷儿有着终生的了解，但直到几年后，塔卢森才有机会与学生的跨性别朋友会面，才会意识到生活可以作为梅雷迪思·塔卢森（Meredith Talusan）过来：“我，一个来自菲律宾省的孩子， 农民，被遗弃移民的儿子。”

college-writing-021528.en: But before this moment is the journey: We see Talusan’s move from childhood sanctuary with grandmother Nanay Coro in the Filipino countryside to freshman year at Harvard learning queer theory in the classroom and the easy cruelty and cool disposability of dating and sex in American culture outside of the classroom; we see Talusan study abroad in London; we see Talusan having found a fulfilling relationship with a mature and loving partner, faced with this horrific impasse: As Talusan transitions to living as a woman, Talusan’s partner “didn’t see the person he fell in love with when he looked at me.”
college-writing-021528.zh: 但在这一刻之前，我们看到了塔卢森从童年避难所与菲律宾乡村的祖母纳奈·科罗（Nanay Coro）到哈佛大学大一的时候在课堂上学习酷儿理论以及约会和性爱的轻松残忍和酷可丢弃的转变 在课堂外的美国文化中； 我们在伦敦看到塔卢森出国留学； 我们看到塔卢森与一个成熟而有爱心的伴侣建立了充实的关系，面对这种可怕的僵局：当塔卢森过渡到女人的生活时，塔卢森的搭档“在看着我时没有看到他爱上的人。”

college-writing-021529.en: This nuance, this careful attention to looking and attempting to understand this journey not just from her own perspective, but also from those affected by it, gives a welcome maturity, depth and resonance to Talusan’s memoir.
college-writing-021529.zh: 这种细微差别，这种对观察和试图理解这段旅程的仔细关注，不仅从她自己的角度，而且从受它影响的人那里，都给了塔卢森的回忆录带来了可喜的成熟度、深度和共鸣。

college-writing-021530.en: One of the most touching scenes in the book is in the beginning of Talusan’s transition to womanhood.
college-writing-021530.zh: 书中最感人的场景之一是塔卢森向女性过渡的开始。

college-writing-021531.en: Talusan’s partner, Ralph, just wants her to look “normal,” as he calls it and asks Talusan to dress like a man, without make-up, for a friend’s important event at Carnegie Hall.
college-writing-021531.zh: Talusan 的搭档 Ralph 只是希望她看起来像他所说的“正常”，并要求 Talusan 穿得像个男人，不化妆，参加卡内基音乐厅的朋友的重要活动。

college-writing-021532.en: Talusan promises─but when she goes to the bathroom to scrub her face free of make-up, she cannot, eventually collapsing crying on the floor.
college-writing-021532.zh: Talusan 承诺——但当她去洗手间擦洗脸化妆时，她不能，最终倒在地板上哭泣。

college-writing-021533.en: To erase her make-up, to erase her femininity─to make herself look like a man when she is a woman─is destroying her in that moment.
college-writing-021533.zh: 抹去她的化妆，抹去她的女性气质——让自己看起来像个男人，在她是女人时——在那一刻正在摧毁她。

college-writing-021534.en: And Ralph, hearing her pain, comes into the bathroom and hugs her.
college-writing-021534.zh: 拉尔夫听到她的痛苦，走进浴室拥抱她。

college-writing-021535.en: He tells Talusan that he will never ask her to take off her make-up again.
college-writing-021535.zh: 他告诉塔卢森，他永远不会再要求她卸妆。

college-writing-021537.en: The make-up, a stand-in for true selfhood and identity, functions in conversation with the usage of the mirror, a central grounding conceit for Talusan’s flights into astute analysis of race, gender and sexuality not just here, but elsewhere in the book.
college-writing-021537.zh: 化妆是真正自我和身份的替身，与镜子的使用在对话中发挥作用，这是塔卢森对种族、性别和性行为的精明分析的核心基础，不仅在这里，而且在书中的其他地方。

college-writing-021538.en: While an argument can be made that the vehicle of a mirror as a tool for self-reflection is a bit on-point, a bit overused, it does hold a productive presence both narratively and structurally in this gorgeous and lyrical debut.
college-writing-021538.zh: 虽然可以说将镜子作为自我反思工具的工具有点过时，有点过度使用，但它确实在叙事和结构上具有丰富的表现力，在这个华丽而抒情的处子中。

college-writing-021539.en: It is worth noting how Talusan begins to unpack the uneasy conversation between herself and the figure of the white, golden-blonde female as the ideal woman still proliferated by post-colonial white supremacy.
college-writing-021539.zh: 值得注意的是，Talusan 是如何开始解开自己与金发白人、金发女郎之间的不安对话的包装的，因为理想的女性仍然被后殖民的白人至上主义所激怒。

college-writing-021540.en: Writes Talusan toward the end of Fairest:
college-writing-021540.zh: 在最公平的结尾写了塔卢森：

college-writing-021541.en: “Barrett’s words kept playing in my head, ‘I don’t see you as trans,’ coupled with ‘I can’t tell you’re Asian.’ The way he looked at me was exactly what I’d honed over many years, this trick of perception, and it puzzled me that I was dissatisfied over having accomplished it, a state of being so many trans women sacrifice so much to achieve.”
college-writing-021541.zh: “巴雷特的话一直在我的脑海中播放，‘我不认为你是跨性别者’，再加上‘我不能告诉你是亚洲人’。他看着我的方式正是我多年来磨练的，这种感知的技巧，让我很困惑。 对完成它感到不满，这是许多跨性别女性为实现而牺牲的状态。”

college-writing-021542.en: Here, Talusan points to the problematic trans and racial double erasure endemic to the cis white gaze.
college-writing-021542.zh: 在这里，Talusan 指出了顺式白人凝视特有的有问题的跨性别和种族双重擦除。

college-writing-021543.en: Later, Talusan again pushes back against this erasure of her trans identity: “I couldn’t bring myself to wish I had never been a man, because my life as a man was part of the complexity of my being, this unusual person I had become, someone whose insights I cherished.”
college-writing-021543.zh: 后来，塔卢森再次反对她的跨性别身份的这种抹杀：“我无法让自己成为一个男人的希望，因为我作为男人的生活是我存在的复杂性的一部分，我成为了这个不寻常的人，一个我珍视的人。”

college-writing-021544.en: In the time in which Talusan was coming into adulthood after immigrating to the United States, there was less space for duality and gender fluidity.
college-writing-021544.zh: 在塔卢森移民到美国后，二元性和性别流动性的空间越来越少。

college-writing-021545.en: Now, however, that Talusan is more centered in her own culture rather than global white supremacy, she is more aware of gender fluidity in her own cultural history: “among my own indigenous ancestors, select male-bodied people who lived their lives as women were held in high esteem and found themselves husbands, in domestic life treated identically as other women.”
college-writing-021545.zh: 然而，现在，塔卢森更多地集中在自己的文化中，而不是全球白人至上，她在自己的文化历史中更加了解性别流动性： 尊重并发现自己是丈夫，在家庭生活中与其他女性一样对待。”

college-writing-021546.en: Now, too, that we are living in a time with more acceptance of nonbinary gender expression, Talusan questions if she even needs the language of identifying as a “woman” anymore.
college-writing-021546.zh: 现在，我们也生活在一个更加接受非二元性别表达的时代，塔卢森是否需要将她的语言认定为“女人”的语言。

college-writing-021547.en: Indeed, at the university reunion in 2018 that structurally grounds the narrative, Talusan wonders: “why becoming a woman had seemed so urgent then, when it felt so mundane now, as I realized that being a woman was less important to me than having experienced being a woman, that I’d grown much less precious about how people gendered me, even though I still felt alienated from the toxic parts of manhood.”
college-writing-021547.zh: 的确，在2018年的大学聚会上，在结构上为叙事奠定了基础，塔卢森想：“为什么当现在感觉如此平凡，因为我意识到作为一个女人对我来说不如经历过成为女性，这对我来说更重要 尽管我仍然感到与人类的有毒部分疏远，但我对人们对我的性别化程度越来越不那么珍贵了。”

college-writing-021548.en: The language we have now, the spaces and community support to exist firmly within a gender fluid and/or nonbinary gender identity are developments made mostly within the last 50 years.
college-writing-021548.zh: 我们现在所拥有的语言、空间和社区支持牢固地存在于性别流动和/或非二元性别认同中，这些是过去 50 年来的发展。

college-writing-021549.en: They have been made, in large part, because of the work of inspiring trans activists like Talusan.
college-writing-021549.zh: 它们的制作，很大程度上是因为激励塔卢森等激励跨性别活动家的工作。

college-writing-021550.en: Because of them, people are no longer faced with erasure or binary opposition as the only realities.
college-writing-021550.zh: 因为他们，人们不再面临抹杀或二元对立作为唯一的现实。

college-writing-021551.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 781

college-writing-021552.en: Just as there are multiple feminisms, there are multiple genders and multiple sexualities along a spectrum.
college-writing-021552.zh: 就像有多种女权主义一样，有多种性别和多种性行为。

college-writing-021553.en: And Talusan, like everyone else, is no longer forced into a binary at either end of this spectrum to exist in this world, but can now exist at various points on this spectrum, engaging with masculinity and femininity in a happy balance that most aligns with her authentic self.
college-writing-021553.zh: 和其他人一样，Talusan 不再被迫进入这个光谱的任何一端的二元，而是现在可以存在于这个光谱上的不同点，与男性气质和女性气质交往，与她的真实自我保持一致。

college-writing-021668.en: In paragraph 9, Wabuke highlights an incident in which Talusan’s partner, Ralph, asks her to look “normal.”
college-writing-021668.zh: 在第 9 段中，Wabuke 强调了 Talusan 的搭档 Ralph 要求她看起来“正常”的事件。

college-writing-021669.en: Here, Ralph is asking Talusan to be something other than she is.

college-writing-021670.en: Have you ever had to erase or negate something about yourself to please others?
college-writing-021670.zh: 您是否曾经不得不抹去或否定自己的某些东西来取悦他人？

college-writing-021671.en: Have you had to hide things from family or friends?
college-writing-021671.zh: 您是否不得不向家人或朋友隐瞒事情？

college-writing-021672.en: Perhaps you had a partner who didn’t like the way you dressed, acted, talked?
college-writing-021672.zh: 也许你有一个不喜欢你穿着、表演、交谈的方式的伴侣？

college-writing-021673.en: For this assignment, describe a situation in which you found yourself pleasing someone else but hurting your own self in the process.
college-writing-021673.zh: 对于这个任务，描述一个你发现自己取悦别人但在这个过程中伤害自己的情况。

college-writing-021674.en: You should provide enough background and details so that the reader understands the conflict you experienced and how that situation changed you.
college-writing-021674.zh: 您应该提供足够的背景和细节，以便读者了解您所经历的冲突以及这种情况如何改变了您。

college-writing-021675.en: You will want to review Chapter 10, “Exemplification,” to help you create an essay that helps your reader understand your experience.
college-writing-021675.zh: 您将需要查看第 10 章“示例”，以帮助您撰写一篇文章，帮助您的读者了解您的体验。

college-writing-021677.en: The author opens the essay by sharing Talusan’s connection to the music of Lea Salonga, stating that “Talusan was enthralled with the music of Lea Salonga upon first listen, connecting with Salonga’s lyric ‘I am the girl with golden hair.’” Music, regardless of type, is extremely important to most people and most societies.
college-writing-021677.zh: 作者通过分享Talusan与Lea Salonga的音乐的联系来打开这篇文章，并说“Talusan在第一次听时就被Lea Salonga的音乐迷住了，与Salonga的歌词“我是金发的女孩”联系在一起。” 无论类型如何，音乐对大多数人和大多数社会都极为重要。

college-writing-021678.en: For this assignment, you are to write about a song or an artist with whom you connect.
college-writing-021678.zh: 对于这项任务，您要写一首歌曲或与您联系的艺术家。

college-writing-021679.en: With the assumption that some of your readers won’t know the artist, you will need to explain to the reader who the artist is.
college-writing-021679.zh: 假设您的一些读者不认识艺术家，您需要向读者解释艺术家是谁。

college-writing-021680.en: You will then need to provide a detailed explanation as to why you connect with that artist or a specific song by the artist.
college-writing-021680.zh: 然后，您需要详细说明您与该艺术家或艺术家的特定歌曲联系的原因。

college-writing-021681.en: You may want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” to help you use vibrant details.
college-writing-021681.zh: 您可能想查看第 8 章“描述”，以帮助您使用充满活力的细节。

college-writing-021682.en: You may also want to review Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” to help you integrate any song quotations you choose to include in your essay.
college-writing-021682.zh: 您可能还想回顾第 19 章，“撰写基于来源的论文”，以帮助您整合您选择包含在论文中的任何歌曲引用。

college-writing-021686.zh: 具有挑战性的社会价值观 785

college-writing-021688.en: This essay is Hope Wabuke’s review of Meredith Talusan’s book.
college-writing-021688.zh: 这篇文章是 Hope Wabuke 对 Meredith Talusan 书的评论。

college-writing-021689.en: To clearly support her claims, Wabuke integrates Talusan’s words within the review.
college-writing-021689.zh: 为了明确支持她的主张，Wabuke 将 Talusan 的话整合到了评论中。

college-writing-021690.en: For this assignment, you are to write a review of a favorite book.
college-writing-021690.zh: 对于这个作业，你要写一篇最喜欢的书的评论。

college-writing-021691.en: The purpose of your review is to get your reader excited about reading the book, so you will need to include good details without giving away the plot.
college-writing-021691.zh: 您的评论的目的是让您的读者对阅读这本书感到兴奋，因此您需要在不泄露情节的情况下包含良好的细节。

college-writing-021692.en: You may want to review Chapter 8, “Description,” to help you select vibrant details to excite your reader.
college-writing-021692.zh: 您可能想查看第 8 章“描述”，以帮助您选择充满活力的细节来激发您的读者。

college-writing-021693.en: You will also want to review Chapter 18, “Summarizing and Paraphrasing,” and Chapter 19, “Writing a Source-Based Essay,” to help you properly incorporate quotations from your chosen book.
college-writing-021693.zh: 您还需要回顾第 18 章“总结和释义”和第 19 章“撰写基于来源的论文”，以帮助您正确纳入所选书籍的引文。

college-writing-022251.en: Preface to the paperback edition -- Prologue: Alone -- Stepping inside: On the brink -- Speaking out/acting out -- High school is for making memories -- Negative is positive -- Honor and other relative things -- School paper and a whole new adolescent world - Making contact: Out of the whirlwind and on to the playing field -- Circle of friends: it's not peer pressure, it's the adolescent way of life -- Graffiti, God, and other meaningful things -- Sex: let's get it out of the way, but don't look at me naked -- Lacrosse and other challenges -- Taking care of each other and other grownup preoccupations -- Moshing is a way to belong -- Shedding light on darkness: school is an uncomfortable place to learn -- Making sense: Rearrange your room when you can't arrange yourself -- Dilemmas of a fourteen-year-old girl: contradictions as a way of life -- Creating my own space: long cold winter and descent into darkness -- Broken promises: theirs and ours -- Doing high school the old-fashioned way -- It's my prom, my life -- Resignation: adolescence is sometimes a life-or-death issue -- Great unknown lies ahead: to the wilderness or to college -- Epilogue: Warm embrace -- Postscript -- Acknowledgments -- Index -- A reader's guide.
college-writing-022251.zh: 平装本版的序言——序言：独自一人——走进去：走在边缘——说出来/表演——高中是为了回忆——消极的是积极的——荣誉和其他相关的东西——学校的论文和一个全新的青少年世界——联系：走出旋风并继续前进 竞争环境——朋友圈：这不是同龄人的压力，而是青少年的生活方式——涂鸦、上帝和其他有意义的事情——性：让我们把它排除在外，但不要赤身裸体——曲棍球和其他挑战——互相照顾 和其他成年人的关注——Moshing 是一种归属方式——在黑暗中照亮：学校是一个不舒服的学习场所——有意义的地方：当你无法安排自己时重新安排你的房间——一个 14 岁女孩的困境：矛盾作为一种生活方式——创造我的 自己的空间：漫长的寒冷冬天和黑暗的承诺：他们和我们的承诺——以老式的方式上高中——这是我的舞会，我的生活——辞职：青春期有时是一个生死攸关的问题——未来是大而未知的问题： 荒野或大学——结语：温暖的拥抱——后记——致谢——索引——读者指南。
